for the criticism have been stated many times. on the institutional level, we believe that the instruments offered by the treaties would have avoided the risk of an intergovernmental agreement and would have strengthened the governance and budgetary discipline of the euro area while remaining within the union's legal framework. it is truly paradoxical that while the ink on which the six-pack is written has not yet dried, some states want to amend it by intergovernmental means, introducing elements which they had not previously requested or even opposed, thus taking a step backwards rather the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, space has become a highly topical subject. this is demonstrated by the intense media interest in the launch of the first two galileo satellites, which took off from the european base at kourou on 21 october, representing the first step towards achieving european union independence in satellite navigation. achieving this ambitious goal is largely due to the impetus provided by article 189 of the treaty of lisbon, which clearly and unequivocally assigns the european union the responsibility to coordinate and consolidate national space policies and programmes through a common approach that can foster scientific and technical progress and industrial competitiveness. the aim of the treaty is to recognise the importance of space and the services it provides for the citizens of the community in the social, economic and strategic fields, and to consider it as a functional means for the european union to compete on the world stage with its competitors. the treaty thus provides an authoritative basis for the achievement of ambitious objectives for which the european institutions must provide adequate resources and appropriate legislative instruments. in this connection, i had the honour of working in the past few months within the itre committee on the draft report on the european union's space strategy for citizens. i hope that the final version of the text will reflect in a strong way the ambitious proposals we have intended to include in the report. i am referring in particular to the disparity in treatment which has emerged between the two strategic programmes of european space policy, galileo and gmes. while i strongly share the commission's view that galileo, one of the pillars of the european space policy, is of great importance, i believe that, in view of the €3.5 billion of investment that has been made so far and the strategic nature of the programme, gmes also deserves equal treatment, both economically and strategically. i am convinced that only by exploiting both programmes in a synergistic way can we guarantee technological and political independence for our continent and bring enormous economic and social benefits to the citizens of europe. it is for this reason that in the report authorised by the itre committee, which we will vote on shortly, i expressed my strong regret at the commission's decision not to include the financing of gmes in the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, aware that the lack of a financial plan for economic support risks rendering useless the considerable investments made to date. another important aspect to be clarified is the strategy that the commission intends to pursue with regard to the management aspects of the galileo and gmes programmes in order to rationalise the organisational structure and have a precise picture of the maintenance costs. the report also stresses the need for europe to be independent in its access to space and for trade agreements with third countries to be based on a perfectly reciprocal relationship, avoiding dependence on suppliers from outside europe for certain key technologies such as launchers. these, together with the creation of a european space surveillance and environment system and the strengthening of research activities, are the key elements of an ambitious text which we hope will provide the answers that european citizens expect. the european space policy must support industry if it is to be forward-looking. at a time of deep economic crisis such as the present one, it is all the more necessary that the union should provide economic support for the space industry in order to maintain the competitiveness of our continent in an increasingly competitive global system. only if we provide european industry with real tangible prospects can we expect it to invest in human resources and in complex technologies in the long term. only if european industry maintains its leadership in space know-how can our continent remain a leader in this crucial sector. it is in this direction that i, as rapporteur for european space policy, have intended to proceed, in the hope that a convinced vote by parliament will give force to a text which, in line with article 189 of the new treaty, will guarantee scientific and technological development in a sector whose sustainable growth is an essential condition for the union.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner tajani, these are real european infrastructures which are indispensable for the implementation of european policies. gmes specifically for safety and environment and the management of mitigation, global warming and extreme weather event review policies. this must be included in the multiannual budget of the european union. if this is not possible, it may be an opportunity to introduce project bonds which also have an anticyclonic function. i have no doubt that this is an investment in our future and that it will pay off in a very few years. we're going to keep going down this road, commissioner.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the members of the committee on agriculture for their cooperation in the preparation of this report. it was a fruitful collaboration which led us to adopt, almost unanimously, a text on a subject which has been underestimated by the institutions and by the political world for too long, namely food waste. an underestimation we can no longer afford. if it is true, as all the most authoritative sources of information now say, that one of the main problems of the immediate future will be to meet a new and very strong demand for food, and that the issue of food security has therefore become one of the most difficult problems to tackle because in the future the demand for food will tend to exceed the supply, we can no longer afford to remain passive in the face of a phenomenon, that of food waste. when we talk about food, we are talking about food that is still perfectly edible, which has assumed an enormous and no longer sustainable dimension. in fact, we have reached a point - fao estimates that one third of the food produced each year in the world is wasted for human consumption, in europe we are already at 50%, and that each citizen on average wastes 105 kilograms of food per year - where we are told that we are not only facing an ethical problem, but a real economic, social issue with enormous implications for the environment. that is why we want to make the fight against food waste a priority on the political agenda of the european union. we therefore ask the commission to guide the 27 member states in adopting a common strategy to promote a real leap forward in reducing food waste significantly by 2025. we therefore ask that all those associations, voluntary groups and centres of initiative which have launched concrete projects in this field in various countries be given greater weight. these experiences have generated a virtuous system which has ensured a considerable recovery of products to be allocated to those segments of the population in economic difficulties. i would remind you that in europe, in rich europe, there are almost 70 million citizens who live below the poverty line and are malnourished. we therefore ask the commission to give us specific directives. in particular, it would be important to amend the rules on public procurement for catering services in canteens and hospitals so that, on equal terms, those undertakings which guarantee a management model aimed at combating food waste are given priority in the award of contracts. in this respect, i would like to stress that the important thing is that the european institutions must set an example, starting with this parliament. finally, we call for accountability for all actors in the food chain. a genuine awareness-raising campaign must be promoted, with the major farmers' organisations, industry, schools and universities at the forefront, in order to bring about a civilized and scientific culture geared to a more sober and environmentally sustainable consumption model. the european parliament has done its part with this report, and we hope that the commission will now take up this work and put in place an effective strategy. firstly, we hope that they will take action now to declare 2014 the european year against food waste; the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. this would immediately send a signal to all citizens that the european union is capable of being at the forefront of defining a fairer and more balanced model of development.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we cannot allow food waste to increase any further and we must combat it by means of specific instruments, but also by means of a culture that shows its economic, environmental and social effects. food waste has increased by 50% in the last 30 years, with consequences not only ethical but also economic, environmental, social, nutritional and health. it does not seem ethically sustainable that, in the face of the approximately 70 million people in europe living below the poverty line, there are still tons of edible food thrown in the garbage and that the materials used to produce and pack these foods cannot be differentiated as much as possible. this elimination therefore comes at a high economic and social cost. the committee on agriculture's proposals cover areas ranging from packaging to more detailed information on expiry, and aim to help citizens avoid waste and reuse products.

in writing. mr president, a study commissioned by the fao reveals that 1.3 billion tonnes of food for human consumption is wasted every year. the study also shows that industrialized and developing countries waste about the same amount of food - 670 and 630 million tons respectively. every year, consumers in the richest countries waste almost as much food (222 million tonnes) as the entire net food production of sub-saharan africa (230 million tonnes). fruits and vegetables are the most wasted foods. the amount of food lost or wasted each year is equivalent to more than half of the world's entire annual cereal production (2.3 billion tonnes in 2009/2010). information in schools and policy initiatives could be a starting point for changing this behaviour by even promoting, along with other policies, the fight against food-based metabolic diseases. we need a collective awareness that can weaken the commercial value of the appearance and quantity of food, adapting it more to the real needs of each consumer. it is a difficult challenge, but the european union can do it, as it has done in the past with policies with a very strong social impact, such as the ban on smoking in public places.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to amend the regulation on the community visa code, as it concerns some technical changes which will not change the practice of the member states. this amendment to the visa code will ensure greater legal certainty and harmonised application of the rules. in addition, they are provisions of practical importance for travellers and airlines, which will avoid the repetition of checks on persons who have already been checked and for whom it has been verified that there is no risk of illegal immigration.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because it is a correction which will not change the practice of the member states but which serves to exempt from the requirement to present an airport visa the citizens of eu member states which have not yet applied all the provisions of schengen (united kingdom, ireland, cyprus, romania, bulgaria). i think the amendment is logical because it would be pointless to check further a person who already has a visa or a residence permit and who has already been checked and found harmless with regard to the risk of illegal immigration. the proposal would also reduce the administrative burden on member countries.
in writing. − we believe that a community visa code should be established in order to clarify the rules on transit through the international airport zone and thus ensure legal certainty and transparency. some technical amendments are necessary to ensure legal certainty and harmonised application of the rules. this clarification is of practical importance for individual travellers and for the airlines themselves. this is a technical correction of the provisions on airport transit visas. this correction will not change the practice of the member states. the amendment to the regulation provides that third-country nationals holding a valid visa or residence permit issued by a member state which does not (yet) apply all the schengen provisions (united kingdom, ireland, cyprus, bulgaria, romania) are exempted from the requirement to have an airport transit visa. we do not think it is necessary to check a person who already has a visa or a residence permit again if he has already been checked and it has been found that he does not pose a risk of illegal immigration. this should also reduce the administrative burden on the member states themselves.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of mr michel's report. i agree with the proposed amendments to the said regulation. it is necessary to eliminate any possible misunderstanding about the rules relating to transit through the international area of airports and in so doing to ensure legal certainty and transparency.
in writing. − the text adopted amending the regulation on the community code on airport transit visas consists solely of a corrective amendment to the code in force since april 2010. this amendment refers to third-country nationals who are subject to specific visa requirements. if they hold a valid visa or residence permit issued by a member state which does not yet apply all the schengen provisions (united kingdom, ireland, cyprus, bulgaria, romania), they are exempt from the requirement to have an airport transit visa because they are already checked within the european bureaucratic apparatus. for the member states nothing changes and for the citizens concerned it is a simplification of practices and the possibility of traveling more easily.

in writing. the aim of today's vote is to clarify the rules on transit through the international airport zone and thereby ensure legal certainty and transparency. the current regulation is flawed. for example, the point concerning the exemption from the airport transit visa requirement is not very clear. since the handbook cannot create legally binding obligations for member states, it is necessary to amend the visa code in order to ensure legal certainty and harmonised application of the rules. this clarification is of practical importance for individual travellers and airlines. now, after this vote, third country nationals holding a visa issued by a member state which does not fully apply the common visa policy must be exempted from the airport transit visa requirement.

in writing. the recommendation we voted on in the house this morning provides a good example of the role of the european union, which is to harmonize the different systems at global level, in this case in road safety, environmental protection and trade, with a view to simplifying the regulatory framework. approvals granted under unece (united nations economic commission for europe) regulations will henceforth be considered eu approvals, thus avoiding duplication not only of technical requirements but also of certification and administrative procedures, to the benefit of industry and national authorities, given the benefits that our approval of the draft council decision on the accession of the union to the regulation of the economic commission for europe laying down uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to the protection of the occupants of the cab of a commercial vehicle will bring to the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the council decision on the union's position in the unece negotiations on the two new draft regulations on pedestrian safety and led lights. i believe that the implementation of the provisions contained in the texts will bring about a further improvement in road safety standards, in which there is still much to be done to reduce the high number of road accident victims. unfortunately, despite the efforts of the member states, many people are still being killed in these very serious events. in fact, in 2009 alone, there were 35,000 deaths and 1.5 million injuries, and according to the latest estimates, 16,000 of them are children. for these reasons, it is necessary for the union, which currently subscribes to 126 unece regulations, to bring the provisions in force into line with the most recent provisions contained in the regulations of the united nations economic commission for europe.
in writing. the measures contained in the draft regulation drawn up by the united nations economic commission for europe propose a series of purely technical measures aimed at producers operating on a worldwide scale. the aim of these agreements, as in the case of more than a hundred similar regulations, is to introduce rules for the approval of a given category of products on the world market, thus reducing the bureaucratic burden on industry. in this case, the text drawn up by unece contains rules identifying common production standards for the type-approval of vehicles, also identified in consultation with manufacturers in the sector. i share the objective of the agreement reached by the geneva economic commission and therefore vote in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision.
in writing. - the draft regulation of the united nations economic commission for europe on the safety of pedestrians and the draft regulation of the united nations economic commission for europe on light emitting diode (led) light sources are also supported. the reasons are the same, so simplification and bureaucratization, increased competitiveness.
in writing. - the text by mr moreira on the position of the european union on the draft regulation of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) is a text on the mandate given to the european commission to negotiate and vote on behalf of the eu within unece, a global un forum for open discussions on motor vehicle regulations to which the eu has acceded by establishing the compulsory application of 62 out of 106 existing regulations. the european commission therefore sends a document to the council and parliament each year on the activities of the world forum for vehicle regulations. in this case, we are talking about pedestrian safety and light sources with light emitting diodes (leds).
in writing. − the world forum for the harmonization of vehicle regulations (wp.29) of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) is a global forum on motor vehicle regulations, with the aim of promoting harmonised technical requirements that reduce development costs, prevent duplication of administrative procedures for industry and thus contribute to efficiency and reduced costs for consumers and society. agreeing that this unece regulation will allow the same standards to be applied in many countries and that the benefits of such harmonised regulations are reflected in road safety, environmental protection and trade, i am voting in favour of the proposal for a council decision on the unece position on pedestrian safety and light emitting diode (led) light sources.
in writing. − in recent years, the european union has done much to improve road safety, and in particular pedestrian safety, by extending the scope of the issue to other areas of the world. the world forum for the harmonization of vehicle regulations, which brought together the main motor vehicle manufacturing countries, not only in europe but also in asia and the americas, has contributed to this process. more than 120 representatives have regularly attended the world forum sessions. with today's vote in favour i hope that the two new draft regulations, the first on pedestrian safety and the second on led light sources, will lead to even better safety results than those already achieved.
in writing. − the commission signed an agreement with the indonesian government to replace provisions in previous eu-indonesia bilateral agreements. the eu's replacement provisions concern the air transport sector and would aim to put an end to discriminatory practices against european air carriers, which were previously made possible by the nature of previous bilateral agreements. in addition to being economically harmful to european airlines, such discrimination also constituted, under community law, a breach of the provisions of the european treaties on equal treatment for nationals established in a member state other than their own. the commission's action is therefore aimed at protecting european airlines and european commercial interests. my vote on the recommendation is therefore in favour.
in writing. - my vote on mr simpson's report is in favour. the conclusion of an eu-indonesia agreement is necessary, in particular, to allow all eu air carriers non-discriminatory access to routes between the eu member states concerned and indonesia.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr simpson's report on the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the eu and the republic of indonesia on air services because that agreement aims to achieve the objective of granting all eu air carriers non-discriminatory access to routes to indonesia. generally all relations between eu states and third countries on air transport are governed by bilateral agreements and in this case the text is merely an addition to the 19 agreements already in existence. greater freedom of movement improves relations between states and makes life easier for citizens; i therefore believe that we shall see a steady increase and renewal of bilateral agreements in the future.
in writing. - bilateral agreements between member states and third countries in the field of international air transport may discriminate against eu carriers established in the territory of a member state but owned or controlled by nationals of other member states. agreeing with the aim of guaranteeing to nationals of member states who have exercised their freedom of establishment the same treatment as the host member state accords to its own nationals and with the aim of ensuring compliance with eu law by amending or supplementing the existing provisions contained in bilateral air service agreements between member states and third countries, i express my vote in favour of the conclusion of the agreement.
in writing. - with today's vote we are correcting the differences and anomalies in the 19 bilateral air services agreements concluded between the member states of the european union and indonesia. in the field of international air transport, relations between member states and third countries have traditionally been governed by bilateral air services agreements. in 2002, the court of justice ruled that national designation clauses in bilateral agreements violate union law, as they allow a third country to refuse, revoke or suspend the permits or authorisations of an air carrier designated by a member state, but of which a significant proportion of the ownership or effective control is not held by that member state or its nationals. our vote will put an end to this discriminatory situation.
in writing. − the international civil aviation organisation, in accordance with its statute, only allows states to join it as members. however, a few years ago the commission tried to open negotiations for eu accession, hoping for a change in the icao statute. this change has not taken place, and the eu remains excluded from full participation. with the memorandum now proposed by the council, the eu is attempting to circumvent the obstacles posed by international law in order to informally join icao and exert its influence within it, even though it is not legally entitled to do so. in essence, the agreement in question appears to be a 'trojan horse' which will allow the commission to circumvent international law, and to the detriment of eu member states which, on the contrary, are legally and fully-fledged members of icao, but could nevertheless gradually lose their ability to exercise their rights within icao itself if this memorandum were to enter into force. there are certainly tangible benefits to be gained from increased eu involvement in icao, but these benefits would be achieved by circumventing the provisions of international law, and by overriding the rights legally granted to member states. i therefore vote against.
in writing. − the eu and icao will undoubtedly strengthen and consolidate their relations if they are formalised and improved. to this end, my colleagues and i unanimously approved the memorandum of cooperation between the european union and the international civil aviation organisation. icao was established as a specialised un agency and member states cooperate in aviation safety, air traffic management and environmental protection. the eu therefore has an interest in contributing to the formulation of icao policies. the memorandum of cooperation (moc) aims to achieve greater harmonization and closer coordination of their activities and, last but not least, to ensure a more efficient use of the limited resources available, for example by avoiding the repetition of the same activities. greater cooperation, such as mutual access to each other's databases, will certainly improve and simplify the whole system.
in writing. − the development of a framework for enhanced cooperation would allow the european union to increase its weight within icao. the memorandum would also be important in ensuring greater harmonisation of standards and closer coordination of their respective activities. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − the memorandum of cooperation (moc) between the eu and the international civil aviation organisation (icao) to formalise and improve relations and cooperation aims to strengthen cooperation in the areas of aviation safety, air navigation security, air traffic management and environmental protection. in the light of the strong interest of the eu in contributing to the strengthening of icao policies and the many icao rules and regulations that have already been incorporated into european union law, i am voting in favour of the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the memorandum establishing a framework for enhanced cooperation and laying down the related procedural modalities for its operation.
in writing. - i congratulate mr simpson on his excellent work. the european parliament, in view of the proposal for a council decision, is committed to helping to strengthen the eu's position within icao by adopting this recommendation. it is necessary, as proposed by the council, to conclude the memorandum of cooperation between the european union and the international civil aviation organisation and, in the light of its functioning, the roles to be assigned within the joint committee should be actively fulfilled by the commission, the council and the member states. this committee will become crucial for the implementation of the memorandum of cooperation and for the adoption of the provisions concerning cooperation in specific areas. furthermore, further rules in the areas of air navigation protection, air traffic management and environmental protection will be necessary to achieve the highest level of aviation safety worldwide.
in writing. the european union is also committed to the development of a common defence policy and to the promotion of the rule of law. the general objective of the memorandum of cooperation is to ensure greater harmonisation of the rules and closer coordination of their activities. furthermore, while preserving the integrity of both parties, the memorandum aims to achieve a more efficient use of limited resources and to avoid the repetition of the same activities. the memorandum of cooperation will provide financial support of eur 500 000 per year for an initial period of three years on the basis of a specific contribution agreement under the financial and administrative framework agreement between the union and the un. this budget may be supplemented by financial support from the member states or the european aviation safety agency.
in writing. the exponential growth of weee waste makes it imperative to make major changes to the regulations governing its recycling and production. the growth of the segment is directly proportional to the impact on the europe 2020 objectives towards a resource efficient economy: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. in line with these objectives, in addition to avoiding further damage to the environment and retaining valuable resources, high collection rates, adequate recycling standards, strong action against illegal exports and a fairer distribution of responsibilities and costs between producers, consumers and public authorities are needed. the text as amended by parliament seems to be in line with these requirements and also contains two particularly sensitive points which deserve attention and support. firstly, environmentally friendly design, not only in terms of energy consumption standards but also in terms of simplifying the procedures for disposal or recovery of raw materials. equally important is the need for the costs of recovery and treatment of raw materials to become an integral part of the product price, so as to provide a form of incentive to purchase products with a lower impact. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. the resolution on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of the european parliament and council directive on waste electrical and electronic equipment was adopted by a large majority in the house today. this is a good result, considering the long road and difficult negotiations that have been behind the compromise reached. as you know, the directive requires member states to separate the collection of electrical and electronic equipment and sets recovery and recycling targets. the update voted today, which must be formally adopted by the council before being published in the official journal, sets ambitious targets, particularly as regards increasing the collection rate of waste electronic products. in this sense, i think it is appropriate to provide for an extension for those countries which, like italy, do not have adequate infrastructure at the moment, giving them more time to implement the new european legislation properly.
in writing. - i am in favour of the text, as amended, proposed by the european parliament. in many cases, this is a request to reinstate the european parliament's position at first reading. the clarifications to the directive requested by our institution are very significant. for example, it is essential that the definition of concepts be definitively clarified in the directive itself and not lead to a fragmentation of the internal market through different national applications and practices.
in writing. the revision of the weee directive on waste electrical and electronic equipment requires member states to develop new techniques for separate collection and recycling of such materials. i think the target that is being set is more than good, because with a common scope for the rohs directive on hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment and a mandatory separate collection rate of 65% for electrical products, we can achieve 5% recycling by 2016.
in writing. - the report by mr florenz on waste electrical and electronic equipment was voted on today in plenary. the new environmental objectives were approved today in agreement with the council. the updated 2003 waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) directive also gives consumers the possibility to return small e-waste to retailers, reducing the bureaucratic burden on businesses. member states will have to increase the collection of e-waste, with 45 tonnes of e-waste to be collected by 2016 for every 100 tonnes of goods placed on the market in the previous three years. by 2019, this figure should rise to 65% or alternatively, 85% of the waste electronic material produced can be collected. ten countries that need to improve their infrastructure, not including italy, will have an intermediate target of 40% and may request an extension until 2021 to reach the final target. once the council has formally approved the new rules, which will be published in the official journal, member states will have 18 months to transpose the provisions into national law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document in question because it will finally update the 2003 directive on the management of waste electrical and electronic equipment and will make it easier to collect and recycle refrigerators, telephones and computer gadgets. i think it is particularly useful that from today consumers will be able to return small e-waste directly to retailers, reducing the bureaucratic burden on businesses and optimising the specific collection procedures. better treatment of such waste will also make it possible to recover more valuable raw materials such as gold used for electronic circuits, and ultimately prevent harmful substances from ending up in landfills.
in writing. - i fully agree with the report by mr florenz on waste electrical and electronic equipment, a subject which is becoming increasingly worrying as this type of waste continues to increase. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that we must do everything possible to ensure that raw materials are recycled and recovered, and that health is not harmed in any way. awareness and information campaigns for european citizens are essential if a drive towards separate collection is to be achieved with a significant impact on prices. the next step will be to close the gaps between member states in the implementation of the directive, as different percentages are currently provided for in the recycling targets. i believe, however, that this report strikes the right balance between the tasks which fall to the european union and those which fall to the member states.
in writing. - the compromise agreement reached at the informal trilogue on 20 december is, in my view, a good result for the protection of the recycling of small household appliances and the consequent protection of the environment. the weee directive currently in force already requires member states to separate the collection of electrical and electronic equipment and sets recovery and recycling targets. the old text implements the principle of producer responsibility and requires member states to collect an average of at least 4 kg of electrical and electronic waste per inhabitant per year. the recast we voted this morning adds important details, such as setting a collection rate of 65% to be achieved by 2016; provide for reuse targets, increasing recycling targets by 5%, with a specific target for medical equipment, and reduce administrative costs for manufacturers in relation to registration and reporting procedures. one note which i find particularly encouraging is the requirement for retailers to collect small appliances even without buying new equivalent appliances, but limited to retail outlets with an area of more than 400 square metres with a collection point that can be set up in the immediate vicinity of the store.
in writing. - the weaknesses of directive 98/8 must be eliminated, as parliament has already called for. i agree with the rapporteur on this point, but also that the authorisation in question is the most effective system for promoting the availability of the products in question, stimulating innovation and improving the protection of human health and the environment. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs klaßper on the achievement of this compromise with the council on the use of biocides in products on the market. this regulation defines the most dangerous substances in disinfectants, detergents, paints, etc. and prohibits their use in products sold on the market. the european chemicals agency is responsible for marketing authorization and will be responsible for monitoring the application of this regulation in order to considerably increase the level of protection of health and the environment that it seeks to achieve. the products will thus be safer for consumers and the trade authorizations will bring costs into line.
in writing. the report on the placing on the market and use of biocidal products was voted on today in plenary. today, a major agreement was reached with the council which provides for stricter health and environmental controls on products to repel insects or kill bacteria and common rules for companies on the authorisation process for sale. this agreement has found ways to improve safety checks and the authorisation process, so that safer products are guaranteed. for the new rules to enter into force, formal approval by the council is still required, with which there is a prior agreement. the new legislation further harmonises the european market for pesticide products and introduces new deadlines for submitting applications for authorisation. the procedures for the recognition of authorisations between countries will also be simplified and from 2013 the possibility will be introduced to apply for authorisation directly at eu level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because it will allow for stricter controls on pesticides, both from a health and environmental point of view, by introducing common rules for companies on the authorisation process for sale. i believe that the final text is balanced and will improve the situation for european producers and consumers alike. finally, i would like to point out the positive turn of events in the restrictions on dangerous substances, such as carcinogens, which will only be used when their use is absolutely unavoidable, for example when a product is necessary to protect public health.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european union's action plan for the environment (2007-2013) and the european union's action plan for the environment (2008-2013). i voted in favour of mr klaß's report because it presents a balanced package which guarantees safer, better controlled and more widely distributed products, also makes the costs of marketing authorizations uniform and increases the level of protection of health and the environment. i think we are making positive progress in terms of facilitating and simplifying the rules in this area. we must maintain a high level of protection of human health, animal health and the environment and extend consumer protection through clear and specific product labelling. i also think it is good that producers outside the community will also have to comply with european standards if they want to market their products in europe.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation, adopted by the european commission on 12 june 2009, aims to revise directive 98/8/ec on biocidal products. the final compromise package, agreed as a result of the negotiations between the council and parliament, seems to me to succeed in combining the objective of a high level of protection of human health and the environment with that of a faster and more efficient authorization system for the industrial sector. among the main objectives of the proposal i would like to mention in particular that of increasing the level of protection of health and the environment, through a progressive elimination of the most dangerous substances and an extension of the scope to articles treated with biocidal products, together with procedures linked to the placing on the market of more precise and better active substances and biocidal products, updating the authorization system and introducing elements of simplification and harmonization. that is why i voted in favour of the measure.
in writing. the report contains interesting insights and shareable reflections on real problems in european agriculture. indeed, the vulnerability of the agri-food chain and the volatility of prices, especially of the factors of production, make the sector highly unequal today and do not help the efficiency and sustainability of the agricultural chain. however, i must say that the reference to the issue of climate change, which has nothing to do with the question of agricultural production factors, is too strong and too insistent. the report also calls for the establishment of a new european price monitoring agency to prevent and correct distortions in the prices of production factors. another agency involves an increase in community expenditure without any benefit being reasonably foreseeable, in this case as in many others unfortunately. i therefore abstained.
in writing. − the report is part of the debate on cap 2020 reform, seeking to inform its content, to better adapt it to the important challenges facing farmers, and to transform those challenges from potential risk factors into opportunities to advance the process of transforming agriculture towards an environmentally sustainable and energy-efficient way of life. to achieve these results, without jeopardizing the survival of a large number of small operators, especially those located in the most remote areas of the continent, it is necessary to act on those levers that make the management of agricultural activities economically sustainable. the report provides for measures to eliminate the distortions which, 'upstream', limit the profitability of agricultural activity. all eurostat surveys agree that the increase in factor costs is out of proportion to the increase in producer prices. the report for which a favourable opinion is expressed has the merit of indicating precisely the areas of intervention, both by calling for a better and more constant commitment to combating cartel formation at the level of suppliers of the main production factors (seeds and fertilisers) and by indicating a transformation of the supply systems of resources, which is environmentally sustainable and economically advantageous.
in writing. − the increasing volatility in the prices of agricultural raw materials and agricultural production factors increases the uncertainty of farmers' incomes and long-term investments. this is particularly dangerous in isolated, mountainous and island regions where the factors of remoteness and extreme peripheral location impose high additional costs, with serious repercussions on the income of farmers working there. i therefore expressed my full support for this report, as it is now necessary to improve the transparency of agricultural inputs prices and to ensure that competition rules are applied and enforced throughout the food chain. we therefore urge the ec and the member states to ensure greater monitoring and analysis at eu and world level of the economic mechanisms underlying the continuing rise in food prices, together with the interactions between fluctuations in supply and demand, and the increasing interactions between energy, factor and food price developments.
in writing. - we support this report because it has the merit of identifying the problems that are at the root of agricultural production, paying particular attention to the increase in the last decade in production factors such as energy, machinery, compound feed, fertilisers, pesticides, seeds and water. this has obvious and significant repercussions on the various sectors of production. we therefore consider it essential to support the policy options suggested here by the rapporteur, with the aim of enabling farmers to contain the costs of the factors of production, in order to increase their autonomy and income and to ensure a more efficient and sustainable use of production resources.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of mr bovè's report. it is right to ask the commission to promote more efficient agronomic practices and improved sustainable management of agricultural resources, with the aim of creating stable and productive agriculture, reducing the cost of inputs and nutrient wastage, and promoting innovation, resource efficiency and effectiveness and sustainability in agricultural systems.
in writing. - community legislation often reduces the overall competitiveness of european enterprises. i voted in favour of the report on the supply chain for agricultural products, because i believe that it is absolutely necessary to intervene at several levels in the supply chain to better understand the mechanisms of what is produced and how. the price mechanism must ensure a good and fair distribution of the proceeds. it is also essential to ensure transparency for consumers so that they can make fully informed choices. i also support the measures proposed in mr bové's report to promote farmers and ensure equal treatment for them.
in writing. the report we have just voted on is of fundamental importance, as it seeks to identify the best way to ensure that large retail companies do not abuse their dominant position and that farmers' incomes accurately reflect the prices paid for food by final consumers. currently, eu agriculture is heavily dependent on imports of production factors (mainly fossil fuels, animal feed and scarce mineral feedstocks such as phosphates) and is vulnerable to price increases. this has therefore raised serious concerns about the competitiveness of eu farmers. we want to emphasise here that the high volatility of agricultural raw material prices and production factors has increased farmers' insecurity about their income and long-term investments. the member states and the commission must therefore improve the transparency of agricultural production factor prices and ensure that competition rules are respected. greater availability of data on factor costs would help farmers.
in writing. - data and research have long shown that large imbalances in the food supply chain persist. parliament therefore called on the commission and the council to take action in this specific area to ensure fair and transparent relations between producers, suppliers and distributors and the effective application, in many cases clearly disregarded or distorted, of the regulatory measures already in force. the commission must also do everything possible to find a solution as soon as possible to the unequal distribution of profits throughout the agri-food chain, with particular attention to the incomes of agricultural producers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the commission and the council are also called upon to take action to combat unfair and abusive practices in the food sector, which are largely responsible for the imbalances in the supply chain itself. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of the joint resolution.
in writing. - i supported the resolution on imbalances in the agri-food chain because i believe that it is now necessary to start the process of creating european legislation capable of regulating relations within the distribution chain, avoiding conditions of contractual inferiority for the agricultural world. today, many farmers and farms are facing unsustainable increases in production costs. however, these additional costs are not offset by the prices paid to farmers by the purchasers of agricultural products, in particular by the goc companies. our commitment here in the european parliament is to make our european agriculture competitive and at the same time to protect farmers who risk not only losing bargaining power in the distribution chain but also seeing their margins of profitability eroded. we must counter these risks and demand a clear definition of the abusive and unfair practices often perpetrated against farmers and conduct an information campaign towards farmers on the most common illegal contractual and commercial practices together with the tools at their disposal to denounce abuses.
in writing. − the problem of imbalances in the food supply chain is clearly of european scope and therefore requires a specific solution at european level in the light of the strategic importance of the agri-food chain for the european union. i am therefore in favour of the joint resolution being adopted.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it is clear that there are huge imbalances in the food supply chain which need to be corrected. profits are left in the hands of a few, especially the large retailers, while farmers are often not paid fairly for their work and their products. the consumers themselves are the ultimate victims, as they are forced to pay a higher price because of the inefficiency of the mechanism. i therefore appreciate the efforts made to develop the short chain, which can bring immediate benefits to farmers and consumers alike. those who abuse their dominant position by applying prices which destroy competition in the market must be punished. the agricultural holdings, especially the smaller ones, are our heritage which must be defended and protected, especially in the face of the power now in the hands of the large organized distribution. i would also like to add my satisfaction at the fact that the house has rejected by an overwhelming majority an amendment aimed at reintroducing quotas for milk and sugar: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on imbalances in the food chain because i believe that parliament, as the direct representative of the people, must make its voice heard by the european commission, so that it can propose appropriate measures to manage the food market and the whole machinery that revolves around it more efficiently. i believe that the problem is strictly european. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the food chain is not affected by external factors. member states should be given the role of promoting the development of best practices for collaboration between all stakeholders, from farmers to retailers, industry, suppliers and consumer representatives.
in writing. - my colleagues and i on the committee on agriculture have repeatedly expressed the need to diversify production, reduce costs by increasing the size of small farms and invest in the food supply chain through marketing strategies. the food supply chain, agriculture, agri-food industry and the distribution sector account for over 5% of european value added and 7% of jobs. in addition, the agri-food industry generates €1.4 trillion a year, more than any other sector. in the context of the discussions on the competitiveness of the sector, any disruption in the food supply chain can have serious economic and social consequences for farmers, agricultural cooperatives and rural areas, and this is precisely what is happening. the evolution of prices in recent years, both at the level of production and consumption, has clearly demonstrated the imbalance of power within the food chain. this seriously threatens the sustainability of the sector, especially for agriculture. european consumers now spend 13% of their household budget on food, compared with 30% in the early 1980s. i hope, then, that the resolution we have adopted today will reopen the problem, but this time with a view to finding an effective solution.
in writing. the report reaffirms the importance of the space policy sector in the european strategy, both in terms of innovation and the production of highly skilled jobs. an ambitious space policy is therefore needed, one that will bring innovation, research and well-being for citizens in their daily lives. the rapporteur therefore appropriately calls on the commission to complete the legislative and financial framework with a view to defining the financial programming for the period 2014-2020. the commission should also, as the rapporteur argues, try to develop, on behalf of the european union, the broadest possible international cooperation strategy, in order to increase and deepen the dialogue and exchange of knowledge and expertise not only with traditional partners such as the united states and russia, which have their own satellite measurement and navigation systems, but also with emerging countries. i therefore vote in favour of the report.

in writing. − with the adoption of this report, we have taken an important step towards defining a future european space strategy. a common space policy can make a significant contribution to boosting the competitiveness of the european economy by promoting scientific and technological progress and stimulating innovation, as called for in the europe 2020 strategy. the economic importance of the european space industry is shown by a few facts: 31 000 highly qualified employees, €5.4 billion in annual turnover, €800 billion of european gdp coming from satellite radio navigation. in addition to being a driver of industrial development, space policy has a crucial role to play in protecting the environment, combating climate change and ensuring the safety of european citizens. this is why the main programmes it uses, gmes and galileo, should receive adequate financial support from the eu. it has been repeatedly stressed that gmes is also a key programme for crisis management operations, civil protection and humanitarian assistance. i hope therefore that a new strategy will be drawn up as soon as possible to unlock the potential for economic development and research in the space sector and its earth observation programmes.
in writing. − space policy is a key element of the europe 2020 strategy and an integral part of the industrial policy initiative. it supports the objectives of a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy capable of creating highly skilled jobs, providing business opportunities, stimulating innovation and improving the well-being and security of citizens. the proposals presented by the commission are a first step towards a comprehensive space strategy for the european union. however, in collaboration with industry, a coherent european approach must be established and financial and legislative mechanisms must be put in place in the medium and long term to stimulate european industry and to allow the continuity needed to support ambitious and competitive projects in an international context. we believe that the priority actions are still too vague. they should be specified and include an assessment of all technical options and their related costs and benefits. it is also necessary to provide for clear governance of space policy, accompanied by effective oversight and coordination mechanisms for the harmonisation of priorities and resources from national and european union funds, the european space agency (esa) and the european defence agency (eda).
in writing. − i voted in favour because strengthening europe's space policy, a key element of the europe 2020 strategy, means promoting technical and scientific progress on the one hand and stimulating innovation by improving the well-being and safety of citizens on the other. i therefore support the inclusion of the galileo and gmes projects as priorities in a european space strategy. the eu is currently dependent on the us global positioning system (gps). in order to reduce this dependence, it is clear that galileo will offer clear advantages over the american gps not only in terms of greater accuracy but also in terms of guaranteeing the service and the strategic autonomy of the european union. the importance of galileo in improving the competitiveness and quality of many services in europe is also of great importance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr patriciello's report on the european union's space strategy because it sets out noble objectives which will really serve the interests of the citizens. in addition to providing more appropriate responses to security and defence, the european space policy will promote scientific and technological progress, foster innovation and make the industrial system more competitive; i am not going to go into the details of the commission's proposals. in the future, it is hoped that europe will play a major role on the international space scene by ensuring that citizens derive maximum benefit from space research projects and investments.
in writing. - i share and strongly support the conclusions of mr aldo patriciello on the european space strategy, both for reasons of appreciation and for reasons of perplexity. there is no doubt that space policy is a great opportunity for europe. it is because it stimulates technological innovation; the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption, and the council will be consulted on it. it is therefore right that the project should play a key role in the europe 2020 strategy. in this context, it is clear that the commission could and should have drawn up a more ambitious governance plan. the commission notes that the financial corrections for the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2015 were made in accordance with the provisions of the stability and growth pact. the references to cooperation with the united states, russia and other emerging powers are too weak to fit space policy into the international context.
in writing. - i believe that the concerns of many of my colleagues about the future of the gmes earth observation programme and the galileo satellite navigation system are well founded, as they risk not being able to obtain the funding necessary for their operation. in particular, galileo, the world's first navigation satellite designed for civilian use, is the only system that could allow the eu to remain independent of the american gps, and for this reason it is necessary to ensure sufficient funds to cover its long-term development.
in writing. − through the lisbon treaty, the european union has acquired a substantial role in the formulation of a policy for the exploration and use of space, with a view to promoting scientific and technical progress. i voted in favour of mr patriciello's report because it provides for the further development and optimisation of the galileo and gmes programmes and i agree with the role envisaged for the latter to assist civil protection and maritime surveillance, thus increasing services for european security. i am convinced that the union's space policy should make it possible to provide more adequate responses to the defence and security of europe's space infrastructures. i believe that the measures in this report bring together physical resources and know-how for the benefit of the whole of the eu and that it is also necessary to coordinate adequately the capabilities of the different member states in the use of space technologies for security.
in writing. the union's space policy, which we are adopting this morning with our positive vote, will make it possible to provide more appropriate responses to the security and defence of europe's space infrastructure. the priority actions for an eu space policy are primarily the galileo and gmes lighthouse projects. as regards the use of space technologies for security (border surveillance, maritime surveillance, emergency management, humanitarian aid, support for eu external action), the union will have to coordinate member states' capabilities appropriately, under conditions to be agreed with infrastructure-owning states, in order to best meet operational needs, including, where appropriate, the development of new infrastructure. space technologies will also need to be protected as infrastructures against the risks of damage and destruction, through the progressive sharing of existing capabilities among member states, the acquisition of missing capabilities and their proper maintenance and management. the union will then be able to play an important role in the field of space exploration, overcoming the current dispersion of interventions, identifying and supporting the development of technologies for exploration in the fields of energy, health and support for isolated environments.
in writing. − i fully support this document because we cannot ignore the fact that every year in europe a growing amount of food, up to 50 %, becomes waste. a study published by the commission estimates annual food-waste generation in the 27 member states at approximately 89 million tonnes. this evidence is unacceptable if we think that in europe 79 million people are still living below the poverty line. food security is a basic human right and for this reason the european institutions and the member states must address, as a matter of urgency, the problem of food waste along the entire supply and consumption chain. reducing food waste is a vital preliminary step in combating hunger in the world, responding to the increased demand predicted by the fao and improving people’s nutritional levels. i believe that a good way to start to reduce this enormous problem is to inform people not only about the causes and effects of waste but also about ways of reducing it. a civic culture guided by the principles of sustainability and solidarity could be the first step in the right direction.
in writing. - mr caronna's report deals with an important issue such as the efficiency of the food chain in the eu member states. food waste statistics tell us that in some cases, almost 50 percent of healthy, edible food is wasted in the food chain. this has implications not only for the sustainability of the food chain and food production itself, but also for product prices and the eco-sustainability of food waste. the report therefore calls on the commission, the council and the governments of the member states to promote measures and policies which will first of all promote greater awareness of the problem among the public. the commission and the council are also invited to declare 2012 the 'european year against food waste' in order to raise awareness among institutions and consumers of the many harms caused by the dispersion of huge quantities of food throughout the food chain and of the need for a change of course in this area. it is also desirable, as the report says, that the commission should encourage the exchange of good practice between the member states in this respect. my vote is in favour of the report.
in writing. − it is no longer surprising that the level of food waste data has ethical as well as social, economic and environmental significance. yet, despite the ever-increasing amount - estimated by the fao to be as much as 50% of total output - of lost goods along all links in the agri-food chain, there is still no clear, univocal and uniform definition of the concept of 'food waste' in europe. as if that were not enough, just a few months ago, we had to fight a bitter battle to allow the refinancing of the fund for the distribution of food to the indigent. in contrast, the deplorable statistic that europeans and north americans waste up to 115 kg of food per capita. this is a situation which is no longer tolerable but at the same time difficult to resolve. one of the main merits of the report is that it does not limit the problem to its most obvious aspect - waste generated by the final consumer - which, however deplorable, is only one part of a wider and more complex problem. on the other hand, intervention strategies must be identified to address the specific causes of waste in each of the five sectors (production, storage, processing, distribution, consumption) that make up the agri-food chain.
in writing. - each year, some 1.3 billion tonnes of food is wasted worldwide, about a third of the food produced for human consumption. it is estimated that each european citizen throws away an average of 179 kg of food per year, much of which is still edible. we must use this data as a starting point for a coordinated european strategy and effective measures that can drastically reduce food waste. until now, the european union has underestimated this problem, which has not only social, but also economic and environmental consequences. recent studies show that as much as 10 percent of greenhouse gas emissions in developed countries come from the production of the same food that is thrown away every day. the resolution adopted today calls for an integrated and shared approach - from producer to consumer - to reduce food waste substantially. consumer awareness and education will play a key role in promoting the idea that what is wasted can instead become a resource. this is what the last minute market, a reality created by the university of bologna, has successfully demonstrated, promoting the 'reuse' of food within solidarity networks.
in writing. - i strongly supported this report because the level of food waste must not increase any further and we must combat it with tools but also a culture aimed at explaining its causes and economic, environmental and social effects. in the face of a phenomenon which has increased by 50% in the last thirty years, with repercussions not only ethical but also economic, environmental, social, nutritional and health-related, it does not seem ethically sustainable that some 80 million people in europe live below the poverty line. the tons of food that can still be eaten and thrown away are often eliminated through high economic and environmental costs that society itself pays for when it could do much, often unconsciously, to limit the amount. i therefore believe that today's vote represents the beginning of a regulatory process which will in future enable us to reconcile consumer needs in terms of hygiene and information, through differentiated and simplified packaging methods at lower cost to businesses and, therefore, at lower final prices.
in writing. - food waste has become a global problem. this question is then contrasted with the fundamental problem of food supply, which is seriously compromised by the limited natural resources in relation to the growing number of the world's population and by the poor access to food by the poorest sections of the population. the amount of food produced today can actually still be reused for food purposes instead of being disposed of like any other waste, with significant environmental and economic impacts and ethical implications. the fight against food waste must therefore become a priority on the european political agenda; the commission, the council and the member states are called upon to adopt concrete strategies and measures to halve the use of lead in the supply chain by 2025, to improve the efficiency of the supply chain and to raise public awareness of a subject that is still largely ignored. citizens need to be informed not only about the causes and consequences of waste but also about how to reduce it; promote a scientific and civic culture oriented towards the principles of sustainability and solidarity in order to encourage the most virtuous behaviour.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of mr caronna's report because i think it is entirely acceptable that the european union should send a strong signal against food waste. food waste is not only a huge problem with the hunger suffered by many of the world's people, but also with the limited natural resources. i think that the european institutions have taken a commendable initiative in declaring 2013 the european year against food waste. given that most waste occurs in the distribution and consumption phases, such a declaration would play a fundamental role in raising the interest of the european peoples in this problem.
