madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the report by mr schwab shows that competition policy within the european union has brought many benefits to consumers. the use of flexible and dynamic procedures has enabled competition policies to be a driver rather than a hindrance to the european financial and economic system. i voted in favour, as i fully agree with the objectives of the report. in particular, i share the intention to make prices more transparent in order to stimulate competition on the market and protect consumer rights. in a recession, we must try to encourage consumers. finally, i would add that the exchange of information between the commission and consumer associations should continue, be intensified and extended to all interested parties.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because i believe it is of fundamental importance for the eu to consider, in foreign policy terms, the growing political and economic relevance of brazil, russia, india, china and south africa. in this renewed world asset, the eu must be at the forefront of the reform of the international system and must use its political leverage to continue to promote universal values. to lead this process the eu needs to act as a single and robust political and economic entity. without an inclusive new global governance system, based on full participation by the brics and other emerging economies, there will be limited international cooperation on major global issues. in addition to that there will be also the potential risk of political and economic fragmentation, and of competing world agendas. with this report indeed, we ask for a strategic partnership with each brics country as a means of advancing peace and global security, the promotion of human rights, democracy, sustainable development and global financial regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr saryusz-wolski. in the perspective of a global economy, in terms of gross domestic product, china is expected to become the world's largest economy by 2020 and india could be the country with the highest economic growth by 2050, while the so-called bric countries (brazil, russia, india and china) together with indonesia, mexico and turkey will have an economic weight greater than that of the g7 countries as a whole. if the economic growth of the brics and emerging economies is further consolidated, these countries will acquire a strong foreign policy relevance on the world stage, but given the interdependence of the world economies, the consolidation of the economic leadership of the emerging economies will depend on the well-being of the emerging economies. this presents a major opportunity for the eu: taking into account the new political weight of brics, it will be able to exert its political influence to promote universal values of the future multipolar system of global governance and to be at the forefront of the process of reforming the international governance system. the eu will therefore have to act as a single, strong political and economic entity, considering emerging countries as valuable partners of the west.
in writing. - as the current economic crisis shows, there is a high degree of interdependence between the emerging and the emerging powers. we support this report because it aims to discuss the foundations of a new inclusive system of global governance and to make recommendations, while identifying key areas of reform where the eu could seek to streamline its action and institutional architecture, thereby increasing its potential and effectiveness as a global actor. the european union has a long-standing commitment to the principle of subsidiarity, and its commitment to the principle of subsidiarity is reflected in the european council's conclusions of 15 and 16 december. the european union will have to take due account of the new political and economic weight of these countries and other emerging powers, use its political influence to promote universal values in the new multipolar system of global governance that is emerging, and be at the forefront of the process of reforming the system of international governance.
in writing. − i agree with the rapporteur that we need to lay the foundations for a new inclusive system of global governance. the european union cannot ignore the growing political and economic weight of the brics countries and other emerging powers. we must use our political influence to promote those universal values that have allowed us to grow in peace for 60 years. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − i am in favour of an eu comprehensive approach to the brics countries, but it must be stressed that these countries are emerging rather than emerging and that europe must increasingly look at them as competitive partners in both its trade, strategic and political relations. today, international trade has become a foreign policy instrument and if we want to create a new system of global governance, we must keep in mind the economic issues and the current position of these countries, which, like china, are pursuing an expansionist policy, not always transparent, in terms of finance, trade and economy towards industrialized and developing countries. europe cannot afford to lose the opportunity to tackle the great cross-border challenges, from climate change to food security, by joining forces with powers destined to have an economic weight greater than the g7 countries as a whole, but at the same time it must be vigilant to ensure that market rules, free competition and mutual political recognition do not just remain on the cards of international agreements but are also respected in those countries, such as the brics, where sometimes the system of values and freedoms takes on forms different from ours. the market cannot ignore the respect for the most basic human rights.
in writing. the brics countries (brazil, russia, india, china and south africa) are emerging as a growing force on the international political scene. in terms of their potential for economic development, these countries will be the main competitors and/or partners of the west both in terms of foreign policies and trade agreements. the report under discussion raises the possibility of the eu opening up its foreign policy to the views of the brics countries, which, aware of the growing weight of their gdp and economies, are creating a common platform in terms of foreign policy. the aim is to seek a new system of global governance that is sufficiently inclusive of the brics countries.
in writing. - i agree with many of the points made by my colleague jacek saryusz-wolski on the subject of relations with the brics: the idea that the union should have its own comprehensive and comprehensive approach to the issue; the idea that the growing role of emerging countries, in particular the brics, should be fully recognised within the framework of rules and values, in particular those enshrined in the un charter; the idea that parliamentary diplomacy can make a decisive contribution to the development of friendly relations, especially in those countries where parliamentarism is becoming more established; the idea that the establishment of a full political relationship with emerging realities cannot be done without considering crucial issues such as the environment, rights and working conditions. on the contrary, i am very puzzled by the request for visa liberalization with brazil. the migration dynamics are too complex to be dealt with by an immediate opening of borders, especially in a time of economic crisis such as the one we are experiencing. that is why i have decided to abstain from voting on this report.
in writing. - to overcome the crisis in the domestic market, european companies are looking for new outlets in the brics countries (brazil, russia, india, china, south africa). this is shown, among other things, by business trips to brazil, which increased by 30% compared with last year. similar speech for the east: the growth in china (+27%) was considerable, with beijing, hong kong and shanghai being the traditional destinations, and other smaller destinations added, reflecting the fact that european companies are increasingly investing in the new emerging economies. the high degree of interdependence between the emerging and the emerging powers also requires a review of the eu's respective bilateral policies towards the bric countries. a final figure for movements to india and south africa, which have also increased by 19 and 18 per cent respectively.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because the european parliament must reiterate once again that sanctions are not an end in themselves and that decisions on sanctions by the eu should be taken only after thorough evaluation of the most efficient way to support democratic change. the eu has often applied its sanctions policy inconsistently by treating third countries with similar human rights and democratic records differently. such behaviour has often encouraged criticism for applying double standards. with this resolution we want to stress that sanctions should be applied regardless of political, economic and security interests. all restrictive measures must comply with international humanitarian law and with the principle of proportionality and must not penalise the most vulnerable population groups in countries affected by these measures. for these reasons i consider the ‘targeted sanctions’ overall a better instrument. sanctioned leaders will be affected only if they are personally subject to pressure in the form of restrictions on their ability to move money, invest and access their financial assets, restrictions for travel or for diplomatic representation.
in writing. - european policy towards regimes that violate the principles of democracy and freedom and the human rights of their peoples has often been the subject of strong criticism. there has often been, and culpably still is, a fundamental ambiguity, which has led the eu, while acknowledging the undemocratic character of many governments, to remain silent on the subject and to continue to forge political and economic links with these countries, limiting itself to inserting clauses on respect for human rights in the various cooperation agreements, which many regimes obviously do not respect. in this own-initiative report, parliament calls on the eu to adopt stricter measures and policies against political actors and prominent figures belonging to non-democratic regimes in third countries when they exercise personal or commercial interests in the territory of the 27 member states. attention is also drawn to the need to make violations of freedom of religion and expression in third countries sufficient grounds for sanctions and non-political responses by the member states and the eu as a whole. the committee also calls for more precise codification of the forms, methods and procedures for applying sanctions. my vote is in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i share the need, expressed in it, to make the european directives which provide for restrictive measures against authoritarian leaders more binding and applicable. the european parliament has been a very active participant in the process of european integration, and it has been a very active participant in the process of european integration. whereas it is therefore desirable to improve coordination between the member states in the application of such measures imposed at community level; in addition, eu member states must actively investigate and prosecute natural and legal persons who have assisted sanctioned leaders and persons connected to them in the european territory to evade or avoid sanctions imposed against them. finally, clear criteria must be established for the application of restrictive measures and the objectives pursued by them must be identified: the european union has also been active in the fight against terrorism, and has been active in the fight against organised crime.
in writing. as the report rightly points out, 'the union's action is based on 'democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity and respect for the principles of the united nations charter and international law'. the european institutions must be consistent with our treaty, we can no longer turn a blind eye to the violations perpetrated by authoritarian regimes around the world, and that is why sanctions policy must be an instrument capable of exerting a real influence on the governments of these countries. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − having a coherent european policy towards representatives of non-european totalitarian regimes is fundamental to the protection of the human rights for which we speak. it must also be in relation to the assets and interests held by these political leaders within the eu territories. from the freezing of assets of former libyan leader gaddafi to those of former presidents of tunisia and egypt, the eu needs to take proportionate and equivalent restrictive measures against every dictatorial regime. i therefore think it is important to urge the council to apply these restrictive measures whenever necessary.
in writing. - i share and support the conclusions of mr watson's report. the union is now the world's largest market and the largest donor of development aid. it is a unique opportunity to promote the rights and respect for the rules of peaceful coexistence of the community of states. unfortunately, bureaucratic red tape and lack of synergy have so far meant that eu restrictive measures against regimes that do not respect international law have not always had the deterrent and sanctioning effect that they should have. it is unfair that sometimes already oppressed populations or european businesses and citizens have suffered the consequences of sanctions while corrupt and violent local elites have been able to evade them. it is also unfair that third countries should benefit from, and have benefited from, european respect for the rule of law and human rights. i therefore join the rapporteur, mr watson, in calling on the council to adopt as soon as possible clear rules, which are uniformly applied and subject to periodic review, so that restrictive measures can be more effective.
in writing. - i congratulate mr watson on his work. the text adopted, in the light of the un conventions on human rights and article 21 of the teu, is intended to be an explicit request by parliament to the council to maintain a consistent approach towards all regimes to which the european union applies restrictive measures. the call for clearer criteria for the cases in which restrictive measures should be applied and for a common and coherent policy on sanctions are top priorities, especially in this delicate international period. it will also be essential to strengthen restrictive measures against recognised authoritarian regimes, seeking to minimise their relations with the european union.
in writing. − this vote will help to develop clearer policy definitions for regimes against which the european union has applied restrictive measures. first of all, it must be recognised that sanctions are not an end in themselves, but must be accompanied by clear and feasible benchmarks for their removal. then there is unity in decision-making: the european union should commit itself to maximising collaboration and synergies between the 27 member states of the european union, urging them to speak with a single and coherent voice against authoritarian regimes through a single integrated approach. in fact, if not coordinated at international level, sanctions may prove ineffective and counterproductive in achieving their stated objectives, undermine the transparency, credibility and coherence of european sanctions policy, strengthen the regime for which they are intended or reduce the credibility and the relative negotiating margin of the european union and the member states with the country concerned.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of mrs regner's report. i find it appropriate to request, on the basis of article 50 (1) and (2) (g) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, a proposal for a directive on the crossborder transfer of company headquarters. the directive must first clarify the question of the separation between the registered office and the administrative office of a company.
in writing. - the transfer of the head office abroad, from the point of view of professional practice, is an operation which, in recent times, is receiving increasing interest, also, but not only, in connection with the growing phenomenon of the relocation of companies, as a strategic lever to manage the current crisis of the economic system. the location of production activities in markets offering highly competitive supplies, both in terms of raw materials and especially labour, or in systems with less onerous tax systems, is in fact one of the main responses that companies are preparing to face globalised markets, where competition with the economies of emerging countries is increasingly strong. the legal continuity of the transferred company, its recognition in the state of destination and in the state of origin, and the legislation applicable to the company being transferred, are all matters which depend on the legal systems in force in the countries involved in the transfer, and in particular on the type of company incorporation and recognition adopted by the states. my vote in favour of this morning's text is therefore aimed at seeking a measure which can bring the different laws of the member states closer together.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr ehrenhauser's report. the report stresses the need to ensure a high level of transparency and reliability within the framework partnership agreement with ngos, for which i believe that the administrative costs for the partners must be drastically reduced. i also welcome and support the decision to increase the budget for humanitarian aid for the period 2014-2020, provided that, in view of the crisis, it is allocated efficiently and managed in a responsible manner. finally, i regret and ask for an explanation as to why the commission did not allow dg echo access to the final reports of the partners on the implementation of humanitarian actions in haiti and pakistan in 2010.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because it points out the need for strengthening the efficiency and effectiveness of budgetary control over the eu humanitarian aid managed by dg echo. the text underlines the areas of weakness in control over the funds and proposes improvements to be made. we stress the importance of establishing a clear regulation with the scope to have a single integrated reporting model, which would simplify the complexity of the administrative procedures. in this regard i also support the fact that echo is currently working on the development of a comparative cost information system in order to analyse the cost-effectiveness of project proposals. the awareness of project efficiency would finally allow echo to avoid investing in unfruitful projects.
in writing. − this report has the merit of focusing the european parliament's attention on the management of the commission's humanitarian policy, which, through the directorate-general for humanitarian aid, delivers humanitarian aid to such an extent that the eu is the world's largest donor. the management of humanitarian funds has long been a matter of concern, which the european parliament and the court of auditors have recognised and often brought to light. our assembly is therefore calling on the commission in this report to take some important steps to improve the management of humanitarian aid. as the rapporteur has pointed out, it is necessary to ensure that the partners actually follow up on the findings made during the audit procedures, and to ensure that case-by-case reports drawn up by the un clearly indicate the results produced by individual projects in the area concerned by the financial assistance. it is also necessary to improve practices and methods of evaluating potential partners in the framework of the partnership agreements, and finally to pay due attention, from a strategic perspective, to the possibility that humanitarian aid policy towards certain actors may generate negative effects, such as the possibility that food aid will depress local productive capacities. my vote is therefore in favour.
in writing. the directive is certainly moving in the direction of better management of humanitarian funds, starting with greater transparency and more effective controls to prevent fraud and corruption. it is essential, first of all, to work to remedy the genericity of the reports submitted, from which it is particularly difficult to obtain sufficient information on the results, the product and the effect of the interventions. the report also lays great stress on the need to create continuity between emergency interventions and development programmes. in particular, it might be useful to think of a period of coexistence between emergency and development agencies, by implementing some form of passing of deliveries. it is hardly likely that those who manage the emergency well will also be prepared to deal with the problems associated with development projects. the current system is likely to create discontinuities, negating or undermining the effectiveness of possible long-term results. finally, the call for greater visibility of the interventions, not for 'advertising' purposes, but to allow greater rationalization of the interventions, is welcome and should be supported. the committee therefore voted in favour of the report and hoped that the recommendations contained in the report would be taken into account in the process of reforming the cqf framework.
in writing. − the european union must strengthen its capacity to respond to the increase in major natural disasters. for years we have been calling for a more realistic humanitarian budget in order to avoid chronic under-financing of the budget lines concerned and to ensure a consistent balance between the financing of actions aimed at preventing humanitarian disasters and those aimed at responding rapidly to emergencies, whether natural or man-made. we therefore recognise the benefit of seeking new funding through dg echo and its partners, but we also stress that effective control of the use of funds in the context of audits of partners by private firms is essential and contributes to legitimising the humanitarian sector. we therefore welcome the efforts made by dg echo to promote the use of innovative approaches such as the cash-based approach, in particular unconditional transfers for the most vulnerable groups. these approaches may be more effective without necessarily entailing a higher fiduciary risk than in-kind assistance.
in writing. - as the rapporteur rightly points out, i find it unacceptable that the commission has not provided parliament with the financial statements and final reports of echo's partners on the implementation of humanitarian actions in the days following the disasters in haiti and pakistan in 2010. parliament must have access to these reports in order to be able to assess the financial management. this practice must also be changed to encourage better interaction between european institutions and with international humanitarian organisations.
in writing. − the european union is one of the world's leading humanitarian donors. in order to organise the work on humanitarian aid, a dg (directorate-general) of the commission, echo, was set up to manage the complex system of managing the budget and the destination and request for aid. the great importance of this directorate-general often creates areas of conflict with regard to competence in the control of financial resources, which is why it was felt necessary to take action for a review of the financial regulation in order to increase the responsibility and competence of those who manage the humanitarian aid budget. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − this vote will ensure more efficiency and effectiveness in the control, monitoring and oversight system of the european commission's directorate-general responsible for the implementation of eu humanitarian aid. the european union is the world's largest donor of humanitarian aid. in 2010, the total contribution in terms of humanitarian aid, including that from the member states, was eur 2 957 million in total. echo also carries out its mandate by funding some 200 partners: non-governmental organisations, un agencies, international organisations and specialised agencies of the member states. the enormous disasters in haiti and pakistan have once again demonstrated that the european union's disaster response instruments need to be improved in terms of efficiency, speed and coordination. these events, however tragic, have highlighted how much more needs to be done to improve and strengthen management and accountability.
in writing. - regulations defining the subject matter of collective actions are not only desirable but urgent and indispensable. this is all the more so when we consider that in most cases the 'collective' victims are those who belong to the weaker sections of the population, both in terms of education and economically. this implies that, in most cases, infringements against these groups go unpunished because of economic obstacles (disproportion between the costs of an individual case and any compensation) and psychological obstacles (fears about the length of proceedings) and the difficulties in accessing the necessary information. on the other hand, the merging of claims would not only strengthen the procedural position of the applicant but also simplify the procedures and reduce costs. on the other hand, there are many difficulties, both in relation to the different jurisdictions in the individual states and in relation to the desirability of containing the abuse of the instrument. in any case, the eu should adopt a common horizontal approach to the issue, without following the us class action model and without changing national legislation, and establish a horizontal reference framework instrument enabling citizens and businesses to assert their eu-enforced rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on collective redress because i believe that the completion of the european single market also and above all requires the harmonization of consumer protection. it is essential, however, that the mistakes made in the united states are not repeated here in europe, where class action lawsuits have become the primary source of income for a handful of powerful law firms, and have only rarely proved to be an effective consumer protection tool. the european union can do better than the united states in this area: firstly, by encouraging the parties to reach alternative agreements, which do not require the formal use of the legal instrument, and thus by simplifying and speeding up the time; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of consumers' interests. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. only in this way can we prevent a useful instrument for protecting citizens from becoming a means of unfair competition between private parties. the report voted on today goes in that direction and is therefore a good starting point for future work.
in writing. − when a group of citizens is suffering the same wrong, individual remedies may not be an effective means of stopping illegal practices or obtaining compensation. i agree with the need for a european collective approach and i also agree that collective actions, by avoiding parallel litigation on issues of the same nature, can bring benefits in terms of reduced costs and increased legal certainty for claimants, defendants and the judicial system. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − i have always maintained that alternative dispute resolution is the most effective measure of mediation in the field of consumer disputes. the single market and the internet create a virtual trading space in which citizens want to place their trust. nevertheless, consumers are often left alone in the face of producers. it is a david-goliath struggle, which leaves no room for recognition of the rights enshrined in the directives on which we are daily engaged. class actions are an experience that consumers have undertaken to make their otherwise thin, isolated voice count. i personally believe that alternative dispute resolution mechanisms should be encouraged, even though they often depend on the willingness of the commercial operator to cooperate. the availability of an effective judicial redress system would strongly encourage the parties to seek an out-of-court settlement and would therefore be likely to avoid a high number of disputes; the establishment of alternative dispute resolution (adr) schemes at european level should be encouraged in order to allow for an effective settlement of disputes which is a more attractive option than judicial proceedings and also proposes the prerogative to order the parties involved to seek first a collective settlement before bringing a collective action.
in writing. the report by mr lehne, for which i voted in favour, aims to improve european regulation on collective redress. the eu needs to protect citizens and businesses who must be able to enforce their rights under existing legislation effectively and efficiently. improvements in legislation on consumer protection cooperation, consumer protection injunctions and injunctions are intended to protect victims of unlawful conduct. it is often the case that citizens give up seeking compensation because the costs of an individual action for compensation are too high and the effective application of the laws in force is thus indirectly undermined.
in writing. - i would like to congratulate mr lehne. the text adopted, in the light of the commission's green paper on collective redress for consumers, is a clear call by parliament for further improvement of access to justice. the collective action should not be seen as a special category compared to the individual action, but simply as the concrete way to achieve the same result for all, through a single legal action. clear and precise rules on collective redress are needed to reduce the burden of litigation and to allow the matter to be dealt with in a horizontal manner.
in writing. - with this vote we have certainly missed an important opportunity to enable our smes to communicate the improvements made to products in terms of reducing salt, sugar and fat. i would remind you that under current legislation, a company wishing to improve its nutritional characteristics must make a drastic change to its recipe, which is a rather problematic operation, particularly for smes, both from a technological and economic point of view. the use of comparative nutrition claims is now allowed only if the product contains at least 30% less of the indicated substance than the average of the product category. the proposed claim would be granted for one year only, thus encouraging a gradual reformulation of the products. this would allow consumers to adapt to the gradual reduction in fat, sugar and salt content with the resulting health benefits. there are already positive experiences in this respect, such as in england, where the population is getting used to a less salty taste through a very gradual reduction in the salt content. i therefore hope that the commission will come forward with a new proposal as soon as possible, which can be accepted by the european parliament.
in writing. - parliament does not doubt the good faith of the european commission, but it cannot refrain from expressing its perplexity in the face of a proposal such as the one under discussion today in plenary. consumers want clear labels and simple nutritional information, not marketing operations disguised as protection of the right to information. claiming that a food now contains x% less of [name of nutrient] could lead to unfair competition with existing claims such as reduced rate of [name of nutrient] and light/light; the latter is also required to be reduced by at least 10% (for micronutrients), 25% (for sodium) or 30% (for sugars/fat) compared to other similar products; in practice, a consumer might think that the quantity specified in the indication 'now contains x% less [name of nutrient]' would result in a greater reduction than that corresponding to the indication 'reduced rate of' or 'light' despite the fact that the requirements for these indications are much more stringent than those applying to the indication 'now contains x% less [name of nutrient]' which requires a minimum reduction of only 15%. i am therefore glad that this parliament has decided to refer the proposal back to the commission for amendments which will balance its main purpose.
in writing. - the resolution, like the one adopted at the january plenary session, proposes the extension of the community method, with the consequent further deprivation of sovereignty of the member states. the position of the united kingdom is deplored for having opposed the latest development towards further centralisation of the european legislative and institutional architecture. instead, i think it's right to look for an alternative to what we've done so far: the crisis also stems from the centralization of the community, the weight of the european bureaucracy and apparatus, and the centralized management that reigns supreme in brussels. the way out of the crisis is for europe to take a path of freedom, not centralism. my vote is against the resolution.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to make it clear that i intend to vote in favour of the resolution, if only in order to preserve the unity of parliament and to strengthen the position of its president within the european institutions. in this connection, the reference to the lack of involvement of the president of parliament in informal meetings within the framework of european summits is welcome, a vulnus which should be rightly stigmatised and deplored. the problem is also to defend and strengthen the positions of those political groups which are fighting for a united europe, confident that the crisis can find a proper solution only if it is tackled in a united manner, avoiding the risks of nationalistic and selfish drift. every day, these groups, especially in some parts of the continent, have to deal with demagogic and populist propaganda which denigrates the union and its institutions. we are also voting in support of these forces. it is important to stress, however, that europe cannot be represented and contained only in the austerity measures of the six pack, a measure which we opposed because we thought it was wrong and which we still consider to be partial and inadequate. we are voting for a united and strong europe which reconciles growth and social equity.
in writing. - the epp resolution on the conclusions of the european council of 30 january, which i voted in favour of, seeks to highlight parliament's position vis-à-vis the council. the agreement reached can and must certainly be improved, but in the meantime progress must be made. the agreement reached by 25 of the 27 member states on the fiscal compact aims to bring public debt to a sustainable level and ensure budgetary parity among the member states. we should probably make sure that we have an internal eu budget that is geared towards a union of european states that is really able to cope with crises, but small steps in the right direction seem to be taking place.
in writing. - the last council summit discussed many measures of paramount importance. but the most awaited of all is surely the international agreement on the fiscal compact. as an italian citizen, i am very pleased with this agreement on confidence in the euro area: the 17 euro countries will now be able to meet on their own at least twice a year, but at least once a year (and whenever topics related to the institutional architecture are discussed) they will have to open up to the other member states. the summit also had the merit of turning an equally important page on growth and employment, two key issues for boosting the economies of all the member states.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because, thanks to the adoption of the amendment tabled jointly by the s&d and the greens, it clearly states that the outstanding issues with iran over its nuclear programme must be solved peacefully and that a military solution to the conflict is not even conceivable. it is also of fundamental importance to reiterate that, contrary to some states already in possession of nuclear weapons, iran is a member of the non-proliferation treaty, and as such allows for inspections of its nuclear installations by the international atomic energy agency. i support the council double-track approach, but i believe that the sanctions must be carefully targeted at and proportionate to the objective pursued. the restrictive measures should be aimed at striking the power elites of a repressive regime, minimising as far as possible the adverse impact on the civilian population, especially the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint resolution on the iranian nuclear programme; parliament's position is to be welcomed in that it reminds iran of its obligations under international law by acceding to the nuclear non-proliferation treaty and expresses concern at further developments in the matter which do not seem to lead to a positive solution. the process of uranium enrichment in iran is continuing uninterruptedly, and well beyond what, according to the international atomic energy agency's technicians, is required to ensure the internal energy supply. iran must comply as soon as possible with the many resolutions of the un and the iaea, without which there is a risk of a dangerous and anything but diplomatic escalation which the whole world, especially in this period of severe crisis and economic and financial instability, would gladly do without.
in writing. - it is very serious that iran has not yet complied with all the obligations arising from the un security council resolutions. the uranium enrichment programme in tehran is also a matter of great concern. i agree with the idea in the resolution for a gradual embargo against the iranian regime. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this joint resolution because it strongly condemns iran for its nuclear programme and for the whole dangerous and destabilising strategy being pursued by its regime. iran has never shown any willingness to actively cooperate with the iaea, the international atomic energy agency: this is all the more serious when one considers that the asian country is one of the signatories of the nuclear non-proliferation treaty, which includes several clauses that are regularly violated. the european union has done well in reacting strongly to the numerous provocations, and the embargo seems to me to be a shared choice: the continuing threats to other countries, israel in particular, which risk precipitating the ever more difficult situation in the middle east, cannot be tolerated. europe must be strong and united in opposing any possible proliferation of nuclear weapons in iran, which could pose a danger to the whole surrounding area and to the whole of the west in general.
in writing. the resolution on iran's nuclear programme adopted by this parliament is an expression of the union's concern about the possible military dimension of the iranian programme. for years now, the un, the eu and the international atomic energy agency have been imposing sanctions and embargoes on iran. unfortunately, by not allowing the iranian authorities to carry out thorough checks and by only reporting part of their work, they are putting the international community in a position to fear that the nuclear programme is being used for war, which is why the sanctions are affecting the oil, gold, diamond and currency markets. these sanctions are intended to be an attempt by the international community to put pressure on the iranian authorities to comply with un resolutions and to restart credible negotiations to restore confidence in the civilian purpose of iran's nuclear programme.
in writing. − in the context of the dual-track strategy towards iran, the sanctions established at community level are intended to put sufficient pressure on the iranian authorities to secure compliance with un and iaea resolutions and the launch of credible negotiations, which will restore full confidence in the international community about the exclusively peaceful nature of iran's nuclear programme. i support an embargo decision in view of the concerns that the iranian nuclear programme is raising in the international community due to suspicions of a military dimension, which have been heightened since the publication on 18 november 2011 of the latest report of the international atomic energy agency (iaea). the foreign affairs council conclusions also express concern about iran's nuclear programme, setting out the restrictive measures adopted and reiterating the objective of a diplomatic solution to the issue and the call on iran to respond positively to the latest offer of dialogue contained in the letter sent to the iranian authorities by mrs ashton on 21 october. i hope that the situation can return to normal as soon as possible, also in view of the possible negative repercussions that the embargo would have on the eu's energy supply.
in writing. − sport plays an important role in the lives of european citizens, considering that mass sporting events involve some 35 million amateurs, but it also plays an important role for the european economy: this is a sector that employs some 15 million people and has an annual value added of 3.65% of the union's gdp. i therefore believe that it is necessary to promote a european dimension for sport which takes account of the benefits that sport brings to citizens, both in terms of health and in terms of social, cultural and economic aspects. sport must be promoted by making it an activity accessible to all citizens, developing its role as a promoter of peace, economic growth, intercultural dialogue, integration and the emancipation of women. sport is also an effective means of affirming european identity, and it would be appropriate to devote a specific funding programme to it at this time.
in writing. − sport is an essential element for health and quality of life in our societies. the report emphasizes the positive aspects of promoting sporting culture, which is inextricably linked to the social dimension. as the rapporteur has pointed out, sport should be promoted and the creation of intra-community networks and the exchange of good practice in the field of sport should be supported. sport can also promote the social inclusion of vulnerable groups such as the disabled and foster the human and social growth of young people, who are increasingly disoriented in the contemporary world, which lacks any reference in terms of values and humanity. finally, i think it is particularly positive to refer to the need to protect traditional and local sports, which are now in danger of disappearing in large numbers, when they represent an invaluable treasure without which it will be difficult in the future to preserve our cultural traditions and our local specificities and peculiarities, a real added value of our continental history. my vote is in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. article 165 tfeu confers on the european union the task of promoting and developing the european dimension in sport. it actively contributes to the eu's strategic objectives because of its cultural, educational and, above all, integration value. although many issues are of close concern to individual member states, the eu needs to focus on major issues such as doping, athlete mobility, racism and violence in sport. in addition, all efforts must be made to combat all types of illegal activity: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the illegal use of drugs, money laundering, match-fixing and the exploitation of children, which are a real threat to sport and the values it represents. i agree with the rapporteur that the commission should be asked to establish a 'european day of sport' every year to raise public awareness of the benefits of sport. sport is a collective good that must be preserved and cultivated.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the fisas ayxela report because i believe it represents an important exercise in defining priorities for european action in the field of sport. i welcome the mention of the respect for the fundamental rights of athletes during the controls provided for by the anti-doping procedures. it is essential to ensure that these rights are respected, in particular by establishing a procedure at european level which guarantees the athlete and does not leave room for arbitrariness, which can have a very damaging effect on the career of athletes. the use of the biological passport as a tool for investigation rather than prevention has led to highly discriminatory incidents, which have led to the termination of the careers of athletes who have been burdened with the burden of proof even without clear evidence of doping. in this situation, the burden of proof is on the defendant, which is contrary to the fundamental principles of the person, in particular article 6 of the echr. i therefore thank my colleague mr fisas for his commitment to guaranteeing and protecting not only the interests of sports federations and clubs but also the freedoms and fundamental rights of athletes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important report on sport which is a response to the commission's communication on sport and anticipates the proposal to create a sub-programme for sport in the multiannual programming 2014-2020. we have been pushing for the following points with the s&d group: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the following issues: the introduction of sport as a compulsory subject in school curricula, the need to encourage the practice of sport by women and girls from disadvantaged backgrounds, the emphasis on sport as a motor of social integration and as a tool to combat intolerance, racism and violence, the increase in the protection of minors in sports competitions, the fight against doping, the use of the european flag at all official sports events, the establishment of a european day of sport and the extension of the erasmus programme to sports.
in writing. - too often, the news still reports incidents of violence linked to sports matches. fan riots are a common phenomenon throughout the eu and require action by all member states. in the text adopted today we are calling for the banning of fans who are responsible for violent and discriminatory behaviour from entering stadiums. more coordinated and effective action will prevent tragic incidents of violence, such as the one that occurred yesterday in egypt, where some 74 people died in the riots that followed a football match, from happening in europe. i agree that it is also essential to adopt a more effective integrated approach in the fight against doping, which, in addition to being contrary to the principles of fairness and justice in sports competitions, is a serious threat to the health of both professional and amateur athletes. i therefore hope that the european union will be able to play a more active role in defending the integrity of sport, by addressing those challenges which undermine its important social and educational function.
in writing. - i supported the fisas ayxela report because i think it has highlighted the main issues that need action by the union. the lisbon treaty gives the union the task of developing the european dimension in sport by promoting cooperation between bodies responsible for sport and protecting the physical and moral integrity of sportsmen and sportswomen. sport contributes to the achievement of the union's strategic objectives by playing an important role in various areas such as social inclusion, education, training and public health. however, corruption, money laundering and other forms of financial crime affect sport at local, national and international levels. given the high degree of internationalisation of the sector, corruption in sport often takes on cross-border aspects. member states must therefore take all necessary measures to prevent and punish illegal activities that undermine the integrity of sport. in addition, with regard to the phenomenon of illegal betting, it is essential that member states develop tools to encourage cooperation between public authorities, sports authorities and gambling operators in relation to cases of sports fraud, as well as to address the issue of gambling addiction and the protection of minors in this area.
in writing. - recognising the european dimension of sport, we believe that sporting rules must be in line with european union law and in particular the charter of fundamental rights. in this respect, we cannot but share the need for transparency and accountability in management structures. we therefore call on sports organisations to adopt a zero-tolerance policy towards corruption and to apply ethical codes inspired by moral integrity and the genuine values of fair competition. we also call on the commission and the member states to adopt a harmonised approach to corruption in sport and stress that the fight against doping should be fully in line with eu law, in particular the charter of fundamental rights, privacy and data protection legislation and labour law.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of mrs fisas ayxela's report because i am convinced of the importance of combining sport and school learning. the aim, which is not confined to one country but concerns all eu member states, must be to bring about greater uniformity and at the same time to ensure that sport is open to all european citizens without any discrimination. the sport is going through a period of crisis mainly because of the criminal activities that have been linked to it. the european institutions should exercise greater control over the world of sport in the face of the current developments. to counter this drift, regulation would most likely improve the standard of sports governance. therefore, action to regulate the activity of sports agents and player transfers and to combat fraud and doping are all measures which are useful to this end. finally, the establishment of a 'european day of sport' and the designation of an annual 'european capital of sport' are, in my view, excellent instruments to bring citizens closer to sport.
in writing. − the report provides a comprehensive overview of the challenges facing the world of sport today and offers interesting insights and suggestions for dealing with these problems. i also believe that the report makes a real contribution to identifying measures that can ensure the sustainable financing of sport and the protection of the integrity of competitions in the future. however, the recognition of a right to exploit sports events for betting purposes is not the only means of ensuring the economic viability and integrity of sport. the eu member states, like italy, have efficient systems for allocating funds and i believe it is essential that they can maintain their good practices in respect of the principle of subsidiarity. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - in the face of worrying rates of obesity among young europeans, which have led some countries such as france and denmark to introduce a tax on sugary carbonated drinks, sport is the best response we can give. our young people do not need to be taxed to understand that what they consume is detrimental to their health. our young people can determine their choice, as long as there is an alternative. today i voted in favour of this report, which proposes sport as a means of providing a common experience and a healthy lifestyle, because that is the alternative. but we need more facilities for young people, we need trainers who are trained and have qualifications that are certified and recognised in every country. we need instructors and agents, as well as players, who are encouraged to move around europe to exchange good practice. healthy sports are those in which you play to stay together and win. it is the antithesis of the message that they want to give instead of doping and easy money, which i voted against in this report.
in writing. - sport is considered to be a competition and physical activity; the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the end of the year. the report by mr fisas ayxela, with which i fully agree, focuses on the social value of sport as a tool for social inclusion, around which the economy, work, health, etc. revolve. the european union is seeking to increase recognition of the importance of sporting activities and hopes that sporting projects between member states will increasingly be a means of social cohesion and improvement of the lifestyle of citizens.
in writing. - i congratulate mr fisas-ayxela on his excellent work. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has brought about a revolution in sport, because it has created for the first time a legal basis specifically for this sector, article 165. we therefore need more coordinated action at european level to combat doping, stadium violence, match-fixing and the abuse of sports agents. the european parliament is calling for the creation of a european blacklist to ban violent fans or those responsible for discriminatory behaviour from all european stadiums. the commission also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. in order to obtain a licence, prosecutors will have to prove that they have the minimum qualifications for this profession, that they are tax resident in the union and that they comply with a code of conduct.
in writing. − more coordinated action at european level is needed to combat doping, stadium violence, match-fixing and abuse of sports agents. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has brought a revolution in sport, as it has created for the first time a legal basis specifically for this sector. and today, by adopting this report, parliament is calling for violent fans and those who have been responsible for discriminatory behaviour to be banned from all european stadiums. a genuine european list will be used by the national authorities to ensure that these prohibitions remain in force also at international meetings. the member states and sports federations must also commit themselves to a more determined policy against incidents of racism and homophobia against athletes. the final text also suggests that trafficking in drugs should be treated in the same way as drug offences. i would like to stress that the final document calls for the eu to identify and remove all obstacles which might prevent girls and women from taking part in sport. increased representation of women in the governing bodies of sports federations could help to promote female sporting activity.
in writing. - after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the european parliament was given new powers as co-legislator, including in the field of sport. the new european agenda on sport aims to promote physical activity for the benefit of health of body and mind, to support the fight against doping and to ensure participation in sport for all, with particular attention to people with disabilities. the report also aims to preserve traditional and local sports as a cultural heritage. i agree with the text, but i think it is pleonastic to stress that sport should enable immigrants and host countries to interact and thus promote integration. i think that at least sport should be considered for all and not favor some ethnic group.
in writing. − the development of a shared european dimension in sport is an action which is of paramount importance to the union. the treaty of lisbon has given the european union a mandate to support, coordinate and complement the measures taken by the member states in the field of sport policy. sport is an important social phenomenon and a public good in itself. for many, it is one of the most important forms of entertainment, whether they are participants or spectators. in european sport policies, the fight against doping must be supported from a sporting point of view, and action must be taken from a cultural point of view to reduce violence and riots by fans. not to mention the importance of sport to public health. with this vote we underline that sport is an important public health tool and an effective factor in reducing public health expenditure, and we reiterate that the positive effects of regular physical activity include the prevention of health problems such as obesity, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, cancer and osteoporosis.
in writing. - due to the numerous petitions concerning waste management, it was necessary to present this report, which i voted in favour of, to supplement the legislation in force. the inability of many local authorities in most member states to manage waste disposal is certainly a cause for concern. the concerns of many communities for human health and the well-being of the land underline that waste management is becoming a real socio-political problem. an analysis of existing policies shows that only a few member states are keeping up with the times and are also making a profit from advanced waste processing systems. in most eu countries, however, there is a worrying delay in implementing waste strategies and an over-reliance on landfills. a coherent policy and a stronger commitment to the proper application of existing legislation and to sustainable disposal plans are therefore urgently needed. more needs to be done, in line with the law, and the waste management process needs to be improved to ensure more effective environmental protection and a more sustainable future.
in writing. the report, which is the result of complaints from european citizens, shows how weak the role of the european institutions and their directives can be if they are not adequately supported by a comprehensive network of control. in this sense, the report is above all an extraordinary demonstration of how a democratic process from below can work and produce results. the report highlights the long delay in the implementation of the waste directive in some areas of europe and the numerous violations of the directive: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. however, the recent events in campania, one of the regions covered by the report, have shown that the community method, if pursued to the end, using all the levers and instruments at its disposal, including coercive measures, can lead to concrete results, allowing the overcoming of structural problems and shortcomings. the role of citizens and their complaints is welcome, but above all the awareness of the european institutions that they fully understand their own strength and role.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on waste management because it is essential to ensure that our citizens have guarantees for their health and well-being. the 177 infringement procedures initiated by the eu reveal that there are 619 unfair dumping sites across the eu. the citizens are demanding clarity and procedural transparency and the number of petitions this parliament receives on waste and landfills is telling: between 2004 and 2010, it declared admissible 114 petitions alleging infringements. 40% of the work is concerned with the authorization procedures for new plants and another 40% with the operation of existing plants, but also with landfills and incinerators. data published by eurostat show that citizens produce an average of 513 kg of waste per year. citizens' reports during the public consultation process and environmental impact assessment on sites for new landfills often relate to alleged violations of protected areas, such as the vesuvius national park landfill, or concerns about the negative impact on health and well-being. europe should provide incentives for citizens who are diligent in separate collection so that taxes can be reduced and waste treatment can be made less impactful for the territory and the citizens.

in writing. - in europe, about 1.3 billion tonnes of waste are produced each year, excluding agricultural waste. however, general waste should not be confused with municipal waste. overall, waste in europe is divided into 29% waste from mining, 26% waste from manufacturing, 22% waste from construction and demolition and 14% municipal waste. the production of municipal waste in europe is therefore 198 million tonnes. with a population of 375 million in the eu, each inhabitant in europe produces 527 kg of waste every year. despite efforts to recover and recycle, landfilling remains the most common solution for 54% of cases. 27% of municipal waste ends up in the recycling or composting chain. the remaining 19% of waste is incinerated with or without energy recovery. the problem of waste disposal is only one aspect of the story. i would like to stress that the amount of waste we produce is the result of our unsustainable lifestyle. our current modes of production and consumption must be changed to minimise the pressure on the earth's (non-renewable) resources. in short, waste generation is one of the best indicators of our progress towards sustainable development.

in writing. - the report deals with a subject which is certainly worthy of attention; women, together with children, are by far the most vulnerable in war situations or in the post-war period, because they are often the victims of sexual and non-sexual violence, physical abuse and psychological violence. although i agree with the general approach, which calls for greater attention to the educational and schooling dimension of women in war situations and proposes a stronger commitment to gynaecological and health care for these vulnerable people, the report proposes specific measures which i do not agree with. the establishment, for example, of an eu special representative for women, peace and security, with a dedicated bureaucratic and administrative apparatus, obviously involves an expense that does not seem justifiable, given the existence within the un of a body that already operates ad hoc in the field of sexual violence in armed conflict. a duplication that is not guaranteed to be useful, but which would certainly entail additional costs compared to today. another problematic element, again for budgetary reasons, is the proposal to open new expenditure lines for gender advisers in the cfsp. for these reasons, i have chosen to abstain on this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the situation of women in war, as it is essential to guarantee the safety of women who decide to embark on a courageous career in war situations. in many war zones around the world, sexual violence in the form of mass rape and other forms of abuse such as human trafficking as a tactic of war are still common, with women being the primary victims. these unacceptable acts of violence have serious psychological and physical repercussions for the victims and their families. we must be more stringent in condemning those responsible for the crimes perpetrated against women in war. impunity cannot be negotiated and there can be no peace without justice! furthermore, the judicial process to convict perpetrators of violence against women in war is often too slow, creating further discomfort for women victims of war. finally, it is important to increase the participation of women in decision-making roles in peace processes and in the definition of security measures. women are often more sensitive to the needs of society and can make a concrete contribution to peacebuilding projects, particularly for needs related to children, school facilities or hospitals.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur that women need to be more involved in military and civilian operations in war zones. women, the pillar of the community, are irreplaceable in the construction and maintenance of peace. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the situation of women in war because i believe that gender equality is an essential element of equality and freedom for everyone. in addition, as in politics and business, efforts are being made to promote the central role of women in international conflict situations. the aim is to include the role of women in the high diplomatic spheres for conflict resolution and in civil aid for the needy and social reconstruction. a project is also under way for the appointment of a european union special representative on women, peace and security.
in writing. − women's participation in peace negotiations continues to be, with rare exceptions, less than 10% of official participants today, despite the creation of the post of un special representative on sexual violence in armed conflict. all too often in war settings, women are victims of repeated sexual violence, in the form of mass rape, human trafficking and other forms of sexual abuse of women and children. and in post-conflict contexts, you can see the deterioration of women's and girls' rights, as seen in libya and egypt. the vote will make eu support for peace processes conditional on women's participation in international groups conducting peace negotiations, so that progress is made on the permanent inclusion of women leaders, local women's rights organisations and civil society groups at the negotiating table throughout the peace process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the neuser report. ensuring universal access to electricity by 2030 is an ambitious goal and fortunately europe has the means to achieve it. i share the concern to include this target in the post-2015 millennium development goals and to consider it as a prerequisite for achieving the mdgs by 2015. nevertheless, the promotion of power stations and the facilities necessary for the distribution and use of electricity will have to be carried out by means of solutions compatible with the territorial reality, considering that small and medium-scale solutions may be more suitable for developing countries. i believe that the development of such a project should be carried out through cooperation between the public sector and the qualified expertise of the private sector. finally, to ensure its sustainability, it is necessary to promote and implement the exchange of best practices.
in writing. − i voted for this text as it makes clear that the millennium development goals will not be achieved unless substantial progress is made on improving energy access. the world energy outlook 2011 of the international energy agency (iea) emphasises that worldwide about 1.3 billion people have no access to electricity. access to sustainable energy sources and modern energy services is a prerequisite for economic growth and social development, as well as for the realisation of several of the rights contained in the 1966 international covenant on economic, social and cultural rights and other international human rights and environmental legal instruments. in addition to that, although there is no millennium development goal specifically related to energy, i strongly believe that energy should move to the forefront of the debate on eradication of poverty. for this reason the commission and the member states must endorse and commit to support the un recently established international target of universal energy access by 2030, and align their policies and development cooperation with this objective. by this same means we also ask for the establishment, within eu development cooperation, of a specific ‘energy and development’ programme, with special focus on universal energy access.
in writing. − access to modern energy services is a key prerequisite for poverty reduction and sustainable human development worldwide. energy services have a general impact on people's lives and livelihoods: without such access, entire communities are condemned to a life of poverty. energy poverty in developing countries is a serious problem. over the last decade, the european union's financial assistance has been modest. bilateral cooperation between eu countries on energy assistance has focused on economic growth and environmental objectives rather than on energy access for the poor. not only will we have to increase funds (european development fund and energy facility) and allocate them more targeted to the poor and geographically isolated sections of the population, but we will be called upon to make greater efforts to invest in small-scale decentralised energy projects and, at least initially, to reduce our profit margins. only by showing political will and financial commitment can the european union play a key role in achieving universal access to energy by 2030 (as envisaged by the un).
in writing. - the vast financial gap to be filled to provide access to energy for all cannot be ignored. the goal of universal access to energy is one of the most difficult challenges, but it is a just battle that we must all fight together. i therefore vote in favour of the neuser report.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, in line with the objective of 'universal access to energy by 2030' launched by the un secretary-general, the european union is developing a common policy for the development of energy systems. energy is the basis of modern life, it affects the life of each of us and that is why the international community is concerned with policies to improve energy development. i too believe that the objective of achieving global energy coverage is necessary because it is a fundamental requirement for poverty reduction and sustainable development. the role of energy services is crucial to the achievement of the millennium development goals as energy development can ensure wealth, access to information, education, health and gender equality, not to mention environmental sustainability and development in general.

in writing. the report is intended to declare parliament's loyalty to the proposal for tax harmonisation in the eu. it is argued that the current system based on different national taxation systems creates bureaucratic difficulties and disparities in treatment between companies, hence the need to move towards a uniform tax system, giving the european union competence in tax matters. tax harmonization is also seen as a driver of growth and employment. i do not agree with these arguments, since it is the competitiveness, also from the tax point of view, of different national systems that creates opportunities for firms and workers within the framework of the common market. the diversity of tax systems also ensures that states try, as far as possible, to change their tax laws in order to try to attract employment and enterprise. instead, fiscal federalism must be encouraged as a means of achieving greater economic efficiency in our continental system, and the proposal for simplification of vat must be insisted on, together with the reduction of bureaucratic burdens for businesses and the introduction of tax incentives for smes. given the substance of the report, which is in favour of tax harmonization within the community, my vote is against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text presented by mr schmidt. for the first time, the european parliament has decided to publish an annual report on taxation. the aim is to contribute to the commission's work in 2012, focusing on the tax initiatives taken by the commission in 2011 and on areas that need further action, to improve the functioning of the single market, in order to create a more competitive and integrated europe. greater coordination of member states' tax policies is therefore needed, and a careful examination of areas where the eu could have a decisive and direct impact on the daily lives of many european businesses and citizens through positive spillovers is needed. the elimination in the member states of discriminatory tax rules which undermine the fundamental freedoms guaranteed by the treaties of the european union is of paramount importance. finally, strong support must be given to campaigns and measures to combat tax evasion and abuse and to encourage tax transparency.
in writing. − for the first time, the european parliament has decided to publish an annual report on taxation, with the aim of contributing to the commission's work programme for 2012. we have focused on areas where we believe new initiatives are needed to improve the functioning of the single market and to create an increasingly competitive europe. we would like to stress the importance of the tax problems that most directly affect european citizens in crossborder situations within the union itself (e.g. cases of double taxation, allowances, exemptions or deductions by foreign tax authorities). we have also called for greater fiscal coordination and a greater role for the european institutions. we consider it of paramount importance to eliminate discriminatory tax rules in the member states which undermine the fundamental freedoms guaranteed by the treaties of the european union and we call for the harmonization of methods of combating tax evasion and abuse and those aimed at increasing tax transparency in all 27 member states.

in writing. - the report on taxation presented by the commission gives us the opportunity to finally define, in line with what the european semester will establish, a common tax strategy. i think mr schmidt's text is a good starting point which, despite some differences, such as the proposal for a financial transaction tax rejected by the united kingdom, can strengthen the european tax system. the first objective must be to achieve a balanced budget for all the member states, and then to reconcile the budgetary system with growth policies and thus promote the convergence of national economic policies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr schmidt's annual report on taxation, which calls on the european commission to make proposals which will contribute to european competitiveness by eliminating the distortions of competition resulting from the various tax regimes which still exist. as regards crossborder bands, differences in taxation - the so-called excise duties - on certain products such as fuel, beverages and cigarettes are particularly important, and can easily distort competition across borders. the current economic and financial crisis has caused a significant increase in public debt in europe, the reduction of which requires both spending restraint and tax increases and the rationalisation of tax systems. therefore, measures are needed to make national tax systems more conducive to common growth, ensuring that tax disparities do not give firms in one country an undue advantage over competitors in other countries.

in writing. − we welcome the commission's annual report on competition policy for 2010. eu competition policy has brought many benefits in terms of consumer welfare and has emerged as an essential tool for removing barriers to the free movement of goods, services, people and capital. we believe that it is an essential instrument for preserving the single market and protecting the interests of consumers, although we also believe that it is important to make changes and adjustments to update certain rules so that they can meet the new challenges. we consider the combined effect of strict principles and flexible procedures to be essential, which has enabled competition policy to be a constructive and stabilising factor in the financial system and in the real economy of the european union in general. we also stress that, in order to complete the internal market, there should be greater consistency between consumer rights across the union and we note that a well-designed system of collective redress can contribute to consumer confidence and, consequently, to the smooth functioning of the internal market and online trade, increasing the competitiveness of the european economy.

companies in their local market, in their own language. we do not intend to withdraw this option, particularly as regards the language question. mrs wikström and mrs ţicău also raised the issue of licences. mrs macovei referred in particular to the question of competition in the operation of collective management companies. yes, there will be, ladies and gentlemen, more transparency in the way companies operate and more opportunities for shareholders to make an informed choice. yes, because a common basis and a level playing field will be established for the operation of collective management societies in europe. after this text, which you will no doubt have the opportunity to improve, it will be easier for rightholders, for commercial users, to compare the levels of service offered by the different collective management societies. we will thus be able, as mr obermayer said, to use more effectively all the creative potential that exists in europe. mrs záborská referred to in writing. the debate, initiated by the regi committee with the question on 'reprogramming the structural funds to improve the fight against youth unemployment and support smes', cleared the field of doubts. the aim of supporting small businesses and promoting youth employment is certainly to be welcomed, but it risks remaining an announcement if the commission does not clarify the actions and programmes it intends to put in place and does not identify the budget line to be used. the 82 billion on which the commission bases its proposal are resources allocated to the member states which have not yet been spent but which are already predominantly committed. the concern that these resources could be diverted from national and regional programmes at the commission's initiative was dispelled by the final speech of commissioner hahn, who, acknowledging the parliament's concerns, announced that the choice of reprogramming expenditure would be left to the states and that the funds would remain at the disposal of individual countries.
