president-in-office of the council. − mr president, let me first take this opportunity to congratulate mr mato adrover on his election as chair of the committee. unfortunately my colleague, the minister for food, agriculture and fisheries, ms mette gjerskov, was not able to be here today. however it is a pleasure for me to take part in this important debate on fisheries. i would like to address the different issues raised one by one. on the horse mackerel multi-annual plan, the council shares the view expressed previously by ms fraga and today by mr gallagher on behalf of the committee on fisheries that the establishment of long-term management plans is key to conservation. that is why the council has adopted 10 such plans since 2003 covering many, if not most, of the major stocks in the union waters. i am pleased to inform you that the committee of permanent representatives in the council made considerable progress last november on a way forward on the proposed multiannual plan for the stock of western horse mackerel. i understand that ms fraga, mr gallagher and the shadow rapporteurs were informed of the outcome in early december. against this background the council will now be in a position to examine in full parliament’s positions in first reading, and to that end work is beginning this week. i would like to take this opportunity to thank the honourable members for their positive and pragmatic approach and i hope that results can be achieved. i turn now to the proposed plan for the anchovy stock in the bay of biscay, which was also raised by the honourable members. the council position is that this plan is not in line with the treaty. the council, at the level of the committee of permanent representatives, therefore asked the commission in the autumn of 2010 to withdraw the proposal. the council has not discussed the plan since then. the council agrees that long-term management plans are one of the key elements of the reform of the common fisheries policy. that is why it has made such an effort to unblock the situation for the plan for western horse mackerel. the council is fully committed to cooperating with parliament and the commission to agree on a way forward. we are ready to work with you on this plan and on other long-term and management plans which are at the centre of conservation and of the reform of the common fishery policy. i now turn to the issue of total allowable catch and quota regulation and begin by thanking mr mato adrover for his question on the adoption of the 2012 fishing opportunities. i would like to start by restating that the council continues its commitment to adopt measures that are fully in line with the relevant legal provisions. i strongly believe that this commitment is also reflected in the adoption of fishing opportunities for 2012. the commission presented two proposals for adoption of measures on the fixing and allocation of fishing opportunities for 2012, one on the internal aspect and the other on the external aspect. the commission based its proposal on article 43(3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, under which the council shall adopt measures on a proposal from the commission on the fixing and allocation of fishing opportunities. the council consistently agreed with the commission’s choice of legal basis for the following reasons. the council considers that article 43(3) represents a self-standing specific legal basis that applies to clearly identified measures to be adopted under the common fisheries policy. furthermore, article 43(3) of the treaty speaks of measures which indicate that the authors of the treaty intended to give the council powers to adopt all measures that are inextricably linked to the fixing and allocation of fishing opportunities. they can only cover measures which have a direct bearing on the quantitative fishing entitlements. finally, i would like to conclude by saying that, since the adoption of the lisbon treaty, the objectives for the common fisheries policies, including those concerning multiannual plans, must be adopted in the ordinary legislative procedure with agreement between parliament and the council. the council is committed to respecting that. thank you for your attention. i look forward to a very good debate here in parliament today.

fishing opportunities and conditions functionally linked to them. let me be clear here: fishing opportunities are quantified fishing rights. the treaty refers to ‘fishing opportunities’. as a matter of principle, a quantified fishing right cannot exist in a void, so – while the treaty does not refer to tacs and quotas – a tac area or an allowed fishing season, for example, is necessary for fishing opportunities to work. let all of us be reasonable here. we are talking about fishing opportunities and we have to respect the treaties, so these conditions are functionally linked to fishing opportunities as they have a direct bearing on them. this, then, is our position: we have to cooperate here and we have to find the best way that all three institutions can live together. i do not think we face a power game here, and it is not a matter of the commission trying to prevent parliament from exercising its new powers. in relation to the last item raised by other members of the house of people working in processing; and that is the best way of encouraging young people – whom mr gróbarczyk mentioned specifically – to come into the sector. if young people see that there is an income mr president, intellectual property rights are an instrument for safeguarding europe's cultural diversity and at the same time guarantee the union's economic growth and are a reservoir for creating new jobs. in view of the enormous economic damage that the non-respect of these rights causes to community revenue, it has become necessary in recent years for the member states and the european institutions to step up their efforts to combat such violations. i therefore believe that it is right that measures should be taken to inform consumers of the dangers of buying counterfeit goods and to make them more aware of the negative impact of piracy and counterfeiting on european industry. that is why i voted in favour.
mr president, the increase in intellectual property infringements in recent years risks undermining the strategy on intellectual property rights in the single market launched by the commission in may 2011. in order to combat this phenomenon and safeguard the success of the policy of protecting intellectual property, it was proposed to entrust certain tasks relating to the management of the european observatory on counterfeiting and piracy, set up in 2009, to the office for harmonisation in the internal market. this is to provide the observatory with human and financial resources to take action against infringements of intellectual property and to carry out awareness campaigns to raise consumer awareness of the risks of buying counterfeit products. the vote in favour of the report is therefore a very important moment in the fight against the trade in counterfeit goods and in defence of innovation, growth and competitiveness of small and mediumsized enterprises, and the employment and security of european citizens.
mr president, intellectual property may appear contradictory in its definition, but it has great moments of coherence. i voted in favour of this proposal because its purpose - namely to entrust the european union trade marks and designs office with certain tasks relating to the management of the european observatory on counterfeiting and piracy - is necessary and indispensable in order to combat infringements of intellectual property rights. the main objectives are to raise public and private sector awareness of the impact of counterfeiting and piracy and to inform consumers of the dangers of buying counterfeit products. on the basis of the 33 compromise amendments, agreement was reached at first reading on 19 december. the amendments provide that the title of the regulation and the name of the office shall not be changed in the sense of the european observatory. more important and fundamental is the participation of civil society in the meetings. all this will make a moment of synthesis like the one we are about to celebrate with today's vote even more democratic and participatory.
mr president, i voted in favour of the text voted this morning in an attempt to revive the functions of the office for counterfeiting and piracy. the european monitoring centre for counterfeiting and piracy has so far failed to produce significant results and to carry out its mandate effectively because of insufficient human, financial and instrumental resources. my vote is therefore for the observatory to be re-launched, and since it is part of the office for harmonization in the internal market, it could make use of the office's financial resources. i conclude by saying that, for the observatory to really take off, the office will have to be equipped with the appropriate resources and professional knowledge and the necessary technical expertise, including that of the national authorities of the member states competent in the field of intellectual property, to enable it to exercise effectively the new powers linked to the operation of the observatory and to carry out these functions with the same effort and respect for each intellectual property right recognised at community level, without any hierarchy in the protection of intellectual property rights.

mr president, knowledge of the facts and events in the life of companies through publicity systems regulated by law is an essential element in ensuring the efficient operation of markets in accordance with the law. to this end, rules exist under very different national regimes, which ensure the management of numerous public registers of an economic and administrative nature. in my country, italy, the most important is the business register, in which all companies operating in italian territory are required to be registered. my vote this morning is in favour of the interconnection of business registers, as provided for in the text under discussion in the house. this proposal for a directive is an important measure to promote further integration of the economic area within the european union and to strengthen legal certainty for businesses and citizens. it also saves - and i stress this - a lot of money for our companies, especially those operating in different countries of the union. in a time of crisis like this, that's not a small thing!
in writing. the report concerns the conferral of new powers on the european office for harmonisation in the internal market with regard to the enforcement of intellectual property rights. the commission is therefore not setting up a new body, but strengthening an existing one to meet the challenges posed by a growing problem such as the trade in counterfeit and pirated goods. the problem is that every year it causes a loss of competitiveness for our companies, it puts the safety and health of millions and millions of european consumers at risk, it takes a chunk out of the coffers of the states and erodes parts of the european labour market. moreover, this increasingly flourishing and difficult-to-control activity fuels organized crime. it is therefore good that efforts are being made to combat this growing phenomenon by all possible means, including the creation of a forum for coordination between the competent national authorities for the exchange of good practice and the interchange of information and common strategies to deal with the problem in a cooperative manner, without, however, compromising the prerogatives of the individual national authorities. my vote is therefore in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr hidalgo's report. the european observatory on counterfeiting and piracy is a centre of expertise for the collection, monitoring and communication of data on infringements of intellectual property rights and a platform where stakeholders can exchange ideas on best practices with a view to developing protection strategies. it is necessary and appropriate to entrust the office for harmonisation in the internal market (ohim) with the tasks currently carried out by the observatory, as the office has the financial resources and expertise to carry out the recently extended tasks of the observatory. the aim of the proposal is to improve the exercise of the powers conferred on the observatory. this is all the more so as in the current context of the continuous growth of counterfeit trade, which causes considerable losses of tax revenue for member states, jobs and a decrease in investment in innovation, it is useful to implement the activities carried out by ohim. the observatory will become a permanent forum for public and private sector representatives on counterfeiting and piracy in europe.

in writing. − unlike ' live attenuated vaccines', the new inactive vaccines do not present a risk of unwanted transmission of the vaccine virus and could therefore be used successfully outside areas where restrictions on movement of livestock have been imposed. in order to make the rules on vaccination against bluetongue more flexible, in particular by allowing the use of inactivated vaccines outside areas where restrictions on animal movements have been imposed, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the commission's proposal to make the rules on vaccination against bluetongue more flexible is valid. the provisions of directive 2000/75/ec relate only to vaccines available at that time, allowing vaccination only in specific areas where the disease has actually occurred and where restrictions on the movement of livestock have been imposed due to the high risk of transmission. the new 'inactive vaccines', on the other hand, do not present a risk of infecting unvaccinated animals and could therefore be successfully used outside areas where restrictions on animal movements have been imposed.
in writing. - bluetongue is a notifiable disease affecting ruminants and is transmitted by flies which, by biting the animal, transmit the disease to it. vaccination is an important tool against the disease. directive 2000/75/ec limits the vaccine to areas where animal movements have been restricted. in recent years, new vaccines have been marketed which, unlike previous vaccines, do not present a risk of unwanted transmission of the virus to vaccinated animals. i am in favour - as is my whole political group and the other groups (the text was unanimous on almost all points long ago in the committee on agriculture and was recently approved without amendments for approval at second reading) - of the objectives of the commission proposal, which is to introduce additional opportunities for vaccination against bluetongue and to reduce the burden of this disease on european agriculture.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr wojciechowski, which aims to update the current rules for vaccination against bluetongue, to make them more flexible and to take account of the progress made in vaccination techniques. i hope that, once the problems have been resolved by an interinstitutional agreement, the procedure can be concluded quickly so that the new rules can come into force as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which aims to create an internal market for payment services in euro, i.e. a single area in which there are no differences between national and crossborder payments. the integration of european payment markets has several economic benefits: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the rules on the free movement of goods and services are respected, and that the rules on the free movement of goods and services are applied. the impact assessment of the proposal estimates that the potential benefits for the european economy are in the region of eur 100-300 billion over six years. the proposed regulation also provides that the direct debit and electronic transfer systems will be phased out within 12 and 24 months of the entry into force of the regulation respectively. the rapporteur agrees, however, that a single transitional period of 24 months from the entry into force of the regulation would be more effective, in order to simplify communication to the public and improve the effectiveness of the necessary information campaigns.
in writing. − the harmonisation of a single area for payments in euro is an important step towards the integration of financial markets. reducing transaction costs will create more competition and intensify economic activity within the single market. however, to achieve these results, the transition process must take place in a harmonious way in all member states: i think that this is why it is important to set a single deadline by which all direct debit and direct transfer operations must comply with certain technical standards. that's why i voted yes.
in writing. - the report by mr essayah takes a closer look at a subject which affects all european citizens to varying degrees: simplification of the procedures for payment by credit transfer and debit in order to make them common to all member states. with the introduction of a single area for payments in euro (sape), a payment transaction made by means of a transfer in a foreign country will be treated as the same transaction carried out in the country of origin. this will benefit both businesses, which will reduce operating costs, estimated to save between eur 100 and 300 million over six years, and citizens, who will see many financial transactions, which are increasingly common and widespread in a globalised market, simplified.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report. the creation of an integrated market for electronic payments in euro, without distinction between national and cross-border payments, is absolutely necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market. i agree that we want to protect consumers: the principle of not charging higher fees should be promoted where the payment service user is a consumer. it is good that the commission does not stop its monitoring.
in writing. - i wanted to express my positive opinion of this report, since it is intended to simplify and better regulate a very important and constantly expanding sector. in fact, both businesses and citizens are increasingly dealing with international payment systems, and this can create problems with different regulations. the creation of a single area for payments in euro (sape) should ensure a single integrated and homogeneous system, in which there is no longer any difference between, for example, a national transfer and a european transfer. this should lead to considerable simplification and considerable savings, to the benefit of both european businesses and consumers.
in writing. - today our parliament has expressed an important position towards consumers: bank transfers between eu countries will soon become cheaper, safer and faster, thanks to new legislation on the single euro payments area. from 1 february 2014, the new eu rules will also ensure that hidden costs in banking operations are eliminated and should save customers, banks and businesses up to €123 billion over 6 years. it is a tangible sign of the will to demonstrate to our citizens that the internal market exists, is developing and is intended to create conditions worthy of confidence on the part of businesses and consumers. it will be possible to make and receive payments in euro throughout the union on the same basic conditions as national payments and we hope that the sector linked to cross-border transactions, including online, will receive a boost to ensure greater competition, competitiveness and quality for european citizens, to the benefit of consumers and businesses.
in writing. the proposal aims to create an internal market for payment services in euro (single area for payments in euro sepa) in which there are no differences in regimes between crossborder and national payments. it brings significant economic benefits by enhancing competition and innovation, helps reduce payment costs for consumers and businesses, and simplifies cross-border payments which will be similar to national payments. in order to set the necessary technical requirements, i am voting in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 924/2009.
in writing. - i would like to congratulate my colleague mrs essayah on her work. the regulation adopted today will bring real benefits to ordinary citizens. the most obvious is the possibility of paying from a single bank account to any country, as if you were executing a transaction at national level. all crossborder transfers will be able to be made as national payments. if a person living abroad does not need a bank account in his country of residence, he can receive his salary on the account of his country of origin. businesses will also benefit from the fact that they no longer have to open a bank account in every country where payments are made. a european citizen will be able to move around the eu and continue to use the same euro bank account, into which he can also deposit his salary earned in another eu country. you can pay a bill in one country with an account in another. competition between service providers should also drive down prices, and a discriminatory transfer cost policy based on the amount of the transfer will be prohibited.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i am convinced that the creation of an integrated market for electronic payments in euro, without distinction between national and crossborder payments, is necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market. the single euro payments area (sepa) would enable citizens, businesses and other economic operators to use payment services common to the union as a whole, replacing the current national services. the integration of european payment markets should also bring significant economic benefits through enhanced competition and innovation, thus allowing consumers and businesses to have access to low-cost, easy-to-use and reliable euro payment services.
in writing. - i welcome the agreement reached today by almost unanimous vote, which speeds up the legislative procedure and brings it to an end at first reading. i am in favour of the text, and i believe that with this morning's vote in the house the hidden bank charges for crossborder payments will have to be eliminated once and for all when the new community rules come into force. ensuring a high level of competition in the banking sector for payments between european countries could save businesses, customers and banks up to €123 billion over six years, according to the european commission. the commission will be proposing a new regulation on the sepa (single euro payment area) by 1 february 2014, which will enable us to see the tangible results of european legislation as soon as possible.

mr president, it must be clear that the eurobonds are not intended to shift the responsibility of the less virtuous countries onto the shoulders of the virtuous countries. everyone must remain calm: no one thinks of being "friends". the german reserves, which were initially understandable, now have no reason to exist, because eurobonds can be designed to allow some countries to reduce the cost of debt without increasing it for others. as some colleagues have pointed out, the introduction of eurobonds must be part of a process of greater fiscal integration and coordination among the euro area member countries: but it will also require the utmost care to ensure that this transfer of fiscal sovereignty takes place through institutions with full democratic legitimacy, such as the european parliament. i want to say this as forcefully as i can: no response to the authoritarian fiscal compact procedure. ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow we shall be voting on a historic vote, planting an important seed to save europe and to move swiftly towards a europe of economic governance, fiscal coordination and hence political europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, too much precious time has already been lost in moving in a direction which seems to me to be both logical and necessary. the member states in difficulty, which are being asked to apply very strict budgetary restrictions and which some people even wanted to supervise, cannot afford to pay billions of euros more than the other countries in the eurozone to refinance their debts, otherwise they will never be able to get out of this crisis. the solution recently proposed by some french analysts seems to me very interesting: the commission has also proposed that the european central bank should be given the task of drawing up a list of the countries whose currency is the euro. this would lead to a general saving in refinancing costs, which would certainly benefit not only those countries which are paying more today but also the so-called virtuous countries. we need to move quickly. europe can no longer be subservient to the interests of one country which claims to decide for all the others.
madam president, after voting on the fiscal compact and the specific budget and setting the tone for the debate on the need for everyone to follow the rules, we are now realizing that there is no single position within either parliament or the governments. we cannot ignore that. the first and second options in the green paper cannot be mutualised for a very simple reason: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the guarantee is valid for all the member states, which is why we have a moral hazard. we cannot afford not to work on the third approach if we want to do it quickly and immediately. that is to say: i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the negotiations, but that it should be involved in the negotiations. so, the debt in the form of eurobonds would be made up of the best assets, so this option is feasible and can be realized quickly, by using, as i said, the best and the most secure assets through liquid reserves and gold reserves. i think that's the only way to go at the moment: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the denomination of these eurobonds will be defined later: but at the moment we have a serious problem which is economic stagnation: we must act now or the countries that need it will go into recession.
madam president, apart from the financial transaction tax, the fixed bonds are the only concrete proposal that has emerged in recent months to start talking again about development and growth and not just about austerity and rigor. we need resources to re-oxygenate the european economy and to restore confidence to the market, consumers and businesses, a new common project that is economic, fiscal and financial. we need new projects to support employment and to combat youth unemployment. or do we think that we can solve everything with the €82 billion announced with great fanfare in the media at the last european council which are nothing but the structural funds not yet committed by the member states? i think we are all convinced that we cannot talk to the people of europe about sacrifices and cuts any longer. in conclusion, i would like to address my german colleagues. i think that at the moment no one can save himself alone and therefore, if the bonds are not a panacea, germany must also be careful, because if the crisis spreads, this very virtuous country will also have to pay the price.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, an important programme and an ambitious plan: to make europe the world leader in broadband speed, mobility, coverage and capacity. as i have already said, we must aim for broadband for all. europe is lagging behind: the united states and china have already liberalised much of their radio spectrum. the agreement to free up the 800 megahertz frequency band for wireless broadband internet services by the end of this year and to further speed up mobile broadband to at least 30 megabytes per second is therefore welcome. these are important objectives. i believe that the european digital agenda is a source of development, growth and jobs in the long term. we must set out with determination to return to a leading role in the global knowledge economy.
mr president, i must admit that our debate today is a reflection of our contradictions and our impotence. on the one hand, i know that the socialist group is denouncing a pension reform which it has just applauded in similar terms in neighbouring italy. it is not clear how a measure which is virtuous for one country can be detrimental to another. on the other hand, governments that ask greece to show virtue and cut public spending are in fact forcing it to buy military supplies, thus exponentially increasing that same public spending. i also think that is a huge contradiction. who is the real victim of this contradiction? the greek people, many say. but there's one more victim: it is europe. i think you all noticed the images of the greek parliament besieged amidst burning buildings, among which european flags were seen with a central nazi swastika. the real victim of this crisis of democracy is an institutional process like ours, which, although it is working for the good of the european citizens, guaranteeing peace and development, is now seen as an absolute evil. let us move then! mr president, i ask you to go to athens and bring the voice of the european parliament to a besieged greek parliament, against all democratic logic. remind everyone what our real goal is: ensuring peace and development for all.
mr president, by participating in a critical but constructive way in the negotiations on the fiscal compact, this parliament has reached an important point of unity. greater fiscal responsibility at national level is necessary but insufficient and, without concrete actions for growth and solidarity, may trigger an unsustainable downward spiral. there is no trace of this serious and balanced approach of parliament in the preparatory documents of the european council. for the council and the commission the word 'growth' seems to mean fiscal consolidation and wage reductions. it is true that there are positive developments in the internal market, but these are not enough. growth needs a robust internal engine, which has a twofold objective: strengthening domestic demand in the surplus countries and promoting an extraordinary plan of investment financed by project bonds. the commission, on the other hand, reads the macroeconomic imbalances one way - ignoring the logic of the ferreira regulation - and there is no trace in the european council documents of joint project bonds and investments, except for an empty game of three cards with the already existing resources of the structural funds, which is more like the way mussolini moved his tanks during the second world war to make people believe that he had a large army which he did not have. it is therefore clear that this ruling class has fulfilled its task and that only a great political change can save europe from catastrophe.
in writing. the next european council will be very important, as, unfortunately, have been the summits of the past two years. however, expectations have often not been matched by results. this summit will also put the final touches on the details of the fiscal compact. i hope, however, that once the framework for budgetary and fiscal discipline in the member states is defined, we will begin to talk seriously about growth. it is not enough to hear the words and statements repeated throughout europe about the importance of growth and the need for new investment. europe as a whole, and no country excepted, needs an effective, serious and concrete strategy for growth. that is what we are asking the heads of state meeting in brussels to do. i hope that in this context a solution will be found to the problem of greece, which cannot and must not be left alone.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, this plenary session should have only one item on the agenda: the european project as it has been managed until now. this is shown by the data published last week by eurostat: 24 million europeans are unemployed, 115 million citizens are heading towards poverty, one in three of whom is a boy under 18. no one has the recipe for solving the crisis. the european commission pretends to have one by imposing austerity measures on the member states to reduce public debt, while it continues to squander millions of euros by, for example, maintaining two offices in brussels and strasbourg. the cuts in social security and the hidden manoeuvres imposed by technical governments, about which nobody wants to talk openly, are now taking away the meaning of democratic institutions, depriving citizens of dialogue with politics. to regain a sense of responsibility, europe should distance itself from the financial lobbies of the occult powers. the approach of identity relativism and the false myth of welfare deriving from open markets have failed. we need a democracy that can give a voice to the regions, the territories and the citizens.
mr president, we are discussing three excellent reports which demonstrate the wide and articulate conviction within this parliament that growth is essential for the future of the european union. but these are countered by a completely unacceptable attitude on the part of the council and the commission, which are dominated by the ideological approach of exclusive action around stability, with an obsession which, as the events in greece these days show, is now leading explicitly to real problems of democracy. i believe that this gap is unsustainable for the future of europe and that the commission and the council must make some serious adjustments. i would add that the insistence on the 2020 strategy is little more than a cultural option. after five years of crisis, with a severe recession that will last for the next two years, those objectives are no longer there. we must now recognize this in order to propose a comprehensive strategy that does not take reference from what does not exist in nature.
mr president, whenever the situation seems to be improving, new downgrades by the rating agencies come in to shake up the international markets. many european companies are in crisis and, on the employment front, the number of people - especially young people - who are chronically looking for work is increasing. if austerity plans and the defence of the euro are necessary measures, then even more so are profound labour market revisions at national level to revive the european economy. only by boosting the competitiveness of the european union will we give investors new confidence and promote the growth of new jobs.
mr president, there is no doubt that the latest figures on unemployment, especially youth unemployment, are a cause of particular social alarm. if the percentage in the euro area is 10.4 and is on the increase, this obviously has to be a cause for particular concern. this is why we must be very careful about the initiative put forward by the commission to set up a task force, an action team, to support the individual governments - initially eight - in channelling community funds to create new jobs, especially for young people. the right to work is sacred and fundamental and, within the framework of the 2020 strategy, activities in favour of employment and growth will have to be concretely promoted, also linking migration flows to the labour market and ensuring above all the community preference.
mr president, the adoption of this resolution today finally brings attention back to a central issue for the future of europe. the great victim of the crisis and the inadequate employment policies of recent years has been work. the situation, especially among young people, is sadly getting worse. the european council will adopt new guidelines for economic and employment policies on 1 march. it is therefore necessary to talk about a new labour market plan, a market reform capable of boosting employment, backed up by a genuine investment policy, directed towards the new generations in order to give them concrete answers: the commission has also proposed a new employment plan to modernise public education and training systems and finally to give value to the individual. work must be returned to a regular and stable status, not necessarily in the same place for life, but not a "use and throw away" experience either. the real challenge will be to enable and encourage different professional experiences over a lifetime, while preserving and guaranteeing professionalism and pay.
mr president, these guidelines on employment policies will be of great help in achieving the objective of increasing participation in the labour market and thus reducing youth unemployment in particular. the future of young people today is increasingly uncertain and precarious. it is no secret that sustained economic growth is now crucial for europe's future. the figures for youth unemployment are dramatic and unacceptable. the european union must commit itself to a medium- to long-term strategy for better, full and good employment, which focuses on young people and youth mobility, but also on gender equality in the labour market and, at the same time, aims to improve the performance of education and training systems at all levels.
mr president, the current economic crisis, combined with the austerity measures adopted in some countries, has created new social categories at risk of poverty, including young people and the elderly. in view of the europe 2020 objectives, the annual growth review should ensure consistency between the different priorities in its policy guidelines, so that budgetary needs are based on social justice. i agree with the rapporteur that we must act now to improve the employment conditions of those at risk of social exclusion and give priority to the fight against youth unemployment. future national reform plans should provide for training pathways that develop lifelong learning and create skilled jobs with decent pay and working conditions.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, at such a difficult time for europe, the distribution of food to the poor of the union, after the council's blockade and the presentation of a new amended proposal by the commission, is certainly a positive development, a useful compromise which has solved many of the issues that had caused the impasse, such as the full financing of the programme by the european union, with the union's own participation in the programme at the distribution points, an annual ceiling of eur 500 million for the community financial contribution, the question of the community origin of the food then distributed and the provision of competitive procedures for the purchase of food. the programme will therefore be operational from 2013 and will allow the supply of food from intervention stocks to the most disadvantaged groups in the union, thus also achieving some of the important objectives of the cap. the fact that we voted in favour today of completing the complex and bumpy road of this report is an important sign of the union's concern for its most deprived citizens.

mr president, the dairy sector has been in a terrible crisis for years now, but there are some internal imbalances which this regulation and its amendment - which i have supported from the beginning - will cause to a lesser extent, affecting the operation and putting an end to, or at least partially correcting, those internal imbalances together with other instruments. this measure was adopted by the working group set up by commissioner cioloş, which identified a number of instruments to rebalance the recognition of added value for all operators in the supply chain. in particular, there will be contracts with certain characteristics in terms of form, requirements, duration, timing and procedures which will be of particular use to producers. an important element will be raw milk processed in less-favoured, mountain, intermediate and island areas, where any transfer of milk from non-less-favoured areas will have to be authorised in advance.

in writing. - we cannot be in favour of a text which aims to solve employment problems and which deals with member states' policies in favour of employment with provisions which seek to 'remove the barriers' which prevent immigrants from accessing the eu labour market. we cannot accept such arrangements, because it is precisely because of the rules which facilitate legal immigrants that it is already easier for them to be called upon to cover a job vacancy than a community citizen. in addition, we have realised that when the european union formulates corrective actions against member states, it is in fact trying to decide for them and, in view of the dramatic consequences of the austerity measures introduced by such measures, we are sceptical of community strategies such as those in question.
in writing. − the commission in its annual growth survey (ags) identified five priorities as actions for 2012: fiscal consolidation, restoration of the normal functioning of the credit market; growth and competitiveness; tackling unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis; modernisation of public administration. i, for my part, would like to stress my full support, expressed in the affirmative vote this morning, for the five priorities identified. i would also like to stress that it is absolutely necessary to speed up the work on the completion of the single market and on extending the scope of the ags. finally, i would like to express my appreciation for the integrated approach of the document and the unprecedented attention paid to social issues. one last word about the young people: the fourth priority is to tackle their unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis, which is having a serious impact on social inclusion and poverty rates. keeping people active - whether in work, training or even looking for work - is crucial both economically and socially. the text therefore proposes to review wage revision mechanisms so that they better reflect productivity, to remove legal barriers to the recognition of professional qualifications between countries, to restrict access to early retirement schemes, and to encourage the creation of enterprises.
in writing. - i welcomed the news that the two-year-long deadlock on the commission's proposal had been overcome in the council. given the urgency of providing support to the poorest sections of the european union and the delay in taking action, i voted in favour of the siekierski report in order to allow for the rapid distribution of food to the poorest citizens and finally to provide them with union support in a period of not only economic crisis but also of difficult weather conditions. i am firmly convinced that the programme must be financed entirely by the union and i believe that it is necessary to accompany the programme with transitional measures to avoid an immediate drop in food aid and to ensure that the beneficiaries of food aid do not suddenly find themselves in food poverty again. i am therefore pleased with the agreement reached, also because the food to be distributed will be of community origin, and will therefore benefit our production and growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the siekierski report, which aims to guarantee and protect the poor citizens of the european union through a financing scheme for the purchase of foodstuffs. the council has now had to vote on the proposal quickly, without any further amendments, because of the two-year deadlock in the council. in the commission's amended proposal, the programme will remain fully funded by the eu budget but, in order to ensure adequate coverage and financial stability, a ceiling of eur 500 million has been set. the programme will be operational for 2012 and 2013 but it is desirable that parliament has a greater say on the future of the programme after 2013. in the light of the economic and financial crisis which continues to worsen europe's economic situation through worrying repercussions on our social fabric, a strong european voice is needed on the issue of aid to the most vulnerable civil society.
in writing. the report follows the controversial confirmation of the european programme for the assistance of the poor. the text represents a compromise between those who were in favour of continuing the programme and those who wanted it to be closed. the compromise reached thus avoided the risk of an abrupt halt to the programme which would have endangered the survival of the part of the population which depends on this food aid. recent statistics have shown how the crisis is affecting wider and more central parts of the continent. this means that ever larger segments of the population in rich countries are at risk of poverty. in this context, the attitude of those who, in the name of useless austerity, persist in opposing measures of such importance, as well as their limited impact on the community budget, appears even more short-sighted and counterproductive. i welcome this compromise and, above all, i welcome a new agreement which also guarantees the financing of the programme for the future. however, it is hoped that the fight against food waste can be supplemented by programmes which make use of food recovered through rational distribution and use, in order to redistribute it to the most vulnerable groups and those most at risk of poverty.
in writing. - according to the most recent statistics, about 16.3% of the population of the european union lives below the poverty line. as the crisis continues, the situation is even set to worsen: it is estimated that millions of europeans could find themselves without money to eat. today's vote means that the european food aid programme will remain operational until at least 2013, providing concrete and direct support to needy citizens who do not have sufficient resources to feed themselves. i believe it is more important than ever, in the light of the worrying economic, financial and social situation, to guarantee the right to food for all europeans and to continue to ensure adequate funding for this programme, which today provides food aid to some 18 million people in 20 member states. i hope that this instrument can be improved and made more effective after 2013.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr siekierski, with which we have achieved a great result in defence of the millions of european citizens who face difficulties in their daily lives. i am pleased to note that the european parliament has played a key role in achieving this, in full compliance with the court of justice's decision, in finding a bridge solution which could unblock food aid to the poor for this year and the next, thus avoiding a dangerous cut in funds, from the current 500 million a year to the approximately 113 million envisaged by the reduction. clearly this response, which represents a success in defence of the less well-off sections of the population, was essential for us, especially in view of the period of global crisis we are experiencing. it is clear, however, that this result does not put an end to the question of financing the post-2013 programme of aid to the poor, which will see us engaged in parallel with the negotiations on the new multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. the programme for the distribution of food to the poor must be financed entirely from the eu budget. we believe it is appropriate to guarantee for the future the current rate of 100% eu funding of the programme but, in order to ensure financial stability, an annual ceiling of eur 500 million is foreseen for the union's financial contribution. we welcome the inclusion of some substantive changes proposed by the european parliament's amendments, namely: the concept of eu origin of the foodstuffs; the obligation to clearly indicate the participation of the union in the programme at the distribution points; the need for foodstuffs to be purchased through competitive procedures; the reimbursement of storage costs incurred by charitable organisations.
in writing. - i support, by my vote in favour, a procedure which can take important measures for those european citizens who live in poverty. the european institutions have a duty to provide financial support for charitable organisations which provide for the disadvantaged and needy. because of the harsh winter, there are many examples of deaths caused by the lethal combination of cold and malnutrition. in the face of such deaths, we cannot remain passive and inactive. that is why i am pleased that the council has approved some of the important amendments tabled by parliament, in particular the amendment which provides for the full financing of the distribution of foodstuffs to be borne entirely by the european institutions.
in writing. − as many colleagues underlined during the debate, the future of the programme remains uncertain beyond 2013. i therefore believe that the european parliament, together with the commission and the council, should immediately begin work on concrete proposals to continue the programme and demonstrate that europe is in solidarity with the most vulnerable citizens.

in writing. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the distribution of food to the poor in the union. once adopted, the regulation will have retroactive effect: it will apply from 1 january 2012 until the completion of the 2013 annual plan. the programme is to be financed entirely from the union budget and is to have an annual ceiling of eur 500 million. the proposal takes account of the notion of food originating in the european union, the requirement for distribution points to clearly display the eu's participation in the plan, the purchase of foodstuffs by competitive procedures and the reimbursement of storage costs incurred by charitable organisations. for our part, on behalf of the european parliament, we meps are now calling for unconditional support for the continuation of the programme beyond 2013, in view of future commission proposals on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020.
in writing. − in 2010, the european commission presented a proposal establishing the first radio spectrum policy programme and setting out policy guidelines and objectives for strategic planning and harmonisation of spectrum use up to 2015. after five informal trilogues, the eu parliament and council reached a political agreement on the legislative proposal. i welcome this political agreement, which lays the foundations for a development which will enable the european union to take the global lead in terms of speed, mobility, coverage and capacity of broadband. in my view, it will be a key element in the realisation of a flexible and coordinated european radio spectrum strategy, which will be able to meet the exponential growth of mobile data traffic. in addition, the support of member states and parliament for the commission's proposal to liberalise the 800mhz band for electronic communications services by 1 january 2013 will help to create a pan-european telecommunications market where new services can generate jobs and growth opportunities for a market of 500 million consumers.
in writing. − the proposal under consideration sets out the policy guidelines and objectives for the harmonisation of the use of radio spectrum, which today affects countless public and private services in a wide range of sectors. the regulation dealt with in this proposal lays the foundations for a development that will enable the union to take the global lead in broadband speed, coverage and capacity, with significant positive consequences in areas such as the economy, security, health, culture, science, environment and technology. for these reasons, my vote was in favour.
in writing. - i voted against this report which calls for the liberalisation of radio frequencies with a view to a new allocation of frequencies. although i am in favour of a liberalised market and the introduction of new competitors in the sector, i have serious doubts about the adaptability of the new frequencies and their distribution at european level. a roadmap on timing and modalities must be drawn up in such a way as to ensure adequate regulation of the sector, since this in particular has a direct impact on the information field, often having important repercussions on the social and economic system. i therefore believe that the objective of the digital agenda must be achieved by taking different paths and reviewing choices which, at present, do not allow the european union to significantly improve its broadcasting policy.
in writing. - my vote on mr hökmark's report is in favour. the agreement lays the foundations for a development that will enable the european union to play a global leading role in broadband speed, mobility, coverage and capacity. this is an important step towards the realisation of a flexible and coordinated european radio spectrum strategy.
in writing. − i believe it is essential that the european parliament and the council of the union agree to plan a common strategy for the use of spectrum by 2015. this will lay the foundations for the european union to become the world leader in speed, mobility, coverage and capacity of broadband. the implementation of an effective strategy for the use of radio spectrum will also help to cope with the exponential growth of mobile data traffic.
in writing. − finally, at second reading, agreement was reached on the policy guidelines and objectives for the planning and harmonisation of the use of radio spectrum. these decisions concern important sectors and services ranging from scientific activities, transport, mobile and television communications, radio and medical equipment. let us not forget how essential careful management is to the security and civil protection services. other key elements are: the deployment of wireless broadband internet in all member states and the increase of capacity by 2020 and the assessment by the commission, in consultation with the member states, to allocate a wider availability of unlicensed frequencies for wireless access systems, radio frequency local area networks and wi-fi. particular attention should be paid to the commission's unreported assumption, not mentioned in this text, that the use of european funds for broadband should be regarded as state aid rather than community aid. it is clear that such a disastrous choice would be contrary to the spirit of this provision.
in writing. − i consider the radio spectrum policy to be a crucial element in the creation of a european digital single market, especially in relation to its objective of defining policy guidelines and objectives for strategic planning and harmonisation in the use of radio spectrum, in order to ensure the functioning of the internal market. under the agreement we approved in the house this morning, eu member states should make the 800 mhz frequency band available for wireless broadband services by 1 january 2013. at least 1200 mhz of spectrum should be allocated to mobile data traffic after 2013 but before 2015, as requested by us in the european parliament. i am sure that this will create a pan-european telecommunications market where new services will be able to create opportunities and growth for a market of 500 million consumers. in this way, europe will be at the forefront of providing broadband internet to its citizens and promoting future developments of the network.
in writing. the so-called 'milk package' contains specific rules for the dairy sector concerning: the setting-up of producer organisations for the collective sale of milk; the recognition of inter-branch organisations which may carry out information and promotion activities for dairy products and provisions for the drawing up of contracts for the sale of milk raw materials. the compromise on the regulation was reached at the community's 'trilogue' last december and contains many improvements on previous proposals, accepting the requests of the italian and european dairy sector to maintain flexibility in the definition of contracts, the basic elements of which, as provided for in the commission's proposal (price, volume, delivery schedule and duration of the contract), will be freely negotiated by the parties. parliament's commitment to the negotiations has enabled the inclusion of production planning for pdo/pgi cheeses in the text of the regulation, which was not included in the european commission's initial proposal. this is an essential instrument which can be used by countries, under certain conditions, to align supply and demand of products, preventing fluctuations resulting from the formation of possible surpluses for italian long-aged pdo cheeses.
in writing. − the crisis has highlighted the lack of market orientation in the dairy sector, making it urgent to introduce rules to stabilise farmers' incomes and to improve transparency in the supply chain. the long period of fixed quotas and high institutional prices - creating guaranteed outlets - has rigidised the market: the actors in the production chain were not stimulated to respond to market signals and were not incentivised to innovate and increase productivity. however, the best way to ensure that the total abolition of quotas is achieved is to make sure that the transaction is smooth and that there is no too rigid and violent impact which could increase the risks for the sector and for producers. in this sense, the use of contracts for the delivery of raw milk, concluded in advance, between producers and dairies appears to be able to rebalance contractual powers, especially because it allows collective negotiation of the terms through farmers' organisations. the possibility - wanted by parliament - of planning and managing production volumes of certified quality dairy products (dop) is also welcomed. it is therefore essential that the urgent reform of the system does not create difficulties for producers of the best that the territory is able to export.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the milk package as the measures introduced will have a positive impact on the dairy sector, which has been in crisis since 2009. the adoption of the rules of procedure is a reward for the long work of parliament, especially during the trilogue with the commission and the council. i am also very pleased with the positive impact that today's vote will have on italy and its production of excellence: i am referring, for example, to the 37 national cheeses with a designation of origin (dop), which are even more protected by the introduction of production planning for dairy products protected by a protected designation of origin (dop) and a protected geographical indication (pgi).
in writing. the dairy sector has traditionally been considered a pride of the european food industry. unfortunately, in the last two years it has been forced to make considerable efforts in an attempt to preserve its functionality and avoid bankruptcy. with today's vote, the european union is making its contribution to trying to prevent a new crisis in this sector, with all the consequences of losing the competitiveness of small producers and losing jobs. i therefore think it necessary to approve the proposals contained in the report, in particular the maintenance of the principle of flexibility in the contracting process, a measure which will allow small producers greater flexibility in production.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal on the package of measures for the dairy sector. i would remind you that from the beginning of this parliamentary term the european parliament immediately set about finding a solution to the crisis which had been going on since 2007. the announced abolition of milk quotas in 2015 provided the impetus for the institutions to find solutions to reorganise the dairy sector to cope with such a radical change. the high level group on milk (hlg) was then set up in october 2009 and the debate on what to do was officially launched in a difficult environment of continued excessive volatility in milk prices. i fully agree with the text that has been adopted, which is in line with the issues that have long been put forward by european milk producers and other stakeholders in the sector. we are therefore moving towards strengthening the bargaining power of producers, which can be achieved through new contractual conditions which are intended to give greater responsibility to operators in the milk and milk products chain so that, taking account of market signals, they can improve price transmission, adjust supply to demand and help to avoid certain unfair commercial practices.
in writing. − the crisis in the dairy sector in europe has been acute in recent years. a substantial change will certainly occur after the abolition of milk quotas, which is planned for 2015. in order to ensure a stable future for the sector, we believe that the bargaining power of producers needs to be improved. we hope that this can be achieved by using contracts and encouraging producers to join together in producer organizations. inter-branch organisations can play a useful role in facilitating dialogue between the various actors in the supply chain and in promoting good practice and market transparency. in order to ensure the rational development of production and thus ensure a fair standard of living for milk producers, their contractual power vis-à-vis processors must be strengthened in order to ensure a more equitable distribution of added value along the supply chain. measures to improve the transparency and comprehensive analysis of milk production data in the eu should replace the relative stability achieved in the past through supply management.
in writing. - i agree particularly with the statement that there are disadvantaged regions which are heavily dependent on milk production and in relation to which the guidelines for the milk and milk products sector, as recognised by the treaties, need to be evaluated so that support for and implementation of these policies continue to be adapted to their specific characteristics. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − in recent years we have seen a number of issues affecting the dairy sector in europe: dangerous swings in demand, extreme price volatility, imbalances in the supply chain, all without forgetting the real problem that is at the root of all the industry's troubles: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. this system has proved to be profoundly wrong and unjust, and it has been particularly punitive, especially for producers: fortunately, the commission has also realised the error, albeit with a culpable delay, and the scheme will finally be abolished in 2015. the report under consideration proposes the right and necessary changes, aimed mainly at protecting the dairy producers, especially the smaller ones, and also encouraging the creation of consortia to protect excellence and quality products. for all these reasons i have therefore decided to support this proposal.
in writing. − following the crisis in the milk sector in 2008-2009 and the abolition of milk quotas from 2015, a high level group was set up to study the problems of the dairy sector. the report i voted for amends, in line with the recommendations of the high level group, the existing regulation on contractual relations in the milk and milk products sector. the contracting power of raw milk producers is strengthened and the possibility is given, through production planning, to place on the market pdo and pgi cheeses, produced in large quantities by the italian supply chain.
in writing. − given that the dairy sector will undergo a substantial change after the abolition of milk quotas in 2015, i am in favour of the use of formal written contracts which could serve to raise awareness and empower operators in the dairy supply chain to take account of market signals, improve price transmission, match supply to demand and help avoid certain unfair trading practices.
in writing. - today, at the plenary session of the european parliament in strasbourg, we voted in favour of the report by mr nicholson, which strengthens the contractual power of dairy milk producers. this legislation will allow milk producer organisations to negotiate the price for raw milk, in order to get the best possible price for their milk. producer organisations should help farmers to organise themselves better, strengthening their position in the food chain, especially in those member states where such a system is limited or non-existent. there will be more bargaining power without violating competition: in order to avoid unfair competition, the volume of raw milk will not exceed 3.5% of total eu production.

in writing. - i supported the motion for a resolution on the feasibility of introducing stability bonds in the european union. in such a crisis, the creation of a market for eurobonds, and in particular for stability bonds, could be a viable alternative to the us dollar bond market. however, member states must be held accountable and ensure the long-term stability of the euro. strict budgetary discipline and erga omnes compliance with the rules must be guaranteed. furthermore, i would like to stress that a sustainable fiscal framework is a necessary condition for joint bond issuance and must be aimed at both strengthened economic governance and economic growth in the euro area. i therefore welcome the presentation of the green paper on this subject, which i believe can provide a valuable starting point for further reflection and development on this subject, a solution which deserves careful consideration by the commission as to its impact, feasibility and effectiveness.
in writing. - i voted enthusiastically in favour of the motion for a resolution on the feasibility of introducing stability bonds, in full awareness that the extraordinary crisis we are experiencing requires the courage to implement innovative financial measures and instruments. fiscal austerity and budgetary discipline are certainly necessary and indispensable: the most destabilising factor is the fragmentation of the stock market, which is currently subject to 27 different disciplines and regulations. but if we stop here, the risk of recession is very real. at the same time, to revive the european economy, it is necessary to support growth, development and employment. i believe, as has been done today, that opening the debate on the possibility of issuing joint bonds at european level is a step we cannot avoid taking if we want to achieve a market with greater liquidity and lower interest rates. we must absolutely overcome the reservations of some people, because the debt that would be created would be used to build european infrastructure, which is the key to the revival of europe's economy and competitiveness in this globalised world, which does not allow us to be left behind.
