in writing. - like many of my colleagues, i share the responses to the public consultation received so far and i applaud the european commission for presenting the green paper on eurobonds. we have long since asked the european parliament to submit a commission analysis of the feasibility of introducing stability bonds in accordance with various options. i think that the result we have reached can be considered as a useful starting point for further reflection. according to the resolution, eurobonds could become a source of stability for the euro area in the medium term, while - as we have already discussed - other instruments will be needed to resolve short-term issues. the text calls on the commission to propose swiftly possible instruments to deal with the current crisis, such as the european debt repayment pact and joint management of sovereign debt issues. the premise for the introduction of eurobonds remains, in my view, to reduce the risk of moral hazard and to make the european system more attractive, both to the higher-rated and the more indebted countries, by increasing competitiveness and introducing compulsory debt-reduction mechanisms, together with greater fiscal coordination.
in writing. - the unemployment rate has reached 23 million people, or 10% of the working age population, not to mention the fact that 22.1% of young people are out of work. europe needs a plan of concrete and immediate measures to counter these shocking figures. following up also the conclusions of the european council of 30 january, i believe that the fight against unemployment, especially among young people, must be a priority for the union, to be countered by immediate and thorough structural reforms, targeted employment policy strategies and measures to ensure the transition between education and work and to promote the flexibility of workers. similarly, to enable the eu to gain competitiveness, it is necessary to increase labour efficiency and productivity and to provide adequate support to smes. the european economic system needs a decisive and immediate response. the future of europe rests on the ability to reverse current trends by boosting competitiveness and reaffirming confidence in the union's growth potential. for all these reasons i voted in favour of mrs cornelissen's report.
in writing. − last november, the commission presented its annual growth survey for 2012, which sets out the eu's priorities for the next 12 months in terms of reforms and fiscal, economic, employment and social policies. the recent economic and financial crisis, followed by the deterioration of sovereign debt in the european union, has highlighted the need for stronger european economic governance to prevent large budget deficits and macroeconomic imbalances from threatening the euro and the european economy. however, although fiscal consolidation is necessary in many member states, i believe that policy orientations towards a general increase in austerity measures are not compatible with the strong employment recovery that the union urgently needs. the crisis has had particularly dramatic consequences for the conditions of young people seeking stable employment. although the annual growth analysis indicates youth employment as one of the priorities, i am concerned about the quality of jobs, traineeships and apprenticeships suggested among the policy guidelines. i take this opportunity to draw the commission's attention to the need to take action to ensure that the fight against precarious work among young people becomes a key element of the policy guidelines on youth employment.
in writing. - the basic view of this report, which is that austerity measures are a very harsh medicine to be imposed on countries in serious budgetary difficulties, is shared. the problem is the proposed recipe for solving the current crisis. we are talking about greater coordination of tax policies and more intensive community action on taxation. the report also calls for the protection of the most vulnerable groups, such as immigrants from outside the eu and the roma, who are more exposed to the effects of the crisis. i do not share these views, because to overcome economic stagnation we need productive energies and freedom for our small and mediumsized enterprises, not centralistic measures on taxation and taxation. nor can we focus on categories such as immigrants, when in fact they are the first of all our young people to lose their jobs, or not to find any at all. we must think of them first, so that our production system can offer them employment and earning opportunities that are not available now. i therefore vote against the report.
in writing. - today we discussed and voted on the three cornelissen, gauzès and berès reports on the annual analysis of growth and employment, drawn up in line with the annual growth survey for 2012 proposed by the commission last november. i have supported the cornelissen report because i share its approach to the need for a profound european commitment at all levels, aimed at achieving the dual objective of economic growth and social protection. i also share the hope that this action can be pursued by acting consistently in fiscal and budgetary policies on the one hand and in social and labour policies on the other. moreover, although i do not believe in 'miracle recipes', i believe that the five 'priority actions' for 2012, identified by the commission's research and taken up by the report (tax consolidation, restoring the normal functioning of the credit market, growth and competitiveness, tackling unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis, modernisation of public administration), are the key to the economic and social development of the european union and are objectives that cannot be postponed.
in writing. - i would like to emphasize the most positive aspects of this report, which reflect well the position of the european parliament in the analysis of policies for growth and employment. it is of the utmost importance that the commission, the council and the member states take all necessary measures to ensure that the main objectives of europe 2020 in the areas of employment, education and poverty reduction are met; in particular, the level of youth unemployment in europe makes it urgent to activate specific measures and the report proposes a useful guarantee instrument for young people to ensure that they are offered jobs, traineeships and further training after a maximum period of unemployment of 4 months. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the financial interests of the european communities is a very good one. finally, it is important to strengthen the role of parliament in defining the instruments for growth, and in this sense we have a clear request to the european commission to transform the annual growth analysis into 'annual guidelines for sustainable growth' for the coming years, so that we can table amendments.
in writing. - i would like to draw attention to the problems of employment, especially youth employment. the economic and financial crisis that started in 2008 had as its main consequence the closure of many productive activities and the loss of jobs for many european citizens. for this reason, europe's recovery from the crisis and growth cannot be achieved without the objective of starting from a strong employment boost. i therefore believe it is essential to identify concrete instruments which can translate the investment effort made at european level into results, such as, for example, the granting of incentives to employment and enterprises, strong support for the training and education sector, to be combined with a new system for managing public employment. i believe that work, especially for our young people, is a key priority, both for the future of our children and to ensure that inclusion and cohesion become the guidelines for an economic policy that will lead the countries of the european union out of the crisis.
in writing. - in line with the growth plans which put employment, competitiveness and the search for a solution to fiscal and financial policy at the centre of the debate, i voted in favour of mrs cornelissen's report. the labour market must be at the heart of the new european policies, and the risk of moving away from the european economic union as envisaged up to a decade ago is high. the fight against unemployment, employment, precarity and youth employment are the main objectives of the 2012 annual growth survey. these topics go hand in hand with fiscal policies and the economic crisis, but are therefore likely to be sidelined as a result of their dependence on them.
in writing. − given that unemployment has increased significantly since 2008 and has reached 23 million unemployed in the eu, and given that the labour market situation is particularly difficult for young people, i am in favour of integrating sustainable job creation through investment and tax reforms into the political guidelines for the 2012 european semester; to improve the quality of employment and the conditions for greater participation in work; addressing youth unemployment, poverty and social exclusion by focusing on groups with little or no link to the labour market.
in writing. the measure is intended, as a shared objective, to denounce the social burden of the 'austerity measures'. in order to boost economic growth, the report aims to increase employment levels, particularly in support of young people and women, and stresses the need to overcome the increasingly widespread forms of precarious work. the rediscovery of traditional trades should be promoted in order to redistribute the labour force fairly, reduce the import of non-community labour and reduce the unemployment rate. the text, rather than dealing with the rights of community citizens as it should, emphasises the need to protect the rights of immigrants by promoting the social inclusion of roma. that is why i am voting against.
in writing. − the current international economic crisis has had a serious impact on many member states. we are talking about the cutting of jobs in the private and public sectors, the reduction in spending on social benefits and public services, and the worsening of poverty in the european union. this vote will give a boost to key issues for the future of europe. consistency and greater ambition are needed to achieve the europe 2020 strategy objectives, to support sustainable job creation through investment and tax reforms, and to improve the quality of employment and conditions for greater participation in work. at the same time, we must support and help the young generations who represent the future of europe, by seeking to reduce youth unemployment and investing more resources in education and training.
in writing. the european union is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy, which is based on the principles of the treaty of rome and the treaty of rome. the efforts of the member states and the community institutions must therefore be directed towards profound reforms in the areas of fiscal policy, financial sector stabilisation, growth and competitiveness, the employment and social consequences of the crisis and public administration.
in writing. − the presentation of the annual growth survey for 2012, as presented by the commission, lays a good foundation for the european semester. priority must be given to tackling unemployment, fiscal consolidation and the promotion of sustainable growth through increased competitiveness and investment, and to modernising the public administrations of the european union. immediate action is needed to support economic activity and employment in the medium term: to reach the eu 2020 targets, at least 17.6 million people will need to find a job. member states must do their utmost to correct their deficits within the time limits set by the council and bring them to a sustainable level. many areas require deep structural reforms, such as labour, pensions, social assistance and the fight against tax evasion. these reforms will have to be carried out through a coordinated approach, but also adapted to the specific needs of the member states. finally, i would like to stress that in the formulation of the broad economic policy guidelines and the ags, parliament should be given a leading role, through a codecision procedure, and not just a consultative role.
in writing. - the report in question is, in my view, a compilation of what has already been said and widely discussed and dealt with in other reports. the need for general or specific measures to restart the engine of growth in europe is recalled, some of which are certainly acceptable, others of doubtful utility or effectiveness. the problem is that the crisis is not being tackled from a different and innovative perspective than has been done so far by this europe, which, on the contrary, believes that a greater degree of centralism, 'more europe', can provide the solution to the current problems. the report does not address the prospect, which i would call appropriate, of a reduction in the community's powers, in order to give more freedom and space to the productive forces of enterprise and to small and mediumsized businesses which are the real engine of the continent. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i therefore abstained from voting on this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr gauzès. each year, the annual growth survey helps to define the budgetary priorities of the european union. in the light of this, member states must vigorously implement the economic policies to which they have committed themselves, measures which must aim at reducing debt and restoring competitiveness and a sustainable economy capable of creating jobs. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a welcome step towards the creation of a european company. investment should also focus in particular on research, education and innovation and support smes, which are the real pillars of long-term sustainable growth. finally, i think that it is useful to strengthen the coordination of macroeconomic policies and structural reforms in individual countries.
in writing. - today we discussed and voted on the three cornelissen, gauzès and berès reports on the annual analysis of growth and employment, drawn up in line with the annual growth survey for 2012 proposed by the commission last november. i have supported the gauzès report because i believe that the highlights of the work of the econ committee in drawing up its report are broadly shared. i refer in particular to the emphasis on the need to respond to economic challenges through concerted macroeconomic strategies; the need to pursue growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, differentiated from one member state to another according to the needs and characteristics of individuals; the need to guarantee long-term financing for the real economy and smes; the need to promote sustainable growth, education, research and innovation through more competitive financing and investment; the need to combat unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis; the need to modernise the eu's public administration and services of general interest. we must be concrete, creating jobs with a plan for investment in infrastructure of european interest based on the issuing of debt by the eu.
in writing. - in adopting this report and the corresponding one drawn up by the empl committee, parliament has taken very clear positions vis-à-vis the commission and the council on the policies which, in a way that is now unavoidable, must be put in place to promote growth and employment. too many member states have lost sight of the main objectives of europe 2020 in terms of employment, education and poverty reduction, focusing only on the sovereign debt crisis and lacking the awareness that only medium- and long-term measures that can promote growth, such as those in education, research, innovation and energy, can respond to the difficult phase that the union has been going through for too long. the call for the introduction of project bonds to finance key infrastructure projects, as well as the call in the empl report for the introduction of a financial transaction tax, provide useful and no longer deferred proposals which this parliament is prepared to support. finally, the proposal to make the annual growth survey subject to a codecision procedure does justice to the key role that parliament can play in the debate on the future of european growth and in the definition of development policies.
in writing. the report voted on today has the merit of bringing the community's discussion on growth issues to the fore. as we know, the last two years have been marked by the economic and financial crisis, which has been the main theme of all political discourse. the objective of the member states has long been to fill the wounds caused by the crisis and, with the agreement adopted at the end of 2011, a common european response on the correction of public accounts has finally been reached. however, this cannot be enough to get the economy back on track: in my view, measures must be taken to enable small and mediumsized enterprises to benefit from european funding, to redefine the labour market by increasing the flexibility and mobility of workers, and to encourage enterprises to maintain current employment rates. the report we have voted on today is therefore an important step forward for the european union: priority is given to growth-friendly policies, to be achieved through action in the fields of education, research, innovation, infrastructure and energy, areas where the european union cannot afford not to be competitive with the rest of the world.
in writing. − i think it is necessary to emphasise some aspects in particular which can really contribute to the annual growth analysis for 2012. it is a text which, looking back at the year we have just begun, sets out the guidelines for an economic, social, political and financial budget. growth is the keyword of the european union's policy, the objective we must aim at to revive our struggling economy. we are aware of the need to act decisively and concretely in this direction and i am therefore very pleased with the recent statements made by both the council and the commission, statements which are in full line with what we have stated since the beginning of the year in preparing the guidelines for the 2013 budget. in this planning context, i consider the annual growth analysis for 2012, which has been approved today, to be important, and the study of which is, in fact, the starting point for this year's work.
in writing. − we believe that the solutions envisaged for the current financial and sovereign debt crisis in the annual review presented by the commission should be accompanied by a greater focus on medium and long-term measures to boost growth, as well as a reorganisation of the overall economic framework, in order to improve the sustainability and competitiveness of the european economy and ensure its lasting success. the democratic legitimacy and national ownership of the changes that have been decided on in relation to future economic governance must be substantially increased. we have an opportunity today to strengthen the role of the european parliament in defining and implementing the procedures for monitoring economic policies in the context of the european semester, in accordance with the provisions of articles 121 and 136 of the treaty. finally, we are in favour of the creation of project bonds to help finance key infrastructure projects in order to promote sustainable growth and employment.

call on the european parliament to intervene to support the signing of a binding international treaty to guarantee blind, partially sighted and hard-of-hearing people free access to books in large-print braille and audio formats, produced in all countries and protected by copyright. only 5% of publications are currently available to this group of citizens. the request follows the position expressed first by the commission and then by the council against the possibility of signing this treaty. both european institutions have proposed agreements between interested parties in the european union, or simple recommendations on a voluntary basis, within the framework of the world intellectual property organization. this is certainly a weak hypothesis, which does not protect the right of a significant proportion of european citizens not to be marginalised. the severe restriction on free access to all publications has significant cultural implications, undeniable social consequences and, what is more, a negative impact on the intellectual recovery and the growth of the level of emancipation and independence of these citizens. important scientific studies have shown that, through the use of braille, even and especially if learned from an early age, the blind person can develop his expressive and communicative abilities for the formation of his personality. allowing more flexible copyright rules for works for the blind and partially sighted therefore means meeting the needs of an otherwise heavily discriminated group. the will expressed by the commission and the council seems to be contrary to the strategy for the disabled for 2010-2020 and does not take account of the indications contained in the report entitled 'cultural and creative industries: a potential to be exploited' which parliament voted in this house in may last year, in defiance of the prerogatives which are also protected by the treaties of this parliament. furthermore, it does not respect the principles enshrined in the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and in the charter of fundamental rights of the union. it is difficult to understand why the commission should change its position on such a sensitive subject. many of the treaties to which the european union is a party deal with the regulation of intellectual property rights. a proposal for a treaty on this subject is currently being discussed before the copyright committee of the world intellectual property organization. it is on this point that we are calling for a review of the position expressed by the commission and the council, because we are celebrating today how these two institutions can discuss, at one table, a european anti-discrimination framework. the economic reasons for this can be discussed and a compromise can always be found. the fundamental principle must always be that economic considerations must never take precedence over the protection of fundamental rights. it is on this point that the committee i chair has decided to put a question to the institutions concerned, seeking to make the position of the commission and the council more appropriate, more coherent, more just than that which this parliament has already expressed recently.

mr president, during the economic and financial crisis it became clear that the individual national deposit guarantee schemes in europe were experiencing problems in a number of cases. in addition to increasing depositors' distrust, the consequences of a bank's insolvency were borne by the state and, ultimately, by the taxpayers. i therefore believe that it is right to adopt measures to achieve a much better protection of depositors which, taking into account the differences in the various european banking markets, can establish common requirements for all deposit guarantee schemes, firstly the respect of the right to be protected up to eur 100 000 and the short deadline for the payment of deposits in the event of repayment.
in writing. - mr simon's report brings to parliament an important legislative dossier, which covers some important aspects of bank deposits and the bank guarantee on them. the current financial crisis has created a climate of understandable distrust of banks and financial institutions, to the extent that the commission considered in 2010 to revert once again to previous directives governing this matter, given the delicate situation many banks are experiencing as a result of the financial turmoil. the proposal is intended to amend and replace old directives by introducing uniform rules for the protection and guarantee of bank deposits. this directive will introduce uniform criteria to restore the minimum level of confidence that citizens and businesses have in banks, which is now at an all-time low. my vote is in favour of the report.
in writing. the position expressed by parliament is broadly shared. one of the priorities must be to prevent future demands on deposit guarantee schemes. for this reason, preventive action and surveillance must be put into practice. it is also necessary to ensure a coordinated and transparent assessment of the business models of old and new operators, based on a common approach agreed with the european supervisory authority. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i wanted to express my vote in favour of this report, since it is especially in times of crisis and economic recession that savers must be best protected against the risks of bank insolvency. in such cases, there is a risk of a dangerous race to the bottom, with destabilizing effects on the whole credit system. this text lays the foundations for a common system of bank deposit guarantees valid throughout europe, in such a way as to avoid the risk of possible market distortions. the proposed threshold of eur 100 000 seems appropriate to me, as does the need for a rapid timetable for any repayments. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - unfortunately, no agreement was reached at the trilogue, so today we voted on the text approved last july in the econ committee at first reading, paving the way for second reading. that text is partly acceptable, but i think that other aspects, such as the contribution threshold and the repayment periods, need to be improved. i hope that the commission will present a balanced text at the second reading. the text, as voted by the econ committee, contains criticisms of the italian system, which has been maintained during the recent crisis, both as regards the financing system and the methods of financing the fund. i therefore voted in favour of the four amendments tabled by mr ford (ecr), which leave the member states discretion as to the methods and system of financing the gbs.
in writing. − banks are special financial intermediaries because they finance themselves through deposits, which are redemptable on demand and without loss. the longer maturity of bank assets makes it difficult to repay deposits in the event of a sudden and simultaneous withdrawal request from depositors. the 'race to the top' can spread to other banks and undermine the stability not only of the banking system but also of the whole economy. to prevent this risk, a growing number of countries have set up deposit guarantee schemes, following the example of the united states. deposit insurance has proven effective in preventing bank panics but weakens market discipline on management and shareholders and creates moral hazard. the commission considers that the measures in question are imputable to the state and that the measures in question are imputable to the state. the lack of attention of depositors may encourage the bank to choose riskier uses, as it will keep the profits but any losses will be borne by the deposit guarantee fund and, if this is not enough, by the taxpayers. i hope that the adoption of the text voted on this morning will achieve the objectives of homogenisation with a one-size-fits-all approach.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr vaughan's report setting out the guidelines for the 2013 budget because i share many of the points it makes. at a time of severe economic crisis, when member states and local authorities are demanding sacrifices, sometimes heavy ones, from their citizens, i believe that the european union must do its part and set an example in controlling public spending. i fully support the call for structural and organisational reforms to be continued in order to contain and reduce the costs of running parliament, also in view of the increased expenditure that full integration of croatia will entail next year. certain proposals in the report, such as the freezing of travel budget lines and the suspension of the indexation of members' allowances, will certainly need to be considered and carefully evaluated. i also think that the controversial issue of the double seat of parliament, which forces us to make an expensive trip every month, should be addressed. in the light of these findings, however, i think it is important to ensure that any discussion does not slip into populist and demagogic drifts, which would damage the image of the union without making a real contribution to saving.
in writing. - it is entirely acceptable that, in the face of continuing economic difficulties, the institutions should set an example of austerity and rigour, first by freezing their own administrative budgets. it is an effective, as well as a practical, way of being credible in relation to the sacrifices we are asking our fellow citizens to make every day. the achievement of savings by strengthening interinstitutional cooperation, sharing best practice between institutions and modernising human resources, technology and environmental policies can and must become a strategic objective for the community institutions. the opportunity of this vote, however, allows us to reiterate once again and more forcefully that - the need for drastic action to cut unproductive expenditure - must be countered by the need to multiply efforts to free up and make available as many resources as possible to get the global economy moving again as soon as possible and to give hope to those who today easily give in to populist anti-european sirens. the assessment of the institutions which govern them by the citizens of europe will depend on their ability to be sensitive to the needs and difficulties of the present situation and, even more importantly, on their ability to devise appropriate policies to get out of the crisis as quickly as possible.
in writing. - i believe it is of paramount importance, especially in the current austerity climate, to continue to demonstrate that the european institutions are acting responsibly, making real savings and respecting appropriate budgetary rigor. for these reasons, my vote was in favour.
in writing. − the rapporteur is right to point out the substantial savings achieved in the 2012 budget through structural changes and reorganisation. so, in addition to encouraging the continuation of structural reforms, it is good to start thinking about saving in the long term. my vote is in favour.

in writing. − in a context of continuing economic difficulties, i believe it is essential for the institutions to strengthen interinstitutional cooperation, making considerable savings also through structural changes and internal reorganisation. today more than ever budgetary discipline must be strict, especially by all the international institutions, which are called upon to be particularly vigilant against any kind of waste and mismanagement.
in writing. − i welcome the fact that in the text of the report on the 2013 budget other sections, a specific reference is made in one paragraph to the progress of croatia's accession, to be taken into account when the budget for the coming year is established. after a long process of rapprochement with the european chapters, croatia will become a full member of the union on 1 july 2013, when all 27 current eu member states and croatia have ratified the accession treaty. already earlier this year, the country held a referendum on membership. during the ratification period, croatia will, however, continue to make progress in implementing the treaty and the commission will monitor the progress made. until accession, croatia will participate as an observer, without the right to speak, in most council groups and council sessions and in meetings of the european council and in commission committees. this will enable croatian representatives to become familiar with the working methods of the eu institutions and to participate in the decision-making process. i therefore welcome this budgetary orientation for next year and hope that it will be retained in the final text.
in writing. - any fish can be processed into flour and oil. however, the target species of industrial fisheries are generally those not intended for human consumption and therefore of low commercial value. these are small-sized species, mainly cod, norway lobster, sprat and watermelon, but other medium-sized species are also caught, such as the sugarcat, which we are discussing today in the house. industrial fishing is fishing activity the production of which is used for purposes other than human consumption. the european union is also concerned about taking measures to reduce by-catches of species such as haddock and whiting for human consumption. the bulk of the production is carried out in an industrial process which, after grinding, cooking and pressing the product, separates solids from liquids: the solid material is crushed and turned into flour, while the liquid material is treated for the extraction of fish oil. as cod is the main stock of fish for this use throughout the european union, i think it is appropriate that, for sustainable exploitation and maximum long-term yield, we should once again be concerned here in parliament with maintaining a strategic sector for many european locations.
in writing. − the fisheries sector makes a major contribution to europe's economic growth, not only because of its main activity, which places it fourth in the world in terms of production, supplying 6.4 million tonnes of fish per year. it is therefore right to ask the commission to take a holistic approach to the sector, particularly with regard to the reform of the cfp, rejecting reductionist perspectives, which not only undermine the direct and indirect benefits of the sector but also ignore the wider range of benefits it offers. my vote on the joint resolution is in favour.
in writing. - i believe that the contribution of the european fisheries sector to europe's economic growth is crucial, not only because of its main activity, which places it fourth in the world in terms of production, but also because of its contribution in other sectors. fisheries now represent an economic and social added value, contributing to the food security and self-sufficiency of the european union on the one hand, and to the development of several regions of europe that are highly dependent on it, in particular by providing jobs for more than 350 000 people. the multi-purpose nature of the fisheries sector and its production of public goods ensures social and territorial cohesion and promotes vocational training and socio-economic dynamism. finally, due account should be taken of the full integration of the fisheries sector into the europe 2020 strategy, recognising this common policy as a development engine in the context of the european growth project.
in writing. - a survey by scientific experts of over 54% of mediterranean fish stocks shows that these resources are being overexploited. the mediterranean regulation, which aims to improve fisheries management in order to achieve sustainable fishing, protect the delicate balance of the marine environment and bring fish stocks back to safe levels, came fully into force on 1 june. but it is not reasonable to think that regulations or the european union can alone ensure the management of fisheries in the mediterranean. the participation of all mediterranean countries, including my own, is crucial, and the eu is actively working within multilateral organisations, including the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean and the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas, to improve scientific knowledge and ensure a level playing field for promoting sustainability. at the same time, it is essential to preserve local fishing traditions and coastal habitats in order to maintain the long-established population, which often lives off the fishery itself as their only resource. i therefore call on the european decisions to take account of both aspects: sustainability and local development.

in writing. - the agricultural liberalisation agreement, as it has been conceived, would have a worrying economic impact on european farmers, especially in the fruit and vegetable sector, with dramatic repercussions on employment in rural areas of the european union. for example, if 55% of european imports from morocco were immediately liberalised, many fruit and vegetable products typical of italian territory would be threatened by the entry into the european market of products obtained under more competitive conditions. we must take into account that moroccan farmers not only face production and labour costs that are far below those in the eu, but they are not even required to meet the same production standards in terms of environmental and food safety. it is therefore appropriate to carry out an impact study on the possible economic and social consequences of such liberalization before it is implemented. i hope, therefore, that there will be a willingness to proceed with a revision of the proposed agreement which safeguards the principle of reciprocity and the possibility for our farmers to compete in a competitive situation which is, if not equal, certainly sustainable.

in writing. - this agreement best sums up the european union's unfortunate and self-destructive trade policy. with today's approval we shall be witnessing a real invasion of moroccan agricultural products, which will risk dealing the final blow to many of our country's fruit and vegetable excellences. it is absolutely impossible to compete with a country like morocco, where the cost of labour is much lower and where children are often employed. i wonder what the european union can gain from this agreement: the only beneficiaries will be the large multinational farming companies which have already relocated or will soon do so. i do not think that there will be any great benefit for the simple moroccan farmers, nor for the thousands of small and mediumsized farmers in the southern european countries, for whom the consequences would be devastating. i voted against this proposal, but unfortunately the usual european commercial logic has prevailed today. i can 't imagine where this is going to take us . the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - i voted against the eu-morocco agreement on the liberalization of agricultural products and fisheries, as did the italian delegation of the epp. the italian position is against ratification of the agreement because it is against the interests of european producers in the mediterranean countries, in particular farmers and fishermen in the southern regions of italy. in particular, such an agreement, although broad in scope in view of the opening up to the countries of north africa, would create major problems for all those small private individuals who risk losing their competitiveness on the market for agricultural and fishery products. i would stress, however, that my vote against the agreement is not a vote to close it, but to open it up in defence of the european market, and that is why i am proposing, together with my italian colleagues, an agreement with gradual liberalization in each sector in order to reduce the possible negative effects of the agreement.
in writing. the agreement between the european union and morocco on reciprocal liberalisation measures only affects one sector: the european one. the same committee on agriculture of the european parliament has expressed a different opinion because so many fruits and vegetables will be able to enter europe freely from morocco, paying less tax than ours. europe will suffer a loss of eur 21 million if the duties on agricultural and fishery products from morocco are reduced or eliminated. this amount will only increase because imports, no longer being taxed, will increase exponentially, exposing european producers to unsustainable unfair competition. the agricultural workers in morocco earn 5 euros a day and it is therefore obviously unthinkable for our producers to compete with similar costs. for these reasons, i voted strongly against it, because i have always supported zero-mile products for the sake of quality and the good of consumers.
in writing. since march 2011, when peaceful protests were suppressed by the army, more than 4,000 people have been killed and 14,000 have been imprisoned for political reasons. not only that, but at least 400 children lost their lives, and some 380 others were arbitrarily arrested and beaten to death. according to the un report on the syrian arab republic of 23 november 2011, the syrian armed forces subject children to physical and psychological torture, even leading to death, and horrific sexual violence, either in person or indirectly involving them as witnesses. the vice president, are you aware of this? what measures will you take to prevent further torture and sexual violence against innocent children and to put an end to violations of human rights, respect for human dignity and the integrity of freedom?
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i value its aim to express our deepest concern at the gravity of the human rights violations perpetrated by the syrian authorities. mass arrests, extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detention, enforced disappearances, torture and ill-treatment of detainees must end. the first step to be taken by the european union is to draw up a black list of companies that deliver arms to syria. all eu actors must fully respect the european union code of conduct on arms exports. it is of fundamental importance to repeat that for the international community the syrian regime has lost all its credibility and legitimacy and that president bashar al-assad must step aside immediately, so as allow a peaceful and democratic transition to take place in syria.
in writing. the resolution condemns in the strongest terms, as in the past, the abominable use of violence by the syrian regime to suppress the bloodshed of the population. i share the call of our assembly for assad to leave with his ruthless government, to give the syrian people a chance to have a different future, despite the concern that syria may fall into the hands of other brutal political figures. we condemn with this resolution the russian and chinese vetoes at the un, which have prevented a faster solution to the syrian crisis, and rightly call on russia, the main arms supplier to the assad regime, to immediately cease the sale of military supplies to damascus. my vote on the resolution, which is broadly shared, is in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the situation in syria because i share the concerns expressed about the serious acts of repression which have been taking place in that country for many months. demonstrations by those calling for reforms to further democratize syria are constantly and brutally suppressed by the armed forces, which on government orders respond with torture, mass killings, and the bombing of towns and villages, as reported by un reports. i join the call on the syrian government to cease all violence against civilians, and to respect human rights and fundamental freedoms which have been denied for too long. i also support the call for the european union to make greater efforts in the international arena to defend the oppressed syrian people, so as to ensure a common position within the united nations assembly and in particular the security council.
in writing. - the situation in syria is becoming increasingly serious. since march 2011, when the violent crackdown on peaceful protesters began, the systematic killing, violence and torture have escalated dramatically, and the syrian army and security forces continue to respond with targeted killings, torture and mass arrests. according to united nations estimates, over 5,000 people have lost their lives. immediate, independent and transparent investigations into these widespread violations must be carried out to ensure that all those responsible for these acts are held accountable before the international community.
in writing. - for too many months now, we have been watching impotently all kinds of violence in syria; the ruling regime has dramatically lost much of its support within the country, and is therefore reacting with the typical methods of those who are at the end of an era of absolute power and who do not want to accept the reality of the facts. in these situations it is always desirable to find a political solution to the matter: the european parliament has been very active in the fight against terrorism, and it has been very active in the fight against terrorism. the middle east has always been a very critical area, and instability in one country can have negative repercussions for the whole region. we must therefore act as soon as possible to try to resolve the situation: i think that the european parliament has done well to express itself in these terms today, and that is why i supported the joint resolution.
in writing. the resolution adopted by the european parliament on the situation in syria shows us the reality of events in a country which, because of the power cravings of its 'dictator', is in danger of falling into a full-blown civil war. in addition to the eu, which is ready to recall all accredited ambassadors in syria and freeze diplomatic contacts with syrian ambassadors in member states, the king of jordan and turkey have also called on assad to step back. i hope that the international appeal will reach russia, in the hope that it will stop selling arms to syria. russia together with china should give up its veto on the resolution presented by the un security council to unblock the syrian dossier.
in writing. − in the light of the continuing deterioration of the situation in syria, the eu's efforts to increase pressure on the assad regime and to try to relaunch the diplomatic initiative, in conjunction with the arab league, following the security council veto, continue. the eu has been saying since 18 august that assad has lost all legitimacy and must step aside, a position which has been repeatedly reiterated by us in the european parliament. the list of persons subject to restrictive measures was extended in november, and again on 23 january, by the foreign affairs council (now comprising 108 individuals and 38 entities), in parallel with the suspension of eib loans to syria. sanctions in the oil and investment sectors were adopted in september and strengthened on 1 december, with measures also added on telephone and internet interception equipment. the further extension of the eu sanctions package is currently under consideration, with the impact on the civilian population to be minimised. we hope that the repression will lead to the rediscovery of democracy in the country.
in writing. the european union cannot remain indifferent to the violations of human rights and civil liberties in countries which have recently achieved democratic emancipation. the union promotes respect for fundamental rights and democracy in the world and is legally bound to respect them by the eu charter of fundamental rights. it must therefore work to ensure that the protection of these rights is a priority in the activities of the united nations and therefore provide full support for the actions undertaken in this regard. i welcome the work of the un human rights council and hope that the next meeting of the council will conclude with further progress in this area. i hope above all that the deadlock that has developed within the security council over the situation in syria will be overcome soon. unacceptable human rights violations are taking place and the international community cannot remain silent. thousands of prisoners are subjected to torture and sexual violence every day, including some 400 children. we cannot allow such violence to continue or to be repeated.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because it stresses parliament’s strong support for the eu’s active participation in the work of the un human rights council and the importance of holding common positions on the key issues that will be discussed during the 19th session of the council. it is fundamental to underline that, with regard to human rights issues, all international actors must work for the elimination of double standards and for the avoidance of selectivity and politicisation. for these reasons, with this resolution we express our concerns regarding the persistence of the practice of ‘bloc politics’ which continue to affect the selection of the countries receiving the unhrc’s attention. this practice indeed is having a negative impact on its authority and credibility. in view of this i also believe in the necessity, for the eu and its member states, to ensure that human rights are fully respected in internal policies, in order to increase consistency between internal and external policies and to enhance their moral authority on the international scene.
in writing. − respect for, promotion of and safeguarding the universality of human rights are an integral part of the european union's ethical and legal acquis and constitute one of the cornerstones of european unity and integrity. the ongoing review of the eu's human rights policy should therefore help to make its foreign policy a more active, coherent and effective force in the world. in this context, i agree with the eu priorities for the 19th session of the human rights council. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - during the 19th session of the human rights council in geneva, direct accusations were made against syrian president bashar al-assad. the un high commissioner for human rights, navi pillay, has spoken clearly about indiscriminate attacks on the civilian population. she said she was particularly struck by the continuing carnage in homs. since 3 february, in a continuous wave of attacks, the government has used tanks, mortars, rockets and artillery to strike the city of homs. the eu is also calling for the immediate release of all political prisoners and for the immediate release of all political prisoners. since we intend to intensify diplomatic pressure on the regime and against assad's campaign of violence, i would not be surprised if there were tougher decisions on targeted sanctions and perhaps the very occasion of this human rights council could bring the international community together to condemn the actions of the assad regime. i would like to conclude by pointing out that the report we have been examining this morning makes no reference to the assad regime.
in writing. − the european union has adopted the european disability strategy 2010-2020 with the aim of promoting and achieving the social integration of disabled people into society and ensuring their full enjoyment of rights. i am convinced that to this end it is advisable to reach a binding treaty within the world intellectual property organization (wipo) that strikes the right balance between respect for copyright and the enjoyment of rights by people with disabilities. i therefore join the questions put by mrs mazzoni on behalf of the peti committee: does the commission really believe that its initiatives are consistent with parliament's wishes for a binding treaty within the wipo framework, as called for in the report 'cultural and creative industries, a potential to be exploited'? does it therefore consider that european law is in conformity with the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, in particular on the basis of articles 21 and 30, and with the obligations laid down in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union regarding the fight against discrimination against persons with disabilities?
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on access for visually impaired people to printed products and books, as i believe that member states should change their international behaviour in this area. europe must urge states to do all they can to achieve the signing of an international treaty at wipo that is binding on the parties, and that finally allows for greater distribution and dissemination of bibliographic material translated into languages or printed in ways that are understandable to the blind and visually impaired. until now, the states have opted for the possibility of signing a non-binding treaty, but a change of perspective is necessary, otherwise the objective, which is nothing but the implementation of already existing international conventional standards on the rights of the disabled, will never be achieved.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution proposed by mr mazzoni on the basis of petition 0924/2011 because it refers to a problem which is widespread throughout the eu, namely the limit imposed on blind people in accessing books and other printed products. at present, due to restrictions imposed to protect intellectual property, only 5% of publications are available in braille, large print, audio and electronic formats. blind, partially sighted and reading-impaired people are denied access to a great many works and are thus discriminated against by other citizens. i believe that culture is a value that cannot be put on the back burner. i also firmly believe that reading is a right of all citizens, and that this activity that enriches each of us and our society cannot be denied to those citizens who cannot read in the traditional way. i believe that the technological development and the possibilities offered by new technologies must be made available to the public for the benefit of the citizens. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to provide a solution to a problem which affects almost all blind people. and just think that as much as 95% of the works, to date, are not converted into braille or into formats suitable for use by people who are visually impaired or blind. the failure to reduce this percentage has been compounded, so far, by the difficulty of finding an international treaty that can reconcile the transmission of content for the visually impaired and the blind with respect for copyright. in the spirit of solidarity and cooperation in breaking down barriers for disabled people, we must raise the threshold for blind people to have access to publications and mark the crucial milestone in ensuring equal access to culture for all.
in writing. − given the limited access to books for blind people in the european union, i support supporting a binding wipo treaty on copyright in books and printed matter for blind and partially sighted people. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − access to books and other printed products for blind and partially sighted people in the european union is severely limited, with 95% of all published works never being converted into 'accessible formats'. in the absence of international legal rules providing for a specific exception to copyright rules for the crossborder distribution of formats adapted for the benefit of individuals with reading disabilities, the copyright committee of the world intellectual property organization (wipo) is considering an international treaty to improve access for persons with such disabilities. so far, no legally binding text has been adopted at european level, favouring non-binding recommendations instead. i therefore welcome the european parliament's call on the council of the european union and the european commission to support a binding wipo treaty on copyright in books and printed matter for blind and partially sighted people.
in writing. the motion for a resolution voted today stems from a petition by a european citizen - in this case the british - who was the first to call for greater guarantees on access for blind people to books and other printed matter. the world blind union and the european union of the blind have already proposed an internationally binding treaty within the world intellectual property organization providing for a specific exception to copyright. whereas in the european union, access to books and other printed products for blind and partially sighted people is severely restricted as much as 95% of all published works are never converted into 'accessible formats'. it is time to speed up the pace of the process of ensuring that the blind have access to all the cultural offerings available in europe.
in writing. − the adoption of this report is necessary for the entry into force of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean rules of origin. the convention contains rules which in future would govern the matter of preferential origins in products packaged in the countries party to the convention, namely eu, efta, north african and eastern european and balkan countries party to the stabilisation and association policy. such a convention, which contains rules which are potentially harmful or misleading for our quality products, does not bring any particular benefits to our production, whereas it is of great benefit to the countries of north africa. in addition, there is no guarantee that the regulations are being properly applied in the southern mediterranean, nor is there sufficient guarantee of administrative cooperation and the correct issuing of certificates of origin in those countries. the convention also does not provide for mechanisms for settling disputes or for clauses for reviewing or revising the text of the convention. i therefore vote against.
in writing. - the regional convention on preferential rules of origin, while presenting a precise and well-detailed system of rules, contains within itself some critical aspects which i believe should not be underestimated. the text does not contain any system of guarantees to ensure that the competent authorities of the north african states involved in the agreement comply with the rules, nor does it provide for mechanisms for settling disputes. the total absence of any review or revision clauses in the convention is also noted. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. - in line with the barcelona process, the convention we voted on today is intended to anticipate the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area, which will also define the pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin, which have hitherto been the subject of specific trade agreements. the adoption of a single and simplified instrument will make it possible to facilitate the use of the pan-euro-mediterranean system of cumulation of origin. the adoption of this new legal instrument will certainly provide a potential incentive to increase south-south trade and contribute to economic growth, economic diversification, poverty reduction and democratisation in the region, as well as to promoting social, commercial and economic integration between the countries of the southern shore of the mediterranean. this single instrument will have the advantage of including not only the traditional southern mediterranean countries but also the participants in the stabilisation and association process and the efta states, thus creating a wider geographical area of cumulation and a wider outlet for cumulated exports. we are aware, however, that the conclusion of this convention must necessarily be followed and consolidated by other more ambitious projects aimed at improving and promoting trade in the region.
in writing. - i voted with conviction in favour of the resolution on the future of the gmes programme because i share the concerns about the survival and continuation of this project. gmes is one of the two flagship initiatives of the union in the space sector and is of key political, strategic and technological importance in monitoring climate change, preventing environmental disasters, managing emergencies and organising mobility and energy exchange. it therefore leaves the commission's decision to exclude gmes from the multiannual financial framework and its proposal to finance it through intergovernmental agreements in doubt. although many governments in the council have already expressed their support for the programme, the risk that opposition from certain countries could wreck it and make all the efforts and investments made to date worthless cannot be totally ruled out. it would also be detrimental to the exclusion of parliament from the decision-making process and therefore to the absence of democratic participation. i hope that the commission will reconsider its position and decide to heed parliament's call for the reintroduction of gmes within the multiannual financial framework. i personally believe that this can be achieved through the use of a public-private partnership to maximise the investment of the community budget, as has been done for the sesar project.
in writing. - the importance of the gmes programme has been repeatedly stressed in numerous and heated parliamentary debates. its role is crucial in ensuring europe's independent access to earth observation information. we must not forget that accurate and timely information about our planet is essential to ensure safety, to alert citizens to disasters or to simple air quality deterioration and to mitigate the effects of climate change. gmes provides the necessary geospatial data, ensuring its full reliability and verifiability, through harmonisation and comparison at european level, it is therefore necessary to ensure that this important programme receives adequate long-term financial support to prevent any discontinuity in the receipt of data and, ultimately, a dependence on space infrastructure of third countries to the detriment of european industries linked to the sector. i hope that the european commission will present as soon as possible a new legislative proposal for the governance, funding and operation of the gmes programme with the aim of ensuring its full and effective operation from 2014.
in writing. − i am pleased to have contributed to the adoption of the text on the future of the gmes programme. we have been discussing the financing of this rather controversial programme for some time in the committee on budgets. i believe that financing gmes outside the multiannual financial framework (mff), as proposed in its communication by the european commission, is not a feasible option, as also stated in one paragraph of the text. while i understand that the gmes programme is one of the initiatives on which there is a large investment by the european union and that the programme plays a key role in earth observation, i would simply stress the fear that funding for gmes could subtract important investments from other budget lines.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the fukushima tragedy has shown that there is still no absolute safety of nuclear power stations after chernobyl. it is true that the cases are very different: as regards chernobyl, it was an internal accident at the plant; as for fukushima, the causes were external, an earthquake and a tsunami of unprecedented intensity among the highest that have occurred, at least from what is known from the history of the planet. this, however, raises serious doubts about the safety of nuclear energy. i am not one of those who say that, in view of the accidents, we must absolutely abandon nuclear power, even though in many countries this seems to be the way forward, but in any case a thorough reflection must necessarily be developed, taking into account, as has been repeatedly said, that the responsibilities are those of the national states but parliament must also have a say. and i would like to conclude by expressing my condolences and solidarity with all those affected by this catastrophe.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i believe that taking stock and setting more advanced targets for equality between men and women - in this march 2012 - means facing up to the dramatic data of the economic crisis, which is seeing an increase in female unemployment, especially among young women, an increase in poverty among women and an increase in violence against women, especially in the private sector. there is a situation of suffering, exacerbated by the cuts in welfare, education and social security systems in many countries, which have hit women particularly hard. i believe there is a link between this situation and the continued exclusion of women from decision-making and therefore an underestimation of the impact of the crisis and policies on women. in this context, the two reports focus on a number of shared objectives: a stronger orientation of the programming of the 14-20 structural funds towards actions also targeting women; economic independence, including the promotion of women's entrepreneurship through guarantee funds and support instruments; closing the gender pay gap by reassessing women's professionalism and work; the prohibition of discriminatory behaviour - for example in my country, the preformed resignation. we also call for rules and measures to allow a rebalancing of representation with transparent selection procedures for men and women in politics and decision-making and for commissioner reding, as she has announced, to really get parliament's support for a directive on quotas in enterprises. we must also act on a symbolic level, not only by countering stereotypes in the media, but also by promoting the value and respect of the dignity of women, which is too often commodified and violated. i regret that mrs t. veld has proposed an amendment to remove this reference to the dignity of women, perhaps failing to grasp the fact that the degradation of their image becomes a justification for violence against them. thank you, sir.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too will quote many of the figures which have already been discussed: women represent more than half the european population, but they suffer from many disparities in treatment and, of course, in pay. this terrible figure of 17.5% less average pay than men is truly unbearable! a woman will have to work 14 months to earn what a man earns in a year! this has to be seen in the light of another fact which concerns the merits of women: 59% of graduates are women! the european institutions are not immune to inequality either, although they have always attached great importance to the issue of equal opportunities. in the european parliament itself, the figures are contradicting good intentions, with 34% of the seats in this house currently held by women. since the beginning of the legislature, the number of female vice-presidents has gone from 6 to 3 out of 14, while the number of female chairpersons of committees and subcommittees has now fallen from 10 to 8 out of 22. since 1952, there have been only two women presidents out of 28, simone veil and nicole fontaine, and in the administration women - although 60% of the staff - actually only 23% have a significant role. so there is still a lot to be done from the european parliament and the question is: how can we set a good example for the member states with the statistics i have just mentioned? i would like to take this opportunity to thank commissioner reding for her efforts, including the opening of this important consultation, and i also share her views: i do not believe in quotas either, i have always thought that women should stand out for their qualities and merits, but it is right, madam commissioner, that the debate should be open and i thank you for that.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the participation of women in the political decisionmaking process at all levels is essential, since it allows for the adoption of concrete measures to facilitate women's activities in their difficult task of reconciling private and working life. without women's participation in policy-making there is no necessary sensitivity to women's specific issues and attention to their discrimination - both in access to employment and to childcare facilities for their children. to address this strong imbalance in women's participation in politics, i support the introduction of quotas in the electoral lists, i don't like them, but i like the result that quotas can bring and have brought in recent years: just a few days ago, on the occasion of international women's day, a draft law was adopted by the committee on constitutional affairs of the italian chamber of deputies which provides for the obligation to include 30% of women in electoral lists in municipalities with more than 5 000 inhabitants. this is therefore a great step forward and i hope that it can be accepted by the other member states as a best practice. increased participation of women in business and leadership positions, particularly in company boards and supervisory bodies, must be achieved. numerous studies have shown that the increase in women in these positions contributes strongly to the competitiveness of firms and to profit growth. and this also seems to be in line with the kratsa report which we voted on a few months ago in this very house. i share the european commission's view and i am glad to congratulate commissioner reding on launching a public consultation to examine the possibility of proposing legislation on gender quotas in enterprises. i hope that the european parliament can be a model in this respect, that it can increase the participation of women in the next term of office 2014-2019 and i hope above all to make colleagues like nuttall, who is not present in the chamber now, believe that in this parliament only three women are worthy of being vice-presidents, i do not think so and i wanted to ask him in fact what strange country he lived in. thank you.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank the two rapporteurs, ms in ’t veld and ms pietikäinen. they have given us the basis for a very animated debate. in this chamber i have often criticised the fact that there were very few men in the chamber during debates on women’s and gender equality questions, but i must say that tonight was a first. there were many more men than usual. it is good that this debate – where both sides are heard, where people have different opinions, because it is a question of society and not a question of women alone – is led by men and by women. i think we all agree that there are many challenges and that the challenges have not become less but that problems are growing. where we do not agree is on the measures to be taken in order to change this situation. mostly we do not agree on what should be done at european level and what should be done at national level, although very often the two have to be combined. so i really need the support of parliament in order to go forward in those areas where there is a very clear european competence. i need the help of parliament to continue to raise awareness about the very large number of inequalities and to take the measures that are needed to change this situation. by the way, i would like to tell you that all commissioners are aware that in their portfolio the balance between men and women needs to be tackled. one example i could give of how european law and national action have to be combined is the question of the gender pay gap. several members who asked this question are no longer in the chamber but, at any rate, i think it is important that i tell you this. we do have a european directive on equal pay for equal work, and there was a very interesting hearing concerning that problem last week in parliament. the result of this hearing was that, where the directive is applied by national courts, direct discrimination is no longer very high. we are discrimination. women earn less because they make up the majority of people in part-time work and because they leave work when they become mothers. fathers do not leave work when they become fathers. other problems can only be solved at the level of the labour market, at the level of the social partners working together and at the level of national governments introducing transparency rules. i mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, there are almost 450 000 international successions opened every year in the european union, with a total value, as has already been said, of over 120 billion euros. nevertheless, there are still many difficulties for citizens to determine which state, which authorities are competent in matters of succession law. in addition, most member states do not allow the citizen to choose the jurisdiction to which he or she will apply at the time of the succession. in addition, numerous issues arise when judicial recognition of official notarial acts of a member state other than that in which they were produced is sought. the regulation we are about to adopt responds to these serious shortcomings, to these concrete needs of the european citizens, and in doing so, ladies and gentlemen, we are not approving a classic piece of legislation, but are creating an instrument which regulates a crucial aspect of the institutional organization of every society: the concept of inheritance and succession, and the rules governing their effects and their individual aspects, have a primary impact on the organisation of any company. i therefore warmly thank all those who have contributed to the completion of this difficult project, and in particular my colleague mr lechner for his work and commitment during the difficult legislative process which is now coming to an end. i also thank him, and i do so on behalf of the millions of european citizens who will benefit from an instrument which fully meets their needs and makes a substantial contribution to the process of european integration. thank you, sir.
in writing. the proposal for a directive under discussion introduces a system of judicial cooperation between member states in matters of succession where the deceased has interests spread over countries other than the one in which he is habitually resident. i would like to express my appreciation for the work done by the rapporteur, mr leichner, who has been able to translate the different approaches into the text and to synthesise them into a complete discipline. at the legal level, the primary interest is protected by a simplified succession procedure, anchoring the provision to meritorious principles (protection of heirs, legates and creditors, which have hitherto been penalised in crossborder successions) and to innovative procedures (introduction of the european certificate of succession or the possibility for the testator to choose which legislation to apply to his succession). from a political point of view, the breaking down of barriers between states of all kinds, including those relating to law, represents a valuable step towards the creation of a 'common space' governed by shared laws, in which citizens can really identify themselves as 'european citizens'.

the rapporteur. the aim of this report is to relaunch the bologna process with the important aim that the qualifications awarded by universities throughout europe should have a general value and validity. if you get a degree from a university in a member country, it must be recognized by all the other universities, that is the main objective! it is a mistake to consider the university as an activity exclusively within the state! the real dimension of the university and the place of study is international because the studies and research are international, the professions are international now. the market for professions must be freed from the shackles and fetters which today hamper the mobility of labour within the european territory. this is a precondition which has economic value and also the answer to a great youth aspiration. who is responsible for this? the organization of studies is a matter for the individual member states, but recognition abroad is not a matter for the state itself. it is a matter for the european union, which must provide for it and which must make a policy to encourage it. article 149 of the lisbon treaty also refers to the union's role in the recognition of qualifications, in contributing to the development of the quality of education and higher education, and in developing the european dimension of education. for this reason, our report stresses that the union must also be given responsibility, in addition to the states, and that the biennial meetings of education ministers, such as the one to be held in bucharest, must gradually be made part of the union's competence. what do you do?
