madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the adoption of the report on the statute for a european cooperative society, to which i have made a substantial contribution. i would like to emphasize the important role of cooperative experience in italy and europe and its impact on the territory, particularly at the time of the crisis we are now experiencing. i am sorry to say, however, that the european cooperative society has not yet become established, given its limited use: in 2010, only 17 companies were registered. this should raise questions about the applicability of the legal framework. i believe that today more than ever there is a need for simplification to enable small organisations to access information on the national provisions implementing the regulation and the directive. i also think it is necessary to recall the commitments made by the commission, and in particular the inclusion of cooperatives in the financial instruments of the european investment fund, and to make explicit reference to more favourable conditions for cooperatives such as access to credit facilities and favourable taxation. italian experience has shown that when supported by appropriate instruments and facilities, cooperatives produce excellent results in terms of employment and social conditions. thank you, sir.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr berlinguer's report, which i congratulate on its work and its excellent analysis. the report highlights the problems and shortcomings which are hindering the effective creation of a european higher education area. i am referring in particular to the insufficient relationship between universities and the world of work, the still incomplete review of national certification systems and the unequal access to university systems. i therefore share the call made by my colleague for the adoption of a common certification system to achieve mutual recognition of university degrees. at the same time, i hope that the next ministerial conference scheduled for april will address the real pain point of the matter, namely the need and urgency to move rapidly forward with the revision of the directive on professional qualifications and their recognition. thank you, sir.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in 1999, when the bologna declaration was signed, the european countries that signed it committed themselves to working together to create a european higher education area by 2010. this objective was to ensure academic quality, economic development and social cohesion, employment and lifelong learning for graduates. i agree with the report by my colleague, because it calls for decisive and coordinated action at european level. recognition of qualifications on the basis of an efficient quality certification system is a good starting point to encourage member states to adopt the national qualifications framework for lifelong learning. it is essential to implement and develop a european higher education system which allows and encourages the free circulation of knowledge. i think that the measures in the report are the right way forward to increase european productivity and competitiveness. thank you, sir.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report by mr berlinguer on the bologna process. the creation of an open european higher education area is an important achievement for all of us. the need to harmonise the recognition of qualifications and the framework of qualifications, and to completely revise the national systems for certifying the quality of higher education is even more important. we still have students who, through erasmus, acquire qualifications which are not recognised in their universities or whose access to universities is too different and sometimes questionable. this is why we need to strengthen the process to achieve the objectives of the 2020 strategy in terms of job growth and economic recovery, also thanks to better synergies between universities and the business and labour world.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the creation of a european higher education area is a great goal that the european union has been able to set itself. however, despite the progress made since the bologna declaration which dates back to 1999, as has been mentioned, we must note that as regards student mobility and the equalisation of qualifications between countries, the results are far from satisfactory. that is why i voted in favour of this report. we need to accelerate in this direction, we need to reverse the trend, especially in some countries, and reduce investment in training, and for this reason the harmonization envisaged by the bologna declaration remains essential to make the whole european training system stronger and the labour market more dynamic. i too would like to congratulate mr berlinguer on his excellent work. thank you, sir.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the agreements between the european union and iceland and norway. in order to guarantee security within the european union, the abolition of frontiers and the consequent freedom of movement of european citizens must be accompanied by greater cooperation and better coordination between the judicial authorities of the various countries. in particular, the agreements in question make it possible to improve cooperation between the judicial authorities of two countries which are not currently members of the union but which are part of the schengen area, such as the kingdom of norway and the republic of iceland. following the amendments introduced by the treaty of lisbon, parliament's consent is required for such agreements to be concluded. finally, i join the rapporteur, mr moraes, in stressing the importance of eurojust's involvement in the project and i congratulate him on the excellent work he has done.
in writing. − we are in favour of the conclusion of this agreement because it aims to improve judicial cooperation between the member states of the european union, iceland and norway by applying almost all the provisions of the 2000 convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union and its 2001 protocol. the agreement extends to norway and iceland the application of rules on mutual legal assistance which are already in force and widely applied in the other member states. we are convinced that this will contribute to the fight against crossborder crime and will strengthen cooperation with two countries which are already members of the schengen area and, in the case of iceland, will also have positive consequences in the negotiations under way for its future accession to the european union.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr moraes, which aims to improve judicial cooperation between the member states and iceland and norway by applying almost entirely the provisions of the 2000 convention on mutual legal assistance between member states and its 2001 protocol.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr lechner's report, which has the merit of clarifying the situation in the field of succession law by ensuring legal certainty. european legislation is characterised by the collection of national rules which create fragmented and problematic situations in the recognition of citizens' rights. the creation of a european certificate of succession will serve as cross-border proof for registrations and will protect those who in good faith take possession of an estate. for citizens habitually resident in their home country, nothing will change if all their assets are located in that country. the new legislation is aimed at citizens who intend to reside, or who reside habitually, outside their country of origin: in this case, they will be allowed to opt for the law of their home state. the implementation of probate practices will thus be considerably streamlined and at the same time a solid basis will be provided for advisers dealing with successions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation on the recognition of decisions in matters of succession and the creation of a european certificate of succession. it contributes to the recognition of documents in matters of succession and resolves legal uncertainty by defining jurisdiction in matters of succession according to the principle of the 'habitual residence' of the deceased. i also fully agree with the decision to leave the testator the option of making a different choice, choosing as the governing law the law of a state of which he is a national rather than that of his habitual residence. i would also like to stress that the introduction of the european certificate of succession will help to simplify the procedures in this area, as it provides sufficient proof of the quality of the heir. finally, i believe that this regulation, together with the amendment of the directive on the recognition of qualifications, fits into the wider context of reducing barriers to the free movement of persons within the european union and thus contributes to making the freedom of movement of european citizens a reality.
in writing. − the proposal aims to enable european citizens to organise their succession in advance and to ensure effectively the rights of heirs and legatees in an international succession. while the proposal seems useful and justifiable in substance, it must be acknowledged that, from the point of view of the means by which this aim is pursued, there are still unresolved issues which not only do not simplify the rules currently in force but sometimes even complicate them: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right of initiative. for these reasons, i thought it appropriate to abstain.
in writing. - in general, the conflict of jurisdiction between the various national legislations is one of the classic obstacles to be overcome in the perspective of creating an ever more cohesive european community. this case has concerned or concerns several areas of european law: one of these is the area of succession rights. this is not a purely legal issue: it is something which unfortunately concerns the painful personal and family history of many european citizens who, when they lose a member of their family in a member state other than their own, are forced to face complex legal problems which are all too often characterized by inconsistencies between the legal systems of the two countries. the european certificate of succession finally fills a legislative vacuum which, over the years, has inevitably caused problems in all european countries and serious inconvenience to many citizens at a particularly difficult time in their lives.
in writing. − the right of a deceased person to choose the law of his state of origin as the law applicable to the succession must not be called into question. the european certificate of succession is the best way to regulate this aspect. i therefore agree with the rapporteur and i shall vote in favour.
in writing. whereas deceased nationals who were habitually resident outside their state of origin and who had not opted for any legislation will in future be subject to the law of succession of the state of residence; i am not going to go into the details of the commission's proposals. whereas the commission proposal is further developed by the introduction of a european certificate of succession; the court has already held that the contested decision is not a final and legally effective decision on the succession but an attestation of that decision, capable of serving as cross-border proof for entries in the register and designed to protect those who take possession in good faith of an estate.
in writing. - the report by mr lechner was voted on today in plenary. the new regulation aims to facilitate the enforcement of wills and to avoid lengthy and costly litigation in the case of a european citizen who dies in a country other than his country of origin and whose will involves more than one national legal system. the rapporteur believes that cross-border successions represent 10% of the total in the eu, almost 450,000 per year, worth some €123 billion. the new european rules would also introduce a european certificate of succession, which would facilitate legal procedures and ensure that the rights of heirs, as well as other parties involved, such as creditors, are respected, making the procedure quicker and clearer. the certificate would have a voluntary use. the new regulation would not apply to succession of persons who remain in their country of origin and would not change national legislation on succession, property, taxation and would not introduce any harmonisation of national procedures.
in writing. − this vote will enable european citizens to plan their wills in an appropriate way by deciding for themselves. it will provide legal certainty on a complex issue. european citizens will finally be able to choose between the legislation of their country of origin or that of the country to which they have moved. the standard will facilitate, simplify and streamline cross-border succession practices. we may not be able to solve all the problems, but we will certainly make improvements. the european certificate of succession, issued by a notary, will improve the autonomy of citizens.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because, although equality between men and women is a fundamental principle of the european union, there is still huge gender discrimination in the labour sector. this situation, in 2012, is unacceptable. women across the eu earn 17.5% less on average than men. i would like to underline that women represent 60% of new university graduates but continue to be under-represented in economic decision-making posts. indeed, within the eu, on average only 12% of the executives of the major listed companies are women, with only 3% female chairs. in times of economic crisis, strengthening women’s position in the job market is not only a moral imperative but also an economic necessity. for this reason member states must invest in affordable, high-quality facilities for the care of children, the elderly and other dependent persons, making sure that as many people as possible can combine professional and private life. i also would like to express my great concern about the legislation in some member states which does not expressly forbid the handing of pre-signed resignation letters to employers when women are recruited, which has the effect of enabling maternity laws to be circumvented. any further delay in that prohibition is intolerable.
in writing. - i could not express my approval of this report because the provisions contained in it go far beyond the defence of equal rights between men and women, and are intended rather to promote genuine discrimination at the expense of meritocracy, which should be the only benchmark, especially in the field of employment. i therefore voted against.
in writing. − the issue of equality between men and women is a very sensitive one and should be approached with due caution. the issue of employment is more important than ever in times of crisis, given the worrying statistics we have on youth unemployment. one of the objectives of our policy action, within the europe 2020 strategy, is to increase employment for men and women aged 20-64 by 75%. we know that this is an ambitious target, but we must do everything possible to achieve it. much more needs to be done in the area of gender equality, especially in the workplace, by seeking to reduce the difficulties of access to employment and career opportunities for women. in the future, action will also have to be taken on the pay front, where the gender gap remains very wide, considering that, with equal roles, men in the european union earn on average 17% more than women.
in writing. - i wanted to express my strongly negative opinion of this report, since it contains many frankly unacceptable passages. it goes from pushing for recognition for same-sex unions and families, to safeguards for same-sex parents. i will never tire of repeating that the family is one and only one, that is, that of a father, a mother and any offspring. no one forbids two persons of the same sex to live together freely, but the family is something else and therefore must have different guarantees and protections. it is in the very nature of the concept of humanity that the meaning of the term family, and of parenthood, is expressed: only a union between a man and a woman can lead to the conception of a new life, and the continuation of the human species. we do not want to give in to these new conceptions born out of nothing in recent years: history and human nature cannot and must not be changed. finally, i would like to emphasize that the title of the report referred to equality between men and women, and all these references in the text seem to me to have a completely different content and a totally different meaning.
in writing. i have chosen to abstain on the report 'equality between women and men in the european union 2011' because i note many advances in it but also elements that did not allow me to fully support the text. one point in particular weighed heavily on my decision, namely, the definition of family. this is a matter of subsidiarity policy, and i believe that this is a matter for the states and not for europe.
in writing. - i did not vote for, and regret having to renounce this right and duty, the report on equality between women and men in the european union 2011. many of the statements are principles that i have always supported and promoted: the gender pay gap - still unacceptable a gender gap of 17.5%; the difficulty of remaining in the labour market after the first child; the higher risk of poverty for women; the europe 2020 targets of 75% female employment; the need for a gender budget that takes account, in every public dimension, of the different needs for equal rights between men and women. but once again, an opportunity has been missed, by diverting the real meaning of this resolution into a swamp of demagogy - to please everyone, in fact, everyone is displeased - and by going so far as to discuss the right of adoption of children for same-sex couples or to criticise the definition of family and parenting in certain european union states as being 'too restrictive'. i believe that these areas deserve a broad discussion, as do the assessments on the need to open up to de facto couples, including homosexuals, but that the occasion should not be, for political strategy's sake, the text voted on today.
in writing. - i am strongly opposed to the report because, instead of proposing initiatives to achieve effective equality between men and women in the field of work, politics, decision-making and pay, it wants to implement the recognition of homosexual families and again discusses the 'necessity' of abortion. another consideration which convinces me even more in voting against is that we want to guarantee reproductive rights to women regardless of their sexual orientation, so we should give men who feel they are women the opportunity to have children or even adopt them. the consideration is also that families include not only married parents but also same-sex parents, so allowing adoption of children by homosexual couples. a report which could have been absolutely accepted in favour of the rightful recognition of the female gender has been turned into a senseless series of declarations on the alleged rights of so-called homosexual families, including the possibility of adopting children. i believe that the family in the strict sense of the term can only be considered when it is formed by a man and a woman and any children.
in writing. − despite the fact that the european union has been working for years to combat discrimination between men and women, and despite the cultural progress that has been made, equality between the two genders has not been fully achieved for a number of reasons, one of which is economic. it is therefore necessary to promote improvements in the working situation of women. efforts to improve labour market participation and access to positions of power, such as company boards, must therefore remain a priority. in some non-european countries the gap between the position and status of women and men often takes on dramatic dimensions. women have fewer rights or none at all. the european union is committing itself by this vote to doing much more to improve the situation of these women, starting with their health. it is not just a sufficient amount of funds that is needed, but also a radical change in mindsets and traditions.
in writing. − in the member states of the union, women are still underrepresented in the political decision-making assemblies: the gender balance in the regional assemblies has changed little since 2004. i would like to take this opportunity to draw the commission's attention to the fact that these percentages are fixed and are not showing any positive trend. one explanation for this phenomenon could be attributed to traditional barriers that women have to overcome, such as lack of financial resources, stereotypes, difficulties in reconciling family life and political activity. i therefore share one of the measures proposed by the rapporteur, which is to design and implement effective strategies at both union and member state level to increase women's involvement and participation in decision-making and leadership, through quantified targets, continuous monitoring mechanisms and clear action plans. i also believe that active and concrete measures must be promoted to ensure gender balance in all government bodies and in all public appointments. in my view, to increase women's political participation, we need to tackle the structural barriers that prevent them from taking an active part in political life.
in writing. - this report on the representation of women in political decision-making is not acceptable. the report calls for special measures to strengthen the political representation of women from ethnic minorities. secondly, the intention to impose a predetermined quota for women in government appointments, at both national and community level, is not acceptable, as such a selection criterion would violate any meritocratic principle.
in writing. - in our europe too, gender equality is unfortunately still an objective and not a result already consolidated in practice. just to give an example, in all eu member states women are still underrepresented in political assemblies, making up only 24% of the members of national parliaments, with different but all equally discouraging percentages in different states. although theoretical equality has already been achieved in legal systems, there are still numerous subtle cultural and practical obstacles which too often prevent women from realistically aspiring to positions of responsibility held by men. as in politics, so in public administration, in private enterprise, in education and in the armed forces, in all fields of civilian life which involve the assumption of responsibility and prestige. in today's highly competitive global environment, it is no longer acceptable that the gender gap is a discriminatory factor that can have such a profound impact not only on the professional prospects but also on the civil dignity of all women.
in writing. − equal participation of women in power and decision-making, in addition to being promoted at international level by the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, is provided for at eu level by the strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015. gender equality in decision-making is a matter of quality and equality. a more balanced gender participation certainly contributes to more diversified decisions and better decisions. in all member states women are still underrepresented, due to a number of factors, such as lack of financial resources, the dominance of male culture, stereotypes, and the difficulty of reconciling family life and political activity. we therefore intend to encourage national parties to take measures to increase the participation of women. we believe that active and concrete measures to ensure gender balance in all government bodies and in all public appointments should be promoted at national level. the promotion of gender balance in politics is a prerequisite for stable and transparent democracies.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy includes the main objective of aiming to increase the employment rate of women and men aged 20-64 to 75%. in times of economic crisis, a stronger position of women in the labour market and their economic independence is an economic necessity. the full inclusion of women in the european labour market must be a priority from now on and that is why i am voting in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution because i do not think it is absolutely necessary to introduce quotas for women in politics. it is true that up until a few decades ago women were severely penalized, but fortunately for at least fifty years now in europe there have been equal rights and equal opportunities for men and women. there are many examples of politically engaged women who have merited to reach the top of the political hierarchy, and this has been due solely to their abilities, not to any special facilities. a quota system is also counterproductive for women themselves, in my view, because it would not reward merit properly, but rather only numbers. i'm for equality in every way: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. - president, today we have finally tackled a subject which not only puts the role of women at the centre of a field, the political and decision-making one, which for too long has been classified as a male prerogative. at the same time, a path to modernity has been marked. let 's get this straight . the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the women we support in politics are not just figures who are listed simply because they respect the law, but people who are aware that they have made a reasoned choice to participate actively. to these motivated and passionate women, who organise their family, social and professional lives to make their contribution to creating a better society - whether public or private - we give our consent and the means to follow their inspiration. in some italian regions, if two candidates are elected, one of them must be a woman. gender dual preference is a choice that is given to those who wish to express more than one vote. it also appears to be the only way to enable good, prepared, competent and generous women who want to get involved in politics to do so. thank you, sir.

in writing. − the european union strongly promotes equal participation of women and men in power and decision-making. women's political participation, in particular, is fundamental to democracy and is essential for achieving sustainable development and peace. in all the member states of the european union, women are still underrepresented in the political decision-making assemblies: the european parliament has a right to vote. this vote also reaffirms that the active participation of women, on an equal basis with men, at all levels of decision-making is essential to achieve equality, sustainable development, peace and democracy. to increase women's political participation, it is necessary to address the problem of structural barriers that prevent them from taking part in active politics. the creation of conditions favourable to women's participation in political life at all levels is another necessary measure. the possibility of reconciling work, private and family life is recognised at eu level as an important priority for achieving gender equality and making it easier for women to participate in political life.
in writing. - after a decade of studies, research and investment aimed at implementing a european cooperative society statute, and after as many negative responses in terms of appreciation and feasibility by european citizens and the internal market, i did not intend to support this report with my vote. the text is based on principles which tend to make its content a mere ideological exercise rather than an instrumental and objective assessment of the economic value of this initiative for european citizens.
in writing. - the vote on this own-initiative report gives us the opportunity to stress the need to plan and launch, as soon as possible, an initiative by the european commission to relaunch the statute of the european cooperative society. the adoption of the report should be seen as a stimulus to act as soon as possible, not to miss the important opportunity presented by the un's proclamation of 2012 as the international year of cooperatives. the fact that only 17 of the approximately 160000 cooperatives in europe have adopted the form of the statute indicates the urgency of amending the statute in order to make it more attractive without losing its most important and positive aspects. there is widespread awareness of the value of the cooperative form in the european economic landscape, and our debate clearly showed that cooperatives, better than other forms of economic enterprise, have been able to withstand the economic crisis. it is therefore our duty to support them and to promote vigorously and consistently the spread of the sce as a positive model towards which to direct the development of european cooperatives.
in writing. - the promotion of european cooperatives is problematic, in my view, mainly for three reasons: first, it is clear from the small number of companies created since the entry into force of the directive. the insufficient number of workers involved and the analysis of the results of the commission's studies show that there is a substantial lack of interest in this field. secondly, the viability of such companies is strongly hampered by the diversity of the economic and legal contexts of the member states, which prevents the harmonisation necessary for the creation of trans-european companies. finally, the report considers that such companies represent a social economy model, as opposed to the capitalist one, which could help europe to emerge from the crisis, a point with which i disagree and which has been refuted by studies carried out in italy, where such companies were created for the sole purpose of achieving administrative simplification in the management of companies. for these reasons, i shall vote against.
in writing. - cooperative societies are a major european reality, comprising 160 000 units and employing some 5.4 million workers. however, the statute for a european cooperative society has, to date, not been widely adopted by european companies. it is therefore necessary to take steps to improve this instrument; the commission has already taken steps to simplify the document and to involve workers in its drafting, which is a key pillar for the future of cooperatives. working on these fronts, with a view to the wider extension and spread of the ece, is a priority step to stimulate growth and safeguard the european cooperative reality, which is a significant resource for the union's economy.
in writing. − social economy enterprises deserve our recognition and very significant support. the revision of the statute must make it possible to develop the recognition of this form of company in the eu given the central and indispensable role they now play in society. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i congratulate mr giegold on his work. the report adopted today, in the light of articles 4, 54 and 151 to 154 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, shows that parliament does not forget that cooperatives and other social economy enterprises are part of the european social model and the internal market and deserve absolutely greater recognition and support, as is also provided for in the constitutions of some member states and in several key eu documents. i also think it is very important to stress that, because of its complexity, the statute only partially meets the needs of cooperatives. it must be made easier to use so that the rights of information, consultation and participation of all employees are guaranteed without, however, leading to a reduction in quality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i consider it essential to protect the cooperative society, which is structurally linked to the territory in which it operates and is therefore a key factor in accelerating local development, which is essential for the creation of real social, economic and territorial cohesion in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. at present, the legislation on cooperatives and worker participation varies widely between the member states and the statute for a european cooperative society is currently the only legal form of social economy available at european level. its introduction would therefore be a major step towards the recognition of the european cooperative business model.

in writing. − the cooperative society is by its nature structurally linked to the territory and therefore plays an important role in accelerating local development, a true social, economic and territorial cohesion. in addition to a social cooperative's bonding and solidarity function, cooperative banks have demonstrated high levels of sustainability and resilience during the financial crisis, thanks to their cooperative business model. the latter, in fact, increased business volume and growth during the crisis, with fewer bankruptcies and excesses. this vote affirms that cooperatives deserve strong recognition and support, as provided for in the constitutions of some member states and in several key european union documents. in particular, it is welcomed that the provisions on worker participation are considered a central element in the framework of economic cooperatives.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, with tomorrow's vote we will officially launch the procedure leading to the adoption of the 2013 budget. the key word in budgetary matters in times of crisis is certainly the word austerity, and i think we cannot ignore it at the moment. however, i believe that the european union will never be able to respond adequately to the current economic and social crisis or to prevent any future crises without greater integration of common instruments and measures to strengthen solidarity between member states. the problems associated with the crisis affecting european economies are many: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of unemployment. it is precisely on the young that i would like to dwell briefly. today's young people are better educated, more technologically advanced, more mobile and we must focus on them because they are and will be the most important resource for the growth of the union. unfortunately, the statistics we have are alarming: one in five young people under 25 is looking for a job and cannot find one. there are also 7.5 million young people under 24 who are not in work or education. i therefore believe it is essential to use the resources at our disposal to help young people develop skills that meet the needs of the labour market, by ensuring that they have the opportunity for professional experience and training to facilitate their entry into the world of work. i strongly believe that to respond adequately to these problems, swift and coordinated action at european level is needed, with targeted investment to ensure the achievement of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for growth and jobs, with particular attention, as mentioned, to youth employment. in this context, support for small and medium-sized enterprises, which have the greatest potential for economic growth and innovation and which have created 85% of new jobs over the last decade, is crucial. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the definition of the term 'competition' in the definition of the term 'competition'. the guidelines we shall be voting on tomorrow do not go into the specifics of the individual headings and policies, also because it would be too early, we are waiting for the commission to present the draft budget to begin working on the figures, counting on the valuable contribution of guidance from the individual specialised committees. but we want to send a message, and we want to send it to all the european countries, and that is the message of strong european added value. national budgets alone are not enough, and no member state can think of going it alone. in this respect we need strong synergies within the european semester between national and european budgets. i have to add one last comment on the issue of payments: 2013 is the seventh and final year of the financial perspective: we all remember what happened during the conciliation procedure last year and it is therefore in this direction that we must expect an increase in payment requirements. parliament therefore declares from now on that it will not welcome artificial cuts in payment appropriations, because this practice risks leading us to an unsustainable level of payments in 2013. a simple net contributor/beneficiary approach does not take due account of the important spill-over effects that the union budget produces between member states for the benefit of common policy objectives of the european union.

member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to start by thanking mr moreira and the committee on international trade for their proposal that this house consent to the conclusion of the international cocoa agreement. the commission agrees with parliament’s view that the new agreement is a good platform to promote international cooperation in the world cocoa sector and that it will contribute to the strengthening of the national cocoa economies. this agreement will enable the world markets to strive towards obtaining fair prices for both producers and consumers, while also leading to equitable economic returns and promoting a sustainable cocoa economy. all these elements are of paramount importance for cocoa producer countries, which also, in most cases, happen to be developing countries. being the world’s main importer and consumer of cocoa, the european union has a clear role and a responsibility to promote the increased sustainability of a fair cocoa trade in these countries. with this responsibility in mind, we recognise that the question of child labour represents one of the most difficult challenges – the controversial aspect being that, in our view, the idea is abhorrent, while in some other traditions it is an accepted practice. however, we agree with the ilo, icco and the world cocoa foundation that the agreement is a good starting point to address the issue of child labour in this particular sector. we could even go further on this issue by saying that the problem of child labour goes well beyond the cocoa sector and, unfortunately, affects nearly all our developing partners. as you know, the rights of the child are enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights. it is a priority for us to protect and promote these rights, and the commission is deeply committed to this cause. the eu remains engaged in eradicating the worst forms of child labour at global level and in ensuring that a child’s education is not sacrificed to the need to work and that children’s physical and emotional development is not adversely affected. at international level, under article 32 of the un convention on the rights of the child, children have the right to be protected from economic exploitation and from child labour. nevertheless, the commission has repeatedly expressed its profound regret that, despite the efforts of the international community – including the near universal ratification of ilo convention 182, which requires the complete eradication of this practice – an ever-increasing number of children are engaged in activities that meet the ilo definition of child labour. i would like to point out that today a shocking 124 million children are engaged in the worst forms of child labour and that the overall trend in sub-saharan africa is up by nearly 30%. this should give us all food for thought. i therefore really appreciate and welcome the interest that mr moreira and a large number of members of this house attach to this issue. but the issue is complex. in developing countries, and in particular in the cocoa sector, the problem of child labour cannot be considered in isolation. an integrated approach must tackle other very relevant issues stemming from the root causes of poverty and the subsequent need for child labour and trafficking of children for this labour. as the draft recommendation rightly acknowledges, 90% of cocoa farmers in west africa are smallholders. these are family farms facing huge challenges. they are sometimes located 40 km down a dirt track and have extremely difficult access to infrastructure. in these circumstances children will, of course, be working on the farm. in order to assist communities to provide the conditions where children will no longer need to be employed, the commission is fully engaged through its development cooperation and its policies that we apply in this sector. the eu’s engagement is outlined in the 2010 commission staff working paper on child labour and the june 2010 council conclusions. policy coherence and coordination are essential components to this effort and, with this in mind, we have in place a coordinated eu approach, working with the relevant international organisations and bodies. this is coupled with helping west african countries to address the issues themselves, including through cooperation on improved infrastructure and farming methods and providing for more and better labour inspection and market organisation. to conclude, i would like to reaffirm my strong belief that a child’s place is at school and not in the fields or factories. eradicating poverty is the first objective that we should try to achieve: tackling the root cause of child labour in africa and in all developing countries. i am therefore very grateful to the european parliament, which has once again put this very important issue high on its agenda. the commission, as usual, will address the issue i would like to thank mr moreira for his excellent work on both the resolution and the convention. this new international cocoa convention which we shall be voting on tomorrow certainly contains very timely measures which improve the previous one, measures such as the development of the producing economies, fair prices for both producers and consumers and a sustainable framework in environmental and social terms. i believe that it is precisely in this social context that the resolution accompanying this convention, which we are also going to vote on tomorrow, is emphasizing. i think that the fact that it is basically focusing on the eradication of child labour is a great success, because it is one of the problems we have and, as the commissioner has said, we have been trying to fight it for some time, but the truth is that the figures you have given us of 124 million children working in the world do not give much joy. i think, in this sense, it is a very difficult battle and it is one of those battles that must be fought from many fronts. and what i would like to put forward here are three specific fronts that i think would be vitally important. the first would be the obligation for all states to ratify the united nations convention on the rights of the child. the second would be to apply - and this i think is important and has not been mentioned here - the advances in research and development so that we have techniques for growing and harvesting cocoa that do not require this child labour. and finally, the development of a european standard on traceability and sustainability. i think the commission would do well to try to study these proposals and i would also like to know the commissioner's opinion on them.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the cocoa market, paradoxically sweet in its final product, is almost cursed from the beginning. when francesco carletti, a florentine merchant who was the first to circumnavigate the globe using merchant ships in the late 1500s and early 1600s, brought cocoa to europe, he denounced a trade in which the slave trade was the main source of funding for the plant's investments. and since then the inhumanity of the cocoa trade has persisted. if the product originates from ghana and côte d'ivoire almost 60% of the world production the role of children, the majority of whom are under 14 years old, is obvious, often subject to a real trafficking that takes them away from their families in neighboring countries to lock them up in plantations. last week i was in côte d'ivoire for an annual meeting of the liberal-democratic euro-african parliamentarians and i met the president of the main non-governmental organisation fighting against the exploitation of children in cocoa plantations, an organisation which is not alone, even president ouattara's wife joined them in starting the work of the national monitoring committee against trafficking and exploitation and child labour. but we must move beyond voluntarism, good examples and complaints, and invest the organization of markets with a social responsibility which has so far been lacking in cocoa plantations, due to the particular, non-intensive, non-mechanical culture, and the worsening use of pesticides for workers. the agreement signed - and i thank president moreira and the commission - is the first piece of good news, it makes the chocolate chain more transparent, involves non-governmental organisations and promotes fairer world prices. and the eu, which has the majority of the votes of the importing countries in the international cocoa organizations, has a particular responsibility in implementing the agreement quickly and making it a tool for humanizing the production of this great food temptation. but the agreement, important as it is, is not enough on its own. consumers must also be made more aware of the need to enable them to make ethical purchases, and the production and marketing of fair and supportive chocolate must also be promoted, with prices guaranteed to producers and no child exploitation on african plantations. the eu can do much more in this respect by regulating a european guarantee mark which has so far remained a private initiative. thank you, sir.

member of the commission. − mr president, i think there has been a great convergence of views during the debate. it is true that cocoa is a great product. it is also true that for many countries, such as côte d’ivoire, it is an important product for the economy. fair trade should be practised and a fair price should be paid for the product. it should also be the industry’s responsibility to ensure are doing in ghana, côte d’ivoire and other countries. but further measures are needed to address the problem of child labour. i will just recall a couple of them: the european union is conducting a lobbying campaign to support the ratification of ilo convention 182 on the worst forms of child labour and two optional protocols to the convention on the rights of the child. child protection with regard to child labour has been identified as an eu priority in a number of the human rights country strategies that the eu has been drawing up. this is a very important point because we are engaging in political dialogue with our developing partners. this is where we could and should address this issue, with the aim of ensuring that countries also see it as a clear priority. the commission has also produced its guide to socially responsible procurement, which pays attention to labour practices. there are also relevant projects and programmes in development assistance. some of these are specifically targeted at child labour, for example the eur 14 million tackle project on child labour and education which the ilo is carrying out in 14 acp countries, and last year’s eur 10 million call for proposals to combat child labour under the ‘investing in people’ programme. more specifically in the cocoa sector, the edf cocoa sector support programme effectively contributed to improving the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and making cocoa production more sustainable in ghana. i would like to assure all of you that the commission is fully committed to maintaining policy coherence in all its initiatives related to trade, development, human rights and corporate social responsibility, bearing in mind that in developing countries the problem of child labour cannot be just looked at in isolation as a separate problem. taking into account the importance of ensuring that trade agreements include effective provisions on poverty reduction and the promotion of decent work and safe working conditions, the commission is concretely looking into the issue of traceability of goods produced using forced child labour.

in writing. the proposal we voted on this morning aims to amend an existing european parliament regulation opening an autonomous tariff quota for imports of quality beef from the united states and canada, thus ending the longstanding transatlantic dispute over hormones in beef. the solution to the trade dispute which has been proposed has my agreement and my vote in favour. in particular, the eu will gradually increase the tariff quota for high-quality beef not treated with growth hormones to a total of 21 500 tonnes (first stage) and subsequently to 48 200 tonnes. so there will inevitably be a gradual reduction or suspension of sanctions on european union products by the united states and canada. in order to make enforcement more effective, the timing for the first and second phases in the united states and canada protocols is the same: the second phase will start on 1 august 2012, according to both protocols. our request to the commission is to ensure that the settlement of the dispute will ensure that beef imports will be in line with eu requirements.
in writing. - this report aims to end two decades of trade relations between europe and the united states in agricultural products, which were affected by the controversy over beef hormones in the late 1980s. the agreement reached with the united states and subsequently with canada provides for duty-free quotas for american meat not treated with hormones in exchange for the elimination of trade restrictions. the rapid and smooth adoption of this regulation will therefore be mutually beneficial, helping to rebuild and strengthen trade links on both sides of the atlantic.
in writing. - the report under consideration today is of particular importance as it proposes to amend certain basic regulations relating to the common commercial policy in order to ensure their compatibility with the new provisions introduced by the treaty of lisbon. the aim is to ensure that the european union's trade defence instruments are not weakened by the introduction of procedural changes which, although necessary following the entry into force of the treaty, were likely to have significant consequences on substantial aspects of trade defence proceedings. in this context, one of the objectives of the regulation proposed by the european commission in march 2009 is to ensure that the exercise of the commission's implementing powers is not monitored by the council or the european parliament, but by the member states of the european union. i welcome this report and hope that it will be further strengthened in the course of the subsequent negotiations with the council in order to reiterate the importance of the european union's trade defence instruments, which represent a real possibility of protection for european companies against anti-competitive commercial practices by non-european competitors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending the regulations on trade policy for the sake of rationalization, regulatory coordination and adaptation to the changed conditions of international trade, in the light of the experience gained in the years since the lisbon treaty. in particular, the proposed amendments meet requirements of transparency and effectiveness from an executive and practical point of view, with the possibility of adopting immediately applicable measures. the delegation of power to the commission shall be provided for in terms which are balanced and satisfy parliament's prerogatives, with appropriate guarantees as to the necessary flow of information on the content of the exercise of that power, its renewal and the reserved power of revocation. i also think it is realistic and balanced to have the provision for assistance to the commission by the member states in the adoption and application of urgent implementing measures in the form of a regulation. the inclusion of regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 in the scope of the new framework indicates an appreciated sensitivity to legislative activity which does not lose sight, in the detail of the regulations, of the cultural horizon of our time and the star of european values.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because it aims to adapt 26 regulations in the field of the common commercial policy, in line with the new primary law provisions of the lisbon treaty. for example, the legislator will be able to delegate non-essential legislative acts to the executive, while retaining the right to revoke the delegation at any time. the regulations concerned are mainly designed to allow the use of trade safeguard measures, apart from the regulation on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community. the commission proposal provides for adjustments only where council decisions were specifically provided for. because of these special decision-making mechanisms, european trade policy has so far been largely explicitly excluded from the comitology procedure. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and the adoption of the regulation (eu) this special scheme has now come to an end.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the amendment of the trade policy regulation. the omnibus proposal for a regulation aims to adapt 26 council legal acts in the field of the european union's common commercial policy to the post-lisbon system of delegated and implementing acts. unlike the text voted in the commission, the report adopted today has made some amendments aimed at strengthening the anti-dumping rules. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the protection of the european union's financial interests against counterfeiting.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation aims to adapt 26 regulations in the field of the common commercial policy to the new primary law provisions of the treaty of lisbon. in this case, it is intended to bring those regulations into line with the requirements of articles 290 and 291 tfeu and with the provisions of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers. in order to include european trade policy in the comitology procedure, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. the report deals with a set of amendments to regulations on commercial policy, mainly on the use of safeguard measures. it is precisely because of the specific nature of these measures and the sometimes necessary rapid changes, that the instrument of the delegated act has been used, which allows the commission to intervene when necessary. the commission also fully agreed on the need to restore the 15 month deadline for the imposition of duties and anti-dumping measures. the vote is definitely in favour.
in writing. - i take this opportunity to congratulate the rapporteur who has been able to propose in the committee on international trade a number of amendments to a proposal from the european commission which contained some absolutely unacceptable steps such as the extension of the time taken to reach a decision to introduce trade duties. these are acts which are necessary to protect our production system and which therefore require rapid action and not additional bureaucracy or time-consuming measures. i voted in favour of this measure, which is very technical, partly because it was necessary to adapt these regulations to the new comitology.
in writing. - we have today been asked to approve at first reading the report by mrs quisthoudt-rowohl on the proposal for a regulation known as 'omnibus i', which aims to align certain legislative acts on trade policy, including the anti-dumping regulation, with the new 'comitology' procedures. i am pleased that the proposal was adopted by a large majority - to ensure that the text is not weakened, but if necessary further strengthened, in the course of subsequent negotiations with the council and to stress the importance of trade defence instruments, which are the only possible protection for european companies against anti-competitive commercial practices by non-european competitors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which aims to bring certain commercial policy legislation, including the anti-dumping regulation, into line with the new comitology procedures. the text voted today, supporting the arguments put forward by european industry, of which the 'made in italy' is a source of pride, even in a time of crisis, strongly supports trade defence instruments, which represent the only possibility of protection for european companies against anti-competitive commercial practices by non-european competitors.

in writing. - i welcome the report by mr la via, for whom i voted in favour. the guidelines are the first step in the annual budgetary procedure. it is therefore necessary that the 2013 budget forecast is well coordinated and responsible and that the measures taken so far to counter the economic crisis now encourage stable and sustainable growth, including through targeted investments that promote sustainable economic development. the 2013 budget should therefore focus on the implementation of the union's priorities and programmes, including the recovery of overdue payments, especially in the light of the end of the current period of the multiannual financial framework. the budget of the european union is one of the most important instruments for demonstrating solidarity between member states and between generations, and, especially in the light of the financial crisis, it also represents an important added value. the collective efforts made at european union level to ensure the effectiveness of the actions undertaken must be intensified more than ever today.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the general guidelines for the preparation of the 2013 budget because, firstly, i agree with the statement that the eu budget is an instrument that demonstrates solidarity between member states and between generations and that it represents a substantial common saving for the general welfare. secondly, i believe that it is more than appropriate to promote the growth of smes, which have proven to be the key pillar of economic growth in europe, having created 85% of new jobs in the eu between 2002 and 2012; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs for human consumption. thirdly, i share the urgency of recovering the arrears in payments and commitments, which are close to eur 152 000 000 for 2013, in order to respect the amounts of the financial programming and so as not to jeopardise the eu's zero-debt policy. finally, i welcome the agreement on the financing of the additional costs of the iter project, which will not jeopardise the proper implementation of eu policies during the last year of financial programming.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2013 budget guidelines. the year 2013 is a watershed moment in europe's path to economic recovery, and after the necessary austerity measures, it is finally time to boost growth. the european parliament, therefore, also because of the economic situation we are facing, has a responsibility to clearly identify the strategies it considers most appropriate and the points it considers to be priorities in order to combat the current economic crisis and its depressing effects on the real economy, in particular the resulting unemployment. i therefore fully agree with the principles expressed in this resolution, and in particular i stress the importance of promoting growth by promoting youth employment and facilitating small and medium-sized enterprises, objectives which are in line with the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. in congratulating the rapporteur, mr la via, i join him in stressing the need to provide adequate funding in order to meet the commitments made in previous years without involving the budget for next year.
in writing. − the adoption of the 'general guidelines', although only the first step in the long and complex process leading to the adoption of the 2013 eu budget, should be an opportunity to strongly underline the role of the european parliament in the future negotiations, especially with the council, which is strongly aiming to influence the guidelines that the commission will express in its draft budget. it must be clear from the outset that the budgetary approach cannot avoid the urgency of reviving sustainable growth and quality employment, in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the european commission and the council cannot continue on the path of austerity which leaves no room for the needs of economic growth which creates new jobs. we have a duty to call for measures to support growth and employment, finally going beyond the mere need for a balance between investment and austerity. we also want to draw attention to the worrying situation of payments: the experience of 2011 and 2012 must not be repeated and the council can no longer claim to decide a priori on a final level of payments on the basis of political considerations, without taking into account the impact on commitments made in the past.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the general guidelines for the 2013 budget as they take note of the economic crisis affecting europe, and propose serious and decisive measures for our future, such as the need to intensify collective efforts for the effectiveness of actions undertaken, specific actions and increased budgetary efforts to promote growth and employment. support for competitiveness is essential, with investments that would increase jobs, especially for young people who, through education, mobility and technological knowledge, are the main actors in the future results that are hoped to be achieved with the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i believe that an effective solution to the delicate issue of payments must be found as soon as possible, especially since 2013 will be the last year of the current multiannual financial framework, by which time a significant amount of outstanding payments will have to be settled. i also believe that it is essential to use the union budget to boost the economy and get out of the crisis by promoting growth and, in particular, youth employment and small and medium-sized enterprises, which, let us not forget, are the backbone of the european economy. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − i am very pleased with the outcome of today's vote on the guidelines for the 2013 eu budget. as you all know, it is not easy to talk about the budget in times of crisis, especially when we consider the measures taken in each individual member state. balancing austerity and rigour on the one hand, with targeted investment and ambitious targets on the other, is not easy. but the message i wanted to send with the report which has just been adopted by a large majority in this house is that we must use the proven added value of the union budget, as an investment budget, to bring europe out of the crisis and stimulate growth, development and employment, with particular reference to youth employment. these are the objectives of our political action, these are the answers we want to give to our citizens, showing them that european resources, used efficiently and in a coordinated way, are capable of producing tangible effects in their daily lives.

in writing. − whereas the budget of the european union must play a decisive role as a tool to ensure timely and coordinated action in all sectors in order to mitigate the effects of the crisis on the real economy and to act as a catalyst to stimulate investment, growth and job creation in europe; agreeing with the importance of well-coordinated, consistent and timely implementation of shared political priorities and commitments at national and european level, i vote in favour.

in writing. - with the adoption of the budgetary guidelines, we presented the priorities for expenditure for 2013, thus trying to make our weight felt as co-legislators with the council, so that the needs of this assembly can be made known. as also mentioned in the text on the guidelines, we ask governments and therefore the council not to propose artificial cuts to the 2013 community budget which would otherwise risk not covering real needs and outstanding payments. we want to avoid a repeat of last december, when the european commission was unable to honour its contractual commitments. the themes of the 2013 budget will be youth employment and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). without denying the importance of these two chapters, i would like to point out that agriculture remains a central issue in the development of european spending policy, where operators in the sector have long been calling for simplification and transparency for the paying agencies, and above all for clarity on the sanctions to be applied to those who do not comply with the commitments made under the cap. a budget at least as large or larger than last year's is therefore essential to keep alive such a vital sector for the whole eu.

in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of this proposal to set up a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, since it is undeniable that these problems have a crossborder dimension, affecting all the countries of the union, and it would therefore be desirable to propose common and shared solutions to combat these phenomena. italy can be seen as a positive example in this respect, thanks in particular to the measures taken in recent years by former interior minister roberto maroni, which have enabled extraordinary results to be achieved, which had never been achieved before. the basis for a serious fight against organised crime and illegal activities in general must therefore necessarily be a clear political will. let us hope that europe can show the same determination: we in the league will endeavour to bring our ideas and initiatives to brussels and strasbourg, which have certainly brought good results in italy.
in writing. the vote decided the setting up of a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, which will have various tasks. first, the commission - which will be composed of 45 members - will have to analyse and assess the current state of implementation of the union's anti-corruption legislation as well as monitor its compatibility with fundamental rights. to establish the necessary contacts, it will have to make visits and organise hearings with the institutions of the european union, international, european and national institutions, national parliaments and governments of the member states and third countries, and with representatives of the scientific community, the business community and civil society. the term of office of the special committee shall be 12 months from the date of its establishment, with the possibility of extension.

in writing. − according to the latest data, judicial training is currently far from the commission's target of being accessible to half of the legal professionals in the european union. to this end, it is necessary to coordinate the training provided by existing judicial training institutions and to facilitate and promote professional dialogue and contacts. this vote could also allow judges to take part in erasmus exchanges and training courses abroad. in addition, it lays the foundations for the organisation of an annual forum where judges at all levels can hold discussions on areas that have caused recent litigation or legal difficulties. this will encourage discussion, establish contacts and create channels of communication. this forum could also provide competent authorities, training providers and experts, including universities and professional organisations, with the opportunity to discuss judicial training policies and the future of legal education in europe.

in writing. - today, in strasbourg, a resolution was voted in plenary on child labour in the cocoa sector and the european parliament gave its consent to a new international agreement on cocoa trade and production which will also provide valuable instruments to tackle the problem. many children working in cocoa fields are involved in dangerous activities, such as exposure to pesticides and child trafficking. the agreement should also introduce a traceability system controlled by an accredited third body and require signatories to collect and analyse data, resulting from appropriate studies, which can provide clear statistics on child exploitation in the cocoa production sector. the european union, as the world's largest consumer of cocoa and home to many chocolate producers, cannot remain silent in the face of this injustice and cannot fail to take measures to ensure the legality of production.
in writing. - my vote in favour of this resolution is motivated by the need to stress at all times that trade with our international partners must always be conducted with respect for human rights. in this case, the committee on international trade has drawn up a text which accurately highlights the facts of a serious phenomenon such as child labour in the cocoa production sector. it will be difficult to eradicate these phenomena, but it is the duty of the european institutions to try to do so, even with resolutions such as this one.
in writing. - it is estimated that there are over 215 million child workers in the world, 152 million of whom are under 15 years old and 115 million of whom are engaged in hazardous work. considering that 70% of the world's cocoa production is grown in west africa and that some 7.5 million people are employed in cocoa production in that region, there is a need to protect children and young people from exploitation. this vote calls on all those involved in the cultivation and processing of cocoa beans and cocoa products - namely governments, the global industry, cocoa producers, trade unions, non-governmental organisations and consumers - to take their respective responsibilities in the fight against all forms of forced child labour and child trafficking, to share expertise and to work together to eliminate child labour from the cocoa supply chain.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 2010 international cocoa agreement. in 2010, the conference of the parties agreed on a new text, which effectively replaced the 2001 agreement. it is an important step forward as it aims to bring more transparency and sustainability to an industry on which the lives of 50 million people worldwide depend. in particular, the agreement aims to promote international cooperation in the world cocoa economy; provide an appropriate forum for discussion of all cocoa-related issues between governments and with the private sector; to contribute to the strengthening of the national cocoa economies of the member states; seeking fair prices that generate fair revenues for producers and consumers; to promote an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable cocoa economy; to promote transparency in the operation of the world cocoa economy and the removal of barriers to trade. the 2010 international cocoa agreement will therefore have a positive impact on all actors involved in the cocoa economy, with the hope that it will also translate into tangible long-term benefits for small farmers and their communities.
in writing. - on the report on the approval of the 2010 cocoa agreement, i considered giving a favourable opinion. i believe that europe must act responsibly to ensure that the world cocoa market is fair, is socially and environmentally sustainable and guarantees a high quality final product, also because we europeans are the world's largest consumers of chocolate. i also welcome the promotion of cocoa production by small local farms, and i believe that this promotes a quality product and at the same time represents an opportunity for sustainable development for many countries. finally, i would like to stress the importance of promoting greater international cooperation and dialogue between all the stakeholders.
in writing. − this agreement will promote greater transparency in a market which is constantly expanding and with a constantly growing demand and will provide more scope for projects to support national cocoa economies and their capacity to respond to this demand. it also aims to pursue the objectives of a sustainable cocoa economy and the promotion of cocoa quality, and stresses the need to develop food safety procedures as well as ensuring fair prices and fair revenues. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
