in writing. − diabetes is one of the most widespread and common threats to eu citizens among non-communicable diseases. it is estimated that one tenth of the european population is affected by this disease. we must also take into account that this figure, taking into account the progressive ageing of the population, is set to increase, with forecasts reaching 16% in 2030. i therefore believe that we must respond to this threat in a concrete way and i think that one of the priority actions must be the choice to focus on prevention and information. european citizens need to be increasingly informed about the possible consequences of their dietary and social lifestyles on their lives and about the simple rules to be followed to avoid the onset of diabetes. on the other hand, in addition to prevention, more information is also needed in the management phase of the disease. in fact, some studies show that 75 percent of the sick are not receiving the most appropriate treatment. investing in research and leveraging prevention and a widespread information campaign are the initiatives to be implemented as soon as possible to reduce the impact of the disease on the european population.
in writing. − diabetes is one of the most common non-communicable diseases and is estimated to affect over 32 million eu citizens and is increasingly common, especially among children. i believe that in order to clearly identify risk factors, to carry out and implement research, to promote prevention and awareness-raising policies, it is appropriate to do so. in addition, standardised common criteria and methods for the collection of data on diabetes should be developed in order to coordinate, collect, monitor and manage, in collaboration with the member states, epidemiological data and data on direct and indirect costs related to the prevention and management of the disease, as no cure exists at present. since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the european union has extended its remit to include health, and i believe it is appropriate to promote the exchange of best practice between member states, improve the coordination of european research activities on diabetes and encourage interdisciplinary collaboration. for these reasons i shall vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. − diabetes is one of the most common non-communicable diseases, estimated to affect over 32 million eu citizens, or about 10% of the total population. due to the obesity epidemic, the ageing of the european population and other factors yet to be determined, the number of people with diabetes in europe is expected to increase by 16.6% by 2030. the vote lays the foundations for the development and implementation of a targeted eu strategy on the prevention, diagnosis and management of diabetes, as well as on diabetes information and research. common standardised criteria and methods for the collection of data on diabetes and for the establishment of coordination tools between the various member states will need to be developed. the member states will thus have to develop, implement and monitor national diabetes plans aimed at health promotion, reduction of risk factors, prediction, prevention, early diagnosis and treatment of diabetes.
in writing. - my vote on this resolution on the accession process of the fyrom was decidedly against. our position is firmly against the accession of this country to the eu, firstly because of the profound democratic deficit in its society and government institutions (which is also recognised in the resolution itself), but above all because the acceptance of fyrom into the union would also constitute a legitimation of the unacceptable historical falsifications promoted by the government of this country over the last 20 years, to the detriment of the cultural heritage on which the historical identity of europe and the west is based. i am also absolutely against statements that praise the country's commitment to the integration of the roma community. i therefore voted against.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the progress made by the former yugoslav republic of macedonia as it positively highlights some crucial elements of the country's eu accession process. the parliament's proposal is in the spirit of the commission's 2011 progress report, which welcomed the country's good performance in terms of political criteria, the acquis communautaire and the development of the market economy, but noted some remaining weaknesses, most notably the achievement of a full rule of law, reflected in the general inefficiency of the public administration and the failure to complete the internal market. in particular, i voted against the proposal to delete article 15 of this report because i believe that the identity of the macedonian people cannot and should not be degraded or denied. i also remain convinced of the need for the european parliament to promote dialogue at regional level and to promote the country's integration process while respecting the efforts now under way and the rights of all the parties concerned.
in writing. - i am opposed to the forthcoming accession of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia to the european union. i agree with the rapporteur that some progress has been made - progress in some respects too - just think of the last elections, economic reforms or the end of the parliamentary boycott. i am, however, puzzled by the accession, because there is still too much distance between the social and political institutions of the balkan country and those of the members of the european union. the sudden entry of a state, in which there is still separation and distrust between ethnic groups, could lead to an outbreak of tension within the union and slow down the path of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia towards a pluralist society.
in writing. - today's vote on the progress made by the former yugoslav republic of macedonia (fyrom) takes account of the difficult challenges facing the country. although much remains to be done, i am pleased with the progress made in the social field and in the fight against corruption, considering that in the last five years the country has gained 40 positions in the "tansparency international" corruption perception index. however, recent serious incidents of violence, the worst since 2001 when the country came to the brink of civil war, pitting the muslim-albanian minority against the orthodox christian-macedonian majority, are of concern. in line with the 2011 progress report, i deplore the risk that forms of power sharing will institutionalize ethnicities and transform the country into a bi-national state, putting democratic principles at risk. i hope that the fundamental freedoms and rights guaranteed by the rule of law will be respected.
in writing. − the commission's 2011 progress report on eu enlargement to fyrom confirmed for the third consecutive year its positive assessment of policy criteria, the acquis communautaire and the development of the market economy, while noting some weaknesses in the area of the rule of law, which are reflected in the overall efficiency of the public administration and the internal market. the fact that for three years now no decision has been taken on the opening of accession negotiations with the former yugoslav republic of macedonia is a matter of grave concern. i think it is time to overcome the current stalemate, also to avoid fueling a general movement of disappointment in the country: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i therefore believe, as do the other member states, that athens and skopje must make a real effort to reach a compromise and to overcome the dispute over the country's name.
in writing. - i voted with satisfaction in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled by mr preda on the progress made by iceland towards its forthcoming accession to the european union, because i share his generally positive opinion. iceland is a country with a long and established democratic tradition, which has long been cooperating with the european union and has already adopted part of the community acquis by joining the schengen agreements and the european economic area. i am therefore convinced that the attention and respect shown so far for human rights will certainly be confirmed in the new constitution currently being drafted. the icelandic authorities have also provided evidence that the icelandic economy is in a difficult economic situation. i hope that the negotiations on fisheries, which at the moment seem to be the most critical, will also be able to be resolved soon with an agreement which takes account of the interests of all the parties concerned. however, recent polling data, which suggest that 67% of icelanders would oppose membership, raise some concerns: the eu must reverse this negative trend by regaining its credibility.
in writing. − considering that iceland fulfils the copenhagen criteria and that accession negotiations with iceland started on 27 july 2010 and that the screening of the eu acquis is almost complete, it is a fact that iceland's accession to the european union is closer. in addition, the country already cooperates closely with the european union, having acceded to the european economic area, the schengen agreements and the dublin ii regulation, and has therefore already adopted a significant part of the acquis. the icelandic government is promoting a well-informed and balanced debate on the accession process and on the participation of icelandic society in public discussions on accession to the european union. the opening of the european union information centre in iceland is an opportunity for the european union to provide the citizens of the country with all the information possible on all the consequences that accession may have for the country.
in writing. - the recent installation of a new government in bosnia and herzegovina on 10 february brought an end to the political deadlock that had been creating a constraint on the country's development. this provides a good basis for a revival of the european agenda in bosnia and herzegovina. among the most significant actions of the new government, i would mention the initiatives to implement the census, the approval of the state aid laws and the adaptation of the country's constitution to the provisions of the european convention on human rights (echr). i share the proposal put forward by mr pack, we must urge the bosnian authorities to make further efforts and steps towards meeting the eu accession criteria. however, i believe it is essential that bosnia-herzegovina complies with the sejdic-finci judgment, as well as with article 2 of the stabilisation and association agreement (saa), which provides greater guarantees in the field of human rights and democratic principles. the decision to dissolve the local office of the high representative is right and i think it will encourage greater accountability on the part of the bosnian authorities.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because i support the prospect of eu membership for bosnia. the european perspective is one of the most unifying factors amongst the people of the country. nevertheless, to go further with the accession negotiations, there is the need to strengthen the rule of law in bosnia. corruption continues to seriously plague its socio-economic and political development. trafficking in human beings, especially women and girls, is still a serious problem there. for these reasons we ask the bosnian government to ensure the establishment of an independent, impartial and effective judicial system in line with eu and international standards. i value this text as a good starting point to encourage bosnia to take further concrete steps to put the country firmly back on track towards the eu.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution on bosnia and herzegovina's progress on the roadmap towards eu membership. the enlargement of the union to the balkan region is one of the eu's most dangerous foreign policy choices, as most of the states in this region (including bosnia and herzegovina) continue to be affected by high levels of government corruption and patronage, strong inter-ethnic tensions and the growing religious fundamentalism of islamic communities. opening the eu's doors to countries that are still heavily affected by socio-political instability is an unacceptable choice, dangerous for the security of eu citizens.
in writing. - i express my support for this resolution, which we are voting at a most appropriate time in the light of the recent political developments in bosnia-herzegovina. after more than a year of deadlock, a new government took office in february and it is hoped that the agreement reached will allow the country to begin the reforms needed to move closer to the eu. in addition to strengthening relations with the other countries in the balkan region and taking full advantage of the integration competences hitherto held by the eu special representative and head of delegation, the country will have to embark on a path towards stabilisation and socioeconomic development that does not leave it behind on the path to accession. as commissioner füle has also pointed out, this path has been followed up to date too slowly and in an uncoordinated manner. i believe that the eu should help bosnia and herzegovina by supporting it in setting a clear agenda with the main objectives of fighting corruption at all levels of society, too high unemployment and the precarious state of the judiciary, the main factors that have so far slowed down investment and growth.
in writing. - this report, while highlighting the many obstacles to bosnia and herzegovina's accession to the european union, is nevertheless intended to state that the country must join. i do not believe that a country which is deeply divided internally and therefore incapable of producing laws and reforms, marked by corruption, the lack of an independent judiciary, insufficient legislative, executive or budgetary powers, and characterised by weak social dialogue and rising youth unemployment, can fulfil the commitments and obligations imposed by accession to the european union, so i voted against.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution, although there is no shortage of conclusions in mr pack's report which i can support. what does not convince me is the underlying argument, the idea that, despite the critical points, the process of bosnia-herzegovina's accession to the european union must proceed without pause. there are still too many doubts about the full powers of the balkan state. there are too many questions about the effective independence of the judiciary, which is a prerequisite for the rule of law. finally, there are too many criticisms that can be made of the country in terms of its economic fabric. the european union's role as a driving force for development and political stability requires a certain degree of convergence between the member states, which bosnia and herzegovina currently lacks.
in writing. − bosnia and herzegovina has been recognised as a potential candidate since the thessaloniki summit in 2003. the country has been part of the stabilisation and association process since 2000, but the stabilisation and association agreement (saa) was only signed in 2008; however, the treaty has not yet entered into force and the application for accession to the union has not yet been formally submitted. the ratification of the agreement by the last member state in february 2011 was supposed to lead to the entry into force of the saa within 40 days, but the failure of bosnia to comply with obligations under previous agreements led to the freezing of the saa. the commitments in question concern the adoption of state aid laws, the national census and the implementation of the judgments of the european court of human rights, which called for the amendment of the constitution to extend the passive electorate to members of ethnic minorities. despite the continuing difficulties of the internal political situation, i believe it is in our best interests to continue to maintain the european anchorage of the country, the only guarantee of stability and progress. in the current scenario, the enhanced eu presence on the ground plays a key role and can help to give new impetus to the country's internal reform process and thus to its european perspective.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i shall vote in accordance with the guidelines of my group, but that does not prevent me from expressing some of my views, even if they differ slightly from those of the group. our parliament's observers have verified that the russian elections were conducted in an orderly manner, with full guarantees for voters in respect of their freedom to cast their votes and the guarantee of secrecy of the vote. internet footage also allowed for remote control. president putin is certainly a strong, authoritative and enduring figure in russian politics but this does not automatically imply irregularity in the vote. in this sense i want to emphasize how dissent to putin was also guaranteed in his street demonstrations. the european parliament must take this into account by recognising an election result which saw vladimir putin elected president of russia, whether it likes it or not.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, it is again a pleasure to deal with the latest developments on eu activities in kazakhstan on behalf of vice-president/high representative ashton. kazakhstan is a key player in the wider region of central asia and an influential actor in international forums. it has recently held the chairmanship of the organisation for security and cooperation in europe (osce) and the organisation for islamic cooperation (oic). since its independence 20 years ago, it has been the european union’s policy to support kazakhstan’s economic and political progress. the eu has a strategic interest to further deepen our involvement with kazakhstan and to fully develop mutual political cooperation potentials, especially considering the rapidly evolving regional integration dynamics. kazakhstan is a pragmatic partner, open to reform and willing to explore opportunities. the eu is also an important trade and investment partner for kazakhstan. the recent start of negotiations on a new enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement with kazakhstan was a sign of the importance that the eu attaches to its cooperation with kazakhstan. however, strengthening eu-kazakhstan relations does not – and cannot – occur independently from the progress of political reforms in kazakhstan. the respect for common values of democracy, the rule of law and human rights are the basis for deepening our relations. this is a statement we jointly made with kazakhstan in 2009, and we stand by it. therefore, we maintain our position that the success of negotiations on the new agreement will be influenced by the advancement of political reforms and fulfilment of kazakhstan’s international commitments. in this context, we are concerned about the recent developments and the overall slow progress of political reform in kazakhstan, including the limited implementation of international commitments. according to independent observers from the osce, both the early presidential and early parliamentary elections in 2011 and 2012 fell short of meeting democratic principles. for the first time since kazakhstan’s independence, we have seen considerable social tension, including a number of terrorist attacks. the strike of oil workers that started in may 2011 culminated in violent clashes with the police in december 2011, resulting in 17 dead and about 110 injured. to cope with evolving security challenges and threats, the kazakh government has amended a number of laws over the past few months. it has introduced changes that seem to empower the state more and more, while restricting the rights and freedoms of citizens, civil society and political opposition. the vice-president/high representative received several questions from honourable members of the parliament about these developments and about the eu’s approach, opinions and actions taken. she and her service are actively following the situation in kazakhstan. over the past 11 months there have been more than 10 statements issued by catherine ashton herself, and by the eu, at the osce permanent council. on 17 december 2011, immediately after the violent clashes, the high representative’s spokesperson published a statement expressing concerns, calling for immediate investigation of the events and a peaceful solution to the situation of the striking oil workers. the european external action service and the eu delegation in astana have maintained regular contacts with the authorities, calling on kazakhstan to uphold its international obligations and commitments, in particular regarding freedom of expression, freedom of association and assembly. the prosecutor general’s office in kazakhstan is carrying out an investigation, and the eu has requested that this process be thorough, transparent and not used to target any specific group or intimidate the kazakh opposition. on 2 february the vice-president/high representative met with the kazakh minister of foreign affairs, mr kazykhanov, where she expressed her concerns and raised specifically the issue of the arrest of a number of opposition activists, including mr kozlov, leader of the alga opposition movement and mr vinyavski, an independent journalist. as a follow-up, on 9 february the eu delegation in astana carried out a démarche, asking for information on the health of mr kozlov and access to him for his wife and lawyer. as a result, the eu delegation visited mr kozlov in a military hospital in almaty where he had undergone surgery. the eu delegation was able to confirm that he had not been ill-treated and that his surgery was due to a previously-existing health issue, which was not an urgent matter. the eu’s efforts and communication with the authorities, notably the cases discussed in the regular human rights dialogue with kazakhstan, also yielded results. the jailed human rights activist mr zhovtis was granted amnesty and released in february 2012. the trade union lawyer, natalya sokolova, who was sentenced to six years due to her role in the strikes, was also released, on 7 march, and her sentence was replaced by a three-year conditional sentence. the eu has several times expressed its readiness to provide support to kazakhstan for reforms and for the investigation of the events in december, as well as to address the underlying socio-economic problems that led to tensions in the country to begin with.the eu is funding several projects that are already tackling issues that contribute directly to the improvement of the social, economic and political situation. these include projects on regional development, public service reform and modernisation, support for judicial and legal reform, for local governance and for civil society development, as well as several projects relating to democracy and human rights. promoting and supporting reforms in these areas, and further establishing relevant actors, are priorities both for civil society and the kazakhstani authorities, at both central and regional levels. we also expect that the perspective and negotiation process of the new enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement will provide a stimulus for kazakhstan to make more progress, notably in enhancing freedom of expression and freedom of association and encouraging real political pluralism. to motivate progress, we foresee including fundamental political and economic reform commitments in the new agreement, including aligning regulations to eu norms and standards, and essential political clauses on human rights and the rule of law. kazakhstan’s commitments to these fundamental principles will be a strong and clear expression of its will to step up political and economic reforms. wto accession would also be a clear expression that the country is taking economic transition seriously and is ready to commit to multilateral rules and would show that kazakhstan is willing to bring increased legal certainty to our relations. this is in the interest not only of kazakhstan but also of the eu and the wider international community. this is, by no means, a simple process. we are only at the beginning of these important negotiations. however, we are determined to ensure that the european union continues to stand alongside the republic of kazakhstan and its citizens, both as a friend and a partner, on the path of political reform and economic development. in this endeavour we count on the support of the european parliament and we look forward to the resolution that you will adopt tomorrow.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, thank you again for giving me the opportunity to speak on nigeria on behalf of the high representative. it is a pleasure to be here today to discuss this matter. nigeria is at a crucial juncture. president jonathan’s reform policy can shape nigeria’s future. its democracy is consolidating and its economy is growing rapidly. nigeria has the potential to become the biggest economy in sub-saharan africa within a few years. it plays a major role on the african continent, it was a member of the security council last year and is a member of the human rights commission this year. former president obasanjo recently led the economic community of west african states (ecowas) – african union mission in dakar to monitor the elections and this sent a strong message in support of democracy and people’s rights. i would like to thank the honourable members for their interest in nigeria for recent months. i say this with particular conviction, because i had the pleasure of representing high representative/vice-president ashton at the recent ministerial meeting with nigeria in abuja on 8 february. it was a remarkable occasion and a very positive one. nigeria still faces crucial challenges: the european union strongly condemns the recent attacks carried out by boko haram, with appalling loss of human lives. the christmas bombings of churches and the recent suicide attack on a church in jos on 26 february and again on 11 march are deeply shocking. so are all of the other attacks, including that in kano some weeks ago. they should all be condemned. unfortunately, the number of attacks and human losses are increasing every day in an unacceptable spiral of violence. high representative ashton has repeatedly expressed her solidarity and sympathy with the victims, the injured and their families. i also wish to make use of this opportunity to express our profound sadness at the loss of life of two european hostages in nigeria on 8 march. we condemn in the strongest possible terms criminal actions such as the taking of hostages. our heartfelt condolences go to their families for the irreplaceable loss they have faced. may they find strength in this difficult time. the eu stands alongside the nigerian authorities in their fight against terrorism, to protect all citizens, in particular the most vulnerable, and to preserve the right to life and the rule of law. the root causes of boko haram are many, but it is no coincidence that it is strongest in the north of the country, which has some of the worst socio-economic indicators in africa. nigeria’s north-east region is one of the world’s forgotten emergencies: the grievances there need to be addressed urgently, and we as partners and friends have promised the government to help them do so. boko haram is targeting the secular democratic state, and muslims and christians. nigeria remains a secular state with religious freedom firmly enshrined in its constitution. however, boko haram is trying to exploit the ethno-religious differences, which will always exist in a country as big and diverse as nigeria. nigeria’s complex problems certainly have religious dimensions, but they cannot simply be blamed on religion. we have a well-established regular local human rights dialogue with nigeria, during which all important issues, including freedom of religion or belief, are raised. the most recent such dialogue meeting took place in february this year. the eu is committed to supporting the government and people of nigeria in ensuring religion is not misused to legitimise politically or criminally motivated violence. i would like to add that the eu has been very active on the issue of freedom of religion or belief, especially during the last two years, as many countries – not only nigeria – have experienced a surge of acts of religious hatred and violence. we have used our full range of instruments, either bilaterally or in multilateral fora, in new york and geneva, to be at the forefront of the fight against religious intolerance. we will continue to do so. eu delegations have been requested to follow closely the situation of their host countries and report on issues and actions taken. as required by the eu foreign affairs ministers in february 2011, the overall action of the eu in this respect should be reviewed by the foreign affairs council in the coming months. there are, fortunately, some positive signs of nigerians taking initiatives to ease the situation, such as the association of muslim students, who exposed on facebook the fallacies of boko haram. important leaders of islam in nigeria have rejected boko haram as misguided and murderous fanatics. nigeria’s catholic bishops have highlighted that the boko haram crisis has also brought the best out of many nigerians such as muslims and christians protecting each other. the government is also making progress in developing and implementing a comprehensive counter-terrorism strategy, and several prominent boko haram members have been arrested. during my meetings with the nigerian government in february, i encouraged them to explore this counter-terrorism strategy further. nigeria matters to the wider world. it plays a big stabilising role in the region. it is the fourth-largest oil exporter in the world and the second most important exporter of natural gas to the eu. nigeria is firmly committed to the un, is a major provider of un peacekeepers and is vocal and robust in its support for democracies and freedom. nigeria’s positions in the recent ivorian and libyan crises speak for themselves. in short, i found a strong and open african partner, which in many ways shares our views and our values. the ministerial meeting resulted in several openings, which we should now explore further. one is the agreement on establishing a local dialogue on peace, security and stability, and others openings are nigeria’s interest in climate change and rio+20. it was interesting to hear from nigeria’s leaders how they see their economic development. they are diversifying to reduce their dependence on oil and gas, investing in infrastructure and agriculture, and focusing on job creation for their young and growing population of 160 million people. i heard many times that nigeria strongly encourages european investment and participation in its strong growth. on the other hand, nigeria faces serious challenges, not least widespread poverty. better governance, maintaining ethnic harmony and fighting corruption and crime are some of the big tasks it faces. although nigeria’s human rights record has improved steadily in recent years, there are still areas where further improvement could be achieved. the security situation in the niger delta, although improving, remains fragile. the region is vital for the national economy because of its oil production so ensuring its peaceful development is essential. the eu is currently implementing a eur 200 million programme to assist the development of the region. bricks, stones and words can be used to separate people, but they can also build bridges. therefore, honourable members, i call upon you to use your contacts with nigerians to support and facilitate this absolutely essential bridge-building with nigeria and i look forward to the resolution that the european parliament will adopt tomorrow.

member of the commission. − madam president, that was a very emotional debate. the accusation that the eu is not supporting the repatriation of the two italian servicemen is a false accusation. i would mention just a couple of the steps it has taken. the eu has made approaches to the indian ministry of external affairs, to the indian chargé d’affaires in brussels, and to the indian deputy national security advisor, and that is not all. baroness ashton is fully committed to doing everything we can do from the eu side, but there is no magic wand solution. however, we are fully committed and we will take full care of the issue. on atalanta, this has actually been much more successful than was said; the number of ships in the hands of pirates has been reduced from 20 to eight. while there is still concern over around 200 hostages, there are sufficient resources for this year at least, and good coordination. on the somalia strategy, it is true that for 20 years there has not been sufficient international involvement, but the eu alone does not hold the magic key to solving somalia’s problems. first of all, somalia needs legitimate representatives, and today we have the transitional institutions. they are the only institutions we have in that country, and we should support them because of this. second, we support – and i mentioned the figures – the security operations. it is not easy to fight al-shabaab. now, the number of african troops that are risking their lives, and taking quite heavy casualties – many soldiers from burundi and uganda have lost their lives fighting al-shabaab and preserving security – has increased to 17 000, so that might make a difference. however, the fact that a blast was reported at the presidential palace in mogadishu today shows that the fight to ensure security is not an easy one. we have made quite substantial investments in development and humanitarian aid – i have mentioned the figures – and it is true that we are doing more in somaliland and in puntland, where the security situation is better. however, it would not be true to say that we are not doing everything in our power. we are actually using all the financial resources that the member states are prepared to give us. on international shipping, we need the imo. the imo has responded to the call we made to it by organising a conference on how to protect merchant shipping. that conference will be held in may. i could go on and on, but my point is that we need to find a solution to the security situation in somalia and its political development. this is what is needed. the accusations that the eu provoked the crisis are ridiculous. we have not provoked the crisis. we are trying to resolve the crisis, as far as this is in our powers. by the way, last year there was only one eu vessel taken in somali waters. this is a lot about alliances. the eu is doing its full share. we are engaging with our international partners. it is very important to understand that the eu’s efforts alone cannot provide a lasting solution to this issue. we need other members of the international community, and the bigger countries, to become fully involved. only then will we be able to find, step by step, lasting solutions to fully eradicating piracy.

member of the commission. − mr president, the 2050 roadmap communication provides a solid basis for discussing the further development of eu climate policies. it represents an incredibly strong signal for the whole process in this parliament on this issue. i would like to thank in particular the rapporteurs: chris davies from the committee on the environment, public health and food safety and mario pirillo from the committee on industry, research and energy. it sends a very strong message about what this is all about, namely the environment and industry going hand in hand and seeing that this is not harming the potential in europe and is actually something that can enhance our growth. we just heard chris davies, a liberal, say that financial mechanisms alone are not enough, and often it also takes regulation: that is also a very clear statement and is exactly what the low carbon roadmap is about. after the second failure of the environment council to adopt council conclusions on the 2050 roadmap, it is even more important that the european parliament gives its support to an ambitious eu climate policy in line with the global requirements, integrating the discussion on the short-term policy needs with the longer-term perspective. although one country blocked the final compromise in the council, 26 member states explicitly asked the commission to move forward. we should not allow the most reluctant among us to dictate the pace of the rest. this is a very clear signal coming out of the european parliament today: that you really want us to move forward and take the measures needed. we welcome the report, as it endorses the central findings of the commission’s 2050 roadmap – in particular the interim milestones for domestic greenhouse gas emissions reductions, as set out in the roadmap. in the context of the difficult economic circumstances we are facing, the european parliament’s report strikes the right balance and creates the right vision. it is of paramount importance that parliament recognises that a gradual, cost-effective transition to a low-carbon economy passes through the milestones for domestic greenhouse gas reductions of 40% by 2030 and 60% by 2040 in order to achieve at least 80% by 2050 as compared to 1990. this is strong guidance for our policy for decades to come. it is the starting point for further work related to the preparation of the 2030 policy framework, which is reasonably foreseeable and the focus of most current investors. business needs clarity in the long term in order to be able to keep costs down. if there is one thing business always asks from us as politicians and regulators, it is long-term predictability. if you are a company, a sector or an investor, you are already looking beyond 2020 and planning investments which have a much more distant horizon. the report confirms that, if the eu delivers on its current policies – including its commitment to achieve a 20% energy efficiency improvement by 2020 – this would add a further 5% greenhouse gas reduction through domestic action. while this does not require any change to our current targets for 2020, it shows a very practical and economical way to achieve higher reductions in line with the cost-effective pathway to 2050. the energy efficiency directive will play a vital role here in providing the legal framework for reaching the 20% efficiency target. as you know, we are by no means on track to meet that. the report also recognises that the ets remains the principal instrument of the eu climate policy, though not the only one. the commission is monitoring the situation closely. for the longer term, we take note of the various proposals put forward by the european parliament for future changes to the ets. we will assess how to take these into account in our further work. with regard to the risk of carbon leakage, i understand that this is present throughout the report, but the eu has included specific measures in the climate and energy package, as the report also states. these are adequate. border measures are not necessary and are counter-productive, at least at the moment. as i have said before, they are a tool in the toolbox, but they should stay there for as long as we can move forward through other means. as outlined in the roadmap, we will continue to observe the international situation in order to ensure that these measures remain adequate. in the commission we fully share the strong focus set on energy efficiency and renewables. this is key to combining emission reductions, improved energy security and sustainable growth and jobs. in this respect, the commission urges the council and parliament to reach an agreement on the energy efficiency directive rapidly. in addition, the commission will soon come forward with a communication considering the eu’s strategy on renewable energy post 2020. we strongly support parliament’s call for enhanced action to reduce emissions in the power, industry, transport and agriculture sectors. let me highlight just one example from the transport sector. the report affirms that the commission should be proposing ways of ensuring that average co2 emissions from new cars meet the target of not more than 95g/km by 2020. as requested in the existing legislation, the commission will this year produce a proposal to establish the modalities for reaching this target. furthermore, the commission intends to submit a proposal addressing emissions of hfcs and other fluorinated greenhouse gases in the second half of this year, which is also mentioned in the report. finally, we also welcome the balanced considerations on competitiveness, research, innovation, growth and jobs in the context of moving to a low-carbon economy, confirming the main conclusions of the commission assessments. last but not least, we thank you very much for supporting the commission’s proposal for the next multiannual financial framework and the intention to a very substantial degree to mainstream climate action in it. the commission has proposed to increase the proportion of climate-related expenditure to at least 20% of the whole budget, either directly on climate action or through other policies where climate action is also addressed and where the different initiatives will help us move in a greener direction and the direction of a low carbon economy. we count on your support on this matter in the upcoming budgetary discussions. in conclusion, i would encourage the european parliament to adopt the resolution as a further step for developing the appropriate policy framework for the transition to a competitive, energy-secure and resource-efficient low carbon economy. what you are about to adopt today will send a very strong and timely signal that europe is ready to move on. thank you very much for that.

in writing. − in 2011, the commission presented a strategy paper setting out an ambitious european pathway to reduce greenhouse gas emissions after 2020: reducing emissions by 40% in 2030, 60% in 2040 and reaching a reduction of 80-95% in 2050. this document, in defining a european environmental strategy, has a major impact on the industrial policy of the member states. the report makes even more stringent demands than those outlined by the commission with more ambitious climate targets by 2020 and binding european targets beyond 2030, irrespective of the achievement of a global climate agreement. i am against a change in the emission reduction commitments already made for 2020, mainly because the emission reduction commitments made under the 'climate and energy package' approved in 2008 are the result of a long and difficult political negotiation which has allowed a compromise to be reached between member states to distribute efforts fairly and safeguard the competitiveness of the respective sectors involved. in addition, the european union must not, in pursuing its climate objectives, change the regulatory framework already adopted, risking further penalising european businesses vis-à-vis global partners.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr davies on the roadmap to a low-carbon economy by 2050 because i believe that environmental issues should not be underestimated and should be one of the eu's top priorities. reducing dependence on fossil fuels is essential to safeguarding the climate and reducing pollution, both to protect the global environment and to protect human health. the benefits of these choices will also be felt in the economic and commercial sector, reducing the heavy import of oil from third countries. we must be careful, however, that we are not the only ones to impose such strict rules and limitations: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. only uniform rules can be effective in combating pollution and global warming. otherwise, we will not only fail, but we will risk being exposed to ruthless competition from economies whose success is based on the very absence of restrictive environmental and social regulations such as ours.
in writing. − the need for the international economy to move increasingly towards a production system based on reducing carbon emissions is a requirement imposed on us by the increasingly looming risk of irreversible climate change, as well as by the need to gradually free our production system from the use of exhaustible sources. however, it is simply incomprehensible - and in many ways out of time and history - that the forces on the right have insisted on re-proposing the nuclear issue. it is out of date and out of date, as are all the recommendations on the safety of power stations which have been repeatedly put before us and which have been consistently refuted by the facts. this is even more unthinkable in a country like italy, where after almost 30 years of the closure of the power stations, we still have waste that has not been disposed of and where, a short time ago, a new popular consultation reaffirmed the absolute opposition to the reintroduction of nuclear power. we therefore ask that the right objective, the reduction of emissions and the transition to a renewable energy economy, should not become the pretext for letting a tool that has proved to be unsafe and dangerous, and which the people of europe have therefore chosen to abandon, back through the window.
in writing. - the emissions game no longer has the same rules for everyone. the eu's climate and energy package was adopted with the assurance that other major emitters would make similar commitments, but this has not happened and some major economies have already said that it will not happen in the near future. furthermore, given that the union's gdp growth has been almost stagnant since the package came into force, unlike in other countries not applying such measures, i believe that the current climate strategy is a factor in the slowdown of economic recovery and that, consequently, the adoption of new and more restrictive very long-term limits, such as those proposed in this report, would risk losing europe the race to be competitive on the global market. that is why i voted against.
in writing. − the environmental challenges facing the planet are urgent and require immediate action. as the european union we can do a lot to reduce carbon emissions with the international target of an 80% reduction in emissions compared to 1990. in this difficult challenge, all sectors of manufacturing and industrial processing contribute to the 2050 target and to the intermediate targets, as called for in the report, of 2030 and 2040. we are all called upon to do our part, at european level, to make our contribution to reducing carbon emissions in the atmosphere a concrete and achievable goal.
in writing. − europe cannot tackle the climate and environmental problems of the entire planet on its own: i think it is absurd that the european union should want to proceed unilaterally, by proposing stricter limits on carbon emissions. i am aware that we must move in this direction, but this must not be at the expense of the competitiveness of the whole economic system. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. the newly emerging countries, whose growth rates are staggering in comparison with the stagnating european economy, have not been confronted with these problems, nor have the united states of america, which has never even agreed to respect commitments which all the other developed countries have long since made. the european union can be an example in meeting the challenge of climate change, but not by acting in this self-destructive way: i think that the commission should use its influence, if it counts for anything, to persuade all the major economies to come together in a common and sensible action in this direction, in defence of our planet and our own future.
in writing. − with this vote, the european union will be able to continue to invest in processes that use energy and resources much more efficiently. europe must continue along the path of the competitive economy, even if the decision-making process is too often slow. the european union will only be able to build and exercise lasting leadership by reducing co2 emissions and substantially increasing the level of investment to create a leading industrial sector.
in writing. − while an initiative document, the report responds to a strategy paper from the european commission in march 2011, in which the commission set out an ambitious european pathway to reduce greenhouse gas emissions after 2020: reducing emissions by 40% in 2030, 60% in 2040 and reaching a reduction of 80-95% in 2050. the draft report by john davies intends to make even more stringent demands than those outlined by the european commission, in particular a 25% climate target by 2020 and binding european targets for 2030 and beyond, irrespective of the achievement of a global climate agreement. the report also argues that the european commission needs to intervene in the current regulatory framework for the emissions trading system by 2020, either by withdrawing emission allowances from the market, or by increasing the annual emission reduction factor at european level. both measures, if introduced, would in fact change the decisions taken by member states on the european commitment to combat climate change by 2020. with this declaration of vote i wish to express my opposition to more demanding changes to the commitments already made for the reduction of emissions by 2020

in writing. − in early february, the party for freedom in the netherlands launched an online complaint site called "meldpunt midden en oost europeanen", inviting people to submit complaints about the "massive labour migration" of "citizens from central and eastern europe". all this is against the free movement of citizens in the european union. the vote strongly condemns the website run by the pvv, as it is contrary to the fundamental european values of human dignity, freedom, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights and risks destroying the very foundation of the union, which is pluralism, non-discrimination, tolerance, justice, solidarity and freedom of movement. it is also necessary that the dutch government should intervene and verify whether this initiative has turned into incitement to hatred.

in writing. − i support this resolution because the past months have been marked by a deterioration of the human rights situation in kazakhstan. the violent crackdown by the police forces on demonstrators in zhanaozen in december must be condemned and an independent investigation of the events is necessary. in addition to that, in the osce/odihr-led international delegation, several observers found that the 15 january 2012 parliamentary elections did not meet fundamental principles of democratic elections. for these reasons, with this text we ask the kazakh government to rapidly improve respect for freedom of expression and to respect international election standards.
in writing. − the european union and kazakhstan could benefit greatly from closer cooperation. economic cooperation must go hand in hand with political cooperation and be based on the political will to implement and defend common values, given the key role played by kazakhstan in the socioeconomic development of central asia and in the stability and security of the region. however, the events of 16 december 2011 in the kazakh district of zhanaozen, in which 17 people were killed and 110 injured, are of concern. the vote strongly condemns the violent police repression of the demonstrators in zhanaozen and calls for an independent and credible investigation into the incident, with the participation of an international team.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because the recent violence in nigeria, carried out by the boko haram criminal cartel must be strongly condemned by the international community. boko haram is blamed for the deaths of more than 900 people in roughly 160 separate attacks since july 2009. a contribution to put a definitive end to this awful situation is a wider examination of the root causes of the conflict. it is essential to avoid simplistic explanations based only on the label ‘terrorism’ or ‘religion’. although nigeria is the world’s eighth largest oil producer, the majority of its 148 million inhabitants live below the poverty line. a peaceful resolution of conflicts implies fair access to resources and a redistribution of revenues from the oil market. in addition to that, we must reaffirm the importance of an independent, impartial and accessible judiciary system to stop the impunity and to enhance respect for the rule of law and the fundamental rights of the population. for all these reasons, with this text we called upon the federal government of nigeria to fight corruption, poverty and inequality and to push for reforms aimed at creating a democratic, stable, free state which takes into account human rights.
in writing. the climate of renewed violence in nigeria for more than two months now required a firm condemnation by the european union. the situation in the african state is very worrying as regards the protection of both human and religious rights. the murder of 185 christians on 20 january is cruel testimony to a violent climate that shows no sign of stopping its hatred and which bases its foundations on religious discrimination. among other incidents, i think it is right to mention the kidnapping and subsequent execution of the italian engineer franco lamolinara, whose family members i extend my heartfelt condolences to. it is our duty to take all the necessary cooperation measures to ensure that the situation in nigeria returns to normal as soon as possible, by encouraging interreligious dialogue and, above all, freedom of thought.
in writing. − the situation in nigeria has deteriorated dramatically in recent months: the killing of two european civilian hostages, including italian franco lamolinara, following a kidnapping by the islamist terrorist group boko haram, was reported last week. this is unfortunately only the latest in a long series of attacks by this sect, including, and this is also of profound significance, the attacks on several christian churches on christmas day last year, which led to the death of dozens of people. i had already expressed my concern about the situation in nigeria earlier this year by addressing a question to high representative ashton, who assured me that the european union would act appropriately. so far i do not think that has happened, but we hope that this joint resolution which i have supported will help to try to bring the necessary stability to the interior of nigeria.
in writing. − in nigeria, the latest wave of gun and bomb attacks by the islamist terrorist sect boko haram in kano on 20 january killed at least 185 people. boko haram warned kano residents through leaflets distributed at night in the city that attacks on security services would continue and urged them to resist as the group struggles to establish an "islamic system". this vote underlines the importance of regional cooperation in dealing with the threat posed by a possible link between boko haram and aqim. the countries of the region should strengthen their cooperation, including through the relevant regional organisations, in order to prevent synergies between the two groups.
in writing. − water is the key to life, a determining factor for economic growth and prosperity, through activities such as agriculture, commercial fisheries, energy production, manufacturing, transport and tourism. water is also the crucial factor in the urbanization of territories and the source of many geopolitical conflicts. today we are witnessing a real imbalance in ecosystems, which poses a risk not only to the climate regulation that makes the planet work, but a serious danger to human health and the quality of life. i hope that in the coming days, during the sixth world water forum in marseille, concrete proposals will be discussed with a 'multi-level governance' approach in support of poverty and hunger halving and environmental sustainability. the protection of water resources, their quality and availability is a responsibility that each of us must assume.
in writing. − despite the efforts made by the international community in recent decades, the figures which describe the world situation in terms of water use and quality still present a scenario which is unacceptable, both from a health and ethical point of view. in fact, according to the latest figures, over 800 million people drink from unsafe sources, and as many as 2.5 million children die each year because of a lack of water supply and quality. these are numbers that require a strong stance. that is why i think it is very important that the european union presents itself at the next world water forum, to be held in marseille from 12 to 17 march, with a strong common vision, where the issues that the eu has long placed at the top of its agenda are clearly outlined, namely the protection of water resources and greater efficiency (and consequently a reduction in waste) in their use.
in writing. − efficient management of the world's water resources has a direct impact on human health, energy production, agriculture and food security, and is a key prerequisite for poverty reduction. the world water forum provides a platform where the water community and policy and decision makers from all regions of the world come together to seek solutions to achieve water security. i hope that during the forum concrete commitments will be made to follow up the key priorities for action identified in this area, ensuring the well-being of all and contributing to global economic development.
in writing. − nearly half the population living in developing countries lack sanitation facilities, over 800 million people still use unsafe sources for drinking water and have inadequate access to safe water and sanitation. a critical and sometimes dramatic situation for millions of people. this vote will seek to achieve the un millennium development goals in the field of water and sanitation as soon as possible, taking into account also the relevant outcomes of the rio+20 conference on sustainable development. the debate in the world water forum should focus on strategies and solutions for agricultural and economic development that ensure a high level of accessibility to water resources and water quality.

and government put it at the council meeting in january – must be pursued in parallel with fiscal consolidation and this is, as you are aware, where the eib comes into play. it comes into play with long-term investment in key drivers of economic expansion. i welcome your backing for our commitment to focus on the knowledge triangle of research and development, innovation and education. indeed, investment in that area is vital for europe if it does not want to be sidelined by new actors in the global game. you will be aware that, since 2008, the eib has, on request by the member states and as a timely targeted temporary measure, extended extraordinary lending volumes in support of growth and jobs. last year the bank provided its highest ever contribution to the real economy: some eur 60 billion actually disbursed to clients at favourable conditions and long tenors. however, this has brought us to a limit, and this was clear from the beginning. this is because the eib does not spend taxpayers’ money but obtains all the resources it needs for lending by borrowing on the markets – eur 76 billion last year, almost half of which was from countries outside the european union which, by the way, is also an indication of trust and confidence in the european union. this gradual decrease which we now have in the operation plan was planned, foreseen and necessary for us to protect the finaical strength of the bank and retain the full confidence of our investors. however, it is definitely not satisfactory; i agree with that as well. so how do we reconcile this decrease in lending volumes with the request from our shareholders to, as it is said, strengthen support for smes and infrastructure and enhance action to support growth – to use the wording of the european council meeting in january? how do we make sure that, in times of need, the eib does not work pro-cyclically due to its capital constraints? rather than reducing the number of projects, we have financed a lower proportion of projects – and in practice a constant number of projects – in order to maintain our impact across a wide spectrum of areas. we have also made sure not to withdraw from countries in need, as that would contradict our role. we are aware that the current economic climate and budgetary shortfalls mean that we must find ways to do more with less. combining eu budget funds with eib resources, risk sharing and guarantees for financing mechanisms is one way of achieving this. however, at the end of the day we have come to the conclusion that the overall lending capacity of the eib remains constrained by its very capital base. this means there are limits to what these risk sharing instruments can achieve. a conventional capital increase, as you mention in your report, would definitely be the most effective way to remedy that but so far, understandably, the readiness and willingness of member states to boost our paid-in capital appears limited. given these constraints, another way to construct capital support for the eib would be to allow the eu to provide quasi capital. in the meantime, we continue to explore other alternatives in order to strengthen the bank’s capital base so as to allow the bank to do more. we do this while very clearly and precisely following best banking procedures and sticking to very basic principles which provide, or which are the guarantee of, the preservation of the triple-a status of this bank. this is essential for the business model of the bank and the european union member states. the shareholders of the eib should have a keen interest in the european investment bank, maintaining the balance – and this is the job of any bank – between risk orientation and preserving the good quality of the portfolio, in order to be able to maintain a high rating on the market, because that is the basis for our ability to borrow at very favourable rates and pass this on to the final beneficiary. that is the real economy, and that is where we must make a difference. (applause)

in writing. − in recent years, some raw materials, including natural rubber, have experienced significant price increases and high price volatility. for the european union, which is both import-dependent and the world's second largest consumer of natural rubber, it is essential to ensure fair, predictable and economically sustainable access to this raw material. the international rubber study group (irsg) is an intergovernmental organisation whose objective is to collect and disseminate comprehensive statistical information on the world rubber industry. i believe that this activity plays an important role in improving the transparency of the rubber market and market trends, which is a necessary condition for a better understanding and therefore control of the volatility of raw material prices. however, i would point out that the non-membership of some of the world's major rubber producing and consuming countries - thailand, the united states and china - weakens the authority of the organisation and calls into question its objectives and, above all, its representativeness. i therefore take this opportunity to draw the commission's attention to the need to do everything possible to increase membership of the group by extending the dialogue to the main rubber producing and consuming countries, as a prerequisite for its long-term effectiveness on the market.
in writing. − in recent years there has been a significant rise in natural rubber prices. the studies have shown that these increases are caused by short-term supply shortages, increased demand (in particular from china), decreased number of rubber trees planted and heavy rainfall in the main producing countries. such wide-ranging problems need to be addressed and resolved within the international rubber study group (irsg), the intergovernmental organisation, of which the european union is a member, whose purpose is to collect and disseminate comprehensive statistical information on the world rubber industry. with the recent amendment of the statute and the rules of procedure, the irsg will be in a better position than ever to be the forum for discussion in which to find common solutions for the rubber world, with the aim of better addressing the future problems of the sector.
in writing. - i am in favour of approving the text as amended. i am also in favour of extending the membership of the international rubber study group. the main rubber producing and consuming countries need to be involved.
in writing. − the amendments to the rules of procedure of the international rubber study group (irsg) in july 2011 take account of developments and the new legal status of the european union within this world organisation, which was established in 1944. the organisation has seen its membership decline over the years and has even been abandoned by some countries, although it has a central role in market transparency and the fight against abuse. the changes made seem to be effective and, as the rapporteur has pointed out, it is necessary for parliament as an institution to support and approve the conclusions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is essential to work towards enlarging the membership of the international group on rubber by extending the dialogue to the main producers and consumers of this raw material. the fact that some of the most important producers and consumers are not members of the group weakens the authority of the organisation and its role as a platform for dialogue. the amendment of the group's statute and rules of procedure could ensure the relaunch of the group as an essential forum for discussion to improve the transparency of the rubber market and its trends, and thus to control the volatility of rubber prices.
in writing. the international rubber study group, which was set up in 1944, has lost credibility in recent years as asian countries such as thailand, malaysia and indonesia have been excluded from it. china and the united states, the world's first and third largest rubber consumers, have also been removed from the circuit. the individual european countries are now represented in the international group by the european commission. i am in favour of the text of the report because the problem of rubber supply is a problem felt by industry in europe and is closely linked to the more general debate on raw materials. the risk, as is happening with rare earths, of restrictions on the market for availability could create problems for our industries, favouring those of the rubber-producing third countries.

in writing. − in recent years, some raw materials, including natural rubber, have experienced significant price increases and high price volatility. the studies have shown that these developments are explained by the increase in demand, in particular from china, the reduction in short-term supplies, the decrease in the number of rubber trees planted and the heavy rains in the main producing countries. this combination of factors has put pressure on the global supply of rubber. it is therefore necessary to increase the transparency of the rubber markets. this vote strengthens the international rubber study group, which is the most appropriate body to ensure equitable, predictable and economically sustainable access to rubber in the world. finally, efforts should be made to increase membership of the group by extending the dialogue to the main rubber producing and consuming countries.
in writing. − there are currently many european laws concerning air passenger rights, but i feel that there is a need for greater legal and interpretative certainty and for uniform application of the regulations in the union. i believe that information on passenger rights should be provided in a simple, appropriate and comprehensible way at all the essential stages of the journey, starting from the decision to purchase a ticket by the passenger. in my view, to ensure that rights are respected, it is necessary that there are contact persons at airports who can make timely decisions on the provision of assistance, reimbursement, re-routing and other problems that may arise as a result of flight disruption. i agree with the rapporteur that it is useful to formalise a european network of efficient and independent bodies, coordinated by the commission, and to publish information on complaints received from passengers. finally, i believe that passengers should have the right to change their personal information on their tickets in the event of an error without having to bear any costs for the operation, thus countering the widespread practice in many airlines of the general proliferation of unfair clauses in air carrier contracts.
in writing. - i welcome the initiative of this parliament on the application of airline passenger rights, which is why i have decided to give a favourable opinion on the report. i believe that the air transport sector needs stricter rules on the protection of consumer rights, in particular i believe that it is essential to pay greater attention to the rights of disabled passengers, who must be guaranteed access to a barrier-free environment, and to the safety of infants, who currently do not have seats adapted to their physical characteristics. i also think that the current legislation lacks in terms of the measures that airlines must take in the event of a flight being cancelled or seriously delayed, and for this reason i am absolutely in favour of imposing information requirements on alternative means of transport and temporary accommodation in these cases. finally, i stress the need for greater transparency in the area of co2 emissions and for better information on passenger rights, because i believe that a right can only be a right if it is recognised by all the citizens concerned.
in writing. the report also calls for the establishment of a european air traffic control system, which would enable airlines to comply with the rules on the safety of passengers. it will be necessary to ensure greater and more effective cooperation between the various actors, thus ensuring the protection of passengers' rights and making clear respect for their respective responsibilities. in addition, existing rights should be clarified and strengthened and consumers should be made aware of them. it is essential that passengers know their rights so that they can exercise them. for this reason, information on passengers' rights should be provided in a simple, appropriate and comprehensible way at all stages of the journey, starting from the decision to purchase a ticket by the passenger. to ensure that rights are respected, it would be desirable to have contact personnel at airports who can make timely decisions on the provision of assistance, reimbursement, re-routing and other problems that may arise as a result of flight disruption.

in writing. - i fully agree with the text of parliament which welcomes the commission's commitment to analyse and review the existing rules on air passenger rights in order to improve the situation of passengers, especially in the event of prolonged delays or cancellations. member states and air carriers should apply the rules in force correctly. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - what is contained in the regulation on the application of air passenger rights establishes a common assistance plan which would certainly improve the uncomfortable conditions which often arise between cancellations, prolonged delays or denied boarding. it is essential that passengers are informed of their rights in a simple and understandable way, have the possibility to change their ticket details without additional costs, be informed promptly in the event of cancellation or failure of the aircraft and that they have the choice between reimbursement, re-routing and rebooking. another condition that must be stressed, and i agree with it, is the unhindered access and equal opportunities for transport for people with reduced mobility. the lack of trained staff and infrastructure to cope with the obstacles that these people often encounter is one of the primary urgencies that must be addressed.
in writing. - mr taylor's report was voted on today at the mini-plenary session in brussels. the report aims to strengthen the rules on assistance and compensation in the event of cancellation or delay of flights, including delays in the delivery of baggage exceeding six hours. eu legislation has done much to strengthen air passenger rights, but more needs to be done to ensure fair treatment and wider rights for all travellers. among the highlights of the resolution is the call on the commission to draw up a standard form for any complaints translated into all the languages of the union; harmonise rules on hand baggage, put an end to unfair commercial practices, unilateral rescheduling of flights and price discrimination based on country of residence; in addition, the environmental impact of the journey should be indicated on the air ticket. passengers should also have the right to cancel or change their booking free of charge within two hours of booking. the resolution also calls attention to passengers with disabilities or reduced mobility who must have unhindered access to air transport services, including the right to use mobility aids.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe that the existing rules on air passengers' rights should be revised in order to improve their situation, especially in the event of long delays or cancellations. i believe that the proper application of the rules by member states and air carriers, the use of simple and appropriate means of redress and the provision of accurate information to passengers about their rights are the essential prerequisites for regaining passenger confidence. finally, the role of enforcement bodies set up by the member states needs to be better defined, as the effective protection of passenger rights is not always ensured.
in writing. - on the subject of air passenger rights, there is a need to clarify the notion of 'extraordinary circumstances' and the definition of 'cancellation'. this disparity between the laws of the member states and the behaviour of the different airlines requires the development of a unified, comprehensive and detailed system for assessing the value of the elements provided by airlines in order to demonstrate the existence of 'exceptional circumstances'. the vote seeks to harmonize the matter and to guarantee passengers all their rights and the utmost transparency. it requires timeliness and accuracy in the information provided to air passengers, which must specify the reason for any delays or cancellations, the expected duration of interruptions and what happens in the event of overbooking. not to mention the possible alternative travel solutions available to passengers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr taylor's own-initiative report because it calls on the commission to take action both to ensure that existing legislation is implemented effectively and to promote and simplify the use of instruments to protect air passengers' rights. the report emphasises the legal certainty of passengers' rights, their right to information and the independence and transparency of the modus operandi of the independent enforcement bodies to sanction violations and resolve disputes between passengers and industry. all too often passengers are victims of abusive behaviour by airlines which, taking advantage of the lack of information on their rights, arbitrarily delay or cancel flights without assuming the responsibilities that they would be legally bound to. i therefore hope that this report will provide useful suggestions for the review - due to take place next year - of regulation (ec) no 261/2004 on compensation and assistance to air passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation of flights or long delays.
