in writing. − according to recent research, global spending on technologies for the management of otc derivatives alone has grown from just over usd 1 billion in 2008 to usd 3.5 billion in 2009. these products are traded between private contractors on a scale unimaginable a few years ago, with mainframe systems capable of completing thousands of transactions on the international market in seconds. the entire derivatives market has remained essentially unprotected from the risks it generates and the systemic repercussions on the global productive fabric, which were dramatically revealed by the crisis triggered in 2008, with the so-called collective investment undertakings in transferable securities (ucits) playing a leading role. in line with the g20 resolutions of pittsburgh (2009) and toronto (2010), the regulation lays the foundations for system governance based on risk mitigation, enhanced market transparency and operator accountability, anchored in the strengthening and reform of ccps, in line with esma's guidance. i therefore vote in favour of the report on the regulation, which also transposes the principles adopted by this parliament in its resolution of june 2010 on derivatives markets.
in writing. − otc derivatives are directly contracted between parties and are not traded on financial markets, so that the control of these instruments by the competent authorities is difficult and, given the legislative vacuum in this area, regulation is urgently needed. i believe that derivatives, when used properly as insurance instruments, contribute to growth and to global economic stability, but the recent financial crisis has highlighted the underlying risks in this market, and the danger is that the insolvency of a single operator has a knock-on effect on the whole system. this regulation contributes to financial stability by introducing the obligation to clear through central counterparties for most contracts, by making capital requirements more stringent for those that do not fall under the former, by ensuring greater dialogue between the national competent authorities and esma, and by imposing greater transparency on the contracting parties. the approach adopted is also consistent with the g20's approach to financial stability. in the light of the above, and in the belief that the new measures introduced constitute a significant step towards a more solid financial market and at the service of the real economy, i have expressed my favourable opinion on the emir regulation on derivatives and central counterparties.
in writing. - i welcome legislative action on this subject, particularly in the light of the role played by the derivatives market in generating the ongoing economic and financial crisis. improving regulation in this area means bringing transparency, clarity and stability to financial markets, as well as reducing the many risks that this market entails, and this text, through the introduction of uniform obligations for the exercise of the activities of central counterparties and trade repositories, fulfils this function. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i am satisfied with the text adopted in the trilogue. the european union needed a comprehensive and single regulation for all derivatives traded on both regulated and unregulated markets and more powers for esma, the european securities and markets authority. i am glad that despite the pressure from some states the compromise reached did not introduce too many exemptions from the application of the legislation and did not make the supervision by the european authority less stringent. the text has taken up many of the points made and supported by me in the econ committee, in particular the extension of the framework to all otc and non-otc derivatives and the introduction of some regulatory differences for non-financial institutions that use derivatives to finance certain activities and hedge risks; financial institutions that do not engage in speculation.
in writing. − financial derivatives are widely recognised as one of the causes of the global financial crisis. the regulation adopted today requires transparency and data availability for the benefit of the european securities and markets authority (esma), the european systemic risk board (esrb), supervisory authorities and central banks. it is a pillar of financial market regulation. this approach will offer consumers and investors greater choice and more efficient services. esma will monitor the functioning of such 'directories' and may authorise or refuse registration. esma will also intervene in the event of disputes between national authorities on the authorisation of ccps. the compensation obligation for pension funds will not start until after three years, with a possible extension to five. ccps from non-eu countries will be recognised and will only be able to operate if the legal regime of the countries in question provides for an equivalent system of recognition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the extension of the scope of application to standardised otc derivative contracts. those provisions are necessary to improve the transparency and the management of systemic risk in the otc derivatives market. at the same time, i believe that uniform rules should be introduced to ensure that the activities of central counterparties are carried out under good conditions. this vote underlines the importance of a stronger instrument for business. finally, good proportionality at the regulatory level must be maintained to avoid price increases to the detriment of consumers.
in writing. − given the concerns expressed by the parties concerned, i am in favour of postponing the deadline for transposition of directive 2004/40/ec on the exposure of workers to electromagnetic fields by two years in order to undertake a more thorough assessment of the issue, with a view to a more considered definition of exposure limits. while it is certainly necessary to ensure the safety of workers in the sectors concerned, it is also essential not to place excessive and unjustified limits on the use of the technologies, particularly in the health sector, where imposing disproportionately low exposure limits would directly affect the rights of the patient by limiting the possibility for the physician to use mri technologies. i believe that the entry into force of the directive in question without proper assessment could lead to member states not transposing it and to the inevitable infringement procedures. in order to avoid this unfortunate situation, i therefore consider it necessary to postpone the entry into force of the directive in question.
in writing. − considering that the concerns expressed by the european commission regarding the too low level of electromagnetic radiation tolerable for medical devices have been shown to be in line with the criticisms made by the medical community and companies relying on the use of radiation emitting machinery, i believe that it is necessary to support the new directive, which aims to amend directive 2004/40/ec, and therefore delay the entry into force of the latter, which is scheduled for april 2012. as regards the terms of the postponement, i think it is more reasonable to delay it to 2013: the definition of clear limits for electromagnetic fields is essential for the operation of companies and the transposition of the directive in a short time will benefit not only them but also the workers and the medical community. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i am fully in favour of the amendment of this directive on the safety and health of workers. we are now living in an age in which we are aware of all the risks to which many categories of people are exposed and therefore there is a need for specific safeguards and for efforts to prevent exposure, in this case to electromagnetic fields, from causing such high risks as to lead to permanent disability or death which could have been avoided.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report because it is important to lay down minimum safety and health requirements relating to the exposure of workers to the risks arising from electromagnetic fields. the medical community has expressed concerns that the entry into force of directive 2004/40/ec, which regulates the levels of electromagnetic radiation that can be tolerated by medical devices, is too low for both operators and industrial activities that rely on the use of machinery that emits radiation. the only point of contention is the deadline for transposing the directive, which was initially set for 2012, but the european commission wants to "delay" the deadline by two years. i think it is important, in order to protect workers and ensure a healthy environment for them, which respects the limits of tolerability, in this case, of radiation, not to accept the commission's request for a two-year extension to assess the problems associated with the limits considered too low, but to opt for one year.
in writing. − the current financial and economic crisis in europe requires strong and decisive measures to stimulate economic growth. tax revenue is certainly one of the most important instruments with which the member states can deal with the problems of the crisis. i fully support the proposal put forward by mr casa. i believe it is essential to create a european tax union which includes a comprehensive, rapid, efficient and user-friendly exchange of information between member states in order to improve the fight against tax evasion and to optimise the revenue of the member states' coffers. i hope that the partisan positions can be overcome and that common sense prevails in this difficult time. we must find a compromise, we must find new resources to deal with the crisis.
in writing. the report welcomes the implementation of the commission's proposal to the council. the technological advances now available to the emcs require an adaptation of the regulatory framework as a facilitator of administrative cooperation between states on the application of excise legislation. more than ever, economic operators are demanding quality of service and certainty of the standard: in this context, the increasing automation of the system will allow for a significant reduction in administrative burdens and streamlined procedures, to be accompanied by regulatory alignment initiatives, which serve to promote enhanced cooperation between member states in the field of vat and direct taxation, including in the prevention and fight against fraud, through automatic exchange protocols open to different and gradual options, to which member states are free to accede. it also stresses the lack of alternatives: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to establish a network of bilateral agreements in the european area, capable of supporting a coherent system of information exchange and administrative cooperation. the framework proposed by the proposal, which the report endorses, is characterised by its effectiveness, rationalisation of resources, regulatory and operational coordination, and the strengthening of legal certainty in the tax field: the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. i can therefore only express a favourable opinion.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties. the creation of a european tax union should include a broad, rapid, efficient, user-friendly and as much as possible automatic exchange of information between member states to improve the fight against tax evasion.
in writing. − the idea of improving and strengthening cooperation in this area would itself be highly desirable: the regulation presented by the european commission was precisely in this direction, providing for faster information exchange systems, more accurate controls and a serious fight to prevent fraud and evasion. however, during the parliamentary debate, the committee on economic and monetary affairs felt it was necessary to include a clear reference to the creation of a european fiscal union in the text: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i had tabled an amendment to delete this reference, but unfortunately the majority of the house voted against it. for these reasons, while i share the aims and much of the content of the text, i wanted to vote against the resolution, as i do not think it is right to insert clear political indications into a mainly administrative agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr haagerup because i think it is important to try to work on an eu regulation on excise duties. the aim is to create a european tax union, an ambitious and difficult project to achieve, but one which can already be discussed in relation to specific areas of application. administrative cooperation should include a comprehensive, rapid, automatic and user-friendly exchange of information between member states in order to improve the fight against tax evasion with particular regard to financial transactions and the internal market. taking into account the special conditions and characteristics of the tax system in each member state and the particular constraints of the outermost regions of the european union, the council will propose specific measures to define the conditions for the application of these policies.
in writing. − this report supports the european commission's introduction of administrative cooperation in favour of automatic exchange of information, as it reduces the burden and costs on businesses. it would also be good to introduce a common authority for vat and to set up a forum for excise duties where businesses can discuss related issues and where disputes between member states can be resolved. i believe that excise duties and vat should be harmonised at european union level to avoid unfair competition between companies operating in countries where excise duties are low compared with those operating in countries where they are high. i do not support the creation of a european fiscal union, because it risks creating a super-tax that will overlap with national taxes. for these reasons i am voting against it.
in writing. - i supported and voted in favour of the report by mr vaughan setting out the 2013 budget as regards the european parliament's expenditure. the report, in line with the need for austerity and moderation, focuses on identifying areas where savings can be made: freezing of travel expenses and allowances for members at 2012 level; new organisational measures for committee and delegation meetings to save on interpretation; reduction of 2,36% in mission expenses between the three places of work despite the increase in the number of agents. it is crucial to continue to demonstrate that the eu institutions are acting responsibly in the current moment of crisis.
in writing. - i believe that the european union should contribute to the process of rationalising public spending to help member states overcome the current unfavourable economic situation. the european parliament has therefore chosen to implement a reduction in real terms of its expenditure, a reduction which must of course be seen in the wider context of waste reduction, and which in itself represents only a small step in the desired direction. i have therefore decided to give a favourable opinion on this report. i believe that the line adopted is entirely consistent with the general objective of consolidating the national budgets pursued by the member states, and i take this opportunity to stress the need to move towards a reduction in the number of plenary sessions in strasbourg in order to reduce the burden of the double seat of parliament.
in writing. - having already argued on other occasions for the need to demonstrate that, in the current climate of austerity, the european institutions must be an example of budgetary responsibility and compliance with spending forecasts, i support this report which, despite some problems still to be resolved, seems to me an acceptable compromise. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - the fact that the european parliament has two seats, one for committee work and one for voting in plenary session, is frankly anachronistic. the monthly commuting costs are very high and are unknowingly borne by european citizens. at a time when the world economic situation requires everyone to adopt austerity plans, the cost of relocating members, assistants, translators, interpreters and officials, together with documents and technical equipment of all kinds, is totally unjustified. the economic waste is due to the maintenance of two virtually twin seats which are both used by part-time members. i am referring in particular to the strasbourg office, which is kept up and running so that it can be used only five days a month. in order to take account of the environmental impact, in line with the attention parliament pays to the protection of the ecosystem in its activities, the transport of all the material on the trucks that make the brussels-strasbourg-brussels route once a month, together with the transfers of thousands of people, is certainly a cause of a co2 emission that we could save for european citizens. for these reasons, i therefore vote in favour of the establishment of a single seat for the european parliament.
in writing. - i believe it is essential, given the heavy burden of public debt and the efforts to consolidate national budgets, that the european parliament commits itself to a sense of responsibility and budgetary rigour, and that budgetary negotiations always aim at maximum efficiency. the commission has also been asked to present a proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use.
in writing. - by voting in favour of paragraph 2, i wanted to express my agreement to a single seat for the european parliament. at a time of severe crisis such as the one we have been experiencing since 2008, and with the incessant demand for budget cuts, it seems to me right to review the position of the european treaties on the triple seat of the european parliament. it would be difficult to explain to the european citizens a different position from the one i have decided to take. i hope that our vote (passed by a majority of 429 votes to 184 against) will shake this historically unsustainable situation.
in writing. - i believe that the european union should continue to finance those sectors and enterprises which require economic support for the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by the global financial and economic crisis. i therefore voted in favour of mrs matera's report on the mobilisation of the building fund in the comunidad valenciana. the globalisation adjustment fund is necessary for the reintegration of workers into the labour market or for the protection of workers in precarious business situations, and it is also an indispensable tool for receiving the support from the european union that many small local businesses need.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i believe it is essential to provide additional support for workers who are suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows. i therefore welcome the proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf for spain to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis.
in writing. - the amendments to the rules of procedure, in particular to rule 116, which this report proposes, in addition to making it possible to lighten the agenda of plenary sessions, appear logical and consistent with the new institutional framework resulting from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which sees the european parliament in the role of co-legislator. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the lamassoure report. i think it is right to maintain the possibility of asking the council specific questions during question time on matters which fall outside its legislative and budgetary powers, while the fact that question time has been abolished naturally reflects the institutional changes which have taken place in recent years.
in writing. - i congratulate mr lamassoure on his work. the text adopted in the light of rules 211 and 212 of its rules of procedure and in the light of the report of the committee on constitutional affairs is only the first step taken by parliament to underline its leading role in the european institutions and in particular vis-à-vis the council. following the discussion of the working document in committee on 27 november, when the working document was presented, it was pointed out that the abolition of question time reflects the change in the institutional balance. i think it is essential, however, to leave open the possibility of asking the council questions on matters which fall outside its legislative and budgetary powers.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because the recent deterioration in the political situation in belarus must be condemned. since the presidential elections of 19 december 2010, and despite repeated calls from the international community, repressive measures have been taken against members of the democratic opposition, the free media, civil society activists and human rights defenders. in addition to that, an eu-belarus diplomatic conflict escalated after the belarusian authorities requested that the eu ambassador and the polish ambassador leave the country, and recalled their own ambassadors from brussels and warsaw. in view of these last events i support the decision to withdraw all eu ambassadors from belarus and i believe that a firm commitment by all eu member states to act in a united manner can promote universal values in belarus and bring the country closer to the path of democratic transition. it is of fundamental importance to stress that there cannot be any progress in the eu-belarus dialogue without progress by belarus in terms of democracy, human rights and rule of law.

in writing. - i fully support the motions for resolutions tabled to deal with the delicate situation in belarus. this country has seen a deterioration in its conditions since the 2010 elections. repressive measures have been taken against members of the democratic opposition, the free media and human rights defenders despite repeated calls from the international community. we must embark on a path which will help the country in practical terms and bring it to a level of civilization and freedom equal to that of the countries that are part of our union.

in writing. − the idea of a european democracy fund has been introduced into the wider debate on the review of european union policies and actions to promote democracy following the events in the southern mediterranean. the polish presidency of the council has made the european fund one of its priorities, working with all stakeholders to make the idea a reality. in my view, any new initiative or body for the development of democracy must have a clear added value compared to the existing instruments and organisations of the european union, especially in order to avoid duplication and overlap between the instruments and activities of the european union in the field of democracy building. while i recognize that the aspiration for democracy is expressly enshrined as a fundamental principle for the european union's action on the international scene, i express concern that many developing countries are currently experiencing a phase of development in economic terms only, without freedom or democracy for their citizens. finally, i would stress the importance of introducing a mechanism for accountability to the union institutions, including the european parliament, for the allocation of european democracy fund funding, in order to ensure the necessary transparency.
in writing. - in the face of the events which, together with the arab spring, have reshaped the geopolitical landscape of north africa and the middle east, i believe that the creation of a non-profit-making fund to provide funding to strengthen and support the democratization processes is more than ever necessary. i therefore wanted to support the report by mr lambsdorff, who, in addition to analysing the weaknesses of the eidhr instrument, which was created for these purposes but lacks in terms of effectiveness, makes a number of very interesting requests with regard to the new features of the fund: for example, the guarantee that it provides specific, flexible, transparent and controlled assistance.
in writing. - the report, which i voted in favour of, calls for the creation of a european democracy fund. the idea was put forward by the high representative for foreign affairs last may as part of the new profile of the european neighbourhood policy, especially in the light of the events in the southern mediterranean. the european democracy fund should become a priority of the european union and should be a semi-autonomous entity that can support activists for democracy and democratic developments, and which is characterised by a truly coherent and strategic approach to issues of democratisation. its operation should be light, flexible and effective, including through simple grant mechanisms, in order to respond rapidly to democratic crises and thus provide assistance capable of rapid reprogramming, where necessary, to facilitate the democratic transition. the fund will promote 'rooted and sustainable democracy' in pre-transition, transition and post-transition countries, with a particular focus on the european neighbourhood.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i firmly believe that europe must support the wind of freedom blowing in the mediterranean with a strategic commitment to the promotion of democracy, through concrete and urgent assistance. in this respect, i believe that the creation of the european democracy fund could be one of the most tangible responses by the eu to the challenges of democratisation in the european neighbourhood. the arab spring has brought europe face to face with the great democratic aspirations of the peoples of the mediterranean, as well as the urgency of dealing with the instability generated by undemocratic regimes in the eu's neighbourhood. in particular, the events we witnessed surprised us with the role played by civil society and the power of street protests. for this reason, i am very much in favour of a bottom-up approach that will ensure direct support to civil society. however, this instrument will only be able to operate effectively if clear and transparent rules for the allocation of funds are adopted, inspired by a cross-cutting involvement of civil society and a pluralistic approach to supporting parties and associations.
in writing. - i fully support the establishment of the european democracy fund as a flexible and effective instrument of support and assistance for all countries in transition from unstable and oppressive regimes to democratic political forms and systems. i believe that the time has come for the european union to ensure that this fund is in place as soon as possible (in the light of developments in north africa and the middle east) so that it can begin to provide coherent, immediate and respectful aid to the human rights and democracy community. the european democracy fund could be a unique instrument of action, in support of popular sovereignty in the eu's external relations, capable of supporting cooperation and fostering, as well as 'monitoring' the various processes of democratisation under way.

in writing. - my vote in favour of the establishment of a possible european democracy fund is motivated by the fact that i find it necessary that there should be a semi-autonomous body to protect and promote those rights and those foundations which are at the heart of our constitutions and which, as has been found over the years, go to improve the quality of life of citizens. it is now up to parliament to give its support to an initiative of this calibre.

in writing. - the events of the arab spring and the eastern neighbourhood have demonstrated the need for a strategic and urgent commitment by the european union in authoritarian countries and those aspiring to democratic reform. the creation of the european democracy fund could therefore be one of the union's most tangible responses to the challenges of democratization in many countries. political parties, leading politicians, social movements and representatives of civil society, the cultural sector and the media - including journalists and bloggers - continue to play a central role, but too often due to a lack of resources, support for these actors has been limited. the european democratic fund will be able to guarantee policies and strategies for democracy, coordinated and financially supported by the union, with this vote.

in writing. - it seems absurd to discuss any further the progress, which is nonexistent, made by turkey in its prospective accession to the european union. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. how can we open our doors to a country which does not even recognise the sovereignty of a member state and which even threatens to sever relations with europe during the next cypriot presidency? how far will the european union go to accept these continuing outrages? we must not forget that turkey has been occupying the territory of another country for almost 40 years, which is of course unique and unprecedented in europe. turkey is not part of europe, neither geographically, nor even less so historically and religiously: i do not understand why we want to continue on this absurd path of enlargement. we in the northern league have always been very clear on this point: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - i am strongly opposed to the text of the resolution on turkey's european integration process. there is an eu-turkey agreement, purely economic in the energy sector, both for supply and transit, but this cannot be enough to allow accession to the eu. unfortunately, the attitude of too many hypocritical europeans is aimed at a process of turkish accession. i would remind you that turkey should be a democratic state first and foremost, and it is not so today, since it occupies a part of europe (northern cyprus) militarily, has not solved the kurdish question and its foreign minister has reiterated that turkey will have no contact with the european presidency, which will be held by cyprus next july. it is unacceptable that the european union should succumb to the blackmail of a state such as turkey, which is far from meeting the criteria which the european union has set itself in the copenhagen agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the progress made by turkey, particularly in stressing the critical issues still open. as mentioned in paragraph 11, it is of paramount importance that turkey has a modern and efficient judicial system, which is fully independent and impartial and which guarantees a fair trial for all citizens. the fact that this objective has not yet been achieved is evidenced by the growing number of cases before the european court of human rights. the question raised in paragraph 29 also appears to be of fundamental importance for the purposes of modernisation. the government must (is called upon to) take the necessary measures to increase women's social inclusion and their competitiveness in the labour market, in particular through policies aimed at reducing the gender gap, especially in secondary education. it is even more important to mention here that turkey has been occupying the northern part of cyprus militarily and without any legitimacy since 1974.
in writing. − the turkish economy has tripled in size over the last decade, growing by almost 10% in the last year and is considered one of the fastest growing economies in the world. but because of its inadequate judicial system, as the hrant dink case demonstrates, the idea of joining the european union is still premature. the judicial procedures have not yet been sufficiently improved in terms of efficiency and standards to guarantee the right to a fair and speedy trial, including the right to access incriminating evidence and investigative documentation in the early stages of the proceedings and sufficient safeguards for all suspects. finally, there is concern about the wide scope of interpretation and application allowed by the anti-terrorism law and the criminal code, in particular in cases where membership of a terrorist organisation has not been proven and where an action or statement is believed to coincide with the objectives of a terrorist organisation.
in writing. − montenegro was granted the status of 'candidate country' for accession on 17 december 2010. the european council of 9 december 2011 asked the council to examine montenegro's progress with a view to opening accession negotiations in june 2012 and the commission to prepare the negotiating framework for the montenegro-eu negotiation. at a critical moment like the present, europe's insistence on enlargement is an irrational and illogical choice: it is not enough to assess the potential of the entry of a new economy, but it is also necessary to consider its social and sociological implications, which are too often underestimated.
in writing. - there is still much progress to be made, but i believe we should be satisfied with montenegro's commitment and constructive role in contributing to regional stability and strengthening good neighbourly relations with the other western balkan countries. it is also positive that montenegro is actively involved in several regional initiatives in south-east europe.
in writing. - in the context of enlargement to the western balkans, montenegro has proved to be the most successful country in meeting the requirements for opening accession negotiations. giant strides have been made in the fight against corruption and organised crime, in strengthening the rule of law and in terms of euro-atlantic integration, with the granting of nato membership, visa liberalisation in the schengen area and candidate status for the eu. i am therefore extremely in favour of the opening of accession negotiations with montenegro, which has been an official candidate since 2010, and i hope that the european commission will respect the deadlines set by the december council for the opening of negotiations as early as next june.
in writing. − montenegro has been a candidate country for accession to the european union since december 2010. on 9 december 2011, the european council concluded that accession negotiations could be opened in june 2012, provided that the country had made sufficient progress in implementing reforms, in particular in the area of the rule of law and fundamental rights. the main challenges for montenegro involve the fight against corruption and organised crime, the reform of its judicial system and public administration, and the creation of sustainable economic development for the country's recovery after the 2009 recession. montenegro continues to apply the stabilisation and association agreements without any problems. important laws have been adopted and the dialogue with the eu institutions and civil society has been further improved in line with the european acquis. progress has been made in science and research, audiovisual policies, public procurement and company law. nevertheless, montenegro faces important challenges both in adopting and implementing the necessary legislation in order to ensure alignment with the acquis in key areas such as social policy and employment, regional policy, environment, competition, and financial control, as well as free movement of goods, protection of intellectual property, agricultural policy, food security, fisheries, justice, freedom and security.
in writing. - i have defined corporate governance as the system of management and control of a company and therefore as the development of relations between managers, the board of directors and shareholders. i voted in favour of mr bodu's report, which highlights some important issues for the transparency and security of listed companies. among these is the 'respect or explain' principle which would oblige listed companies which decide not to comply with the code of conduct to provide reasons for this choice.
in writing. the report recognises the green paper as an important step forward in the rationalisation of the corporate governance system. as such, the book is open to critical review, with recommendations representative of the wealth offered by the diversity of business cultures in the union. the recommendations on boards of directors and shareholder rights are particularly significant. the social tensions across the continent, triggered by the financial crisis, have in fact dramatically raised the need to promote the values of transparency, rigour, measurement and the enhancement of human capital, within a framework of principles that is as homogeneous as possible. in recent years, the lack of a culture of moderation and sobriety, of transparency and of checks and balances has not failed to generate distortions and bad practices, the negative effects of which have regularly been felt by the majority of citizens. while respecting national cultures and the principles of individual and business freedom, the green paper, as complemented by the report's recommendations, represents an act of responsible governance in tackling with determination the deviations and anomalies that are harmful to european citizens. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.

in writing. − with regard to this resolution on corporate governance for european enterprises, i am in favour of the planned revisions and the input that will be made and that are contained in the green paper. our aim must be to create a more stable, transparent and reliable business sector within our union, so as to mobilise the economy and give a boost to the labour market.

in writing. the european investment bank contributes to the development of the single market and to reducing development disparities between regions. the group's loans reached eur 52 billion in 2010, used mainly to support the external action policies of the european union itself. the institute carries out its activities to support the development of the european economy and to promote growth, stimulate employment and promote social and territorial cohesion, with a particular focus on projects for the benefit of less developed regions. this vote encourages the european investment bank to continue its activities. at the same time, a european system of prudential supervision is needed, under which the eib will be subject to the same prudential rules as credit institutions.
in writing. - the committee on petitions found that 25% of the petitions received concern issues related to free movement. this is not surprising, since many citizens feel a certain dissatisfaction with the european project when they find that some member states offer less favourable treatment than others, discrimination, lack of recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications, lack of adequate services for people with disabilities and problems in the field of family law. as the european parliament's ombudsman for international child abduction cases, i have noticed in recent years that with free movement there has also been an increase in the number of bi-national families, of which about 140 000 divorces per year are related to these families. the problem is compounded when child custody is involved, an issue that is often problematic and regulated differently in different countries. a striking example is germany, with the institution called "jugendamt", which gives a german parent the right of custody over a foreigner and tries in every way to prevent the child from being taken away from germany. is the commission aware that this example also constitutes a violation of the freedom of movement of persons?
in writing. − in recent years there has been an increasing number of petitions concerning the problems encountered by union citizens in exercising their right to freedom of movement. the statistics in the annual reports of the parliament's committee on petitions show that about 25% of the total number of petitions received concern problems related to the free movement of persons. the case law of the court of justice of the european union has, over time, given greater substance to european citizenship by placing free movement in a prominent role as a fundamental right from which a wide range of other essential rights for citizens derive. in my view, the right to freedom of movement is one of the european union's most valuable achievements. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's emphasis on informal networks for solving the problems of the citizens of the member states. finally, i take this opportunity to stress here the need to improve the union's communication policy, which is intended to ensure that european citizens enjoy the full rights enshrined in the treaties and thereby remove the obstacles to their full enjoyment.

in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur on her work, for which i gave her my vote in favour. the report welcomes the 2010 citizenship report published by the commission, which aims to remove obstacles to the exercise of rights by citizens of the european union. it also points out that, although the right to petition the european parliament is expressly provided for in the european treaties, it is not sufficiently known or used and that it is necessary to move towards better and more active communication with citizens. the report must therefore produce a greater sense of belonging to the european identity which must not only be recreated but also nurtured and through the european year of citizenship, which will be celebrated in 2013, it will have to be demonstrated to citizens that with free movement there is also a free exercise of rights in europe. finally, i believe that the european citizens' initiative, which will enter into force on 1 april 2012, will represent the first instrument, and an important step, of direct and transnational participatory democracy, which will give citizens the opportunity to participate more actively in the definition of european policies.
in writing. − freedom of movement is one of the eu's most valuable achievements, as confirmed by the fact that 88% of european citizens (interviewed) perceive it as the most familiar of the four freedoms established by the eu. the 'fundamental rights and citizenship' programmes, together with the strengthening of synergies with other eu programmes, can certainly help to give new impetus to the concept of european citizenship and to remove the obstacles which still contain it. in this sense, the smooth functioning of the single market is based on the removal of obstacles to the economic and social cohesion of the eu, which can be achieved, as also reiterated by the commission, by updating directive 2005/36/ec in order to allow for faster and less bureaucratic recognition of professional qualifications. the 2013 european year of citizens should therefore be a further opportunity for europe to remove the additional obstacles which still prevent community citizens from fully enjoying their rights as european citizens, and to help build a single market at the service of citizens. finally, it should be stressed that eu citizenship, often considered as 'second-class' compared to national citizenship, can be used as 'preparatory citizenship' for non-eu nationals who meet certain requirements, such as 'good conduct'.
in writing. - women have equal dignity and rights with men. that is why i am voting against the introduction of the so-called 'pink quotas'. a man or a woman should be chosen for a given role on the basis of their competence and preparation for the job for which they are applying, regardless of their gender and sexual orientation. deciding in advance that a number of jobs, in politics or in business, should be allocated to a woman solely because of the sex she represents actually increases the discriminatory attitude that she will be hired because she is a woman, not because she is good". women have the right to be hired because they are competent, good and prepared. it is a question of finally banning the hypocrisy with which men try to ghettoise the role of women by granting them little formal benefits, in order only to lower the threshold of social discomfort. i believe in the extraordinary capacity of women workers and i am sure that with the right instruments, including incentives for companies, the need to consider the influence of pregnancy protection in the world of work will no longer be seen as a factor that is detrimental to the employment of women, but as a resource to make the opportunity of access to the world of work truly equal.

in writing. − one of the objectives of the european union is to remove obstacles to the exercise of citizens' rights. the '2010 citizenship report' identifies many problems faced by european citizens in their different roles (as private individuals, consumers, residents, students, tourists, professionals or politicians) and proposes some solutions to overcome them. a quarter of the problems are related to freedom of movement and residence. citizens often face difficulties in accessing social security benefits, in particular because the legislation on social security is complex, difficult to understand and sometimes inadequately applied by the competent authorities. they often fail to complete the correct forms or to meet the deadlines for submitting the necessary documentation because they were not properly informed or did not find the necessary instructions before leaving their country of origin. problems in the area of family law were identified, particularly with regard to child custody in the event of divorce or the recognition of marriages registered in another member state. the vote will seek to remove the obstacles to the exercise of the rights of the citizens of the union by harmonizing and creating continuity between the various national legislations.

that fall under the universality of human rights. there are many many points that we can reflect upon. let me, in the short time i have, try and pick up on a few of these. first of all, may i say how pleased i am that mr sannikov and mr bondarenko have been released from prison in belarus. we are in touch, and i hope that we may be seeing an opportunity with belarus. this shows the strength of the european union; it shows the importance of being decisive in what we do, and it shows more than anything that standing together is so important. a number of honourable members have rightly raised the importance of faith, belief, conviction; the ability to worship and exercise belief, faith or none. i agree with all the concerns that have been raised about the importance of making sure that this is a core part of the work that we do on human rights. this is why we will dedicate a chapter in the annual report specifically to that, so that it becomes part of our human rights work but is highlighted appropriately. i hear what a number of colleagues have said about the situation in egypt, and we will continue to keep a watchful eye on how this is evolving. mr donskis talked about the subtle undermining of human rights. the challenge is to make sure that we focus not just on the most obvious ways, for example, the abolition of the death penalty (which is, as you know, something i consider to be a fundamental part of the work that we do), but also on the ways in which people are prevented from exercising their rights in more subtle ways. these two things are very important. who are in prison should be released immediately, and we have suspended most of our aid to guinea bissau. we are, of course, looking at how to make sure we can continue to give direct support to the was a separate discussion before the debate. i agree, too, that honourable members have been in the forefront of wanting to see a special representative, and as you know i am currently working on the mandate for that person. we are looking for someone of enormous integrity and with great ability in this field. it will be an important role, and the appointee will need to have a good relationship with this house. this is something we want to continue to discuss. i was very pleased to see that so many people mentioned the issues of women’s rights and the importance of continuing to support women, especially women going through extreme circumstances of horror and terror, but also women trying to engage in the political and economic lives of their countries. very simplistically, we know that when women are engaged in society, societies are richer in every possible sense: economically, socially and politically, and the issue of forced marriages is one that affects many countries. when i was a minister for human rights in the country i came from, i did legislation on forced marriages there. this is something we need to take seriously everywhere. mrs ludford, i have already said before that we will look into that, but you know that i am deeply concerned about the use of the death penalty everywhere, especially, as i said to you earlier, over the 100 instances of the death penalty in iran so far this year. mr stevenson, you have been a champion on the issue of camp ashraf because of your concern for the people there. we are still in touch with martin kobler and are still pushing hard on member states, and i need the help of meps to make sure that we can resettle as many people as possible. this is crucial, but we are also offering to support the un financially in moving forward on this. so in a sense, the more i can rely on help from this house, the more i will be able to do. but you know how much i am concerned about this and how engaged we are on this. in about the importance of meeting with human rights activists. i try to do that in every country i visit in order to listen to them and hear from them about the situation on the ground and the realities of the life that they lead. i support fully the rights of lesbian, gay, transsexual and bisexual people, and this should be fully reflected in everything we do on human rights. such rights are universal. in terms of how we work with different countries, i have talked before about the spectrum of engagement to isolation and the importance of ensuring that human rights is one of the indicators of how we work with countries. we are often, as the honourable members know, trying to work with people in countries in order to support them while also trying to isolate and put pressure on their governments. the spectrum really matters in that we do not abandon people who are desperately trying to obtain their rights, but we engage where we can. on that spectrum of engagement to isolation, where engagement can be more effective (and it very often is), we need to make sure that we are there, willing to put the pressure on to try and make the difference. my final point is a bureaucratic one: benchmarking. we are working now on how to develop the methodology for this. we want to measure the performance, as a number of honourable members have indicated. there is quite a long way to go, but the action plan may also be an opportunity for us to examine. my final comment is to thank richard howitt again for the work he has done on this very important report. i know his personal conviction and commitment to this, and i pay tribute to that.

the agenda includes the statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation in mali.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam high representative, after so much good news from africa, so many bad surprises in mali, a country which has also been a successful democracy in recent years: we have kidnappings, the threat of secession from the north, the coup d'état, fundamentalist gangs with the application of sharia law and the risk of famine; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of the lack of access to the market for the products concerned. mali is a collateral victim, partly also of the conflict that took place in libya, and it finds itself in a story that is bigger than itself, bigger than the malian political class. the real reasons lie outside its borders and in a history linked to the libyan conflict and, as has been said, even further afield. when we call in our resolution for a post-gaddafi strategy for the whole region, we want political cooperation and also security cooperation to be much deeper, to go beyond contacts, but to ensure food and political security together with ecowas, the african union and the un in their respective roles, knowing that the later we intervene, the more difficult it will be to find a solution.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the last few weeks there have been a number of incidents which i would simply call curious, but which are a very serious and dangerous idea. in italy, a group of pseudo-researchers, who have won european and international recognition, have expressed their intention to reconsider, or even ban, the reading of the divine comedy, dante's masterpiece known and appreciated for centuries by millions of citizens in every part of the world. they say the poem contains too many racist, anti-semitic and islamophobic references and should be revised in a modern and politically correct way. in vienna, the association of citizen restaurateurs has proposed banning certain traditional dish names, such as gypsy cutlet or negro bread, so as not to offend the sensibilities of others. these are not isolated incidents, but they represent a common and widespread feeling in europe, namely that we must deny our roots just to please different cultures, but a tree without roots dies, and so europe risks doing if it does not immediately change its tune and defend its origins and traditions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the situation in italy is dramatic and our participation in europe is in crisis. this is because italian workers do not understand europe when they lose their jobs because large companies close down in italy to open in european countries that have lower labour costs. they do not understand europe if the ecb ostensibly finances small and mediumsized credit, but only helps banking institutions. they do not understand europe if a government democratically elected by italians is sacked and replaced by technicians who, as the only solution to the crisis, propose higher taxes and higher petrol prices. they do not understand europe if italian fishermen on the croatian border are penalized by rules which the croats, who will soon be entering the common market, do not respect. they do not understand europe if they exploit our resources in countries which have nothing to do with the old continent, which has historically defined borders: the rocks of stonehenge to the west, the grain of budapest to the east, the brandenburg gate to the north and castel del monte to the south: this is europe.

member of the commission. − the issue of social rights and social dumping has been mentioned in a question. i have been at the centre of discussions on the posting of workers, especially following a few famous court rulings in this area. this is why the commission wanted to address this problem through various proposals, but particularly as part of the posting of workers package amounting to a regulation. if adopted, it will help to address such situations in the future. i should say again that we have discussed the structure and the content of this proposal with all the stakeholders over the past two years, and we have said on these occasions that the commission will not reverse the jurisprudence of the european court of justice, but rather that it will do as much as possible to prevent similar conflicts from occurring in the future. in the event that such conflicts do occur, it will facilitate a much faster solution. we take a practical view of this problem as opposed to various ideological approaches, and i think that the document which we adopted in march delivers much to improve the situation in a very concrete way on the ground.
member of the commission. − there are two key points which i would like to make in response to this very concrete question. one of them is that, of course, in the judgment on this specific matter we have to see how the working time directive is applied in the country concerned. it varies greatly across member states, and that is why it is very important that in the current period the social partners at european level are negotiating about the working time directive and how to revise it. but secondly and most importantly, in this document, which we adopted in march, there are many points about improving administrative cooperation, and such differences in national regulations will be sorted out and addressed more easily in the future through this improved administrative cooperation.
member of the commission. − ms jazłowiecka, the intention and in fact the objective of the commission with this work is to continue to facilitate cross-border services while at the same time fighting social dumping and protecting the posted workers better. i believe we delivered this. the particular elements in this proposal concerning the construction industry will help clarify and improve the situation and build confidence around posting practices. the number of posted workers will not depend on this. companies will enjoy the same opportunities to provide cross-border services as in the past, but there will be a greater clarity about how to implement the existing regulation and how to avoid the problematic cases of the past. whether there is a demand and indeed a practice of posting depends on a variety of factors. it depends on the situation in the given industry and the markets and the needs for labour, geographic proximity, and various other economic factors. the fact that we now propose new practices to ensure and guarantee rights and improve administrative cooperation will, i believe, not undermine cross-border services. they will actually clarify the situation, build confidence and thus perhaps even facilitate more than in the past.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i wanted to put a question to the commissioner on the monti regulation on the exercise of the right of collective action. i think that the commission's proposal is unacceptable because it infringes the fundamental rights of the individual and the collective rights of representatives, because when it presupposes mutual respect between the freedom of establishment and the exercise of one's rights, and when it says that the strike must be balanced with economic freedoms, it interferes in an area which should be left to the parties. i believe that a formula of this kind is contrary to the material interests of the people they represent, but also to the rights which have been enshrined in international organizations and in the laws on the rights of working people, as well as on those of citizenship. i think that this proposal should therefore be radically changed, or even, as would be better, withdrawn, in order to open a debate which provides for a balancing point, but which is left to the social partners.
member of the commission. − mr president, this is indeed a sensitive point, but i believe that the correct interpretation will help to eliminate concerns and anxiety regarding monti ii. to clarify: the draft regulation confirms that there is no primacy of the freedom to provide services or the establishment of the right to strike. it will not impose any additional obstacles on exercising the right to strike. in fact, the monti ii regulation aims – without reversing european court of justice case law – to clarify the extent to which trade unions may exercise the right to strike in cases of cross-border operations, and to put forward rules for dealing with obstacles to the free provision of services or to the freedom of establishment created by the exercise of fundamental social rights. the monti ii regulation recognises that member states have limited possibilities to intervene in strikes and that the eu is not competent to legislate on the right to strike, as you can read in article 153 (5) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i believe that the right interpretation of monti ii will help to eliminate misunderstandings on this issue, as was the case with monti i.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the regulation we are discussing is in fact contrary to the existing case law. in some member states there are forms of self-regulation which have been freely decided by the workers' representative organisations and are not imposed by law, and woe if that were so. i think that this is a sphere which should be left to the discretion of the individual - where forms of definition of the relationship between the strike and the effects it has on the user are necessary - and should not be in any way invaded by case law, whether these are actions taking place within a single country, or whether these are actions which may concern cross-border activities and therefore involve different countries.

member of the commission. − i would like to make two points in response to this question. one of them is that there is indeed an important focus in this proposal on the so-called letterbox companies that simply move their centre of establishment to another country without having a relevant part of their economic activities in that country. it contains important provisions seeking to diminish – or even eliminate – such practices in the future. this is indeed a form of social dumping, and it does not help in maintaining fairness and a level playing field in the european economy. the second point i would like to make is that in europe the reality is that there are wage differences between various countries and various regions. there should be broader consideration of many policies – not simply a matter of legislation on one particular working practice – in order to see how convergence might be facilitated and the various tensions which are connected to these wage differences reduced in the future.
member of the commission. − what we judge to be a critical (minimum) level of economic activity should also depend on the sector and various other parameters which have to be looked at in the case of particular companies and countries. the important thing is that within a sectoral context it is possible to define and draw conclusions, if necessary, about improving the situation. the enforcement directive will in fact clarify the elements of the notion of posting, which will help to combat the use of temporary posting by so-called letterbox companies as a subterfuge to circumvent the applicable law. the letterbox company, i may remind you, has no genuine economic activity in the member state of establishment, and this is what we have to look at. concerning further proposals, yes, we will also be looking at the question of a minimum wage and other important issues in the labour market in the forthcoming employment package.

in writing. - i have decided to abstain from voting on this report. on the one hand, at this particularly difficult time for european society, it is certainly necessary to improve the functioning of the systems of protection of workers, but on the other hand, considering that the social and employment situation is profoundly different in each member state, it is appropriate that the various social security systems remain separate, avoiding creating transnational interference such as that suggested by the report in question. the overlap of european systems, especially on specific issues such as unemployment benefits, is not advisable. for these reasons i preferred to abstain.
in writing. − the free movement of persons within the borders of the european union is one of the four fundamental freedoms guaranteed to citizens. in order to make this freedom effective, it is necessary to avoid, as far as possible, that the decision of a european worker to move to another member state entails a loss of rights acquired in the country of origin. to this end, a regulation was voted by the european parliament in 2004 to ensure greater coordination of the social security systems of the member states. in order to adapt that regulation to the changing legislative and labour market conditions, it needs to be amended. i therefore voted in favour of this amendment, which clarifies the position of selfemployed workers who receive unemployment benefits and of airline workers who work in several countries, who will be subject to the legislation of the country where the parent company of the airline is located, as laid down in the new legislation.
in writing. - the updating of regulations (ec) no 883/2004 and (ec) no 987/2009 which we approve today at first reading, thanks to the agreement already reached with the danish presidency - necessary to reflect the changes in the member states' legislation on social security and the coordination of social security systems - is a text widely shared by this house because it has been able to accommodate the positive needs of the trade unions in the sector. the clarifications on certain key concepts in the air transport sector will help and protect company employees against the risk of frequent changes in the legislation applicable to their contract due to industry work patterns and seasonal demands.
in writing. - while protection against unemployment for crossborder selfemployed workers seems to be a more than acceptable objective, the proposal under consideration raises a particularly sensitive issue concerning the social security system of each member state. the aim of the proposal is to harmonize and coordinate the social security systems of the member states in order to protect crossborder workers, but it is forgotten that social policies also include the thorny issue of unemployment benefits and minimum income, on which legislation differs significantly and which are the subject of heated debate, especially in the current economic climate. for these reasons, i thought it appropriate to abstain.
in writing. − the amendment of regulation (ec) no 883/2004 was made necessary to ensure a fairer and more appropriate treatment of social security schemes for crossborder selfemployed workers. the text is intended to provide certain guarantees for these workers, who are often involved in situations where the legislative framework is not always clear, since they work in a member state other than their country of origin, with different social security legislation which, in some cases, does not provide for depreciation or subsidies for selfemployed workers. the successful coordination of social guarantees for crossborder selfemployed workers through an amendment to the existing community regulation is a sign of attention to the variety of conditions in which european workers work, which are constantly changing.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report presented here. the fact that new social security systems must be created to coordinate with the requirements of new types of jobs, which we could also define as atypical, leads to the study and presentation of criteria different from those usually followed. these criteria must of course be respected by all the member states and must therefore be elaborated in detail in order to present a common plan. the re-training must lead to the employees being reintegrated into the labour market of their own state even after a prolonged absence.
in writing. - the report by mr cabrnoch was voted on today at the strasbourg plenary session. this report will improve the functioning of the single market by strengthening the social protection of many mobile workers in the eu, such as flight attendants and cross-border self-employed workers. the regulation also focuses on the situation of crossborder selfemployed workers (a worker who returns to his/her home country at least once a week) as regards access to unemployment benefits. in italy, there is no unemployment benefit for selfemployed persons. however, according to the text, a selfemployed person who works in an eu country other than his home country, where he pays the necessary contributions to unemployment benefit, and who returns to his own country, where such financial support is not provided, would still be entitled to receive the benefit paid by the last country where he pursued his activity. this measure would therefore apply to italy.
in writing. the text of the report aims to update the changes made by the national legislation of the member states in the field of social security. one of the most significant aspects of the proposal concerns the question of crossborder selfemployed workers, for whom greater protection and guarantees against the risk of unemployment are required in the member state where the last activity was carried out. the part we are not in favour of is the management of social policies, as we find it difficult to achieve harmonization in the short term. the risk for the member states with the highest numbers of non-eu nationals is that they will be obliged to provide for guaranteed minimum incomes. if italy were to make such a choice it would become a magnet for all the desperate people of north africa. i am afraid that the vote will be abstentive.
in writing. - i agree with mr cabrnoch's report on the coordination of social security systems, as i believe that there is a great need to update, update and clarify the social security conditions in the various member states of the european union. we are living in a historical moment in which crossborder mobility has become an increasingly important phenomenon and there is a real need for coordination in this area in order to ensure the security of our citizens and their future, without neglecting legal certainty for those concerned. i am therefore in favour of the need to find standard solutions to avoid discrimination between citizens of the union.
in writing. the variety and evolution of the conditions under which occupational activities are carried out require that the situation of highly mobile workers be taken into account. the coordination of social security systems has made it possible to ensure that all workers who are nationals of the member states are treated equally and enjoy social security benefits, regardless of their place of employment or residence. i voted in favour of this report because it provides a necessary update, incorporating the content of national legislation and introducing the individual amendments into european legislation. it also clarifies the conditions under which social security is guaranteed to those who work in the various member states. this is all part of the principle of free movement of workers, which is an integral part of the internal market.

in writing. - the position of ireland, following the negative outcome of the referenda held in the republic, presents a delicate problem from the political, institutional, cultural and governance point of view. it also represents a challenge, which many have long imagined they could postpone indefinitely, compared with the development of governance models which, within a framework of institutional cohesion, can demonstrate that they are able to enhance the cultures of the member states, respecting the sensitivities of each european people and responding to legitimate concerns, when they should arise, on individual aspects of a political, social or cultural nature. in this sense, the decision of the heads of state or government to take up the concerns of the irish people on the lisbon treaty in relation to the right to life, the family and education, taxation and security and defence, through a legally binding decision and subject to a subsequent and specific protocol, is to be considered responsible and courageous. this assumption of political responsibility makes it possible to identify an alternative route to that of a specific convention. i therefore vote in favour of the motion for a decision before us.
