in writing. - the report receives a favourable opinion on the assessment of the european council's decision to examine a proposal to amend the treaties by adopting the said protocol. the concerns of the irish, which did not fail to influence the outcome of the 2008 referendum, will be addressed in the document annexed to the treaty on european union and its functioning. the council will make progress on the difficult terrain of compliance with their respective constitutional rules and the specific concerns expressed by the irish government, which is calling for a new protocol. the report's approach is therefore fully acceptable.
in writing. − at the european council on 19 june 2009, the heads of state or government of the 27 member states decided to provide the necessary legal safeguards in response to the concerns of the irish people on specific issues such as the right to life, family and education, taxation, security and defence, and agreed on the desirability of providing for a future ad hoc protocol to be annexed to the treaty on european union and to the treaty on the functioning of the european union. we therefore welcome the drafting of the text of this protocol, considering that it is necessary to respect previous political agreements between governments and that the content of the draft protocol refers exclusively to the situation in ireland.
in writing. − the main objective of cohesion and internal market policy is to organise policy initiatives aimed at smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, promoting a high-employment economy that fosters social and territorial cohesion. however, the initial conditions in the outermost regions (ors) are an obstacle and a slowdown in achieving the objectives set, particularly in the europe 2020 strategy. as highlighted in the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the octs are entitled to a different treatment allowing them to benefit from the maximum level of aid, irrespective of their level of development. in this respect, i welcome the commission's intention to include a budget line dedicated to 'outermost regions and regions with very low population density' in the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. i fully agree with the idea that the outermost regions should pursue the main objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy, but i think it is necessary to stress the need to adjust the objectives to the specific situation of each outermost region, taking into account their regional diversity, their structural conditions and their potential benefits.
in writing. - i have supported the report by mr teixeira because i am convinced that cohesion policy in the context of the eu 2020 strategy, which focuses on the outermost regions (ors) of the european union, can only be effective if it is structured in ad hoc programmes and pathways that take account of the specificities of these areas and territories. the outermost regions differ from other european regions in that they are characterised by environmental, logistical and social constraints and permanent difficulties, but which can also be exploited as strengths for their small-scale economies. in particular, i believe that the historical relations which the ors have developed and consolidated over the years with third countries should not be underestimated either, since they can be a source of ideas and good practices for developing new opportunities in the future.
in writing. - the report deserves our support, particularly because it stresses that cohesion policy - by its very nature - must take account of regional and ultraperipheral specificities, but also, more generally, of all specificities. the very existence of funds for the 'cohesion' of regions with different degrees of development presupposes the need to operate in different structural situations, due to geographical characteristics or socioeconomic deficits. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the implementation of the cohesion fund. while efforts must be concentrated on the objectives considered to be fundamental, it must not be forgotten that, in order to achieve the same objectives, it is not possible to ignore the different starting points of the areas in which the instruments are actually operating. otherwise, efforts may prove not only futile but even counterproductive. the report also provides an opportunity to stress that future financial allocations must not be lower than the present ones. the only way out of the crisis is to boost investment and, even more so in the lessfavoured areas, the community institutions have a duty to create the preconditions for this to be possible.
in writing. − the eu is one of the richest regions in the world, but there are large differences in the level of prosperity between and within the various member countries. the 2004 enlargement further reinforced this phenomenon: it is not surprising that almost all the funding from the cohesion fund is allocated to the 12 newest member states of the european union. in addition to these countries, the european union also has 8 outermost regions, which are geographically distant from the european continent but which are an integral part of the member states to which they belong. however, the starting conditions for these regions are often less favourable than for other european regions: the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. this requires adaptation of european policies to the specific conditions of the eu's outermost regions, as only a programme that takes account of their specificities will enable these regions to achieve the objectives of economic, social and territorial cohesion and contribute to the achievement of the eu 2020 strategy objectives.
in writing. − cohesion policy, in the context of the eu 2020 strategy, must increasingly take account of the specific needs of the outermost regions of the european union. the octs require special and differentiated attention on a case-by-case basis, based on assessments of individual needs and difficulties, which are useful in order to apply the most appropriate and correct policy strategies for the growth and development of these territories. in this respect, both the reform of the new common agricultural policy and the definition of the new multiannual financial framework, which is currently being defined, are fundamental factors. it is not possible to imagine a europe that travels at two speeds, or that considers the ors as a whole, without providing specific economic policies to promote their growth. i therefore believe that in order to have a truly effective eu 2020 strategy, the objectives must be achieved by the european territory as a whole.
in writing. - the text by mr teixeira, for which i have given my favourable opinion, lists the measures to be considered as a matter of priority in order to adapt the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy to the eu's outermost regions. these regions enjoy a special status due to their remoteness and geographical configuration and therefore need appropriate analysis to be integrated into eu programmes and to achieve the goals of social inclusion, cohesion (a better tool for their small economies) and development of the eu 2020 strategy. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on climate change and its impact on the environment. only through a specific eu policy framework will they contribute to the achievement of the eu 2020 strategy objectives
in writing. − i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is essential to adapt the implementation of european policies in the eu's outermost regions so that they can be facilitated in achieving the objectives of economic, social and territorial cohesion, contributing to the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy objectives. european investment in these areas is not only a policy to make up for the delays and compensate for the disadvantages, but also an investment for the benefit of the whole european union. in order to assist the outermost regions, it is necessary to adopt a territorial approach to the implementation of european policies, thus pursuing the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the outermost regions of the european union are characterised by physical and structural disadvantages due to their remoteness and insularity, topography and difficult weather conditions. to counter these disadvantages, the outermost regions enjoy a special status established by the treaty, which allows for derogation from and adaptation of the treaty rules. this vote will be aimed at a better integration of these regions into the european union. the objective will be achieved through more effective governance through a multi-level governance system and through territorial continuity to improve access to the benefits of the development of a single market and its integration in the context of regional neighbourhood plans. this is not just economic support, but a tailored strategy that provides a development model that can take advantage of their opportunities for greater competitiveness, growth and employment.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr barroso, i agree with those who say that there is a qualitative leap forward in european policy. the response from the eurozone has been strong, we have adopted new, strict rules on national budgets to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past, but these rules, which impose heavy sacrifices on our citizens, cover only one aspect. the time has come to focus on growth, and i agree with all those who speak of growth, because if we are to increase our public budgets by demanding even rigorous structural reforms, we must at the same time implement measures for growth, because otherwise in a global context europe or many of its countries risk recession. the problem we have today is the lack of an investment policy, the only way out of another danger, that of economic stagnation. this parliament is therefore at the forefront of these issues, such as the introduction of a discount factor - and i am addressing president barroso on the basle reform - a supporting factor for smes, that is, a supporting factor for small and mediumsized enterprises, on which a unanimous common response by all the european institutions is needed. in this context we cannot ignore eurobonds, but we must make a distinction because there is a lot of confusion on the subject. these eurobonds must be created by avoiding debt mutualisation. the third approach in the green paper also seems to me to be correct, but some changes are needed: there can be no revival of the european economy if at the same time the strength of the euro is not used. eurobonds make it possible to organise and contain public debt and to raise the necessary financing for the future of europe on the market.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, on behalf of the european commission, i would like to thank you for organising this debate so quickly. since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, foreign direct investment, and in particular the protection of such investment, has been an exclusive competence of the european union, which means that the european union has both the right and the responsibility to act in defence of european union investment. the issue of the nationalisation of repsol's holding in ypf raises serious concerns. we need to look at this measure in the context of a series of protectionist measures taken by the argentine government in recent months, such as, for example, extensive measures to make import licences non-automatic. we have already pointed out these protectionist measures to the world trade organization, along with more than a dozen countries. we are now looking at what further action we need to take against these protectionist measures, including the way of the trade dispute settlement mechanism. i have listened carefully to all your arguments and concerns. i can assure you that the european commission will look at the situation carefully and will strongly remind argentina of its obligations under international law, using all the means at its disposal.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i would like to thank everyone present here today for sending a very clear signal to the argentine government. it is a signal sent by the commission, the danish presidency and a huge majority in this house. i hope that the argentine government will listen, because this is not only an issue implicating a firm or a country, it is an issue between argentina and the eu, and it is therefore important that we see it that way. the council will now discuss the matter at the foreign affairs council next monday, under the leadership of the high representative, lady ashton. as i said in my first intervention, we will take full account of the debate this afternoon. i might add that the issue will also be dealt with in several other forums at a technical level in the council, and the options that the eu has will be examined here in order to take concrete action against the plan to nationalise ypf. against this background we will be working closely with the commission and this parliament to make sure the right solution is found.
in writing. the spanish reaction to the argentine government's move to expropriate the oil company ypf has led the eu foreign minister to finally promote a meeting of the council of foreign ministers on eu-argentina relations, to clarify relations in economic and financial matters. many european investors have long been calling for the intervention of the european institutions, claiming their rights, violated by the decisions taken by the argentine government after its "default". the committee on petitions has dealt with this issue in the course of its work, prompted by numerous petitions. the commission's declaration that it had no competence to regulate financial relations with argentina, which were relegated to the realm of bilateral negotiations, led me to address the request for intervention to the eu high representative, inviting her to review trade relations and to use them as leverage to obtain due compliance from the argentine government. the privatisation of the group's capital, of which the spanish company repsol holds 57.4%, will certainly have a strong negative impact on the markets. but the ones caused by the non-payment of millions of citizens have contributed not a little to worsen the financial crisis, intervening more widely but certainly not less accidentally.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is all very well to defend and protect the environment, but i would like to know how far we are going to go. the price of energy products in many countries has reached historic highs, as in italy, where filling up your car has become a real chore. the proposed solution would certainly lead to further increases in fuel prices and the usual people will always pay, those for whom the use of a means of transport is essential for getting around and for work. i do not think that the european union can afford this situation, which would bring many strategic production sectors to their knees and would ultimately result in higher energy and fuel bills. in italy, the monti government is also considering introducing a "carbon tax" at the national level. one blow is followed by another and in so doing citizens and businesses will die in the name of a false and exaggerated environmentalism which, in italy as in europe, serves only to make money indiscriminately.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, since mr lambert has said that the best way to eliminate the views of those who oppose these rules is to identify them as dangerous lobbyists, i shall base my speech on an automobile-type system. it seems to me that we are operating under the principle of 'the polluter pays', which is a good principle, a sacrosanct principle, as sometimes happens on formula one circuits. in formula one, you race to win. when someone runs to throw the other person off the track instead of to win, accidents happen. the safety car then enters the field to restart the race on a more level playing field. i believe that if we approve this new tax without approving the rapporteur's line, and therefore approve the amendments, indiscriminately, we will have run a race to get rid of the opponent, which in this case are our companies, it is the citizens who have the right not to perceive these taxes as a way of taking over their lives, and we will also be doing a disservice to the polluter pays principle. i think we must have a balanced attitude, so we support the rapporteur's line, we want the amendments she has proposed to be adopted, precisely because it is possible to give the whole of europe the chance not only of having a better environment, but of having that better environment while continuing to compete with the other great world powers, otherwise we will make our proposals unreliable to the citizens, and the citizens will punish us, considering all our positions to be abstract.
in writing. one of the aims of the amendment of this directive is to introduce a taxation component linked to co2 emissions in order to favour less polluting products from a tax perspective. however, the commission's proposal - by requiring member states to tax products used for the same purpose at the same rates and by eliminating the possibility of exemption for certain products - is likely to have the only effect of unsustainably increasing the tax burden on those fuels and fuels which are actually helping to reduce environmental pollution. for example, in the case of lpg used as fuel, there would be an increase in taxation of about € 0,370/litre. it goes without saying that lpg vehicles would lose any economic advantage in use over their petrol counterparts. the same applies to natural gas and methane: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not only more environmentally friendly but also more environmentally friendly. i therefore hope that the principle of proportionality of excise duties will be abolished, so that member states can have the flexibility to set the level of taxation according to their energy policy.
member of the commission. − mr president, in june 2011 the european council encouraged the commission and the eib to enhance the synergies between loan programmes for greece and eu funds. the aim was to increase greece’s capacity to absorb eu funds and to stimulate growth and employment creation. in july 2011 the heads of state and government of the euro area and the eu institutions extended the scope of that political mandate. they invited the commission and the eib to enhance the synergies between loan programmes and eu funds in all member states benefiting from eu or international monetary fund assistance. in january 2012 the european council invited the council, the commission and the eib to consider possible options for enhancing eib action to support growth, including the possibility of using the eu budget to leverage the eib group’s financing capacity. in october 2011 the commission adopted a proposal to amend council regulation (ec) 1083/2006. the objective was to enable the use of available allocations under programmes cofinanced by the european regional development fund and cohesion fund to back up guarantees and loans granted by the eib or by other national or international bodies with a public mission offering adequate guarantees – the so-called ‘risk-sharing instrument’. the target member states are those experiencing serious difficulties with respect to financial stability and which have been granted financial assistance according to one of the existing mechanisms. the measure is intended to address the serious obstacles faced by some member states, particularly greece, in raising the private financing needed to implement infrastructure and productive investment projects, which can only be part-financed by public funds. this is particularly the case for infrastructure projects which generate net revenues, the value of which cannot be covered by grants financed through cohesion policy instruments. it is also the case for productive investments, for which the maximum allowable public aid is capped by state aid rules. the recent approval of an increased rate of co-financing by the eu to 95% is part of the eu response to the crisis. however, it is not enough, in particular for the revenue-generating projects, since the investment costs covered by revenues are not eligible for eu co-financing. the measure proposed is an exception to the normal framework in which cohesion policy is implemented and is justified by the circumstances imposed by the crisis. since the publication of the commission’s proposal, there has been intense debate with the council and parliament. i would like to take this opportunity to thank the members of the committee on regional policy, and in particular its chair ms hübner for her support in this process. i would also like to thank the members of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and of the committee on budgetary control and their rapporteurs for their support. the adoption tomorrow of the hübner report will open the way to securing strategic investment projects financed by cohesion policy without increasing the eu budget allocated to it and without having a significant impact on the eu budget. it will facilitate the implementation of important transport and environment infrastructure, as well as other economic infrastructure projects which will provide a much-needed boost to economic activity and job creation in greece. in greece alone, the effective implementation of important infrastructure projects in the transport sector will, it is estimated, create some 50 000 new jobs. other member states most affected by the current financial and economic crises may also benefit from this legislative proposal. in recent years, cohesion policy has been mobilised several times to contribute to the changing needs of member states under severe crisis conditions. excellent interinstitutional cooperation made it possible to shape tailor-made crisis assistance, which was available within a short time. i therefore call on the members of the european parliament to give their support to this legislative proposal.
the commission has already submitted a proposal for a regulation to the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal to amend regulation no 1083/2006 may make it possible to transfer to the direct management of the commission funds allocated to member states which, because of the current financial difficulties, are in danger of losing part of their own resources allocated to programmes co-financed by the erdf to the cohesion fund. the extension of this proposal to all member states, which i propose as rapporteur for the cont committee, would be strategically relevant for countries such as italy which, although not in the same debt situation as greece and portugal, are also having to fight the crisis. the picture is therefore clear, although there has been no release of funds, the programming is very poor and does not allow for the achievement of positive results. the possibility envisaged by the amendment would therefore not be the transfer of funds or the loss of resources, but an act of humility which would allow some countries to organize their spending better and to direct it towards objectives consistent with the needs of the community. the financial crises have not spared any european nation and to limit this opportunity to a few countries is a grave mistake.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank all the members for their remarks. i am glad to see that we share the will to help those member states most threatened by the economic and financial crisis. in terms of extending the proposal to all member states, i know that this issue was raised during the discussions in the different committees and during today’s debate. let me underline that this is an exceptional crisis response measure, justified primarily by the severe situation of greece, even if some of its elements may also be present in other member states receiving financial support. on the other hand, at a time of strong budgetary constraints, extending the proposal to all member states would potentially have a strong budgetary impact. regarding the scope of the legislative measure, initially the commission proposal addressed only national strategic reference framework projects. after discussions with the member states, the eib and meps, it was agreed to enlarge the measure to operations which contribute to the objectives of the national strategic reference framework of the requesting member state and the community strategic guidelines on cohesion. in the commission’s view, this is a good compromise that will secure cohesion policy projects, taking into account other projects which fall under cohesion policy objectives. the commission expects that a significant number of projects will be in the environment sector, including renewable energy. i would like to draw your attention to the fact that covering projects which are not related to cohesion policy would raise a series of questions, mainly of a policy and legal nature. the risk-sharing instrument is a specific response mechanism addressed to a specific number of member states. it cannot be considered to be a mechanism that offers an easy way out of reprogramming structural funds or accelerating absorption. in conclusion, i would take this opportunity to underline that cohesion policy has again proven that not only is it a structural investment, it can also provide short-term assistance. i therefore call on the members of the european parliament to give their support to this legislative proposal.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the third amendment to regulation no 1083/2006 which the european commission has recently presented contains provisions to create a european risk-sharing instrument. the aim is to overcome the difficulties encountered by some member states in obtaining the private financing needed to implement investment projects which can only be partly financed by the use of public funds. although there is still a long way to go to overcome the economic crisis, i believe that the work done to reach a compromise text that has set a ceiling on the funds available for the financial instrument and has better defined the risk-sharing instruments has been fruitful.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i fully agree with this report, which is an important signal from parliament on the subject of simplification and harmonization in the field of corporate taxation. the existence of 27 different corporate income tax rules entails, in addition to high costs and administrative burdens for companies operating in several countries, serious risks of tax evasion and discrimination. this is essential to reduce the costs of companies operating in several states and to promote growth and economic recovery within the internal market. finally, the optional nature of the measure, which leaves the choice to undertakings to assess the benefits and costs when choosing the new system, neutralizes the backlog of some member states which see their sovereignty in tax matters or revenue threatened. i hope therefore that the council will be able to reach an agreement without recourse to enhanced cooperation, in the interests of citizens and businesses and not solely on the basis of calculations of national selfishness.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are still a long way from the completion of the single market, and in particular 27 different rules on corporate taxation pose three main obstacles: high administrative costs and burdens for companies operating in several countries, an increased possibility of tax evasion, as well as of double taxation and tax discrimination, an incentive to business policies of 'regulatory shopping', with potential economic distortions and, in connection with this phenomenon, an incentive to national policies of gradual shifting of taxation from mobile to less mobile bases, with clear socioeconomic distortions. the harmonization of the methods of calculating taxable profits so that companies in the 27 member states are subject to the same rules, regardless of the member state in which they are taxed, is therefore a necessary measure. that is why i voted in favour of the text, despite the retreats of some member states who see their sovereignty in tax matters threatened.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of a partnership agreement between the eu and the republic of liberia on the forestry sector, as i believe that this agreement has very positive objectives concerning a particularly sensitive sector for the republic of liberia, as timber revenues were used to fuel the conflict during the country's civil war, which ended in 2003. the republic of liberia has undertaken to ensure that all timber products exported from the country are legally produced. i hope that the commission will ensure that the liberian government actually complies with the agreement, and i support the contents of the agreement itself: combating illegal logging, improving forestry regulation and enforcement, developing traceability systems and monitoring activities.
in writing. - the republic of liberia is rapidly moving away from the less happy pages of its history, thanks in particular to a series of tax and business law reforms. although remaining among the least prosperous countries in sub-saharan africa, liberia has nevertheless shown significant improvements in its economy, growing at an average rate of around 6% per annum. in this context, flegt fpa can bring about particularly marked positive effects, because it invests in an important sector of the liberian economy, also in its social, institutional and political implications. from the point of view of building a more robust legal framework, a system of widespread opportunities (starting with the communities living in the production areas), and a greater integration of liberia into international markets, which is a guarantee of political stability, the agreement certainly constitutes an important and positive contribution. i can therefore only vote in favour of the proposed text.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this agreement and i am voting in favour of it. however, doubts remain about the real possibility of liberia being able to fulfil its commitment to europe. it will be the task and duty of the european commission to ensure that the forest heritage of this country is kept intact and that a limit is put to illegal logging, a real scourge afflicting the african continent. so my vote in favour is intended to be a vote of confidence in the two contracting parties. i very much hope that flegt measures, including this one, will be effective and helpful in preserving nature and creating development in certain areas of the world.
in writing. − forests cover about 45% of liberia's territory, and the country is home to over half of the remaining rainforests in west africa. the long civil war, which lasted from 1997 to 2003, deeply affected the forestry sector: the timber revenues were used to fuel the conflict, prompting the un security council to impose sanctions on liberian timber imports. in addition to providing a partnership instrument to enable liberia to halt illegal deforestation and forest degradation, which contribute to climate change, the voluntary partnership agreement should enhance market opportunities for timber products in europe and other international markets. in this way it will also be able to make a positive contribution to the general development and growth of liberia.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the eu-liberia agreement on forestry enforcement, governance and trade in timber and timber products because it is an important step forward in putting a stop to illegal logging. the agreement, in fact, in addition to offering guarantees on the quantities of timber imported, offers greater transparency, especially on the characteristics of production.
in writing. - i supported this proposal because it aims to make it possible to continue programmes co-financed by the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion fund, which are experiencing implementation difficulties in member states which are affected by financial assistance programmes and are facing liquidity problems as a result of the continuing economic and financial crisis. this proposal for the six eligible member states (greece, ireland, portugal, hungary, romania and latvia), although the situation of greatest urgency is currently manifesting itself in greece, will ensure the implementation of programmes financed by the structural funds and the cohesion fund on the one hand, and the maintenance of access to project financing on the other. the proposal contains provisions which would finally allow the creation of a risk-sharing instrument. the operation would cover, without any increase, the resources already allocated to the member state concerned at the beginning of the 2007-13 programming period under cohesion policy, thus without any additional impact on the community budget. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster.
in writing. - i support the report by mrs danuta maria hübner, which amends the regulation on the european regional development fund, the european social fund and the cohesion fund in the light of the global economic crisis. this amendment opens up the possibility for the countries of the union which have encountered serious difficulties to be able to use part of the financial resources of these funds to create instruments capable of ensuring a greater economic recovery. the member states which request it will have to provide adequate guarantees and present concrete investment projects, and the eib will be responsible for supervision, which will then ensure further management controls. this is an exceptional and temporary measure, which does not involve any increase in appropriations over those already provided for in cohesion policy and which will naturally come to an end once the crisis has been overcome.
in writing. − the report clearly sets out the reasons for this further amendment of council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 in the context of the situation created in some countries affected by eu or imf assistance. the european institutions must make every effort to decipher the developments in the crisis and to adopt rapidly effective measures to deal with the new situations; the commission has also taken the view that the measures proposed by the member states are not sufficient to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market, especially if important stabilisation operations are jeopardised by changes in the general framework and, above all, by the subsequent unavailability of private financing necessary for investment in the recovery. failure to take appropriate action risks undermining the whole recovery strategy and means failing to fulfil our moral obligations towards the citizens of the member states who are suffering the negative social consequences of the stabilization measures, which are being adopted in the form of structural reforms imposed with a sense of extreme urgency, without adequate political and cultural mediation processes. this further change in the risk-sharing instruments framework is therefore an expression of vitality and of timely and effective policy action, and prudent in the nature and purpose of the measures envisaged. i am in favour of the report.
in writing. the report aims to help member states that are most affected by the financial crisis and unable to secure the private financing needed to complete revenue-generating infrastructure. the private partners are unable to invest because of liquidity problems and difficulties in accessing loans, so part of the financial allocations of the individual member states is transferred to the commission to create a fund to cover risks linked to loans. this means that, in order to allow the completion of works under construction, some states are in fact depriving themselves of part of their appropriations. for our part, despite the support for the instrument, we would have preferred some kind of structural intervention to address the endemic liquidity shortage in a large number of member states in order to ensure an improvement in expenditure performance, thus avoiding having to resort to drastic measures that could lead to a reduction in resources. in this connection, we are convinced that these difficulties can be overcome by introducing a derogation from the stability and growth pact to allow national co-financing of projects deemed particularly relevant to economic recovery and job creation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr hubner because i believe that, in a time of crisis such as the one we are going through, the establishment of a risk-sharing instrument at european level is a necessary initiative. the definition of this instrument involves the definition of specific rules and criteria to be met in order to access the risk-sharing fund, rules identified in close cooperation with the european investment bank. the ability of each member state to participate in this instrument, which is activated at european level, is also regulated. there is no doubt that this initiative, which is being taken at a historic time of economic and social crisis, will strengthen the role and significance of parliament, both at the democratic level and, above all, by restoring its role as guarantor of solidarity between member states, which is essential to overcome the financial crisis we are experiencing.
in writing. − in the member states most affected by the economic and financial crisis, several strategic projects selected for co-financing under cohesion policy programmes risk not being implemented because private sector investors and banks do not have the liquidity to lend to projects and project promoters, or because they are no longer willing to bear the investment risks in the current environment. the risk-sharing instrument therefore constitutes an exception to the normal framework of implementation and aims to cover part of the risks associated with lending to banks or project promoters in member states experiencing or threatened with severe difficulties with respect to their financial stability. we welcome this proposal which aims to ensure that programmes co-financed by the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion fund continue to be implemented. however, we consider that only projects for which the eib or other similar institutions have adopted a positive financing decision and those generating revenue and state aid projects already included in the operational programmes of the member states concerned are eligible for funding under the risk-sharing instrument.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment. these are the countries of the union which are affected by financial assistance programmes because of the economic crisis and it is for these countries that the commission has put forward the proposal, which was approved by parliament thanks also to my vote, which outlines the 'risk-sharing instruments' for carrying forward the implementation of programmes financed by the structural funds and the cohesion fund for the period 2007 to 2013. the text provides for the possibility of transferring funds allocated to the member state to the commission for direct management so that agreements can be concluded with financial institutions (eibs) guaranteeing resources for the protection of investments without additional costs. this will limit the risk of losing the funds already allocated to member states in difficulty for cohesion policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i consider the creation of such a financial instrument to be a priority. i believe that a commitment is needed to deal with the serious difficulties encountered by some member states in obtaining the private finance needed to implement investment projects in infrastructure and production, which can only be partly financed by public funds. it should be noted that the proposed measure is an exception to the normal framework for the implementation of cohesion policy and is justified solely in the light of the exceptional circumstances imposed by the current crisis. the aim of the fund remains to cover part of the risks associated with lending to banks or project promoters in the member states.

in writing. - i believe that the differences in the methods of calculating the tax base of the different european states involve enormous bureaucratic costs and represent one of the main remaining barriers to intra-eu trade. the establishment of a common method of calculating the taxable base (ccctb) would therefore lead to a reduction in these costs, with clear advantages for companies operating in different countries. the proposal contributes to simplifying bureaucracy and reducing the cost of tax compliance by defining a uniform approach to the calculation of the tax base and by adopting the concept of a 'one stop shop', whereby companies will be required to provide a single return. it also provides for the possibility of offsetting budgetary assets generated in one country against liabilities incurred in another, thus eliminating the phenomenon of double taxation. i believe that this directive can help to increase the growth of companies operating in more than one country, especially smes, for whom the costs of excessive bureaucracy are proportionately higher. the proposal therefore contributes to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives and represents an opportunity to boost growth and jobs in the union. for these reasons i thought i should give my favourable opinion on the proposal.
in writing. - in a time of deep economic crisis such as the one we are experiencing, simplifying the tax system and reducing the tax and administrative burden on our companies is not only desirable but necessary. this legislative measure is intended to benefit both smes and large european companies by encouraging the former to expand in the medium term and by reducing the costs of setting up subsidiaries in other member states of the union for the latter. it also aims to stimulate foreign investment in europe, which is currently discouraged by the fact that the interaction of different national systems can cause double taxation or overtaxation. for these reasons, my vote will be in favour.
in writing. the introduction of a common corporate tax base, based on a fixed formula taking into account turnover, labour and fixed assets, is a step towards reducing red tape for companies operating in cross-border market conditions. the reality of this type of business is increasingly widespread and the harmonization of the tax system, at least as regards the tax base, is indicative of the desire to move towards a tax regime as clear as possible for operators in the sector. the report also provides that each member state may continue to apply its own rate of taxation to the part of the tax base for which it is responsible. the tax harmonization sought will concern the calculation and apportionment of the taxable amount. this is to ensure that individual member states can continue to retain their autonomy in taxation systems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which seeks to introduce a common consolidated corporate tax base at european level. the aim is not to harmonize the tax rates of the various member states, which will retain the greatest degree of autonomy in this field: the aim of this proposal is to establish common rules for the calculation and allocation of the taxable amount of corporation tax for companies operating in the european union. this entirely optional formula can help companies operating within several european states, or those which would be interested in doing so by expanding their activities; this can be particularly true for small and mediumsized enterprises, which have to deal with different legislation and different bureaucratic and administrative systems. after a first experimental phase, it will then be seen whether this new formulation has been of any use to our companies, in order to be able to exploit to the full the potential of having a single european market, which too often remains unexpressed.
in writing. - currently in europe, a company that decides to invest outside its home member state has to take into account the tax regime of the country in which it opens up its activity, facing enormous difficulties due to too many differences. the aim is to integrate and promote the european single market, facilitating the movement and investment of small businesses throughout the union. that is why i find the report by mrs thyssen very interesting, which aims to establish a european tax system for a common consolidated corporate tax base. the proposal for a council directive also lays down the rules which the companies concerned will have to respect for the calculation of their contributions, rules of a single european tax system.
in writing. - the report by mrs marianne thyssen on the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) was voted on today in plenary in strasbourg. the differences between the tax systems of the eu countries are sometimes enormous and often difficult to interact with, so that it can be complicated and costly for a company to expand its business in the single market; the ccctb scheme would instead give companies the possibility to calculate their taxable income according to a single set of rules, instead of having to comply with different tax rules in each member state in which they operate, and would also make it easier to have and maintain subsidiaries in different states by reducing the bureaucratic burden for the same companies. the planned plan envisages the binding of the ccctb at the end of a transitional period; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the tax base is not used to finance the production of goods and services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i consider it essential to define common rules for the calculation of the taxable amount of corporation tax for companies operating in the european union. i am convinced that the common consolidated corporate tax base is an indispensable instrument for the completion of the european internal market and for the european economic integration necessary for the stability of the euro area. the current crisis should not be an obstacle but a catalyst for the introduction of this element.
in writing. - i believe that a process of simplification and harmonisation of the tax rate in the various member states is necessary. the fact that there are 27 different regulations has many disadvantages: high administrative costs and burdens, socioeconomic distortions, risks of discrimination and, finally, increased opportunities for tax evasion. that is why, despite the retreats of some member states which see their sovereignty in tax matters threatened, i voted in favour of the report on the common consolidated tax base for mr thyssen's tax. i am firmly convinced that in order to complete the project of a single market it is necessary that all member states comply with the same legislation.
in writing. − the harmonisation of the methods of calculating taxable profits of companies within the 27 member states is a measure desired by the european business system. by reducing costs and administrative burdens, the growth potential of enterprises operating across borders will be strengthened and access to the internal market will be facilitated for smes and enterprises that currently operate only on national markets. tax transparency will also be improved, with less scope for fraud and evasion and reduction of double taxation and tax discrimination.
in writing. - the european union has a responsibility to promote responsible and sustainable energy policies, and i have therefore decided to express my favourable opinion on the report on the taxation of energy products, which prescribes a series of measures to promote energy efficiency and reduce co2 emissions. i also believe that the amendments adopted by parliament have brought about a considerable improvement in the commission's proposal, and i particularly stress the importance of abolishing the article which would have required member states, in order to ensure tax neutrality, to standardize the rates of energy sources used for the same purpose. this amendment allows the states to maintain differentiated levels of taxation on diesel and petrol. the increase in excise duties on diesel fuel would have led to a loss of competitiveness in the european automobile industry, which has traditionally been stronger in the production of diesel engines, and to a clear drop in employment. the greater energy efficiency of diesel engines is also scientifically proven, and for these reasons it is necessary to be able to maintain a favourable tax regime for diesel. for these reasons i voted in favour of the amendment to the commission proposal which abolishes the principle of fiscal neutrality and i gave a favourable opinion on the report.
in writing. - i welcome the report by mrs lulling on a proposal for a reform of the taxation system for energy products. i think it is essential that amendment no 7 be adopted, which maintains the tax exemption for fuel for the agricultural sector. this vote therefore constitutes a strong signal of defence against the agricultural sector, which is rightly concerned about the consequences that would have been caused by an increase in the price of agricultural fuel in a period such as the present one. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the common organisation of the market in bananas is particularly important in view of the ongoing negotiations on the reform of the cap for the period 2014-2020, which will be launched in the coming months with the presentation of the european parliament's proposals.
in writing. the rapporteur, while acknowledging the commission's contribution to the implementation of the european strategy, rightly points out the implications for industrial and transport policy. the road freight transport sector would face serious challenges with the increase in the price of diesel as a consequence of the co2 emissions reduction target in the sector. the environmental sustainability of road transport is already guaranteed by strict legislation in force and companies in the sector are already required to pay for emissions in accordance with precise community and international obligations. the principle of 'proportionality' between the various minimum tax thresholds set at union level needs to be seriously reviewed in order to avoid an indexed increase in the price of diesel and to avoid the consequences for competition and inflation. the excise duty on fuel, expressed as a percentage, should not automatically follow the price increase, as is the case in italy, where fuel is among the most expensive in europe (€1738.19 per 1000 litres of diesel, compared with the european average of €1,521.4). this mechanism must be stopped if the member states do not want to lose control over whether or not decisions are taken in tax matters. tax automation is a hellish device to be avoided
in writing. - although a legislative consultation procedure, the revision of the directive on the taxation of energy products and electricity has proved to be an extremely sensitive subject. the debate in the commission on economic and monetary problems has brought to light important critical points. the main point of contention was the concept of 'fiscal proportionality' inserted into the text of the directive by the european commission. the tax provides for the same mandatory minimum rate of taxation on energy products in all member states, which in turn will tax the various products proportionally, depending on the energy value and the co2 emission coefficient. the imposition of rates in the same proportion for all products would, however, reduce national sovereignty to a minimum, limiting the area of manoeuvre of the states with negative consequences in the energy sector in which each country is specialised, inflation risk, damage to businesses and consumers. fortunately, the epp succeeded in suppressing the 'proportionality' principle by introducing a specific amendment, thanks also to my vote, during the vote in plenary. the ball now goes to the council, which will have to take account of parliament's position.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because i consider it to be an important contribution to the europe 2020 strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. i think the commission's methodological approach to taxing energy on a double basis, that of co2 emissions and that of energy content, is correct. the energy taxes will be partly linked to co2 emissions and partly to energy content. the energy tax structure will thus be designed to support the objective of a low-carbon economy that is equally energy efficient. the proposal also aims to bring energy taxation into line with the eu's commitments to combat climate change by introducing a co2-related element in energy taxation.
in writing. - in view of the current economic crisis, the european parliament should send a strong signal by voting against the report on the taxation of energy products and electricity which envisages an increase in minimum excise duties in europe for all energy sources. this proposal is an environmental contradiction, since it favours renewable energy sources over 'clean' gases such as methane and biomethane. if the price of energy were to rise, what sad fate would befall small and mediumsized industries, the real engine of the economy? in italy, where the cost of energy is higher than the european average, a further increase in prices would be detrimental to our businesses. the national governments are already thinking of raising excise duties, and there is no need for europe to raise those within its competence which are then used as the basis for calculating national excise duties. the idea of raising the cost of energy by about 80% by 2023 by taxes alone is an unsustainable burden on citizens. finally, the continuing increase in diesel fuel for motor vehicles should not be underestimated and the new taxation would therefore place an even greater burden on european taxpayers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr lulling's report on the taxation of energy products and electricity because i fully share its key principles, namely to achieve an alignment of energy taxation provisions with the environmental objectives set within the europe 2020 strategy and to reduce distortions in the internal market between the member states of the union. the community framework for the taxation of energy products must be as consistent as possible with the union's environmental policies. there is no agreement between the political groups on proportionality. i have supported amendment no 53 in particular, which seeks to remove the principle of proportionality from the text of the proposal, mainly for pragmatic reasons. we cannot allow further increases in diesel prices at a time when, for fiscal reasons due to austerity measures, the prices of energy products are under constant pressure. in addition, diesel is heavily used for professional purposes and it is clear that road transport would suffer significant negative effects from regulated increases in minimum rates. finally, the european citizens would not understand such a choice.
in writing. - the proposal to amend directive 2003/96/ec which we put to the vote this morning was tabled by the commission on 13 april. the purpose of this legislation is to align energy taxation provisions with the environmental objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy and to reduce distortions in the internal market in relation to the current difference between eu member states in energy taxation levels and scope. these objectives are essentially achieved by dividing the current taxation of energy products into two components: a carbon tax component, based on the level of emissions, which would have the specific objective of reducing co2 emissions not captured by the ets covering only 50% of co2 emissions (small installations, services, agriculture, transport, heating) and an energy tax component, based on energy content (fixed rates per gj regardless of the energy product). in voting this morning i wanted to remove the obligation for member states to reproduce a fixed ratio between the minimum levels of taxation applied to the different energy products ('chained excise duties' or 'proportionate excise duties') which would have led not only to a sharp increase in the prices of certain energy products but also to the gradual disappearance of certain industrial sectors.
in writing. the disproportionate size of the public debts of the countries of the union, further aggravated by the financial instability characterising this economic phase, makes the problem of tax evasion even more burdensome. increases in rates due to the inevitable austerity policies implemented by the member states may be ineffective unless accompanied by a strengthening of the instruments to combat tax evasion. it is also necessary to prevent measures taken by states in financial difficulties from resulting in a migration of firms to countries offering tax privileges. these forms of tax competition are among the most harmful and in the long run could lead to a disproportionate reduction in taxation on productive activities, offset by an increase in taxation on employed labour, which is less mobile by nature. i have therefore decided to express my support for the resolution of parliament which identifies concrete methods of combating tax evasion. among these, i would particularly stress the need to abolish banking secrecy, to increase controls to prevent the transfer of resources to so-called tax havens, and to define new instruments to combat the evasion of value added tax. finally, i would stress the important role played by the ccctb system in the fight against tax evasion.
in writing. − the resolution stresses the link between decisive measures to boost growth and the definition of a clear and unified community strategy to halve tax evasion by 2020. the lack of revenue from the shadow economy has a perverse effect on the european economic system and negatively affects levels of investment for growth and employment. by recovering this revenue shortfall (20% of public expenditure and even 105.8% of total health expenditure), governments could zero out public debt within 8 or 9 years. at the same time, they could increase public investment, contributing to the achievement of the eu 2020 strategy objectives. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. the fight against tax evasion must become a top priority for the eu; so far, much has been said, but too little has been done. it is time to act decisively. paying taxes is a basic civic duty and a matter of social justice, capable of generating the resources needed to emerge from the crisis and to revive the real economy, without burdening workers and the most vulnerable once again.
in writing. − the fight against tax fraud and evasion must be an objective to be pursued vigorously at european level as well: the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information it receives. there is one point in the report which puzzles me and for which i have therefore decided to abstain on the final vote: i believe that member states should retain the possibility of concluding agreements with third countries if such negotiations can bring benefits in terms of recovering illegally exported money. it would be desirable, however, to prevent these problems in advance, making it more difficult to resort to tax havens or to complacent states, where it is extremely difficult to investigate the nature and origin of money. the phenomena of tax fraud and tax evasion are common to all the countries of the union and therefore coordinated action can certainly be useful, without this however being a renunciation of fiscal sovereignty and a limitation of the action of the member states. if wrongs have been committed, they have been committed against the citizens of each country, and each country is therefore entitled to act in its own interests and in the way it deems most appropriate.
in writing. - i wholeheartedly support this request, especially in view of the difficult historical period we are going through. the problems of tax fraud and tax evasion must be kept under the strictest control, given the risks we face as a union, but also as individual states. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this type of crime.
in writing. − today, by adopting this motion for a resolution on the call for concrete measures to combat tax fraud and tax evasion, in the light of the conclusions of the european council of 1 and 2 march 2012 and in the light of the oecd study of march 2012, parliament calls on the member states to review their tax systems and make them more efficient, by removing unjustified exemptions and broadening the tax base. i also believe, as the report stresses, that member states need to focus on tax collection and the fight against tax evasion, and to ensure that there is mutual cooperation between tax authorities and that the latter have the necessary resources to tackle and combat fraud.
in writing. - a proper fight against tax evasion is an essential element for a fair and modern tax reform, adapted to crisis situations such as the present one, where a reduction in the tax burden on households can have a profound impact on a decisive recovery in consumption, on employment, and on a decisive recovery of the economy. i believe that effective action against fraud is of paramount importance in order to raise the resources needed to increase public investment to reinvigorate europe's international competitiveness and growth potential. in italy, the new government has introduced a number of anti-fraud measures which are producing satisfactory results. i welcome the mandate given to the council and the commission, because i repeat that vigorous action at european and national level is necessary and must be taken.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i join in thanking the commission and the council presidency, but this debate is timely and important, especially because we are faced with two unacceptable violations of the letter and spirit of the lisbon treaty. the violation of the letter, as has already been mentioned by many speakers, concerns the boycott of the european union's accession to the european convention for the protection of human rights, which is clearly established by the treaty of lisbon and which is an essential complement to the adoption of the charter of fundamental rights. the breach of the spirit of the treaty concerns the proposal currently under discussion in brighton to amend the convention by unacceptably reducing the possibilities for citizens to appeal. these are truly paradoxical proposals, not only because protocol 14 has already significantly reformed the court's procedures, but also because, more generally, solving the problem of too many pending cases by reducing the possibilities of appeal is like fighting an epidemic by closing the doors of hospitals. the problem is not too many appeals, the problem is too many violations of rights in europe and this is what governments should be concerned about. the european parliament is therefore very concerned and very vigilant and considers it absolutely important to react in order to prevent this kind of reforms being discussed in brighton.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, this was certainly a very interesting discussion of the issue of accession to the european convention on human rights. i remember that this was a topical issue 15 years ago in my own country, where the european convention on human rights was already regarded very positively as a means of improving the judiciary and the legal system. by acceding to the european convention on human rights, the european union will integrate itself into a pan-european legal space of fundamental rights protection. it will enhance its credibility by entering into a commitment under international public law to respect fundamental rights. the eu will submit itself to external judicial control. so accession also means that the eu reaffirms the pivotal role played by the convention system in the protection of human rights in europe. much has already been done on the way to accession. but some important steps still remain. negotiations with the 20 non-eu states of the council of europe must be completed. once a final text has been agreed, the commission will submit the draft agreement to the court of justice for an opinion on its compatibility with the treaties. after a positive opinion, the council will have to adopt – by unanimity – decisions on the signature and conclusion of the agreement. the latter decision requires the consent of the european parliament and will only enter into force if member states approve. regarding international law, the accession agreement has to be ratified by the 47 current state parties to the european convention of human rights and approved by the union. the eu legislature will also have to adopt internal legal rules to properly implement accession internally. i am absolutely confident that the parties involved are fully aware that the governments and parliaments of all member states made a promise to citizens, and gave a strong signal to the outside world, when they committed the union to accede to the convention. i can also add that the commission agrees that it is necessary to work intensely on the internal rules from now on. solutions must be workable in practice and respect the institutional order of the union as defined by the treaties.

in writing. − in an increasingly competitive and economically interconnected world, a good basic education is a crucial starting point for every young person entering the world of work. however, young europeans often start from a disadvantaged position compared to their peers in the rest of the world: a recent survey shows that only 200 european universities are among the top 500 in the world. the challenge of preparing european students for the world of work is one that must be met with determination and without delay, by increasing funding for student mobility programmes (such as the erasmus programme, which has proved to be one of the most successful instruments among young europeans) and by providing loans to students to pursue a master's degree abroad. this will raise the quality of european students' training and at the same time strengthen the eu's competitiveness.

in writing. − the conservation of biodiversity is not only a moral obligation for future generations, but also of intrinsic economic and social importance. for example, the pollination of insects cannot be replaced by any artificial means, or the self-purifying capacity of soils makes it possible to obtain clean water easily and cheaply. what is missing for biodiversity conservation is not new programmes, policy statements or instructions for use, but action. it is also of the utmost importance to integrate the biodiversity strategy into the eu's forthcoming reform processes (e.g. fisheries, agricultural, energy and cohesion policies). future funding will play a very important role in this respect. the eu and its member states have so far spent less than 0.004% of their economic capacity on global measures to safeguard and promote biodiversity: it is necessary that member states begin to understand the importance of integrating natural capital into their public accounts. i therefore hope that the next multiannual financial framework will provide for the availability of adequate financial instruments to help prevent the loss of biodiversity and the degradation of ecosystem services in the eu.

in writing. − the eu biodiversity strategy to 2020 offers the opportunity to take the necessary steps to protect nature and ensure ecosystem services for future generations. all major european policies are currently under review. the common agricultural policy, cohesion policy, common fisheries policy and the european roadmaps for energy, transport and resource efficiency will soon be transposed into legislation. it is necessary to demonstrate that biodiversity claims are much more than just promises and must be reflected in concrete policy measures. i am in favour of the text of the report, but i have serious reservations about the development of new ad hoc financial instruments. it is necessary to provide for the availability of adequate financial instruments in the next multiannual financial framework. the value of biodiversity and ecosystem services must be integrated into our economies. only then will their costs and benefits be reflected in product prices. that is why the member states should integrate natural capital into their public accounts, but this would imply the current economic and financial crisis and above all would expose the member states to a huge risk that could turn out to be another failure at european level.
