i'm not going. no, because a european internal market requires that the tariffs be similar between domestic and non-domestic, there is no longer any difference if we talk about the single market, and above all because there is no technical justification for the increase in costs. i remember when in 2007 we started talking about voice roaming, the first third-party roaming we've ever been to. there was a certain incredulity and also a certain difficulty, not on the part of the commission - i have to acknowledge your predecessor, commissioner reding. the difficulties were widespread, coming from those who said that the position of a real market does not require regulation of tariffs, that they were political prices, that they belonged to an old conception of the left, and so on and so forth; and there were people who said it wouldn't work and so on, that it would slow down the market, but we did it. the interest of the citizens and the finding that there were no such technical justifications for the increase in costs led to this. so the world is traveling, things are becoming more and more, let's say, possible, so i think an even bolder outcome is possible. the last point, because there is no other point to make: we had a delegation of tunisian citizens today, i don't know if they are still here. perhaps among the many benefits of this extra-eu enlargement is that the possibility of using it without the cost of the scarecrow also helps democracy.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, there are more than 120 million broadband users in europe and at least 70 million citizens who use their mobile devices to connect to the internet, to work, to study or simply to obtain information. thanks to this regulation, the european union has finally decided to act in favour of all these consumers by reducing the cost of international telephone traffic: voice, data and sms. this is a positive decision because the price-cutting programme will lead to an average reduction in tariffs of 35% over the next three years. but that 's not enough . in a difficult time like the present one - both economically and in terms of employment - communication, new technologies and innovation are a primary asset that europe must defend with greater courage. every european citizen must be able to move freely between member states, using the telephone tariff set by his national operator. no more fraud and high-fee bills for people moving within the eu! if we really want to give a concrete answer to the citizens, let us create a kind of telecommunications schengen, which no longer imposes different tariffs on the citizens depending on the countries in which it operates.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i think there is no better day to have this debate: today is the celebration of europe, the celebration of an idea which has brought together twenty-seven nations, creating a single market, a common currency for many of our states, a continuous exchange in the field of culture, in the field of education, in feeling, in short, that we are all more united and closer. what tool today unites more than communication? the existence of a single internal telecommunications market cannot be maintained without telecommunications and if there were still significant differences between national and roaming prices. the ultimate objective is therefore also the hypothetical elimination of the difference between national tariffs and roaming tariffs, with the consequent establishment of an internal market for mobile communications services: that's one of the goals we have to set for ourselves. this improves competition, protects citizens and saves money, because high roaming charges are always a hindrance to the union's efforts to move towards a knowledge-based economy and the creation of an internal market for 500 million consumers. and not just that. the creation of a social area of education, culture and european enterprise, based on the mobility of people and digital data flows, should facilitate communication between people in order to achieve our goal of a true europe for the benefit of citizens. i therefore thank the rapporteur, mrs niebler, for her expertise, for her great ability to mediate, but also to achieve the objectives that have been achieved, for the importance of this dossier, and together with her, of course, for all the shadow rapporteurs.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, on europe day this regulation is a good example: the harmonisation of roaming charges is fundamental to the process of completing the internal market of the european union. there is always much talk about the single market and the removal of tariff frontiers, yet the barriers between european countries in the field of roaming telecommunications seemed insurmountable. that is no longer the case, and it will not be until july 2014 and beyond. the reduction in tariffs is finally real and tangible, and that is good news for citizens throughout europe. the agreement commits all operators in the 27 member states without exception to reducing roaming charges for calls, messages and internet connections as from 1 july next. a significant saving at a time of crisis and severe economic hardship for many families. i am also pleased with the rule which will allow users abroad to choose the cheapest operator from 2014. so no more restrictions! but all this is not enough, it is only a first step, the real objective is zero roaming, the real objective is the total abolition of roaming charges. the construction of a fair and competitive market also depends on europe's ability to protect the needs and rights of its citizens.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i would like to thank parliament for the opportunity to participate in this debate and to respond to some of the issues arising out of the recent visit by a delegation from the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs to sicily and lampedusa. we all know the challenges that some member states are facing when it comes to large and mixed migration flows to the eu. a number of these issues are more for the commission to address. furthermore, some of your questions should be answered by italy as a member state herself. i will therefore focus my comments on those issues which fall specifically within the remit of the council. i will particularly try to clarify how the council has sought to respond to the migratory pressures which italy, among others, has faced recently. the situation in the southern mediterranean has been an important item for the justice and home affairs council, in particular following the arab spring. in that respect, the council adopted last year conclusions on the management of migration from the southern neighbourhood, as well as on borders, migration and asylum. these conclusions underlined the need for genuine and concrete solidarity towards those member states most directly affected, as well as for a comprehensive response to the underlying causes. therefore, and building upon the work of the former polish presidency, the council has discussed ways of better managing asylum and migration within member states, in particular by preventing irregular migration and through cooperation with third countries. as part of this work the council agreed in march this year on a set of conclusions for concrete and practical ways to ensure solidarity towards member states facing particular pressures on their asylum systems, including through mixed migration flows. they highlight, for example, the importance of responsibility and mutual trust, preventive cooperation, the need for solidarity in emergency situations, strengthened cooperation between easo and frontex, financial solidarity and strengthening cooperation with key countries of transit, origin and first countries of asylum. on 26 april 2012 the council agreed on an eu action on migratory pressures as a strategic response containing an extensive list of actions in six priority areas. the action plan aims to prevent and control the pressures arising from illegal migration as well as abuse of legal migration channels. it combines and develops common eu action points and tools to prevent irregular immigration. in addition to these measures, member states have been encouraged to support the activities of frontex in the region. this support includes a joint operation, epn-hermes, in the mediterranean sea, intended to assist italy to address the increase in immigrants from north africa trying to reach lampedusa and sicily. frontex has also assisted italy in the area of border surveillance and search and rescue operations, screening of intercepted persons, debriefing activities and reaction capacity. according to data provided by frontex, approximately 51 000 people were detected during 2011 in or near lampedusa or in the surrounding area of sicily. most of them were tunisians and sub-saharan nationals. preventing such tragedies has to be a top priority. support for italy has also been provided through funds made available under the ‘solidarity and management of migration flows’ general programme. we are also working on long-term solutions for those in need of international protection in the countries of the southern neighbourhood, such as resettlement opportunities and humanitarian assistance to countries in the region having to deal with people displaced because of the libyan conflict. hopefully this will help relieve some of the pressures on italy. the council is expected to adopt a set of conclusions soon concerning the eu approach to migration and mobility, including on eu cooperation with third countries regarding migration. of course we are also working to put in place a strengthened legal framework which will enable the union and member states to provide better responses to situations of this kind. the establishment of the common european asylum system is an important part of this and the danish presidency looks forward to continuing to work with parliament and the committee on civil liberties and the commission in this area. for the council it is crucial that member states fulfil their obligations both in eu legislation and in international treaties, and that will be and will continue to be the position of the danish presidency.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, everybody is aware that italy faced very high migratory pressure from north african countries last year, especially after the events in tunisia and libya. some 60 000 migrants arrived, many of them needing protection. numbers so far this year are much lower: 790 people were intercepted in the first three months of the year. we all hope the situation in north africa will continue to stabilise, but people are still likely to try to cross the mediterranean. large influxes remain possible, and europe needs to be ready to react. that, by the way, is not just an italian issue; it is a matter of concern to the whole of europe. the eu acted quickly last year to support italy, notably through the hermes and aeneas border surveillance operations coordinated by frontex. frontex stands ready to support italy this year too. those operations both intercept irregular migrants and rescue those in distress. preventing tragedies at sea is a key objective. the eurosur system we proposed last year should also help by improving detection and tracking of small boats, which should enable faster rescue missions. some of those arriving are fleeing persecution and violence and need international protection. eu asylum rules aim to ensure that those who need it have effective access to asylum procedures, even when they are part of mixed migration flows. the commission closely monitors the implementation of those rules. the closure of lampedusa as a safe port of disembarkation is a matter of concern, something we quickly communicated to the italian authorities. commissioner malmström was in rome two weeks ago, and she was pleased to hear that italy intends to renovate the damaged facilities so that lampedusa can again become a point of first reception, assistance and initial screening before migrants are transferred to centres elsewhere in italy, where their possible needs for protection can be assessed. the commission looks forward to hearing the date for the reopening, and that reopening is part of a wider proposal which the new italian government has run up for an integrated strategy on management of the eu southern border. this proposal is very welcome, and we look forward to seeing how it is taken forward. the reception conditions directive obliges the member states to provide asylum seekers with appropriate accommodation. the member states have some flexibility in how this is provided, and specifically-designated reception centres are one option. the commission is in close contact with the italian authorities with a view to ensuring appropriate conditions and will not hesitate to take appropriate action. when it comes to the detention of irregular migrants, the return directive includes important safeguards, notably that the detainees must be kept in specialised facilities and must always be separated from ordinary prisoners. families must be given separate accommodation, and children need access to education. the ngos should be able to visit, and the detainees need to be able to contact their families and legal representatives. both asylum seekers and those subject to a return procedure must have access at least to essential healthcare. italy notified the commission of its transposition of the return directive last year. we are currently checking that this was done in line with the directive. as far as the guarantees i just mentioned are concerned, initial findings are that italy has correctly transposed them. to help address those challenges, italy has received substantial financial support from the eu, with a total of eur 232 million allocated for 2010, making it one of the largest beneficiaries of the ‘solidarity and management of migration flows’ general programme. this is before you count emergency financial support, which was over 18 million last year – and part of that was used to expand and develop government reception centres. the eu is also developing deeper contacts on migration and mobility issues with the southern mediterranean countries where possible, notably including tunisia and libya.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i apologise to the commissioner - my dear friend the commissioner. so, it is time to offer concrete responses to the arab spring. europe has followed with passion what has happened on the other side of the mediterranean. we followed with passion, with anxiety, with great participation of the citizens, even with a feeling of surprise over what happened and was happening in those months and still continues to take place with very difficult situations in egypt, in libya, in particular, not to mention syria. sometimes even hesitantly, i recall here some statements of european foreign ministers who a little over a year ago defined verbatim and i remember this because it makes us understand where we come from gaddafi as an example of reformism for the rest of africa, statement of february last year, syria as a country capable and i quote again verbatim of meeting the need for modernity of its citizens by its leadership. we come from this. another statement from february last year. but in the end, even with the support, the european empathy, the arab spring has worked hard to assert itself, and it's been a beautiful change. what has happened in the southern mediterranean is extraordinary, it is also a reason for great hope, but of course how difficult it is still. and what contribution can we make as europeans? in order to overcome the fragmentation of the trade relations between the european union and the mediterranean countries. only a short-sighted view of the european union's strategic role can suggest that a policy of closer integration with the countries of the southern shore of the mediterranean contradicts the european union's western vocation. trade, regulated by a balanced new free trade agreement, could also be an instrument of stability in an area affected by ferment that has not yet found a full democratic outlet, which also involves reducing inequalities, strengthening the productive fabric, better protection of civil and social rights, and the commitment to avoid drifting towards islamic fundamentalism. of course, it is not just up to us, not just the european union. it also depends on the great difficulties of cooperation and integration between the countries of the southern shore. but if the mediterranean, in the words of a great writer, becomes a project and not just a state of affairs, then together we can overcome the current political and economic obstacles that have delayed a good agreement for so long. the european union must take an initiative in the israeli-palestinian conflict, deepen the regulatory dialogue with all the countries to eliminate the excessive tariff barriers and not open their markets on the basis of reciprocity, which implies that a larger dose of aid must be linked to a greater commitment by our partners. in conclusion, i can only reiterate my appreciation of this report and i trust that the executive committee will take it as a priority objective of its political and administrative agenda.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think that mr rinaldi's excellent report has been a success in this house. i agree with the flattering assessment of the report. however, i would like to raise a small question: our europe, compared with this new world which is trying to find democracy and different economic conditions, is a europe divided by the mediterranean. it is precisely this particular attention to the mediterranean that i would like the commission to pay, both in terms of environmental aspects and in terms of economic transactions in the mediterranean. the mediterranean is a fishing place. we are building a new fisheries policy in europe which will set very strict rules on the part of europe. on the other hand, there are no rules. so why not use some form of fisheries agreement, support for these countries so that they apply the same rules as those applied in europe. this would be good for european fisheries, it would be good for the sea, it would be good for the environment, it would make this rift less and less divided and more and more a homogeneous place on which to build the future of europe and of this new world.

president-in-office of the council. − madam president, i am very pleased to be able to participate today in this very important debate on the correct implementation of the eu budget. i would like to take this opportunity to thank mr geier and the rest of this house for its very warm reception of the danish presidency. let me start by stressing the particular importance which the council attaches to the proper spending of eu appropriations. this applies especially in times of economic and financial crisis, when many member states have to cut their national budgets and keep their expenditure under strict control, and when european citizens and taxpayers pay even closer attention to the correct use of public funds, not only at the national but also at the european level. on 28 february my colleague minister vestager was in the european parliament’s committee on budgetary control to present the council’s recommendation to give a discharge to the commission in respect of the implementation of the budget for 2010. on that occasion she was able to participate in a very interesting and fruitful debate on the implementation of the eu budget, which concentrated in particular on its implementation under shared management by the commission and member states. it again became evident that the european parliament and the council share the same concerns. we therefore both addressed the fact that a large share of payments from the eu budget is still materially affected by error, and we both follow the overall aim of attaining an unqualified audit opinion from the european court of auditors. in that context i would like to mention that minister vestager has informed her colleagues in ecofin about the issues raised by the committee on budgetary control during the debate. i can only repeat what was said in february. the council would like to see more progress in the financial management and control of eu funds. it encouraged the commission to fully assume its responsibility in the implementation of the budget, to reinforce its supervision and control structures and to strengthen its cooperation with and its guidance to member state authorities. the council recalls in this context the importance of recoveries and financial corrections which are an essential element in protecting the union’s financial interest and in improving the management of eu funds. payment should be interrupted and suspended whenever significant deficiencies are identified and until corrective action is fully implemented. unduly paid amounts should be recovered without delay and full transparency in the implementation of corrective action must be ensured. i can assure you that the council presidency will make all possible efforts to make progress on this issue and i have noted that many of the council’s priorities are also those of the european parliament; i therefore count on your cooperation and support. we can improve the situation if all actors – the european parliament, council, commission and member states – work constructively together towards the sound financial management and an efficient control of eu funds. the ongoing negotiations and the revision of the financial regulation are a perfect opportunity to improve and simplify procedures, and to reasonably strengthen supervision and control without creating any excessive administrative burden. finally, i have to say a few words on the disagreement between the european parliament and the council on the discharge procedure between our institutions. the council is of the opinion that it is important to find a durable solution to this recurring problem and that this solution should be based on three principles: accountability, transparency and reciprocity. therefore, the council has made a proposal to the european parliament on the discharge procedure, and the council has asked the european parliament to appoint a formal delegation to discuss this proposal and to solve the outstanding issues. the danish presidency looks forward to the continuing informal dialogue between our institutions on this issue, which we hope can pave the way to solving our disagreements. i welcome therefore this debate today and i am looking forward to a very constructive cooperation with the commission, the european parliament, the member states and the council.
member of the commission. − madam president, first of all let me start by thanking you for the constructive and fruitful work achieved over the last few months. the commission has been in close contact with your rapporteur and your colleagues on the committee on budgetary control to discuss all kinds of issues related to the sound financial management of the main eu programmes. six members of the commission and the secretary-general of the commission participated in very lively discharge hearings. this intense dialogue between the institutions demonstrates the importance, but also the complexity, of the matters which we have to deal with. the commission appreciated very much this trustful and good cooperation and i am looking forward to continuing to work with you on the topics we have discussed. the rapporteur mentioned four priority actions for the commission and i would like to stress that the commission is fully aware of your concerns and your expectations vis-à-vis the commission, but also vis-à-vis other financial actors. i would like to highlight the implementation of financial engineering instruments as one example where the commission has proactively taken into account the outcome of the discussions we had. following the commission’s proposal, member states have to provide more focused and detailed reports on the implementation of these instruments. as a consequence, by the end of the year, we should have all necessary information to hand to provide you with an analysis per member state and a comprehensive evaluation of the use of financial engineering instruments. but more has been done. in anticipation of the need for closer monitoring, the commission proposal for the next programming period already envisages enhanced monitoring and control mechanisms for those financial instruments. apart from the priority actions highlighted by the rapporteur, the discharge report includes many more requests to the commission. they are all being analysed and will be followed up. a comprehensive report on the follow-up to the discharge requests and on the concrete actions taken will be issued later this year, together with the evaluation report required under article 318 of the treaty. i consider the effective implementation of these recommendations to be of the utmost importance in addressing the weaknesses identified in the implementation of the eu budget. we have discussed the role of member states in the implementation of the eu budget many times already. member states have a crucial role when it comes to the operational implementation of eu programmes and projects. the authorities of the member states are paying out, and controlling on the spot, some 80% of the eu budget to final beneficiaries. there is no doubt that the commission will continue to assume its final responsibility for the correct implementation of the eu budget, in accordance with the treaty. but to reduce the error rate under shared management, we do need the member states’ cooperation and commitment to assuming their responsibility as the first-level financial actors in direct contact with the final beneficiaries. as the last annual report from the court of auditors has revealed, member states’ authorities did not detect and correct many errors, even though they had the necessary information available. further work on effective – but also proportionate – supervisory and monitoring mechanisms in the current period and for the future is therefore necessary. the commission appreciates your support in further developing these mechanisms and improving the implementation procedures at member state level. the provision of reliable and complete financial information and audit data by the member states is one example of an area where improvements are necessary. we can see some progress in this regard, but this is not yet satisfactory. this is why the commission will, from now on, transmit the annual summaries of the member states with an analysis of their content to the committee on budgetary control, in accordance with article 319 of the treaty. where appropriate, the commission will make recommendations to the national authorities on how to further improve this reporting instrument so they can contribute better to the commission’s assurance process. the discharge authority will be informed about these recommendations. however, their publication remains subject to the conditions set in the legislation on public access to the eu institutions’ documents. in this context, i would like to recall the importance of introducing a management declaration of assurance, which the commission has proposed in the revision of the financial regulation. this would be an important building block towards an improved assurance chain between the management and control bodies in the member states and the commission services. here as well, in the negotiations on the financial regulation, the commission is on the side of parliament to ensure the highest level of transparency and accountability from the member states. we have, moreover, proposed introducing political accountability through the possibility of submitting national declarations of assurance. provided that member states’ national declarations respect necessary conditions, the commission will, as an incentive, take those declarations into account in the establishment of its own audit strategy. as regards the european development fund, we welcome the parliament’s recommendations. the area of external aid is by nature a risky and complex one. an error level of 3.4 % is limited but remains a source of concern for both this house and the commission. we will take all necessary actions to further improve the edf’s financial management, securing the effectiveness and sustainability of the eu’s support, which is badly needed by the acp countries. this discharge procedure provided valuable input for the negotiations on the next financial period. several new measures included in our proposals for the next generation of eu spending programmes were inspired by the european court of auditors and the discharge authority. the commission will demonstrate its firm commitment to achieving all possible improvements. the discharge report on which you will vote is a clear road map for actions to be taken by the commission and the other financial actors.
president of the european court of auditors. − madam president, i am honoured to be the first president of the european court of auditors to be invited to address parliament at this stage in the discharge procedure. the discharge procedure is essential for european union public accountability. it helps provide citizens with assurance as to what european funds were spent on, whether they were used correctly, and what was achieved with them. the primary responsibility for answering these questions lies with those responsible for managing european funds: the commission and the relevant national authorities. they need to put in place systems capable of doing so. the court’s role is to provide independent assessments of the quality of their financial management and reporting systems. for the financial year 2010 the court concluded that the european union accounts prepared by the commission do provide a reliable picture of what european union funds were spent on. we noted, however, that the commission does not yet provide a complete and reliable set of information on whether european union funds have been correctly raised and spent. on the basis of our own audit testing, the court concluded that revenue and commitments underlying the european union accounts were legal and regular in all material respects. in contrast to this, payments underlying these accounts were affected by material error with an estimated error rate of 3.7% overall. as in previous years, the area most prone to error was cohesion. we also concluded that systems were only partly effective overall and that there continued to be risks in the other areas of expenditure, which need to be managed and disclosed. the court recommended that due account should be taken of these risks when revising the legislative instrument for the next programming period. in particular, the court stressed that reforms should focus on both reducing errors and improving the results we achieve with the funds of the european union. it is also important to ensure there is adequate provision for transparency. the commission’s reporting on results achieved needs to be improved. in particular, we emphasised the need to set smart objectives and milestones for the new programming period. this is a point we also stressed in our recent opinions on the new legislative proposals governing the main areas of expenditure for the period 2014 to 2020. in the discharge decision on the 2009 financial year, this parliament invited the court to present an opinion on the evaluation report required by the lisbon treaty. this report was delivered in february this year by the commission and we will issue an opinion shortly. the court believes that this first evaluation report represents an initial step in the right direction and provides parliament, the council and the commission with an opportunity to discuss and agree how it can be made useful to the discharge authority as an instrument for european union transparency and accountability. the court believes that an effective discharge procedure is essential for the european union’s accountability and we are fully committed to working with parliament and the other partners in this process to achieve that goal each year.

mr president, this document focuses on the importance of regional airports as potential vectors of territorial, economic and social cohesion. such infrastructure can and must play this role, especially for citizens living outside large urban centres. the rule that lowers the threshold for determining which airports can receive state aid to two hundred thousand passengers a year is a good one. regional aviation can ensure that free movement in europe is a reality not only for people living in the big capitals but also for citizens of europe living outside these areas, ensuring that these cities and regions can enjoy the benefits brought by not only increased mobility but also the tourism that comes with it.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as rapporteur for the alde group i am voting in favour of the own-initiative report on regional airports and i am sure that it will provide the legal basis for further regulation of these airports. this dossier testifies to the importance which the european parliament attaches to these airports in the context of air transport and the important role they play in promoting territorial, economic and social cohesion in the territory of the european union. the definition of regional airport was given for the first time and an attempt was made to narrow down the scope by means of a division into major and minor, also in relation to criteria such as the volume of passenger traffic and the connections provided by these airports. it is certainly desirable that the commission should then follow up with more stringent guidelines on their definition. a particular step is the recognition of the need to guarantee public service obligations in relation to isolated, insular and peripheral territories, for which we know that there is a handicap in relation to participation in the single market. finally, i think that the definition which sets out and clarifies a negative indication of the irrational proliferation of new regional airports was useful.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, regional airports are important for better connecting europe and for enabling its citizens to move within the union, but these structures must be built and must operate in accordance with the environmental standards set by the union itself. we cannot allow air traffic, and with it regional airports, to go further at the expense of the european environment, the quality of our air and the integrity of our territory. in northern italy, for example - i am thinking of the cities of treviso and verona - airport facilities have been expanded in recent years without taking due account of the realities in which these hubs operate every day. it is good to have more air connections in europe, but not at the expense of the environment, the air and the territory of europe itself.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, regional airports are essential transport hubs and factors for growth and territorial cohesion. these airports often depend on large injections of public money, but these are now becoming increasingly scarce and it is therefore important that they have a specific purpose, avoiding a proliferation that would lead to the non-use or insufficient use of airport infrastructure. the scores of airports in northern italy, situated a few dozen kilometres apart, are a typical example. the commission has not yet defined a precise definition of regional airport and should therefore establish common criteria for a correct definition. finally, i am concerned about the wording concerning the scope and in particular the exclusion of airports whose main catchment area is a capital city. i do not think that is correct, as the definition of the user pool is not uniform and can change. despite these criticisms, i voted in favour of the proposal to draw the commission's attention to these important points.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the potential of the new communication channels is enormous, in a world where everything is digital, information is a commodity for every european citizen. the european union needs to protect all end-users and try to minimise the disparities between member states in the european market. i would remind you that the european union, as the promoter of a single internal market, cannot ignore the implementation of the internal telecommunications market. the considerable differences between domestic and roaming prices obviously make these objectives difficult to achieve. i agree with mrs niebler's proposal: each supplier in the country of origin must clearly and adequately inform the customer of the consumption levels reached and agreed. transparent information on the conclusion of contracts and on the charges for the use of data roaming services will be a means of protecting european consumers, and that is why i voted in favour of the report.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the adoption of this resolution is a very important political signal in the fight against maritime piracy. paragraph 30 of my motion for a resolution specifies that in the event of disputes between states as a result of military action to counter piracy in international waters, the national jurisdiction of the flag state over ships and military personnel on board should apply, as required by international law. this is crucial to avoid future disputes like the one currently taking place between italy and india and to defend the prerogatives of the military involved in the atalanta mission and as vpd on merchant ships. i dedicate the approval of this text to massimiliano latorre and salvatore girone, the two italian soldiers who have been unjustly detained in indian prisons for almost three months, waiting for india to recognise italian jurisdiction and for these two soldiers to be tried by the national judiciary. i hope that european diplomacy will renew its support for italy in this battle of civilisations.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i did not support mr moreira's report. at a time like the present, when uncontrolled relocation and the economic crisis are putting western europe in serious difficulty and would require a review of all the principles underlying the common commercial policy, the fact that the wto decides to accept a chinese complaint against an article of the anti-dumping regulation in force in the european union, or of council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community, clearly shows that there is no will at world level to defend our productive and industrial fabric and that the commission has not yet understood that anti-protectionism does not benefit european companies and its consumers, but the harmful behaviour of third countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr moreira's report on defence against dumped imports from non-eu countries. to promote the development of world trade, the 27 member states have drawn up a common commercial policy towards third countries, seeking to abolish trade restrictions and excessive tariffs. this liberalization of trade does not imply a failure to respect the rights and obligations of trading partners operating at international level. i believe that real reforms and a serious commitment to tackling problems of market distortion by ensuring consistency between business behaviour and rules of international free competition are essential.
in writing. - in a globalised market environment and in the light of the recent opening up of the so-called 'arab spring' countries, it is most appropriate and necessary to pay attention to illegal trade practices such as dumping, in order to protect european businesses. strengthening the network of safeguards in defence of our entrepreneurs means not closing ourselves off to competition fears but allowing access to the global market with clear and legitimate conditions for both european and non-eu competitors. i therefore voted in favour of the report which provides for measures to combat the phenomenon of dumping which is likely to favour some importing firms at the expense of others, thereby altering the nature of the markets.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the vital moreira report. i agree with the commission's proposal. i agree with the wording of the new article 9 (5) in particular because an anti-dumping duty must be imposed at the appropriate level in each case and without discrimination on imports of products found to be dumped and causing injury.
in writing. - the economic crisis in europe is such that more decisive action is needed to defend our industry and our small and mediumsized enterprises, especially when they are subject to dumping or other unfair behaviour by economic operators from countries where the rule of law does not apply and where the protection of social and environmental rights is de facto non-existent. the fact that the wto decides to accept a chinese complaint against an article of the already unambitious anti-dumping regulation in force in the european union is a step in the opposite direction, making it more difficult to defend our companies and our jobs. i cannot therefore agree with the content of this regulation, which is likely to aggravate the difficulties of our economic operators.
in writing. - i wish to express my vote against this measure and i wish to state the political reasons which led me to this decision. we must send a signal to the european commission to represent us properly in the wto. the european parliament's defeat in a dispute with china at the world trade organisation would today oblige it to delete an article of our basic regulation on anti-dumping rules. it is wrong not to be more firm in the face of international bodies such as the wto. it's wrong not to defend our production system. it is wrong not to expect china to reciprocate our products and services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr sturdy's report because, after russia's accession to the world trade organisation, the eu can no longer impose quantitative limits on imports from wto countries into the union, as it did in the case of steel from russia. in addition, this measure could favour trade relations between the eu and russia and would therefore be very positive for our country and our companies, as the russian market is rapidly expanding and very dynamic.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1342/2007 on the administration of certain restrictions on imports of certain steel products from the russian federation contains a clause according to which the rules contained in the regulation cease to apply when russia becomes a member of the world trade organisation. this was done last december, and it is clear that an outdated regulation must be repealed. in addition, the union has no right to apply import quotas to other wto countries and would be subject to sanctions or legal proceedings if it did so. finally, considering that russia's accession to the wto can also represent an important opportunity for our companies, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i agree to the abrogation of the previous regulation as russia is now a member of the world trade organisation. i also agree with the rapporteur that he wants to see trade relations between the eu and russia developed in full compliance with the commonly agreed provisions of existing bilateral agreements. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − russia's accession to the world trade organisation means that the eu must adapt to the new market scenario: the opening to the russian federation with consequent limitation of restrictions. the text specifically abolishes the quantitative limits on steel imports into the eu, as provided for in the 1997 partnership and cooperation agreement. the opening up in this sense is certainly positive and considering that the rules to be followed will be those imposed by the wto, the eu's import - export will be able to improve.
in writing. - my vote in favour of this measure is not just a due act. indeed, wto rules require the european union to remove rules imposing restrictions on the import of products from other wto members. since russia has joined the wto, if we had not started with today's vote to remove certain rules, we would have faced certain trade sanctions that would have harmed our production system and our companies.
in writing. − since russia joined the wto on 16 december 2011, the eu no longer has any right to impose quotas on steel imports under regulation (ec) no 1342/2007 and therefore the perpetuation of such quotas would constitute a breach of wto rules and expose the eu to legal action by russia. i voted in favour of this text, as it is very likely that with the repeal of the european regulation, the eu will benefit from more liberalised access to the russian steel market. there will still be minor restrictions on bilateral imports, but these should not, in my view, constitute obstacles within the framework of the wto rules. it is expected that european steel and metallurgical exports could benefit from an increase of some eur 107 million each year, which is to the benefit of our companies working in this sector.
in writing. − independent research shows that the so-called 'digital divide' is largely overcome in all age groups, weighting education and volume of interactions. we live in a world with over 600 million websites and a lot of interaction with government and public administration is now done online. according to eurostat, in 2009, at least 65% of european enterprises used e-government, rising to 83% for large companies. the oecd has repeatedly pointed to the development of e-government as a key axis for improving transparency and simplification processes. the imposition of onerous paper-based consultation procedures on a society that now lives, communicates and informs itself digitally and relies on it for essential aspects of its daily existence, from financial markets to telemedicine, seems to be an outdated legacy that must be urgently corrected, given its widespread negative effects, for example on the economy and business, in terms of legal uncertainty and the resulting slowdown in investment, trade and development. i therefore support the recommendation and hope that the new council regulation will enter into force as soon as possible.
in writing. − european integration also involves recognising the role played by the union's institutions. in my view, the actions promoted by these institutions do not have adequate visibility at national level. i therefore believe that an effort is needed to promote transparency policies and to make official documentation easily accessible to all european citizens. the electronic publication of the official journal is already a reality and is now the main form of consultation. the court of justice has, however, clarified that, in the absence of a legal basis, publication on the internet has no legal value and therefore no rights and obligations can be asserted. the legal status of the electronic version of the official journal will significantly increase transparency, since it will be immediately and freely accessible to all, and the information contained therein will be reliable and binding. i believe that it is our duty to make official information accessible to the widest possible public, and i therefore gave a favourable opinion on the report on the electronic publication of the official journal of the european union. i also take this opportunity to underline the importance of implementing the digital agenda set out in the europe 2020 strategy by promoting access to high-speed internet connectivity for all european citizens.
in writing. - i believe that this report should be fully supported, in the name of that transparency and closeness to the citizens which is so much demanded of the european institutions. the publication of the official journal of the european union in electronic format, with its authentic value and legal effect, will also be made mandatory, thereby ensuring faster and cheaper access to it and promoting the development of a digital internal market. i also consider that the report does not overlook the aspects relating to the protection of the authenticity, integrity and unalterableness of the electronic publication of the official journal, so i voted in favour.
in writing. − the introduction of the legal basis equivalent to the legal value of documents published in the official journal of the european union in electronic format is an indisputable step towards opening up public institutions to their citizens. the fact that this gap has been closed gives added meaning to the other initiatives taken by the european parliament to make its own workings, and those of the other european institutions, as transparent as possible for the citizens of the union. i believe that a common legal basis for the legal documents of the official journal was necessary in order to be able to fully grasp the social and technological changes that are evolving with increasing speed and require ready responses from the institutions.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we welcome this draft council regulation which aims to strengthen legal certainty by making community law more accessible and allowing all citizens to rely on the electronic edition of the official journal of the european union (oj) as the authentic, official, up-to-date and complete version. the electronic publication will therefore be legally equivalent to a publication of the oj with legal value. only in exceptional and temporary cases of unexpected interruption of electronic publication would the printed edition have legal value. we are convinced that this regulation will allow for an appropriate reform of the way the oj are published, ensuring greater legal certainty and better access for citizens to the legal acts of the european union. the reform will also increase legal certainty and reduce the cost of access for citizens and businesses.
in writing. it is a fact that almost all people consult the legal acts of the european union in electronic format. it is therefore appropriate that it should be brought up to date. the publication of the official journal on the internet will ensure greater legal certainty and facilitate citizens' access to the legal activity of the european union. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − citizens' free access to information and the dissemination and publication of european legislation are at the heart of this council proposal for the electronic publication of the official journal of the european union. easier access to eu law will make it easier for all citizens to understand and be sure of community law; in addition, texts published electronically will have legal value and will be available for consultation at any time. this is a good idea for communicating the work of the institutions to european citizens more quickly and clearly.
in writing. - i congratulate mr ziobro on his work on this new regulation which provides for the electronic publication of the official journal of the european union, in order to ensure faster and cheaper access to official information. while it is true that rules must be established to ensure the authenticity, integrity and unalterability of the electronic publication of the official journal, it is also true that in the age of the internet and the digital revolution european citizens cannot be denied unlimited access to the rules of law in all the official languages.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i consider it a priority to strengthen legal certainty by making eu law more accessible and allowing everyone to rely on the electronic edition of the official journal of the european union. given that almost all people now consult eu legal acts exclusively in electronic format, it is unacceptable that this version is not legally binding. moreover, consultation of the printed version of the official journal is a long and costly process, carried out by a very small number of users. i therefore believe that the reform can increase legal certainty and reduce the cost of access for citizens and businesses.
in writing. − strengthen legal certainty by making eu law more accessible, enabling everyone to rely on the electronic edition of the official journal of the european union as the authoritative, official, up-to-date and complete version. this vote establishes the principle that electronic publication will therefore be equivalent to a publication in the official journal with legal value. only in exceptional and temporary cases of unexpected interruption of electronic publication would the printed edition have legal value. this will ensure greater legal certainty and better access for citizens to the legal acts of the european union. at present, almost all people consult the legal acts of the european union exclusively in electronic format. the fact that the electronic version is not legally binding is unacceptable in itself and is a source of uncertainty which must be removed.
in writing. - i fully share some of the principles set out in my colleague mr bradbourn's report in helping regional airports, especially those in remote areas or on islands, to develop and strengthen existing links while avoiding becoming the exclusive domain of low-cost airlines. it is right to start with a cost-benefit analysis so that a national plan for airports can be drawn up and, if necessary, new airports built. good planning can only bring benefits and answers to social and territorial needs, thus creating new jobs and services, improving the quality of life of citizens and also of businesses and even more of tourism. let us not forget that tourism is the third largest socioeconomic activity in the eu, accounting for 10% of gdp and 12% of employment. in line with the strategy on the future of tourism adopted on 27 september, this report makes a significant contribution to boosting the competitiveness of the tourism sector and to consolidating europe's image and visibility as a tourist hub. finally, i think it is appropriate that regional airports should be included in the ten-t guidelines alongside the terrestrial transport networks and that they too should be able to benefit from private and public funding.
in writing. - i support the resolution by mr bradbourn calling on the commission to pay greater attention in eu legislation to the situation of 'regional airports', whose function is predominantly linked to the territory. they must be included in the planning of the community transport network in order to offer them greater accessibility and to ensure a fair allocation of slots to different air carriers, so as to ensure proper competition which protects both the airport itself and the consumer who approaches it.
in writing. - the report deals with problems, prospects and developments in the air transport market which have sensitive implications, particularly in terms of economic growth and consumer rights, and which should be examined and addressed with the instruments at our disposal, and the relevant local authorities should be called upon to reflect on their own. i would like to highlight four main themes: territorial cohesion, which involves sensitive citizenship rights profiles and problems of maintaining local economies in peripheral areas; the practices introduced by some low-cost airlines, which are only partly due to the low margins of this sector, which call for a reflection on consumer rights, especially as a result of the intervention of the spanish government; the role of regional airports in the economies of the territory, and in relation to structural weaknesses that expose them to the leverage of dominant positions; finally, and most importantly, the need to integrate regional airports into the sphere of attention and intervention of the european legislator, with a simplification and regulatory alignment activity and the incentive to build integrated systems and networks that enhance aspects of multimodality. the report, which i approve and endorse, opens a more attentive view of the role of air transport in our societies.
in writing. − the free movement of persons within the union's borders is one of the four fundamental freedoms guaranteed to european citizens. in order to guarantee this right de facto, it is necessary to establish a capillary transport network, which is not limited to the large capitals. parliament therefore has a responsibility to correct the direction taken by the commission, which is too focused on the development of hub airports and too little on the potential of regional airports. the full development of these airports is essential both to guarantee the freedom of movement mentioned above and to promote the economic development of the areas where these airports are located, since their expansion would also help to alleviate the congestion problem of hub airports and, consequently, to make the transport system more sustainable also from an environmental point of view. for the reasons i have just mentioned, i therefore voted in favour of the report on the future of regional airports. finally, i hope that malpensa airport will be strengthened and will once again play its role as an international hub, because the city of milan, as the economic capital of our country, and its businesses must be properly connected with the other member states.
in writing. − regional airports are taking a very secondary role in eu legislation despite the increasing difficulties they are facing. difficulties caused by the monopoly of low-cost airlines and the unfair practices of these airlines, as well as the isolation from the rest of the transport network and infrastructure, which forces passengers to change transport several times before reaching the regional airport. this results in the cancellation of the advantage originally sought by the traveller, inevitably leading many potential passengers to prefer travel with scheduled airlines via the larger and more functional hub airports. i therefore believe that this report deserves my full support, since it seeks to ensure fair competition between air carriers and greater accessibility to these airports. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − air transport is of fundamental importance both as a transport and as a generator of economic growth. however, there is a tendency on the part of the european commission to underestimate the impact of some of its regulations on regional airports, while concentrating almost exclusively on major airports. this is an unjustified trend affecting airports which already face obstacles from the environmental impact of air traffic, congestion and competition from larger airports. the present report takes these issues to the european commission and makes several proposals (moving some air traffic to regional airports, integrating them into the ten-t network, establishing a common definition of regional airport) to improve the current situation.
in writing. − the development and growth of regional and peripheral airports is an opportunity for the growth of local economies and currently less developed areas of europe. the current under-used and under-exploited airport terminals are diverse and action to improve their efficiency is desirable. the economy of the territories would clearly benefit, particularly in the tourist sector. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the free movement of goods are respected. in this resolution we call for the european union to support regional airports more and more and to take full account of the economic opportunities they represent for the territories in which they operate.
in writing. − with this report we want to underline the important role played by regional airports and their air services as they not only help to facilitate the smooth functioning of the single market of the european union by transporting people and goods between regions, but are capable of producing economic growth in themselves by attracting more economic investment. on the contrary, they have often been affected or excluded from community legislation, sometimes unintentionally but in a highly disproportionate way. we therefore call on the european commission to pay particular attention to regional airports and regional air services, as they risk being excluded from the market in the face of increased consolidation between large airports, airlines and airline alliances. a non-competitive and monopolistic market would not only be extremely damaging to regional aviation but also to european citizens, who would face a reduction in choice and an increase in prices. we therefore call for greater commitment to the development of sesar and the single european sky, as their completion could lead to major economic and environmental savings through increased efficiency and would allow some small regional airports to benefit from new investment and technology.
in writing. - avoid an unnecessary proliferation of regional airports; we must avoid the creation of airport infrastructure which is then unused or used inefficiently, and which would end up being a financial burden for the responsible authorities. i agree with the need to encourage the strengthening of existing links, especially in areas with geographical difficulties. my vote on the report on the future of regional airports and air services in the eu is in favour.
in writing. − the issue of air transport within community policy is increasingly a topic of discussion as, for cohesion and development policy, the eu needs to regulate funding for airports. these are divided into two types, regional airports and hubs: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all air carriers, including those operating in the eu, and to extend the scope of the directive to include air carriers operating in third countries. the eu should focus more on managing funding for these national scales which are crucial for territorial, economic and social cohesion.
in writing. the european commission should not underestimate the importance of 'regional airports', which differ from 'hub airports' in that their function is mainly linked to the territory in which they are located. unfortunately, these airports are increasingly being neglected by european legislation and are considered secondary in recent proposals for the development of the european transport network. i share the rapporteur's view that many regional airports are monopolized by individual airlines and isolated from the transport network. unfair practices such as the 'one-baggage rule' imposed by carriers, which reduces passenger expense at airports by up to 70%, with consequences for the local economies linked to regional airports, must be prevented.
in writing. - today parliament voted on the report by mr philip bradbourn on the importance of regional airports as a development engine for regional tourism and for specialised freight transport, which are crucial for the territorial cohesion and economic diversification of the union, especially in regions where other means of transport are lacking. however, the crisis has hit regional airports hard, which are currently out of the market, leading to a greater consolidation between the main airports and airlines, with the result that there is less choice and higher prices for customers. the inclusion of regional airports in the ten-t guidelines could facilitate access to private finance and encourage member states to invest in better land transport networks, in particular high-speed trains. however, to improve the overall quality of services, it is necessary to address some practices adopted by the main low-cost airlines, such as excessive booking fees and restrictions on hand luggage that discourage travellers from buying products at the airport.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is essential to strengthen the role of regional airports in facilitating the smooth functioning of the eu single market, in transporting people and goods between regions and in generating economic growth in its own right. i firmly believe that european regional airports and air services should be seen as key elements in creating an efficient european transport network that will facilitate trade and ensure mobility for more people. finally, i hope that regional aviation can ensure that eu citizens living in these areas enjoy the benefits of not only increased mobility but also the resulting tourism, access to new markets and the ability to attract more economic investment.
in writing. − there is currently no definition of 'regional airport' in europe: there are major and minor airports according to the types of connections provided, the volume of passengers and the connections with the main cities and the main airports. once the criteria and parameters for defining regional airports have been established, with a view to efficient intermodal mobility, they can make a significant contribution to improving access to regions and businesses, promoting tourism and the development of related services and spreading economic prosperity. the vote draws attention to the way in which regional airports and air services have often been unintentionally, but disproportionately, affected by european union legislation. the operational and economic efficiency of regional airports and air services needs to be improved, as well as the passenger experience of using these facilities and services.
