in writing. the proposal aims to increase the level of competition in the mobile roaming segment by means of the so-called structural solution: the user will be able to sign a separate contract exclusively for roaming charges, keeping a single telephone number and a single sim card. i am convinced that the proposed solution will help to establish a more competitive system in this sector, and i have therefore expressed my favourable opinion of this report. i regret, however, that the amendment was not adopted, which would have prevented telephone companies from charging roaming charges to the user for calls within a 10 km radius of the border of the country where the telephone contract was concluded. this amendment would have avoided the unfair application of roaming charges for calls made in municipalities bordering foreign countries, and would also have alleviated the costs of use for crossborder workers, such as citizens residing in italy but employed in swiss companies close to the italian border.
in writing. - i welcome the proposal by mrs niebler on roaming on public mobile communications networks within the european union. today, with the rapid increase in mobility within the union and at the same time with the considerable developments in the telecommunications sector, we cannot ask citizens to bear excessively high costs, particularly in 'data roaming'. i therefore agree with the further reduction of roaming charges, which guarantee full transparency and consumer protection. i believe that these new measures, which will take effect from 1 july 2012 and will be fully implemented from 1 july 2014 with the possibility for customers to choose a different operator than their national operator for roaming services, will encourage more operators to compete by further reducing tariffs.
in writing. - i welcome the desire expressed in this report to make it easier for citizens to move within the union by allowing them to use their national mobile phone number to make calls, send sms or surf the internet at lower prices than those currently in force. this not only benefits travellers, but also contributes to the development of a competitive european digital market, facilitating access to the wholesale market for new alternative operators. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs niebler's report because i believe that the mobile telephony market needs structural reforms to ensure that consumer rights are protected and at the same time to allow for greater competition in the roaming market so that the cost of tariffs can be reduced. among the measures envisaged, the introduction of tariff ceilings is in line with the proposed direction and continues the path of a commitment to streamline the european single market and make it competitive in trade relations with non-eu countries. in view of the exponential growth of roaming services, the adoption of this resolution is a significant act that takes the needs of european consumers and citizens seriously.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we welcome this report because for years we have felt that there is still little competition in the telephone roaming market, to the direct detriment of our citizens who are consumers. roaming charges remain excessively high, despite our 2007 measures, and this results in a consequent low usage of roaming services in the eu in clear contradiction to the fundamental principles of an ambitious european digital single market. the commission already set itself the objective of broadly aligning national and roaming charges for mobile telephony services by 2015 in its 2010 digital agenda for europe. in order to increase competition, the commission proposal for a regulation which we voted on today now provides for the introduction of structural measures which we consider appropriate, in addition to the existing tariff ceilings, and which will help to protect consumers adequately. we believe, however, that further efforts are needed in the area of transparency: the commission has also proposed that the commission should provide more comprehensive information on the new opportunities and tariffs that customers will be able to enjoy as a result of the scrapping measures and the more ambitious retail data roaming caps than those proposed by the commission in this case.
in writing. - my vote on mrs niebler's report is in favour. the demand for roaming services is growing exponentially. however, high prices for data roaming services discourage customers from using mobile data services when travelling within the european union. i therefore agree that there should be no obstacles to the use of alternative data roaming services, provided directly on a host network, either temporarily or permanently, irrespective of the existing roaming contracts or agreements with national providers and without additional charges being charged by the latter.
in writing. − in recent years, the number of people moving frequently across europe has increased considerably, for a variety of reasons. one of the biggest inconveniences these people face is certainly the astronomical cost of using mobile phones abroad. the situation has gradually improved in recent years, and the text we have adopted today is a further step in that right direction. the measures provided for in the regulation will lead to a significant reduction in the prices of calls, sms and data roaming. the commission has also proposed that the market should be opened up to more operators, so as to allow for effective competition and thus reduce the monopoly of the few telephone companies currently offering roaming services. initiatives such as these at european level are certainly useful and desirable, with positive repercussions for all citizens and consumers, and without causing any damage whatsoever. it is on actions such as these that the european union should concentrate, that is, on proving itself useful, and for which it can therefore have, as in this case, our full and resolute support.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs niebler's report because i am one of those mobile phone users who, when using telephone services outside my country, feel that they are spending too much on national tariffs. the commission's analysis of the proposal for a regulation on roaming on public mobile communications networks in the eu shows that high prices or risks of high costs are due to low competition in this market. the mobile operators are not very numerous and this allows them to keep the costs to users much higher than they would be in the event of increased competition. this is why the eu, in addition to setting tariff ceilings for international incoming and outgoing calls and sms, is planning system structural reforms that will open up international roaming networks to operators in other countries, thanks to regulated wholesale tariffs.
in writing. - the report by mr bradbourn was voted on today at the brussels plenary session. the cost of using mobile phones, smartphones and tablets when travelling within the eu will fall dramatically from 1 july this year, under an agreement with the council approved today. the new rules will also allow customers to buy roaming services from operators other than their national operators and open the market to new competitors, in order to increase competition and reduce prices. the proposal will enter into force on 1 july 2012, replacing the 2007 regulation which expires on 30 june 2012. during the summer holidays, our citizens will be able to benefit from more favourable fares. parliament has been successful in its call for lower prices for consumer roaming, and in particular for data services. in addition, as from july 2014, consumers will be able to choose a provider other than their national provider for roaming services. the new rules will help to open up the market to new players, thus increasing competition.
in writing. - mobile phone roaming charges have long been much higher than domestic calls. the new eu regulation, for which we voted this morning, puts an end to these unfair tariff practices. this is a victory for this parliament, which has always fought for the citizens to have the system of spending on calls abroad reduced to avoid the abuses of the big telephone companies. many of the positive points of this text, first of all that from 1 july 2012, the regulation will also apply in the event that european consumers move abroad outside the territory of the eu. another big news is that from 1 july 2014, consumers will have the option to sign up for a cheaper mobile roaming contract, separate from their domestic mobile contract, while keeping the same number. in short, a very good agreement at first reading following three trilogues with the council, in which european citizens can appreciate the new weight of the european parliament after lisbon in decisions that positively affect their daily lives.
in writing. − the european union plays a crucial role in environmental policy at european level. by signing regulation (ec) no 689/2008, the eu set itself the objective of encouraging and increasing the exchange of information on chemicals placed on the market between the parties to the rotterdam convention and also of implementing the prior informed consent (pic) procedure. this ensures that countries exporting chemicals formally obtain the consent of importing countries before export can take place. the proposal by mr jørgensen seeks to limit the derogations which are usually adopted in opposition to the pic procedure, thus trying to defend the original meaning of the convention. joint action between the commission and the relevant national agencies will also be of great help. such synergy will certainly lead to more accurate and reliable documentation of the possible impacts on human health or the environment resulting from the use of hazardous chemicals in the importing country or another exporting country.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have supported mr jørgensen's report. transparency in the marketing and therefore export of chemicals between the parties to the rotterdam convention, implemented in the eu by regulation (ec) no 689/2008, is a political and common sense priority that must always be defended in the name of the safety of all european citizens.
in writing. − this regulation provides a clear legal basis for companies trading with foreign countries in the chemical sector, thus contributing to clarity on substances that can be traded within the union's borders, and on labelling conditions for their export. the proposal thus contributes to security within the eu's borders without adding burdens to exporting companies in the sector or making the task of the competent authorities more difficult. as regards substances which, although not banned, require authorisation by the country of destination, this regulation will now make it possible to export such substances to countries which have not responded within the prescribed time limits if there is evidence of use of the same substances in the country of destination for a period of at least five years. despite the commission's efforts, some 30% of previous requests have not been answered, effectively preventing trade in chemicals that are not prohibited. in my view, this regulation represents the right balance between the safety needs of citizens and the consolidation of the european single market, and i therefore considered that i should express my favourable opinion on the report on trade in dangerous chemicals.
in writing. - i think that the amendments are very important. i agree that it is appropriate to promote the exchange of information, the sharing of responsibilities and cooperation between the union and the member states and third countries in the proper management of chemicals. this is despite the fact that third countries are not party to the convention. in addition, technical assistance to developing countries and those with economies in transition must be provided directly by the commission and the member states or indirectly through support for projects carried out by non-governmental organisations. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 689/2008 implements in the european union the rotterdam convention which promotes the exchange of information on chemicals placed on the market between the parties and introduces the prior informed consent procedure. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the matter. the regulation also goes beyond the convention itself in that it covers a larger number of chemicals and applies the informed consent procedure to all countries importing from the eu, including third countries. the commission proposes to increase the possibilities for derogating from the prior informed consent procedure with regard to third countries, thus allowing, under certain conditions, the export of a substance even without having received consent. some of these substances, however, can be very harmful to health and the environment. i therefore consider it too dangerous to apply the commission's proposal in this case and i support the report by mr jørgensen, who has expressed his disagreement. the eu should continue to play a leading role in environmental legislation, ensuring the health of citizens and the environment.
in writing. − the european union is playing a leading role in environmental legislation and should continue to do so. it is the union's responsibility to ensure that the chemicals we export do not cause unnecessary damage to human health or the environment. the current prior informed consent procedure in the field of exports and imports of dangerous chemicals is a mechanism which ensures that countries exporting substances obtain the formal consent of importing countries before export can take place. this vote confirms and strengthens the previous provisions in this area without any distortion. one of the objectives is to make it difficult for producers of chemicals which are banned or subject to strict restrictions in the european union to sell them in europe.
in writing. - i think it is very important to stress the excellent work of clarification of the committees' powers in the casini report, which i shall vote in favour of. the adaptation of the regulation required by these amendments resulting from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has been carried out correctly and will certainly allow the request of the president of the european parliament to be met, which is to provide for a procedure clarifying the procedures for the rapid adoption of a delegated or implementing act.
in writing. - my vote on the wikstrom report is in favour. i agree in particular with the need, in order to promote the collective benefits of reducing the costs of litigation, facilitating access to justice, ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market and ensuring an appropriate balance between freedom of expression and the right to privacy, for the commission to conduct extensive consultations with interested parties, including journalists, the media and lawyers and specialist judges, with a view to proposing the establishment of a centre for the voluntary resolution of crossborder disputes arising from violations of privacy and personality rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i am in favour of the recommendations on the law applicable to non-contractual obligations, as provided for in the rome ii regulation. the basic principle will therefore be supplemented by a predictability clause. in a democratic society such as ours, the right to privacy is a fundamental and sacred right. when personal liberty is violated, there must be a right of appeal. the aim is to ensure both freedom of expression and the right to privacy, while ensuring a balance between the two priorities.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because it states that the arab spring has offered the eu the opportunity to match its commercial and foreign policy interests with its core value of human rights. the lisbon treaty defines international trade as one of the three arms of the eu’s external action and requires coherence between foreign affairs and international development policies. it is in the highest interests of the european union to adopt a strategy that is flexible, mutually beneficial, and based on support for democratic transition. in addition, i believe that the call for the reconsideration of the public external debt of the countries in north africa and the middle east to be of fundamental importance. that debt was built by the dictatorial regimes, mostly through the personal enrichment of the political elite and the purchasing of arms, which were often used to oppress their own populations.
in writing. - despite some positive steps, on the whole i do not share the rapporteur's approach and i voted against the report. in particular, i find some of the assessments of the arab spring too optimistic and i do not support the proposal to facilitate the issuing of visas under the pretext of facilitating the mobility of businessmen. in addition, two factors were decisive in my vote against the report: the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will be consulted on the matter.
in writing. - i express a favourable opinion on the report, emphasising its strategic and organic nature and the careful articulation of the lines of political action, in relation to the instruments currently available. moving from an honest analysis of the mistakes that have prevented decisive action in the past to stabilise the area, to the benefit of tactical visions that are relevant to bilateral and sphere policies, it recognises the need to relaunch the creation of the free trade area as an expression of the eu's external policy action, to involve the eib and the ebrd (with the extension of the mandate), to promote global ftas, to support the construction of legal, administrative, financial and civil frameworks and systems that are relevant to a business-friendly environment and to strengthen the middle class which is the indispensable factor in the difficult equation towards the development of models of complete and stable democracy. the delicate issue of the dubious automatic correlation between free economies and civil rights is also being tackled with courage through the doctrine of 'more for more', which will ensure a more targeted aid policy based on regular and careful verification of results.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it seeks to make a concrete contribution to relations between the eu and all the countries bordering the mare nostrum, in the light of the changed conditions resulting from the arab spring revolutions. on the one hand, the proposal calls for the eu to take increasingly stronger action to encourage international trade and with it all european businesses wishing to invest outside the community's borders, contributing to the establishment of a free and inclusive euro-mediterranean market. on the other hand, the text looks at those countries which after the arab spring started a path towards democracy to try to make these peoples understand that economic development is possible and is the first step towards a better life prospect. finally, i support this initiative because i believe that it is not just a commercial strategy that is an end in itself, but the beginning of a series of initiatives that the eu and the countries of the southern mediterranean will have to be able to pursue and coordinate with ever greater strength, capacity and impact in terms of democracy, development and the well-being of all the citizens involved.
in writing. the arab spring has raised enormous expectations of democratic and economic growth for the countries of the southern mediterranean. these two phenomena will only be able to reinforce each other, creating a virtuous circle from which europe will also benefit. the european union must therefore seize this opportunity to promote development in the countries concerned. economic and democratic growth in the countries bordering the union is beneficial not only to the countries themselves but also to all the member states. by establishing trade relations with these countries, european companies, especially italian ones for obvious geographical reasons, would have an opportunity to recover from the current economic contingency. migration problems would also be alleviated. the eib has a key role to play in this context, as it is responsible for promoting the development of smes in the area. the territorial integration of the area must also be promoted in order to develop the trade within the area, which is currently very limited. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the trade and investment strategy for the southern mediterranean.
in writing. - this report is a document with a strong political content. in my view, it is too premature and optimistic in its assessment of what has happened in some countries in the region, and it ignores the concerns about the escalation of violence and religious fundamentalism. it is also a report of the committee on international trade: the commission should therefore consider the legitimate interests of european companies in the first place, not assistance to third countries. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union, especially after the recent events of the so-called 'arab spring', should be able to play a much more ambitious role with the countries of the southern mediterranean, particularly in the economic, entrepreneurial and commercial fields, in order to offer opportunities for exchanges between the social and business communities, and finally to gain political leadership. we believe that european activities in the field of trade, investment and financial support in the region need to be fully coordinated in order to achieve the greatest possible positive impact. this strategy should be implemented in full cooperation with other policy areas in order to create training opportunities for entrepreneurs, promote participation in eu programmes and facilitate the visa procedure. we therefore welcome the commission's 'more for more' principle and believe that the achievements in the field of democratic reforms and individual freedoms must be followed by a process of liberalization in the economic and commercial spheres as well, with a view to dismantling the oligarchy which has traditionally held power.
in writing. - as in the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs of 17 february, i would like to stress the importance of tolerance and economic development, which are essential for long-term political and social stability and for an improvement in the standard of living in the countries concerned. i also believe it is important that countries in democratic transition ensure full respect for all fundamental rights, including freedom of expression, the right to peaceful assembly, freedom of association and freedom of religion, conscience and thought for all citizens, men and women, including members of the coptic christian communities.
in writing. - it is undeniable that the events of last spring have profoundly changed the face of all these countries bordering the southern shore of the mediterranean; it was about coming out of regimes that had been in place for several decades, and often dominated by the presence of a charismatic leader. so we must welcome a change that brings more democracy and participation, but with a careful eye to how different situations are handled. in all the countries where elections were held, which were more or less free, the parties of muslim religious fundamentalist inspiration were very successful, and thus influenced the political and social climate. i therefore think it is perhaps a little too risky to undertake such important initiatives with these countries today, which do not yet offer the necessary guarantees, especially in terms of socioeconomic stability. europe has made a mistake in behaving in a sometimes servile way towards its old leaders, but i would not want it to make a mistake again today by launching enthusiastically into openings, especially commercial ones, which i would not want us to regret any time soon. i therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. − the arab spring represents the greatest opportunity for the eu to expand its market and create development in the countries south of the mediterranean in an unprecedented civil atmosphere. but the eu needs an appropriate strategy for investment, for enlargement to trade, for market opening with the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area; it has been discussed for a long time but never put into practice. unfortunately, the eu's foreign policy is still very weak and unable to take strong and common decisions, but the future seems to be improving the room for manoeuvre towards a good integration and exchange policy with the arab spring countries, following the principle of more aid for more commitment, in which we are committed to a bilateral opening of markets for the benefit of the citizens and to the benefit of the economic and social reforms of these countries.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr rinaldi's report is a very ambitious document, which allows us to reflect on the effects, but also on the causes, of the so-called 'arab spring'. unlike the rapporteur, however, i think that the view advocated is too optimistic and that many of the measures proposed are more related to the field of development cooperation than to that of international trade. the growing instability and the more extreme political tendencies that are increasingly expressed in countries such as egypt and libya prevent me from sharing the general feeling of confidence in the so-called "arab spring" and the parallelism - in my opinion premature - with the fall of the berlin wall. the principle of 'more for more' should be the cornerstone of european policy towards the mediterranean countries and any increase in european contributions should be conditional on genuine reforms to achieve a deep democracy in these countries. only then will it be possible to discuss any revision of the tariff barriers.
in writing. the text of the report is a highly political document, containing a number of very unrealistic and overly optimistic views on the arab spring, the greatest political transformation since the fall of the berlin wall. the rapporteur strongly criticises the union's weakness on the north african chessboard but fails to mention that the absence and the strong limits of the high representative do not apply only to that area but are prerogatives that highlight the lack of a european foreign policy. i am opposed to the text of the report because it contains some criticisms such as the call for increased european investment bank financing and aid, especially for smes in the southern mediterranean; the commission has also proposed that the visa system be simplified to the benefit of businessmen, as it is for turkey. in view of the fact that the report does not deal with the common commercial policy in the interests of our undertakings, i am voting against.
in writing. - i am firmly opposed to voting for this report. i understand the rapporteur's position, but i do not share his enthusiastically positive view of the outcome of the so-called arab spring. i do not agree with the call for the creation of a free trade area with the countries of north africa, which would seriously damage our textile and agricultural production sector, which is already suffering from an unprecedented crisis. finally, i do not agree with the general tone of the report which focuses exclusively on protecting and promoting the interests of the other party and completely avoids citing and defending legitimate european commercial interests. it sounds like a report from the development committee and not from the international trade committee!
in writing. - while i am in favour of the report we voted on overall, in the sense that the eu and the member states should make greater efforts to support the transition to democracy in the arab spring countries, i voted against two paragraphs which refer to the promotion of trade relations which could harm the european agricultural sector. the case that has caused controversy over the eu-morocco partnership agreement on certain agricultural products is still a recent one. this agreement provides for an increase in goods traded at low customs rates. the risk of a further positive vote on the text in question could in fact form the basis for new agreements which would in the long term prove harmful to our farmers or to other sectors.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the joint resolution. i particularly agree with the call to the epo to exclude from patentability products derived from conventional breeding and all conventional breeding methods, including breeding using advanced breeding technology and markers (smart or precision breeding) and breeding material used in conventional breeding methods.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which reaffirms the principle of non-patentability of essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals and of all products derived from conventional breeding. the commission had brought an action against the grant of patents by the european patent office for tomatoes and broccoli. i believe that intellectual property rights are fundamental and, in this case, vital in order to stimulate the development of new plant varieties and plant-related innovation. the patent allows small and medium-sized enterprises in particular to boost growth and innovation and to help european companies cope with the economic crisis and global competition.
in writing. − maritime transport is one of the cornerstones of economic growth and prosperity on our continent. moreover, over 80% of world trade is carried by sea. today, piracy is a threat to international security and regional stability. tackling the root causes of this phenomenon is a priority for the union. in today's vote the european parliament has reaffirmed the commitment of our institution to combating this phenomenon and has emphasized that under international law, on the high seas, the national jurisdiction of the flag state always applies to ships and the military personnel on board - and therefore also in the case of anti-piracy operations - and no authority other than that of the flag state can order the arrest or detention of a ship, even if it is an investigative measure. it is a fundamental principle of international maritime law, but one that is too often ignored. this is the case of the two italian seamen who are still unjustly detained in indian jails today despite serving on an italian-flagged ship in international waters. we call on india once again to respect these standards.
in writing. − i support this resolution because piracy continues to spread in the indian ocean, particularly off the coasts of somalia. in that country, one of the causes of piracy is political instability. indeed, i believe that an effective approach to countering maritime piracy must include a broader strategy to lift somalia and the whole region of the horn of africa out of poverty and state failure. for this reason, i am particularly concerned about the deteriorating humanitarian situation in the region. the international community should increase its provision of aid assistance and prevent any further worsening of the situation. in addition, third counties and those eu member states that have not yet done so must transpose into their national law all the provisions laid down by the un convention on the law of the sea and the un convention for the suppression of unlawful acts against the safety of maritime navigation.
in writing. - authors such as w. bernstein and niall ferguson explain how large international trade has reorganized itself along sea routes: the european union has a duty to protect its citizens and to protect the environment. according to the csis think-tank, piracy costs the global economy between usd 7 and 12 billion each year, with estimated profits of around usd 250 million from hostage trafficking alone. a threat of this nature, which challenges international law and global stability, by parasitically growing and parasitically flourishing in regions affected by government failure and the penetration of terrorist or criminal organizations, requires a firm and measured response, such as that called for in the joint resolution, which i wholeheartedly support. the framework for international cooperation must be strengthened as a matter of urgency, as the violence of these criminal gangs is triggering individual responses by sovereign states and private operators, in a context of legal and organisational coordination which risks undermining efforts and investments in the fight against piracy and multiplying crises resulting from divergent interpretations of operational protocols and the institutions of international law, such as the one affecting the two italian marines still detained in india.
in writing. - the persistence of impunity for piracy is at odds with the need for a deterrent. despite the european union's transfer agreements with third countries (kenya, seychelles, mauritius) and the bilateral agreements on the return of convicted pirates between seychelles, puntland and somaliland, many pirates and other criminals have not yet been arrested or, after arrest, have often been released for lack of solid legal evidence or the absence of political will to prosecute them. we therefore call for immediate and effective measures to prosecute and punish those suspected of committing acts of piracy .
in writing. - the resolution we discussed this morning was signed by almost all the political groups, which shows that the problem has been tackled in a transversal way. the text reminds us that some 200 seafarers are currently being held hostage by pirates who continue to hijack boats carrying humanitarian aid, merchant ships and fishing vessels for ransom. the attacks are taking place mainly off the coast of somalia and in the western indian ocean, as we are reminded by the un forces currently deployed there. with this resolution we call loudly on the eu high representative to secure the release of the hostages and the ships and to support the establishment of an international tribunal against piracy. the fight against piracy can only be won if the union tackles the root causes of piracy, namely extreme poverty and state failure in the region.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i fully share the priority and the emphasis given by mr busuttil in his report, which i hope this house will adopt by a full majority, in order to strengthen ever more the functioning of the single market, which is absolutely strategic in the development policies of the european union. this would send a strong signal to the individual member states. the latest results of the evaluation framework have shown that member states are increasingly failing to meet their obligations in relation to the transposition of european legislation. for this reason, i agree with my colleague that we need to give greater strength and flexibility to infringement procedures, while at the same time rethinking the role of solvit as an alternative to judicial review. in this respect, i too have reservations about the risk of encountering problems with respect for the principle of subsidiarity if the legal basis of solvit is over-formalised. i therefore believe that the commission should carefully explore all possible solutions with a view to making the portal more operational without running the risk of getting bogged down in legal tricks. finally, i would like to recall that the treaty of lisbon has greatly redefined the role of the european parliament, giving it substantial powers to structure and review european union legislation. in this regard, it is essential, in order to enhance cooperation with national authorities, that the conclusions of the evaluation framework are properly analysed in the structured dialogue between the european parliament and national parliaments.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, we are all convinced of the importance of the internal market, which has even become one of the defining features of the union in the course of the last 20 years. we also believe that the internal market has the potential to make a strong contribution to the growth of individual countries and the union as a whole. for these reasons, and precisely because we share this view, we must pay close attention to certain aspects which have been summarized in today's debate. the first of these aspects is that the real enemy of the internal market today is the crisis. it is the crisis that is calling into question the value of the internal market in the eyes of many citizens and it is the crisis that is taking away the potential of the added value that the internal market represents. therefore, as has been said by many, even in this house, we must focus on the priority of growth, because without growth our work - the work on the internal market - becomes objectively more difficult. the crisis process which is affecting our countries is actually having another negative effect: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as has already been said, we are faced with two problems. the first concerns the delays in transposition by the member states, delays which are not due to the complexity of the measures but are often the result of a wrong policy choice. the other concerns alterations, defects, in the transposition. too often we deviate from the text and the intentions themselves. the differences are very significant in some areas: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used in a way that is compatible with the common market. the instruments needed to give substance to the internal market must therefore be revised and strengthened. the penalties for incorrect or late implementation of decisions were discussed: but i would also like to emphasize the importance of solvit. i am aware of the delicate nature of the legal basis: but an instrument which has proved its worth cannot be left in its present condition. i would now like to make one final point to the rapporteur: i do not understand why, at this necessary stage of difficulties caused by the crisis and external circumstances, the hypothesis of the internal market ombudsman, that is to say, a third party, has been put forward, which would lead to a lengthy discussion, when we need to decide quickly with as much unity as possible, that unity which has been highlighted and which this proposal is likely to call into question.
the rapporteur. - madam commissioner, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am very excited to present my own-initiative report on internal security in the european union. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject. i would like to dedicate the approval of this report to all the victims of the mafia, organised crime and terrorism, and in particular to melissa bassi, the young victim of the bombing of a school in brindisi last saturday, in which six other girls were also injured. the motive for the act is still unknown but it is clear that it is part of a growing climate of tension and insecurity caused by the crisis, which organizations or individuals may be tempted to exploit for violent subversion. i also think of the victims of the earthquake in emilia romagna, because natural disasters are also an issue of internal security for the union. the text we are voting on tomorrow underlines the importance of a coherent union strategy on security, and i would therefore like to thank the european commission for the considerable effort it has put into its preparation. as we have repeatedly stressed in the report, security must always be guaranteed in full respect for the rule of law and fundamental rights, which are an integral and inseparable part of this strategy. this is another reason why the role of the eu institutions in defining and implementing the strategy, particularly in the post-lisbon framework, is of particular importance. in this context, an appropriate role for the european parliament is needed, both in the development of the strategy's priorities and in the evaluation phase. this is a role which derives from the full legislative power which parliament has assumed in the field of security. but it is also an essential element in ensuring adequate democratic control which the european parliament must have together with the national parliaments. that is why we will work to establish a regular relationship between the european parliament and the national parliaments - a parliamentary policy cycle linked to the commission's annual report on this matter and ending with an annual parliamentary report on the state of implementation of the internal security strategy. we think that the union must be clear about the extent of the threats to internal security, which it is not today. we therefore ask that europol, with the support of the institutions and other agencies, be able to carry out a comprehensive analysis of the threats to be addressed at union level, based on a more robust and transparent methodology and on the information contribution of the member states. with reference to the five priority objectives identified by the european commission, we argue that this should not be an exhaustive list and that the order of priorities could probably have been better structured. the fight against terrorism, organised crime and the mafia is and must remain for us a key priority of an internal security strategy. the union must not only react, but also anticipate and interpret what is happening in europe: the events in utøya and brindisi have shown us that. we must be able to detect early signs of violent radicalisation, of the disruption of the social climate and of violent extremism. judicial cooperation is the major missing element in the commission's security strategy and this gap must be filled. joint action by the judiciary is vital in europe to combat and strengthen crime and terrorism, as is the fight against corruption and environmental, member of the commission. − madam president, i am very pleased to note the considerable interest that parliament clearly attaches to consumer issues. this is evidenced in several own-initiative reports that have been very helpful to the commission in the preparation of the consumer agenda – our new consumer strategy – which we are presenting tomorrow. i would like to thank, in particular, the rapporteur, mrs irigoyen pérez, and the shadow rapporteurs for their valuable work on this latest own-initiative report. your input will contribute towards developing further actions for protecting and strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers. the commission wholeheartedly agrees that it is important to address the vulnerability of consumers, and this will be reflected in the consumer agenda. this initiative will present a coherent, strategic vision for consumer policy for the years to come, focusing on concrete measures that put consumers at the centre of the single market. special attention will be paid to those markets also identified by the parliament report as being particularly problematic for consumers. this includes financial services, energy, transport, telecommunications and the digital market. i would agree with parliament’s view that it is not possible to encapsulate vulnerability in a single definition. instead, we need to identify the various factors that can contribute to consumer vulnerability in specific markets or in particular circumstances. to this end, research and innovation have an important role to play. we are fully committed to mainstreaming the issue of vulnerability into market surveys and consumer studies, including consumer behaviour studies. as also pointed out by parliament’s report, the concept of ‘vulnerable consumer’ has only been introduced relatively recently in european legislation. however, we already have in place provisions that safeguard the interests and rights of groups of consumers that can be considered more vulnerable in a structural sense – children, elderly people and people with disabilities. i can assure you that the commission is constantly looking to improve these measures. i fully acknowledge that we also need to anticipate market developments and innovation to make sure that these also deliver benefits for vulnerable consumers. let me briefly outline just some of the initiatives that the commission has already brought forward and which focus on the specific areas highlighted by the report. these initiatives include: revising the general product safety directive; evaluating the implementation of the consumer credit directive; looking into ways of tackling the problem of over-indebtedness; and assessing the functioning of the unfair commercial practices directive, especially in the digital and financial markets. we will also further monitor and assess the application of the rules of the audiovisual media services directive in order to strengthen their effectiveness, in particular with regard to the protection of minors, across different audiovisual media environments. we are bringing forward a proposal on web accessibility. we have set up a working group across the commission services on the exchange of best practices across member states and long-term solutions and appropriate non-policy solutions that better target vulnerability in the area of energy. finally, the commission is launching guidelines on the application of the regulation on the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility when travelling by air. if vulnerable consumers are to be properly protected, member states, businesses and intermediaries, such as consumer ngos, also have an important role to play. there is a need for close cooperation and the active involvement of all the main stakeholders. we must collectively remain constantly vigilant to market and societal changes that increase the risk of exclusion for certain groups or individuals. to conclude, may i say once again that i very much appreciate the valuable report that parliament has produced, and which i know will make an important contribution to the commission’s work.
in writing. membership of the european union provides an element of protection for citizens by establishing an equivalent level of safety for different consumer goods and by introducing measures to protect the general interests of the consumer against unfair business practices, misleading advertising and abusive contractual clauses. however, vulnerable or vulnerable consumers represent a subset of the general category of consumers who require special protection and a specific strategy from the authorities. i believe that the creation of a strategy to strengthen the rights of the most vulnerable consumers can contribute not only to their social inclusion but also to ensuring a more dynamic and competitive internal market. i agree with the rapporteur that it is important to improve consumer information so that they are more aware of their rights, but i also stress that practice has shown that the vulnerability of many consumers is in fact due to a lack of understanding of the information they receive or their ignorance of existing complaint and refund practices. i would urge the commission to consider specific legislative measures to ensure adequate protection of vulnerable consumers, which go beyond mere information and are in line with the consumer programme 2014-2020.
