in writing. the initiative report welcomes the work being done to establish an internal security strategy for the european union. in this context, parliament, under the terms of the lisbon treaty, has the right to participate as the main actor in defining the priorities and the future model of internal security. i think the work done by the libe committee and by mrs borsellino is significant. the key areas of european intervention are highlighted here, with the primary objective of achieving greater cooperation at the level of judicial and police bodies between member states to deal with threats from organised crime, terrorism, corruption, cybercrime and natural disasters. i fully agree with the intention to build a common european area of freedom, security and justice and to adopt a unified strategy for all member states. i believe that there is a great need to increase efforts to improve the consistency of information and data on which risk assessments by union bodies are based and to ensure transparency in the methods used and thus achieve the fundamental objective of ensuring the full protection of citizens.
in writing. − the main common threats identified by the internal security strategy of the member states are many: from organised crime to terrorism, from cybercrime to corruption and border management. all these phenomena are interconnected and therefore coordinated and coherent action in both areas is needed for the response to be effective. the vote underlines the importance of a comprehensive approach to a european union security strategy based on a concept of human security anchored in human rights, freedom, democracy, the rule of law, good governance and peace. finally, there is a need for closer cooperation with other international institutions responsible for security strategy, such as nato and the osce.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it clearly defines the principles that should be taken into account when developing an eu approach on criminal law. so far the european union has often developed criminal law provisions on an ad hoc basis, thus creating the need for increased coherence. it is fundamental to acknowledge that an eu criminal law should constitute a coherent legislative system governed by a set of fundamental values in full respect of the eu charter of fundamental rights and of the european convention on human rights. i also believe that the harmonisation of criminal law in the eu will contribute to the development of a common eu legal culture in relation to fighting crime and to a more coordinated action against the most serious crimes. in addition i would like to stress the importance of the establishment of uniform minimum standards of protection at the highest possible level for suspects and defendants in criminal proceedings in order to strengthen mutual trust amongst the legal systems of the member states.
in writing. − the entry into force of the lisbon treaty laid the foundations for the development of criminal law integrated into the community law of the union, which was previously the exclusive competence of the member states. despite the importance of this new provision, i am concerned that a number of new union initiatives in the field of substantive criminal law may represent an excessive burden for national administrations. the competent national authorities have, in fact, also as a result of the recent economic crisis, reduced financial resources and, in this context, there is a well-founded risk that the adoption of new legislation will not only not result in better application of criminal law, but also undermine the credibility and effectiveness of the union's criminal law to the clear detriment of citizens. in my view, the european union should take a very cautious approach in drawing up or revising additional criminal law provisions. the european institutions must also agree on the principles and working methods to be applied. in order to facilitate cooperation in the future, i believe it is essential that the european institutions agree on a common framework, which includes a set of principles governing each criminal legal instrument.
in writing. − the adoption of the treaty of lisbon has laid the foundations for greater european integration in the field of criminal law. without prejudice to the prerogatives of the member states, which are not affected by this report, which in fact reaffirms the competence of the states in the main areas of criminal law, a strengthening of the european criminal justice system would help to increase its coherence and, consequently, its certainty. measures such as the strengthening of the legal advice service at the european parliament and the promotion of greater interinstitutional coordination represent a step forward in the process of defining guidelines and core principles at european level, which is essential for the effective adoption of new european criminal law.
in writing. − the harmonisation of criminal law in the european union must help to create a common eu legal culture in the fight against crime. i therefore agree that the harmonization measures should be proposed primarily with a view to promoting the practical application of the principle of mutual recognition. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - if a judicial area, however partial it may be, exists in the union, it is normal, lawful and desirable that it should develop in particular in the area of criminal law, in order to avoid the incongruities we are witnessing and to provide both the states and the union with guidelines aimed at its harmonization. the commission's november 2011 document on criminal policy is valuable to me, as is the study by parliament's services on harmonisation. the matter is delicate and directly affects the sovereignty of states. but there is no doubt that, with great care and foresight, it is necessary to manage this sovereignty in certain areas in common. in the customs sector, for example, it is useful for the functioning of the internal market and for the users themselves. in the case of criminal law, certain anomalies would probably be avoided, which affect hundreds of citizens who have a nationality different from that of the state in which it is practised in a more than singular way: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european arrest warrants issued for citizens who leave germany with their children are not used to further the aims of the treaty. if the european approach to criminal law will help to eliminate these aberrations, it will be a triumph of legal civilization to be hailed with satisfaction.
in writing. the legal system of the european union often and willingly lacks coherence and certainty, especially as regards criminal law. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has seen a major acceleration of european legislation in criminal matters, to the extent that the european commission has already presented a communication in favour of a single european criminal law. the road is still long, of course, but despite the resistance of some member states and procedural difficulties, the process has begun. the european parliament, thanks also to my vote, has given a positive assessment of these first steps and has pointed out the need for an internal legal advisory service to assess and weigh the proposals in balance with the law of the member states.
in writing. mr president, we voted today in strasbourg on the report by mr de jong. the own-initiative report states that in order to ensure a coherent and high-quality european strategy in the field of criminal law, there should be agreement between the three institutions on working principles and methods. the emphasis is on the importance of mutual recognition, the harmonisation of protection rules and the principle of the presumption of innocence. the main areas of criminal law will be the responsibility of the member states, while a 'coordinating authority' should be appointed within the european commission.
in writing. - the report by mr de jong stresses that to ensure consistent and high-quality european legislation in the field of criminal law, it is necessary to reach agreement between the european institutions on working principles and methods. i agree with this own-initiative report because of the serious approach which has been taken in regulating such a delicate policy area. in particular, i agree with the importance attached to mutual recognition, the harmonization of protection rules and the principle of the presumption of innocence. i support the creation of a common european legal culture and a coherent and uniform strategy and the promotion of greater institutional coordination, while leaving the main areas of criminal law to the member states. the law must be extremely clear and easily understandable, which is why i agree that the european commission should appoint a specific coordinating authority.
in writing. the new treaty allows us greater flexibility in adopting criminal law, in all areas of the union, but at the same time obliges us to exercise greater caution both in adopting new rules and in introducing them in such a way as to ensure respect for fundamental rights and the most classical principles of criminal law. i believe that we must avoid the use of the criminal instrument being motivated by purely symbolic reasons and that the reference to the charter of fundamental rights or other international instruments designed to protect them is merely rhetorical. among the operational proposals in the document we voted on this morning, i find particularly interesting the call for the strengthening, through the allocation of additional resources, of the legal advice service at the european parliament, which allows for a systematic study and evaluation of proposals relating to criminal matters and the promotion of interinstitutional coordination for a serious study of the problems on which action is proposed, as well as the evaluation of the effectiveness of the legislation in force and the possible impact of the legislation to be adopted.
in writing. - the protection of the consumer, and even more so of vulnerable categories of consumers, must be considered as the basis of the project for the development of the european project. the text of this own-initiative report proposes practical solutions to safeguard this principle, which is why i have decided to vote in favour of its adoption.
in writing. - i appreciate and approve the report, emphasising its balanced realism. in areas such as this, there is a high risk of a heterogeneity of aims, for which legislation is enacted in defence of certain categories which end up being even harmed by unexpected effects of the legislation. another risk, which the report has been careful not to take, is that it will end up serving an abstract model of the nanny state in the laudable but illusory prospect of eliminating the risks associated with the exercise of citizenship from our lives. i would stress, among the laudable recommendations, that of consumer protection against bad practices, which unfortunately are widespread in the consumer credit industry, which exploded with the crisis. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full, and i am pleased to say that the commission has taken the necessary steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the defence of vulnerable consumers is morally justified but also in the interest of the maintenance of welfare networks in our countries, which are often called upon to deal with the effects of bad practices to the detriment of the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. − while providing adequate information to consumers is a necessary condition for ensuring their protection, it is not sufficient in itself in some cases, especially for vulnerable consumers. the report therefore urges the commission to take this into account by developing protection instruments for the most vulnerable groups which go beyond mere information. the proposal, adopting the principle that every consumer can, in the course of his or her life, become a vulnerable consumer, avoids giving too rigid a definition of vulnerability. the need also emerges for action in the online sector, identified in the proposal as one of the sectors at risk, where inefficiency in age verification systems exposes underage consumers to misleading advertising, and where social networks allow sellers to promote their products through ad hoc advertising, by offering preferred brands within the social network, leveraging social pressure. i am convinced that the guidelines set out in the proposal will help to identify an effective strategy for protecting consumers, particularly the vulnerable, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i think that this text is entirely acceptable for three reasons. first, it proposes strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers through a horizontal approach, i.e. taking into account the different needs and capacities of consumers, as well as the various circumstances in which they may find themselves acting. secondly, i welcome the principle on which the report is based, namely that all consumers could become vulnerable in their lifetime, for exogenous or endogenous reasons. finally, the concrete measures proposed in the report are aimed at improving the existing tools and their effectiveness, and at providing easily accessible and understandable information to consumers themselves. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - one of the most frequent criticisms of the european union is its democratic deficit, i.e. the lack of opportunity for citizens to influence european decision-making processes. the european parliament, as the only institution whose members are directly elected by citizens, is particularly attentive to these issues and already in 2010 had approved the report on the proposal for a regulation on the citizens' initiative: it is an opportunity for citizens to make their voices heard and to bring issues of interest to the attention of the european institutions. a first example was a few weeks ago, when a committee of citizens from austria, belgium, italy, luxembourg, romania and spain presented an initiative to improve eu exchange programmes.
in writing. − new forms of trade and new ways of accessing products inevitably require a strengthening of consumer rights, particularly for the most vulnerable. as proposed in the report by mr irigoyen pérez, for which i voted in favour, we must take action in this direction, following a broad approach. the strengthening of consumer rights is achieved through improved legislation, more extensive and easily perceivable information campaigns and, finally, through the empowerment of the consumer himself. in this sense, taking into account the results of recent research available to us, particular attention should be paid to the purchasing behaviour of financial products. this is the sector where consumers are most exposed to illegal practices, which must be vigorously combated with a view to greater information protection.
in writing. − i fully agree that the strategy for the rights of vulnerable consumers must focus on strengthening their rights, ensuring that they are effectively safeguarded and enforced, and providing the consumer with all the means necessary to ensure that he can make the right decisions and assert himself, regardless of the instrument used. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - mr president, i support this initiative by mr irigoyen pérez which tackles a key issue for the fair functioning of the market: the protection of the rights of consumers, and in particular of the most vulnerable consumers, against unfair practices. the consumer must be made more aware of his responsibilities by providing accessible and comprehensible information. this is particularly true in sensitive areas such as financial products, and in the field of new technologies and social media, which require a reflection on how to protect the consumer.
in writing. - i congratulate mr pérez on his work. in adopting this report, in the light of directive 2005/29/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 11 may 2005 concerning unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices in the internal market and article 9 tfeu, it is reiterated that membership of the european union provides consumers with an additional element of protection. the report is based on the principle that all consumers can be considered vulnerable and in particular stresses how the creation of a strategy for strengthening the rights of the most vulnerable consumers, aimed at enabling them to participate in the single market, can contribute not only to their social inclusion but also to the creation of a more equitable and tolerant society, with a dynamic, secure and competitive internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because it is necessary to guarantee greater protection for european consumers, especially the most vulnerable and those at risk of unemployment. this requires rapid action, through a specific and far-reaching strategy that takes account of social habits and changes in consumer behaviour that are most at risk.
in writing. - mr president, i am in favour of the text of the report on the strategy for strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers, as they represent a special category of consumers who require special protection and a specific strategy. such vulnerability may arise either from endogenous causes, i.e. whether the consumer's vulnerability is due to temporary or permanent causes related to their nature or physical or mental condition, or from exogenous causes, i.e. caused by external agents such as lack of information. i share the view that strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers implies not only regulatory development but above all efforts to promote the strengthening of their responsibilities by providing accessible and understandable information. i believe that strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers, with particular attention to those with disabilities, such as accessibility in reading for the visually impaired and the use of universally recognised symbols, should be included among the priorities of the new consumer protection programme 2014-2020.
in writing. - i welcome the report by mr irigoyen pérez, which seeks to ensure equal treatment and the elimination of discrimination in the internal market and in particular the protection of the most vulnerable consumers, through a targeted strategy consisting of the promotion of programmes to support consumer information and education, the uniform application of standards in all member states, price transparency, particularly in relation to online trade. more stringent rules on advertising, which can be misleading, and greater control over the information provided to the public are also needed to avoid uninformed choices by shoppers. consumers need to be better protected when they make purchases. they need to be given careful protection, guaranteed by the creation of fair, clear and precise information legislation, which also contributes to the creation of a more transparent and competitive single market.
in writing. − one of the objectives of the european union is to protect the general interests of consumers against unfair business practices, misleading advertising and abusive contractual clauses. in a complex social and economic context, there are some consumers who for various reasons prove to be weaker and more vulnerable than others. the areas of high concern for consumers include the financial sector, the food sector, transport, the internet, liberalised markets and access to justice. one of the aims of this vote is to clarify the term 'vulnerable' so that the subject and the regulations relating to it can be harmonised. the creation of a strategy for strengthening the rights of the most vulnerable consumers will contribute not only to their social inclusion and progress towards a fairer and more tolerant society, but also to ensuring a more dynamic, secure and competitive internal market.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report, particularly in its commitment to examine the implications of the circulating one and two cent coin and the planned introduction of the one and two euro banknotes. as part of the spontaneous adjustments that internal markets trigger in response to the crisis, the introduction of one and two euro banknote values could have positive effects for consumers, particularly in countries most affected by the fall in demand and especially in certain sectors, such as food and public services on individual demand. it is now clear that the introduction of the one and two euro coins in some countries has contributed to higher consumer prices and an overvaluation, implicit but no less real in relation to purchasing power, beyond the value fixed in national currency. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is based on the principle of the protection of the euro against counterfeiting.
in writing. - i am in favour of the proposal to issue one and two euro banknotes. the issuance of small denomination banknotes, replacing those currently in circulation, would create a better perception of the value of money and would probably improve its use. we must not forget that in a crisis such as the one we are experiencing, the recession in many member states is also marked by a lack of confidence in our european currency and by rising consumer prices. the introduction of the one and two euro banknotes is therefore an important step towards the development of a new monetary policy which also involves these small but significant measures.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report. i particularly agree with the amendment calling on the commission to assess the effects of continuing to issue 1 and 2 cent coins and to assess the effects of the possible issue of 1 and 2 euro banknotes.
in writing. - the issue of euro coins has been a topic of discussion since the introduction of the single currency. at the beginning there was talk of withdrawing the one-cent euro coins, but now the debate is on the conversion of the one- and two-euro coins into banknotes. the european parliament's proposal for a regulation is aimed at demonstrating how the changeover from the euro coin to the euro 1 and 2 notes can have a positive effect on the real economy. in addition to the improved handling of the banknote, there would be positive effects on tourism as it would be much easier to get the european union to accept the one and two euro banknote. moreover, this would bring benefits to the member states.
in writing. − the issue of one and two euro banknotes would lead to a reduction in the number of one and two euro coins in circulation but the use of such banknotes would at the same time bring benefits to the member states. firstly, the issuance of small denomination banknotes would increase the handling and acceptance of the euro and would have a positive effect on european tourism, without diminishing the value of the other euro coins in circulation. it would also increase the value of euro collector coins. that is why i am in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 'internal market scoreboard' because i share the need to promote a coordinated and cooperative approach in order to make the internal market work better through the timely and full transposition of community legislation. full transposition would allow the single market to be strengthened and its functioning to be made more efficient. given that the definition of the category of smes (micro, small and medium-sized enterprises) must be economically objective, certain and easy for the administrations of the member states to apply, i welcome the creation, as suggested by mr busuttil, of a body headed by an internal market ombudsman who can operate without political pressure, addressing and resolving possible infringements. i also agree with the reference to solvit, a very useful tool as it allows member states to work together in resolving issues concerning the misuse of internal market rules: i therefore believe that it is necessary to ensure a good level of funding by the member states to ensure that it functions properly. finally, i hope that the new instruments will increase transparency and make it possible to understand the reasons for the failure or partial transposition by those member states which do not adopt community legislation in this field in a timely manner.
in writing. - i have often voted in favour of the annual report of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. this year, however, i think that the report contains excessive criticism of the member states, which are too often guilty, in the rapporteur's view, of misapplying the directives. if this is sometimes true, i think it is necessary to point out that this often happens because of complex texts, which are not explicit, which are difficult to apply in the territory or which are strongly opposed by citizens, by categories of workers or by companies. in my view, the present report lacks almost entirely an examination of the social, political and economic reasons for some of the failures to transpose the treaty, and it seems to be irrelevant that the union is made up of countries with completely different constitutional structures and dimensions, some of which see in them a division of legislative competence between the state and the regions. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. − the internal market scoreboard is a useful tool for constant and timely monitoring of the european economic and trade situation. in particular, there is a sense of urgency in having a precise picture of how individual member states transpose european directives. a constant monitoring, annually or biennially, would give us a precise picture of the application of the directives, which would enable the european union to act in the right direction, calling on the member states to fulfil their obligations in a short time. finally, i would like to stress the importance of the internal market at a time of crisis, which some member states are experiencing more acutely than others. i believe that finding and strengthening instruments of cohesion and cooperation such as this is a good way out of the crisis.
in writing. − it is right that the commission should work towards offering citizens and businesses an integrated virtual package of information and support services. i also agree with the importance of direct human contact and the proposal to complement these efforts with a single point of direct contact for citizens and consumers, through the commission's representative offices in each member state. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - this year marks the 20th anniversary of the european single market but unfortunately, despite the adoption of the single market act last year, the report assessing the european single market is not positive. never before have the member states been so far from implementing what the european commission has asked for. the crisis period certainly does not help, but the single market is the real field in which the crisis must be fought. the european parliament therefore hopes that the member states will change their priorities and implement the measures needed to achieve the objectives of the single market as soon as possible, as the european commission cannot be satisfied with its information portals for citizens and businesses.
in writing. - mr president, today in the chamber parliament voted in favour of the report by mr simon busuttil on the evaluation framework for the internal market. the rapporteur states that the internal market is the best instrument the european union has to boost the growth of the member states' economies and that it must be used to the full. in the past, there have been positive trends which unfortunately are not reflected in the latest internal market scoreboard; it is therefore necessary to continue efforts to achieve and exceed ambitious targets: the lowest possible transposition deficit, the shortest possible transposition delays and the highest possible quality of transposition. the commission has also made considerable efforts to set up fast and efficient information portals to ensure that citizens and businesses are in the best position to benefit from the single market, but these mechanisms are often coupled with many others, resulting in duplication of effort and insufficient coordination. the rapporteur therefore believes that the european commission's efforts in this area require greater clarity. a stronger commitment is also required from national institutions and administrations to ensure the correct and timely transposition and application of internal market directives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because the creation of a single market for citizens and businesses requires not only coherent legislation but also strong synergies between different national administrations. this internal market assessment framework is a key instrument for the completion of the single market, as it provides an incentive for european states to transpose directives on the internal market quickly.
in writing. − in an international context of economic crisis, the internal market is the best tool we have to boost the growth of the member states' economies. to date, several instruments have been developed to further encourage the completion of the single market and to assess the contributions of individual member states to achieving this objective. the internal market scoreboard is one such tool and encourages member states to improve the quality and timeliness of their transposition of directives into the internal market. the vote underlines the need to achieve the more stringent transposition and implementation targets. the latest results of the internal market scoreboard have shown that member states are falling further behind in their obligations.
in writing. − the european union is experiencing the worst economic crisis since its inception, a crisis that threatens the very foundations of the european economy. i am convinced that the internal market is a valuable instrument we have at our disposal to boost the growth of the economies of the member states, and i have therefore expressed my support for the text presented by mr busuttil, who supports stricter transposition and implementation targets because the member states are increasingly failing to meet their obligations. in order to achieve the objectives set and to get out of the crisis as quickly as possible, member states cannot put the internal market at the bottom of their priority list. the present difficulties should be a signal that the internal market is being given due consideration and should not be used as an excuse to evade one's commitments to a fully functioning internal market.
in writing. − i support this report because fighting violence against women, including honour killings and forced marriages, remains a major challenge for turkey. i am particularly concerned by the ineffectiveness of the existing remedies and by the lenience of the turkish authorities as regards punishing the perpetrators of gender-based crimes. for this reason it is fundamental that women’s rights and gender mainstreaming are upheld in the new turkish constitution. coordinated action is also needed in the areas of education, work, and representation at national and local level. it is important to stress that economic and social underdevelopment in disadvantaged areas of turkey, as well as problems stemming from immigration, poverty and prevailing patriarchal social structures, aggravate women’s problems and undermine their position.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on a 2020 perspective for women in turkey, as turkey as an eu candidate country must continue its path towards greater participation of women in all spheres of society. there is still worrying discrimination against women in turkey which must be eliminated urgently. i am referring in particular to violence against women, since two or three women are killed every day by their husbands, boyfriends, families or ex-husbands. the turkish statistical institute even claims that 39% of women have been victims of physical violence at some point in their lives! the turkish government must increase the penalties and adopt a zero-tolerance policy towards those responsible for such acts. a further major source of social marginalisation of women in turkey is the high female illiteracy rate, which particularly affects rural areas. it is essential that the turkish government persevere in its campaigns to increase women's participation in primary and secondary education. only in this way will it be possible to facilitate women's participation in the labour market and to increase the female employment rate, which currently stands at 30%.
in writing. - there is an urgent need for a change of mindset in turkey that can transform the patriarchal structure of society into one based on gender equality. the figures on violence against women in turkey and on women in employment are still alarming, to say the least, especially as we are talking about a country that is a candidate for accession to the european union. my vote is in favour of the report.
in writing. - mr president, the situation of women in turkey is still far from being acceptable. beyond some stark disparities in education and employment, the 'moral issue' is still more worrying, namely the consideration of women as such in turkish society. in the countryside in particular, there are still many cases of "honor killings", with the perhaps even more tragic variant of so-called "honor suicides". these impositions, often dictated by religious issues, have nothing to do with reality and the european dimension. the women's issue is just one of the many problematic aspects of turkey, and we cannot understand how anyone can still talk about possible accession to the european union. i hope that the turkish government will work to ensure that the status of women can be brought to a level of effective equality; but this must be kept absolutely separate from any possible negotiations on an accession agreement with the european union, which i still abhor.

in writing. − turkey is a candidate country for accession to the european union and is therefore obliged to respect the union's acquis and to commit itself to areas such as respect for human rights, including women's rights and gender equality, a priority within the europe 2020 strategy. unfortunately, some negative aspects have emerged with regard to the respect of these rights in turkey, a country where violence against women continues to be repeated day after day. i believe that there is a pressing need for a change of course, for a transformation of the patriarchal structure in turkish society and culture. the report calls on the turkish government to take concerted and coordinated action to implement legislative measures on women's rights, education and political participation. turkey does not protect women sufficiently. in fact, there are still countless cases of forced or early marriages. it is essential that we develop a better education of everyone in respect for fundamental rights.

in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs bozkurt's text which, in examining the situation of women in turkey, stresses the need for a change of mentality which could transform the patriarchal structure of turkish society into one based on gender equality in the years to come. this would be of fundamental importance to ending gender-based violence, to increasing female participation and, in general, to empowering women. i also agree with the rapporteur that in order to achieve these objectives and to bring about this change in mentality, a more active role for the media is essential.
in writing. − the citizens' initiative aims to give citizens the same powers of political initiative as the council of ministers and the european parliament. it is an important tool for european citizens to define the issues to be put on the union's agenda. the citizens' initiative complements the direct link between citizens and the union institutions by ensuring that the latter respond to their concrete problems. parliament approved the report on the proposal for a regulation on the citizens' initiative by an overwhelming majority, thus demonstrating the strong consensus surrounding this new instrument of participatory democracy at european level. in this context, i believe that a 'one-stop shop' should be set up to facilitate the practical aspects of exchanges and dialogue with citizens, representative associations and civil society in relation to citizens' initiatives. parliament is called upon to contribute to the achievement of these objectives by using all the means at its disposal to support citizens' initiatives, in particular by organising public hearings. i therefore hope that parliament's rules of procedure will be amended as soon as possible to provide the necessary rules for the organisation and conduct of such hearings.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty introduced the right of initiative for european citizens, extending to them the same rights of initiative as those granted to the parliament and the council. while the power of legislative initiative in the strict sense remains a prerogative of the european commission, the citizens' initiative is an important tool in the hands of european citizens, giving them the power to set the political agenda, and to urge the commission to legislate on matters they consider to be priorities. this report contributes to strengthening this instrument of direct citizen participation by requiring that public hearings on petitions which meet the necessary requirements be organised by the relevant committees, and by creating a single desk to facilitate their practical implementation. i believe that the involvement of citizens in the shaping of the agenda is an integral part of the democratic process and that their inclusion in forms of direct democracy helps to bring the institutions closer to the people and to fill the lack of confidence in the european union, so i have expressed my favourable opinion on the report.
in writing. − one of the most frequent criticisms of the european union is its democratic deficit, i.e. the lack of opportunity for citizens to influence european decision-making processes. the european parliament, as the only institution whose members are directly elected by citizens, is particularly attentive to these issues and already in 2010 had approved the report on the proposal for a regulation on the citizens' initiative: it is an opportunity for citizens to make their voices heard and to bring issues of interest to the attention of the european institutions. a first example was a few weeks ago, when a committee of citizens from austria, belgium, italy, luxembourg, romania and spain presented an initiative to improve eu exchange programmes.
in writing. - the vote on the gurmai report marks an important step in the life of the european parliament and in the process of building the europe of the peoples. following the adoption of regulation 211/2011 on the citizens' legislative initiative, which gave the european parliament the task of organising the public hearing of the promoters within three months of the date of submission of the initiative to the european commission, it was necessary to amend the parliamentary rules to define the procedure. the new rule 197a of parliament's rules of procedure provides that the president of parliament shall instruct the committee responsible for the subject-matter, in conjunction with the committee on petitions, to conduct the hearing. the involvement of the latter confirms the will to guarantee the citizens a free dialogue with parliament, while safeguarding their centrality vis-à-vis the institutional legislators. the hearing phase precedes the actual legislative process and is intended to enable the promoters to explain their initiative and to clarify the reasons for it, in order to provide the executive commission with a better understanding of the matter, which will then have to set out its political and legal conclusions in a communication. as chairman of the committee on petitions, i thank the european parliament, which has given us such a high-level responsibility by a large majority.
in writing. − the citizens' initiative introduced by the lisbon treaty is an instrument of participatory democracy, involving citizens in decision-making and actively contributing to setting the political agenda for a shared path towards a stronger european construction. the fact that we now recognize the possibility of presenting the initiative in a public hearing with the direct participation of the parliamentary committee concerned goes in the direction of strengthening our dialogue with the european citizens at a particularly difficult time for the economy and for the consolidation of political europe. the period we are living in is characterized by the development of eurosceptic movements, and i therefore believe that the initiative is an important step towards bringing european citizens closer, even physically, to their own community institutions. that is why i voted for the amendment to the rules of procedure.
in writing. − the european citizens' initiative, provided for by the lisbon treaty, entered into force on 1 april 2012, as an example of direct democracy and a useful tool for opening up new horizons for european citizens. this initiative puts the citizen at the heart of the european decision-making process. one million citizens from at least seven eu member states can ask the european commission to make a legislative proposal. i am in favour of the text of the report because the legislative initiative, if it is well developed, is a genuine democratic instrument. the european structures and their members are often far removed from their relationship with the territories and citizens: the council and the commission are appointed and only the parliament is elected.
in writing. − with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, european citizens have, for the first time, the possibility of making suggestions for new laws directly: the european union's citizens, numbering at least one million and coming from at least one third of the member states, will be able to invite the european commission to submit legislative proposals in its fields of competence. the citizens' initiative is a powerful tool for european citizens to define the issues to be put on the union's agenda. it is introduced in the treaty to give citizens the same powers of political initiative as the council of ministers and the european parliament. the changes which parliament has made in the amendments further improve the system as described above. that is why i voted in favour of the text.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is certainly right to combat discrimination and to condemn all violence: however, there are certain fixed points which we cannot ignore. first, the family, which must be understood as the union of a man and a woman, completed and fully fulfilled by the possible birth of children, which cannot happen between two people of the same sex. two homosexuals can live together freely, perhaps even finding any means of recognition on a voluntary basis. but one cannot speak of marriage, let alone adoption. i don't think you can go against nature itself, which requires a man and a woman to procreate. the rest is just sterile selfishness, which comes to the point of absurdity in some glaring cases, such as that of mother men. everyone has the right to live his or her life in peace, regardless of sexual orientation, with mutual respect. but also in the natural order of things.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i think there was quasi-unanimity among the speakers. homophobia has no place in europe, either in an open form or in a hidden form, in any member state, and that includes those member states which are newcomers to the european family. it has no place against any citizen, wherever he or she may be, in the eu or in those countries outside the eu which want to have relations with us. i made that clear in my speech and i quoted baroness ashton, who regularly intervenes on specific issues in such countries. because i agree with it, i will not repeat everything that has been said. there was, however, one question which i have already answered several times in written form but which i think it is important to answer in this chamber in order to make things clear. it concerns the link between the free movement directive and the mutual recognition of same-sex couples. you know that the free movement directive provides for the right of entry and residence for union citizens and their family members, regardless of the recognition of same-sex marriages or partnerships. such recognition is immaterial for the purposes of the application of the directive. article 24 of the directive ensures that same-sex couples who exercise their right to free movement have the same rights within the scope of the treaty as same-sex couples in the host member state. the mere fact of having exercised the right to free movement does not imply that same-sex couples would acquire more rights in the host member state than those guaranteed to their own nationals in that member state. the question of recognition of marriages does not fall within the scope of the free movement directive. in order to apply it correctly, member states do not need to address the recognition of same-sex unions. they need simply to grant entry and residence to the couples in question and to their family members, including spouses and partners, irrespective of their sexual orientation. this means that all member states are obliged to grant the right of residence to a union citizen’s spouse regardless of sexual orientation, but the host member state is under no obligation to recognise the marriage under its national law. so much for the legal question, but when this legal question is not handled properly what do we do? i shall give you a very concrete example. a polish authority refused to issue certificates on civil status to citizens wishing to marry, or conclude a registered partnership with, a person of the same sex in a member state where this is possible. the commission intervened on the basis that such a stance was incompatible with respect for private and family life, and the polish authorities informed us that steps would be taken to abolish the practice of asking the sex of the future spouse or partner. i give you this example in order to explain what the law says and to explain how, without making a big fuss, we can intervene in the application of the law in a member state in order to have that member state change a practice which is not in accordance with our european rules.
president of the council. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. if i were to sum up briefly the impressions i take back to the council, i would first of all like to say that, whether we are talking about parliament, the commission or the council, we share the clear view that discrimination must be combated and that the protection of fundamental rights is the foundation of european cooperation. as i have made very clear in the debate today, the council is in full agreement with the european parliament in this assessment and the council naturally respects the principle that no citizen should be discriminated against on the grounds of, for example, his sexual orientation. it is a fundamental principle. it is also of course crucial that all member states take the necessary measures to ensure that the fundamental rights of all eu citizens are respected and enforced not only in law but also in practice. the danish presidency will therefore continue work on the anti-discrimination directive, which could be a very important contribution to implementing the prohibition of discrimination outside the labour market. i have noted the strong and correct statements that have come here today and i would like to promise to take them to the council. i would also like to stress that the danish presidency will focus on protecting the fundamental rights of citizens until the last minute of our presidency and then, of course, onwards as one of the 27 member states. for all of us in this chamber, whether we are members of this parliament, the commission or the council, wherever we come from, whatever our beliefs, whatever our sexuality, we have a common task, and that is to ensure that homophobia, which was a disgusting part of our history, is never, ever allowed to become part of the european future. this is our joint task.
