answer to a blue-card question. mr martin, i think that china's membership of the world trade organisation is a positive development. it would be a mistake to have it outside the wto because things would be much more complicated. the commission's efforts in the world trade organisation to bring about a number of changes, such as the one on raw materials, have been very helpful and satisfactory. in addition, the wto is certainly supportive of certain anti-dumping procedures. this does not mean, however, that we should not be very cautious in recognising china's market economy status on the one hand and taking advantage of our provisions, such as reciprocity, to show a more firm stance on the other.
mr president, finally, the european parliament today recognizes the serious problems china is causing the internal market: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. china is without doubt the main cause of the decline of european industrial policy. our companies are being shut out of the market by the invasion of cheap asian products. so who can relocate, maybe to china, and who can't close. we must not just talk about it, but act on it, and fight against a phenomenon which has too high an economic and, above all, social cost. while china, with a gross domestic product of 8%, is growing, exploiting workers and producing without rules, europe today has as many as 23 million unemployed and tens of thousands more waiting to be laid off. in my area, veneto, companies like safilo, redi and ditec, in the early months of 2012, decided to relocate, leaving thousands of employees at home. ladies and gentlemen, many member states, driven by the hidden powers of finance, have every interest in pretending not to understand what this trade imbalance means for the european economy. we, the citizens of europe, must put the individual and the protection of his work before everything else, by protecting the made in, by fighting against counterfeiting and the relocation of goods and by imposing duties. this is the only way to return the european market to its citizens.
mr president, china is an important trading partner for europe and i am convinced that our relations must be intensified, without neglecting the many and persistent obstacles which prevent fair and balanced trade. a new phase in eu-china trade relations is needed, based on reciprocity and respect for the rules. it is regrettable that china continues to use non-tariff barriers which restrict the presence of european companies on the chinese market, causing additional costs and trade deadlocks. non-tariff barriers, violations of intellectual property rights and respect for human rights remain among the major issues to be addressed. i hope that cooperation with the chinese government will remove the remaining obstacles by 2016, when the world trade organization should recognize china as a market economy.
in writing. i thank mrs de sarnez for her precise and thorough analysis of the subject of trade relations between the european union and china. the results of the indiscriminate opening up of the european market to chinese goods are plain to see: relocations and job losses in europe; china's average annual growth rate of 9 percent, compared with european countries experiencing a dramatic recession; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the spread of counterfeit goods, including the introduction of a new anti-counterfeiting system. in the face of all this, it is necessary to respond by demanding at least some level of reciprocity from china in very sensitive areas such as public procurement and the provision of services.
member of the commission. − mr president, i will try to go so as quickly as possible because we are already over time. let me take as a starter the question of whether i agree that we should have another agreement before we can vote on the ratification of the trade agreement with colombia and peru. i do not think so, because what some are in fact asking the european commission is to restart negotiations with colombia on a roadmap which would probably take another six months. we would then have to translate it into 23 languages, which would take another six months. the agreement was, in fact, concluded with colombia more than two years ago; we now have to come to terms with this. i have outlined in detail the provisions of the agreement, i am not going to repeat them. there is also a very clear human rights clause in the agreement. i expect the european parliament to follow up what happens once the agreement has been ratified; the commission will do the same. we have a lot of possibilities to steer the process; it would not be a good idea to restart discussions at this point. is everything perfect in colombia and peru? it is not, but i have the conviction that much has changed for the better. secondly, the politicians in both countries are serious when they claim that they are trying to resolve sometimes very difficult and long-standing situations. i think we have an honourable partnership with them in this enterprise for the better. i hope that the parliament will give its assent to what we have proposed.
in writing. first of all, i would like to make it clear that i consider this trade agreement between the eu, colombia and peru to be fundamental to optimising relations between these countries and the union. however, as the oral question we are debating today shows, there are some issues which give rise to some concern, especially as regards respect for human rights. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. but threats to the exercise of labour rights and trade union representation still persist. we therefore believe that it would be very helpful if the commission proposed mechanisms to ensure that trade agreements represent real progress in development, human rights and labour. in this respect, the more stringent clauses allowing for immediate and unilateral suspension in the event of serious human rights violations are moving in the right direction. in the case of latin america, this new agreement helps to strengthen our strategic partnership with the region, which is one of the most similar to europe in cultural and political terms.
the agenda calls for the report by anni podimata, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the proposal for a council directive on a common system of financial transaction tax and amending directive 2008/7/ec (com (2011) 0594 - c7-0355/2011 - 2011/0261 (cns)) (a7-0154/2012).
i would inform my colleagues that i do not intend to accept any more 'blue card' questions, since the discussion has been very rich and we must give the minister the opportunity to leave on time.
mr president, from an ethical and moral point of view, a measure which targets those who use finance to enrich themselves in a speculative way is certainly right and proper. the revenue generated should be used to help households and businesses, i.e. the real economy, which is deeply affected by a crisis for which finance is primarily responsible. however, in order to be truly effective, this tax should be applied globally, otherwise it would not be difficult to circumvent and would create potential competitive disadvantages for european markets. an even worse scenario would be that european countries would apply it in a disorderly manner, without common agreement. the united kingdom has already made this clear. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. this is a scenario that we absolutely must avoid. so either a unanimous consensus is reached or the measure becomes almost useless, losing much of its potential benefits.
mr president, on the subject of taxation of financial transactions, i think we must be realistic and avoid statements of principle. we must put in place a tool that is really effective and that hits the target. i am personally in favour of the idea of ftt and support the plant presented by the commission. i agree with the need for the private sector to help pay for the crisis it has caused. in recent years we have seen state intervention in the private sector, precisely to remedy critical situations caused by unbridled speculation and lack of control. however, care must be taken that this tax is not passed on to the end users, as is often the case. a further doubt concerns the effects on the financing of sovereign debt resulting from the inclusion of securities in the scope of the tax. although sovereign debt securities are exempt from tax, the reduction in liquidity on the secondary market caused by the introduction of the tax affects the price of the securities in the primary market auctions, resulting in an increase in the interest rate that the state must pay to investors. this is a damaging effect for the states with high public debt. the imposition of such a tax at eu level or only at eu level should be a first step but the ultimate objective must remain the introduction of a global tax to stabilise markets and prevent speculation.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, a big thank you to mrs anni podimata and all the other members who have worked most actively to bring about today's vote. ladies and gentlemen, this proposal has an undeniable logic and is based on a clear, rigorous and fair foundation, if it is possible to use the latter adjective in the economic field. the objections raised today do not affect this logic, and the understandable concerns expressed about possible counterproductive or undesirable effects - if they are raised in good faith - find answers and possible solutions, as the debate of these months has shown. of course, there are ways of avoiding undesirable effects, provided that there is a real will to introduce this tax, because sometimes it seems that the request for caution is made only in order to slow down or block the approval process by predicting economic disasters. and here i turn to my colleague mrs ford: we have already seen these catastrophes because of harmful and reckless speculation. there was also talk of difficulties: but today the citizens of europe are asking the institutions to regain the ability to play their general role and to give the financial world precise rules, because that is our task and that is our sovereignty as a general body. today, therefore, it is a right choice, appreciated by the citizens.
mr president, we still have a long way to go, but today's vote can be an important step towards finally introducing and implementing a financial transaction tax. i understand the prudence, the caution, the need for gradualness expressed by commissioner šemeta and the technical problems rightly mentioned by minister margrethe vestager. but that is precisely why i hope that parliament will express a clear political will, with a large majority, to give impetus and impetus to the initiatives needed to deal with the problems that remain open, especially at council level. we all want to assess carefully the impact of this tax: but it's not right to stir up unfounded fears, which can also lead to contradictory and counterproductive choices. i refer, for example, to the logic of the proposal for exemptions. if you are concerned with reducing the impact of the tax, then it is important to have the broadest possible tax base with a low rate, and not to try to extend exemptions indefinitely. for those who are concerned about the impact on small investors, i would remind them of the progressive nature of the tax, which affects those who carry out more operations and transactions more than others, and it is clear that the competent authorities will have to ensure that no attempt is made to pass any costs on to customers and end users. i hope therefore that parliament will vote in favour of this tax by a large majority.
mr president, today parliament can give the council a strong signal for the introduction of a financial transaction tax. above all, it can send a concrete message to citizens and businesses who ask us what we are doing to deal with the economic crisis. in the name of concreteness, a financial transaction tax will generate almost €60 billion to be spent on development, employment and reducing the tax burden on citizens. but it would also be a message of fairness, because the financial sector too, as our citizens have demanded, must make the right contribution to meet the costs of the economic crisis, it must absolutely do its part. i thank mr podimata for his efforts.
the martin report paves the way for the full implementation of the treaty provision governing a power of inquiry, which is essential to the performance of one of the fundamental functions of a parliament: political control. the treaty of lisbon introduced a special legislative procedure and we therefore hope that in the negotiations both institutions - the council and the commission - will adhere to the spirit of a rule which explicitly entrusts the power of initiative and regulation to parliament, limiting the role of the council and the commission to the simple expression of consent. the martin report draws on the experience of previous temporary committees of inquiry which have highlighted the limitations of this instrument and proposes significant innovations. the informal negotiations with the danish presidency and the commission have resulted in satisfactory compromise proposals which meet some of the member states' and the commission's demands, but which do not restrict parliament's right to hold the community and national institutions to account for the correct implementation of european legislation and to identify any instances of maladministration. some of the formulations may be further specified: but it is essential that we do not compromise on one point, namely that the committees of inquiry must have access to documents and to people. this has nothing to do with judicial tasks but with the full implementation of political law as clearly laid down in the treaties: the right of political control.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the definition of the bluefin tuna recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean has been, as you know, a very controversial and debated subject, mainly because of the difficulty of finding the right balance between tuna harvesting and environmental sustainability. with today's vote we are giving a first response to the demands and needs that have emerged at national level through a management tool that ensures the homogeneity of procedures. the next step will be to work hard for a fair distribution of quotas between the various fishing instruments. in this respect, we must not forget, especially in a time of crisis such as the present one, that while it is important to protect biological resources by strengthening measures to protect tuna, it is equally important to ensure that employment levels are safeguarded and that the entire fisheries sector is socially and economically sustainable.
mr president, the management of bluefin tuna fisheries has a long and rather complex history, dating back to the 1990s, and today it is probably the subject most strictly regulated by the european union. although large investments in control have led to increased compliance, concerns remain about overfishing. i therefore supported the romeva i rueda report, which proposes a reduction in the allowable catch rate, increased control and more stringent measures to reduce capacity.
mr president, i voted in favour of the amendments to the regulation on the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks because, as the international scientific community has recognised, this is a species threatened with extinction. the data speak for themselves: since 2009, we have seen a sudden decline in catches in all our seas. it is therefore necessary to act quickly to avoid their total disappearance. the reduction in the average size of tuna is a significant example of the seriousness of the situation, a phenomenon which has been demonstrated with striking clarity in the adriatic sea, in my region. the commission has already taken a number of measures to protect the fish stocks of bluefin tuna in the mediterranean. the controls must be intensified because illegal fishing in all european seas is still too widespread and too frequent. the measures envisaged, such as seizures of illegal vessels and means of transport, must be accompanied by effective and efficient checks carried out by an appropriate number of staff. finally, it is essential to raise the minimum weight of tuna, now set at 30 kilograms, and to prohibit fishing during the breeding season. more can and must be done to save bluefin tuna.
mr president, since 2010, i have supported, together with the italian delegation of italy's securities, the introduction of the tobin tax, this tax on financial speculation. parliament has today voted in favour of the introduction of this tax, which we consider to be a fundamental instrument for empowering the financial sector and bringing it back into the real economy. the introduction of a european system of taxation on financial transactions represents for us the reaffirmation of the prerogatives of democratic politics in the face of the serious anomalies in the functioning of the financial markets, which have been the cause of the economic crisis we are experiencing today. the tax on financial transactions abolishes the exemption for financial transactions and makes speculation as responsible as ordinary citizens, who are also called upon to pay taxes on bread and petrol on a daily basis. with a budget of over 50 billion a year, we are sending a signal today of the european parliament's commitment to a more supportive approach.
mr president, i am one of the large majority who voted in favour of this report and who are in agreement with mrs podimata. i am answering the question put by some colleagues about the reasons which led us to draw up this document, since the majority of member states are against it and approval of any introduction of the financial transaction tax would require unanimity. i would like to say that we did so because we feel it is the duty of the european parliament to give the council a political signal and to do its part. we have done our part by a large majority today. the fact that we voted for it does not mean that we have removed all doubts. i think that the council and the national governments must take account of those elements which are still unclear and which, although they are understandable concerns, do not justify the catastrophisms which i have heard in the course of the debate today. i think it is important to assess both the impact on consumers and the effects that the application of this tax to only a part of the member states could have. i also think it is essential to take action on the regulation of financial markets, which is not clear from the commission's proposal.
mr president, i voted in favour of this resolution, although i am convinced that the introduction of new taxes is not in itself a solution to the problems, although the introduction of some taxes may lead to relief in other areas. the financial sector is not contributing fairly to the costs of the global crisis at a time when citizens of the european union are facing an increase in both direct and indirect taxation, as well as severe cuts in wages and pensions. the financial sector is still exempt from this for its activities and transactions. i therefore agree with the proposal of my colleague, which calls for a tax of 0.1% on transactions not relating to derivative contracts and 0.01% on those relating to derivative contracts, which would generate revenue of eur 57 billion at the level of the european union. one last note: i would remind you that according to a eurobarometer survey carried out in june 2011, the citizens of the european union overwhelmingly supported the introduction of these measures.
mr president, we hear daily from the newspapers and television, but above all we see with our own eyes on the streets of our cities how deep the impact of the economic crisis is on the citizens of europe. with today's vote on mrs podimata's report, we intend to send a signal. the introduction of a financial transaction tax, in addition to the objective of achieving a future increase in revenue, shows that the european institutions are working daily to deal with the crisis, without forgetting the difficulties that our citizens are experiencing every day.
mr president, we welcome the report which stresses the importance for the union of focusing on a trade policy which does not go in the direction of an open-ended opening of european markets, but which is able to impose fair and shared rules, based on the principle of reciprocity. the union continues to negotiate with countries such as china, which are already market economies, without taking into account problems such as the lack of fairness in public procurement for our european companies, the imbalances in the protection of intellectual property rights, the lack of guarantees in the supply of rare earth raw materials and the absence of controls on the export of counterfeit goods, the growth of which, not coincidentally, goes hand in hand with the increase in chinese exports. the union must ensure, by appropriate trade measures, a policy of investment which is beneficial to our manufacturing industry, which is in danger of disappearing because of europe's inability to defend our economic model. for these reasons, i have tabled, together with my colleagues susta, rinaldi, daul and guerrero, written declaration no 16 so that the commission and the council can begin to reflect on the importance of a sound trade policy for the development of the union, for the defence of employment and for the protection of citizens.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the time has come to build a more balanced partnership with china, based on reciprocity, fair competition, friendship and trust. china's economy has grown a lot in the last 30 years. the european union has benefited from trade and will become the strongest economy by the middle of the century. it is therefore necessary to open a new phase in europe-china trade relations, based on transparency of rules, a partnership of equals and common development. we must therefore encourage china to open its market more to european companies and allow our companies to invest under conditions similar to those which apply to chinese investment in europe. a new partnership, therefore, to enable china to be seen no longer as a cause for concern for our companies, but as a great opportunity, a great opportunity for development and growth for our economy and above all for work and employment.
mr president, i am in favour of the text tabled by mrs de sarnez because it very accurately highlights the trade imbalance between the european union and china, with elements of concern that i share, especially at a time of international crisis such as the one we are experiencing. the relocation of many businesses, encouraged by the lack of labour and environmental legislation, has led to the loss of many jobs in europe at the expense of our citizens. the social costs of the eu-china imbalance are increasingly high. in addition, in the face of the dramatic recession affecting european countries, china's economy is expected to grow by 9 percent a year. it is important that the european commission should first of all work towards achieving a level of reciprocity on the part of china in very sensitive areas such as public procurement, the provision of services, the protection of workers. the european union should be more strict towards third countries which, by unfairly competing with us, penalize european companies.
mr president, i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is a good first step towards putting the obviously unbalanced relationship between the european union and china in order. the european union is founded on a number of fundamental values: for example, we rightly ask our companies to respect the environment. we have attention to workers' rights - especially women's rights - we do not have child labor nor do we have concentration camps where inmates work for free. in china, however, all these protections and rights do not exist, in fact! there are still barriers to european products entering the chinese market and it is obviously produced at lower costs, creating genuine unfair competition with european firms and products. we must create a genuine reciprocity in relations with non-eu countries, so that where there are reasons for imbalances, these are compensated by financial and commercial forms that protect our companies and our products.
mr president, relations between the european union and china clearly show that there are trade imbalances. it is therefore the duty of the european institutions to make every effort to help european companies to emerge from the crisis and to make their access to international markets more equitable. i therefore expressed my support for this report, particularly agreeing with the rapporteur on the application of the principle of reciprocity to relations between the european union and china, in order to allow fair competition on international markets, and calling for greater protection of intellectual property rights.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report because it expresses many of the concerns that we in the northern league have been supporting for a long, long time. we were perhaps the only ones who understood the damage that the growing chinese economy would do to our businesses and our workers. but when we talk about tariffs on chinese products, we are seen as backward and anti-development. the tragic results of this liberalism are, however, plain to see, and i am particularly aware of them, as i come from prato, the main chinese city in italy. we say 'better late than never', but i am not sure that europe has really realised that it is close to the so-called point of no return. and to think that someone still sees china as a possible lifeline. it would be interesting to actually understand how much european public debt is in chinese hands. perhaps this can be a key to understanding europe's weakness and at least trying not to make these tragic mistakes in the future.
mr president, the available data suggest that there is no such thing as a europe-china imbalance. but there is an imbalance - and many colleagues have already spoken about it - which we are sometimes afraid to mention, and it is not just the trade balance. it is the imbalance of social and environmental dumping that some of these chinese goods are produced with. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption, and the council will be consulted on it. i believe that these questions require more careful and more strategic reflection.
in writing. - it is true that the phenomenon of illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing seems to have been reduced over the last decade, also as a result of the countermeasures adopted by the international institutions. but it is a figure which we can consider incidental and entirely provisional, in relation to the general trend of the market. the pressure on this type of fishery is also high because technological progress puts so-called fads (fish-aggregating devices) in the hands of a wide range of operators for quite negligible amounts. it is reasonable to expect recurrent increases in non-selective fishing, including by iuu fishing, and especially in the mediterranean and atlantic neighbouring areas, which are characterised by political instability and hence by setbacks in the path of economic and civil development. the considerable discrepancy between the volume of fish caught declared and that sold on the market shows, if there was any need for it, that we have not yet achieved a balanced and reasonable system of exploitation of this resource. i am well aware that from a technical point of view we have no alternative to incorporating the amendments to the icaat plan, to which no objections have been raised, but i would like to record my favourable opinion on the report.
in writing. - urgent action is needed to protect atlantic bluefin tuna stocks, which have been drastically reduced over the years. i therefore believe it is of great importance to transpose into community law iccat recommendation 10/04 which aims to increase protection measures for bluefin tuna, especially since the european union is a contracting party to iccat. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which aims to establish a plan for the protection and conservation of bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. in recent years, in fact, a massive and poorly regulated fishing activity has threatened to seriously endanger the existence of this fish in our seas. the measures taken are in the right direction, providing for greater regulation and even proposing the creation of protected areas to encourage the re-population of this species. fishing is certainly an important activity which should not be abandoned and which can provide more and more opportunities, also in the immediate future: however, the resources are not infinite, which is why we must act in a planned way, so as not to risk irreparably compromising certain difficult situations, such as the one with bluefin tuna.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because we need a new pact between fishermen and the need to rebuild the bluefin tuna stocks. the new rules on reducing stocks are a good balance between compensating european fishermen, who compete with americans and japanese in the tuna fishery. we call for appropriate transitional processes during the conversion of those european fleets which will have to be phased out in proportion to the reduction in stocks and the fishing season. the measures focus on reducing the size of fishing fleets, but also on extending the closure of the purse seine season and strengthening controls, including those relating to the transfer of tuna from the nets to the cages. the objective must be to strike a balance between the conservation of the species and the socio-occupational needs of the fishermen and the fish processing industry, so as not to jeopardize thousands of jobs, which have already been badly affected by the stock reductions of recent years.
in writing. the aim of the proposal for a regulation just voted is to restore the stocks of bluefin tuna in the mediterranean and eastern atlantic in line with the decisions adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas. the conservation of bluefin tuna is at risk because of the fishing practices of the last 20 years, and we need appropriate rules to facilitate the repopulation of our seas. firstly, we must control the fishing flows and the derogations granted to fishing vessels, and then we must ban tuna fishing during the breeding season. the balance of our seas is more important than trade in a product and that is why this balance must be protected and guaranteed by means of control measures.
in writing. - the report by mr raul romeva i rueda on bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean was welcomed today in the house in strasbourg. the problems of managing bluefin tuna fisheries originated in the 1990s, caused by the introduction of caging to fatten bluefin tuna for the japanese market, and to date, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) seems to be at least one step behind in adapting to current fishing activities, often due to a lack of means or political will to ensure fisheries control. the rapporteur therefore believes that iccat must change its approach and move ahead, make further progress and act more quickly. the eu could, for its part, declare certain areas a protected 'sanctuary' for bluefin tuna and prohibit fishing there during the breeding season and could remove the derogation for its vessels for fishing bluefin tuna weighing at least 8 kg for farming purposes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union must re-launch the protection of bluefin tuna, a predator of the utmost importance for the maintenance of the mediterranean sea ecosystem. the plan for the re-establishment of bluefin tuna in the mediterranean must be consolidated immediately, even if it is to advance the achievement of the objectives set by the european union. breeding areas in international waters could also be declared 'marine protected areas', allowing for a prohibition of fishing during the breeding season.
in writing. the report which is currently before the house provides for the first reading by our institution of the council regulation incorporating a recommendation by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas on the multiannual recovery plan for that stock. the purpose of the proposal we are voting on in this house is to incorporate into union law the iccat recommendation amending the recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. i personally voted in favour of the text, as i welcome the decisions taken by iccat on the reconstitution plan. it is considered a useful management tool. i would like to stress only one point, namely the need to pay particular attention to the correct transposition of what has been decided at iccat, especially in order to ensure a homogeneity of procedures with the other contracting parties.
in writing. - i congratulate mr riquet on his work. in approving this report, parliament, in the light of article 294 (3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and in the light of the report of the committee on transport and tourism, has taken a position to ensure the protection of the environment and to learn from past mistakes by proposing to reduce the risks of accidental pollution by hydrocarbons in european waters by means of the accelerated introduction of double-hulls. parliament also proposed that the deadline for parliament or the council to object to delegated acts adopted by the commission in this field be extended by two months. this would give a total of four months for the necessary procedure to be carried out, ensuring a more realistic deadline for objections.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because the ecological disasters of recent years have made it clear that a substantial change in the existing legislation is needed. the question of the accelerated introduction of double-hull or equivalent technology standards for oil tankers which are now single-hull is of great importance in ensuring adequate protection of the marine and coastal environment. in particular, the risk of catastrophes is particularly acute in enclosed seas such as the mediterranean, which, due to its particular geographical nature, would be irreversibly contaminated if it were lost.
in writing. - too often oil is spilled into the sea as a result of accidents on oil tankers. the environmental damage which has been caused for decades by the lack of double hulls in many ships, which would prevent oil spills, is now intolerable. it is therefore essential that all tankers, even single-hulls, be equipped with double hulls or equivalent technologies to eliminate or minimise oil spillage in the event of accidents. the report was therefore approved.
in writing. − the accelerated introduction of double hull or equivalent technology standards for single hull tankers is a matter of great importance. black tides caused by oil tanker sinkings are a major ecological disaster, a tragedy for marine fauna and flora. the vote will seek to reduce the risk of pollution from oil tankers. the new regulation aims to reduce the risks of accidental oil pollution in european waters by accelerating the introduction of double hulls. in single-hull vessels, the oil in the cargo tanks is separated from the seawater only by a sheet on the bottom and on the side hull. if this plate is damaged by collision or by freezing, the contents of the cargo tanks may spill into the sea and cause serious pollution. an effective way to avoid this risk is to apply a second inner sheet around the load tanks at a sufficient distance from the outer sheet.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of this report. it is important to promote sustainable fishing practices by ensuring that all fishing activities carried out under the fisheries partnership agreement meet the same sustainability criteria as those for fisheries in european union waters. it is also right to ask the commission to ensure that european union vessels only catch the excess of the fish stocks concerned that cannot be caught by the mozambican fisheries sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the new protocol because the proposed amendments are aimed at improving the management of fisheries control and regulation in mozambique's waters, with the aim of boosting the direct economic income of the country. the project aims to promote responsible and sustainable fishing and to promote a partnership relationship based on respect for the legal and regulatory provisions in force in the european union and in mozambique, in the interest of both parties. the agreement also does not limit the continuity of the european fleet's fishing zone in the indian ocean.
in writing. − one of the objectives of the european union and mozambique is to strengthen economic, scientific and technical cooperation in the fisheries sector and in all related areas, in order to establish a partnership framework that allows the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fisheries resources, in the interests of both parties. after long and difficult negotiations, a new protocol between the european union and the republic of mozambique has been concluded. the protocol, which will be valid for three years, provides for an annual contribution of eur 980 000 from the eu budget, which provides for access for european vessels to mozambique's fishing zone and support for the country's sectoral policy. this vote will help to support both the fisheries sector and the african country, by improving the management of fisheries control and regulation in mozambican waters. we must not forget that there will be an obligation to recruit mozambican seafarers, also to increase the direct economic benefits for the country.
in writing. - on 2 june last year, after lengthy negotiations, a new protocol between the european union and the republic of mozambique was concluded for a period of three years. the agreement which includes clauses on the annual payment linked to respect for human rights is undoubtedly strategic because, given the increase in piracy in other fishing areas further north, it is a viable alternative. the european union and mozambique also aim to strengthen economic, scientific and technical cooperation in the fisheries sector and in all related areas, in order to establish a partnership framework that will enable the development of a sustainable and responsible fisheries policy.
in writing. - i decided to abstain from voting on the report on the common system of financial transaction taxation because i believe that we need to think more carefully about the consequences, both positive and negative. i am convinced that it would be a means of expanding and stabilising the internal market, limiting distortions of competition and the risk of double taxation between uncoordinated national taxes. it would also make a significant contribution to curbing financial speculation, which is the main cause of the current crisis. thirdly, i can only agree that the european union must find a way of raising its own resources with which to operate more freely. on the other hand, it must be borne in mind that not only third countries but even some member states are opposed to the introduction of this tax. this rejection risks not only compromising their effectiveness but also producing adverse effects: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the tax system is not distorted. i therefore believe that, while approving it in principle, this taxation should only be implemented by a broad agreement between the g20 member states or, at least, between all the states of the union.
in writing. - the introduction of a financial transaction tax would achieve the dual purpose of discouraging very short-term speculation, which often disrupts markets by generating speculative bubbles, and of raising a significant amount of resources, which could help to revive the real economy. the commission estimates that the introduction of a rate of 0.01% on derivatives and 0.1% on other assets would generate revenue of eur 58 billion. the introduction of such a tax would also be an element of fairness, involving the financial markets in the process of consolidating public accounts and discouraging the overly risky investment practices that have led to the current crisis. i therefore voted in favour of this report. i would point out, however, that the european parliament has only the right to express an opinion, since unanimity in the council is required for taxation matters. i hope, therefore, that the resistance of some countries will be overcome and that this instrument of stability will finally be introduced. finally, i would stress that the introduction of this tax at european level could provide the necessary lever for its adoption at global level, which is essential to avoid distortive effects and capital flight from european markets.
in writing. − the global financial crisis that began to emerge in 2008 is, unfortunately, far from over. in fact, in some ways, with the productive sectors now weakened by the past period, it is even more serious and now risks becoming structural in economic systems. on the other hand, the repeated and numerous cases of recurrence of the original causes of the crisis also show that the 'market' is not an abstract entity capable of self-regulating itself efficiently, as the specialists in the new welfare economy would still like to make us believe, but is instead a system managed by a few players worldwide who, often without scruples, attack financial markets, production systems and institutions in the hope of profiting from their weakening, or even their failure. the measures taken by each country are not sufficient to deal with this global crisis. we need to make choices on an equal footing. a financial transaction tax would be useful in mitigating the devastating effects of financial assault, especially if it were adopted globally and if it did not impact government bonds and pension funds. in the expectation and hope that this can happen, it is important that it should start at least in the european dimension. this report and the amendments adopted are geared to this perspective.
in writing. − as we all know, the global financial crisis, which started in 2008, had tragic consequences, with an almost immediate impact on the real economy. the mismatch between consumer demand and supply has also had a devastating effect on employment, thus generating major problems in the labour market. europe needs more convergence, solidarity and responsibility to cope with the crisis. among the various measures to be taken is the strengthening of the stability of the single market through the introduction of innovative strategies aimed at pursuing not only economic but also social growth. i believe that fiscal consolidation through the introduction of a common system of financial transaction taxation can have a positive effect on the single market, and for this reason i voted in favour of mrs anni podimata's report. the positive effects could be many. however, i believe that the very globalised nature of the financial sector and its services now calls for a further step, promoting the introduction of a worldwide financial transaction tax: the eu's 27 member states first, and then the g20, should show cohesion in pursuing this objective.
in writing. - while i agree with the proposal on some points, there are some criticisms which should not be overlooked: the commission has also taken into account the fact that the tax on financial transactions is not a single tax, but a single tax on transactions between member states. secondly, the granting of taxation powers to the european union limits the autonomy of the member states. finally, the sector's volatility, which makes it difficult to legislate on the subject, and the risk that the burden expected from financial institutions may be passed on to citizens, who are already victims of the economic crisis, should not be overlooked. for these reasons, i thought it appropriate to abstain.
in writing. − the global crisis that began in 2008 has called on us repeatedly, and will call on us again in the future, to make unpopular and difficult decisions to get out of it and build a future that can be characterised by growth, development and employment. in this context, however, we cannot forget the role that finance, especially speculative finance, has played in causing and aggravating the crisis. it is also worth noting that the financial sector has never been affected by taxation measures that have limited its scope. but we want to send a clear message with mr podimata's report: the financial transaction tax, introduced with the double rate for government securities and derivatives, aims to create tax revenue that can be used partly to structure the european budget and partly to strengthen the economies of the member states.
in writing. - a financial transaction tax, if it is to be effective, should be applied globally, otherwise it could be easily circumvented and would still risk creating problems for the european financial sector, problems which we do not need today. the greatest danger would be to reduce the already poor liquidity of the markets and thus make it more difficult to access the credit necessary for the survival and development of our enterprises, especially small and mediumsized ones. on the other hand, if properly applied, this tax could be a means of finding resources without always hitting the usual well-known people, that is, those who are already bearing a very heavy tax burden, and who have been overwhelmed by a crisis that has many other responsible parties, including certainly those who have used finance in a reckless manner and for purely speculative purposes. i therefore share the general objectives of the report, but i still have some doubts about the way in which it is to be implemented, which is why i have decided to abstain from the final vote on this report.
in writing. - we voted today in the chamber in strasbourg on the report by mr podimata. parliament has been calling for a financial transition tax (ftt) for almost two years and the commission put forward a legislative proposal in 2011. the eurobarometer shows that 66% of europeans are in favour of a ftt. the ttf is an integral part of the strategy to get out of the crisis. it will bring about a fairer distribution of the burden of the crisis and will not cause relocation outside the eu, as the cost of relocation is higher than paying the tax. the commission also proposes to extend the scope of the directive to include the principle of issuance, so that financial institutions established outside the ttf area would also be required to pay the levy if they traded securities originally issued within the zone. the 'residence principle', already provided for in the commission text, should be maintained so as to cover also financial products issued outside the ftz but marketed by at least one institution established within the ftz. an ambitious ftt system will also give us a tool to reduce speculation and to ensure that the financial sector returns to its original role of serving smes and other businesses.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this measure because i believe that the introduction of a common system of transaction tax will also enable the financial sector to make a real contribution to the costs of the crisis. the economies of the member states are paralysed, unable to cope with the social and economic challenges: shifting the tax burden away from labour and productive investment is now a priority. this is why the financial transaction tax can contribute by generating new revenue estimated at up to eur 57 billion with the positive effects of redistributing the tax burden and stabilising markets.
in writing. the world economic crisis remains a concern for the european institutions and the citizens of the union. the creation of a financial transaction tax (ftt) has some aspects of relevance to the union budget. i voted in favour of mrs podimata's report because it once again underlines the constant attention that the european union is paying to the effects of the crisis. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the power to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu in order to amend the rules on the application of the ttber. it is important to stress that the ftt must be applied globally and not just at eu level, otherwise there is a risk of financial institutions migrating to markets outside the eu, with the resulting weakening of the european market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive to introduce a financial transaction tax in europe. this is because, in the context of the proposals for the new eu's own resources, the european executive wants to achieve a greater capacity to generate its own tax revenue. the commission intends that two thirds of the total revenue from the financial transition levy should be allocated to the community budget. the commission proposal has a threefold objective which i thought it would be useful to support: generate new tax revenues from the financial sector, counter speculation resulting from high-frequency financial trading (millions of financial orders in seconds handled by suppliers or holders who do not hold liquidity but only handle orders), and improve the internal market by avoiding distortions of competition and the risks of double taxation resulting from the application of national taxes in an uncoordinated manner. a proposal, the one put forward by this parliament, which i believe is necessary to avoid a repeat of the crisis of 2008. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report, supporting in principle the objectives of the commission's proposal.
in writing. − i abstained in the vote on this text because china is the most important challenge for eu trade policy and i believe that the commercial relations with this country should be evaluated from a much larger perspective. we must consider that china is not only the world’s second largest economy and the biggest exporter in the global economy, but also an increasingly important political power. in addition, china has in recent decades achieved important social progress and such an improvement in the quality of life for a huge country in such a short period of time is unique in history. in fact, the economic growth in china has lifted half a billion people out of poverty since 1990. i agree on many points stressed by this report, but at the same time there is a lack of strategic consideration. by the middle of the century china will become the world’s most powerful economy and for this reason we need to build a partnership based on mutual respect. in addition it is important to consider the potential benefits for developing countries from deeper economic relations with china and that the growth in trade between all the eu member states and china represents a crucial opportunity for growth.
in writing. − china's economy, which has grown by almost 10% a year for the past 30 years and is predominantly export-oriented, will become the world's most powerful economy by mid-century. the european union, the world's largest trading power and the largest recipient of chinese exports, has seen its trade deficit widen from eur 49 billion in 2000 to eur 168.8 billion in 2010, with weak growth. there is a clear imbalance which must be corrected. despite the progress made by beijing to reduce trade barriers that impede access to its markets, obstacles remain numerous: european companies cannot invest in china under the same conditions as chinese investment in europe. in addition, the lack of protection of intellectual property in china is increasingly deterring european investors. in 2010, 85% of the goods infringing intellectual property rights seized by european customs came from the chinese mainland. in my view, a renewed framework for eu-china relations is urgently needed. europe's approach should be to build partnerships based on the principles of reciprocity and fair competition, which are factors in easing trade tensions and in shared growth.
in writing. − immediately after the ninth china-europe summit in 2006, which some experts consider to be the zenith of bilateral relations to date, relations between the union and the people's republic of china were beset by a series of tensions, particularly around the open issues that the report identifies very precisely. i therefore vote in favour of it. if it is inevitable that countries define themselves in relation to each other in bilateral relations, this is all the more true for china, whose internal tensions are intertwined with foreign and security policy, trade policy, energy policy and monetary policy. the most attentive observers point out that certain positions of the people's republic are often the result of a close comparison of internal positions. today, the rmb, the rare earth policy, the return of state ownership with the restriction of the free enterprise space, are a hot debate ground between different lines of thought. it is all the more important to remember that a clear and determined european position can also contribute to the satisfactory solution of the unresolved issues within the chinese institutions, in a fair and in any case more favourable way to us.
in writing. − the globalisation of the economy has led to the need to strengthen economic cooperation between the eu and other areas of the world. this objective must be pursued not only through some fundamental principles that make trade balances sustainable, which are certainly important, but above all through support for the eu's production systems, to make them more competitive on a world scale. the principle of legal and economic-financial reciprocity and the principle of anti-dumping, with particular reference to the fiscal and social security aspects, must therefore always form an essential part of economic agreements, so that there is a correct approach based on the comparative and competitive advantages of undertakings and production systems. in addition, the principle of reciprocity must also be applied to access to chinese public procurement. finally, the eu should pay greater attention to investments in developing countries, including those made by competitors such as china, in order to better assess the impact of such interventions, both politically and economically, socially and environmentally. i believe that the report we have approved pursues these objectives.

in writing. − economic exchanges between china and the european union have reached considerable levels in recent years: the eu has become the largest recipient of chinese exports, while china is the eu's second largest trading partner. at the same time, this trade relationship is highly unbalanced in favour of beijing: in 2010, the trade deficit was eur 168.8 billion (compared to eur 49 billion in 2000) and eu foreign investment in china was eur 4.9 billion, while chinese foreign investment in the eu was eur 0.9 billion in the same year. we cannot forget the difficulties faced by european companies when they try to enter the chinese market, due primarily to the lack of transparency of national rules and the protectionist policy of the beijing government which causes heavy dumping, caused by the massive subsidies granted by the chinese government to national companies. the report analyses the reasons for the imbalance and makes a number of proposals to improve the current situation, ranging from the application of the principle of reciprocity to the public procurement market (in order to ensure greater openness in the chinese procurement market) to the protection of intellectual property rights.

in writing. - if the aim was to adapt the exercise of the right of inquiry to the implementation of the lisbon treaty, without affecting other national supervisory bodies and not, the text can be considered a good summary and as such i find it favourable. it was necessary to promote parliament's work in this field, which would not be redundant but could at the same time be effective in the political control of cases of infringement or maladministration of union law. this need is reinforced by the emergence of figures such as the ombudsman and by the powers now granted to other bodies. in the context of a plurality of these instances - also taking into account the degree of heterogeneity in the member states' legal systems - experience has shown that the instruments available to parliament, deriving from decision 95/167/ec, euratom, ecsc (which was a descendant of the maastricht treaty), are inadequate. the modest activity of the committees of inquiry reveals, in addition to the cautious attitude of members and parliament, which we do not doubt, a picture of substantial impotence. it should not be overlooked that the european citizen probably finds in parliament the only instrument (in this case, the instrument of verification of the administration of community law) which is completely under his control, which is necessarily responsible and easily revocable.
in writing. - the european parliament's right of inquiry was enshrined in the maastricht treaty and strengthened and further defined by the recent entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. a europe which wants to be strong politically and administratively finds in this legal instrument a lever of strengthening of paramount importance. the limitation of the european parliament's right of inquiry, especially in exceptional cases or when the need to set up temporary committees to analyse and propose effective solutions to particular problems becomes apparent, is essential in order to be able to act with a greater degree of cooperation and effectiveness between all the member states and at the european level as a whole.
in writing. - it is essential that a committee of inquiry can rely on concrete evidence gathered in the course of its inquiry. to that end, the committee of inquiry should be able to carry out, within the limits of its mandate, any investigation it deems necessary for the performance of its task, in particular to carry out on-the-spot investigations, to request documents, to summon witnesses, to hear officials and other servants of the union or of the member states and to request expert reports. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this reform proposal because, compared with the old decision, it provides a clearer and more logical regulation as regards the procedures for the european parliament's right of inquiry. the committee of inquiry should be able to carry out any investigation and to summon any person whose testimony or expertise is deemed necessary in order to reach its conclusions on the basis of evidence only. this would allow the european parliament to exercise serious and effective control without disappointing the expectations of european citizens in terms of accountability and good governance.
in writing. - the right of inquiry is an important aspect of parliament's powers of scrutiny. the right of the european parliament to set up temporary committees of inquiry to investigate alleged breaches or maladministration in the application of community law became a primary right with the maastricht treaty. but the treaty did not provide information on the specific powers granted to the european parliament's committees of inquiry, leaving instead the definition of the detailed arrangements to a future interinstitutional agreement. the time has come, therefore, - also with this vote - to define and regulate the matter, especially in the light of the treaty of lisbon, which has changed the institutional balance of the union and strengthened the political stature of parliament.

member of the commission. − mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate mr gerbrandy on this report, which recognises the high level of ambition needed to achieve the transformation to a resource efficient europe. it reaffirms the political importance of the resource efficiency agenda and the urgency of the need to take action in order to respond to the economic and environmental challenges we face. resource constraints are a real global trend that we must certainly address. the economic crisis has demonstrated the need for urgent changes in the economy and the need to consider our growth model. without new policies we will put even more pressure on the environment, we will not deliver on our climate change targets, and we will expose our economy and well-being to systemic risks. sustainable resource use is the condition for the long-term resilience and competitiveness of our economies. resource efficiency is also a promising source of growth and jobs, which offers multiple benefits and opportunities for business and policy-making in the short, medium and also long term. the commission has laid out its vision for the path to sustainable growth and competitiveness in the long-term strategies under the europe 2020 resource efficiency flagship initiative, ranging from energy to transport to climate, water and biodiversity. we have integrated resource efficiency into our proposals for cohesion, for research, for development, and for agricultural and fisheries policies. i hope that the outcomes of the legislative process will match the ambition you show today so that we can address the scale of the resource challenges we really face. with the roadmap to a resource efficient europe we have put on the table a coherent framework to achieve the 2050 vision of sustainability. the commission has proposed a set of 2020 milestones and concrete actions to start the process of transformation. resource efficiency policies are approached from three angles, and i am glad to see from your report that you share this view of the priorities. first of all, we highlight the need to provide the horizontal conditions for transformation of the economy. we address consumption and production, emphasise the importance of measures such as eco-design, and highlight the importance of research and innovation, and the crucial need to phase out inefficient subsidies and shift to environmental taxation. turning waste into a valuable resource is key to boosting the resource productivity of the eu economy and also enhancing growth. full implementation of eu waste legislation alone would save eur 72 billion a year, increase the annual turnover of the eu waste management and recycling sector by eur 42 billion and create over 400 000 jobs by 2020. secondly, the nature target. we should try to ensure that our natural capital and the ecosystem services this provides are used efficiently in the short and long term, as they are the foundation of our economy and our quality of life. this reflects the broad definition of resources that the commission seeks to promote. thirdly, we target the economic sectors that are responsible for the greatest share of environmental impacts – namely food, buildings and mobility. i am glad to see that you also put these as a first priority in your report. governance is the key element of the strategy, because resource efficiency is an integration agenda and eu member states have a key role to play in bringing about the necessary changes. integration of resource efficiency into the european semester will ensure that member states are moving along a sustainable path. we will also launch a process to define the appropriate targets with solid, effective and science-based indicators with a view to agreeing on a lead indicator, a dashboard and thematic indicators by 2013. naturally, we also need the full implementation of european union environmental legislation, coupled with actions at international level to ensure a level global playing field. as always, the commitment of all stakeholders is fundamental to the success of any programme. we need to mobilise actors at all levels, and in all relevant sectors, to do their part. i count of course on your support for this. i will be following today’s debate with very keen interest. thank you.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, this report is yet another statement of intent which is difficult to achieve, especially in a time of economic crisis such as the one we are experiencing. the main issues dealt with by parliament are almost exclusively environmental issues. intervention at the level of the european union alone can only impoverish our businesses and our citizens, to the exclusive benefit of third countries. too stringent and burdensome rules lead to the relocation of firms to third countries, which have lower tax burdens, costs, rules and controls. the transfer of these companies also leads to a worsening of atmospheric emissions as they are no longer subject to the already strict european limits. our citizens are being duped twice: we are losing jobs and increasing emissions into the environment. further loss of competitiveness for europe means a longer period of recovery. for these reasons, we voted against the report in the envi committee. if the outcome of the votes in the house, with the adoption of important amendments, improves some of the most controversial points and also takes into account some positive indications contained in this measure, our vote may turn into an abstention. if not, we will speak out against it.
mr president, what we are discussing - the protection of the environment in conjunction with economic growth - is certainly a central theme, which is widely agreed upon at all levels. a more efficient use of resources plays a leading role. it is our absolute duty to ensure that development meets the needs of present generations without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own. however, i am deeply convinced that it is about promoting a culture. i am therefore concerned about some of the overly managerial aspects already mentioned in the commission proposal and excessively emphasized by the rapporteur's work. much has already been said; i am concerned, for example, about the shift of taxation from labour to the environment. i am of the opinion that, in the absence of a comprehensive impact assessment, also at the macroeconomic level, such a measure risks having the sole effect of increasing the already heavy tax burden on european taxpayers. the rapporteur, mr florenz, has already spoken about food habits. i do not think it is our job to tell our citizens whether or not to eat animal protein, and i think it is important that the european parliament has spoken out against food waste, since some 20 per cent of food is thrown away as waste. i hope, therefore, that we will adopt a more constructive and realistic approach. i think we should support in particular proposals to facilitate access to innovative technologies for small and mediumsized enterprises, with a focus on research and innovation. but we must also work with the help of the productive sector: clear and reliable indicators of resource efficiency are absolutely needed, but they must be based not only on economic assessments but also on precise scientific knowledge. finally, as regards the timing: where i come from, in italy, they say "the hasty cat made the kittens blind". don't speed too much! mr president, i would like to congratulate mr gerbrandy on his excellent report. the transition to a resource-efficient economy is inevitable and necessary. by 2050, the world's population will reach 9 billion people, and each of them will aspire to a better life. as the commission points out, at the current rate of resource exploitation, it will take the equivalent of two earths to support the world's population in 2050. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very important one. member states must remove any obstacles to the recycling and reuse of waste market and provide for economic incentives to promote innovative technologies for the collection and separation of waste. it is right to achieve zero waste, by prohibiting landfilling and phasing out the incineration of recyclable waste. it is necessary to agree on indicators of the use of resources in economic activity, i.e. the land footprint, the water footprint, the material footprint and the carbon footprint. these indicators should be used to promote legislative initiatives for sustainable development and reduction of resource exploitation.

caution. this reallocation of the funds is possible and makes a difference. we can reallocate to more efficient and more effective projects, but this is not a magic solution. it is also important to that the banks can revive themselves and then they will be able to support the real economy. that is why the microfinance initiative – for which we also thank the parliament – is so important because general terms. i very much agree with those who frame the discussion in the context of the general discussion on employment and growth in the european union today. i think this is extremely important. why? because in the countries of the eu where youth unemployment is excessively high – terribly high, particularly in spain and greece – there is not just one problem. we discussed many: education and training; school to work policies, or the lack thereof; segmentation of the labour market, which labour market reforms inside the member states will help to sort out. that is why the reform in italy is so important, because it will also help the young people. i hope that this reform will be concluded successfully very soon. but it is also very important to notice that we are speaking about a gap periphery of the european union. the big problem is that, until now, there has been no macroeconomic policy in the european union able to establish cohesion and bridge the gap between the core and the you, mr becker – originate from berlin. mr becker, mr mann, mrs steinruck, mr händel, you are meps, but you also have a right to speak in your national parliaments. please help the bundestag and the the time has come to change the macroeconomic policies, to allow the peripheral countries and regions of the european union to regain their growth potential and provide job opportunities for people, and especially for young people who are now excessively affected by unemployment. this is my conclusion for today, and i thank you for this extremely important discussion.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to thank the rapporteur for her work. 55 years after article 119 of the treaty and after article 157 of the treaty of lisbon, the average wage gap in europe is 16.5 per cent, which shows - as the report also states - that a more comprehensive approach must be tried. the nine key issues identified in the report constitute, in my view, an important basis for the amendment of the 2006 directive requested by parliament to the commission by february 2013, providing for both legislative and non-legislative measures. i would remind the previous speaker that the legal basis is article 157, which provides that parliament and the council may act by means of a legislative procedure, together with the commission, to provide for measures to ensure that member states implement measures of parity. in particular, i think that the need for transparency in the definition of the equal value of a job, based on a classification of professions with reference to professionalism, competence and responsibility, should be emphasized. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be given the right to vote in the council of ministers. in addition, in the assessment of remuneration, there is a need for greater transparency of the part of the salary which is generally the same as the other components where the gap tends to grow, such as benefits, allowances or posts. this is demonstrated by the fact that the gap increases as women's professional level increases, which means that this is the aspect on which we must concentrate, together, of course, with the need for reconciliation and training opportunities, as well as the value of parttime work in relation to career opportunities, a factor which is still a handicap today.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the adoption of this resolution is very important because, until a few months ago, volunteering was a kind of mysterious object for the european union. even though it involved 100 million volunteers and 5% of the gdp produced by this world, it seemed like this sector didn't exist. and then, despite a lot of difficulties, we were able to dedicate the last year, 2011, to volunteering, and we all saw the great potential of it. states that did not have legislation on this subject have adopted it, others have modernised it, many have strengthened the activities of associations and, especially in a time of crisis such as the one we are experiencing, have given an important - subsidiary - role to the non-profit world. we have taken this as a starting point to emphasize the role of volunteering within the european union, as the report we are discussing this evening shows. we started with a very good communication from the commission, which i thank for its work, and i thank the shadow rapporteurs and the officials of the groups and of parliament who helped me to prepare this report. what did we plan? firstly, a portal to inform citizens about the possibilities of volunteering in the various member states and how they can participate. secondly, the possibility of using the international labour organisation's volunteering measurement manual and the united nations non-profit organisation manual to provide comparable statistics and data that provide a clear picture of the significant contribution of volunteering and the needs of volunteers across the european union. we want to give volunteering a high profile in sport, particularly at the grassroots level. we would also like to recognise the important contribution of volunteering to environmental protection and support volunteering activities in the fields of environmental education, emergency prevention and management, and the protection of artistic and cultural heritage. we support the commission's proposal to establish a european skills passport, so that skills acquired through volunteering are officially recognised for both professional and learning purposes. a passport which is a complete document recording, at the request of the volunteer, all practical experience, training, transversal and vocational skills acquired in the lifelong learning programme, including skills acquired in a volunteering activity. we call on the commission to implement this european skills passport as soon as possible. we also support the commission's proposal to set up a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps, which will increase the participation of volunteers in solidarity actions within the framework of humanitarian aid policy throughout the european union. we would like to ensure adequate funding and establish and simplify administrative procedures, including tax incentives, for voluntary organisations, including associations and networks, particularly those of small size and with limited resources, in order to enhance their role, activities and results for the benefit of society as a whole. henri de montherlant said it best: "selfless acts are the stars of the earth". volunteering has that ability. with his free activity he manages to bring the stars to our earth and plant them firmly. our flag, mr president, is made of stars, and that is why the european union cannot help but empower volunteering and its world of small, big everyday gestures.
