year of volunteering, which gave a lot of momentum to volunteering in europe and showed that volunteering contributes to our democratic and pluralistic society and lends added value to eu policies. a large and varied number of activities took place during the european year of volunteering – many of which will continue beyond that european year – and a significant number of structures put in place in 2011 have become permanent. so far, six important policy documents have been adopted as a result of the european year. mr scurria’s report on ‘recognising and promoting cross-border voluntary activities in the eu’ will be the seventh significant policy document in this series in support of volunteering. the report links in perfectly with the commission communication on eu policies on volunteering. our communication aimed to outline the ways in which the commission already supports the voluntary sector and how it plans to further improve the recognition and promotion of volunteering in the future. we agree on many points. both parliament and the european commission recommend that member states should assess the need for creating a clear legal framework for volunteering and develop appropriate national strategies to achieve that. together, we are encouraging member states to make volunteering accessible to all sectors of society and to support cooperation between providers of voluntary activities in the eu. another common recommendation to member states is that they should adopt the volunteering measurement methods developed by johns hopkins university to get a clearer picture of the role of voluntary activities in our economy. the european commission is committed to ensuring long-term follow-up of the european year and has taken concrete steps in this direction. overall, the european year of volunteering 2011 influenced positively volunteering in europe. this positive influence will continue, since it may take several more years for some of the benefits of the year to bear fruit and become tangible. the european year of volunteering lies behind us, but we are now at a starting point for ensuring that the legacy of that european year remains in place. the commission communication of last september and your report today show us ways to follow up on that year, including by developing synergies with the proposed european year of citizens in 2013. the commission looks forward to working with parliament towards our common objective to further facilitate and promote volunteering in the european union.
in writing. 2011 was the european year of voluntary activities', with a number of initiatives involving volunteers across europe in activities to promote, inform and raise awareness of this issue. recent figures show that a body of 100 million european citizens engaged in various voluntary activities can contribute to the production of 5% of european gdp. volunteering is, in my view, an expression of active citizenship in all areas of social life, and crossborder volunteering in particular is an opportunity for intercultural enrichment for young european citizens. after the visibility gained by the european year of volunteering, i think it is appropriate to concentrate action on a series of concrete measures to promote these activities. to this end, i welcome the rapporteur's proposals, including the idea of establishing a centralised union portal on volunteering with a specific section on crossborder volunteering and the creation of a 'european voluntary humanitarian aid corps'. the latter, by selecting, training and sending volunteers to provide support to local organisations in the event of natural disasters, has the valuable advantage of developing synergies with existing organisations and structures, avoiding overlapping and dispersion of funds.
in writing. volunteering enables people to do work of social benefit and to acquire skills and knowledge that should be used when looking for a job or when integrating into a particular training path. this is why the creation of a 'skills passport' should be supported: the commission will also be supporting the development of a european voluntary service to facilitate the formal recognition of professional experience across the eu, which must go hand in hand with increased funding for european voluntary activities. volunteering is in fact experienced and regulated in too different ways in the member states and the recognition of the activity provided, even if it is entirely selfless, is not uniform between the states. we therefore call for the creation of a centralised european portal to help voluntary organisations to disseminate information, improve cooperation and exchange best practice and experience, the recognition of a 'volunteer passport' which can accredit volunteering experience also for university or professional purposes, the employment of our young people while they are looking for a job, the dissemination of good practice among voluntary organisations in europe,
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are discussing new measures today, a few months after other similar legislation was adopted. it seems to be a constant race to recover from a situation which is now difficult to recover. i do not think that putting straitjacket on the states and even proposing legal protections can solve this dramatic situation in which the eurozone finds itself. if we want to keep economic and monetary union alive, we must also find growth instruments, such as eurobonds, or measures that can in any case encourage investment. the euro has brought benefits to a few and enormous problems to many. some countries, such as germany, should understand this situation and accept some compromises, as other countries have done in the past. if this is not the case, then economic and monetary union may well end here, certainly without any great regret for us. perhaps it would be germany that would suffer the most in the end.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i feel particularly responsible for the reasons for the italian delegation of the epp's vote on the two-pack. we will vote with conviction for the text which dismissed the econ committee because we want preventive checks on the budgets of the member states of the union. we want to see more rigor. at the same time, we are voting for the two-pack because we think it is the ideal complement to what the six-pack was. but the fiscal compact has not yet been ratified in many member countries. it has not been ratified in italy, it has not been ratified in germany, it has not been ratified in france. to be ratified by qualified majorities it needs a compromise. we shall therefore vote in favour of mr gauzès' report and also of mr ferreira's report, because we believe that only a compromise can put the necessary majorities in our countries in a position to ratify the fiscal compact. we shall vote in favour, including the redemption fund and the investment scrap. these are our reasons. these are the reasons for a vision which knows that at the heart of europe there is first of all a concern for peace and development and that the political families must guarantee through compromise the possibility of rigor and development for all.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the two-pack demonstrates that there is a legal basis for a community governance of the euro area, which this parliament had asked to be used in the reform of article 136. what we now have to assess is whether these two regulations appear adequate in the face of the crisis's precipitation and the potential of their legal basis. here the answer is clear: the commission proposal seems to belong to another historical epoch. as commissioner rehn has said, the commission is proposing a complement to the six-pack without taking into account the obvious limitations of austerity policies and economic governance that is only focused on introducing rigid constraints and not on giving the eu real powers to govern the economy. the committee on economic and monetary affairs has made important improvements to the commission's proposal, which are particularly visible in mr ferreira's report, firstly with the article on the debt redemption fund. however, several limitations remain. it is striking that the rapporteur, mr gauzès, is deaf to the proposal to involve parliament in the activation of the enhanced surveillance procedure by introducing a procedure similar to that for delegated acts. our group has, however, responsibly decided to concentrate on one point, but there seems to me to be some confusion about it. amendment no 82 is not a weakening of the stability pact and is not a classic golden rule clause. it is rather a tool to defend the stability pact and to make it effective and enforceable, including by giving the commission a greater role. the amendment is based on the concept of sustainable discipline and gives the commission the task of prioritising investment for growth and jobs when setting medium-term objectives and assessing member states' budgets. i therefore call on my colleagues in the epp to read the amendment, to reflect and to avoid this parliament appearing closed and complacent in the face of a situation which is developing throughout europe and also in the council.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to support the reintegration of workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the globalisation process of world markets. spain saw the closure of 188 leather and leather-related packaging businesses, due to the tendency of the european industry to move production sub-processes to non-eu countries where labour costs are lower. in view of the above, and given that spain has confirmed, on the one hand, that the egf contribution does not replace measures falling within the competence of undertakings and, on the other hand, that the planned actions, which are intended to provide support to individual workers, do not receive support from other financial instruments of the union, my vote was in favour.
in writing. − the egf, the european globalisation adjustment fund, is used to help european companies in difficulty or to encourage their development towards a balanced position in the european market. the request in question, for which i have given a favourable opinion, concerns 876 redundancies in 146 companies operating in the footwear sector in the comunidad valenciana, for which eur 1 631 565 was requested. the application, which has already received the official endorsement of the european commission, was assessed on the basis of the link between redundancies and changes caused by the financial crisis. spain classified these redundancies as a consequence of the decrease in footwear trade due to the dominance of china and india.

in writing. − the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund has been extended and, as from 1 may 2009, it is possible to apply for support for workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. in this respect, spain is in a deep crisis in the footwear sector, due to the impact of the imbalance between imports and exports, which is reported to be higher than that recorded throughout europe, thus generating a considerable wave of redundancies resulting also from the general tendency of the footwear industry in the union to relocate most of the production sub-processes to countries outside the european union. employment in this specific sector fell by 31.80% and 188 enterprises ceased their activities. the vote in favour supports the request for access to the european globalisation adjustment fund to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, and seeks to ensure a rapid procedure, in compliance with the interinstitutional agreement between parliament, the council and the commission, for the adoption of decisions on the mobilisation of the fund.

in writing. − the application submitted by italy in october 2012 in support of the damage suffered in the regions of liguria and tuscany due to floods which caused serious damage to homes, farms, the agricultural sector and caused a disruption of the main transport networks and thus damage to essential public infrastructure, is of common interest and raises awareness throughout the community. the total direct damage caused by the floods, according to the italian government, amounts to eur 722,5 million. the disaster was of natural origin and falls within the scope of the solidarity fund. the commission has proposed to mobilise the eu solidarity fund to the amount of eur 18 061 682 in commitment and payment appropriations. i am voting in favour today, with the hope that these funds will be allocated as quickly as possible to meet the commitments made earlier and that they will help to alleviate the serious problems still affecting these regions.
in writing. the floods that hit tuscany and liguria in october 2011 were dramatic: in addition to the deaths and numerous injuries, there were roads and railways disrupted, homes and businesses flooded and extensive damage to public infrastructure, with direct damage estimated at around €720 million. i therefore voted in favour of the entry in the 2012 union budget of commitment and payment appropriations which, through the mobilisation of the solidarity fund, will make it possible to help the victims of the floods.
in writing. - i am opposed to the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the technical management of the fund. first, i consider that the amount requested is excessive and is based on too vague accounting information. secondly, in view of the serious economic crisis we are facing and the serious problem of redundant workers in several member states, i believe that the commission should avoid unnecessary expenditure and instead internalise the tasks for which it requires the mobilisation of the fund. the fund itself will thus be able to remain available for its primary purpose: aid for the reintegration of redundant workers. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. − dear mr. president, i voted for this report because i agree with the need of finding new channels of development cooperation between the european union and the latin american region. the eu is the principal donor of development aid, the principal investor and the second trading partner in the region. the eu aid to latin america throughout these years has contributed positively to the efforts of each country to consolidate their rule of law and to reduce their pressing poverty issues. now is not the time to abandon them but to redirect cooperation where it is needed the most in order to address poverty reduction through the development cooperation instrument and the new partnership instrument.
in writing. - whereas the report calls for an improvement in the distribution of development aid and, in the light of recent developments in latin america, for aid to be redirected towards the promotion of education and health programmes and towards the sectors with the greatest impact on the fight against poverty, i voted in favour;
in writing. − the eu's development cooperation policy plays a key role in achieving the millennium development goals and international commitments on human rights, food security and environmental sustainability. we have made steady progress in advancing relations with the countries of central america, with the activation of the eu-lac foundation, with the launch of an investment instrument for latin america and with the extremely important dialogues on climate change, innovation, drugs or migration. we believe that the time has now come to give a new impetus to our development cooperation policy. the need for coordinated cooperation on request, taking into account the situation in each country and based on broader indicators than those for measuring income levels, is becoming apparent. it is important to recall that the eu's strategic partnership is based on common values and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, and it is also necessary to stress that challenges such as the food crisis, the fight against climate change and the social solution to the crisis are common to the eu and latin america and must be addressed by strengthening multilateralism.
in writing. - i fully agree with the need to link progress in relations with latin america to a coherent development policy. it is necessary to develop country-specific cooperation objectives, focusing resources on the most vulnerable countries and improving policy coherence for development. i also agree with the request to the commission to maintain the volume of the development cooperation instrument for latin america for the period 2014-2020 at one third of the total geographical amount. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i agree with mr cortés lastra's report on development cooperation with latin america because i believe that partnerships with third countries are a springboard for the eu to enter the union market and, above all, a great incentive for developing countries and the less fortunate to lay the foundations for growth. promoting sustainable development in other countries at the economic and socio-political level is the basis for a better future for both the eu and the partners, which in the case of latin america are characterised by enormous disparities in wealth and social reality. investing, therefore, is not only a european interest but also a means of combating poverty and unemployment and a stimulus to growth in many south american countries.
in writing. - the report by mr cortés lastra on development cooperation with latin america was voted on today in plenary. the lisbon treaty stipulates that the union shall endeavour to develop relations and establish partnerships with third countries, promoting the sustainable development of developing countries in economic, social and environmental terms, with the primary objective of eradicating poverty. latin america has 180 million people living below the poverty line and includes ten countries that continue to rank among the fifteen most unequal countries in the world. the cooperation offered by the eu, the largest donor of development aid and the largest investor in latin america, through the association agreements signed and, above all, through development aid, is a positive contribution to the effort made by each country to consolidate its rule of law and reduce the pressing problems of poverty within it. despite the global economic crisis, the eu must continue to support latin america's key sectors, such as education and health.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i believe that increasing the european presence in latin america could be beneficial to both sides. while the global economic and financial crisis has hit european economies hard, it has had a lesser impact on latin america, where growth prospects for 2012 are even around 4,5%. the eu's cooperation with latin america, including through association agreements and specific development aid, must be the basis for consolidating its rule of law and taking concrete action to support the 180 million people on the south american continent who still live below the poverty line.
in writing. the partnership between the european union and latin america has always been very strong, both from the cultural and commercial point of view. the union is the main donor of development aid and investor in the area. i voted in favour of the report on development cooperation with latin america because it deals with issues of importance for future cooperation between the european union and latin america in a precise and timely manner. in this period of economic crisis, the relationship that already exists between the eu and latin america must be strengthened. food crises, climate change and social problems are common challenges in these two areas. the successful resolution of the above issues will depend very much on the relationship of cooperation that will be established in the coming years. multilateralism and the strengthening of cooperation are two paths which must be pursued with determination. cooperation and collaboration with latin america, with targeted aid tailored to the specific situation and needs of each country, is not just about moving towards the millennium development goals (mdgs). this cooperation will also help to combat poverty and inequalities and stimulate economic development in the area.
in writing. − the principles of the universality and indivisibility of human rights, respect for human dignity and the principles of equality and solidarity enshrined in the lisbon treaty aim at eradicating poverty as well as increasing international relations and partnerships. fundamental in this respect, at a time of deep crisis in the european union as a whole, is the relationship between the european union and latin america, where, despite 180 million people living below the poverty line, gdp growth is forecast to be 4.5% for 2012. the eu is the largest donor of development aid and the largest investor in the latin american region, as well as its second largest trading partner. the vote in favour supports the continuation and increase of aid to latin america, ensuring that the current commitment to allocate 20% of aid to the crucial sectors of education, training and public health is maintained through the proposal for the next cooperation and development plan, without penalising those who are already falling into severe poverty as a result of the economic crisis, and thus guaranteeing the opportunity for millions of children to grow up, develop their skills and improve their living conditions.
in writing. - i support the report by mr scurria, which seeks to ensure that volunteering can develop at european level in new and better structured ways. the objectives are ambitious but very useful. especially at this stage in european history, it is necessary to promote cooperation between the eu member states and the organisations operating in them, to remove the bureaucratic constraints that often prevent access to certain activities and to recognise the skills that are effectively acquired through voluntary activities. the project aims in particular at the creation of a european voluntary corps and a european skills passport. the first would train volunteers and then coordinate them, for example by sending them to various countries to assist local groups in response to natural disasters. the second will be developed on the existing europass model.
in writing. - i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr marco scurria, on his excellent work. the report tackles a broad and complex topic the role, meaning and future of volunteering in europe from a comprehensive and ambitious perspective. with a few reservations, such as that concerning paragraph 9 of the rules of procedure, i think that the report should be approved because of its value as a principle and because of a number of points and points of emphasis which it contains and which deserve attention and practical follow-up. among the many, i would like to mention the request for recognition of the passport of competence as a certification of voluntary activities. volunteering is already an important element in the welfare and personal services system, from a subsidiarity and sustainability perspective, and the state apparatus will only be able to provide it to an increasingly reduced extent. volunteering therefore acquires a pedagogical value which is indispensable for a full and conscious contemporary citizenship. it is important to encourage their transnational mobility as a pedagogical tool in general and in particular as a preparatory experience for knowledge and integration into an increasingly continental labour market. finally, i believe that greater mobility in volunteering also means more healthy competition, more comparison and more supply not only between ngos but also in the comparison of the ways in which member states are making the most of these civil society resources.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr scurria's report on a sector which, although it affects 100 million citizens and 5% of gdp, was until last year hardly regulated at european level and therefore needed more regulation. sport, environmental protection, emergency prevention and management, and the protection of artistic and cultural heritage are areas where volunteering is essential. the commission's 'communication on eu policies and volunteering: recognising and promoting crossborder volunteering in the eu' was a good starting point for the document we have adopted today, which highlights the role of volunteering within the union. the report envisages the establishment of several positive tools, including a portal to inform citizens about the opportunities for volunteering in the various member states and how to participate, a european skills passport allowing for the official recognition of skills acquired through volunteering, a measurement of volunteering on the basis of ilo and un handbooks, in order to have comparable statistics and data that provide a clear picture of the significant contribution of volunteering and the needs of volunteers across the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr marco scurria on crossborder volunteering in the eu. after the visibility gained with the european year of volunteering, it is appropriate to concentrate its actions towards concrete measures for further promotion of the activity. the creation of a 'european voluntary humanitarian aid corps' to train people who are primarily engaged in crossborder volunteering makes an invaluable and absolutely necessary contribution to society, showing the need to build a europe which is to be modelled around respect for fundamental rights and the creation of solidarity and well-being not only within national borders and not only from an economic point of view. in a society as rapidly changing as the european one, the promotion of solidarity is a valuable element; the european commission has published a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which aims to promote the development of a european approach to the problem of climate change. today the european union has 100 million volunteers helping to improve europe and the world, and i am sure that this number is set to increase significantly.
in writing. - i also support the intention, expressed in this report, of promoting and developing voluntary work on the one hand and, on the other, of encouraging the recognition of the informal skills acquired through it, by means of the creation of a european skills passport. i also think that the report analyses both the positive aspects and the critical aspects of the current situation in volunteering and proposes good solutions. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - as was also the case during the recent earthquakes in northern italy, the work of volunteers makes a fundamental and irreplaceable contribution. the voluntary sector has a european dimension. in fact, some 100 million european citizens participate in the various activities of volunteering. it is important that the european union should contribute to encouraging and strengthening crossborder volunteering, which is an important tool for improving social cohesion, for strengthening integration and solidarity, and for building european identity. parliament called in particular for the removal of bureaucratic obstacles and for the recognition of the professional skills acquired by volunteers in the course of their work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, because i believe that it sets important objectives for volunteering. although it accounts for 5% of european gdp and affects some 100 million people in the eu, it has not yet been regulated at european level. volunteering is a valuable activity from both a human and social point of view and an economic one, since it is an integral part of the welfare policies of individual countries. in this context, transnational regulation of this activity is highly desirable. i think it is also worth highlighting the positive effect that volunteering has on young europeans, especially in terms of professional and personal growth, opening up the frontiers of the generations that are called upon to lead europe in the years ahead.
in writing. − in the light of the many initiatives and debates held in the context of the 2011 european year of volunteering, it has become clear that volunteering activities are an expression of active citizenship in all areas of social life and are a key activity for the development of democratic values, human dignity, equality and subsidiarity. the figures speak for themselves: some 100 million european citizens are involved in various voluntary activities and contribute to the production of 5% of european gdp. we are convinced that crossborder volunteering represents a unique and unmissable opportunity for intercultural enrichment for our young european citizens. we therefore have a duty to support all kinds of initiatives which involve an increasing number of european countries in the joint organisation of events. unfortunately, we find that problems still persist in this area, due to linguistic and bureaucratic barriers, which can be reduced by appropriate european support policies. we must therefore commit ourselves to doing more and better. among the concrete measures we support the idea of establishing a centralised eu portal on volunteering with a dedicated section on cross-border volunteering, creating a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps and developing a european skills passport.

in writing. − volunteering is a fundamental resource of our society: there are about 100 million volunteers in europe, who also contribute to the achievement of 5% of european gdp. it is therefore clear that it is important to encourage and promote the development of this culture, which places availability and generosity towards others at its centre. the report supports the need to coordinate these activities, including through the creation of cross-border exchanges, and evaluates the establishment of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps, to be used in particular in cases of natural disasters and major events. the development of a european skills passport can also be useful, as it provides a guarantee of the professionalism and competence of those who work as volunteers. for all these reasons, and in view of the enormous and valuable service that volunteers of all ages perform on a daily basis, i have decided to support this proposal, hoping that it will serve to give a further boost to this vital sector.

in writing. − with today's vote, the european parliament has once again fully recognised the importance of volunteering in terms of cross-cultural enrichment, social inclusion and active citizenship. i believe that europe has a duty to promote and enhance this activity among our citizens. i would like to stress, in the context of social capital creation and crossborder development, that the promotion of volunteering is a valuable opportunity for the european union to affirm and achieve the solidarity and socioeconomic cohesion which inspire our founding principles. to this end, i support the creation of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps and the provision of instruments to enable the training acquired to be more widely recognised for professional purposes.
in writing. - today at the plenary session in strasbourg we voted on mr scurria's report. the resolution was intended to highlight the role of volunteering in the european union. the formal recognition of skills acquired during volunteering activities can add value to a cv and should facilitate young people's career choices and job search. the skills passport could thus become an essential tool in europeans' career or training path. the committee also urges national, regional and local authorities to ensure stable funding and provide tax incentives for voluntary organisations. the aim is to give priority to small organisations with limited budgets and to cross-border volunteering activities by facilitating access to european programmes and funding. in addition, the creation of a centralised european portal can help voluntary organisations to disseminate information, improve cooperation and exchange best practices and experiences.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on crossborder volunteering activities, presented on the eve of the conclusion of the european year of voluntary service. i believe that it fills the existing regulatory gap and represents a step forward compared to the present situation. this report sets out the necessary objectives, such as removing barriers to volunteers and thus allowing them greater and easier mobility or deepening the knowledge of volunteering in areas such as cultural heritage, sport and health. voluntary activities, which account for 5% of european gdp, ensure a better quality of life for our citizens, represent a huge added value and allow for the training of young people to be increased, so that they can look to a better future in work. today, 100 million european citizens are involved in voluntary activities, a fundamental expression of active citizenship and an inexhaustible source of learning and personal growth. voluntary activities, however, involve costs, even if they are not paid, and there is therefore a need for a tax exemption. the scurria report promotes high-quality volunteering, both nationally and across borders, and makes important proposals such as the creation of a european humanitarian aid unit and the introduction of a european skills passport.
in writing. − volunteering is an expression of active citizenship in all areas of an individual's life and acts as a catalyst for social change as well as a tool for raising awareness in society and for personal development. there are so many natural and environmental disasters that affect the european union and so many volunteers who come from all over the union to provide their help, labour and solidarity, regardless of the linguistic and bureaucratic barriers that exist in the union's multifaceted territory. in particular, cross-border volunteering is an opportunity for intercultural enrichment for young european citizens. the vote in favour supported the idea of establishing a centralised eu portal on volunteering with a dedicated section on cross-border volunteering, the creation of a european voluntary humanitarian aid corps to select, train and deploy volunteers where necessary, and the creation of a european skills passport to ensure the recognition at european level of professional qualifications acquired through volunteering.

in writing. − technology is playing an increasingly important role in all daily activities, from communication to financial and banking activities, from transport to energy, from culture to health. in view of the increasing use of the internet and information technology, internet security has become one of the most important policy priorities for the european union. the europe 2020 strategy, launched in 2010, has included the eu digital agenda as one of its flagship policies, setting ambitious targets for the european union's technological development. i agree with the rapporteur that the spread of innovative technologies depends on a number of crucial aspects: safety, resilience and reliability. i also believe that the potential for internet damage could result in substantial losses and security risks that could have a negative impact on a large number of european citizens and businesses. i therefore draw the commission's attention to the need to continue improving cybersecurity in the european union, including through an efficient system of international cooperation between states and transparent international standards. in this context, it is essential to ensure effective interaction between governments, business, civil society and all the actors concerned.
in writing. - i have supported the report by mr kalfin because i believe it is of the utmost importance to support and develop the eu initiative on critical information infrastructure protection (ciip), which aims to strengthen the current security system of information and communication technology structures at national and european level, by defining guidelines and with the support of enisa (european network and information security agency). in today's world, the interdependence and interconnectedness of the socioeconomic fabric is increasingly dependent on technologies and the internet, which must be secure and reliable. protecting the global network is necessary and the most effective way to do this is to ensure efficient interaction between governments, businesses, individuals and stakeholders. only an efficient system of international cooperation will achieve this effectively.
in writing. − in 2007, estonia was crippled by a massive cyber attack. in 2008, the us department of defense reported over 50,000 attacks. the list of attacks compiled by the csis study centre shows that, as far as europe is concerned, in 2011 alone, the british ministry of defence, the bbc, the norwegian national security agency, a major dutch certification body, the german federal police, the eu carbon trading market and the french public administration in the vicinity of the g20 were affected, among others. italian scholar stefano mele recently summarized the impact, including on human lives, of possible attacks on critical transport, energy, water and security infrastructure. not to mention the silent toll that cybercrime takes on private companies alone, which is about 20 billion dollars a year. the report addresses the concerns of this scenario, providing timely indications and suggesting measures to be implemented in the short term, including with regard to the defence of our economies, freedoms and citizens' rights, in particular paragraphs 10, 20, 32, 38 and 39. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − according to recent estimates, it has been calculated that 73.8% of the population in the most developed countries access the internet regularly. you have to start with data like this to understand the role of the internet in everyday life. but there is another significant statistic, which says that approximately one million people a day are victims of online crime. the scale of these figures requires strong initiatives to improve user safety. with the report adopted today, the european parliament is calling for a regulatory framework to be put in place to simplify interaction and exchange of information between governments. the commission also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the risks arising from the use of radioactive substances. the european union has been working for years to make online activities safer, and today's report is a further step towards making the internet safer.
in writing. - the current economic and commercial environment sees the internet as the protagonist of economic activities and practices which, until a few decades ago, existed in different forms and instruments. with the internet becoming a major part of everyday life, from commerce to personal use, from accessing public administration data to storing one's own data, it is becoming ever more necessary to strengthen its structure and protect its users. this is why i support the implementation of ciip (critical information infrastructure protection) and all policies to ensure greater security and confidentiality of sensitive data circulating on the network, so as to make it a virtual place where you can increasingly act with real-world safeguards.
in writing. − technology is playing an increasingly important role in all our daily activities, from communication to finance and banking, from transport to energy, from culture to entertainment and health. the increasingly widespread use of the internet and information technology makes cybersecurity one of the most important policy priorities for the european union and the rest of the world. the increasing use and diffusion of innovative technologies depends on critical aspects such as safety, resilience and reliability. all the latest regulatory interventions by the european commission do not exhaust the efforts to improve the security of cyberspace in the union. we agree with the rapporteur on this point. the rapid development of technology requires that the prevention of attacks on the internet, remedial actions and the resilience of the global network are based on a broad, responsive, flexible, innovative and long-lasting framework. this framework must necessarily ensure efficient interaction between governments, businesses, individuals and all other stakeholders. the european union is also called upon to play its part. it should be considered that improving the resilience of the internet can only be achieved when there is an efficient system of international cooperation and standards.
in writing. − i fully share the call on member states to develop national contingency plans in the event of cyber incidents and to provide for key elements such as relevant contact points, the provision of assistance, containment and repair in the event of cyber disruption or attacks of regional, national or cross-border scope. i believe it is also very important to encourage coordination measures at national level to ensure better coordination between the competent national authorities and to make their actions more consistent. my vote is in favour.

in writing. − europe is one of the largest energy buyers on global markets. i believe that in the framework of the definition of european energy policy, we must work towards a common approach extending our sphere of influence beyond the mere frontiers of europe and, in particular, in the field of energy market rules. we need a functioning internal market which will create more competition between our external partners. in my view, also in the light of the current union objectives set out in the 20-20-20 climate-energy package, it is crucial to ensure reliable and competitively priced access to global energy supplies to support europe's competitiveness and security of energy supply. a coherent and coordinated approach by the member states, the commission and the council can allow for effective promotion of the union's energy objectives outside the union and a better contractual position vis-à-vis third countries. in this context, research, development and innovation are of strategic importance: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. the report is very much in line with the commission's approach. i am voting in favour of this approach, which, by presenting a wide range of content and analytical forecasts, is firmly anchored in the principle of a common policy based on energy solidarity and cooperation as a strategy for promoting the values of political stability and global security. while it is appropriate to find ways of involving the eu more closely in negotiations between member states and third countries, it is also dramatically urgent, in a global and sensitive market such as this, to define solid guidelines in relation to key countries in terms of supply and demand, represented by the brics or, to keep even closer, by turkey as a strategic hub, especially in relation to technological and market developments which have already fully invested in the clean coal and lng sectors. finally, i would like to emphasize, as the reason for my vote in favour, the courageous positions set out in paragraphs 86 and 106, which are the hallmark of the eu's commitment to promoting universal values and human rights, beyond the contingencies and purely important assessments of a strictly economic nature.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs herczog's report because i share her call for greater security of energy supply. the european economy relies largely on imports of energy and raw materials from third countries, which makes it vulnerable to the high risks inherent in this system. the diversification of the energy mix to increase the share of renewables in it, while a valid alternative, cannot in itself be a satisfactory solution to the problem. i am therefore convinced that the european union must strengthen its negotiating position through greater coordination between member states, an increase in the number of suppliers and greater collaboration between the public and private sectors, in order to make imports more stable and less susceptible to the shifting political balances that have often put them at risk. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union.
in writing. − the lack of a common energy policy has been hurting the european union for years: we spend over 400 billion euros a year importing energy produced by others. it is clear that strong measures are needed. while respecting national specificities, it is important that coordination between member states is increased so that the european union can speak with one voice towards international suppliers, thereby increasing its negotiating weight. at the same time, it is necessary to diversify energy supply routes and increase information sharing. the creation of a coordinated energy policy at european level is the key to ensuring that european citizens enjoy a reliable and competitive energy policy.
in writing. - the report by mr herczog, for which i voted in favour, has the advantage of highlighting certain specific features of energy policies and relations with non-european partners on this subject. particular attention is paid to the issue of safety. this is of particular significance in the light of changes and developments in the supply of energy sources. the same applies to environmental safety, which is a subject that requires increasing attention. the points of interest are those relating to the idea of cooperation and communion which emerge from the first articles of the text and which fully reflect the spirit of the european union.
in writing. − it is essential that the european union recognises the security and development of internal fossil fuel resources as a priority, particularly in relation to the significant reserves recently discovered in the mediterranean sea, which could reduce europe's dependence on energy imports. i agree with the rapporteur that energy policy must be an integral and important part of the common foreign policy and that it should be developed and implemented in synergy with other policies which have an external dimension.
in writing. the common energy policy is the future we all want for europe. unfortunately, our energy efficiency depends on other countries, the eu imports some 400 billion energy products a year, which is why it needs a policy of energy cooperation with third countries. the text voted in parliament aims to ensure a secure, sustainable and competitive energy supply. in addition, the partnership offers the possibility to develop, together with countries outside the eu, new projects for the union's energy policies, from sustainability to efficiency to clean energy. another objective is a common energy policy, which goes beyond the interests of individual member states to ensure the common european need for common access routes to energy infrastructure corridors.
in writing. − the european union is one of the world's largest energy importers. i therefore believe that by coordinating the different negotiating positions with third countries it could increase its bargaining power as the largest applicant. a common approach is therefore needed, extending the sphere of influence beyond european borders, especially in the energy market. the european union needs a market in this area which is able to create competition between external partners and which can promote convergence with neighbouring countries.
in writing. - having participated in the working groups which, under the leadership of the previous president of the european parliament, mr buzek, were concerned with laying the foundations for a common energy policy, i can only support this own-initiative report on cooperation in the field of energy policies. if the european union could coordinate and represent the purchase of energy, including oil and gas, with third countries, it could obtain much more favourable economic conditions and greater guarantees of supply. the important point is that the choice to give the eu this role must be made autonomously by the member states, which, under the treaty, have full competence over energy supply. ensuring reliable and competitive access to energy supplies is essential for european competitiveness and for maintaining an optimal contractual position vis-à-vis third countries.
in writing. − the issue of energy security is of fundamental importance in the policies of the european union. europe spends over 400 billion euros on energy imports each year, which makes it highly dependent on third countries. coordination between member states, diversification of energy suppliers, routes and sources, extension of the european sphere of influence beyond borders, sharing of information on energy data and projects in third countries and partnership with suppliers and international organisations are the cornerstones on which the new european energy policy will have to be based. by putting these guidelines into practice and by following the european union's lead in energy efficiency and the development of new forms of energy, we will be able to achieve a secure, sustainable and competitive energy policy. the work to be done to achieve a genuine common energy policy is still long, but there is no doubt that parliament intends to move decisively in this direction.
in writing. - energy, a common good of the citizens of the union and beyond, has become a means of instrumentalising foreign policy in the last decade. europe's submission to global markets for its energy supply puts europe in a weak position but at the same time gives it bargaining power. if the whole union used this role in a coordinated way and took a firm and common negotiating position with third countries, it would almost always have good bargaining power on the demand side. the vote in favour underlines the importance of defining a common approach in conduct and dialogue with cross-border countries, not only in competition matters but also in promoting regulatory convergence with neighbouring countries that is consistent with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the european union spends more than €400 billion on energy imports each year, which shows how important the issue of energy security is on the european agenda. the key elements on which european energy policy will have to be based, in addition to what has already been done on energy efficiency and renewable sources, are increased coordination between member states, diversification of suppliers and the sharing of information on energy sources and projects in third countries.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, mrs ashton, there is no doubt that this appointment is of extraordinary importance and that the european union, in order to be even more concrete, more authoritative and more charismatic, must take care of the weak and the vulnerable. there is no doubt that the appointment of a special representative for human rights is a very valuable thing. i would like to congratulate president salafranca on his excellent work. solidarity, responsibility and cooperation: we need to ensure that member states who develop these activities are consistently supported and we also need to have a positive con dition towards third countries which show great interest and attention in the protection of fundamental rights. this is the case with regard to the profile of trade relations. as regards immigration, we still have a number of unresolved issues concerning the protection of the fundamental rights of those who flee because they see their interests and needs trampled on in their own territory. they too will need to be treated with great respect. these are natural rights, rights which pre-exist in man and which are closely linked to the expansion of each individual's personality. the european union must therefore ensure that this role is fulfilled to the best of its ability, and the person chosen must meet two requirements: he's going to have to be a charismatic person and a courageous person who believes to the core in the role he's going to be given.
madam president, the international community devotes a great amount of time and resources to the issue of weapons of mass destruction that have a very small chance of being used. countries are invaded and wars are fought for a threat that is largely improbable. at the same time, conventional weapons and small arms kill tens of thousands of people every year and this issue is almost unnoticed. so this arms trade treaty is welcome. the socialists and democrats regret that the eu member states continue to sell large amounts of weapons to dictatorships, authoritarian regimes and countries whose leaders use weapons to suppress dissent. the same member states, on the other hand, declare their support for democracy and human rights every day. but the conventional weapons and small arms often sold by them are the material instrument of the most blatant crimes. these small arms and weapons have been extensively used in egypt, tunisia and libya against peaceful demonstrators. so, any instrument like this treaty that goes in the direction of resolving these inacceptable paradoxes and contradictions is welcomed by us.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, baroness ashton, it is not enough for those with political and institutional responsibilities to express their indignation, as is rightly the case, at the horrors of syria, and i think you are aware of that. what is happening outside this house requires adequate response capacity, and frankly, i do not think that the european union's response capacity is up to the challenges we face. how long are we going to watch the carnage in syria? the difficulties arising from the fragile balance in the region are understandable. the position of russia and china, which do not allow for a more decisive initiative by the united nations, can be understood and not shared. the european union is also prepared to take action to help the syrian opposition, which is facing a serious crisis. but what is happening is no longer tolerable. the european union must move from its current activism to greater prominence. we must defeat the argument that the assad regime can do anything because the international community is powerless and because the european union, which is in the midst of an economic and financial crisis, cannot afford to intervene in the syrian situation. the decision to build a humanitarian corridor has not been implemented. but i think we have to start from there, accompanying this decision with all the instruments, no one excluded and i emphasize no one excluded , because this is an essential condition to start the process of transition and transfer of power. i think that we must move from words to deeds, and that is a task which objectively falls to you.
mr president, can i say to mrs ashton that i largely share her view of the syria crisis and i share in particular her stress on the annan plan as the only viable solution on the ground for this crisis. i do not agree with those colleagues who dismiss this plan so easily in just a few words. if anyone has any better ideas to lay down in an intractable crisis like the syrian one, then please do tell us what should be done. i also do not agree with colleagues who very superficially ask for military intervention – a sort of second libya solution with nato intervention and so on – in a completely different situation, after the disasters we have just suffered and are still suffering due to this kind of solution. the libyan crisis was a typical crisis that can only be solved through international intervention, with the blue helmets and with a large mandate to separate parties and to stop violence that comes mostly from tyrannical governments that will one day have to answer for these crimes to the international courts. in tandem with this, we have violence by rebels using heavy armaments who are funded by foreign countries and who are armed through covert operations. we do not know enough about this and we are not speaking enough about this component. this is a fourth reason why the only solution is the one that mrs ashton outlined.
in writing. many are hoping for a new role for european policy on the israeli-palestinian conflict. we all want europe to promote peace initiatives more effectively than it has done so far and to play a more appropriate political role in relation to our financial commitment in the area. to achieve this, in such a complicated and difficult situation, the european union must be credible to both sides and perceived as equally divided. both the palestinians and the israelis must be convinced that the union has no other interest than peace, without prejudice to anyone. do we really think that the european union can be considered a credible partner for israel in the light of the recent positions adopted by the foreign affairs council last may which totally ignore the legitimate security demands of israel, which is in fact surrounded by hostile countries? at a time when the hopes raised by the arab spring are being dashed and we are seeing islamic extremism prevail in the maghreb countries, what security guarantees can the eventual new palestinian state, which we all hope for, give?

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, although our budget is limited, the budget for one year amounts to what can be burned in one day by the markets. the mff is very important, but on the condition that the member states do not see the budget as a source of expenditure to be cut, like all public spending, but as a resource that can help the economy to grow, that is, an investment, not as a cost to the citizens but as a way of producing tangible results. the figures are programmes, projects, things to be done. so no short-sighted cuts, no fighting between countries, because growth is a common opportunity for all european citizens. the european budget should not be seen as a separate budget but as a complement to national budgets. a new approach is needed to strengthen the link between the european budget and national budgets. in some ways, ours is the 28th budget of the same european countries. only then can we create the global mass that can develop effective policies. what we are asking for is a more coordinated approach. the european semester can also serve this purpose. finally, as regards the role of parliament - and i say this to the council - we will not accept facts or take or leave, but we want a preliminary comparison before the formal proposal for approval. we are the voice of the citizens, of those citizens who are concerned about the future of europe, and we want to be involved in the decisions as their representatives.

ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to express my pleasure at being here, at the seat of the european parliament, which is the expression of a melting pot of diverse communities and cultures that make up this europe with which peru has deep ties. peru, a multilingual and multicultural country with a thousand-year history, has been involved in an intercultural dialogue with european traditions since the 16th century. i would like to highlight the contribution of distinguished europeans to peruvian causes and issues, such as the italian scholar antonio raimondi, the french admiral petit-thouars, the german scientist alexander von humboldt and the german researcher maria reiche, to name just a few of the europeans who stood for peru and the strong link between our country and the european continent, a task that endures over time and we value in its real dimension. the european union is currently peru's second most important trading partner, the main destination for our exports and with significant investments in peru. in this century, marked by an increasing process of globalisation of resources, goods and services and by a breakneck speed in the development of new technologies, peru and the european union have a common destiny and challenge to advance on the path of cooperation through the recognition of their own values, identities and projects, which, at the same time, are common in their ideals. peru is a representative democracy whose macroeconomic policies, together with the stable legal framework, have resulted in sustained economic growth and a fairly remarkable social outcome in terms of poverty reduction, reduction of inequality, higher employment rates and the achievement of the millennium development goals in general. our gross domestic product has tripled in the last decade, with growth forecast to be close to 6% this year, and we aim to maintain that growth over the next five years, despite the complicated international environment. several studies agree that this trend will continue in the coming years. this makes peru one of the major regional economies. in this context, my government has set as a priority objective social inclusion, which will come with economic growth, so that the benefits that peru has brought, its good business climate, commercial openness and investments extend to all sectors of peruvian society, in particular the poorest in our country. we need to bring the most disadvantaged into the economic circuit of wealth creation and decent employment through modernising and diversifying our production, encouraging local innovation and tapping into the development of knowledge, supporting our population to build skills and giving them the tools to be more competitive. my government intends to consolidate democracy in a way that is capable of solving the problems and needs of peruvian society as a whole but, very especially, that of the minorities of those who have been postponed and forgotten by the state. let us be clear: there can be no development and no democracy in an economy that generates inequality, poverty and exclusion. the great transformation that my government is determined to achieve is based on the process of social inclusion, that was our main commitment to the peruvian people. that is, transforming economic growth into development and well-being, transforming wealth into quality of life. peru is a country of just over 29 million inhabitants. it has already succeeded in reducing poverty from 54% in 2001 to 27% in 2012. my government has set itself the goal of lifting more than 3 million peruvians out of poverty by 2016, that is, to have a poverty rate below 20%, and to reduce as much as possible the rate of extreme poverty, which today is around 7% in peru. to this end, my government is committed to a proactive public policy of development and social investment. therefore, despite the fact that the millennium development goals have been exceeded, we continue to make greater efforts to continue reducing inequality gaps. the budget allocated to social and human capital in 2012 has thus increased by 20% compared to 2011. social inclusion allows for the transformation of the human being into a citizen and, to carry out these tasks, we have created the ministry of development and social inclusion. through this we seek to transform social programs into a unique social inclusion policy for our government where obviously we will create a set of programs of a multisectoral nature with a view to improving efficiency and focusing attention on the most needy. in this context, a series of social programmes have been developed, ranging from early childhood (the cuna más programme), through the youth population (the beca 18 programme), to the retirement stage (the pensión 65 programme), in addition to the expansion of the juntos programme of conditional transfers for the most vulnerable families and the mobile emergency assistance system (samu). cuna más is the programme for children, which has already begun to be implemented. this year it will serve more than 90 000 children aged up to three in the poorest areas of the country, providing them with food and daycare services, educational components and comprehensive health care. the 18th scholarship programme will facilitate higher education for qualified and disadvantaged young people. it is aimed at capacity building and the appropriate assimilation of science and technology transfers to diversify our productive matrix. the target for our first year of government is 5,000 fellows and 3,000 scholarships abroad in master's and doctoral degrees. the pension 65 programme provides financial support to adults over 65 who are living in poverty or extreme poverty. in this programme, my government has approved the first list of beneficiaries, comprising 126 787 adults in over 14 regions of the country. my government plans to allocate this year over 790 million dollars for social programs implemented by this ministry. other programs are the cooperation fund for social development, which promotes productive local development, and the qali warma (vigorous child in quechua) food program, which will have as its main objective to ensure food service for children in public educational institutions of initial level from 3 years of age. the increase in the efficiency and coverage of the juntos programme is essential, as it is a programme that provides direct financial incentives to households in poverty and extreme poverty, subject to the fulfilment of the commitments assumed by the mothers representing the household to care for their minor children in health and education establishments. we've expanded this program from 350,000 to 450,000 families this year. in this context, the peruvian state is making efforts to include all sectors of society in the benefits that will be brought by the trade agreement with the european union. the agreement presents an important opportunity for small, micro and medium-sized enterprises from both sides, from the european union and from peru. in peru, these types of enterprises represent 98% of all enterprises, employ 75% of the economically active population and generate 42% of the national gross domestic product. in addition to economic growth with social inclusion, a second axis i would like to highlight is the sustainable development of our natural resources and the promotion of responsible mining. the fundamental interest of my government is to promote a responsible policy in the use of our natural resources, and in particular water resources, aimed at solving the just concerns and demands which the population has expressed in various ways because of the fear generated by the implementation of certain mining projects. today we have been working on building a new relationship between the state and the mines. this new relationship will allow us to include the communities, to include the peoples of the area of mining influence, and will allow us to address the legitimate uncertainties and doubts that the population living in the area may have in a transparent, participatory way, using dialogue as the main instrument for conflict resolution, as well as strengthening our environmental policy and sustainable development, for which the ministry of the environment has been created. peru in particular and latin america in general have concrete challenges to ensure social and environmental sustainability in their development model. among the most important challenges are the change in production and consumption patterns, the promotion of business agriculture and a peasant economy that adapts to climate change, an integrated management of natural resources and water resources, a land-use planning policy that ensures the security and integrity of indigenous peoples and communities in harmony with protected natural areas, as well as the promotion and development of clean technologies that adapt to the needs of each of the many ecological floors we have. my country has ratified the main international environmental conventions. as a mega-biodiverse country and highly vulnerable to climate change, it gives high priority to policies for climate change mitigation and adaptation, conservation and sustainable use of the amazon forest and protection of biodiversity. finally, in addition to being a full member of the convention on biological diversity and having ratified the cartagena protocol on biosafety, we have signed - and are in the process of legislative approval - the nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources and have recently passed a law establishing a ten-year moratorium on the introduction and production of living modified organisms for cultivation and breeding purposes, based on the precautionary principle of protecting human, animal and plant health and the environment. however, peru is particularly affected by the indecisiveness and non-compliance of the 1992 rio agreements. the industry in peru, including mining, currently operates under a legal framework that protects the environment and includes indigenous communities in decision-making, through the prior consultation mechanism, whose law has been unanimously approved by congress, and i believe - without any doubt - that we are the first country in the world to establish a law of prior consultation with communities. (applause) in this respect, the drafting of its rules of procedure - which have already been promulgated - involved the participation of organised civil society and, in particular, indigenous communities. this will involve indigenous peoples in the evaluation of measures that may affect them. they will be able to voice their concerns and their voice will be heard. this is intended to implement best practices combining prior consultation with the promotion of private investment. on the other hand, we have taken specific measures to increase the share of the state in the revenue generated by the extraction of our mineral resources. in september 2011 a new levy on mining was approved through constructive dialogue with mining companies. these additional resources will be used for infrastructure works in the poorest areas of the country that do not have resources from the mining quota. to strengthen the policy of social inclusion, the government will promote mining or oil investment projects as social inclusion funds, which will be used to develop projects in education, health, sanitation, drinking water, public services, electricity and agricultural infrastructure. we will continue to call on private enterprise to develop human capital in the areas and create jobs for all peruvians. the development of a major mining project can take four or more years, enough time for these companies to set up specialized technical training centres in the project's areas of influence. we also think it is necessary for mining companies to have a guarantee fund which would be triggered when there is any environmental damage. we need to strengthen the corporate social responsibility of all mining and extractive companies that come to my country. respect for and protection of human rights will be a fundamental pillar of the policy of the peruvian state, not only at the domestic level but also in the field of foreign policy. peru is a party to and strictly observes the provisions of the eight major international human rights treaties. my country is currently a member of the united nations human rights council for the period 2011-2014. we are committed to building a culture of peace, not only to ensure that acts of terrorist violence are not repeated, but to initiate a process of confidence building, pacification of the country and consolidation of democracy. thanks to the support of the european union and countries such as germany and sweden, as well as the united nations development programme and the resources allocated by my government, we hope to complete the construction of the 'place of remembrance' museum by the end of this year. peru has also ratified 67 ilo labour conventions. my country remains strongly committed to promoting decent work opportunities in conditions of freedom, security and equality, as well as improving social security, strengthening dialogue and promoting the guarantee of labour rights and freedom of association. the interaction between the state, the committee on freedom of association and the ilo commission on the application of standards is fluid and permanent. i would also like to emphasise that the country has different national mechanisms to ensure implementation, monitoring and inclusive dialogue on such issues, such as the national human rights council, the national labour council and the recently organised economic and social council. with this support we have achieved in the first year an increase in the minimum living wage, a promise we made to the country in the election campaign. the trade agreement with the european union clearly reflects this commitment by containing disciplines developed under a trade and sustainable development approach that reaffirm the core ilo conventions. i would like to emphasise that my government is determined to work in concert with the democratically elected local authorities and civil society institutions. my government is firmly committed to this purpose and has declared a frontal struggle against issues affecting security, such as narcoterrorism and drug trafficking. peru has allocated nearly $100 million of its own resources in 2011 to combat this phenomenon. peru has reduced the growth rate of coca leaf crops by 2.2%, from an average of 5% per year in recent years. on the other hand, peru has been implementing sustainable alternative development programmes which are already benefiting 84 000 families, which has meant expenditures of more than 100 million dollars per year. the concern of peru in the fight against drugs is permanent and we have to work together with the european union. ladies and gentlemen, peru is a country that respects what it signs and maintains legal stability that generates confidence. the agreement concluded between peru and the european union - which is about to be signed - is a fundamental partnership of multiple and reciprocal benefits which will contribute to promoting development with social inclusion, thus projecting us towards the century that is just beginning. this is a good opportunity to express my appreciation and thanks to the european parliament for the adoption of the report on the definition of a new policy of cooperation with latin america. the european parliament, supported by 640 meps, has recognised the need for coordinated cooperation which takes account of the situation in each country and at the same time is based on broader indicators than those measuring income levels. this will contribute, in the case of peru, to the efforts of my government. in conclusion, i should like to say that this process of multilateral agreement began several years ago in the andean community of nations. for various reasons, it has been reduced to two countries: colombia and peru. today is a chance. latin america has a very important economic strengthening, but not everything is perfect. we have our own problems and one of our weaknesses is that we are exporting countries of raw materials. we, the citizens of the latin american region, need to break down this barrier, to stop being primary exporting countries and to start on the path you started decades ago: industrialization, the domination of science and technology. that is why it is important for us that this agreement should ensure that peru has access to technology transfers, fair and reciprocal trade, that we can both use this agreement not for the benefit of economic lobbies but for the benefit of our citizens, that this agreement should be an important step towards the integration of america with europe. and we have to understand that america is not just the united states. america is peru, it's chile, it's colombia, bolivia, ecuador, panama, mexico and so many other countries, and, today, america is fine, it's an investment opportunity. today we express our solidarity with the serious crisis in which the european union is now found. today we say to you that we hope that the cloud that is bathing the skies of europe will not reach latin america. we from our territory blow to prevent that cloud from arriving, but we have done our job. we are prepared to deal with this crisis and that is important; that is, we, in this multi-party agreement, also contribute, we come with our bread under our arm and we want to work in a transparent, open, cooperative and mutually beneficial way, in a way that is beneficial for both sides, the two-way street, not just the one-way street. that is why i have come here today, and it is important to me, because i, like ollanta humala, have always had a critical discourse on free trade agreements. but today, as president for ten months, i have to respect the policies of the state and we have to do it well. that is why i firmly believe that the signing of this agreement will benefit you and it will benefit us. i firmly believe that if we go alone, we may go a little fast, but if we go together, we will go further.
