madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european commission has proposed to review the system of generalised tariff preferences which the union has granted since 1971 to goods entering the european market from developing countries. although the new criteria for preferences will reduce the number of beneficiaries by about half, i believe that the system continues to provide a real opportunity for these countries to increase their international trade, generating revenue to be used for income growth, sustainable development policies and poverty eradication.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we are pleased with the agreement reached in the trilogue on the negotiations for the new gsp regulation, both because of the complexity of the regulation itself and because of the political value and the marked differences which characterized the debate. in the present situation it is essential to ensure that european small and mediumsized enterprises with similar industrial sensibilities, especially in the textile, leather and agricultural sectors, are able to compete on international markets by carefully assessing the various preferential treatment which the union grants to our main partners. we cannot allow countries which have proved to have a competitive economy, such as brazil, russia, argentina, etc., to be helped by tariff reductions to enter european markets to the detriment of our manufacturing sector, which has been suffering for years now from the consequences of the financial crisis and protectionist choices on exports and procurement from the same third countries. we are therefore in favour of greater control over the principle of differentiation, thus avoiding the favouring of countries with offensive interests in strategic european sectors, and we welcome the strengthening of the safeguard clause extended to textiles as well. we also thank the rapporteur for the excellent work he has done.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i certainly appreciate the fact that the number of countries benefiting from this system is being considerably reduced. it is right and proper to support with favourable trade policies only those states which are really in difficulty, and to concentrate on those where our intervention can be most beneficial. however, according to the calculations, pakistan should also be among these new beneficiaries. it is a country with a very developed textile sector, thanks also to the existence of economic and social rules which severely penalise our companies. i come from a town, prato, which was one of the first textile districts in europe and which has suffered badly in recent years from unfair asian competition. i am therefore opposed to this agreement which includes pakistan, as i was opposed to the removal of duties for that country because of the floods in 2010. trade aid must be targeted, but it certainly cannot lead to the death of entire european manufacturing sectors, as might be the case with the further invasion of pakistani textiles.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, with today's vote parliament completes the package on european governance already approved at the end of 2011. the continuing crisis affecting the whole of europe has made it necessary to strengthen the economic and budgetary surveillance of those member states which see their financial stability in the euro area at risk, effectively giving the union's supervisory bodies the power to intervene if necessary with the appropriate preventive tools.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this legislative proposal raises questions because it would give the commission greater powers of control over the fiscal policies of the eurozone countries but without any counterpart for greater democratic control. greater powers mean less sovereignty for the states, and that is fine, but not without transferring control to parliament. the democratic deficit will increase if parliament does not have a stronger role. the second reason for concern is the budget cuts and the policy of strict austerity imposed by the executive, with no proposals for investment in growth and development except for the amendments which fortunately passed in this house. we have seen that policy has failed so far: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of unemployment. to continue in this direction would be unreasonable and masochistic. let us take the delors white paper as an example. it was 1993, 19 years later, and we're even worse than before.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because i think it is important that parliament should express its respect for a document which i hope will also be brought to the attention of governments at the next important meeting on 28 and 29 june. with the vote on the gauzès report we said as a european parliament that it is not possible to accept ever stricter control rules without a balance of power in the direction of democratic participation. parliament must be there. it is important and desirable to strengthen the link between surveillance and the conditionality of financial assistance programmes, but it is equally important that the conditions for this should be established together with those who represent the european people.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am making a joint declaration of vote, including mr ferreira's report, because i believe that the time has come to overcome the contradiction between growth and rigor, which is in danger of becoming stagnant. we have actually made a statement today in favour of growth and at the same time in favour of recovery. it is a contradiction when we say that we do not want to approve a report such as that of mr gauzès - on which i have abstained for the reasons i shall give - and at the same time we call for a consolidated budget, a european budget, a fiscal union. we need fiscal union, we need to monitor the budgets of the member states and at the same time encourage growth, also with the amendments we tabled and voted for in mr ferreira's report. so i think we did something important. we have done so even though there is a chapter in mr gauzès' report, chapter 10, which is a negative message to the markets, because it concerns controlled default procedures, which we do not even have to communicate at the moment, because we have to communicate to european public opinion that we want to go ahead with the euro and that we want to go ahead with greater integration.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i too voted in favour of this document and the other two-pack documents because i believe that they can be an important element for stability and at the same time for growth. we do not think that these measures alone will be enough. we believe that it is useful, however, that at a time of serious crisis such as the one the european union is going through, parliament should take on an even more courageous role than it has so far played, just as we believe that development, employment and the labour market go hand in hand with a mechanism for verifying the budgetary policies of each member state, because rigor is extremely important. the european debt reimbursement fund is one instrument that can be useful, as is the one concerning the coordinated annual framework for the issuance of public debt. the role of the european investment bank is greater in achieving the budgetary, political and fiscal union which is the essential port of call for the growth and development opportunities we feel and fully appreciate the need for at this stage.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report, unlike mr pieper and for exactly the opposite reasons. with the two proposals for regulations which were tabled last november, the commission said that if we are to achieve real risk sharing, we must first ensure greater responsibility sharing. the vote we have taken in this house on mr ferreira's report, and in particular on the amendments with which we have begun to pave the way for the redemption fund, project bonds and the scrapping of investments, has reiterated the same concept by simply reversing the order of the factors. if you want more responsibility sharing, you have to share the risks. in other words, if we want stronger governance and budgetary surveillance, we must also introduce forms of joint issuance of public debt and share the risk.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal to establish a special representative for human rights is a result of the treaty and a series of requests from parliament. although the appointment is made by the council on a proposal from the high representative, it is essential that parliament and the commission also have a say. he also asked to be allowed to intervene in the election procedure and to have responsibility for monitoring his work by means of hearings before the committee responsible. the human rights officer should provide an annual report on his or her activities to the council, the commission and parliament. i hope, however, that the new body which will be set up will be able to separate the protection of human rights from financial interests, because i do not think it acceptable, for example, that many states are too tolerant of china's violation of human rights in tibet simply because china is an economic power.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union has always implemented all international agreements on the arms trade. i believe that the sector should be regulated by providing operators with a clear and common regulatory framework. it is also important and necessary to distinguish between weapons for military use or possible military use, which should be regulated separately, and weapons for sport or recreation. if these efforts are not supported, the european manufacturing sector, in particular civil and sporting arms, will be penalized. once again europe is in danger of failing to protect our small and mediumsized enterprises which export weapons all over the world and which could be unilaterally subjected to greater restrictions by legislation which tends to put a sporting weapon on the same level as a tank. fortunately, this morning an amendment by a political group was rejected which proposed a ban on the export of all types of arms, without any consideration of the damage that such a choice would cause to our economy.
in writing. − despite her young age, ms ivanova has gained professional experience in banks, multinationals and the bulgarian government, which has allowed her to acquire skills in financial management not only in the public sector but also in the private sector. in view of your background and your commitment as vice-chairman of the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, i consider you to be a suitable candidate for appointment as a new member of the court of auditors.
in writing. - the united nations is by its very nature subject to scrutiny, sometimes tainted by partisanship or political prejudice. however, it is impossible to dismiss the recurring problems of legitimacy and adequacy in the light of the proven instances of maladministration and the history of lack of response to global challenges and the need for consistency with universal values such as peace and civil, religious and economic freedoms. in direct terms, the report addresses these two nodes, building on the shared assumption that a strengthened partnership with the eu can strengthen the un in a wide range of activities, such as cooperation, conflict prevention, peace-keeping, and the promotion of governance models that, while preserving diverse cultural traditions, respect human and civil rights, with positive effects on global stabilisation. despite the difficulties in the process of integration, the eu has a more cohesive profile in terms of its cultural fabric, governance philosophy, core values and strategic interests than the united nations. in this sense, it seems reasonable that the eu, considering its financial and operational contribution to the un, should work towards a more assertive role on the international scene. the report, in its recommendations, therefore meets my favourable opinion.
in writing. − we call on the council to take all possible initiatives to strengthen the coherence and visibility of the european union's action as a global actor at the united nations, and to work closely with the member states to improve coordination, transparency and the exchange of information. the pursuit of effective multilateralism in foreign policy is not only one of our fundamental objectives, but also one of the union's main strategic interests. we therefore need to engage more actively with strategic partners and other bilateral and multilateral partners, in particular the us, in order to promote effective solutions to the problems affecting both european citizens and the world at large, including the poorest and most vulnerable. the operational partnership should therefore be strengthened and strategic coherence and effectiveness for peacebuilding promoted, based on the concept of strengthening the eu's dialogue and mediation capacities. our international efforts must be directed towards ensuring that all human rights, as recognised by our treaties as well as by the un conventions, are considered to be universal, indivisible, interdependent and interrelated.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report. i particularly agree with the need to strengthen international efforts to ensure that all human rights recognized by the un conventions are considered to be universal, indivisible, interdependent and interrelated. we must also help to strengthen national capacities to meet international human rights obligations. finally, it is right to stress the need to guarantee the right to freedom of religion and belief for all.
in writing. − with regard to the proposal for a european parliament recommendation to the council on the priorities of the european union for the 67th session of the united nations general assembly, i consider it necessary to define a comprehensive international framework for the period after 2015, with the following key objectives: enhancing the application of innovative financing mechanisms to achieve climate change objectives, focusing on the assessment of successes and failures against current targets achieved and not achieved; fully pursue the objectives of rio + 20; renew the commitment to food security in member states and to stimulate agricultural production capacity, infrastructure, new enterprises, access to technologies, human and social development in the least developed countries; fully support the central role played by the united nations, in particular the office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs.
in writing. − at a time of crisis such as the one we are experiencing, the european union needs to strengthen its cohesion in order to remain a key player in the international political context. given the importance of a strong and stable eu-un partnership for the work of the united nations, the union is called upon to engage on several fronts to strengthen the international criminal justice system, to further ensure the protection and recognition of human rights, to promote the culture of democracy and the rule of law, and to take a leading role in global climate governance by supporting biodiversity and climate protection in developing countries.
in writing. the report, which i welcome, completes a courageous effort to rationalize and adapt the gsp to changing economic and geopolitical conditions, while safeguarding its incentive value for development and cooperation and thus, ultimately, for stability and security. while for many countries the status of gsp beneficiary was superseded by free trade agreements with the union, in other cases the gsp beneficiary status was clearly a legacy that was superseded and no longer in line with the objectives of the system. the sensitive issue of the so-called gsp+ countries remains, but it can be addressed in the light of the experience of the reform itself, as it will evolve in the application of the provisions contained in the delegated acts, including in the context of the five-yearly review. similarly, it is desirable that every possible care be taken in monitoring the implications at regional level of the possible co-existence of signatories to free trade agreements and of countries with gsp status. i have no doubt that any inadequacies would be detected in a timely manner, also in view of the close monitoring of the threshold and the competitive value of imports. the overall result is a more streamlined, transparent and certainly adapted to the pace of relatively rapidly changing economies.
in writing. − the system of generalised tariff preferences needed a definition that would improve the status quo and make the application of these procedures uniform and, at the same time, contingent on the particularities of the individual member states. to this end, it is important to introduce evaluation and monitoring tools which enable tariff preferences to be applied and adjusted to new economic, social and technological circumstances. my vote in favour is therefore an incentive to continue along this path, on the one hand, and to keep in mind the changing conditions of increasingly globalised markets, on the other. this will make it possible to avoid favouring or disfavouring member states which would be in a very unfavourable competitive situation.
in writing. − while we must monitor the effects of these measures closely in the future, i agree with the rapporteur's proposal that the revision of the gsp system should seek to extend benefits to the poorest countries remaining in the system, in order to increase development potential.
in writing. - i congratulate mr fjellner on his work. the adoption of this report, in the light of articles 294 (2) and 207 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and in the light of the report of the committee on international trade and the opinion of the committee on development, represents parliament's intention to introduce several changes to the rules on imports of products from developing countries, with the aim of 'concentrating import preferences on the developing countries most in need'. the scope should therefore be extended to certain products which are important to developing countries, while taking care not to affect the preferences of the least developed countries for products which are essential to them. in addition, the proposed reform highlights two fundamental needs: the need for a more targeted grading system and further promotion of fundamental human rights, labour and the principles of sustainable development.
in writing. − developing countries need to participate in international trade, as their increased presence would enable them to generate additional export earnings, supporting income growth and the implementation of sustainable development and poverty reduction strategies. the revision must now succeed in extending the benefits, especially in the poorest areas, by increasing their development potential and also by including products of particular value to developing countries.
in writing. - my vote on the fjellner report is negative, despite the fact that the european commission's proposal is certainly an improvement on the previous generalised system of preferences and despite the fact that the council, in its negotiations with parliament, has introduced further restrictive elements for the gsp+ system. unfortunately, however, a country like pakistan, which in the textile sector represents a serious threat to european companies which are still resisting in this sector, will soon be able to make use of the gsp+ instrument. i don't think that's a good thing. access to these trade preferences had to be further restricted. that is why the northern league voted against it.
in writing. the european commission has proposed to review the system of generalised tariff preferences, in force in the union since 1971, in relation to non-reciprocal trade preferences for goods entering the european market from developing countries. although the new preference criteria will reduce the number of beneficiaries by about 50%, i believe that this system will be a real instrument for increasing the gdp of developing countries and will be implemented through measures to overcome the critical problems in these countries and will be a real fight against poverty.
in writing. - we have approved the two-pack, the two reports which, together with the six-pack voted last september, complete the package of reforms concerning european rigour and governance, with a view to achieving economic stability in the euro area. i have given my support to the gauzès report, which i believe is vital for real growth. growth must start in europe, not only to set in motion a financing mechanism for the sectors which favour european growth, such as infrastructure and research, but also to enable the member states to keep to their commitments. the growth tools are: forms of debt mutualisation, such as the european redemption fund, proposed by the german economic council in november 2011; the issuance by eu financial institutions of bonds, which are intended for infrastructure investments and which are subject to a golden rule excluding them from the deficit accounts; the commission has also proposed the creation of a european deposit insurance scheme to avoid the run on the bank's doorstep in the euro area. this vote is an important step towards a genuine union, which is monetary, economic and political.
in writing. - i have chosen to vote against mr gauzès' report because it reiterates, for the umpteenth time, the terms of an analytical approach which i did not consider and do not consider to be valid and which, over time, has contributed decisively to the worsening of the economic and social situation in europe. i have refuted and challenged the theory that the root cause of the crisis is the large number of countries which have failed to put their budgets in order. on the contrary, the facts show that it is a crisis of growth and lack of investment. in the face of this reality, the recipe that is being proposed to us is wrong and will prove to be counterproductive once again. we have fought a hard battle against that in the past, opposing and not voting for the six-pack. since then, in the face of a worsening economic and above all social situation, rather than calling for a reversal of course and a radical change of pace, we have been backtracking by removing those economic analyses which, in reality and unlike those of the right which have brought us to this situation, we know to be correct and potentially capable of putting a stop to that drift which is becoming irreversible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution. i am very sad to see the negative effects of this social depression, if that is what you want to call it, and i am firmly convinced that we must act quickly to avoid a worsening of the global economy. the treaty requires them to regard their economic policies as a matter of common concern, driven by a need for sound finances that cannot jeopardise the functioning of economic and monetary union. the stability and growth pact itself stresses the need to create incentives for prudent budgetary management, avoiding of course excessive government deficits and strengthening the monitoring procedure. this monitoring will help us to identify risks and to take responsibility in a timely manner. the european union, as the commission has said, must share responsibility, and this, in my view, also implies sharing the risks. only then can a coordinated and highly supervised budget be guaranteed.
in writing. the arab spring revolution has just celebrated its first anniversary. the nascent democracies of morocco, tunisia, libya and egypt are still struggling to find their own democratic forms and the necessary legitimacy among their peoples. the difficulties facing the economies of these countries compel us, as the european parliament and, more generally, as the european union, to adopt policies in line with our values of solidarity. in the past i have spoken out against measures to favour these countries by abolishing duties on certain agricultural products, as was the case with the controversial eu-morocco agreement. but i'm criticizing the method, not the goal. that is why, in this particular case, i voted in favour because i believe that extending the geographical scope of operations of the european bank for reconstruction and development is an important measure. this is provided that the real needs of these countries are taken into account and that the quality of investment is such that it does not adversely affect the economies of the member states.
in writing. - i am in favour of the so-called two-pack. i agree with the text which dismissed parliament's committee on economic affairs. the budgetary controls of the member states must be carried out in advance: i think it is right to demand greater rigor. this also applies to the redemption fund and the investment split.
in writing. i voted against this report on the surveillance of states in financial difficulty because we cannot allow third parties, institutions which do not represent any citizen and are devoid of any popular legitimacy, to even think of determining the economic and financial policies of the member states, even to the point of legal protection. the european commission should simply indicate the way forward and the objectives to be achieved, but the various countries must remain free and sovereign as to how they will intervene, since there are situations and realities which are extremely different from one another and brussels cannot have a fair and equal solution for all. it is also a new proposal on economic governance, coming a few months after other similar measures in this area. the commission is continuing to try to save a sick eurozone, but i do not think that this is the right recipe.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the rapporteur points out that the serious economic and social consequences faced by some member states today could have been avoided if preventive, timely and targeted measures had been taken. but the european union lacked the necessary instruments, a gap which is now being filled by combining the six-pack on european economic governance with two new dossiers, providing that a member state whose currency is the euro must be subject to enhanced surveillance when it is exposed or is likely to be exposed to serious financial disturbances. the commission will take the necessary decisions in this respect and the council may reject them by a simple majority within 10 days. it is also proposed to create a legal protection regime applicable to a member state which is likely to be in a situation of permanent default or suspension of payments.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis that began in 2008 actually opens up a deeper reflection on the economic and social problems that this crisis has caused. the economic and budgetary surveillance procedures of the member states must necessarily take account of the sharp slowdown in growth in the union and the serious budgetary difficulties for the member states. i therefore support the objectives which the community as a whole must pursue, not just by focusing on the budgetary positions of the member states, but by supplementing this instrument with investment in the labour market, public investment in training and research to increase the competitiveness of the member states and incentives to consumption, thus maintaining a constant internal gdp to better withstand the crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the two-pack which, with the six-pack, completes the part concerning rigour and governance for economic stability. i also gave my support to important amendments, which i consider vital, concerning real and concrete growth, starting from europe, in order to enable the states to keep the commitments they have made to europe. this growth consists of: debt mutualisation, a european redemption fund, a proposal made by the german economic council in november 2011; the issuance of bonds by eu financial institutions for infrastructure investments, to which a golden rule is to be applied to exclude them from deficits; the commission has also proposed a european deposit insurance scheme. this vote is an important step towards monetary, economic and also political union.
in writing. - i have chosen, albeit painfully, to vote against the report because i believe it is absolutely inadequate and inadequate to meet the pressing and growing urgencies of the social and economic crisis. i have voted against because i think the report's opening up to growth is totally inadequate. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the redemption fund, the opening to eurobonds and chapter 3 as a whole were approved by a very risky majority, due to the strong opposition of the conservative forces who, after having collected the consent to the austerity measures, did everything to boycott any reference to investments. this says a lot about the council's attitude. we must find the courage to take our ideas and our instruments back to the fore. if we do not, we shall be complicit in the stupidity of the conservative forces and their inability to change the destiny of europe.
in writing. - the current global crisis has made it clear that there is no political dimension to economic governance, especially in the european union. when, in 1988-89, european leaders courageously decided to launch the process of convergence of the economies of the member states towards the single currency, both by completing the internal market and by coordinating the economies of the member states, it was emphasized with force and a europeanist vision that this objective could only be fully achieved by combining the pillar of monetary governance, with the autonomy of the european central bank, with the pillar of economic governance, with the commission, council and parliament. the future of the european union can only be built on both pillars. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. just as at national level the different economic growths in the regions are compensated by a single state governance, including through a common participation in the public debt, so it must happen at european level in the relationship between states, whose relationship must evolve by inverting common, cooperative and solidary destinies. this report and the amendments adopted seem to me to support this view.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this regulation. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. in this, i have voted strongly in favour of eurobonds and the redemption fund, in contrast to the line of my group, the epp. i voted in favour of the amendment in favour of the golden rule for the disengagement of investment from the deficit and i regret that this amendment did not pass. with the current scenario, it's time to act and fast: we have seen that it is not enough. we must mutualise debt while demanding austerity and above all support growth before it is too late. the european union must assume shared responsibilities, and this, in my view, also implies shared risks.
in writing. - i think the regulation is a good proposal because it sets out some additional monitoring provisions for national budgetary policies, proposes a common timetable and calls for stricter control of the decisions taken by member states subject to an excessive deficit procedure. fiscal policy should be in line with the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to overcome the crisis and move the economy towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, coupled with high levels of employment, productivity and social cohesion.
in writing. − six proposals make up the overall legislative package to strengthen economic governance in the eu and the euro area approved by the european parliament and the council in november 2011. four of the proposals concern the financial question and two concern the macroeconomic imbalances in the euro area. as regards the increased monitoring of the processes in countries with large budget deficits, and the commission's request to increase the provisions for national budgetary policies, i am voting in favour, while also stressing the need to align these upgrades with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, which is aimed, among other things, at helping the eu to overcome the crisis and to move its economy towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. - already from articles 1 and 2 of its statute, the ebrd is distinguished from other regional investment banks for the purpose of accompanying the transition to complete democracies, supported by robust material constitutions of western culture, through the growth of the private sector and the orderly conversion of centralized and state economies (also in their oligopolistic version) into mature and functioning market economies. the countries of the south-eastern mediterranean have many similarities with the specific cases for which the bank was set up. i am thinking of the weight of state industry in their economies, a factor in slowing down development and often an incentive to inefficiency and corruption. this is a state of affairs which, by the way, has been systematically exploited by radical and islamist political organizations. as the union's member countries are generally the leading trading partners in the region, it is clear that the ebrd should be reconfigured to support cooperation policies in the region, particularly in the context of stabilisation, the growth of the middle classes and the promotion of a moderate and reformist culture. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr binev's report on the activities of the european bank for reconstruction and development because i share the rapporteur's proposals. the ebrd was set up in the wake of the collapse of the soviet bloc to help the countries of eastern europe to rise from years of oppression. now that many of these countries have become part of the european family, it is more appropriate than ever to take account of other geographically close realities. today, especially as a result of the recent political events which have revolutionized the political landscape of the southern shore of the mediterranean, with the collapse of many of the regimes which had characterized the last decades, the need has emerged to provide adequate support to these countries as well. i believe that we should strengthen cooperation with those who are proving to be strategic partners in the commercial and, possibly, political fields, encouraging and supporting initiatives that stimulate their progressive transition to efficient and inclusive market economies, so as to enable the people to enjoy the benefits of progress that have been denied to them for too long.
in writing. - believing that the extension of the mandate of the european bank for reconstruction and development to the south-east mediterranean area could promote the development of the region and reduce migration from its member countries to europe, i voted in favour.
in writing. the adoption of a new economic governance for the european union is a crucial step in bringing the entire continent out of the crisis. proposals such as the 'two-pack' which are geared towards support on the one hand and careful monitoring on the other, are concrete responses to the difficult times we are going through, together with the other 500 million european citizens. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that legal safeguards for countries at risk of default are very necessary and are synergistic with the proposal for economic surveillance. this aspect should not be seen as a 'compulsory' imposition, but as aimed at protecting the economic and social interests of the european union as a whole. finally, these initiatives cannot solve the situation without support. they must necessarily be accompanied by new and decisive measures at european level. firstly, policies which are no longer a symbol of rigidity but a beacon of growth and development, such as the fight against youth unemployment, must be adopted: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.
in writing. - i voted in favour of extending the activities of the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) to the countries of the southern and eastern shores of the mediterranean, such as egypt, morocco, tunisia and jordan. these countries are crucial in preparing important investment projects for the creation of inclusive markets for people and investment measures aimed at energy development and eco-sustainability that will serve as a good practice for other states in the arab world.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. the european bank for reconstruction and development should be encouraged to apply a country-specific approach and to take into account factors such as the revolutionary context, the role of extremist forces and the role of military and monarchical political structures.
in writing. the esrb was set up to help the countries of central and eastern europe and the countries of the former soviet union transition to a market economy following the collapse of the communist regimes. unlike other international multilateral banks, which require the mediation of national governments, it can invest directly in direct shareholding, merchant banking and venture capital. the extension of the operation of this instrument to the south-eastern mediterranean region finds its undeniable coherence in the events that took place in that area at the end of 2011 and commonly known as the arab spring. the eu cannot fail to show its solidarity in the difficult transition under way, contributing with its own financial instruments to promote the economic and social growth of the populations concerned.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to extend the activities of the european bank for reconstruction and development to certain mediterranean countries. the esrb was originally set up to help develop and reconvert the economies of eastern european countries which had been emerging from decades of socialist economic model. in this area it has managed to operate quite well, with satisfactory results. over the years, the scope of the institution has expanded considerably, covering many central asian countries and even mongolia. it seems to me, of course, to be more than reasonable that the ebrd should also operate in certain states much closer to our borders, for which supporting action can mean development and, as a result, a brake on possible new waves of migration. of course, the measures must be accompanied by certain guarantees of transparency and compliance with well-defined criteria, which are essential especially in this area which is still not well established. finally, the bank's capital will not be increased, but it will simply be a matter of diverting funds from other areas, far removed from our reality and our interests. this was a prerequisite for our support for this initiative.
in writing. − the role of the european bank for reconstruction and development is to stimulate the recovery of economic and commercial activities through the reconstruction of infrastructure and services where necessary. the eu must beware of the events in the southern mediterranean countries, historically vital trading partners. these cross-border areas, following the arab spring, need new incentives for economic and socio-political growth. the european interest is to ensure and help reconstruction and growth by rebuilding the socioeconomic fabric to stimulate investment and prevent illegal immigration. i therefore welcome the geographical extension of the operations of the ebrd to the south-eastern mediterranean.
in writing. - on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision to extend the geographical scope of operations of the european bank for reconstruction and development to the south-eastern mediterranean, i express my favourable opinion, being in favour of opening up markets by promoting private initiative and entrepreneurship in the countries of central and eastern europe which recognise and apply the principles of multi-party democracy.
in writing. - the recent social upheavals in the african and asian countries bordering the mediterranean have led the european union to provide adequate support to these countries, which play an important role not only in terms of political stability but also in terms of trade. i therefore expressed my support for mr binev's report, which proposes to extend the activities of the european bank for reconstruction and development to the countries bordering the mediterranean, including jordan, confident that the local populations will derive the benefits which have long been denied them.
in writing. - the maximum political autonomy of a territorial entity is attained when it has full fiscal autonomy and, therefore, full economic and financial autonomy in determining its budget. unfortunately, the serious delay in achieving this level of autonomy is particularly evident in the context of the agreement on the multiannual financial framework. it is precisely in this process that european and europeanist ambitions and responsibilities clash with the selfishness of the member states, with a strengthening of national and nationalist interests. it is regrettable that the political dimension, which has always been concerned primarily with the common european interest, has been lost and that instead there is an accounting dimension, with which the balances between giving to the community budget and having at national level in the implementation of 'community' policies are continually calculated. the eu's full political capacity can be achieved by a real strengthening of the community's budgetary powers, both fiscal, in relation to the actual own resources, including through eurobonds and a financial transaction tax, and in the size of the resources themselves, appropriate to the political challenges and objectives it intends to pursue and achieve. this joint resolution seems to me to support this approach.
in writing. − the european budget is a very powerful instrument for increasing european strategic investment, for increasing growth and employment, and for stimulating economic development and social cohesion in the union. this requires adequate coverage in terms of appropriations for the period 2014-2020 and the maintenance of the guidelines already defined in the sure committee last june during the negotiation phase with the council. the new mff will need to be flexible in the years ahead so that it can respond promptly to unexpected crises and channel resources where they are most needed. i believe that parliament should not give its consent to the mff without a real political agreement on the introduction of a system of financing the budget from own resources, as provided for in the treaty of lisbon. how else can we explain to the european citizens that the institutions do not respect the provisions of the treaties?
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the resolution. the eu budget must present a fair balance between revenue from actual own resources and expenditure, in accordance with the treaty. the commission is right not to adopt the regulation establishing the next mff in the absence of a political agreement on the reform of the own resources system, which would put an end to the current reductions and other correction mechanisms and lead to greater transparency, fairness and sustainability.
in writing. the resolution adopted today proposes a flexible multiannual budget to meet new challenges and the replacement of national contributions with other types of resources for financing the union budget. the lack of flexibility in the current system makes it very difficult to react quickly to new challenges. the more scarce the budget, the greater the need to be able to reallocate resources to deal with unexpected events. according to the treaties, the eu budget must be financed entirely from 'own resources'. parliament argues that reforming the current system and introducing new sources of financing, such as a financial transaction tax or a new european vat system, would reduce the level of national contributions based on gross national income (gni) from 75 to 40% by 2020. the regulation establishing the next mff will not be adopted unless there is political agreement on the reform of the own resources system, which will put an end to the current reductions and other corrective mechanisms.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy was created primarily to promote sustainable growth, competitiveness and employment in europe and was adopted to deal with the current wave of economic and financial crisis that has hit europe since 2008. in order to achieve optimal results for sustainable growth and territorial development, solidarity and cohesion, priority should be given to improving synergies between all union budgetary funds that have an impact on economic development. i therefore vote in favour of the need to harmonise the allocation of funds for the europe 2020 strategy so that it is transparent, ensuring consistency between its objectives and the funding allocated to them at national and european level, and that it leads to a fair balance between revenue and expenditure, leaving room for a wide range of management flexibility in view of the unpredictable changes in the world.

the next item is the commission's debate on female genital mutilation.
member of the commission. − madam president, all forms of gender-based violence constitute an unacceptable violation of fundamental rights and a clear obstacle to gender equality. female genital mutilation is one form of violence against women that is particularly unacceptable. it is degrading, it violates fundamental rights, it violates the right to health and it violates children’s rights. an estimated three million women and girls in the world suffer female genital mutilation every year. up to half a million women living in europe have suffered genital mutilation already and many thousands are at risk. female genital mutilation can under no circumstances be justified by cultural or religious traditions and practices. it has both immediate and long-term consequences for the health of women and can cause death. the commission is determined to take concrete action and develop a strong policy response to tackle the issue of violence against women in europe. female genital mutilation is of particular concern. the commission has already said so in its strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015. the lack of reliable and comparable data is a huge challenge. my colleague, vice-president viviane reding, has asked the european institute for gender equality to assess the reliability and comparability of data available in member states and to identify data gaps. on this basis, the institute will report on the state of play with regard to this phenomenon, and of the replies drawn up in the member states. we should get a report in the second half of 2012. its results will help us to take even-better-informed action in this field. in 2011 and 2012, the commission has made funding available for combating harmful practices through the daphne iii programme. financial support will be granted for the implementation of transnational projects to grass-roots organisations working to prevent such practices by raising awareness and changing social attitudes. although there is no specific eu-wide legislation on female genital mutilation, it is criminalised in most eu member states, either through specific laws or under the general criminal codes. a large majority of eu member states have also included the principle of extraterritoriality in their criminal provisions, thus enabling prosecutions to be brought for female genital mutilation that has been committed outside the european union. the commission is taking measures in the criminal justice area and has proposed legislation on the rights of victims of crime. the aim with the victims directive is to ensure that all victims across the european union have a basic set of minimum rights, that they are treated as individuals and receive appropriate treatment. this instrument notably aims at ensuring that the needs of victims are individually assessed and that the most vulnerable, including victims of female genital mutilation, receive specific treatment appropriate to their needs. the commission proposal, with changes proposed by the european parliament, will significantly improve the situation for women as victims of violence. the eu also addresses the issue of female genital mutilation in its external actions. it supports advocacy and lobbying initiatives for promoting and protecting women’s rights and prohibiting harmful practices. the commission and the european external action service systematically raise the issue of female genital mutilation in their dialogue with african, caribbean and pacific countries. in this framework, we underline the need for african states to ensure that female genital mutilation is legally prohibited and that legislation prohibiting female genital mutilation is effectively enforced. we strongly support the united nations general assembly’s planned resolution to ban female genital mutilation. it is crucial that the countries with the highest occurrence of female genital mutilation, in particular in africa, take ownership of this resolution. the european external action service is currently preparing a campaign, under the eu human rights guidelines on violence against women and girls, to draw attention to the need to step up efforts to eradicate this practice, particularly on the african continent. female genital mutilation is an extreme and unacceptable practice. the commission is determined to combat it and to help empower women inside and outside the european union through legislation, financial programmes and a range of other means, including support to grass-roots organisations.

member of the commission. − madam president, during the last 20 years, the medical device regulatory system has, overall, provided for safe, reliable and performing devices in europe and has provided the flexibility needed for the high number of medical devices and the short life-cycle of these products. it has also proven to be a system that is cost-effective and sme-friendly. it has put europe in the forefront of innovation. for months before the pip case, the commission was reviewing the medical devices directive, because we found that it needed quite a number of improvements. the pip case is indeed appalling. it is a case of fraud which went undetected due to weaknesses in the post-market phase. nevertheless, the case has highlighted a number of weaknesses in the regulatory framework. in order to provide a rapid answer to european patients’ concerns, i have identified, and shared with the european parliament, a number of actions to be taken immediately, together with the member states, on the basis of the current legislation. this includes tightening market controls, in order to provide a better guarantee of the safety of medical technology, especially high risk devices. i have therefore written to the health ministers of all the member states to ask for their support, and together we are now putting these actions in place. for the longer term, the revised medical device legislation that the commission has been preparing – independently of the pip case, as i said –will also take on board the experiences of this affair. the commission intends to adopt its proposal shortly after the summer break. a number of improvements were already foreseen to reinforce the system. these improvements will contribute to avoiding cases like the pip implant case. to mention but a few: we want to strengthen the designation, monitoring and functioning of notified bodies and ensure that this is carried out in accordance with the same high standards across the eu; and we want a stronger role to be given to competent authorities, both in pre- and post-market phases. the system can only be efficient if we make the best use of the limited number of experts available. this is why the commission foresees a pre-market scrutiny mechanism to be put in place for high-risk devices, and other devices where necessary, but on a case by case basis. this mechanism will allow a committee composed of member states’ experts to check certain notified bodies’ assessments before the devices can have access to the market. the advantage of doing so will be twofold. first, it will ensure an equal level of assessment by notified bodies, in particular with regard to clinical evidence. second, it will allow member states to be informed of products coming onto the market so that they can ensure targeted controls of these products. this mechanism has the advantage that scarce resources and expertise are used to ensure efficient and proportionate pre-market control and reinforced vigilance and market surveillance. last but not least, we want to improve the traceability requirements for medical devices, for instance by means of a unique device identification and a single registration system. following the pip case, the commission performed a ‘stress test’ of the medical device legislation in order to identify additional possible shortcomings of the regulatory framework and address them in the context of the upcoming revision. as a result of the stress test, additional measures will be included in the commission proposal. these proposals will concern the audit activities of the notified bodies. particular attention will be paid to the obligatory unannounced visits to the manufacturer, testing of products and rotation of auditors. information will be given to national authorities with regard to negative outcomes of such audits. measures should also be put in place to enhance the reporting of incidents by healthcare professionals and patients. patients’ awareness should also be improved through, for example, implant cards providing appropriate information. this is where i believe that the transparency of the market should be enhanced, by giving all interested parties the right information not only – as mrs mcavan has said – about costs and benefits, but also about the duration, durability and consequences of the implants or whatever other device they are using, because this is not only a question of implants and there are other devices in use. i believe everybody needs to know all the implications of using such devices, because some people really do think that once they go through a procedure, it is a once in a lifetime procedure, which in many instances is not the case. this has to be continuously put in front of our patients, or our consumers, in the way we are suggesting. these cards have to be given to every single patient who undergoes any type of procedure involving such implants. in this way, patient awareness will be greatly improved. i do believe that the set of measures already foreseen, combined with additional measures deemed necessary in the light of the result of the stress test, will considerably reinforce the system, favour innovation and ensure that only safe and performing medical devices are placed on the european market, for the benefit of european citizens. i have taken note of the points raised by mrs auconie and i must say that all her points are, in fact, included in the proposal that we will be presenting, as i said, just after the summer.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank all members for their comments on this very important issue. we all agree that patient health comes first and foremost in our policy deliberations. this is exactly what we are doing too when we insist that we must continue to have a flexible system that delivers innovation as fast as possible to our patients, because that is also a function of patient health. being able to use innovative products at the earliest possible time – and in europe we deliver innovation about three years before our american counterparts with their own system – is a benefit to patients that we cannot put aside. so when i was asked by mr pargneaux why i would not be pushing for pre-marketing authorisation, this is why: because i do not believe we need it. we do not need to go the way of pre-market authorisation. we have a system in europe that has worked in the past. we are enforcing this system so it works even better. we are ensuring the competence of all the bodies that are involved in the authorisation process and this is the package that we will be proposing to this parliament and to council just after the summer. this, mr tarabella, is what the outcome is, and what my position is on this issue. we have been deliberating, we have been studying and we have been stress-testing what we have done because of the pip case, and we will be coming forward with a formal, concrete proposal in a few months time, around september. when we talk about authorisation, what we are saying here is: let us continue to keep the flexibility that we have in europe; let us enforce and make sure that whoever is involved in the process is competent to do so; let us make the competent authorities in the member states more involved in what is happening in their own countries within this process, and then let us have a europe-wide expert group that will ensure the consistency, all across europe, of a standard level of authorisation. the pip case is not about authorisation. the pip case has nothing to do with authorisation. the pip case is a fraud which could have happened under the most robust authorisation process you could possibly have. the pip case is an indication of the weaknesses we have in our processes: not necessarily in the legislation itself, though the legislation will be strengthened as well, but more in the way it was being implemented in market controls after authorisation. as some of you have said, competent authorities in member states simply let the medical devices that were in use in their countries not be subject to any kind of controls, and this is what is wrong. it was unbelievable to hear – and i am an accountant by profession, so for me it was even worse – that all audits held by the notifying bodies on companies were all pre-notified two months in advance! it is unbelievable that this could happen! this was all due to their interpretation that this was what was required in our legal process – which is not the case. in fact, in the letter i have written to the ministers, i have told them that this is not the case, that non-notified audits are provided for in our legislation today, and they should also be making sure that this is happening with marketing controls today. we do not need to wait two years until this legislative process that we will be launching very soon is finished. we are pushing for transparency; transparency not only in the information that is given to everybody who might be deciding on making any type of procedure, but transparency also in the vigilance aspect so that all incidents that happen within the medical devices sector have to be reported back. a database will be set up to put all this information together so that we can really take the necessary actions. the traceability of medical devices, which we are also proposing and will be proposing, as was mentioned here again today – and i am pleased that it was because this is also a very important aspect – and especially of risky medical devices would also be part of the proposal. therefore, we are keeping our word on this. we will be coming back in september with a robust proposal that will drastically improve our safety issues – and without going overboard, without overreacting to an incident and trying to find a way of transmitting the sense that we are doing something by really doing something where it is not indicated that it needs to be done. the problem of the pip fraud was not authorisation. it lay in market controls, and this is where we need to really put our foot down and really ensure that we introduce a robust market control procedure.

in writing. − over the years, the most serious industrial accidents resulting from the loss of control of certain dangerous substances, such as those in seveso, the netherlands, france and the united kingdom, have cost many lives and caused billions of euros in damage. in order to reduce the likelihood of such accidents occurring and to limit their consequences, the european union has adopted the seveso iii directive applicable to european establishments where dangerous substances (or mixtures) are present in quantities sufficient to constitute a major accident hazard. the introduction of this directive will strengthen the provisions on safety information and, in more detail, the operators of all establishments falling within its scope will be required to notify the competent authority and to draw up a strategy for the prevention of major accidents. while i welcome the introduction of new rules which are more restrictive than in the recent past in the area of plant inspection, i think it is important to stress here that the new environmental legislation as a whole will lead to a significant increase in the administrative burden on european companies.

in writing. since 1967, the year of the tragic seveso chemical disaster, europe has done much to ensure that accidents involving certain dangerous substances are prevented and their serious consequences for the environment and humans are reduced. among the new features which will be introduced by the new rules, i would like to focus first on easier access to information for the public. prevention and information are inseparable concepts. citizens should be given the tools to become more aware not only of the risks associated with industrial sites located in their territory, but above all of the possibility of mitigating the consequences of a major accident by adopting self-protection rules and implementing the safety measures indicated in the emergency plans. the information must be comprehensible, up-to-date and timely. in the event of an industrial disaster, constant communication via the internet with the affected populations can certainly facilitate the implementation of ongoing operations. finally, let us not forget that we cannot compromise on security: more effective prevention also requires strict controls of the plants at risk through constant inspections and the correct application of the rules in force.

in writing. − the most serious industrial accidents in the eu member states have cost many lives and destroyed property and seriously damaged the environment, causing billions of euros in damage. this vote in favour will be an attempt to reduce the likelihood of similar accidents in the future. the obligations of operators and the authorities of the member states should be increased and better regulated in order to prevent accidents and limit their consequences. the different levels of obligations imposed on operators reflect a progressive approach whereby the higher the quantities of substances, the stricter the rules. all operators of establishments falling within the scope of the directive will be required to notify the competent authority and to develop a major accident prevention strategy. in addition, operators of 'upper-threshold establishments' will be required to develop a safety report, a safety management system and an emergency plan.

in writing. − it is currently difficult for both the consumer and the control authorities to distinguish between food products for everyday consumption and those intended for specific groups. the reasons for these ambiguities may be differences in interpretation and application of the rules between member states. i have therefore voted in favour of the report by mrs frédérique ries: we need a new legislative order, uniform laws, to ensure innovation, the competitiveness of businesses and the protection of information for consumers. the european union must commit itself to a harmonised treatment in the field of food which is capable of guaranteeing greater legal, economic and social security, including not only goods consumed and produced within the european union but also those exported and imported. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's milk production is not affected by the increase in the quantity of milk products. statistics show that eating disorders are increasingly causing depression, stress, and malaise: let's help them make a life that's already complicated easier.

in writing. - we support the commission's approach to carrying out a thorough review of legislation on foodstuffs intended for particular nutritional uses and to abolish the concept of dietary feedingstuffs, which often no longer makes nutritional sense. we believe, however, that it is necessary to provide greater legal certainty for the industrial players and vulnerable sections of the population concerned. the legal certainty that this implies is that the european parliament must regularly carry out democratic controls on the definitions and composition of foods for infants, children under three and certain groups of patients for whom a particular diet is of vital importance. this legal framework, which is simplified but also capable of providing greater protection, should apply in a similar way to imported and exported food products, thus facilitating the adoption of the precautionary principle. the proper functioning of the internal market is at stake, and the health of the most vulnerable groups of the european population cannot be neglected.

in writing. the proposal for a regulation is aimed at a thorough review of the provisions on foodstuffs intended for particular nutritional uses contained in the framework directive on dietetic products, which essentially refers to the 1979 legislation. the proposal aims to abolish the concept of dietary foods and to establish a new framework containing general provisions only for a limited number of well-defined categories of foods which are considered essential for certain particularly vulnerable groups of the population, such as foods for infants and children and foods to be used under the supervision of a doctor. vulnerable persons need greater protection than the rest of the population and must be able to benefit from a high level of legislative certainty. the proposal also aims to create a single legal act laying down the lists of substances which may be added to the categories of foodstuffs covered by this proposal. the current divergences between member states in the implementation of existing legislation are too wide, causing market distortions and administrative burdens.
in writing. − dietary foods, which have been part of the european legislative body since 1977, and were then considered 'food for particular nutritional uses' in 2009 in a framework directive, are currently difficult to identify and associate with the right categories of intended use for both the final consumer and the control authorities. it is precisely the lack of transparency in this situation that clearly calls for a reorganization of food legislation aimed at specific groups of the population, starting with infants and children under three years of age for whom a specific diet is of vital importance and who deserve special attention and harmonized treatment in the european union. i am voting in favour of this, because i believe that legislation is needed to safeguard the health of the people of the union, including proper nutrition from birth, and to ensure that there are no pesticides or any toxic substances in food intended for children and infants or for special medical purposes.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the shadow rapporteurs who have worked with me on this important recommendation, the secretariat of the committee on transport and the socialist and democratic group. after almost two years of long and difficult negotiations with the shadow rapporteurs, the council and the commission, the european parliament has managed to make a lot of progress, in particular by ensuring more competition between railway operators, the supervision of a strong and independent national regulator, which ensures fair competition, and the obligation to deal with complaints for the first time within a set timeframe of six to a maximum of 16 weeks, the creation of a european network of national regulators and a rendezvous clause for the creation of a european regulator. the new rules, which should also provide a solid basis for infrastructure financing with contracts of a minimum duration of five years, and the agreement reached to strengthen the existing rules and to create a single european railway area should also allow all railway undertakings to have equal access to a wider range of services, such as maintenance and station services, including ticket sales, and ensure equal access to the railway network. the new rules provide for stronger rules for the appointment of staff and for full independence through cooling-on and cooling-off and the provision of a declaration of interest to be submitted by members of the regulator. the regulatory recommendations to licensing and security authorities are also provided to avoid that, for example, security standards can be used to restrict market access. the new regulation will extend the competence of the regulatory bodies to the related rail services and the control of the separation of accounts. it will be clarified that regulators are required to review both the provisional and the final versions of the network information leaflets, which are an essential tool to ensure that market access conditions are known by all operators. in addition to intervening in a limited time in the event of a complaint, the regulator will be able to intervene for the introduction of markups on the direct costs of infrastructure managers, will be able to control the criteria for the introduction of reservation rights and will be able to consult railway users regularly. thanks to the european parliament's intervention, a network of regulatory bodies has also been established: the content of the information will be exchanged in a clear manner and will be guaranteed by the commission, which will have to assess the efficiency of the regulatory bodies' cooperation with the new network and propose complementary measures to ensure more integrated control of the european railway market, hoping that a european regulatory body may be established in the future. as regards infrastructure financing, the multiannual contractual agreement has a minimum member of the commission. − madam president, i am pleased to see that many events and discussions have taken place this year in the european parliament, in the council and elsewhere, in the light of the commission’s communication which introduced the eu animal welfare strategy. the strategy proposes a new approach to the future of animal welfare in europe. after nearly 40 years of legislation, there is still room for improvement in this field, across the eu. the strategy is about better enforcement of eu legislation, better information for consumers, a simplified legislative framework and a focus on education and technical assistance to stakeholders at grassroots level. before addressing specific issues, let me first express my appreciation for the excellent work of the rapporteur, ms paulsen, who has produced a balanced report on this complex and highly sensitive area. i am glad to note that parliament supports the commission’s view on the key elements of the strategy: proposing a simplified framework law that, while taking into due account specificities of particular species and sectors, covers all animals kept in the context of an economic activity; considering a european network of reference centres for animal welfare to ensure that competent authorities receive uniform technical information on the way that eu legislation should be implemented and to disseminate expertise, research findings and technical innovation; developing animal welfare indicators in the framework law to optimise animal welfare outcomes – and i am aware that there are remaining issues of practicability to be considered here; and introducing legal milestones to help ensure that member states implement new legislation properly. in addition, the report emphasises the need to ensure better enforcement of existing legislation – something that is also of central concern to the commission. i share the views expressed in ms paulsen’s report on the importance of supporting and optimising international cooperation in the multilateral arena, especially the food and agriculture organisation of the united nations (fao) and the world organisation for animal health (oie) – as well as in bilateral negotiations by including animal welfare in negotiations with third countries – and on promoting eu views and understanding on welfare standards. this is all the more important because food production has, in the meantime, become a global activity with a possible influence, inter alia, on competitiveness. there are, however, some elements of this report on which the commission has not formed a definitive position, and on which more reflection is needed before any action is proposed. for example, the report suggests that the commission should consider developing a coherent eu-wide labelling scheme for producers, which would go beyond the current legislation on labelling. i too would like eu producers who wish to improve the welfare of animals beyond minimum standards to receive a better price. however, we need to consider all options carefully, and indeed to ask whether a legislative approach would be the most appropriate. the report also calls for mandatory animal welfare measures in the framework of rural development programmes. as honourable members will know, the revision of the regulation on rural development programmes is part of the revision of the cap. this idea would therefore be best explored within the context of cap reform discussions. i do, however, share the view expressed in the report about improving coherence in our overall approach. animal welfare is a cross-cutting issue on which a range of other policies have an impact. i therefore consider this to be a very sound and useful suggestion. let me turn to the welfare of pet animals. the commission has agreed to make a series of studies, including one on this specific issue in the context of the strategy. on the basis of the results of this exercise, we will consider how best to proceed. allow me to address one issue relating to animal transport, which ties into the important discussion on animal welfare. some weeks ago, i had the pleasure and the honour of receiving a delegation that handed me a petition to legislate for an eight-hour transport limit. i explained that, for various reasons, we are not in a position to agree to this request, although we will be tackling the issue in the context of the revision of the framework law on animal welfare – which is proposed as part of the animal welfare strategy we are discussing today and which could suggest, inter alia, new tools to improve the enforcement of animal welfare legislation, including during transport. i have been consistent in saying that enforcement is key to the issue of animal transport, and in saying that the commission is not considering proposing any changes to the animal transport regulation. in council on 18 june 2012, i stated that we have proposed a broad array of legislative and non-legislative actions to improve the welfare of animals during transport substantially. i have to admit that i have particular sympathy for the situation of animals travelling excessively long journey times to slaughter. as i announced at that council meeting, i am ready to examine all data that could shed light on this issue. we must also look into the proposals in the animal welfare strategy which, i believe, contains several actions that have the potential to improve the welfare of animals during transport substantially. i would like to comment on a couple of other points. first of all, on the incomprehension in hungary over the issue of cages for laying hens, i must say that the directive in question was enacted 12 years ago. the prescribed transition period ended at the end of last year and, while some countries had a shorter time to prepare and change, one has to consider that all these countries, including my own country, negotiated about this directive during their accession negotiations. therefore everyone knew exactly what the timeframe and the commitments were. on cloning, i have also gone on record many times to say that the commission is currently undertaking an in-depth impact assessment of the cloning issue, and i will be coming before this parliament and the council with a proposal on a stand-alone directive on cloning. to conclude, may i once again thank parliament, and in particular ms paulsen and her team, for this valuable report. i look forward to parliament and the commission making further progress together as the strategy unfolds.
