mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on macro-regional strategies, especially with a mediterranean perspective. the macro-regions have proved themselves, and that is why at a historic moment like this it is necessary to give a great deal of development to the mediterranean as well. the mediterranean can become the place where culture, education, training, tourism, trade, environmental protection, transport and fisheries can become elements for the take-off of this area, precisely at the time of the ensuing arab spring. tourism brings wealth along with trade, education brings democracy and job training, because culture with its artists tells us how we are united, and gives us a perspective of what we could be. the mediterranean is important for all of this, and also and above all for all the other areas of europe and the middle east in general.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report we have voted on today proposes the creation of a system of common work and services for the maritime, mountain and lake areas of the mediterranean area, with the involvement of national governments and especially those of the local regions. this project is a revival of the political ideal of a europe of the regions, as originally envisioned by the founding fathers. to emphasize the importance of the macro-regions, i would like to draw your attention to an initiative that was born of the contributions and ideas of representatives of my party, an agreement signed on 29 june last in st. gallen, switzerland: the pact for the creation of the alpine macro-region between france, italy, switzerland, austria and germany. the meeting was attended by the heads of the three regions of northern italy - veneto, lombardy and piedmont. i hope that this initiative will soon be adopted in this house, so that europe can develop towards a genuine europe of the peoples and regions, the only solution to overcome this financial crisis and to make the most of our territories and their exceptional quality products, to relaunch the economy in a concrete way and to apply the principle of subsidiarity to 100%. that is why i voted in favour of the report by mr françois alfonsi.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the agreement reached with the council has brought about significant improvements, such as the establishment of strong and independent national regulators to guarantee fair and non-discriminatory access to the market, one of the key points of the reform, the minimum duration of contracts between a member state and an infrastructure manager, which will therefore allow better planning of long-term investments, the greatest possible attention to the issue of safety, both in the maintenance of rolling stock, with a clear distinction between light and heavy maintenance, and in the technological adaptation for the safety of infrastructure and trains (think in particular of the ertms mode). in short, the overall result is positive, but a key point for the completion of the single railway market remains open, namely the opening up of national passenger rail traffic. i hope that the commission will keep the commitment it made a few months ago and that a new proposal to this effect will be made by the commission before the end of the year.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, after long and difficult negotiations, an agreement has been reached which ensures that the european railway infrastructure strikes the right balance between financial transparency and the flexibility needed to ensure adequate investment. in particular, the minimum duration of five years for the contract between a member state and the network operator guarantees those medium and long-term investment plans which are fundamental in the railway sector. i would have thought it useful, however, to include measures relating to the opening up of the national passenger market to complete the european single market and not to penalise companies already operating in open markets.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree with mrs serracchiani that we must ensure financial transparency and the separation of the accounts of rail transport companies from those of railway network operators, and then liberalize rail services for a truly open and competitive market with more and better services for the transport of goods and passengers. the railway system is still not up to par with other modes of transport, partly because many states have neglected to finance railways. we consider that road freight transport has increased by up to 45.9%, with an increase in traffic and, of course, also in road accidents. it is true that lorries can cross borders without difficulty, whereas trains encounter technical and legal obstacles that must be removed. in conclusion, fair and non-discriminatory market access should be ensured by planning investments to modernise and create quality infrastructure and services.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the creation of a single european railway area represents an important opportunity to support the recovery of the economy and to make the internal market more competitive. the coexistence of different national railway systems hinders this process: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the railway sector's policy on the basis of the results of the european council in copenhagen in june 2014. we need to create transparent rules for access to rail services and to line services such as freight yards, maintenance centres and train composition areas. the commission's proposal is in that direction, and that is why i have given you my support. the council is taking too long to implement this new directive, up to 36 months. i therefore support the rapporteur's call for a 12-month deadline for the transposition of the entire directive.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the text adopted today provides a good starting point for further negotiations with the council. i am convinced that this innovative tool will contribute to improving road safety, the working conditions of drivers and competition in the sector. i am particularly pleased with the amendment i tabled on behalf of the ppe group on co-responsibility. i believe that all those involved in the transport chain, and not just road haulage companies and their drivers, should be able to be held liable in the event of infringement of the regulation in question. the text also provides for the fitting of smart tachographs on all vehicles, old and new, by 2020. this forecast will certainly involve a major effort for the industry in this sector, but it is equally important to remain ambitious and gradually replace even those carriers using the analogue tachograph with the digital tachograph. a final point of criticism i believe is represented by a definition of 'daily working period'. i think it is not consistent with other definitions given in existing legislation and particularly with regard to periods of rest or break for the driver, which would thus remain part of working time under this definition.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, since the late 1960s, legislation has been introduced in europe to improve the road situation and the working conditions of road hauliers. however, the situation has deteriorated dramatically in recent years, with an increasing number of companies breaking the rules. in particular, failure to respect minimum rest periods and maximum driving times leads to fatigue of drivers and potentially increased risks to road safety. i therefore voted in favour of the text as i believe it will improve the implementation of social standards and ensure fair competition between transport companies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the digital tachograph, by improving the uniform control of driving and resting times, could play an essential role in ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market in road transport, with great benefits for road safety. recent reports by law enforcement agencies in some member states have shown an increase in fraud involving this device and a change in the current regulation was therefore urgently needed. the commission estimates that the cost increase for the purchase of a new tachograph would be approximately eur 5 per vehicle, a cost which is insignificant in comparison with the potential benefits which could result. i voted in favour of the motion because i believe that the tachograph and satellite tracking devices in cars must be synchronised in order to achieve more efficient and more reliable services. the possibility of transmitting tachograph data also at a distance will also allow for better control and will greatly increase road safety.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, infringements of intellectual property rights and the worldwide trade in counterfeit goods are a growing concern because of the economic impact on european industry and the risks to the health and safety of consumers. parliament has long been speaking out on the need to regulate the flow of goods from third countries, which without efficient and harmonized customs controls risks being the unintended instrument for the traffic of products harmful to consumers and against the proper competitiveness of the commercial space. i have long been calling for customs systems to be harmonized for a more competitive europe, and this is now at last at the heart of the political debate, along with taxation. we welcome the creutzmann report's attempt to simplify the existing regulatory framework and to make action to combat unfair competition more effective. in the committee on trade we are working on the reform of the customs code to give operators greater certainty about the destination of goods in transit and to act promptly on false declarations of origin, a problem which would have been solved already if the council had adopted the regulation which this parliament adopted in october two years ago.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, water is life, water is a common and precious commodity which we have a duty and an interest in preserving and managing in a sustainable way to ensure the preservation of ecosystems and the very survival of man. this important report takes stock of the state of implementation of the european water standard pending the blueprint, the plan for the protection of europe's water resources announced by the commission this autumn. it is 12 years since the water directive came into force, much has been done, but much remains to be done, particularly in many southern european countries such as italy, which will be brought before the court of justice for delays in the implementation of the directive. we must ensure that there is sufficient water and that it is of good quality, given that water resources in europe are unevenly distributed and that we must therefore integrate this issue into all european policies. it is not possible that as much as 70% of the water supplied to the community could have been lost due to leaks due to poor maintenance of water networks. we need to achieve the goal of a green economy and have locally established water plans that seriously combat waste, aim at saving, reusing and recycling water, whether for irrigation, private households and in all the various sectors.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, water is increasingly being valued as a common good, a precious resource for all mankind. it is therefore essential to develop an integrated and efficient strategy for the wise use of this non-infinite resource. action at eu level must address the current and future water challenges facing our continent, and so the water conservation plan that will be released in november is essential to ensure that we have - as we have heard - sufficient and good quality water for sustainable and equitable use. i think this is an important part of the europe 2020 strategy. water binds to food, water is in food, and a small amount of food contains a huge amount of water, so a water strategy is also a strategy for food security in europe and the world. water can be a source of war, but it can also be a factor in development and peace, and that is why i strongly support the proposal in the report that 1% of water tariffs, for example, should be allocated to decentralized cooperation projects and to projects for world growth. i hope that this legislation, which already exists in some member states, will become, as a good practice that spreads to other countries, legislation in all the member states of the european union.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr seeber's work is the european parliament's contribution to the preparation of the plan for the protection of europe's water resources, with which the commission will take stock of what has been achieved as a result of the water framework directive, which has been one of the main pillars of european water policies since 2000. the report for which we voted in favour highlights the challenges to be faced, the gaps to be filled, especially in relation to the objective of sustainability in terms of good ecological, chemical and quantitative status, which, according to the same framework directive, should be achieved by 2015. the measures suggested include the inclusion of water-related issues in all eu policy areas, the development of a holistic approach that considers all water uses and their implications, the promotion and advocacy of efficiency and sustainability in the management of this fundamental resource, and the achievement of water security, not only at regional but also at international level.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, water is central to ecosystems and the climate, and it is a determining factor in the growth and development of many economic sectors. today we are witnessing an imbalance in ecosystems due to indiscriminate water use, with water use sometimes exceeding 40%, resulting in high water stress. i agree with mr seeber: the commission is also proposing to create a european water framework that supports the green economy, including the polluter pays principle, with transparent and efficient charging systems, and then incentives and investments for the use of treated waste water, grey water, storm water, and the implementation of a quality control system on the status of the european water network, to prevent about 70% of the water supplied to european cities from being lost to leaks in the network.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, water is a vital public good which must be protected by a holistic approach to its protection and rationalisation. improving efficiency and sustainability is a duty we cannot shirk, even in the face of the challenges of climate change. the objective we have set for 2015 of achieving good ecological and chemical status of water is the sine qua non of european environmental policy and a commitment to be rigorously monitored. the european union's water legislation must be respected and more stringent sanctions introduced. in europe, about 20% of water is lost due to outdated infrastructure, which must be improved if we are to use water resources efficiently and manage water sustainably, in order to tackle water scarcity and drought.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the health and safety of the citizens of europe is one of the main objectives of our action and our work. i think that the measure we voted this morning is very important, of course, ecall does not anticipate accidents, it does not reduce them, but it provides much faster intervention procedures which can, through their application, ensure an appropriate intervention to help the suffering of those involved or even save their lives, and all this is very important. the real and consistent application of this instrument by all actors, states, companies and then the operators, will now be decisive, but i believe that the transition from a voluntary experimental phase, such as the one we are now going through, to this new mandatory standard is a very important one. we have put in place a measure that can help many people to avoid suffering and many more to save their lives.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, already in 2002 road safety experts considered a pan-european ecall service to be implemented in all vehicles to be one of their priorities, partly because after an accident the people involved may be in a state of shock, not knowing their position, or simply unable to communicate with them. especially in accidents, rapid first aid is vital to saving lives. the ecall system based on the 112 call platform reduces the time it takes to respond to an accident, saving approximately 2 500 lives a year and reducing the severity of injuries by up to 15%. ecall can reduce the response time of emergency services by about 50% in rural areas and up to 40% in urban areas, and can also help reduce traffic jams that can form following road accidents by up to 20%.

in writing. − this directive establishes a new and modern solvency regime for insurers and reinsurers in the european union. it provides for a risk-based economic approach that provides insurance and reinsurance undertakings with incentives to measure and manage risks appropriately. these new rules are essential to ensure that the insurance sector is safe and sound. the proposed amendment to directive 2009/138/ec ensures an orderly transition to the new regime. in view of the imminent expiry of the previous regime and the need to avoid a legal vacuum, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.

in writing. − regional macro-strategies bring together a coherent approach to territorial cooperation, meeting the demand for investment in europe on a territorial basis in a new way. they help rebuild connections and cooperation. the report supports regional macro-strategies based on the principle of multi-level governance, in order to ensure collaboration between local, regional and national authorities. it called for a greater level of coordination between the different funds and asked the commission to consider the future of a macro-regional approach in europe, identifying the priority areas to be involved in the new strategies, especially when there is a lack of cooperation between neighbouring territories, which is evident in several member states. in this connection, i welcome the implementation of a macro-regional strategy for the mediterranean basin.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution to sustain the great opportunity represented by the eu macro-regional strategies. first of all, macro-regional strategies frame the eu’s neighbourhood policies in a way that encourages renewed dialogue and new prospects for territorial cooperation projects supported by cohesion policy. the baltic sea strategy is a perfect example of that. when it comes to the mediterranean, we must consider that the entire basin shares the same natural environment, and its shores are connected by the same history and culture. in terms of developing potential, maritime traffic must be placed at the heart of a transport strategy for the whole area, particularly for goods. a macro-regional strategy can provide tailored responses to these objectives. the mediterranean, due to its 500 million inhabitants (less than one-third of whom live within the european union), represents the main ‘neighbourhood prospect’ for europe. for this reason i believe that a development dynamic based around the mediterranean could drive forward the whole european economy.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the report by mr alfonsi, which, while acknowledging and emphasizing the undeniable existence of a historical and cultural system which unites the mediterranean countries, aims to establish a common political and service infrastructure divided into macro-regions (western mediterranean, central mediterranean, eastern mediterranean), which would allow the creation of a synergy capable of giving a new and stronger input to coordination between member states and a more effective distribution and re-investment of resources.
in writing. the mediterranean basin shares the same natural environment and the same historical and cultural reality. the south of europe is rich in great potential, which cannot be exploited without coordination or vision. the 'mediterranean climate' gives rise to similar ecotypes: the products of the earth are alike and in their variety they constitute a single range of products. at the same time, environmental problems are the same everywhere. the mediterranean is therefore particularly rich in biodiversity, but it is also under threat. appropriate and synergistic responses are needed. within the eu, the mediterranean area is too weakly structured and there are poor results in terms of cooperation and interconnection. moreover, on the eu's doorstep, the people of the mediterranean - despite the developments of the last year - still have inadequate living standards. the development of these societies is a necessity for them and an opportunity for europe. the latter would gain greater security, more 'sustainable' control of immigration flows and direct participation in a growing area, with positive effects on its economic performance. for this and many other reasons, it is important to support the creation of a mediterranean macro-region.
in writing. the macro-regions meet the criteria of simplification and coordination which have always inspired the european union's regional policy. the macro-region is the ideal institutional framework for member states, regions and local authorities to interact, in order to solve common problems and implement shared policies. it is important that a similar opportunity be given to those operating in the mediterranean basin, whose tourist, commercial and economic importance is obvious to all. unfortunately, the mediterranean area is not structured to the same extent as the european union, and as a result, there is little progress in terms of cooperation and interconnection. the division of the mediterranean into three large macro-regions (western, adriatic-ionian and eastern) would not only increase the coherence and effectiveness of mediterranean policies, but would also promote greater coordination between the different instruments of intervention available to the eu. the creation of a mediterranean macro-region therefore represents an opportunity for the whole mediterranean area to undertake coordinated policies in the interests of development and growth: it would be a mistake for the european union not to grant it.
in writing. − the case-law of the eu's macro-regional strategies has produced positive results in the baltic region and is undoubtedly one of the best european practices in the field of interinstitutional cooperation. the alfonsi report, for which i voted in favour, aims to develop this strategy and to implement it in those territories where cooperation has shown signs of giving way. the application of the macro-regional strategy to the mediterranean basin is certainly useful in bridging the communication gap at the different institutional levels and is aimed at ensuring a better participation process in order to increase the development of the territory it targets. it is therefore necessary to work towards making these strategies increasingly effective and efficient in their programmatic implementation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report not so much because of the important dimension of the mediterranean sea as because of the concept behind it, namely the overcoming of the now anachronistic division of the sea between the member states. the reality clearly shows that there are areas and peoples that have many similarities in common, although they are part of different countries: the baltic experience is emblematic of what can be a useful process of european integration which starts from below, a process which is born of sharing common interests and feelings, and is not imposed from above, as has unfortunately happened too many times in recent european history. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european network of national airports is a good one. on 29 june, the presidents of the alpine regions of italy, switzerland, france, germany and austria met in st gallen to lay the foundations for what could be the future alpine macro-region, in which the peoples of europe, too often marginalised in the european decision-making process, should once again play a leading role.

in writing. − the macro-regional strategy for the baltic sea was adopted in 2009 with clear commission interest as this new mode of cooperation is intended to open up an innovative field for cohesion policy in europe, aiming at development on a territorial basis. this strategy aims to bridge the gaps created by historical frontiers, thereby promoting the integration of the new member states and their regions. this macro-regional approach would make it possible to define an overall plan for cooperation within the union, thus overcoming the current crisis and providing concrete responses to neighbouring countries, especially in the southern mediterranean, and i therefore support the importance of territorial cooperation projects, since this would strengthen synergies with the union's major strategies such as the transeuropean transport networks and the integrated maritime policy.

in writing. − the proximity of the various national rail systems means that the sector is hampered by geographical boundaries which significantly limit both the development of the sector and the competitiveness of rail transport in relation to other modes of transport. in the light of these considerations, i believe that the creation of a single european railway area should be one of the main priorities for the european union. in order to facilitate the construction of a single european railway area and to create fair conditions of competition between large and small railway undertakings, i believe that the existence of regulatory authorities which are independent of each other is essential. in the long term, national regulatory bodies must also strive to become reliable and timely decision-makers. i agree with the rapporteur that in the long term it is appropriate to establish a european regulatory body to enable efficient control of crossborder transport. finally, i welcome the european parliament's achievement in making changes to the original text of the proposal to increase the transparency of financial flows, in particular in the integrated undertakings providing rail transport services and infrastructure management.
in writing. − during last month's plenary session, the issue of strengthening the single market was widely debated and the house agreed on the need to extend and implement the functioning of the internal market through the rapid transposition and full transposition of european legislation by the member states. in line with this objective, we discussed yesterday the recommendation for the second reading of the report on the single european railway area, but i believe that this represents only a small step towards the creation of a genuine european railway market. for too many years we have heard about the potential positive impact that the full realisation of the single market could have on the union's economy, but then we all go around backing positions of national advantage whenever we have the chance to make sectoral reforms for its full realisation. without going into the details of the individual measures, i would remind you that we are continuing to delay the recasting pending a commission position which can really lead to full liberalisation of the market, which would be impossible today, regardless of the fact that we have given ourselves 30 months to transpose the legislation. we cannot afford to wait until the internal market has brought us out of the crisis.
in writing. the full development of the european railway sector is a key step towards the full establishment of a common market at continental level. the greatest possible freedom of movement and the possibility of unhindered movement of goods can make the difference between a functioning and expanding economic system and a shaky and disintegrating one. at the same time, this development process must be guided by the same principles as the common market, namely free competition and transparency. in this sense, the measures adopted are in the right direction because they aim to stimulate the supply of transport services, both for goods and passengers, and to ensure fair competition. the establishment of strong and independent national regulators, coordinated by the european commission to facilitate mutual cooperation, is the best system to ensure the correct application of the rules, while the obligation to draw up separate and transparent accounts by railway undertakings and infrastructure managers should prevent any illegal transfer of public funds between these two entities. at the same time, competition should be stimulated by the separation of the accounts between the operator and the undertaking, so as to ensure the necessary balance between transparency and flexibility to ensure adequate investment.
in writing. − the creation of a single european railway area must remain our main objective, because the interconnection of the various national railway systems means that the sector is hampered by geographical boundaries which severely limit both the development of the sector and the competitiveness of rail transport compared to other modes of transport. we believe that the existence of independent regulatory authorities is essential to create a level playing field between large and small railway undertakings. we must continue our efforts to ensure a more stable financing situation for rail infrastructure and to increase the transparency of financial flows, particularly in the integrated undertakings providing rail transport services and managing the infrastructure. we therefore insist on the need to introduce a mandatory mechanism to limit the noise emissions of trains. trains with high noise emission levels have negative effects on people's health and their acceptance of rail transport and end up jeopardising the development of the sector. the strengthening of the role and competences of the infrastructure manager is another key objective for network management more geared to free competition in the sector.

in writing. − to facilitate better use of the eu's rail networks, we have clarified the rules on competition between railway undertakings and infrastructure managers with today's vote. the rules adopted are intended to stimulate the supply of international freight and passenger transport services and to improve their quality. independent regulatory authorities will ensure fair competition. in future, separate and transparent accounts by railway undertakings and infrastructure managers should prevent any illegal transfer of public funds between these two entities, even if they belong to the same holding company. the costs of railway concessioning will include bonus/malus incentives to reduce noise pollution and to equip trains with a european traffic control system (etcs) for maximum safety.
in writing. the aim of this vote is to facilitate better use of the european rail networks through clearer rules on competition between railway undertakings and infrastructure managers. the provision of international rail freight and passenger services needs to be stimulated immediately and their quality improved. for this reason, the cost of railway concessions will include incentives for the installation of noise abatement technologies and the installation of a european control system for maximum safety on trains.
in writing. − in the process of european integration, the creation of a single railway area plays a key role. it is sufficient to recall that one of the four fundamental freedoms on which the european union is founded is that of the free movement of persons throughout the community. that is why i strongly supported the recommendation of mrs serracchiani. there are two aspects of this report which i should like to stress. the first concerns the creation of a network of national regulators, totally independent and with more powers, coordinated by the commission, with the possibility, in the future, of seeing the figure of the single european regulator emerge. the second concerns the change from three to five years of the contract between a member state and an infrastructure manager. this change will allow for greater medium- and long-term guarantees on investment plans. a single railway area will allow for non-discriminatory market access and will make our rail network more competitive, stronger and healthier.
in writing. − quality, reliable, safe and efficient rail transport services can only be guaranteed through a common policy to facilitate the sustainable development of the european economy. the european parliament adopted its position on this subject at first reading on 11 november 2011. subsequently, the council reached a political agreement and a position at first reading on 8 march 2012 by qualified majority. since january 2012, the parliament, the council and the commission have been holding informal negotiations aimed at preparing an agreement at second reading. the council's request for the entry into force of this new directive, which amounts to 36 months and 60 months for the establishment of the regulatory body, is too long for such an urgent plan to be implemented, and i therefore support the request for the reduction of the transposition period from 36 months to 12 months.
in writing. − since 1969, the european union has had legislation in the field of road transport to improve road safety, the working conditions of drivers and to ensure fair competition between transport companies. according to the data provided by the commission, on average 9% of the vehicles inspected are in breach of social standards and about a quarter of these are in breach of tachograph standards. in the light of these data, the commission has put forward a proposal for a revision of the tachograph regulation which aims to improve the implementation of social standards and to reduce administrative burdens by taking advantage of new technologies by introducing a number of new regulatory measures such as those which will extend the functionalities of the digital tachograph, with the advent of a new type of tachograph called the smart tachograph. i welcome the proposal, i agree with the highlights and i support the introduction of the smart tachograph because i believe it will help to improve the implementation of the legislation and will be a tool to reduce the administrative burden of the tachograph obligations for the companies that are in compliance. in addition, a harmonised interface with its applications should help facilitate the integration of the various systems and avoid the multiplication of independent devices on board vehicles.
in writing. - i strongly disagreed with the report by mrs ţicău on the proposal to amend the current regulation (eec) no 3821/85 on recording equipment in road transport (tachograph) and to amend regulation (ec) no 561/2006 of the european parliament and of the council. first, i believe that the nature of the tachograph deviates from/does not relate to/does not fall within the definition of what is 'working time': i note that my proposal to use the term 'control' instead of 'work' was not considered/evaluated by my colleague. this can have a negative impact on the autonomy of each company in managing the working hours of employees. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the 'smart tachograph' in all vehicles by 2020 in the name of greater safety, without any preliminary study to confirm its usefulness and which, according to the road transport sector, would have been approved to promote the lobbies that produce this equipment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text proposed by the rapporteur, because i think she has done a very good job in concert with the commission and the shadow rapporteurs, completing a complex intervention in a particularly problematic area. the new digital tachograph will have a direct impact on the current situation of measurement of driving data, speed and rest periods for drivers, and will affect the method of control and the related compliance with the regulations in force. i am particularly in favour of the timetable for the introduction of the digital tachograph, which provides for an adaptation period until 2020, the latest date by which all member states will have to adapt by adopting this new measuring instrument. on the contrary, i do not feel that i support the possibility of derogating from these rules, since this would allow for a fragmentation of the market which would create competitive disadvantages for producers and especially for small and mediumsized enterprises.

in writing. − private emergency call services on board vehicles were introduced in europe in the late 1990s. despite the fact that these services have been widely demonstrated to be useful, their use in europe is less than 0.4% of the vehicle fleet. in addition, private emergency services do not cover all european countries: where the vehicles travel to countries where the private provider is not expected to provide the service, the service is interrupted. in this context, the commission has decided to take legislative action for the mandatory introduction of ecall. the benefits of introducing such devices for citizens are clear: reducing the number of fatalities and the severity of injuries resulting from road traffic accidents by means of a more rapid intervention by the emergency services at the scene of the accident, reducing the time taken to respond, which will allow the scene of the accident to be cleared more quickly, mitigating the impact on traffic and reducing the risk of further accidents at the scene. i welcome the introduction of ecall, but on the condition that any additional in-vehicle applications based on the ecall telematics platform comply with data protection and privacy regulations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr koch and mrs sehnalová in support of the commission's legislative action to introduce the ecall device on all eu-approved vehicles from 2015. this device automatically sends a european-wide distress call in the event of an accident and if the driver is unable to do so. i agree with the report that ecall will make it possible to reduce the number of road accident victims considerably. i also agree with the commission's extensive argument that the reasons for its introduction put forward by the united kingdom, france and poland are unfounded. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the protection of personal data are respected.
in writing. − the adoption of the report on the adoption of the ecall system is a clear signal of the european parliament's support for road safety. in europe, more than 40,000 people die each year in road accidents. the european commission has launched a new initiative to combat the spread of the virus, which is being developed by the european union's emergency response team (eratv). it is also important to remember that ecall will have minimal economic impact on final costs, which amount to about 100 euros per car, a price that is absolutely reasonable given the great benefits it will bring. it is now essential that member states and their mobile telephone services commit themselves to improving their infrastructure to ensure the best possible provision of this service. to date, 5 500 drivers have used the service in 10 countries: the positive effects that could be achieved by 2015 with the introduction in all 27 member states would be of vital importance.

in writing. - every year in the european union, approximately 40 000 people die as a result of road accidents, and over 150 000 people suffer permanent disability as a result: these terrible data show us how dire the situation is and how important it is that we find effective remedies to improve it. the report we have adopted today, which i wanted to support, provides for the introduction of an automatic warning system: the ecall system installed in a vehicle that has been involved in an accident will report the incident by means of a coded emergency call to 112, which has now become the single european emergency number, valid in all member states. this will not of course prevent accidents, but it will certainly help to improve the effectiveness of rescue operations, for which rapid and timely action is essential. it is estimated that this system could save 2,500 lives a year: i hope there are many more, but in any case, every person who is saved by this system will be a great success and an important achievement for all.

in writing. − i voted for this report because it stresses that the conclusion and the implementation of the associations agreements is a priority of the reviewed european neighbourhood policy regarding the eastern partners. the creation of deep and comprehensive free trade areas (dcftas) is indeed one of the most ambitious tools of eu bilateral trade policy with the aim to achieve a stable economic environment which respects democracy and the rule of law. in addition it is important to underline that prosperity and stability in the eu’s eastern neighbourhood are in the eu’s utmost interest and moreover i believe that stable relations between the eu and its eastern partners will undoubtedly increase trade volumes in both directions.
in writing. - i support the ransdorf report on the eastern partnership which provides a framework for relations between the european union and armenia, georgia, moldova, ukraine, azerbaijan, belarus, the first four already wto members and the last four only observers. the area in question is still socially and politically unstable, but the eu cannot avoid pursuing policies of partnership with it, which is dominated by russian influence and is also extremely rich in energy resources. finally, it is likely that such a european union policy can push these countries towards the institutional reforms and modernization they so desire.
in writing. − trade relations with the eu's eastern partners are an important aspect of our economic policies and should be closely monitored to allow for improvement. in particular, the creation of deep and comprehensive free trade areas (dcfta) in the east represents a basket of economic and commercial opportunities with multiple implications for our operators, in particular smes and the tourism sector, provided that reciprocity is respected in important areas, such as compliance with the same safety and control standards. it is clear that the aim of the creation of free trade areas is not only to influence the economic, but also the political and social profile of the countries with which they have trade partnerships. it was clear that a proper industrial development strategy would require cooperation to improve the civil and political characteristics which allow the maximum expression of individual freedom.
in writing. − the creation of deep and comprehensive free trade areas is without doubt one of the most ambitious instruments of the european union's bilateral trade policy, which aims to achieve a stable, transparent and predictable economic environment, while respecting democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law. with this report we want to underline the importance of the global programme for institution building, the instrument for technical assistance and information exchange (taiex) and with the eastern partner countries. in the long run, the benefits of such integration will outweigh the initial efforts: supporting and involving local civil society and international ngos in promoting the long-term benefits that are key to the success of their reform processes. we are in favour of strengthening cooperation between the eu and its eastern partners in a number of areas, in particular industry, smes, research, development and innovation, tourism. the economic integration of the eastern partners with the european union cannot be achieved efficiently without political and social reforms, without the participation of civil society in decision-making and economic integration among the eastern countries themselves.
in writing. − the creation of a comprehensive and deep free trade area with the eu is one of the key incentives for partner countries to pursue their reforms, as it represents one of the most ambitious instruments of the eu's bilateral trade policy to achieve a stable, transparent and predictable economic environment respectful of democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law, allowing not only greater economic integration through the progressive dismantling of trade barriers, but also regulatory convergence in areas affecting trade in goods and services, in particular by increasing investment protection, optimising customs and border procedures, reducing technical trade barriers and other non-tariff barriers to trade. given that greater trade integration requires considerable efforts in the short and medium term on the part of our eastern partners, i am in favour of creating the political and regulatory conditions favourable to the development of trade relations with the eastern countries.
in writing. - mr ransdorf's report seems to be balanced. that is why i voted in favour. the european union must become an increasingly privileged partner for this region, especially for the phase, which i hope will come soon, in which certain ethnic and religious tensions in the caucasus region will finally give way to development and prosperity for the people concerned. europe can do a lot in this respect.
in writing. − the conclusion and implementation of association agreements providing for comprehensive and in-depth free trade areas is a priority objective and ambition of the new european neighbourhood policy towards the eastern partners. especially following the revolutionary movements that took place in 2011 in the southern neighbourhood of the european union, known as the arab spring, europe's interest has also focused on its southern neighbours. the vote therefore calls on the commission to take due account of these considerations and recommendations when negotiating and implementing the trade aspects of the association agreements with armenia, azerbaijan, georgia, moldova and ukraine and in the development of trade relations between the european union and belarus. the commission is also asked to keep parliament regularly and in detail informed of the progress of the negotiations.

the agenda includes the report by mr giovanni la via, on behalf of the committee on budgets, on the mandate for the trilogue on the draft budget for 2013 (2012/2016 ((bud)) (a7-0215/2012).
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the vote on the mandate for the trilogue takes place today at a crucial moment for europe, but above all for the europe of tomorrow. the european council of 28 and 29 june decided to adopt a series of measures to ensure a financially stable and competitive europe. i am glad of this, since the heads of government have basically indicated the way out of the crisis for a stronger europe, as we have been saying since the beginning of this procedure: support for growth, competitiveness and employment, especially for young people, and support for small and medium-sized enterprises. these are the priorities which we have set ourselves as a parliament, aware of the immediate need to revive our economy, which cannot do without competitive growth in the european system, accompanied by measures which can provide strong support for young people to enter the world of work. there is also a need for a sufficient level of payments to cover the costs of implementing european programmes and projects, especially in headings 1a, 1b and 2. as we know, this is one of the central issues in the negotiations, perhaps the most difficult given the different orientations expressed so far by some member states. i would like to point out, however, that we want to include a passage from the european council conclusions in the report for tomorrow's vote, in the form of an oral amendment in which the council states that the european union will continue to do whatever is necessary to put europe back on the path to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. it seems to me clear that such a manifestation of political will cannot fail to be followed by a real commitment by all the member states to do everything necessary to achieve the objectives set, restoring the confidence of the citizens and giving a new impetus to growth. i would also like to point out that the payment appropriations proposed by the commission in its draft budget are based on estimates made by the member states themselves and revised downwards by the commission, and which the member states must of course honour. as regards the ral and the interinstitutional meeting on payments which we held on 30 may, i would add that i believe it is essential for the proper conduct of this year's procedure and for the achievement of a result which is truly centred on the needs of the european citizens that there should be a constant exercise in monitoring expenditure in order to be able to take account of needs and to identify future trends. i believe that strong interinstitutional cooperation is essential for this, which unfortunately has not been the case. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european union agency for fundamental rights. considering that 2013 is the last year of the financial perspective and that we expect a physiological increase in payment levels, it will be all the more important to avoid a dangerous shift in payments from 2012 to 2013. the debate is not only about payments, but also about the need for a sufficient level of appropriations and commitments, because we believe that in a time of crisis, as the council has also said, we need more europe, not less europe, and that is why, in terms of commitments, we need to give force to our political priorities and promote the necessary investments for growth and the creation of new jobs to get out of the crisis. the last aspect, which is certainly important, concerns the financing of iter. we have already taken note of the commission's proposal to use some of the resources made available through some cuts within the seventh framework programme, but i would like to reiterate that parliament intends in any case, as agreed in the joint declaration, to make full use of all the means available within the financial regulation and the interinstitutional agreement. i would like to conclude by thanking my colleagues and especially the shadow editors for their work and, since there is no council, i would like to address only to commissioner lewandowski an invitation to close interinstitutional cooperation throughout the procedure, which i hope will be successful and adequately funded in the interests of the european citizens and within the normal time limits laid down by the treaty.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, there is no doubt that in such a complicated period of rationalization of expenditure, of containment and of restructuring of expenditure itself, to define a balanced and reasonable budget as the rapporteur la via has succeeded in proposing is a clear sign of how well one can do even in a context of great difficulty. that said, the libe committee takes note of the indications which, once received by the committee on budgets, were then translated into positive assessments, i am referring to frontex, as well as to the question of the refugee fund. however, when it comes to the safety of citizens, we believe that something more concrete can be done in 2013, which is also a landmark year for the next financial perspective. i am referring in particular to the list of political priorities in which, madam president, there can be no reasonable doubt that the effective fight against organised crime is being pursued. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question.
member of the commission. − madam president, i should like to thank the members for their comments. i see that it is very fashionable now to compare national budgets with the european budget and this is partly justified, but only partly, as there is no full analogy for several reasons. the european budget is always in equilibrium: no deficit, no indebtedness. this is because of its size: our budget is 1% of gross national income (gni) but it is not comparable to the 4% or 5% of gni spent already on assisting the financial institutions of the european union and this is not the reason for the trillions of debt accumulated in the member states. however it might be part of the solution of how to enhance, in a responsible way, growth and jobs opportunities. if there is an analogy it lies in our efforts to save whatever can be saved. this will be in administration because, for the first time since the beginning of the european community, in 2013 the number of eu officials is going to be reduced, no longer growing. this also concerns agency staff – i am saying this for ms hohlmeier’s sake. are there are performance savings? yes: if we need adjustments, for example in the development cooperation instruments in latin america and asia where some programmes are not performing; then we are making savings and this is clearly reflected in the draft budget for 2013. taken altogether, our spending is now eur 66 billion, less than agreed for the financial perspective for the period 2007-2013. this is the net result of performance savings and being restrained in budgeting in the european union. but what is the budget? this is about the means to cover legitimate bills, bills coming for approved projects in the member states. ninety-four percent of the budget goes outside brussels; only 6% concerns administration. what is the result when we delay or do not pay? that is the problem of reimbursements to the finance ministries: this means deteriorating liquidity in member states, or really reducing investment possibilities in the member states or not supplying the means to overcome the credit crunch for small and medium-sized companies. and the net result, the final result, is the mountain of unpaid commitments. that is about the future bills; no real solution. this is not a real option. the 2013 budget was built on the deliveries coming from the member states and i agree with alain lamassoure that it is perhaps a little bit schizophrenic to send the bills to brussels. we evaluate very critically and then we make an effort to respect the deals and we cannot be criticised for respecting the bills coming from 27 countries. this is a little bit of a schizophrenic approach to the budget. i do not think that anybody is surprised that with the 2013 budget, which is the last, we have additional requests for payments. but it is a practical test of what was called the ‘growth agenda of the european union’, done in a fiscally responsible way.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i must thank you for an interesting debate, which seems to me to have produced a large majority of the speeches in favour of supporting the commission's position, because it is clear that the need for payment must obviously follow the commitments made in previous years, and it is undeniable that today, when we have a level of ral that has now reached eur 207 million, there is a mountain of accounts to be paid, accounts which are obviously legitimate because they concern legitimate commitments made in previous years and which must now be honoured. the need for payments is concentrated on those headings which are most closely related to development, to economic growth. that is why we must fight the battle of payments, and parliament is clearly giving a signal of this with this mandate for the trilogue. we have asked for interinstitutional cooperation, we have asked for it because it is clear that without a common starting point in terms of information we can and probably will reach different conclusions. we have already had the experience of the conciliation last year and we started from different assessments. we must monitor payments, and that is what we are asking for today, in an empty council seat, but through our mandate for the trilogue we are asking the council to take part in our interinstitutional dialogue so that, at the end of our discussion, when we are discussing and closing the 2013 budget, we can arrive at a joint vision of the real needs. finally, i thank commissioner lewandowski for his loyal cooperation and the groups who will support this mandate for the trilogue tomorrow, which i hope will pass with a large majority so as to give us negotiating power in the discussion we will have with the other institutions next week.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the lisbon treaty abolishes the old comitology system and replaces it with a two-tier structure, based on delegated acts which provide for the right of veto of the european parliament and the council and implementing acts which completely exclude parliament at every stage of their adoption. the existing body of legislation had therefore to be brought into line with the new legal situation. we have started this exercise with the three most important regulations which, mr president, i will deal with all three together, and which form the heart of the agricultural policy, the regulation on direct payments, the regulation on rural development and the regulation on the common organization of the market. the commission's proposals seemed to us at first sight to be fairly balanced and the changes made by the committee on agriculture were very few. in particular, for direct payments, delegated acts should be used where the basic act is amended and where rights are conferred on farmers or where negative consequences for farmers may arise. we also felt that, in the light of the spirit of the treaty on the common agricultural policy in budgetary matters, the financial discipline procedure could no longer be applied without the participation of the european parliament. in fact, to leave article 11, which provides that the council shall act on a proposal from the commission, unchanged would be an unacceptable continuation of the council's exclusive right to exercise directly implementing powers. as regards rural development, we believe that the commission has made a careful breakdown between the more general provisions which lay down complementary elements and therefore require delegated acts and the more technical elements, which are closely linked to the discretion enjoyed by the member states in implementing this measure, which therefore require implementing acts. the proposal for alignment on the regulation on the common organisation of the market has proved more problematic, particularly with regard to the elements linked to article 43 (3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. this article provides that the council, on a proposal from the commission, is to adopt measures relating to the fixing of prices, levies, aid and quantitative restrictions. this is a derogation from article 2 (2) of the same regulation, which provides for the use of the ordinary legislative procedure for the common agricultural policy. as a derogating provision, article 43 (3) must be interpreted strictly, that is, only where there are provisions which are not part of the fundamental political decisions, but which must be taken in accordance with article 43 (2) of the treaty. we therefore consider that the committee's proposal does not interpret article 43 (3) narrowly enough. the definition of the conditions and criteria for fixing the aid, the export refunds, the minimum export prices should remain the responsibility of the legislator, that is to say the parliament and the council, while the commission should be left to fix the amounts by means of implementing acts. once these three reports were approved by a very large majority in the committee on agriculture, we began negotiations with the council and the commission to try to reach an agreement at first reading. the urgency was dictated by the imminent process of reform of the common agricultural policy, which we would have liked to avoid being burdened by complex negotiations on institutional matters. despite our willingness to negotiate and to make some concessions to our initial position, and despite the great activism of the polish presidency, followed by the danish presidency, we have not been able to find a compromise solution, hence the need for the commission to act efficiently and in a timely manner on the one hand and the new and stronger powers conferred on parliament by the lisbon treaty on the other. the main obstacles we have seen are from the council, which wants to systematically and horizontally eliminate delegated acts, even when they are legally necessary, and replace them with implementing acts which completely exclude parliament. we cannot accept this position, because it means renouncing the new prerogatives that the treaty gives us, and it severely limits the powers of parliament. another factor which has made the negotiations more difficult has been the attitude of the commission, which has moved from a position close to that of parliament to the council's positions during the negotiations, leaving us alone in the battle to defend the most authentic interpretation of the treaty. we now have the difficult negotiations on the reform of the cap and have therefore decided to ask the house to confirm the vote on alignment in the committee on agriculture, so that we have more power when we negotiate the future agricultural policy. only by defending the prerogatives of parliament will we be sure of respecting the spirit of the lisbon treaty and at the same time making the cap of the future more democratic and closer to the citizens.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the process of aligning the so-called horizontal regulation with the new rules of the treaty is based on a classification into delegated powers and implementing powers of the provisions adopted by the commission pursuant to the said regulation. after careful examination of the commission proposal in the light of the criteria laid down for the two categories of acts, articles 290 and 291 respectively, we have identified the areas where the conditions for delegated acts are met, and then examined the proposal in terms of the conditions for implementing acts. in the committee on agriculture we proposed and voted on amendments concerning the conditions for delegation, duration, deadline for objecting to a delegated act, extension of deadlines, committee procedures, in accordance with the common understanding on the practical arrangements and use of delegated acts, approved by the conference of presidents on 3 march 2011, and regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the exercise of implementing powers conferred on the commission. in this context, among the points of disagreement with the council, i would also mention the willingness to use implementing acts in situations where, according to the treaty, they would be the most logical and appropriate instrument. i think that this parliament, for its part, cannot afford to give up control over such important and sensitive issues as transparency, article 40a, or sanctions on beneficiaries. these alignment reports, we must admit, are the test bed of a new working method which must be established between parliament, the council and the commission, but which must be as effective as possible, according to a framework of articulated competences which i hope will always converge towards the implementation of effective means for the development of european agriculture. in procedural terms, the majorities required within the council to block an implementing act are exactly the same as for a delegated act. the council's resistance to the use of delegated acts is therefore unjustified and, if maintained, could be an unnecessary obstacle to the reform of the common agricultural policy. i should also say that we have proposed some elements which we believe should be improved, but these, as well as the national disengagement, have not been accepted and agreed by the commission and the council, and will therefore be the subject of negotiation and discussion again in the framework of the horizontal regulation for the reform of the cap. the lack of agreement on the alignment of the horizontal regulation has led us to ask the house to vote on this so that we can have, as president de castro said, greater contractual power and a firm position of parliament on the matter. this report, like the others which have been discussed so far, has nevertheless represented an important moment for this parliament, which for the first time is actively involved in the process of defining the new agricultural policy through codecision. it was not a simple process of transposition, as many have pointed out, but a serious awareness on the part of my colleagues in the agri committee of how well the cap instruments have worked so far, and therefore they must be made fit for the new reform by means of appropriate instruments and useful corrections. i wanted to close with a reference: we have seen through a long series of trilogues the difficulty of reaching agreement on alignment, it was a missed opportunity that risks wasting time in the subsequent process of approving the reform of the common agricultural policy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the rapporteur's report on support for rural development that it should include some important simplification measures, such as the reduction in the number of annual progress reports and summary reports. the commission has also proposed that the rules on the use of advisory services be amended to reduce the administrative burden on member states. i also agree with mr de castro that support for producer associations in the fruit and vegetable sector should not be excluded from the measures to support the establishment and administrative operation of producer associations. i also think it is essential, as the rapporteur has said, that member states which have opted for regional programmes should be allowed to calculate the automatic decommitment of financial resources at member state level. i also agree with mr capoulas santos's position on the report on the financing systems of the european agricultural guarantee fund. i also thank the other colleagues i have not mentioned for their work.
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have listened carefully to your various remarks. i would like to emphasize what i said in my introduction and, in particular, to reply to mr lyon. the commission will support the european parliament wherever legally possible, in accordance with the content of articles 290 and 291. article 290 provides that delegated acts are to be applied to amend or supplement non-essential elements of a legislative act. article 291, as you have said, only gives the commission the possibility of ensuring uniform application of the basic acts. it is in this spirit that we have worked and it is in this spirit that i hope we will work to find the final formulas and an agreement. mr nicholson, who is no longer here, spoke of the growing tensions between parliament and the commission. in any case, i can assure you that i will not fuel these tensions. i think it is in the interest of all - the farmers, as mr olejniczak said, but also the consumers and the european citizens - to reach an agreement. as regards the organic regulations to which mrs patrão neves referred, i am prepared to find a solution which involves parliament in the process of deciding on substances. but we also have to assess the interest of the producer in organic farming. how can we avoid making the decision-making process on a substance too complicated and lengthy? for this reason, i propose as a compromise to analyse that, in the context of the adaptation of the basic regulation on organic farming, we now provide, in a more precise way, the criteria on the basis of which the introduction or non-introduction of a substance is approved. when those criteria become more precise, following an ordinary legislative procedure, and only on the basis of those criteria, the commission could present implementing acts to limit its role to the application of the criteria already included in the basic act. there is also the other possibility you mentioned, namely to include the list of substances in the annex to the basic act, but this would require the ordinary legislative procedure to be applied to each substance, which would risk greatly delaying the adoption process. if we can agree on a set of criteria in the basic act for the adoption of these substances, i hope we can get parliament involved in this procedure. i suggest that we work on these options in order to find a compromise, and i hope that we will do so fairly quickly after the vote tomorrow.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i take this minute to thank my colleagues for their comments and also to thank the commissioner. we are not going to vote for the amendments, but we are going to vote for the amendments which are not in the report. i therefore appeal to the commissioner, we are in the era of lisbon, the council must understand that parliament has new prerogatives, which it does not intend to renounce. we shall be voting tomorrow on the commission's proposal, and we hope that the council will eventually adopt these positions.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that this debate was useful, because the way in which a number of members have expressed their views on the alignment of the various regulations with the treaty of lisbon has confirmed in the presence of the commissioner how much parliament is concerned with maintaining its role and its prerogatives. it is therefore clear that in this context, beyond what we will be voting on tomorrow - which in fact does not differ significantly from the positions initially formulated by the commission - it is just another step in the direction and on the path we must take, not only for the implementation of all the prerogatives given by the lisbon treaty to community regulation, but also and above all in the direction of the new common agricultural policy. mr commissioner, you know very well how many times we have met under the various presidencies. he knows how much effort, commitment and time we have spent on this path, when we have become bogged down in horizontal issues which should have covered all the regulations and we have had difficulty in moving forward. we now need to go back to that. tomorrow's vote is simply an intermediate stage in which parliament, by means of its vote, wishes to make clear once again its position and its determination not to give up its prerogatives. on the other hand, we must begin to work so that alignment with the treaty of lisbon, with all the regulations governing the common agricultural policy, does not become a hindrance to the adoption of the policy itself. we shall meet again on the contents of the agricultural policy, we shall discuss them, this parliament will play its part, but on the alignment with the lisbon treaty i believe that we can start working again immediately to speed up the timetable.
