mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the protection of animal welfare is part of and complementary to sustainable development policy. the european institutions, as signatories to the sustainable development pact, must make a serious effort to ensure that this level is adequate. deterioration in the health status of wild animals may result in increased transmission of contagious diseases to domestic animals, with a negative impact on public health. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that there is a need for better implementation of the existing legislation, with particular attention to the transport of animals. i welcome the inclusion in the strategy of a european framework law on animal welfare and i share the wish of mrs paulsen that this law be formulated clearly and then consulted with all the parties concerned.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, following the first comments on the council, we have now entered the phase of reductive reading, and that is wrong, because important steps have been taken. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the spirit of revival and renewed political unity seems to be returning to the european institutions after so much slowness and torpor, and a will to make real progress towards greater integration. we have seen yesterday a strong unity between parliament and the commission on this. i am not talking about winners and losers, but it is undeniable that there has been a new institutional and political vitality compared with the past diarchy, which was the negation, the very antithesis of the community spirit. there has been a move and an activism by several countries, not to create new exclusionary axes, but to build a common and respectful consensus of all the member states. this is the path to the political objective of unity, without which any union, banking, fiscal or monetary, will be wholly inadequate.
mr president, it must be acknowledged that the european council of 28 june represented an important political step forward, finally in contrast to years of renationalisation of european policies, delays in the process of strengthening and completion of the union's institutional and economic structure to support the single currency. today, to question or threaten vetoes by certain governments or political sectors against the decisions taken and which will be confirmed - i hope - and clarified by the next ecofin meeting is irresponsible and risks undermining the commitment of the european parliament to push forward the common objectives, namely to increase own resources, investment, employment and growth. the question of the tobin tax is on the agenda today, thanks to the efforts of our political group and the italian and french governments, in cooperation with the spanish government, but it must also be a question of a renewed drive towards greater political and economic integration of the european union.
in writing. − following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the powers conferred on the commission under regulation (ec) no 73/2009 need to be aligned with the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in this field, alignment is achieved by this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 73/2009 establishing common rules for direct support schemes for farmers under the common agricultural policy and establishing certain support schemes for farmers. in order to simplify the current regulatory environment and reduce the administrative burden on member states and to ensure greater clarity and legal certainty, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i am also in favour of this report because it contains amendments in terms of alignment and simplification. the treaty of lisbon abolishes the old comitology system and replaces it with delegated and implementing acts. one of the first proposals for alignment establishes common rules for direct support to farmers under the cap and establishes support schemes for farmers. the report examines the european commission proposal and proposes to use delegated acts only in certain cases. on simplification, the proposal provides for a number of provisions on the current regulatory environment and the reduction of the administrative burden for member states, for example the possibility of exempting farmers who do not submit area payment applications or who declare only areas of less than one hectare from the obligation to declare area.
in writing. the vote approves a number of provisions aimed at simplifying the current regulatory environment and reducing the administrative burden on member states. these changes will mainly concern farmers who do not own land eligible for area payments. the new proposal contains changes in terms of alignment, but also provides for a simplification of the regulation. although it is difficult to predict how many farmers may be affected by this change, it can be assumed that there are not many if one takes into account the increasing trend towards decoupling of livestock payments and the transfer to area payments. however, the amendment implies a reduction in the administrative burden for certain member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr de castro's text, which contains a number of provisions designed to simplify the current regulatory environment and reduce the administrative burden on member states. these amendments will relate, inter alia, to cross-compliance and the possibility for member states to exempt from the obligation to declare area those farmers who declare areas of less than one hectare. finally, i would like to emphasize the choice made by the committee on agriculture, which, in the absence of agreement with the council, decided by today's votes to send a strong signal in view of the forthcoming negotiations on the reform of the cap.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr de castro's report, as i welcome the simplification elements introduced in the current regulation, which aims to relieve the member states of some of the administrative burden in the process of aligning council regulation (ec) no 1698/2005 on support for rural development from the eafrd with the new rules of the tfeu.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, so the objective is twofold: firstly, to adapt existing legislation to the new provisions of the treaty concerning the commission's implementing powers and, secondly, to simplify the regulation currently in force (reduction in the number of progress and summary reports required for rural development, simplification of cross-compliance checks and rules for the use of advisory services, etc.). this proposal will increase legal clarity and certainty, thereby making the lisbon treaty a reality for the benefit of citizens, and will allow for a more efficient and targeted use of funds.
in writing. - by voting in favour of the various reports on the common agricultural policy presented today in this chamber, we wish to stress the importance for this parliament of proceeding with the alignment, opposed on several occasions by the council, of the legislative procedures provided for in article 290 of the treaty, which also confers delegated acts on the commission on the revision of the cap. this is a procedure which is essential in order to promote rural development and agricultural activities in our territory. we therefore welcome mr de castro's proposal for the effective and targeted use of eafrd funds in relation to the various beneficiaries, but we regret that, in extending to all member states the possibilities for financing producer associations, the fruit and vegetable sector, which is of strategic importance for european agriculture and for the health of our consumers, has been excluded. we recall that the fruit and vegetable sector contributes to environmental protection, economic growth and the creation of many direct and indirect jobs, which have been affected by the current economic crisis in many regions of the union. we hope that the commission can solve this problem and include the fruit and vegetable sector among the beneficiaries of the eafrd.
in writing. − the treaty provisions provide for a distinction between the powers delegated to the commission to adopt non-legislative acts of general application supplementing or amending certain non-essential elements of a legislative act and the powers of the commission to adopt uniform conditions for the implementation of legally binding union acts. in order to ensure an effective and targeted use of the funds as regards the treatment of beneficiaries, by giving the commission the task of adding further elements necessary for the proper functioning of the scheme proposed by the legislator himself, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − in relation to the existing regulation, the commission may, by means of delegated acts, introduce derogations from the rule that rural development support shall not be granted for measures financed by common market organisations. i am in favour of the report by mr de castro which suggests that we should ensure that the resources available are used effectively and in a targeted manner as regards the treatment of beneficiaries when covered by delegated acts. the regulation introduces simplification elements, alongside which the incentive element for measures approved under article 43 of the treaty, cofinanced rural development measures, should be introduced. the commission rightly proposes to extend to all member states the possibilities of financing to support the establishment and administrative operation of producer associations. the report considers the exclusion of fruit and vegetable producer associations from support to be discriminatory.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend to all member states the existing funding opportunities for supporting the establishment and administrative operation of producer associations, but the rapporteur considers it discriminatory to exclude support for producer associations in the fruit and vegetable sector. the aim is to ensure effective and targeted use of funds in relation to the treatment of beneficiaries, which is essentially covered by delegated acts in the proposal. other provisions concerning the practical arrangements for the programmes, measures and standards are covered in the proposal by implementing acts to be adopted by the member states. in order to harmonise the eafrd and the erdf, vat on non-taxable persons such as public institutions will become eligible for eafrd support.
in writing. - the report by mr de castro on the proposal for a regulation on the common organization of agricultural markets and on specific provisions for certain agricultural products (single cmo regulation) was approved by my group. this is a commitment to avoid placing an unjustified burden on the substantial reform of the single market if the commission's proposal for alignment were still being negotiated. i do so in the knowledge that there is still much work to be done within the dossier.
in writing. - recalling the need to align council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 establishing a common organisation of agricultural markets (single cmo) with the new distinction between delegated powers and implementing powers of the commission introduced by articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the proposal gives the legislator the power to define the essential elements of the common organisation of agricultural markets. in order to leave it to the legislator to define the conditions and criteria for fixing aid, export refunds and minimum export prices, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - in a historical context of economic uncertainty and market volatility, community support is essential to boost the competitiveness of the agricultural sector globally. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's trade policy and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's trade policy. i support the need to achieve the fundamental objectives of improving the functioning of the single market, making wise use of the structural funds, maximising the benefits of cohesion policy, ensuring stability and improving access to finance. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not undermined by the introduction of new measures.
in writing. − in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the alignment of regulation (ec) no 1290/2005 with the new treaty rules is based on a classification into delegated powers and implementing powers of the provisions adopted by the commission pursuant to that regulation. in view of the amendments concerning the conditions for delegation and the consequent simplification and reduction of the administrative burden on the member states, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the adoption of this text is crucial because it contains our agricultural policy, which is the most important chapter in the union's budget. the amendments to regulation (ec) no 1290/2005 aim at simplification and efficiency; this means that farmers are actually helped and bureaucracy is reduced by eliminating the complex and burdensome procedures for the member states. i hope that both the commission and the council will adopt a constructive approach to reaching an agreement, and i shall vote in favour of the amendments proposed by mr la via.
in writing. i have wanted to support mr häusling's report, because it takes up and develops, in the field of organic production and labelling of organic products, certain principles which i consider to be fundamental for this sector: to respond to consumer expectations regarding the quality of organic products, to ensure the proper enforcement of the legislation by the authorities, bodies and operators concerned, and to safeguard the proper functioning of the single market and trade.
in writing. − this report calls, in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), for the current regulation (ec) no 834/2007 to be aligned by applying the principle of the distinction between measures of an implementing nature and measures of a delegated nature. in order to better meet consumers' expectations of the quality of organic products, the commission has adopted specific rules for the application of this regulation. the commission has made a clear distinction between the provisions in this respect and i therefore vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the current regulation (ec) no 834/2007 must be aligned by applying the principle of the distinction between measures of an implementing nature and measures of a delegated nature. the commission shall adopt, by means of implementing acts, the necessary provisions to ensure uniform application of this regulation throughout the union, with particular reference, for example, to the details and specifications concerning the content, form and manner of notification, presentation and exchange of information. i am glad that the commission has made a careful allocation of the provisions, and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.

in writing. - the package of basic cap regulations to be adopted in lisbon has been greatly delayed by the council's rigidity and by a shift in the polish presidency which prevented us from concluding the agreements previously defined. today we are dealing not only with the old regulations in the package, but also with new texts on the cap and with the adoption of the adaptation in lisbon, which was approved by comagri in april 2011. the amendments to the treaty of lisbon, which abolish the old comitology system, allow the commission to exercise powers of implementation and execution and change the role of the european council, which may, on a proposal from the commission, adopt measures relating to the fixing of prices, levies, aid and quantitative restrictions, show us even more clearly the important role of parliament. it is therefore necessary to bring the legislative body into line with the new legal reality, an alternative system consistent with articles 290 and 291, a system which enables us, the european parliament, to act for the protection of farmers, land, products and agricultural markets.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr susta's recommendation because by joining the wto the russian federation is obliged to commit itself to adapting its trade agreements with the other countries to the principles of free trade. the agreement on the relaxation of restrictions in the russian services sector will bring the european union considerable benefits in a sector which currently represents 20% of european exports to the russian federation.
in writing. − by becoming a member of the wto, russia will become a country relatively open to foreign services, giving foreign service providers substantially greater market access opportunities. not only will such commitments by russia create more business opportunities for european companies, but they will also improve the situation for european exporters and investors currently working with russia, including in terms of non-discrimination and free competition. in order to ensure that the european union continues to benefit from a regime more favourable than the multilateral one, i am voting in favour of the conclusion of the bilateral 'new agreement' between the european union and russia.
in writing. - i support mr susta's report. of course, these openings by russia, even with its imminent entry into the world trade organization, are good news. russia is a very important market for our companies. i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the community.
in writing. − with russia's accession to the world trade organisation, the country will gradually open up to foreign services. russia has therefore agreed to lower its barriers to trade and investment and to grant more favourable treatment than before to foreign suppliers in eleven sectors including professional services, information technology, construction, postal services, telecommunications, media, transport, distribution, tourism and travel services and financial services. the most important commitments were the concessions in the telecommunications sector, namely the phasing-out within four years of the current limit (49%) on foreign shareholdings in telecommunications groups and the decision to apply the terms of the agreement on basic telecommunications. in the financial sector, the commercial presence of foreign insurers on the russian market will be allowed under certain restrictive conditions, nine years after accession to the world trade organisation. the vote therefore approves the agreement between the union and russia on safeguarding commitments on trade in services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the agreement whereby the eu and russia commit themselves to each other on the liberalisation of services. in particular, this agreement commits russia to amend its domestic legislation to bring its laws in many areas into line with the rules and status of membership of the world trade organisation. as regards the trade effects of the agreement, it will be essential in the course of the negotiations to replace the partnership and cooperation agreement concluded in 1994 to update the terms of the bilateral commitments in order to obtain additional commitments from russia.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr zalewski's recommendation because it is one of the tasks of the european union to combat the practice of relocation where it damages the productive fabric of the member states for the benefit of a third country, in this case the russian federation. i therefore agree with the need to protect european car manufacturers from having to conclude agreements with russia which are disadvantageous to the european union and which involve the production of a large number of cars in russia, as this would lead to a significant drop in european union exports to russia and consequently to a significant economic loss for the member states.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the russian accession package allows for certain trade-distorting measures, such as the package of investment measures affecting trade in the automotive sector in russia, which are largely prohibited by the wto trim agreement. these measures require the location of vehicle manufacturers in russia (which results in discriminatory treatment for imported vehicle parts and components and a restriction on imports) and link them to special investment privileges for the import of automotive components (reduction or abolition of import duties). the maintenance of these mechanisms is detrimental to the eu and russia. in order to encourage the growth of trade in motor vehicles and their components between the eu and russia, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - this agreement with russia is a positive one and i voted for it. i hope, however, that these events will help the european commission to understand that the union will have to think about protecting its own industrial system at least to the same extent as our international partners are doing. this agreement is positive, but it does not remove the difficulties which our companies in this sector have encountered and still encounter in order to continue to produce in europe. the european commission must listen to their needs and defend the work of the 27 member states of the union.
in writing. the russian government has been trying for several years to attract foreign manufacturers of cars and their components to its territory in order to compensate for the decline of its domestic automotive industry and to provide jobs for the industry's workforce. russia is a fast-growing market for the sale of cars and easier access would be very beneficial for european union producers: russia currently accounts for only 8% of total exports of these products. i am voting in favour of the agreement with the russian federation on this matter. of components for motor vehicles. the whole of the european union's automobile industry, which represents 2.3 million jobs in vehicle manufacturing and 10.3 million indirect jobs, will benefit from this.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs vaidere's recommendation because this agreement will ensure the reduction of the duties in force so far by the russian federation on timber exports. european companies in the sector will benefit from this agreement, although russia may continue to apply high rates for certain types of wood.
in writing. − in the context of its wto accession process, the russian federation has agreed to reduce its current export duties on raw materials, including wood products. for certain types of wood, in particular certain species of conifers, russia has introduced tariff quotas. a specific part of the quotas was allocated to exports to the eu. in order to avoid a repeat of the successive increases in the export duties on wood applied by russia and to be able to manage the provisions relating to the application of the tariff quotas, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the issue of raw materials is one of the most sensitive. the union is right to deal with russia, one of the largest holders of natural raw materials, to ensure a source of vital importance for our industry. the same kind of agreements should also be concluded with countries like china. i voted in favour of the vaidere report.
in writing. − in the context of its accession to the world trade organisation, the russian federation has committed itself to gradually reducing or eliminating its current export duties on a list of raw materials. the undertakings concerning the export duty rates have been included in the list of concessions and commitments for goods from russia. the commission has also received comments from the russian authorities. the list contained in the agreement in question is therefore very long and includes very important raw materials. these are raw materials not included in the list of concessions and commitments on the goods referred to above, for which russia holds more than 10% of world production or exports or in which the european union has a substantial interest. with these comments on the subject i am voting in favour of the agreement to introduce or increase tariffs on raw materials.
in writing. − i am against this agreement and therefore i support this resolution. i believe the main problem of this text is its vagueness and the uncertainty over its interpretation. as a member of the european parliament i have the duty to guarantee adequate protection for citizens’ rights. i totally agree on the need for an international agreement to step up the fight against counterfeit products. the debate is whether acta is the right vehicle to do that. and my answer is not. i also would like to stress that the presumed primary beneficiaries of the agreement, the artistic communities and software creators, seem particularly divided on the potential benefits of the agreement. in addition we must condemn the total lack of transparency throughout the negotiations on acta. the commission could have done a lot more to keep the parliament informed about ongoing negotiations and this mistake is for us unacceptable.
in writing. - i voted against the acta agreement for several reasons: first of all, i do not think it is an effective solution to counterfeiting because the contracting countries as a whole account for only 5% of the world's counterfeiting, and it will not affect emerging economic powers such as brazil, russia, india and china, where counterfeiting is very important. secondly, there is no reference to geographical indications and therefore it does not protect the italian and european quality agri-food sector, and therefore it does not bring any benefit to 'made in italy'. these are the main considerations which led me not to support the acta trade agreement in plenary.
in writing. - i abstained on the vote on the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement (acta). my abstention is based on the fact that the european court of justice, after the european commission's request to give an opinion on the compatibility of the agreement with the eu treaties and the fundamental rights of citizens, has not yet ruled. it will take 14 to 20 months before the court gives its opinion. i think it is important that a body like the court of justice has a say in matters with implications for workers' rights and international trade. i would, however, argue that the adoption of this type of agreement can be important in ensuring innovation, creativity and the protection of workers in europe. the marketing of counterfeit medicines or fake fashion products is unacceptable, as they create disadvantages and unfair competition for companies involved in the sector and are dangerous for the safety of citizens, as they are often produced with materials and working techniques that do not meet european safety standards.
in writing. - the fight against commercial counterfeiting and computer piracy is certainly a major challenge, but we must be very careful about how it is implemented and interpreted. firstly, i am puzzled that an agreement of this magnitude does not cover the countries where the most violations of trade rights and protections occur, namely china, india and pakistan. the european parliament has already expressed its views on the commission's proposal. acta has also raised serious concerns as a potential infringement of individual rights and freedoms and as a brake on free access to the internet. for all these reasons i therefore voted in favour of the report, rejecting the text of the agreement: i hope, however, that negotiations can be resumed in the near future to find a more common solution to combat the scourge of counterfeiting, without repeating the mistakes and shortcomings of acta.
in writing. - acta was to be an agreement capable of combating counterfeiting and piracy without restricting the freedoms of citizens, not just preventing unfair competition from industry and protecting intellectual property rights. unfortunately, the text which has been examined by the commission and parliament has not covered the issues which are of most concern to our country, namely the protection of protected designations of origin and geographical indications and the main counterfeiting countries china, brazil and india. the text was so inconsistent that the competent committees inta and itre themselves rejected it, just as a favourable report was rejected in the legal affairs committee and a report against it was approved in libe. it is clear that this measure, in such a negative situation, and which must be approved by both the member states of the union and third countries to be valid, could not have received a favourable vote in the chamber. i abstained because, although i believe that the anti-counterfeiting agreement is essential to protect our companies and farms, i believe that the text under discussion is detrimental to human freedoms and is not suitable for targeting the markets for counterfeit goods, not least because it does not cover categories of products such as agricultural products which i believe should be protected.
in writing. - my vote on acta was negative. one of the main culprits in this defeat for the union's credibility is commissioner de gucht. i think that he would do well to resign rather than insist on this agreement. the european parliament has repeatedly called for geographical indications to be included in acta, but commissioner de gucht has not been able to negotiate this with the counterparties. the doubts about the violation of fundamental rights are too serious to allow an agreement like this to be approved. the fight against counterfeiting requires specific instruments and above all the involvement of those countries, especially those in asia, which are the main producers of this enormous disaster for our companies.

in writing. the report by mr luis manuel capoulas santos on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 73/2009 as regards the application of direct payments to farmers for 2013 and proposing to rebalance national allocations between 'old' and 'new' eu countries was voted on in plenary today. for the former, the adjustment rate in 2013 would be 0% for amounts between eur 5 000 and eur 300 000 and 4% for amounts above eur 300 000. the level of compulsory modulation for the latter would remain the same as in 2012, at 10% for amounts between eur 5 000 and eur 300 000 and 14% for amounts above eur 300 000. the draft amends the total amount of direct payments that each state may pay in 2013: for the eu-15 member states, with some exceptions, the value of the net ceiling in 2013 would be the same as in 2012, adjusted to take account of the estimated grubbing-up of vineyards in that year; for eu-10 countries, the value of the net ceiling in 2013 shall be adjusted to the amounts committed to finance the specific support.
in writing. − the current rules for the system of direct payments to farmers should be replaced by the reform proposals for the future cap for the period 2014-2020. this proposal instead addresses the financial provisions for the transitional year, 2013. the main purpose is to set the net ceilings for direct payments for 2013, providing for a similar adjustment mechanism to that of modulation. continuity in payment levels is needed, taking into account the progressivity of direct payments in the new member states and the end of voluntary modulation. during the first and only trilogue, the council accepted the position which my colleagues and i wanted to put forward as a parliament. the council has asked for a new article to be added to the legal base, which was approved by the european parliament's legal affairs committee. i believe that the rules for direct payments for 2013 will fill a time gap in a valid way and that is why i voted in favour. this period will prepare farmers for the new cap rules after 2014.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the mandate for the trilogue on the 2013 budget: i think that the right priorities have been set, such as the need to provide the resources and instruments needed to honour the commitments and hence the payments already undertaken under previous agreements and now to be settled. this can certainly be a good thing for the economy, and in particular for small and mediumsized enterprises, which are in dire need of these funds. the need to minimise the bureaucratic and administrative expenditure of the european union has also been rightly stressed, and in this sense the renewed call for a single seat for the european parliament should also be welcomed. a budget of the union, however sober and responsible, can help in a difficult situation such as the present one: it is up to those who receive the funds to make the best use of them, and not to do as has unfortunately happened too many times in the past. i am referring in particular to the regions of southern italy, which have a chronic lack of capacity to absorb these funds, which often end up in fraud to the detriment of the eu, as in the recent case of salerno-reggio calabria.

in writing. − today's vote underlines how the european parliament wants to make a full commitment to boosting growth in 2013 and how this must be achieved by fighting unemployment. it is necessary that all the states which have doubts about the estimates of expenditure presented by the commission should immediately ask for explanations in this regard, in order to avoid difficulties later on in the negotiations. with eur 151 million in commitment appropriations and eur 138 million in payment appropriations, a concrete basis has been created for the european economy to be able to intervene effectively, despite the crisis affecting the national governments and their budgets.
in writing. − the mandate for the trilogue contains an assessment of the draft budget, adopted by the commission on 25 april, and sets out parliament's positions for the trilogue of 9 july and for the next eu budget negotiations, starting in autumn 2013. with a level of payment appropriations that is 6.8% higher than in the 2012 budget, i believe that the draft budget represents a positive step towards a realistic budget and a responsible budgetary exercise, but with room for improvement still needed, particularly in the areas of cohesion and agriculture to avoid a lack of funds in 2013. as regards commitments, however, there is some concern that the proposed increase (+ 2%) would virtually freeze commitments at eu level by a projected inflation rate which would not allow priorities at eu level to be clearly identified.
in writing. the report for which i voted in favour today concerns the opening of the second stage of the budgetary procedure and defines parliament's position in view of the next trilogue scheduled for july. the main objective for the 2013 budget is to defend an adequate level of resources to meet the commitments made in previous years, while ensuring continuity of investment to support the competitiveness of european businesses at a time of severe economic crisis.
in writing. - the important and balanced own-initiative report by mrs paulsen. it is significant that he obtained a large majority of the votes in the chamber. equally important is the fact that the principle of equivalence of rules for imports from third countries, with stricter controls on animals, will be safeguarded. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of animal by-products.
in writing. − ensuring the protection and welfare of animals is part of our practices to improve the sustainability of our agricultural and food production. this report sets out a strategy for the three-year period 2012-2014 with the clear aim of strengthening the protection of animals and, consequently, of consumers. animal welfare is a complex and multifaceted issue with implications for policies in individual member states and at international level. the decisions we take in this area are therefore never merely negotiated and require a high degree of deliberation. i am also convinced that greater protection of animal health is also necessary for the protection of the consumer and the environment. however, i think it is appropriate to stress that while it is good that animal welfare is protected, it is also necessary to avoid that excessive legislation on this matter becomes a further obstacle to activities in the agri-food sector.
in writing. - i support the commission's proposal for a european union strategy for the protection and welfare of animals 2012-2015. in fact, i believe that high and controlled animal welfare is a fundamental pillar of sustainable development and that it is essential to protect animal health as well as human health. the proposal is crucial to increasing productivity and competitiveness in the primary sector. the new framework law provides the conditions for the creation of a clear and shared european network for the joint coordination of animal welfare. this will help to increase competitiveness both in the internal market and in trade with third countries, as well as to increase product quality and safety. i also think it is very important that the new proposals on the rights of farm animals should also have the right to good food, medical care and living conditions that are not stressful and forced.
in writing. - i wanted to give my support to this report on the european strategy to support animal welfare. among the stated objectives are, in fact, some issues to which i am particularly sensitive: i am referring, for example, to a serious campaign to combat and prevent straying, through concrete and effective measures which protect the animals themselves in the first place and which also limit the risks to the human population. another important point concerns the call for non-stunning slaughter, typical of some religious rituals, such as the preparation of halal islamic meat: it is a pointless barbarity, which cannot be accepted on the basis of a simple traditional religious prescription, which is far removed from our culture and civilization. a european regulatory framework can certainly be useful in establishing common rules and bases for respecting and protecting animal welfare, without this of course having to mean imposing absurd rules which may penalize, for example, those who produce or trade in this area.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to further improve animal welfare in the european union, despite the fact that animal welfare problems persist in several member states. europe needs a comprehensive approach and a comprehensive legislative framework on animal welfare to maximise policy coherence between member states. the new strategy also draws on experience gained in this field and on recent scientific and technological developments. in voting for this report, i support europe's desire to reconcile economic realities with animal welfare.
in writing. − we welcome the commission's communication on the strategy for the protection and welfare of animals which we have helped to improve. high animal welfare is part of sustainable development and is therefore a key element in defending the health of citizens, productivity and competitiveness of the livestock sector in europe. however, we must ensure a new uniform and harmonised approach in all member states where there is still a lack of compliance with certain national animal welfare legislation: we note the continued abuse of the derogations granted for the slaughter of animals without stunning for religious or ritual reasons, turning a blind eye to the unnecessary suffering and confusion created for consumers; we are not going to allow the extermination of stray animals in some member states through urban cleaning policies, neglecting the state's responsibility for abandoned animals, including stray animals. we allow the establishment of kennels without permits and controls on staff and facilities. we believe that a framework law is essential to harmonize national legislation on animal welfare by requiring the member states to report annually on the implementation of european legislation, thus enabling the commission to take effective action if the obligations are not respected. only then will we have a fairer world for them too.
in writing. - the report on the protection of animal welfare, although it does not deal with the problem of reducing animal transport to 8 hours, a subject for which i have campaigned as it will be dealt with in a separate document later, is overall balanced and therefore my vote was in favour. particular attention was paid to the abuse of derogations to allow for the slaughter of animals without stunning them in the eu, which i consider unacceptable in civilised countries, and to the note calling on the european commission to speed up the assessment of the labelling of meat from these animals. there are also calls on the european commission to improve animal welfare in farms and to adopt good animal husbandry practices, bearing in mind that a better quality of life for the animal often also leads to a better quality of the product that ends up on the tables of consumers. classical examples are cattle grazed instead of kept in pens or laying hens reared on land or in battery farms. i also agree with the passage on the search for alternatives to animal testing, as it is not an indispensable technique and is more expensive.
in writing. − high animal welfare is part of sustainable development and is essential to protect animal health, public health and the productivity and competitiveness of the livestock sector in europe. however, the complexity of european and national animal welfare rules and the lack of information on them create legal uncertainty, while the lack of compliance and 'legal targets' distorts competition. a new approach to animal welfare is therefore needed, one that is based on science and proven experience gained over the years and in which the rules are easily understandable and controllable. an essential factor in achieving a uniform level of animal welfare in the european union is the provision of accurate, practical and understandable training, information and guidance to those who deal with animals on a daily basis. the vote underlines the need for a european framework law on animal welfare. the concepts underlying this law will be clarity, simplification and practical applicability, based on a scientific basis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the establishment of a new european union legal framework for the protection of domestic and stray animals. the resolution seeks to define new rules for the identification and registration of animals and to include strategies for the management of stray animals, including vaccination and castration programmes, measures to promote responsible ownership, a ban on unauthorised kennels and shelters and a ban on the killing of stray animals without medical advice. i also welcome the proposal to set up school programmes for information and education on animal welfare to raise public awareness of the issue. i also welcome the proposal to impose severe sanctions on any member state which does not comply with the rules contained in the new proposal.

in writing. − there is currently no european union legislation on the protection of pets and stray animals, despite the estimated number of pets in europe of over 100 million. often these animals are the victims of ill-treatment and cruelty in many member states and all too often petitioners refer mainly to the member states of southern and eastern europe. the vote aims to define a legal framework for the protection of pets and stray animals. it is therefore necessary to ratify the european convention for the protection of pet animals and to transpose its provisions into national legal systems. measures are needed such as rules on the identification and registration of animals, the prohibition of unauthorised kennels and shelters, as well as strategies for the management of stray animals, including vaccination and castration programmes, and measures to promote responsible ownership.
in writing. − the resolution on the establishment of an eu legal framework for the protection of domestic and stray animals recalls that the european union is founded on the sharing of different principles and values. millions of europeans attach a special emotional value to animals, especially pets such as dogs and cats. there are more than 100 million of these pets in europe, but despite the scale of the phenomenon, the union has not yet developed a european framework legislation to protect our pet friends and stray pets. the european parliament, by voting today, is giving voice to thousands of european citizens and is strongly calling for the union to establish a european legal framework to protect our animal friends, including: • rules for the identification and registration of animals; • stray animal management strategies, including vaccination and sterilisation programmes; • measures to promote responsible ownership; • prohibition of unauthorised kennels and shelters; • prohibition of killing stray animals without medical indication; • school programmes for information and education on animal welfare; • strict sanctions against any member state which does not comply with the rules.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the conclusions of the european council of 28 and 29 june 2012 because i welcome the decisions taken, both in the short and long term, to strengthen our economic and monetary union. in particular, i welcome the short-term interventions, which have been designed to ensure greater financial stability and to break the vicious circle between banks and sovereign debts. a 'single supervisory mechanism' has been established which, through the esm and the ecb's participation, can directly finance banks. the so-called 'anti-spread shield' also provides for the use of the state-saving fund for the most virtuous countries in order to reassure the markets and lower the level of interest rates. the council's decisions on growth and employment are welcome in the long term. this involves the mobilisation of eur 120 billion for new investment and a eur 10 billion increase in the capital of the european investment bank. to this end, the next multiannual financial framework will have to be consistent with the objectives of growth and employment. however, much remains to be done in the completion of economic and monetary union.
in writing. the european council has drawn up a four-point platform for the relaunch of the euro. first, the spread shield will allow european funds from the esf and the esm to be used more flexibly to buy government bonds on the primary and secondary markets. the aim is to achieve a banking union, in which banking supervision will be transferred to the european central bank, and an economic union: the council of the european union will present a road map to strengthen economic integration between the member states and create a budgetary union by the end of the year. the last aspect concerns growth with a 120 billion plan based on a recapitalisation of the eib, new project bonds, a reorientation of the structural funds and a more efficient use of the community budget. this ambitious programme calls for a rapid revival of the euro and the european economy.

in writing. − with this report we ask the european commission to provide a comprehensive picture of the accessibility of basic banking services to european citizens. such a mapping is necessary in order to be able to take the necessary actions to implement these services. basic banking services today serve as a basic requirement for all citizens of the union and also serve as a backdrop for the social fabric of a country. access to banking services is the key to accessing health services, benefiting from the internal market and accessing employment channels. the spread and extension of basic banking services to as many citizens of the european union as possible is the impetus we are giving to the commission, formalising the request to take concrete and timely action in this area.
in writing. − access to basic payment services is one of the prerequisites for european consumers to benefit from the internal market, free movement, money transfers and the purchase of goods and services without excessive transaction costs. access to basic paid services is increasingly a key prerequisite for social inclusion in terms of access to employment, healthcare and housing. general economic and social development contributes to a high penetration of bank accounts: the commission has also been able to identify the most appropriate measures to be taken to ensure that the services provided by the public authorities are not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies. given that not all member states have taken the appropriate steps required by the commission's recommendation on access to a basic payment account, and that in too many member states providers are still not legally obliged to offer basic payment services, we ask the commission to present a detailed assessment of the situation in all member states and to submit a proposal for a directive guaranteeing access to basic payment services for all consumers legally resident in the union.
in writing. - access to basic banking services has become an essential part of every citizen's life and there must be guarantees that this principle is respected. the report adopted calls for european citizens to be given the opportunity to benefit, free of charge or at reasonable cost, from tools such as access to a basic current account and standard payment services. it is right that banks should make this service available to the widest possible range of people, who may not be able to afford the often very high figures associated with the management of a current account. however, there must also be the necessary guarantees, and that is why it seemed to me a risky and perhaps propaganda move to extend this possibility to homeless people: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right of initiative in the matter of the internal market. i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative in this area.
in writing. − whereas access to basic payment services is one of the prerequisites for consumers to benefit from the internal market in this case from free movement, transfers of funds and the purchase of goods and services without excessive costs for the execution of transactions, whereas basic payment services are essential for consumers to reap the benefits of electronic commerce, whereas, in particular, access to basic payment services is increasingly a key prerequisite for social inclusion in terms of access to employment, healthcare and housing, in order to ensure access to payment services for all consumers legally resident in the eu, i express my vote in favour of the proposal, as well as the recommendations contained in the proposal.
in writing. - today at the strasbourg plenary session we voted on the report by mr klute. the non-legislative resolution voted today argues that basic banking services should be a right for the 10% of eu citizens who currently do not have it and urged the commission to come forward with a legislative proposal by january next year to address this financial exclusion. community-wide regulation is necessary because simple recommendations from the commission have had the desired effect in only a few countries and banks have a natural tendency to target only those customers who offer opportunities for profit. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's financial institutions are able to comply with the obligations of the treaty and the treaty on european union. the basic account would allow a person to carry out all the main payment transactions, such as crediting income or other benefits, paying utilities or taxes, purchasing goods and services, making cash withdrawals and printing account statements.
in writing. − the european commission needs to come forward as soon as possible with a legislative proposal that makes basic banking services a right for european citizens. the basic current account must enable all the main operations to be carried out: from the accreditation of income to the payment of utilities or taxes, from the purchase of goods and services to the withdrawal of cash. this opportunity must be given to everyone, including the homeless, students, low-income people and migrant workers, because banks must have a responsibility to society and not be always and only profit-oriented.
in writing. − the smooth functioning of the internal market and the development of a modern social market economy depend on the provision of affordable and easily accessible basic payment services on a universal scale by the social responsibility of the banking sector. access to basic payment services is also one of the prerequisites for consumers to benefit from the internal market, the free movement and transfer of funds and the purchase of goods and services without excessive transaction costs. on average, basic payment services cost between eur 185 and eur 365 per consumer per year. the vote calls on the commission to present a detailed assessment of the situation in all member states by september 2012 and to submit a proposal for a directive guaranteeing access to basic payment services for all consumers legally resident in the union by 2013.
in writing. − it is now established that the smooth functioning of the internal market and the development of a modern social market economy depend, inter alia, on the provision of basic payment services which are affordable and easily accessible to all: in this way, european consumers can benefit from the internal market, in particular from free movement, transfers of funds and the purchase of goods and services without excessive transaction costs. i therefore expressed my support for mr klute's text, which calls on the european institutions to take action to ensure that the greatest possible number of citizens of the union have access to basic banking services.

in writing. the vote will amend the protocol on the statute of the court of justice of the european union. first, it is proposed to introduce the office of vice-president of the court of justice of the european union. this measure is necessary because the workload of its president has increased considerably over time and it would therefore be useful if, in the performance of his duties, he could be replaced or assisted in the future by a vice-president. moreover, for several years now, the imbalance between the cases dealt with by the court of first instance and the new proceedings brought has been increasingly marked and the number of cases not dealt with has been steadily increasing. at the end of 2010, there were 1 300 cases pending, while 527 cases had been dealt with during the year. the average duration of a procedure also increased from 20.9 to 27.2 months. that is why we need to hire 12 new judges.
in writing. - i intend to support the dossier on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on temporary judges of the civil service tribunal of the european union. i agree with mrs thein that it is appropriate to introduce temporary judges in the specialised courts in order not to prejudice the work of the court of first instance if one of the seven full members is absent for a long period. this amendment to the statute and annex i will not impose any burden on the member states.
in writing. the european parliament has adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia, in which it calls on the council to take action to ensure that the situation in the former yugoslavia is not further complicated by the threat of a military coup. the court of first instance shall consist of seven judges and its functioning may be seriously affected if one of its members is unable to perform his duties for a long period without suffering from any form of invalidity within the meaning of article 10 of council regulation no 422/67/eec, no 5/67/euratom. in order to avoid a situation which would impede the exercise of judicial functions, it is proposed to amend article 62c of the statute of the court of justice by providing for the possibility of assigning temporary judges to the specialised courts. the proposal provides that, on the initiative of the president of the court of justice, the council of the european union shall draw up a list of three persons, chosen from among former members of the court of justice of the european union, as interim judges. for four years, they would be allowed to perform judicial duties only in the strict sense of the term and would not be entitled to participate in the administration of the civil service tribunal or in the election of the president of the tribunal and the presidents of the chambers.
in writing. - in order to avoid the civil service tribunal being in a situation which would impede the exercise of its judicial functions, it is proposed to amend article 62c of the statute of the court of justice by providing, in general, for the possibility of assigning temporary judges to specialised courts. in accordance with article 62c of the statute, as amended, the assignment of temporary judges to the civil service tribunal requires an amendment of annex i to the statute. the vote will be taken on the proposal from the court of justice, since it is a reasonable solution to a practical problem which could seriously hamper the work of the european civil service tribunal.

in writing. − finally, after having focused on financial stability and economic rigour, the eu is now once again discussing growth. it is a pity, however, that we have to admit that the means available are not adequate for the purpose. bond lending is undoubtedly a useful tool to attract as much private investment as possible in the financing of infrastructure works in the fields of transport, energy and broadband networks. we are talking here about sectors whose operation is essential for the development of the european internal market. it is therefore easy to imagine the negative consequences in terms of economic growth and employment that would result from the failure to develop these factors. that said, in the face of a need for eur 1 500 billion for infrastructure, we are now talking about a budget of eur 230 million (because that is the figure envisaged by the european union). all we can say is that we have taken a tiny step in the right direction. but very small. it is not with these figures that we can achieve the development that we urgently need in the areas of transeuropean networks. we are giving the european citizens the impression that europe is worryingly lacking in ambition in dealing with the current economic situation.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we have finally reached the final debate and final adoption of this important regulation. first of all, i should like to say that i am personally very pleased with the work done by all the shadow rapporteurs and all those who have spoken, both by the commission and by the council. we've achieved this together. we have also, within a year, approved one of the most important dossiers for the internal market, by passing it at first reading and thus simplifying the legislative procedure. i think i can say very clearly that this is a real success for the european parliament, which has made a considerable contribution to the final text of the regulation. the role of parliament is therefore certainly being strengthened and i hope that this important institution, which is the one that really represents the european citizens, will be given ever greater impetus and involvement in the future. mr president, i shall now briefly highlight some of the peculiarities of the rules of procedure and stress the importance of these changes. firstly, with the entry into force of this regulation, the system will continue to be based on well-established principles, so that it will be voluntary, private and based on the principle of national delegation. in fact, our intention was not to overturn a system that works and has worked quite well, but to identify the adjustments needed to make it more democratic and competitive on a european and international scale. in addition, we have ensured the most active and effective participation of stakeholders, who also have public relevance, in the consultation phase, both before and after the mandate is drawn up. this is a very important point because it increases democracy and consensus around a standard by all the actors involved, both the market and public actors and public relevance. to ensure that this consultation takes place at all stages of the process, parliament asked the european commission to set up a notification system which would allow stakeholders to register and thus be automatically informed. it is right to ensure the participation of businesses and public interest groups in the system, but it is equally important to ensure the presence of public authorities and bodies with legislative or administrative functions in the process. another point of particular importance is the protection of small and mediumsized enterprises and the simplification of their participation, which i personally strongly wanted to see in the regulation, especially at national level, because small and mediumsized enterprises, both because of their small size and because of linguistic problems, have greater difficulties in being an active part of the system, although they are in fact the economic basis of our european system. the european level must help to ensure this representation, but it must start from the bottom up. so we've built a bottom-up system. the system that will come into force will be more coordinated between the different levels of play, from the national to the european level, and will also be better connected to the international level, which is one of the major objectives we are setting ourselves, because it is essential that the european union promotes and disseminates its standards on a world scale, so that they become universal standards. an important dialogue has been initiated with the united states, in particular with the mission we carried out in washington with the imco commission, and we are continuing along this road. the european parliament, however, rejected the council's request for implementing acts on technical specifications in the field of ict, or information and communication technologies, because they would add enormous weight to the commission's work, slowing down the whole process. however, parliament has ensured a consultation phase before the commission can decide whether or not to identify a technical specification. in conclusion, i think i can say that the regulation simplifies the whole system in administrative and financial terms, ensuring a high level of transparency. we have, for example, introduced the publication on the commission's website of the list of harmonised standards which have been the subject of a formal objection decision. i shall not go into this further, partly because the important aspects are innumerable and i would risk going too far into the technical aspects of a very complex dossier. i therefore leave room for debate and remain open to any clarification.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to turn briefly to the commissioner, who has said, and i agree, that the rapporteur's work has been excellent. i think the committees have helped to enrich the original proposal by updating it. there are undoubtedly new elements in the final text, such as the participation of stakeholders in the decision-making process, the access of small and medium-sized enterprises to standards, the introduction of the social clause - not a foregone conclusion but of great importance - and the recognition of the multi-stakeholder platform itself, these are components that add value and quality to the final result. as regards services, while i appreciate and approve the balance achieved, i think it is necessary to take into account, for the future, a new measure which will allow a process of harmonization without this becoming a burden on citizens or an element of unfair competition between economic systems. the work that has been done has been demanding and very substantial, but perhaps we should already start thinking about the next stage.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, there were two specific questions. on the latter question, from mr manders, there is a voluntary agreement between the european union and industry for harmonisation of chargers, and this will be of very great importance for consumers. there was another question on service standardisation, and i would like to tell the honourable member that the regulation reaffirms the possibility for the union to use service standardisation as a policy tool within harmonised service sectors. having said that, i could not agree more with what mr harbour said. this is indeed the first of 12 levers to boost growth and strengthen confidence in the single market act adopted by the commission in april 2011. this is good for industry, for consumers, and for the economy at large, but it is also – and i think many members have underlined this – an evolution, not a revolution. so the regulation builds on the main pillars of the current, successful system, and the improvement it brings will provide europe with a single transparent and comprehensive instrument which will not only support the implementation of policies here in europe but will also help promote the competitiveness of european enterprises throughout the world. so i hope this house will adopt by a massive majority this very important piece of legislation.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased with this debate, in which we have presented the rules of procedure in a very complete way, highlighting the most important points. this regulation will ensure that national and european markets interact better and ensure greater competitiveness, which europe absolutely needs. improving the whole system of standards formation facilitates, simplifies and makes more effective the work of our enterprises. standards have a direct impact on citizens - mr schaldemose is right - and improve their lives, and we must make our colleagues aware of this so that we can spread it throughout our territory. at the same time, it was right to ensure that the european system was more competitive at national level. i also agree with mr andreas schwab that more regulation and fewer directives are needed if we are to have a genuine internal market, as suggested by professor monti and commissioner barnier. this is the right way to achieve a union which is not only economic but also political, so that we can finally call it 'european'.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday, 11 september.
the agenda includes the report by sophie auconie, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the amended proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1760/2000 as regards the electronic identification of bovine animals and repealing the provisions on voluntary labelling of beef and veal (com (2012) 0162 - c7-0114/2012 - 2011/0229 (cod)) (a7-0199/2012).
on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, as has already been said by other members, if this proposal for a directive is not amended by amendments, we will strongly oppose it, because on the one hand the commission is giving farmers the option of voluntarily using electronic identification, which allows more reliable data to be obtained and strengthens the traceability and food safety system, but on the other hand it wants to ban optional labelling. we think it is absurd that a number of additional information, such as the breed or sex of the animal, the feed used, the age of the bovine or other information which can clearly distinguish one type of beef from another, cannot be given on the label. it is not clear to us why the commission intends to abolish a labelling system whose application is optional, on the pretext of alleged, unexplained administrative burdens, since each farmer can choose whether to accept them or not, since he can voluntarily decide whether to apply this methodology. we believe that the abolition of this option favours the less transparent producers and does not provide information to consumers.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the abolition of voluntary labelling of beef is a pointless decision and counterproductive for both consumers and farmers. europe, in words, seems to want to protect consumers and ensure transparency, but in fact it is going in exactly the opposite direction, by eliminating a labelling system that guarantees a genuine and informed purchase. this flattening of the market and the encouragement of the industry of anonymity and counterfeiting to the detriment of quality-oriented breeders. in italy, one steak in two comes from abroad and very often we don't even know exactly where it comes from; this is why it is crucial to know the origin, breed and diet of the cattle. it is not clear why the commission intends to abolish a labelling system which is, moreover, optional and which is working effectively. citizens have a sacred right to know what they buy and eat: that is the way europe must go. we therefore have a great responsibility in the report which we are going to vote on tomorrow, ladies and gentlemen.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1760/2000 as regards the electronic identification of bovine animals and the abolition of the provisions on the optional labelling of beef is of fundamental importance for the defence of quality breeding and the protection of consumer information and food safety. by proposing to remove the optional labelling, the commission is weakening these aspects by preventing the consumer from having access to additional information such as the sex, age or diet of the cattle - elements which i consider essential for two reasons: because they can drive the consumer towards a more conscious purchase and because they add value to the product. the commission's criticism of the optional labelling system is based on high administrative burdens, not balanced by correspondingly significant benefits. i would like to know on what basis this is based, since the simulations provided by independent associations consider these costs to be low and justified in any case in order to ensure information for the protection and benefit of the consumer. for these reasons i do not support the deletion of articles 16, 17 and 18 of the commission proposal.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, as a substitute member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety and as a full member of the committee on agriculture and rural development, i have had the opportunity to work on the dossiers. i have the impression that the commission is not taking account of the real players in this matter: farmers and producers. the proposals aim to introduce a ban on optional labelling a non-mandatory measure allowing producers who choose to do so to provide additional information on the label. since it was the same consortia representing the breeders and producers who requested that this measure continue to be provided for, it is paradoxical not to grant this possibility. on the other hand, the committee on agriculture and rural development is working to ensure that our farmers can communicate the data on the products they sell in the most transparent way possible. it is therefore counterproductive to work for the protection and transparency of consumer information on the one hand and to prohibit measures, even optional ones, which go in this direction on the other. it is clear that these choices are made if the intention is to lower the quality and standards of agri-food products. there is no other explanation for such a measure against farmers who wish to promote their commitment by transmitting quality indicators, such as the choice of one feed over another. for these reasons, i shall vote against certain amendments.

in writing. food safety is one of the main concerns of european citizens; the european legislation is committed to ensuring optimal protection for them, by means of provisions adapted to the changing needs of the market. while i share the commission's general objective of achieving greater clarity in the application of legislation on the identification and traceability of bovine animals, i strongly disagree with the proposal to abolish the provisions on voluntary beef labelling with the apparent justification of the substantial administrative burden not balanced by correspondingly important benefits. since it seems counterintuitive to call for the abolition of an optional rule as such, if this proposal were approved it would create a legal loophole in the field of optional labelling which, on the contrary, is valuable because it provides useful information which contributes to increasing both consumer information and the added value of products. the optimal marketing of products is a key factor for farmers and the approval by the competent authority ensures that the information on the labels is reliable. without such approval, consumers cannot trust the labelling of the product. for the reasons stated above, i am in favour of maintaining the current voluntary labelling system for beef.
in writing. voting for the abolition of voluntary labelling means voting for the quality and traceability of our beef. the cost reasons for proposing to simplify the beef labelling system seem understandable. however, they are not proportionate in terms of the losses or rather damage that this would entail; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive. i hope, however, that it is clear to everyone that proposing to abolish the optional labelling system would be detrimental to the competitiveness of production. in my country, italy, farmers have long invested in quality, traceability and food safety, and have found optional labelling a useful tool to improve information and increase the value of products on the market.
