mr president, the current world economic and environmental crisis requires us to make choices to save resources. with the energy efficiency directive, which was adopted today, we can achieve important objectives such as: addressing climate change and the scarcity of fossil energy sources, such as coal and oil; reduce annual costs for the purchase of energy sources by as much as eur 400 billion, with a potential saving of eur 50 billion per year; reducing europe's dependence on russia and the opec countries, from which we import gas and oil; reducing air pollution, which today in some regions of europe represents an unfortunately unresolved threat to the health of millions of european citizens; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. i therefore welcome the rules introduced for the renovation of public buildings and for the four-yearly energy audits, which are compulsory for all large companies. this is one of the many steps which are mandatory for europe. but we must do more: we must set ourselves more ambitious targets and adopt more binding measures for all member states.
mr president, i voted in favour of the report by mr turmes, which paves the way for the adoption of a directive which will finally close the gap between member states on energy efficiency. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question are compatible with the internal market. according to the commission's figures, the operation will reduce overall investment costs in energy generation and distribution by some 20 billion. this is a key element which will also help to establish the union as a global player, since future geopolitical balances will be mainly determined by policies on the supply and use of energy resources.
mr president, i voted in favour of this dossier because i believe that the question of energy efficiency, linked to sustainability and competitiveness, can certainly be an essential tool in a process, such as the present one, which is particularly difficult. sustainable growth is needed, which must concern small and mediumsized enterprises and which can also be used as a virtuous mechanism through innovative green technologies. all this is achieved through a design culture which makes the best use of these resources and channels them towards building renovation, which involves in particular the full and appropriate use of the european cohesion funds. a third of the buildings in europe were built after 1973, and that is a clear sign. there is also the possibility of moving in this context through better training and design consistent with the aims of the standard.
mr president, energy efficiency is one of the pillars of the union's climate policy. that is why today's vote is particularly important. it is the result of a satisfactory and timely agreement on the content, since it obliges the member states to prepare a strategy based on indicative national targets, which take account of the union's objectives, and at the same time allows energy companies to comply with the requirements for energy saving in accordance with the principle of reasonable flexibility. the target of a 20% increase in energy efficiency by 2020 is therefore within reach. i believe that the credit should go to this house in particular, because if the member states most involved in the council have finally accepted this valid compromise, it is because of the tenacity with which parliament's negotiators, starting with the rapporteur, have safeguarded the objectives. this is an important element in creating green jobs and, ultimately, in boosting competitiveness and sustainability.
mr president, a good compromise has been reached which puts europe on the right track to achieve the objectives of the climate package. one of the successes is that the 3% target for energy efficiency in public buildings has been maintained, an ambitious target in a time of economic crisis, which has a strong environmental impact and will be a lever for the union's economic growth. the directive lays the foundations for redesigning energy saving strategies, for which both private and public actors will need to rely on experts in the field, without whom the objectives set will be difficult to achieve. it therefore opens the door to encouraging national programmes for the training of experts in energy auditing and saving.

mr president, the compromise reached between the council and parliament after a year of difficult negotiations is a starting point for the relaunching of the internal market. by using standards, european companies will be able to obtain certificates of conformity and safety of products and services in a shorter time and at lower costs than at present. the simplifications envisaged will be particularly important for small and medium-sized enterprises, as member states will have to facilitate the participation of smes in standardisation committees and their access to standards.
mr president, i would like to congratulate mr i thank you for your work and the excellent quality of your report. standardisation is one of the 12 levers for the relaunch of the internal market and will play a key role in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the new regulation will enable european companies to obtain certificates of conformity and safety of products and services in less time, through a technically up-to-date, flexible and effective system. this will enable small and mediumsized enterprises in particular to reduce production costs and administrative burdens, thus increasing their representation in the european single market. in this context, it will be necessary to continue to stimulate voluntary consultation between industry, public authorities and other interested parties in order to ensure that standards and standards are developed in a transparent manner and can be updated over time.
mr president, the satisfactory compromise leads to a european standardization system which is technically up to date, more balanced, more effective and more responsive to the real needs of enterprises. the fact that it has tackled the problem of the slow process of developing standards and the issue of the underrepresentation of small and medium-sized enterprises is a credit to the commission. the creation of a notification system through which companies will be informed in advance of the commission's intention to submit significant standards and the extension of the scope of the regulation to these standards, covering all services representing 70% of the eu's gdp, should also be emphasised. we voted in favour of this because it is an important policy instrument to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market in products for consumer and environmental protection, innovation and social inclusion.
mr president, food safety is undoubtedly one of the most pressing issues facing european citizens. in 1997, following the outbreak of mad cow disease, the european union adopted strict rules on the identification and traceability of bovine animals. the text discussed today would amend the legislation in force, but would also introduce limits on the provisions relating to optional labelling. it would make it possible to obtain more reliable data through an electronic identification system for bovine animals and to strengthen the traceability system.
mr president, to abolish voluntary labelling for beef in europe is to arbitrarily choose to go against the safety and quality of our products. in the attempt to simplify, we cannot reduce the useful information to the detriment not only of the consumers who buy the meat, but also of the european farmers who, through labelling, differentiate and market their products. we have long argued that in order to protect production and purchasing, origin must be recognised. we are therefore opposed to a proposal which would return us to the status quo before this labelling, which has now achieved excellent results both in terms of the organisation of the whole chain of the sector and in terms of communication to the final consumer of meat. we want a safer europe, one which is attentive to the needs of consumers, to the quality and safety of food and to the development of our rural system.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to express my appreciation for the adoption of this report, which once again calls the attention of the european union to the protection of health and the protection of citizens. in this report we have in fact tackled the issue of the surveillance of medicinal products once again, following the adoption of directive 2010/84/eu and regulation (eu) no 1235/2010 amending the pharmacovigilance directives. after the so-called 'mediator case', it was felt that the shortcomings identified by the tests themselves needed to be addressed and the system already in place needed to be improved, particularly as regards the obligations to inform and notify the parties concerned and the list of medicinal products subject to enhanced surveillance. the adjustments thus introduced, although of a modest scale, complement and strengthen the legal framework already established for higher levels of transparency and efficiency and improved standards of medicinal product safety for the benefit of the health of european citizens.
mr president, today is a very important day for the health of the citizens of europe. this is certainly one of the most important reforms of the whole legislature, considering the beneficial impact it will have on the health of european citizens. the eu is now introducing stricter legislation and setting new maximum sulphur limits for marine fuels, whose air pollutants are estimated to cause as many as 50 000 premature deaths in europe. for the nordic countries the so-called 'seca zones' from 2015 the maximum sulphur limit in fuels will fall below 0.1 per cent, while for all other countries the permitted limit will be 0.5 per cent from 2020. we should have dared to do more, we should have extended these new limits to the whole of the european union. but how much is life worth? that is what thousands of european citizens are asking themselves in cities with large ports such as my beautiful and battered venice, whose inhabitants and works are constantly poisoned by the smoke from the chimneys of the large ships. well, thanks to europe, that smoke will be a little less black.
mr president, i am against the proposal for a directive because once again the european union wants to be the first in the world when it comes to the environment and climate. unfortunately, this attitude puts us at a distinct competitive disadvantage in the global marketplace, with negligible environmental benefits. the text, which was the result of the trilogue, is better than the one approved by the envi committee, but goes beyond the requirements laid down by the marpol convention: the vessel has not been impounded in the event of infringements, or the vessel has to demonstrate good faith in the purchase of fuel; it is not clear why liner ferries on the high seas are subject to stricter limits than those set at international level. in addition, the ban on the sale in the eu of fuel with more than 3,5% sulphur represents a competitive disadvantage for european suppliers. why does the commission not apply duties to goods from third countries which use fuel with a high sulphur content and which are harmful to the environment as a whole? does he not realise that by continuing to impose restrictions on our businesses he is encouraging unfair competition?

in writing. - i voted in favour of mr bendtsen's motion for a resolution because i am in favour of the allocation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for the amount of eur 6 455 104 requested by denmark, in respect of the four-month period from may to august 2011, for the 981 danish workers made redundant by the shipbuilding company, odense steel shipyard, of whom 550 will be eligible for the egf. the danish application complies with the egf criteria as it demonstrates a correlation between the structural changes under way in that undertaking due to the current financial crisis and the redundancies.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established in 2006 as a support system for workers impacted by global structural change in trade patterns. denmark’s application in respect of the odense steel shipyard notes that the country’s workforce is highly concentrated in manufacturing and metallurgy, but has lost business because many global market shares have been transferred to asia. by mobilising the egf with an amount of eur 6 455 104, workers will be helped to return to the labour market, which is especially important because these employees have highly specialised training in their field which it is nearly impossible to apply in other industries. for these reasons, i voted in favour of mr bendtsen’s report.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund is a very important instrument of the european union. the institute was set up to try to resolve economically controversial issues and offers a chance for companies in difficulty to recover or at least to protect their employees and their families. in the case of odense steel shipyard, the six and a half million euros that will come to denmark, thanks also to my vote, will be used to cover the one thousand redundancies that the company is registering due to the layoffs due to the worldwide decline in shipbuilding, the major structural changes in the world trade system and the financial crisis.
in writing. − whereas the commission's fourth application under the 2012 budget concerns the mobilisation of the egf for a total amount of eur 6 455 104 for denmark and concerns 981 redundancies, of which 550 are recipients of assistance, at the odense steel shipyard, the main enterprise, and at four downstream suppliers and producers in denmark during the four-month reference period from 1 may 2011 to 31 august 2011, this proposal fulfils the conditions for mobilising the egf set out in article 2 (a) of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 and was submitted within the 10-week deadline set out in article 5 of that regulation; i would also like to stress the importance of ensuring a rapid procedure, in compliance with the interinstitutional agreement, for the adoption of decisions on the mobilisation of the fund. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. the crisis in europe has not spared the countries of northern europe either: in denmark, the overall employment situation has deteriorated significantly and unemployment has risen from a record low of 3% in 2008 to a peak of 7% in 2010, with a severe impact especially in the metallurgical sector. the workers laid off by shipyards have a high level of technical expertise, which is difficult to apply in other sectors: the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the situation of the unemployed. for these reasons i voted in favour of the request for the mobilisation of the egf for denmark.

in writing. − negotiations on energy efficiency measures are proving increasingly difficult and complex, mainly because of some large member states, not always and totally willing to support ambitious agreements and prospects, which, in the short term, can lead to costs and negative consequences for their competitiveness. here too, despite some improvements, we are faced with a directive which, while contributing to the 20% energy saving target by 2020, will not be sufficient on its own (an estimated result of between 15% and 17%). we must therefore make a concerted effort to ensure that long-term prospects and needs find a way of prevailing over selfish interests which, in the short term, can strongly influence the governments of the member states, especially in a period of acute economic crisis. a structural and lasting solution to this crisis must be sought in measures that tackle and solve the serious problem of energy poverty at its root. we must rethink the way out, we cannot go back to the pre-crisis patterns of production and consumption, and for that we must be ambitious and courageous in creating new opportunities and new jobs.

in writing. − efforts to save energy, according to the data available to us, are still not sufficient to achieve the target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050 compared to 1990. the report has the merit of highlighting this problem and of presenting solutions to try to implement an energy plan which is sustainable and with measurable objectives. in this sense, all productive sectors, not just the private sector, are identified as operational agents for greater energy efficiency. public buildings, for example, play a key role in this respect and their renovation is desirable precisely to meet minimum energy performance requirements and to get closer to the targets for reducing gas emissions.

in writing. - i voted in favour of mr turmes' report because i believe that one of the most important areas to be promoted, both at european and national level, is energy efficiency. in this context i have greatly appreciated the excellent work done by my colleagues in identifying priority areas for stimulation. the difficulty of achieving the 2020 targets set by the executive commission requires the eu and all member states to be able to commit themselves fully to leading by example and to seeking solutions that can make energy consumption more efficient. i also think it is right to provide for the necessary and periodic management checks, or 'audits', to intervene where and when necessary. this is both to optimise the present and to look to future goals with renewed vigour.
in writing. the text just voted repeals a directive from eight years ago which, in the field of research and development, industry and energy, is old and obsolete. the proposal for the new directive, in line with the eu 2020 targets, aims to reduce the eu's energy use by 20%. the commission will be able to take account of the need to ensure that the community's energy policy is not distorted by the introduction of new technologies. energy efficiency means saving energy costs, increasing safety, specialising and developing industries, and we cannot but share these objectives.
in writing. − considering that the european union's energy efficiency targets are indispensable to achieve, as failure would also mean that the eu would miss the targets on climate change, energy security, green growth and social protection, a common eu approach is needed in order to consolidate energy savings, energy efficiency and innovation, achieve economies of scale and reduce red tape across all member states. furthermore, taking into account that the eu's efficiency policy will be based on existing regional and national policies of some effectiveness, and will provide the necessary flexibility to take account of local and national specificities, based on the advance financing of efficiency measures and stimulation of technological, financial and social innovation, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i am convinced that a net 20% cut in energy consumption in the eu could save €50 billion a year. this ambitious target can only be achieved through new mandatory energy saving measures such as renovation of public buildings, energy saving plans for public enterprises and energy audits for all large enterprises. this decision is doubly important: it is not only critical to achieving our energy security and climate goals, but it will also give a strong boost to the economy and create new jobs.
in writing. - this directive, which we strongly opposed at the beginning of the legislative process, to the extent that we tabled an alternative resolution asking the commission to withdraw its proposal and to reformulate it because it affected the right of a member state to determine the conditions for the use of its energy sources, has been significantly amended. the amendments made to the trilogues compared to the texts produced by the itre and envi committees increase the level of flexibility of the member states, industry and public bodies by significantly reducing the level of ambition proposed. the rapporteur, who was strongly opposed to the amendments, accepted the compromise, even though the 20% energy efficiency target cannot be fully guaranteed as a more ambitious position would jeopardise the agreement. since what we asked for in our alternative resolution has in fact been transposed, our vote is in favour, even if we continue to have doubts about the applicability of the directive.
in writing. - the text we voted on this morning proposes to further strengthen the measures presented by the commission, by integrating them into the european energy policy perspective to 2050, and also by including requests for financial support for programmes/investments for efficiency measures. i think the proposal is particularly worthwhile, as it puts particular emphasis on the identification of energy efficiency targets, the role of the public sector as a role model, mandatory energy efficiency schemes and the promotion of efficiency in heating and cooling, with particular reference to cogeneration and efficiency in energy transmission and distribution. finally, the commission estimates that, in the face of an increase in the cost of investments in energy efficiency of around eur 24 billion per year, the legislative proposal would lead to an overall reduction in the cost of investments in energy generation and distribution and in the costs of the 'energy bill' of around eur 20 billion for the period 2011-2020. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the directive.
in writing. - mr turmes' report introduces a series of energy-saving measures including new obligations for the refurbishment of public buildings and the development of cogeneration technologies that member states will have to apply to achieve the energy efficiency targets foreseen for 2020. in view not only of the difficult economic situation europe is facing but also of the efforts already made by european companies to improve energy efficiency, i believe that the text adopted today is a good compromise: the measures envisaged should allow the commitments made under the 'climate package' to be respected. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. − i voted for this report because i believe that any counter-terrorism strategy should be conducted in strict compliance with human rights obligations. this parliament has repeatedly and strongly condemned ‘extraordinary rendition’, detention without trial, secret prisons and torture. i believe that the eu commitment to human rights must be reflected in all policy areas in order to be credible. for this reason, with this text we call on member states to investigate whether there are secret prisons on their territory or whether operations have taken place whereby people have been detained under the cia programme in facilities on their territory. as regard to ‘state secrecy’, i strongly believe that only genuine national security reasons can justify secrecy, which is in any case overridden by fundamental rights obligations that cannot be derogated from, such as the absolute prohibition on torture.
in writing. - i abstained on mrs flautre's report because i believe that, despite the results achieved by the collection of different information on the location of the illegal cia prisoner detention sites in europe, the eu situation is very uneven in this respect: many member states are not conducting serious investigations into human rights violations linked to cia operations within eu space, in the area of transport and detention of prisoners. i regret the lack of communication, transparency and application of the investigative methods by some member states.
in writing. the resolution on the alleged cases of the cia's transporting and illegal detention of prisoners in european countries draws attention to a subject which continues to be controversial in italy. comparing the air traffic data managed by eurocontrol, it seems there is an illegal system that has led to suspicious disappearances that is not tolerable. all responsibility must be taken to ensure that such cases are not repeated in the future. the fight against terrorism in the eu must be conducted in compliance with eu law and the sovereignty of the member states, which have the right and the duty to prosecute and try suspected terrorists.
in writing. − in relations between the european union, its member states and third countries, it is essential to ensure the full application of the human rights clauses contained in the agreements. the way in which governments cooperate with the repressive apparatus of dictatorships in the name of fighting terrorism must be reviewed. security sector reform must ensure a clear separation between intelligence and law enforcement functions.
in writing. - having regard to the treaty on european union (teu), in particular articles 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 21, the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, in particular articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 18 and 19 and the european convention on human rights and its protocols, as well as the relevant un human rights instruments, and whereas parliament has condemned the us-led cia's programme of surrender and secret detention, which has resulted in multiple human rights violations, including cases of arbitrary and unlawful detention, torture and other ill-treatment, violations of the principle of non-refoulement and enforced disappearances, and has repeatedly and firmly condemned illegal practices such as 'extraordinary rendition', summary trial, detention without trial, executions, secret prisons and torture, i express my vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that eu member states should conduct thorough investigations to find out whether there were secret prisons or facilities on their territory where people from the cia's secret rendition and detention programme were held in the early 2000s. only valid reasons of national security can justify secrecy. that is why it is necessary to reopen the national investigation in order to clarify this case.
in writing. - it is clear that the humanitarian crisis in the middle east is bound to have a strong impact on europe, but especially on the member states, such as italy, which face the mediterranean. efficient action is needed by improving coordination between member states, through an appropriate sharing of responsibility in ensuring that their asylum systems meet european and international standards, and also through a fair distribution of asylum seekers. according to the latest eurostat data, in the first quarter of 2012 alone, italy received 2,210 new asylum applications. asylum seekers are on average very young, aged between 18 and 34 (67.2%) and underage (17.9%). i welcome the establishment of the european asylum support office and also the creation of the asylum and migration fund from 2014 onwards, which are very useful tools for launching targeted actions in support of states with enormous burdens and responsibilities and asylum seekers and international protection seekers hoping for a better future.
in writing. − with this text we reiterate that the right to international protection is a fundamental right enshrined in international and eu law and complemented by a series of additional rights and principles, such as the principle of non-refoulement, the right to dignity, the prohibition of torture, inhuman or degrading treatment. for this reason member states must ensure that fair and efficient asylum systems are put in place in order to respond to varying asylum flows. member states have also the obligation to oppose with all means the rise of xenophobia and racism in europe. a first step to fight the negative and misinformed assumptions about asylum seekers and refugees could be enhanced through the organisation of awareness-raising campaigns on the actual situation of beneficiaries of international protection.
in writing. - experience in this area shows that the loosening of the bonds of responsibility and solidarity between member states invariably results in a losing game, in which from time to time a single country, often a country bordering the mediterranean, fails to cope with a surge in refugee flows and is cited as a negative example. the emotional climate that follows is a fertile ground for opposing demagogues and for manifestations of that particular residual selfishness, inherited from an era in which european countries faced each other instead of cooperating. i therefore support the report which deals with exemplary clarity with outstanding questions of the ceas. i would particularly like to draw attention to the recommendations in paragraph 47, which, if translated into specific measures, would make it possible to bind the member states in an effective bond of shared responsibility and mutual solidarity, ensuring - and this is the fundamental objective - that the plight of asylum seekers is addressed on an appropriate scale, with humanity, reasonableness and realism. it will also be useful to reconsider the alignment of legislation on legal immigration, a closely related area, whose problems are directly reflected in the reception and asylum system.
in writing. − ensuring the smooth functioning of the common european asylum system is crucial at a time when migration flows are mostly mixed in nature and include migrants, asylum seekers, refugees and vulnerable people such as unaccompanied minors. it is worth noting that migration and asylum flows have their own specificities which cannot be ignored or conflated. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − in 2012, the european union committed itself to completing the creation of a common european asylum system (ceas) based on three pillars: the harmonisation of protection standards by further aligning member states' asylum legislation; effective and sustained practical cooperation; and a greater sense of solidarity and responsibility, not only between eu member states, but also between the eu and non-eu countries. given that harmonisation of protection standards is being achieved through the amendment of member states' legislation and that practical cooperation will be strengthened through the european asylum support office (easo), it is now important to focus on the third pillar of the ceas by building on the notion of solidarity and responsibility sharing enshrined in article 80 tfeu, and for this reason i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because the transfer of internationally protected persons within the european union should take account of their interests and the need for solidarity between member states. this is why more appropriations are needed for asylum policy, for the common processing of asylum applications and for a stronger role for the european asylum support office.
in writing. − we are at a historic moment in which migration flows are mixed and we have to deal with asylum seekers by land and by sea. i voted in favour of the report on strengthening solidarity in the field of asylum, as it represents a concrete commitment to ensure adequate and efficient asylum policies. the report outlines a better harmonisation of protection and asylum standards and greater solidarity between member states, i.e. mutual assistance and burden-sharing between member states to ensure that rights are promoted and respected. i share the rapporteur's priorities: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − standardization is one of the 12 levers of the single market act and plays a central role in the smooth functioning of the european market. it guarantees the protection of consumers and the environment, and at the same time the competitiveness and innovation of our companies. i have appreciated, and voted in favour of, the work done by mrs comi and the compromise reached between parliament and the council after more than a year of negotiations. finally, businesses and national bodies will have at their disposal a transparent, effective and less administrative tool. companies which, in italy alone, represent 99.9% of the production fabric, and which will finally be able to: participate in standardisation committees; use standards to obtain certificates of conformity and safety of products and services in less time and at less cost; be informed in advance, through a notification system, of the commission's intention to submit standards.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that the compromise reached between the european council and parliament, after more than a year of negotiations, represents a decisive step forward towards a more balanced, efficient and responsive european standardisation system that meets the real needs of european businesses. the impact of the new regulation can be fully understood only if it is understood that standards are a tool for competitiveness for all businesses and in particular for smes, which can obtain certificates of conformity and safety of products and services in less time and at less cost. in particular, i welcome two aspects of the new proposal: the creation of a notification system through which european companies will be informed in advance of the european commission's intention to submit standards and the extension of the scope of this regulation to standards covering all services, which represent more than 70% of the gdp of the european union. a further positive element is that the new legislation will require member states to facilitate sme participation in standardisation committees and sme access to standards.
in writing. - the commission has tackled a subject which has historically been a constitutive feature of european integration and the report takes up this importance. i therefore express a favourable opinion and congratulate the honourable member on the effective synthesis in defining such a delicate subject. i would like to stress the urgency of aligning the timetable of the european institutions with that of industry and society at large in the field of standardisation. innovation in this field, the result of agreements within the sectors, including through forums, is certainly a sign of vitality, but this activity cannot be entrusted to purely private methods: without institutional impetus, technical and regulatory obstacles and market fragmentation would be difficult to overcome. moreover, a rather disorderly network of standards resulting from commercial relationships, contracted outside the scope of the nso, could generate market distortions. the drive towards standardisation is naturally driven by society and the market and is driven by reasons of development, cost reduction for firms and increasing the value of products and services, which are well known to consumers. it would be very curious if the european institutions were to marginalise themselves in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on european standardisation presented by my colleague, mr comi, because i believe that it brings substantial benefits to the european union and the member states. the rules of the regulation are designed to achieve the objectives of greater efficiency, market competitiveness and speed in the development of european standards with greater transparency and applicability of the same. in particular, the regulation focuses on social inclusion, stakeholder participation and consultation, and services, with particular attention also paid to the role of smes. in this connection, i think it is appropriate to emphasize that rules are important for the competitiveness of companies, especially small and mediumsized enterprises, and are essential for development. this regulation will enable smes to reduce costs and increase their competitiveness on the european market, thereby increasing their participation and access to the rules, and allowing them to have a say in their definition. the main benefits of this regulation are: improved interaction between markets; increased transparency; improved standards; facilitating and simplifying the work of businesses and improving the lives of consumers. it will play a key role in the completion of the internal market and a genuine economic and monetary union.
in writing. − to be able to use your phone charger in a place other than the one you usually live in, the electricity socket must be compatible. or a train that wants to cross state lines, it has to be able to run on proper tracks. these examples show how essential standards are in our daily lives and how important it is to ensure that different technologies are interoperable so that they can be used to their fullest potential. this regulation, for which i was rapporteur, makes the standardization system more effective, improves the quality of life of our citizens, the competitiveness of our enterprises and thus strengthens the whole european market. i am very pleased that this has been achieved in a short time and through complex negotiation between the various interests involved and, above all, that it has been supported so widely by the european parliament. i am sure that this new instrument will have a significant impact on the revival of the market and the promotion of our enterprises.
in writing. - the work carried out by mrs comi on such a broad and complex subject is to be appreciated for its ability to summarise and resolve the proposals in this field. the european legislation that is as regular and harmonized as possible and that takes account of the various components of the european system is all the more desirable. the regulatory system impacts on the activities of enterprises and their competitive capacity. it is therefore important to proceed along a path that reduces bureaucracy and makes the industrial fabric involved in decisions concerning european legislation. if operators are fully involved in this important decision-making process, the benefits will be felt by the whole community and the whole range of services provided to consumers and citizens.
in writing. - it is important that this report be adopted because the rules for all those areas which are often overlooked need to be rapidly proportioned and simplified. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it sets out new priorities and fills the gaps in this important area. firstly, the participation of smes in the european standardisation process is finally encouraged, so that the real productive forces of the eu are fully involved. it also stresses the importance of consulting consumer associations when setting standards, which can be very helpful, especially for certain people with specific needs, such as the disabled. we hope, therefore, that we shall be able to have a more transparent and representative european standardisation, which will be of particular help to the needs of individuals and smaller producers. it could certainly have gone further, for example by proposing that access to standards regulations be free of charge for micro-enterprises: i myself have received several reports from small businesses which have faced objective economic difficulties in obtaining these documents which are essential for their production. however, there are high research costs which must be covered in some way, and so we can regard the text voted on today as a good compromise, the actual implementation of which, in any case, will have to be discussed in more detail later.
in writing. − taking into account the conclusions of the express group report and the replies to the commission's public consultation on the current legal framework for european standardisation, the basis for a review of the european standardisation system has now been laid. in order to ensure that the european standardisation system is not simply a system of standards, but also a system of standards, the commission has proposed a number of amendments to the existing system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation improving the use of technical standards in the services and telecommunications sectors. this new regulation will give european companies more immediate access to standard solutions for technical problems, thereby reducing production costs, facilitating the dissemination of best practice and increasing competitiveness. the new regulation, which aims to modernise the so-called 'normalisation' process, simplifies the whole system in administrative and financial terms, while ensuring a high level of transparency. i think the greatest success has been in ensuring that small businesses and representatives of consumers, environmental organisations and civil society are involved and that they are consulted throughout the process of developing standards. this is a very important point, since small and mediumsized enterprises, both because of their small size and because of language problems, have greater difficulties in being an active part of the system, even though they are the economic basis of our european system. the new rules will also make european standards more compatible with international standards, thus improving the overall competitiveness of eu businesses.
in writing. - i supported the legislative proposal on european standardisation presented by mrs lara comi, as it set itself the important objective of amending a whole series of guidelines in a technical area as important to the business world as standardisation. this will enable smes to be directly involved in the development of the new standards through lower access charges. in addition, in the definition of standards, there will also be room for consumers through their representative associations.
in writing. the new european standardisation regulation is a satisfactory compromise reached after a year of difficult negotiations. i believe that european standardisation is a key step towards achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and a strong relaunch of the internal market. this regulation will enable european companies to obtain certificates of conformity in a system that is constantly updated, with safer products, faster services and lower costs. this is particularly beneficial for smes, which were previously under-represented, but will now be more represented and will have to cope with lower costs and, in general, lower charges. the regulation aims to reduce bureaucratic barriers and increase transparency, while also protecting consumers and the environment.
in writing. - some contradictions have emerged in this proposal for a regulation, since the provisions contained in it on the one hand bring advantages through the electronic identification of bovine animals, which makes it possible to speed up their registration and thus their traceability. on the other hand, they take some steps backwards on the grounds that they are reducing the costs and administrative burdens borne by the member states and operators who choose to apply the voluntary labelling scheme. with great effort we have achieved an optimum level of protection of the health of our citizens in recent years, by trying to provide the consumer with all the useful information that contributes to increasing the added value and quality of products. we have also tried to curb the industry of beef and counterfeit products by optional labelling. then why waste the work we've done? why should we abolish voluntary labelling when the fact that it is voluntary does not oblige anyone to apply it?
in writing. i voted against the amendment tabled by mr auconie because i think that the abolition of voluntary labelling of beef is a pointless and counterproductive decision, both for consumers and for farmers. this proposal flattens the market and encourages the industry of anonymity and counterfeiting, to the detriment of quality-oriented breeders. citizens have a right to know what they are buying and eating: i therefore reiterate my vote against the amended proposal.

in writing. - i wanted to stress the importance and gravity of the possible abolition of the voluntary labelling system for beef and veal, which is why i voted in favour of not abolishing this system. if parliament's position is adopted in the negotiations with the council, there will be a serious lack of transparency for the consumer and a deterioration in the quality of the product, since the optional label allows 24 types of additional information to be included throughout the supply chain and not just the generic 'useful information' of the mandatory labelling: the country of birth of the bovine animal, the country of rearing and the country of slaughter. i hope that in the negotiations the council will not opt for the abolition of the optional labelling system.
in writing. − food safety is one of the main concerns of european citizens. european legislation must therefore ensure optimum protection for them, by means of provisions updated and strengthened in the light of the new needs identified. that is why i am in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. − considering that the databases complying with directive 64/432/eec, containing information on bovine animals, do not currently take account of the advent of electronic identification technology for bovine animals and that the revision of regulation (ec) no 1760/2000 favours the progressive and harmonious development of this new technology, it is also appropriate to adapt the principles for the collection of the data in question by making them compatible with the new methods of identification of bovine animals. taking into account the additional objectives of simplifying the provisions on beef labelling - although the aspects related to labelling are covered by horizontal legislation and should therefore not be the subject of a conferral of powers on the commission - and of updating the powers conferred on the commission, and recalling, however, that the delegation of powers may be revoked at any time by the european parliament and the council, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i have decided to vote against the report on the amended proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on the electronic identification of bovine animals and repealing the provisions on the optional labelling of beef and veal. i think it is wrong to abolish the labelling system, the application of which is optional, by invoking administrative burdens which each farmer can decide voluntarily to accept or not. on the contrary, this labelling system has proved its effectiveness in promoting informed consumer purchasing by ensuring that supplementary information is provided in a harmonised and certified manner. its abolition would favour the least transparent producers
in writing. - in italy, as in most european countries, many operators have been investing for years to comply with european regulations on beef labelling. this important tool aims to provide useful information (such as the breed and sex of the animal, the feed used and the age of the bovine, etc.) which consumers are interested in for the purpose of an informed and informed purchase. its success is now evident throughout europe. the abolition of the provisions on voluntary labelling would create a vacuum, with the consequence of a proliferation of different voluntary beef labelling schemes without adequate and rigorous control mechanisms; the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the directive. that is why i voted against all those amendments which sought to reject the maintenance of the voluntary labelling system for beef.
in writing. - the effects of harmful drugs last for decades, with significant social impact, not to mention thousands of personal tragedies: we're still dealing with the effects of dangerous drugs prescribed in the 1950s and 1960s. we have a moral duty to make the best use of the scientific and regulatory instruments at our disposal to prevent, as far as possible, suffering and damage to health, also in the interest of a sector which contributes decisively to our economies and which should not be criminalised in general, where specific responsibilities fall on a limited number of private managers. the four amendments to the directive proposed by the commission are therefore entirely reasonable and appropriate: they speed up the implementation of procedures for the verification and prevention of the marketing of potentially dangerous medicinal products and help to reveal more clearly any traces of possible malice on the part of companies marketing medicinal products which subsequently prove to be harmful. the amendments proposed by the rapporteur are designed to involve the ema more closely and to ensure full transparency for consumers and the medical and scientific community in general. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. the legislative proposal is based on the desire to avoid that certain provisions are not observed and that this leads to serious health risks. recent cases have in fact demonstrated the urgency of action to improve the system of pharmacovigilance in order to strengthen the existing system. the agreement reached is therefore a clear signal to fill the gaps in the previous system. the vote in the house shows the will to establish a european system for the assessment of potential problems with medicines. the new legal framework will allow for better monitoring of farms: finally, companies withdrawing a medicine from the market will not be able to hide behind 'commercial reasons', but will be obliged to provide precise and timely explanations.
in writing. − a review of pharmacovigilance legislation is absolutely necessary. the safety of medicines at eu level needs to be improved by strengthening the role of the european medicines agency in the collection and response to alerts and by enhancing cooperation between member states.
in writing. − taking into account that in december 2010 the european parliament and the council agreed to a review of the rules on pharmacovigilance at eu level by adopting directive 2010/84/eu and regulation (eu) no 1235/2010, the measures taken in this context will help to improve the safety of medicines at eu level by strengthening the role of the european medicines agency. however, a major drug safety investigation in france in 2011 in the so-called 'mediator case' called for an urgent review of the pharmacovigilance systems in place in the eu. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the pharmacovigilance system is properly functioning.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because it will make it possible to monitor the adverse effects of medicines more closely and to avoid a repeat of the french diabetes drug mediator, which is suspected of having caused more than 500 deaths. the new rules, agreed between parliament and eu ministers, will introduce an automatic emergency procedure, which will allow a medicine to be withdrawn from the community market even if a member state decides to block its sale on the national market.
in writing. − in december 2010, directive 2010/84/eu was adopted and regulation (eu) no 1235/2010 concerning the review of european pharmacovigilance rules entered into force in july 2012. while the new legislation has indeed strengthened pharmacovigilance at eu level, the system has some potential gaps in existing pharmacovigilance texts that need to be addressed. i voted in favour of the report on pharmacovigilance because it guarantees a strengthened surveillance of the use of medicinal products and improves the system of information and notification obligations for the parties concerned. the legal framework is therefore strengthened, which now ensures higher levels of transparency and security.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr mcavan's proposal for a regulation because i agree with the importance of strengthening transparency and enforcing reporting obligations by the bodies authorised to market medicinal products in cases of withdrawal from the market of those medicinal products which are found to be toxic to human health. the continued presence on the market of a medicinal product declared as non-standard poses a major risk to european consumers.
in writing. − a major drug safety investigation carried out in france in 2011 in the so-called 'mediator case' called for an urgent review of the pharmacovigilance systems in place in the eu. considering that while the new legislation has indeed strengthened pharmacovigilance at eu level, there are some potential gaps in the union system that still need to be addressed, it is necessary to introduce an automatic emergency procedure, clarify the company's transparency obligations and expand the list of medicinal products subject to additional monitoring. i hope that these objectives will be achieved and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted against the hassi report amending directive 1999/32/ec as regards the sulphur content of marine fuels. the limits for the high seas are equivalent to those for the following seca (sulphur emission control areas): this will bring the mediterranean into this classification, which goes well beyond the limits set by the marpol convention (international convention for the prevention of pollution from ships). i believe that these changes have a competitive disadvantage for the european market which is far greater than the environmental benefits which are negligible.
in writing. − considering that air pollutants from ships are estimated to cause 50,000 premature deaths in europe each year and that sulphur and nitrogen oxides in the atmosphere give rise to secondary particulate matter, which is harmful to health, it is necessary to apply the maximum sulphur limit values for marine fuels established in 2008 by the international maritime organisation (imo). given that if they are not reduced, by the end of this decade sulphur oxide emissions from ships in the eu's maritime zones will exceed the combined emissions from the union's land areas, and that according to commission estimates the monetary value of the health benefits that can be achieved is greater than the costs of reducing ship emissions by a factor of between 2 and 25, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i congratulate mr hassi on his work. by adopting this report, in the light of the commission proposal to the european parliament and the council (com (2011) 0439), and having regard to the opinion of the european economic and social committee of 18 january 2012, the european parliament takes a serious position on the challenge of improving air quality on european coasts in order to reduce deaths caused by air pollution from ships. the new regulation aims to bring european legislation into line with the limits set by the international maritime organisation and therefore provides for a reduction in the maximum general sulphur content for european seas from 3.5 to 0.5% by 2020. this can easily be achieved through the use of environmentally friendly technologies and fuels. i also find it very positive that the commission is being asked to take account of the seca limits, which are more stringent for all community territorial waters, for example within 12 nautical miles of the coast.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text to make the limits for sulphur in marine fuels stricter by 2020, a change which will have the main effect of improving air quality on european coasts and reducing some 50 000 premature deaths per year caused by air pollution from ships. to meet the new limits will necessarily increase the use of cleaner fuels or technologies, such as smoke cleaning, that can provide this result, all to the benefit of the health of european citizens.
in writing. - i have expressed my support for the text tabled by mr hassi on the proposal for a revision of the directive on the sulphur content of marine fuels. the new directive, which transposes the most recent provisions adopted in this field at community level, introduces obligations for passenger ships operating outside protected areas and further lowers the maximum sulphur content of marine fuels used in sensitive areas such as the emission control areas of northern europe. after a series of long and intense negotiations, a compromise was reached which represents the right balance between european environmental objectives and the positions of the companies involved.
in writing. − the commission's proposal to amend article 103e of the single cmo regulation (regulation (ec) no 1234/2007), which provides for the possibility for member states to grant decoupled aid to wine growers under the single payment scheme (sps), certainly needed to be amended. i agree with the work done and the proposals put forward by mr dorfmann, because they ensure that farmers can be assured of the predictability of payments from aid. the report also effectively addresses the current transitional situation of cap reform. it was important above all to avoid member states planning five-year decisions which were not really compatible with the commission's proposal for a new direct support scheme, just as it was essential to reconnect the timetable of the final transfer decision to the timetable of the future reform. the report takes account of all these problems and the solutions reached are very positive. that's why i gave you my full support.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, considering that this regulation provides a clear legal basis for undertakings trading in the wine sector. the proposal makes it possible for member states, on the basis of the provisions already existing in the existing cmo legislation, to amend their support programmes annually as regards the part allocated to the single payment scheme, while still giving them the possibility of deciding to suspend the transfer of funds from their wine-growing areas to the single payment scheme. the annual measure would ensure, in addition to continuity with the decisions taken up to 2013 for direct payments, that member states would not be able to plan five-year decisions which are not compatible with the commission proposal. i hope that the resistance of some countries will be overcome and that this regulation will be considered to be the right one, since it will guarantee a compromise between the consolidation of the single market and the needs of the companies operating in this sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because only a simpler and more consistent approach will allow effective support for wine growers in the future. the commission proposal calls for member states to decide definitively by december 2012 whether to transfer funds from the wine budget to the single payment scheme. the draft report, on the other hand, aims to prevent member states from planning decisions for the next five years at this stage, and thus before they know the outcome of the cap reform. the proposal suggests that the current five-year measure be converted into a single annual measure. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the aid is not used to finance the production of wine. clearness and timeliness of action are the watchwords of our policy in support of wine growers, for a europe which is friendly to the territories.
in writing. - i welcome the vote on mr dorfmann's report, which seeks to safeguard an important sector of excellence for italy and for europe. parliament gives more flexibility to member states so that the sector can also take final decisions before the reform of the cap 2014-2020 comes into force, a reform on which we are working intensively at the moment. today's vote is aimed at giving member states greater flexibility in deciding on national financial allocations in the wine sector. this is linked to the proposal for direct payments under the new cap.
in writing. - i fully supported mr dorfmann's report on the payment scheme for wine growers in view of the new cap which is due to come into force from 2014. i welcome the measures and elements which would allow for the gradual and harmonious application of the rules relating to vineyards. in my view, it was not possible to plan a five-year payment scheme and to overlap it with the period of the start of the new cap. i therefore believe that this has helped to build a lasting revival for the european wine sector.
in writing. − under the provisions already existing in the current cmos, member states may amend their five-year support programmes once a year as regards the part allocated to the single payment scheme. the commission proposal suggests transforming the current five-year measure into a single annual measure, applicable only for 2014, and provides for the possibility of a single transfer - which would represent a final and definitive decision - from 2015 onwards; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the matter. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the transitional period for the transitional period is not extended beyond the end of the transitional period.
in writing. - the report by mr dorfmann was voted on today at the strasbourg plenary session. the proposal by my colleague is to give the member states more flexibility in deciding on the national financial allocation in the wine sector. it also calls for any reform in the wine sector to be implemented through the new common agricultural policy 2014-2020. member states will have the possibility to make a transfer in a single solution final and definitive decision from 2015 and may react to the commission proposal by deciding before 1 december 2012 to adjust the support to wine growers by transferring a certain amount of the national wine allocation to the direct payments budget. this proposal must be seen in the light of the proposal for direct payments of the new cap, which allows wine growers to obtain payment entitlements for their wine-growing areas and does not allow the amounts transferred from the wine envelope to be allocated to wine growers alone, in view of the objective of convergence of the value of all benefits.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report, as it provides for the possibility for member states to grant decoupled aid to wine growers under the single payment scheme as part of their national support programmes. in substance, decoupled support for viticulture should be extended to 2014. i think it is important that the committee on agriculture and rural development has reiterated its position against the abolition of planting rights in this sector. the real risk is the collapse in the quality of wine products and consequently a significant loss of income for farmers who base their activity on the production of high-end wines.
in writing. − the internal market information system (imi) has been in operation since 2008 as a free service to member states to improve the exchange of information in the internal market. the imi system still operates on the basis of a commission decision and a commission recommendation, in the absence of a single legal instrument. this has been a major obstacle to further expansion of imi, which should have been overcome long ago. we have seen that the system has worked perfectly in relation to the vocational qualifications directive and the services directive. the system has proved to be a fast and secure means for cross-border information exchange and administrative cooperation for over 6 000 authorities currently registered in all eu member states and eea countries. i therefore welcome the proposals contained in the report and hope that the extension of the application of imi to other areas will be in the clear interest of the citizens and the internal market.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report, in agreement with the commission proposal and with the additional, non-redundant caveats contained in the proposed amendments on the secure handling of data. the interoperability of administrative systems, which are the daily interlocutors of citizens and businesses, is essential for the growth of markets, the spread of a transnational culture and a european civil conscience. although there were around 2 000 exchanges of information in 2010, it is likely that increased awareness of the benefits of imi will lead to a rapid increase in the flow of information, especially if the system is extended to other, more complex regulatory areas. in view of the growth in the number of potential and actual users and the volume of data exchanged, it is reasonable to address the processing and confidentiality aspects of information in advance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the internal market information system (imi) because i believe that it can be a useful tool for improving administrative cooperation, also through the novelty contained in the text, which aims to extend the system to additional administrative bodies. this useful tool certainly has room for improvement, and i hope that we can continue to move in this direction, given the crucial role it plays in facilitating communication between businesses and administrations, with all that this entails in terms of the competitiveness of our businesses. the application of the latest technologies and the use of networks will also allow the information system, which has been in place since 2008, to improve its effectiveness by making itself available to all 27 member states.
in writing. − a proper exchange of information between member states' authorities is necessary to complete the single market. imi has proved to be a reliable and efficient tool in the two areas where it is already used, namely the professional qualifications directive and the services directive. my vote is in favour.

in writing. - while in non-eu countries affected by the current crisis, the fight for growth and jobs is governed by economic and financial levers, both legal and monetary, at a single political and administrative level, at european level we continue to suffer the political delays of an eu that still fails to overcome the hurdle of unitary governance. this situation is aggravated by the fact that, despite the strong attempt to strengthen coordination between the member states on their budgets, a decisive intervention in favour of the coordination of tax systems, especially on the direct taxation system, remains excluded from the political debate. this delay creates fiscal competition which may also be seen as dumping, which has a negative impact on the stability of enterprises, including in a geographical sense, and which is likely to have a particular impact on already weak areas and on the social responsibility of enterprises. it is for this reason that i regret that the part of the amendment which highlighted the risks of tax competition to the detriment of consolidating national budgets and which proposed the introduction of a minimum rate of corporation tax for this purpose was not adopted. i hope this delay can be made up in the near future .
in writing. the text of mrs gáll-pelcz aims to amend council directive 2003/49/ec of 3 june 2003 on the common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of member states. the abolition of taxes, whether levied at source or after deduction, on interest and royalty payments in the member state from which they originate is the most appropriate solution to ensure a simplified and more transparent tax system. such a system is all the more desirable in the direction of greater surveillance of tax evasion and, at the same time, of a tax system that is transparent and does not stifle businesses and citizens.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on the common tax regime applicable to interest and royalty payments between subsidiaries of different member states because i fully agree with the main objective of the text amending the 2011 council directive; to combat tax evasion at european level by improving technical regulations. the econ commission had already approved the text on the 'common consolidated corporate tax base', demonstrating that a common tax system for associated companies would lead the countries of the union towards fiscal cooperation. with a regulated system that can clarify company accounts and hold companies accountable for illegal exemptions, tax substitutions and other forms of fraud, the fight against tax evasion has become a priority throughout the union.
in writing. - the council directive on a common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of different member states has been amended on many occasions in recent years, but some technical improvements are still needed for clarity. given that recent estimates show that tax fraud and tax evasion represent a significant amount of revenue foregone by eu governments, it is necessary to amend the directive in order to reduce the possibilities of voluntary non-taxation, double taxation, fraud or tax evasion in the member states. although the question of the 10% participation requirements and the question of the transitional periods is not changed in the rapporteur's draft report, and in the hope that any possibility of tax evasion, tax substitution or unlawful tax exemption will be eliminated, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the commission should set out in detail the 'commitments for european growth' under the european semester and the necessary structural reforms. the european semester should be an opportunity for each member state to give an account of its commitments to the eu 2020 strategy, the euro plus pact and other important eu objectives.
in writing. − the report highlights that in some member states there is both a lack of bone marrow and difficulties in finding suitable cell and tissue donors for patients, mainly due to a lack of cooperation in the field of cross-border donation. i therefore welcome all the measures to promote effective crossborder cooperation in this area, while stressing the need for strict controls to ensure maximum traceability and transparency in the system. i believe that donation should be voluntary and made on a non-profit basis. i am therefore concerned about the problems caused by the existence of numerous websites allowing gamete cells to be sold or bought online. legislation to regulate this sector should be considered as a priority in order to prevent the possible emergence of an online black market. in particular, as regards the donation of umbilical cord blood from which stem cells are derived, evidence is increasingly emerging that the cells thus obtained can be used to treat serious diseases, including childhood diseases. in order to optimise the potential of cord blood, i welcome the possibility of the competent authorities developing awareness campaigns aimed primarily at expectant mothers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr yannakoudakis' report because i share the view that the donation of multiple tissues, reproductive and non-reproductive cells should be voluntary and free of charge. i also think it is important to support research and awareness raising on cord blood donation: it produces stem cells that can be used to treat a variety of diseases, including many childhood diseases.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text proposed by mrs yannakoudakis because, although health remains a matter of national competence, it is right to seek a european approach to the debate, looking at the role that this parliament and the european community can play in defining common rules in this area. this is all the more a thorny issue to tackle given the regulatory differences that exist in eu countries. however, i believe that it is the duty of all of us to work together to combat debilitating diseases. we must therefore work to avoid speculation and anomalies which unfortunately risk breaking out today. the ethical principles which have inspired the european community so far in the matter of donating and using the human body for therapeutic purposes are essentially the principles of gratuitousness, solidarity, safety and non-profit-making, and i believe that this text reflects the main aspects in several parts of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to promote voluntary tissue and cell donation. although this is a matter for the most part of national competence, i believe it is essential that coordination between the member states be improved at european level, especially as regards the exchange of best practice. i agree that the donation system must remain absolutely free, with no economic incentives, anonymous and managed by public bodies to avoid clandestine exchanges and prohibited sales via the web. i also believe that it is more urgent than ever to identify ethical standards to improve trade between member countries.
in writing. - the data show that the supply of tissues and cells is insufficient to meet the immediate needs and requirements of individuals. in fact, those who sign up often face long waiting lists. the legislative initiative provides that the existing practices for compensation, incentives, promotion and publicity, as well as procurement and levies, must be based on the principle of altruism, i.e. voluntary and non-profit-making. although member states have already adopted legislative directives on donation, there is a need for harmonisation between member states, particularly as regards the compensation and promotion of such donations. i hope that this initiative will bring about greater efficiency and transparency, both at national level and in terms of interstate cooperation.
in writing. the issue of illegal organ trafficking is as topical and urgent as ever. the phenomenon, in a period of severe crisis and growing poverty such as we are experiencing, is then experiencing heavy accentuations. the report under consideration has the merit of showing that it intends to keep a high guard in this respect and to tackle the problem with increasing determination and with the aim of proposing concrete solutions. in this sense, the implementation of receptive facilities for tissue and cell donation, an adequate level of information and social and health care that is absolutely suitable to the needs of the case, are concrete actions to be evaluated positively.
in writing. - stressing the argument that donation - in this case of multiple tissues, reproductive cells and non-reproductive cells - should be voluntary and carried out on a non-profit basis in a transparent environment, and considering that health care is largely a member state competence, there is now a need to complement existing practices in the member states and to develop areas such as cross-border donation. in addition, taking into account the shortage of bone marrow and sperm in some member states and the difficulties in many countries to find suitable donors of cells and tissues compatible for patients belonging to ethnic minority groups, there is a need to increase the supply of tissues and cells through the exchange of best practices in relation to joint operations, ethical standards and awareness raising on donation. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.

in writing. − within the european union, women are still subject to severe discrimination in the labour market, even in an expanding sector such as the green economy. member states should therefore provide for specialised courses in the field of renewable energy to promote and facilitate women's access to new jobs. the text presented by mr gustafsson also stresses the need to promote information campaigns on eu funds in this area with the aim of increasing the participation of women at all levels of employment in the transition to the green economy.
in writing. − in 2010, employment in the service sector accounted for 69.4% of total employment in the union and 83.1% of the female labour force was employed in the service sector compared to 58.1% of the male labour force. despite the many legal initiatives taken by the union to pursue the objective of equal pay for men and women, this gap persists and progress is extremely slow. in the european union, women earn about 17.1% less than their male colleagues, while the gender pay gap in the member states ranges from 3.2% to 30.9%. even less encouraging is the fact that the increase in women's educational attainment does not always coincide with their rise in the hierarchy of employment or with improvements in their working conditions. in view of this situation, it is estimated that it will take over 40 years to achieve a significant balance in the labour market between men and women! in this context, i would stress the need for member states to have appropriate work-life balance policies and, last but not least, to have care services compatible with the flexible working hours which, according to recent studies, are gradually becoming established in the service sector.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on working conditions for women in the service sector, as it is crucial to act promptly to improve the conditions for women in this sector, given that 80% of women in the eu labour market are employed in the service sector and still suffer from significant discrimination both in access to technical and highly qualified positions and in terms of pay. i believe that in order to improve the conditions of women in the service sector, it is necessary for member states to facilitate access to vocational retraining programmes under the european social fund to offer computer training courses in order to reduce the digital gender gap and enable women to access numerous high-tech employment opportunities. finally, the eu must put in place measures to transform precarious work, which women often do in the service sector, into work with rights and work with real prospects for training and professional growth, particularly at this stage of the economic crisis when the potential of human resources must be fully exploited to revive the european economy.
