madam president, ladies and gentlemen, europe is called upon to play an increasingly important role in the context of geopolitical changes affecting large areas of the world. i believe that raising the profile and quality of european foreign policy is an increasingly urgent need, especially as many of these changes are taking place not far from our continent. to achieve this, we need to convince member states to invest in the european common foreign policy by strengthening the choices made under the lisbon treaty. we must move from the present activism, which is undeniable and is reflected in the many trips you have made to various parts of the world, to a greater role, capable not only of leaving its mark but also of changing the existing balance in favour of european foreign policy. it would be desirable to have a special session in this parliament for the discussion of foreign policy and the strategic horizons to be achieved.

in writing. i join my fellow members who signed the joint resolution on syria to call on the international community to intervene to try to stop the massacre that is taking place every day under our media eyes. since the beginning of the unrest in march 2011, nearly 20,000 people have been killed, many of them children and defenseless women, targeted by the men of president assad's regime. the number of refugees is much higher. hundreds of people are continually pouring into neighbouring countries, creating instability in geographical areas already marked by considerable political instability. in syria, there are also about 3 million people in need of urgent assistance, as the syrian government has cut off access to food, water and medicine. i regret to say that the united nations has so far been unable to deal adequately with the situation which seems to be getting out of hand day by day, until kofi annan resigned. the syrian regime has now lost all credibility and legitimacy as the representative of the syrian people and it would be desirable for president assad to step back.
mr president, commissioner, one of the facts we have to deal with is certainly the depletion of fisheries resources, on which the various available data converge. some fish stocks are seriously threatened and therefore ensuring sustainable fishing must be the objective to be achieved if we want to increase the productivity of our seas in the future. today's debate anticipates some of the central themes of the reform of the common fisheries policy. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the event of a serious accident. fisheries must continue to be an important source of employment and family income.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, every year millions of people in the european union are victims of crime. according to eurostat, there are about 30 million crimes, many of which, unfortunately, are not reported for fear of retaliation. crime often affects not only the victim but also, indirectly, the family and relatives. whether it is a mugging, robbery, theft, murder, sexual assault, or even terrorist attack, victims all have the same need: to be treated with respect and dignity. the right to support, the right to be protected from physical harm, the right to access justice and to be compensated for damages are all essential rights that every justice system must guarantee. today europe is finally proposing the adoption of a directive which will guarantee a common legal framework for the protection of all victims, thus making a concrete contribution to removing the obstacles which still prevent their genuine crossborder protection. the legislative text aims to strengthen confidence in the judicial system by encouraging the possibility of having the protection programme already applied in another member state. this right will eventually also be enjoyed by the family members of the offended person. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new legislation and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new legislation. so enough of crimes going unpunished, victims without justice and assistance, executioners free and not in prison. the text we are voting on tomorrow is a step forward towards building a model of justice where the institutions fight to defend the rights of citizens, ensuring that no executioner can remain free because of the inability of dialogue between the different judicial systems.
mr president, i too would like to congratulate my colleagues jiménez-becerril barrio and parvanova, the commissioner and the council on this step forward in european legal civilization which we are making with this directive, which is also a way of honouring the victims of 9/11. i think that, after the directives on trafficking in human beings, child pornography and the european protection order, it is very important that this directive focuses on the vulnerable person in a holistic way. it is very important that all countries define a common basis of essential rights, starting with the right to understand and be understood in one's own language, access to services, information, compensation, in short justice for oneself and one's family. it is also important that specific reference has been made in this directive, thanks also to the femm committee, to the specific nature of violence against children and women. i hope that a major effort will be made in this respect to train and update the culture of judges and lawyers, and i conclude, mr president, by saying that we must also ensure that there is no second victimisation, which is often done through the media, which, without self-regulation, disseminate images of minors, exposing them to further violence and violating their privacy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the rapporteurs, mrs jiménez-becerril barrio and mrs parvanova, and commissioner reding for the excellent work they have done together with the committees responsible. as all those who have spoken have said, this directive finally puts the victim, the individual, the citizen, at the centre of attention. i am referring in particular to the most vulnerable victims, the victims of gender-based violence and, above all, the youngest victims of crime, who often suffer from what is known as 'double victimization'. this directive will give more strength and effectiveness to other measures such as the directive on the sexual exploitation of children and child pornography online, for which i was rapporteur for the european parliament, which states the absolute need to support and protect children who are victims of sexual abuse. the new directive thus completes a path of justice and law that strengthens the value of citizenship.

mr president, too often in the european union victims of crime do not come forward because of fear or lack of confidence in the institutions. the text voted today aims to strengthen the rights of victims of crime and to guarantee them the same level of protection, assistance and access to justice in all eu countries, with particular attention to those victims who are at high risk of further harm or intimidation during criminal proceedings. it is therefore of particular importance that the status of victim be recognised, not only for persons who have suffered harm as a result of a crime, but also for the family members and the person who has died as a result of the crime.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am very much in favour of this report because when i was a regional councillor in piedmont a few years ago i was personally involved in the drafting of a regional law which provided for a number of facilities, awards and services for victims of crime. i think it is right that the european union and the member states should recognise victims of crime as subjects to be protected and helped, particularly along the immediate psychological path, but also during any criminal proceedings and until the full restoration of normal living conditions. all victims must have the same rights, be treated with respect and dignity, be protected from repeat offence, and have access to support services, justice and compensation. particular attention must be paid to minors, victims of sexual abuse and those crimes which are particularly heinous.

mr president, the reform of the common fisheries policy is a necessary choice and can no longer be postponed. europe is overfishing and often underfishing. if we are to safeguard marine biological resources, preserve the marine ecosystem and ensure the survival of the fishing industry, we must give overexploited fish stocks time to repopulate. but today, by a few votes, the shortsighted vision of those who want to maintain the status quo and continue to condemn our sea and the entire fishing industry to certain death has prevailed in this house. for these reasons i voted against the report on the reform of the common fisheries policy. we need a coherent reform, one which allows for the sustainable exploitation of marine resources and not a watered-down text with no prospects for the future. multiannual management plans and a precise timetable are needed with the establishment of a network of protected reserves. sanctions should be imposed on those member states which do not comply with the rules, carry out insufficient checks, exceed their quotas and do not provide reliable data. more protection of fish in our seas means more jobs for european fishermen, but there are still people in this house who have not understood that.
in writing. - according to eurostat data, 30 million crimes against persons or property are committed in the european union every year, and many of these go unreported. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a step in the right direction. furthermore, as estimated by the european commission, the total cost of crime is €233 billion, and this is due not only to the damage of each crime, but to the lack of adequate victim support services to help victims recover and face legal proceedings. i strongly support the work of the commission and my colleagues, because to win the confidence of all citizens in european justice, we need a complete and efficient european legal framework. and we took a first big step on 13 december with the adoption of the european protection order directive.
in writing. − citizens' trust in the judiciary is one of the european union's highest priorities. i welcome the commission's general objective of establishing minimum standards on the rights, assistance and protection of victims of crime, provided that greater attention is paid to assistance services for victims who are particularly at risk of further harm and intimidation during criminal proceedings. according to recent estimates, the annual cost of crime to victims in the union, to employers, the state and civil society, is eur 233 billion. these costs are attributable not only to the crime itself but also to the lack of adequate victim support services. i therefore welcome all efforts to strengthen the rights of victims and to provide them with appropriate support services, because they are cost-effective measures which will make a positive contribution to facilitating the reporting of crimes and to maintaining the sustainability of national justice and health systems. i also believe it is essential that the directive provides a unified definition of the concept of 'victim' so that this status is recognised not only for the person who has suffered the crime but also for his close relatives.
in writing. - i support the report, which shows a careful sensitivity to identify possible gaps and shortcomings in the valid implementation of the directive issued by the commission. in order to effectively exercise their rights, victims of crime may need more specific measures and tools of a practical and operational nature, especially in certain areas and in vulnerable segments of society. i would remind you of the observations made in the europol 2011 report on human trafficking, which clearly indicates that economic weakness and cultural conditioning are the decisive factors facilitating the activities of criminal organisations against victims, often children or women from countries marked by poverty and serious political instability, exploited in the most diverse areas, from the textile industry to begging and prostitution. without forgetting that persistent situations of cultural and social weakness in certain areas of our countries still favour phenomena of domestic violence and crimes against the person, which are very rarely reported and prosecuted. additional instruments of protection, including physical and personal protection, immediate assistance, representation in court (criminal and civil) and before the police authorities are therefore indispensable for the application of the provisions of the directive and for the exercise of the rights of victims.
in writing. − i voted in favour of ms parvanova’s report on the minimum standards on the rights, support, and protection of victims of crime because it draws necessary attention to an issue that needs to be addressed by the eu. first and foremost, the provisions will establish uniformity throughout the eu for victims’ rights and protection, ensuring all victims of crime will be treated in the same way regardless of the member state in which they are located. notably, the report encourages the individual assessment of a victim’s needs, particularly those with specific needs, when determining the methodology of protection. it recognises the unique nature of gender-based discrimination and urges particular protection for those who are repeat victims of crime.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report. to ensure that the european union complies with the stockholm programme, it is urgent to establish a common and transparent judicial system applicable in all eu member states. i am sure that the directive under consideration will not only help to defend the rights of victims but also help european citizens to gain confidence in the national judicial system and that of neighbouring member states by harmonizing these minimum standards.
in writing. - i voted with conviction in favour of the parvanova-jiménez-becerril barrio resolution, by which the european parliament wanted to sign its commitment to the protection of victims of crime. the initiative is part of and complements the 2009 stockholm programme, which was enriched in 2011 with new and important regulatory instruments: the commission has also adopted a number of directives on the protection of minors, including the directive on the european protection order, the directive on combating the sexual abuse and exploitation of children and child pornography, and the directive on the prevention and suppression of trafficking in human beings. the directive follows the 2001 framework decision by introducing specific obligations for victims. the definition should be extended to include the relatives of direct victims. finally, i congratulate the rapporteurs on their success in drawing up a transversal text covering all categories of victims, with particular attention to 'particularly vulnerable victims'.
in writing. - i wanted to express my full support for this report which aims to offer greater protection and guarantees for victims of crime. a person who has been robbed, assaulted, harassed, or who has been the victim of more serious crimes such as rape or incidents related to organised crime and terrorism, must be able to feel adequately protected and respected, so as not to risk being a victim twice, of the same violence suffered and of the problems that may arise thereafter. in this connection, it should be emphasized that special attention and specific measures are taken for women, minors and people with disabilities, for whom a criminal episode can leave very serious repercussions that are difficult to overcome over time. the commission is also proposing to introduce a european standard for the protection of victims of crime in the member states.
in writing. - istat reports that women aged 16 to 70 who say they have been victims of physical or sexual violence at least once in their lives number 6 million 743 thousand, or 31.9%; the rate of rape alone is 4.8% (over one million women). 14.3% of women also say they have been subjected to violence by their partner: 12% of physical violence and 6.1% of sexual violence. of the remaining 24.7%, 9.8% were physical violence and 20.4% sexual violence. 2.4% of women say they have been raped by their partner and 2.9% by strangers. 93% of women who say they have been abused by their spouse said they did not report the abuse to the public authorities; the percentage rises to 96% if the perpetrator is not the partner. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. why are these abuses not reported? because the victims don't feel protected. victim protection programmes are therefore a step in the right direction in assisting women as well as the elderly and children.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council directive establishing minimum standards on the rights, assistance and protection of victims of crime. the new directive aims to establish minimum standards on the rights, assistance, recognition and maximum protection of victims of crime, irrespective of their legal status, in the eu, both in terms of content and implementation. as trust in justice is a priority for all citizens, particularly for victims who feel that their rights are being ignored or out of reach, i consider this proposal for a directive to be an appropriate means of overcoming the many gaps and obstacles currently present in the internal market and the european area of freedom, security and justice.
in writing. − since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon in 2009 and the guidelines for the creation of a european area of freedom, security and justice, as set out in the stockholm programme, the protection of victims of crime in the eu has been a priority for the union. now, on the basis of council framework decision 2001/220/jha on the position of the victim in criminal proceedings, it is necessary to adopt a comprehensive european legal framework offering recognition and maximum protection to all victims of crime, regardless of their legal status, on the territory of the eu, and to provide a unified definition of the concept of 'victim', so that this status is recognised not only for the person who has suffered the crime, but also for his or her close relatives. in order to strengthen the rights of victims and to ensure greater protection of their privacy, we vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i congratulate my colleague, mrs jiménez-becerril barrio, on her work. by adopting this report, having regard to the commission proposal to the european parliament and the council (com (2011) 275) and to the opinion of the european economic and social committee of 7 december 2011, parliament ensures that any victim of crime will enjoy the same rights and an assessment of their specific needs throughout the eu. but the positive aspect of this report is that from now on, victims of crimes such as robbery, theft, assault, rape, harassment, hate crime, terrorist attacks, or human trafficking will no longer face problems caused by cultural, linguistic or legislative differences, and above all will be supported and supported, from the moment they are subjected to the crime, by free and confidential assistance services (e.g. psychological support), regardless of where the crime took place.
in writing. - i support the report by mr moreira which aims to bring council regulation (ec) no 774/94 into line with the regime of delegated acts as provided for in articles 290 and 291 tfeu. there are therefore no changes to the content or substance of the regulation but it is merely a technical update.
in writing. - regulation (ec) no 774/94 empowered the commission to adopt the necessary implementing measures and to amend the regulation in the event of adjustments to the volumes and other conditions of the tariff quota arrangements for certain meat and cereals, in particular by decisions relating to the conclusion of agreements with third countries. it is now necessary to align those powers with the system of delegated and implementing acts subsequent to lisbon by conferring the relevant implementing powers on the commission, by aligning that regulation with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). in addition, stressing the importance of the fact that the right of control over the implementing acts necessary for the management of the quota system provided for in the regulation under consideration remains with the committee on international trade, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the commission's proposal, for which i voted in favour, aims to adapt the regulation to the new rules of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, as regards the powers of the european parliament with regard to the management of community tariff quotas for high-quality beef, pigmeat, poultrymeat, wheat and wheat. the european parliament will therefore be involved in the preparation and implementation of delegated acts, the limitation of the delegation of power to tacitly extendable five-year periods, the extension of the time limit for possible objections to a draft delegated act from two to four months and the modification of the application of the written procedure.
in writing. - in view of council regulations (ec) no 2008/97, (ec) no 779/98 and (ec) no 1506/98 concerning imports of olive oil and other agricultural products from turkey, and taking into account that much of the common commercial policy legislation is being aligned to articles 290 and 291 tfeu through two 'omnibus' instruments on trade, it is now necessary to align those regulations to the system of implementing and delegated acts introduced by the treaty of lisbon (articles 290 and 291 tfeu). i would like to see the right of scrutiny for these implementing acts retained by the committee on international trade rather than by the committee on agriculture, and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i support the report by mr moreira on the 'amendment to the agreement on mutual recognition in relation to conformity assessment, certificates and marks of conformity between the ec and australia', an agreement first signed in 1999 and which is being updated in an improving manner by removing certain trade restrictions which have proved unnecessary and reducing the administrative burden of administering the agreement. this agreement provides that australia undertakes to carry out controls on products intended for the eu in accordance with the legislation in force in the union and that the eu undertakes to do the same in return; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. the amendments to the main text of the rra will allow for greater flexibility in the structure of the sectoral annexes. unnecessary restrictions on trade between the parties shall be eliminated. in addition, the administrative burden of administering the agreement will be reduced.
in writing. − considering that the arrs, agreements on mutual recognition in relation to conformity assessment of regulated products, give each party the authority to inspect and certify products in accordance with the regulatory requirements of the other party, on its territory and prior to export, and considering that the arr with australia entered into force on 1 january 1999, there is now a need to improve and simplify the functioning of this agreement. in order to allow greater flexibility in the structure of the sectoral annexes, to eliminate unnecessary restrictions on trade between the parties, and to reduce the administrative burden of administering the agreement, as well as to facilitate and clarify the operation of the agreement, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i support the moreira report on mutual recognition of conformity assessment between the eu and new zealand: its objective is to give both parties the authority to control products intended for export under each other's rules; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject.
in writing. − in parallel to the proposed amendment to the mutual recognition agreement with australia, an amendment to the mra with new zealand, which entered into force on 1 january 1999, was proposed. considering that the arrs are agreements on mutual recognition in relation to conformity assessment of regulated products, which give each party the authority to inspect and certify products in accordance with the regulatory requirements of the other party, on its territory and prior to export, and wishing for greater flexibility in the structure of sectoral annexes, eliminating unnecessary restrictions on trade between the parties, and reducing the administrative burden related to the management of the agreement, i vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr gallagher's report because i agree with the imposition of stricter intervention measures on those third countries which repeatedly violate agreements on the implementation of unsustainable fishing, which consequently cause considerable damage to transnational fish stocks, i.e. those of common interest. i therefore support the restrictions suggested in this report on the quantity of imports allowed, on the use of european ports and on the prohibition of joint fishing between vessels of countries engaged in unsustainable fishing and those of member states.
in writing. − according to the 2010 fao report, the average per capita consumption of fishery products has doubled since the 1960s: fish is the leading raw material in the food industry by trade volume, with an estimated value of $102 billion in 2008. it should not be surprising, then, that a part of the fish stocks is under constant threat of depletion and that the question of environmental and food balances calls for the utmost responsibility and concrete action to combat illegal fishing, the turnover of which, according to some environmental organizations, exceeds 25% of the value of the global market. as the primary stakeholder in this market, the union has a duty (for reasons of self-preservation and fairness) to leverage markets to incentivise less sensitive countries to comply with the stock management obligations established by the conventions. i therefore support the report.
in writing. − the management of highly migratory fish stocks requires constant cooperation and direct consultation between the countries whose fleets exploit these stocks, avoiding the risk of unilateral measures potentially harmful to the long-term sustainability of the resources. on the other hand, it is the eu's responsibility to ensure that this obligation to cooperate is respected and that member states do not take unilateral actions contrary to the general interest in the conservation of the marine ecosystem. however, in addition to effective measures, the eu needs to be equipped with appropriate control instruments to fulfil this task. as in other sectors, unbridled competition between member states can have negative consequences. this is why it has chosen to support the measures provided for in the directive, in particular those aimed at imposing quantitative restrictions on imports into the union of fish caught from the stock of common interest under the control of a third country. it also welcomed the introduction of instruments to ensure that the measures adopted are effective, proportionate and compatible with international standards, as well as respecting environmental, commercial, economic and social standards.
in writing. − the repeated violations of the un convention on the law of the sea and the un fish stocks agreement make it urgent to create an appropriate legal instrument to enable the eu to respond to the lack of cooperation shown by the states concerned. i fully agree with the rapporteur on this point, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − in view of the repeated violations of the un convention on the law of the sea and the un fish stocks agreement, as well as the unilateral actions taken in defiance of the cooperation requirements imposed by the regional fisheries management organisations (rfmos) on coastal states for the responsible management of transboundary and highly migratory fish stocks, it is necessary to create an appropriate legal instrument to enable the eu to respond to the lack of cooperation demonstrated by the states concerned. underlining the eu's responsibility to ensure sustainable fishing and the respect of the obligations arising from the common management of transboundary and migratory fish stocks and therefore the importance of providing the eu with the means to take effective action against states which are not prepared to assume such responsibility, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the report by mr gallagher was voted on today at the plenary session in strasbourg. the regulation adopted allows the use of trade sanctions against third countries which allow unsustainable fishing and fishery products from stocks of common interest. these measures should discourage the overexploitation of certain fish species in the north atlantic. although the legislation can be applied against third countries, the situation in the north atlantic is also in our interest. iceland unilaterally increased its mackerel catch from 363 tonnes in 2005 to 147 000 tonnes in 2012. the faroe islands' share of the mackerel increased from 27 830 tonnes in 2009 to 149 000 tonnes in 2012.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the european commission needs to have more powers to ban imports of fish into the eu from over-exploited fish stocks. the new rules will help to discourage the overfishing of fish such as mackerel, which is particularly harmful to iceland and the faroe islands. the commission will now have to carry out a comprehensive reform of the fisheries policy to make it more environmentally sustainable.
in writing. - finally, this report is a response to those third countries bordering the mediterranean and beyond, which continue to violate fisheries agreements and the un convention on the law of the sea. it is unthinkable to continue to harass european fishermen with rules and restrictions which, on the one hand, reduce their income and, on the other, oblige member states to finance damaged fleets when other countries in our neighbourhood, not respecting the rules, fish unsustainably. so banning imports of fish from third countries which are behaving incorrectly protects our fishermen and discourages those who are behaving incorrectly.
in writing. the report is one of the cornerstones of the reform of the cfp, increasing its competitiveness, particularly of producers, and yet it also has aspects of primary importance for the health and consumer confidence of the sector. in this respect, the interests of consumers and the satisfaction of their needs for clarity and transparency must be the guiding light of our common policies, because they can be a means of stimulating purchases, all the more so at a time of falling sales, when, as all the indicators show, the trend is to favour a conscious and informed purchase, which is synonymous with quality purchasing. we are therefore strongly convinced that the date of actual catching of the fish, rather than the date of landing of the vessel, should be included on the packaging of the product. on the other hand, the landing date, which is supported by moderate and conservative forces, is not only misleading information for the consumer but also an undue interference in favour of large fleets - capable of remaining at sea for several days - compared to small boats that remain at sea for only a few hours. once again, we would have expected more rational behaviour from the moderate forces, which seemed to be bending to the interests of the big groups.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr stevenson's report because i am firmly convinced of the competitive advantage of greater efficiency on the markets of joint organisations and producers in the fisheries and aquaculture sector. the objectives of the common fisheries policy are to improve environmental protection through effective regulation. however, as the report points out, the operators in the sector and the consequences for their business must also be taken into account, so that new regulations do not stifle their entrepreneurship and their ability to compete in the market. i also support the initiative to increase consultation between transnational producer organisations with common commercial characteristics and needs. it is in this direction, but also taking into account the peculiarities of the specific fishing areas, that work must also be done in the drafting of the cfp.
in writing. − fisheries play a very important role in the economies of the union's coastal regions, including the outermost regions. it is the source of income for fishermen in these regions, and it is therefore necessary to promote market stability and a better match between supply and demand. my vote is in favour.
in writing. since 1970, the common organisation of the markets (cmo) has been the first component of the common fisheries policy (cfp). in the context of a genuine reform of the cfp, a more significant role for producer organisations in the day-to-day management of fisheries activities within a more regionalised system is desirable; the use of modern technology to improve market knowledge needs to be promoted in the framework of the future european maritime and fisheries fund; it is important to ensure that consumers have the right to better and comprehensible information on the fishery products they purchase, through appropriate labelling. with these objectives in mind and stressing the importance of rewarding sustainable fishing practices with an eu ecolabel, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr mcavan's proposal for a directive because i agree with the need to increase pharmacovigilance controls in an attempt to tackle the practices of pharmaceutical companies which continue to market products which are declared harmful to the health of european consumers and therefore banned from the market.
in writing. - i would like to congratulate my colleague on the courage and rigour with which he has dealt with some of the problems which, if left unresolved for a long time, could weaken not only the cfsp but also the union's political position and credibility in general. perhaps with the financial crisis the time has come to untie these knots, as i believe the rapporteur has done by moving from a few fixed points of method to a comprehensive, coherent and uniform approach to eu foreign policy, based on a realistic assessment of scenarios, options, resources and results. in defining the eu's foreign policy and its evaluation parameters, parliament now plays a central role as the repository of political legitimacy deriving from the investment of european citizens, to whom it responds. the recent developments in the crisis have accelerated the maturation of the awareness of a common destiny in the maintenance of the currency, the economy and the institutions themselves. foreign policy can only be a fundamental part of this sense of being europe. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. we need a strategic vision. we must replace fear with courage. courage impels us to action which in time generates hope, and the real hope for the whole world is the presence of a europe which has the strength to bet, in international relations, on the convictions which have guaranteed it the exceptional status of these 60 years.
in writing. − the stated ambitions of the lisbon treaty, which provides that 'the union's competence in matters of common foreign and security policy shall cover all areas of the union's foreign policy and all matters relating to the union's security, including the progressive framing of a common defence policy which may lead to a common defence' (article 24 (1) teu), provide the starting point for building a fundamental framework for the elaboration of a comprehensive, coherent and uniform eu approach to foreign policy. to this end, a new contribution from parliament is needed, which is more pragmatic than the 2010 council report on the cfsp, and not up to the ambitions of the lisbon treaty. in the hope of providing a new european security strategy and a contribution to the formulation of the eu's foreign policy, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − we are voting to say that, although the lisbon treaty is giving new impetus to the eu's foreign policy, providing the institutional and operational tools, its effectiveness and sustainability are undermined by the ongoing financial crisis. to make its weight felt internationally, the eu must not only ensure that its policies, actors and institutions are consistent, but also develop a truly strategic concept for foreign policy and provide the necessary staff, financial and diplomatic resources. today we sent a clear signal to the high representative catherine ashton. the european union's foreign policy, in times of increasing challenges and limited resources, must be strategic and forward-looking. the new strategic framework for the european union's external action must also be democratically legitimate. our role as parliamentarians is essential if policy is to be understood and supported by european citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a new overall and strategic concept of european foreign policy is needed if the eu's external action is to be coherent and effective in achieving its objectives. although the lisbon treaty is already giving new impetus to the eu's foreign policy, its effectiveness will be severely tested if sufficient minimum resources are not available. to be effective in the international arena, the eu must not only ensure that its policies, actors and institutions are consistent, but also develop a new strategic foreign policy model to achieve this fully.
in writing. the annual report marks the beginning of a genuine 'new strategic approach' by parliament to the european union's foreign policy, building on the ambitions set out in the lisbon treaty. the aim is to develop a comprehensive eu approach, which is fundamental to the implementation of a common foreign policy. the long-term strategic approach of the 2010 council report is of key importance, despite the fact that it is a step back from some of the ambitions expressed in the lisbon treaty. i therefore voted in favour of this report, given its valuable contribution to the formulation of eu foreign policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr haglund's report because i agree with the proposal to introduce a system of individual transferable fishing concessions, subject to protection measures. i am also in favour of the creation of an ad hoc system for artisanal and coastal fishing, to protect it from competition from industrial fishing activities, and of a second system for environmentally friendly fishing vessels. these measures are designed to reduce the overcapacity of fisheries currently operating in european waters.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. it is right to stress the need for a balance between the ecological and the economic and social situation in each fishing activity, recognising that without abundant fish stocks the fishing industry will not be viable.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because fish stocks in danger of extinction can no longer wait for bureaucratic delays on the part of the states. long-term management plans must be well defined and based on an ecosystem approach to find the solutions needed for the management of mixed fisheries. but as long as some member states continue to delay in communicating these plans to the european commission, the difficulty of precisely identifying areas of intervention will be to the detriment of the objectives of protecting certain endangered species, such as bluefin tuna in our mediterranean. this neglect also hinders the granting of the necessary funding for well-defined areas of relevant scientific research and the european parliament has on several occasions spoken out to urge member states which have failed to comply with their obligations. the real problem is not to apply the sanctions provided for, but to speed up the timely collection of data to protect the marine ecosystem.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 requires the commission to report, by the end of 2012, to both the european parliament and the council on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources and on the achievements of the member states in the adjustment of fishing capacity. the result is definitely negative: the efforts of member states to improve the conservation and restoration of fish stocks have been insufficient. this requires a reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) which strikes the right balance between ecological and economic aspects and provides a general definition of overcapacity at eu level and a specific definition at regional level, taking into account the different weighting factors in the regions. with these objectives in mind, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the results of member states' efforts to conserve and exploit fish stocks for their own sake are rather poor; the failure to meet their obligations, especially in relation to communication, the setting of appropriate reduction targets, and the collection and transmission of data is not encouraging. i therefore support parliament's position, stressing that it is unacceptable that member states do not provide the data necessary for sound scientific advice. the system of restrictions on fishing activities in waters within 12 nautical miles is a positive development, since it is effective in achieving the objectives of the cfp.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr salavrakos' own-initiative report because i am in favour of the three objectives of this reform. first, i believe that measures to conserve marine resources should be strengthened, for example by creating a voluntary 'ecological quality' label, increasing the amount of co-financing allowed and continuously collecting data to monitor the state of biodiversity in the various european basins. i also believe that, because of the volatility of oil prices, the fisheries sector requires strict control and certification of all products on the eu market, especially those imported from third countries. finally, i am in favour of the regionalisation of the fisheries sector to ensure capillary control and efficient management of each european sea basin.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report. i agree that the fisheries sector can only remain sustainable if a balance is struck between socioeconomic and environmental aspects and if there is a sufficient number of properly trained and qualified workers. to achieve this, employment in the fisheries sector must be attractive.
in writing. - the debate on fisheries was the focus of this plenary session, starting with this report on the reform of the common policy. firstly, we must stress the failure of the action taken so far at european level, since the sector does not seem to have given the answers we had in mind, namely, first of all, an increase in employment and less dependence on the outside world. unfortunately, neither of these two hopes has come true and today we are faced with a situation of objective difficulty for the system: the proposed solutions include new action to promote the conservation and enhancement of marine biological resources, a more rational management of the socioeconomic and employment sustainability of the sector, and a call for strict rules against non-eu states that do not respect certain maritime environmental protection characteristics. in addition to these measures, regionalisation is proposed as a key principle of fisheries reform: this should mean having more freedom in relation to different needs, while fully respecting the principle of subsidiarity. for all these reasons i have therefore decided to support all the reports on fisheries, a sector which can and must still do a lot in terms of the environment, food, the economy and employment.
in writing. − given that one of the eu's objectives is to ensure the long-term environmental sustainability of the union's fisheries and aquaculture sector, which is one of the prerequisites for ensuring its economic and social sustainability as well, the common fisheries policy needs to be reformed in a radical and ambitious way. in order to conserve marine biological resources, the cfp should apply the precautionary approach to fisheries management and ensure that the sustainable exploitation of living marine biological resources restores and maintains populations of all stocks of harvested species above levels capable of producing the maximum sustainable yield. i would like to stress the importance of the fisheries and extensive aquaculture sectors for the creation of direct and indirect jobs in our maritime regions, and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we have had the opportunity during this plenary session to discuss this reform, which is the dominant theme of the current fisheries negotiations. the green paper on reform of the sector was presented in april 2009. the various council of ministers meetings on the subject discussed its basic aspects with a view to reaching an initial agreement on shared texts. one of the key points in the text is, in my view, paragraph 58, which calls for the emff (european maritime and fisheries fund) to provide financial support for the renewal and modernisation of fishing fleets in order to achieve the objectives of the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). the average age of fishing fleets in the eu is 27 years. i voted for the amendment, but unfortunately it did not pass. i therefore felt obliged to vote against the whole text, since i consider it of fundamental importance to modernise the fishing fleets for reasons of safety, environmental protection or reduction of fuel consumption, as the text states.
in writing. − in sharing and supporting the identification of the main objectives of the reform of the common fisheries policy, such as environmental sustainability, socioeconomic sustainability and regionalisation, i voted in favour of the own-initiative report discussed here. the commission recalls that a thorough reform of the eu's common fisheries policy (cfp) is needed, given that its objectives have not been fully achieved. it should also be stressed that sustainable fishing will bring enormous environmental, social and economic benefits, as a non-damaged environment will ensure a secure future for fishing communities and a profitable fishing industry without the need for public support. it is also essential that the cfp is in line with environmental and development policies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, we are discussing today the political situation in a country which has been a member of the european union since 2007 and which is complying with the obligations imposed by the acquis communautaire. among the legal duties and political objectives which unite and bind the members of the union is the rule of law as an indispensable condition for the democratic organization of society. this makes it important to discuss the current situation in romania, which is taking on worrying contours caused by an unprecedented power struggle and institutional war. a conflict in which a majority attempts to occupy, bend and enslave all other bodies, including constitutional and judicial bodies and other institutions at will, by overriding and upsetting the balance of power and functions and institutions. it is strange that a section of this parliament, which is always attentive to the level of democracy and freedom in the countries that are part of the union, should be indifferent or even justify it on this occasion. i think that this parliament and the commission are doing a very good job of keeping a high level of attention on what is happening in romania.
mr president, for eight years romania was ruled by an authoritarian president who violated fundamental rights, who regularly attacked the parliament, the government, the judiciary, the trade unions and all the media that opposed him. băsescu’s regime was based on a parallel system of personal power. it was the same old story – using intelligence services, the police, and the office of the prosecutor to spy on citizens, to intimidate political opponents and protect friends. the mafia, corruption and clientele were closely associated with this parallel system that was finally challenged by a popular reaction. the commission did not lift a finger against all these abuses. romania got a new parliament that started an impeachment process which it carried out according to constitutional rules. at this point the commission intervened, endorsing all the allegations brought by băsescu. so, ms reding, you should apologise for the irresponsible language you used against a member state and a democratic government calling a process that was constitutional and legal a parliamentary coup.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i wonder what the purpose of a banking union is. if this is about greater supervision, then i wonder what the recent establishment of a european banking supervisory authority has done, if not to decree the bankruptcy of these authorities which have been unable to provide any useful response. many banks have continued to act in a disorderly manner, not helping the real economy but instead focusing on risky and ethically questionable operations such as, for example, the continuing financing of spanish banks to the main and indebted football clubs of the iberian country. i think that instead of banking union it would be more useful to talk about banking separation, i.e. the division between deposit banks and investment banks, on the model of the american glass-steagall act. the banks that collect money from current accounts and small savers should be protected, but i do not see why they should be covered by common guarantees - that is, with the money of all citizens - those banks that seek their profit through speculative activity and high-risk investments.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are not convinced by this banking union, because it seems to have no other objective than to put a fine tombstone on any prospect of the adoption at european level of the regulatory principles of the glass-steagall act. in this connection, how can we not agree with the concern expressed by the president of the german savings banks, mr fahrenschon, that a banking union with central supervision in the hands of the ecb and a common deposit guarantee fund is equivalent to life insurance for the systemic banks, that is to say those, not all, in whose belly there is a sea of derivatives waste? we all know it, but no one dares to say it! with this solution, healthy banks, for example the savings banks - not only german but also those of padania - and the popular banks, close to the territory, the peoples and the regions - we remember the message that yesterday gave two million catalans who want freedom - pay to allow the sick to continue to speculate. one last question: the president of the ecb, mario draghi, says every day that the euro is irreversible. i would like to know if any of you have found an article in the treaties which allows you to decide which currency the member states should have. i didn't find him.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the proposals you have outlined are very important, both for their substance and for what the banking union will have to do, but also for the political message they contain. it is a way of sharing sovereignty which goes in the direction of building a european institutional set-up different and more advanced than the present one. i think, however, that some non-marginal aspects must be carefully considered. the first is the time of completion. you have said, quite rightly, that this is not the time to distract us by discussing the people who will have to take on these functions. but that is a subject which must be tackled, and quickly, so as not to undermine the potential of the instrument we are discussing. the second aspect concerns the need to properly dissolve the knot between the supervisory and the autonomous functions of the central bank. the autonomy must be defended, and the monitoring must be linked to the functions of parliament. what is happening in national parliaments today is clear; what will happen here in the future is still undefined.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, we support the compromise proposal in the committee on international trade. we believe that a very reasonable balance has been struck. on the one hand, we have a certain date, a deadline. i would ask everyone to reflect on the absurdity of rejecting the committee's proposal because we have obligations in the wto which we have to respect. on the other hand, we are giving a couple of years more, meeting at least partly the demands of the acp countries. i think this is a debate that needs to be de-dramatized. in the end, as the commissioner has already said in his speech, we are talking about a very limited volume of trade, although the decision we are going to take tomorrow is very important for some of the capitals of the acp countries. there is a kind of asymmetrical importance between our perception of what is at stake and that of some acp countries. i do not think that by setting a deadline so close, as some acp countries may feel, it is almost inevitable, that the negotiations on the economic partnership agreements can be brought to a speedier conclusion. we want these agreements. but these are partnership agreements which must be concluded in the best possible way, by persuasion, through an effort of persuasion. these two additional years, if all of them are really necessary, can be an opportunity to increase our efforts in the negotiations, and to extend the network of partners, not just the governments. there is a certain mistrust in the societies of these countries; we also need to engage with national parliamentarians who often do not ratify, but have a political voice and influence in the debate in their countries and complain that they are not getting enough information. as i suggested to mr horsens at our acp parliamentary assembly, we may need to organise public seminars with the media and ngos to explain our position. there's a kenyan proverb that says, "if you want to go far, go together".

quality systems will strengthen and simplify european quality policy. from now on we will have a single instrument for geographical indications, designations of origin, traditional specialities and coherent and strengthened quality policy, will certainly best serve the diversity of producers, products and consumers in the european union. i can therefore conclude by confirming that the commission supports this political agreement and i hope that parliament will adopt it tomorrow. in reply to mrs garcía pérez's question about the specific mention of mountain areas, we will finalise the proposal as soon as the impact study has been carried out. i would like to conclude by saying a few words about comitology. during the trilogue on that draft regulation, the commission agreed not to adopt the draft implementing act if the committee responsible does not deliver an opinion, in which case the third subparagraph of article 5 (4) of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 will apply. this is contrary to the general rule followed by the commission, but in this particular case, the agreement could not have been obtained if it had objected on this point. therefore, in a spirit of compromise, the commission does not wish to oppose a qualified majority in favour of the text of the presidency and wishes to make the following statement: the commission emphasises that it is contrary to the spirit of regulation no 182/2011 to invoke article 5 (4), second subparagraph, point (b) in a systematic way. recourse to this provision should meet a specific need to derogate from the rule of principle that the commission may adopt a draft implementing act where no opinion is delivered. since it is an exception to the general rule laid down in article 5 (4), recourse to the second subparagraph, point (b), cannot be regarded simply as a discretionary power of the legislator, but must be interpreted restrictively and must therefore be justified. in conclusion, i note that the two institutions have considered it appropriate to continue discussions on marketing standards, in particular, but also on other points which were originally envisaged in this draft regulation in the context of the reform of the common agricultural policy which is under way, and the commission will give its full support to ensure that this can be carried out successfully.

states. for example france has recently made a request to monitor car exports from korea into the european market. that is a first step in the safeguard that we would obtain by monitoring. if we get such a question we duly research it and only take a decision after having considered all elements of the file. so we are very serious about this, not only where the major economic interests of the the agenda includes the report by lidia joanna geringer de oedenberg, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on certain permitted uses of orphan works (com (2011) 0289 - c7-0138/2011 - 2011/0136 (cod)) (a7-0055/2012).
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating mrs geringer on her very patient and tenacious work, which has led to a result which we regard as positive, despite some difficulties. the directive we are going to adopt is important not only because it will increase the number of people who can enjoy the cultural benefits of works of art and invention - which is already very important - but also because it breaks with a position which has hitherto been negative for the dissemination of culture, namely a sacred conception of copyright, to the point where copyright is considered so sacred that it is defended even when the author is not there, does not exist, perhaps because the author is dead or is not interested. the closure of management companies is also an obstacle to the spread of culture, which is why we arrived late and with many difficulties. i am referring, for example, to the attitude taken towards access for the blind and visually impaired to cultural works and the attitude towards private copying. we have been faced with a kind of wall in these respects, which we have been able to break down today, or at least to open a breach. the measure we are going to adopt has great political significance and the step forward that is about to be taken must be voted for. there are certainly inadequacies - and i understand the misgivings of our friends in the green group - but they cannot be a reason for not grasping the opportunity and the innovative significance of the operation that is being carried out. fortunately, commissioner barnier has tabled the regulation which we are discussing in our committee on management companies, and so we are touching on a very important point in order that the whole complex of copyright issues and topics can finally be tackled in the right way. it is a positive proposal which we consider should be amended and improved, but which we should support and which is indeed something which convinces us even more to vote in favour.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur and all her colleagues who, with their excellent work, have helped to bring about one of the key actions of the european digital agenda. the directive we are about to adopt will help to achieve two fundamental objectives for the development of european copyright. firstly, it will allow the dissemination and use of works which would otherwise be at risk of disappearing from our cultural heritage. this is an initiative which fulfils a fundamental principle of copyright, namely the protection and promotion of culture and intellectual creations. secondly, this directive will make it possible to modernise and improve the legal framework of the member states by adapting the existing legislation to technical developments and the need for greater flexibility. this will help to strengthen the economic benefits of copyright by ensuring fair remuneration for work done and identifying any rights holders within a very secure framework of rules. as regards the commercial use of orphan works, i share the approach adopted by this parliament, which provides for commercial use only to offset the costs of the public service provided by the various institutions responsible. this directive does not concern issues related to the commercial exploitation of orphan works, but rather to the legitimate and cross-border access to works with the ultimate aim of promoting the diversity and richness of europe's cultural heritage.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the excellent report by mrs geringer, which we have helped to enrich in the committee on culture. the reasons for this appreciation are primarily the recognition of copyright as the economic and principled foundation of the creative industries, since it stimulates innovation, creativity, investment and production. the dissemination of works, after their digitisation, is the primary means of safeguarding and promoting europe's cultural heritage. the european union has a very rich cultural heritage, but much of it lies unused in the archives and libraries of our member states, with no possibility of access by the public. it is therefore appropriate to make these works as accessible as possible to all. the real wealth of our union is its cultural heritage, which has no equal in the world, but which is often neglected and loses its value not only culturally but also economically. the compromise reached between copyright protection and the use of the public is the best way to reverse this trend and revive our cultural heritage without infringing any rights. it is true that perhaps not all the objectives have been achieved, but the glass is not half empty but certainly half full.

in writing. - i welcome the regulation of the european social entrepreneurship fund (esf) set out in this report. the determination of access to the fund, the scope of application and the conditions of use are necessary procedures to make the efsi a business development and growth instrument as close as possible to the needs of operators and transparent in its articulation. the efsi, on the other hand, must be one of the levers for the development of the european union's economy and be used in accordance with criteria of efficiency and effectiveness that accompany the measures taken to adopt useful instruments in the strategy for exiting the crisis.
in writing. - the difficulties faced by many european companies call for a political commitment to improve business conditions. it is necessary to establish a common framework of rules regarding the use of the designation 'european social entrepreneurship fund (esif) ', with particular reference to the composition of the portfolio of funds operating under that designation, the eligible investment objectives, the instruments they may use and the investors who may invest in those funds under uniform rules in the union. in the absence of a common framework, there is a risk that member states adopt divergent measures at national level which directly affect and hinder the proper functioning of the internal market, as funds would be subject to different rules in different member states. in addition, the existence of divergent qualitative requirements on portfolio composition, eligible investment objectives and eligible investors could result in different levels of investor protection and confusion regarding the investment proposal associated with european social entrepreneurship funds. finally, we ask that investors be able to compare investment proposals from different efsi. it is necessary to remove significant barriers to cross-border capital raising and to avoid distortions of competition between such funds.
in writing. − social entrepreneurship plays an important role in the european union by bringing vulnerable and marginalised people into the world of work. we are very sensitive to and in favour of their economic support when it comes to european citizens belonging to vulnerable groups and in particular the disabled. we have our doubts about those social enterprises which try to consider "weak" people who are not weak. i am referring in this case to non-eu citizens who, in a time of economic crisis such as this, if there are no jobs available, would be better off not coming to europe. particular care must be taken to ensure that social entrepreneurship does not become a loophole for some firms to operate at lower prices than others and thus actually alter market conditions.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution. we must promote european culture by overcoming an anachronistic and restrictive bureaucracy but guaranteeing copyright. orphan works are works whose rightholder (s) cannot be identified or located, although in order to make a work accessible to the public an authorisation from the rightholder is required. for the new generations in particular, who are used to digital formats, what is not found on the internet may not even exist. a forgotten heritage, in short, that a powerful american search engine would like to take possession of exclusively, although for now limited to us works only. despite the commission's recommendation of 24 august 2006, only a few member states have introduced legislation on orphan works but allowing online access only to citizens residing in their national territories. what we parliamentarians are asking for today is that libraries, educational institutions, museums or archives be allowed to provide specific services by providing for the online dissemination of orphan works whose ownership right would be immediately recognized if, one day, a copyright holder came forward with a properly documented request.
in writing. the solution was finally found to establish a legal framework to promote the digitisation and dissemination of copyrighted or related works whose owner has not been identified or can not be traced. a work may be considered orphan after diligent and good faith research and may not be made public for profit. if the rights holders are eventually identified, the orphan work status will be terminated and they will be paid a lump sum considering that the distribution was free of charge. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. the commission's current proposal, on which parliament has delivered its opinion today, aims to allow libraries, educational establishments, museums or archives to provide specific services in the internal market for the online dissemination of orphan works, that is, works whose owner or rights holders cannot be identified or traced. the operational objectives of the proposal include reducing transaction costs associated with the online use of orphan works by such institutions and facilitating cross-border access to works.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, minister mavroyiannis, commissioner lewandowski, by voting tomorrow to ask parliament to support by a large majority what was approved in the committee on budgets, we intend to send a strong signal to the council in view of the forthcoming conciliation. before i go into the details, i would like to thank the shadow rapporteurs and all the colleagues, as well as the officials and staff who have contributed during these months of work. as you know, the council has proposed a significant series of cuts, in clear contrast to the indications given by the european council of 28 and 29 june, where, at the highest political level, it was decided to invest to support europe's growth and development. we have therefore decided in our reading to restore the commission's draft budget and to increase resources selectively in certain budget headings closely linked to growth policies and job creation, especially for our young people. as i have said on other occasions, this is not a careless attitude in today's context: we are all aware of the financial difficulties facing each member state. but the response to the crisis, as the european council has also stressed, must be more europe, not less europe. i would call the position we are going to vote on tomorrow responsible. but responsible doesn 't mean renunciate . the commission's proposal is to contribute to economic recovery by means of specific and selective increases, which are more limited than in a normal reading of the european parliament, especially in terms of commitments, but which respect the general climate of austerity and the sacrifices imposed at national level. i therefore believe that the member states cannot accuse us of demanding increases which are not in line with the present crisis and i reiterate our determination to maintain an adequate level of investment to generate new economic impetus, in defence of the demands of our citizens in difficulty. i would now like to turn to the subject of payments. it is not lost on anyone that this is the most delicate point of the negotiations, but i think that this issue must be dealt with in technical rather than political terms. the level of payments fixed by the commission in the draft budget was determined on the basis of the member states' own estimates, revised downwards. the proposed 6,8% increase compared to 2012 is therefore nothing more than a realistic indication of the resources needed to pay member states' bills and to honour all commitments made from 2007 to date. we cannot today think of jeopardizing the implementation of certain european programmes, as has happened in recent days, and i find it inconceivable that the council's reading and the statements of certain ministers should be based on figures which are clearly not sufficient to finance these projects. the european parliament has been a very active participant in the negotiations on the maastricht treaty. it is a pity that these words are not followed by concrete actions. i think it is no exaggeration to say that we are facing a problem of credibility and reliability of the european union. paying bills is a legal obligation which we cannot afford to ignore and it is not for parliament to explain this to the member states. i would like to conclude by recalling the passage of the resolution accompanying tomorrow's vote in which parliament gives its conciliation committee the mandate not to accept the level of payments, both for draft amending budget no 6 and for the 2013 budget, if it does not adequately cover the payment needs for 2012 and 2013 as estimated by the commission.
member of the commission. − mr president, the commission is submitting what is called the ‘draft budget’ as a basis for reading here in parliament and in the council. this is not our invention. to a large extent we are taking as a basis and verifying very critically what comes from 27 member states, both net payers into and net beneficiaries of the budget. i think jan mulder has posed the right question: what if we take at face value what is coming from the member states for next year? if we took at face value – without downward revision – what was coming from the 27 member states for next year, we should submit a draft budget which was 15 % higher for next year and not 6, 7 or 8 % higher, because we have critically revised what is coming from the member states. it would be more or less eur 10 billion more in the draft proposal. mr van dalen – who is no longer here – was asking on what planet our proposal was born. the planet is populated by the governments in the hague, in stockholm, in warsaw, in sofia, everywhere, and we are critically revising what is coming from these governments as their request for decent financing for 2013. as for the payments – the most sensitive issue in negotiations for next year – you can compare these to your monthly credit card bills. when the bills come in, it is too late to discuss them: you have to pay the bills, it is your contractual obligation to pay. that is why, especially now – at a time of austerity – we need to supplement the consolidation of public finances with a realistic growth and jobs agenda, as we have the tools in the budget, which is by nature an investment budget. however – and here it differs from national budgets – it also has macro-financing facilities for small- and medium-sized companies. therefore we should exploit all the possibilities of the european budget rather than cut it, in clear contradiction of the announcements by the member states in june 2013. i still remain hopeful for a decent budget for next year which will resolve the tensions of this year’s budget.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i have noted with interest the various points raised during this debate and will inform my colleagues in the council accordingly. i know that one should never shoot the messenger. at the same time, as president of the council and the personification of the institution i represent, i have to defend the position of the institution i represent, and i have to take some hits. all your comments, criticism and disagreements are welcome. however, i would like to make a small clarification concerning the way the council’s position on the 2013 budget was interpreted. the council has indeed scaled back the commission’s proposal, but it has accepted a 2.79 % increase on the current year. that is definitely not a decrease. the council has not made horizontal cuts across the board. we have established priorities, as suggested by mr torvalds, and we have examined every heading, policy and institution carefully and individually. we do not intend to let the union run out of money. for instance, we have kept the over eight percent increase for cohesion funding, as well as the full eur 55 billion for the european council’s growth and jobs pact referred to by mr lamassoure. this debate has certainly contributed to clarifying our respective positions. let me assure you that the council will do its utmost to find an agreement on the 2013 budget within the deadlines foreseen by the treaty. thank you very much for your attention. i hope i can count on your constructive cooperation in order to finalise the important task we have in front of us.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you for this debate and for the useful speeches by the president-in-office of the council and the commissioner. i think it is clear from most of the speeches by our colleagues in parliament that this parliament intends to defend the union's budget as proposed by the commission, because we are firmly convinced that the needs to get out of the crisis are found in certain headings and in certain policies of the european union: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. that is why we have proposed selective increases in heading 1a and if president mavroyiannis criticised the breaking of the ceiling, he must take account of the fact that, under the same heading, we have made cuts and made considerable savings, although we must also provide, under the same heading, eur 360 million for additional funding for iter, which the council had granted and planned for the current year with all the instruments available, including, of course, flexibility. on the other hand, i would like to point out that in terms of commitments parliament has not departed from the commission's proposals and has only made selective increases, whereas in terms of payments we have adjusted to the actual needs for payment. as president lamassoure said, it is a technical matter, not a political one. we must honour the commitments made, including by the council, in previous years. i hope therefore that during the conciliation process an agreement can be reached with the council on a satisfactory level of resources, which will ensure that the european budget is endowed with the sums needed to invest in growth and development, create new jobs and with a level of payments sufficient to honour all the commitments made.
in writing. i welcome the spirit of the draft report in question, which, rejecting the logic of cuts adopted by the european council, puts at the centre the idea of a european budget 2013 with a view to supporting growth and employment. i believe that the way out of the crisis is certainly a policy of austerity, but it is also necessary to put the question of the quality of spending at the centre of the choices, without this resulting in indiscriminate cuts which can only inhibit the already timid signs of economic recovery in europe. as the rapporteur has pointed out, 2013 is the last year of the current multiannual financial framework and it is essential that the balance between commitments and payments is maintained. in this context, i am concerned about the figures presented by the european commissioner for the budget, mr janusz lewandowski, concerning the deficits affecting all the headings of the european budget and, in particular, the cuts to the erasmus project. i am well aware that the general political guidelines on the 2013 budget largely reflect those on the negotiation of the next programming cycle 2014-2020, and i stress the importance of continuity over time in supporting investment in the training of our young people.
