mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president of the commission, even though i think things are going better, the impression after this council is that the principle of the 'penelope curtain' is valid if you have actually had to go back twice on things you thought you had already acquired. so i ask you, with regard to the single supervisory mechanism, which is certainly a good compromise, what does the commission intend to do to put pressure on the member states which are pushing for its postponement? what is being done to get them to settle down in more reasonable positions? in fact, time is also money, as has been repeatedly pointed out by authoritative officials in various countries. and while there may be the problem of those countries asking for more time, there does not seem to be much consideration given to the fact that decisions are postponed indefinitely and that these decisions are pursued with determination. i believe that the council's results should be welcomed, but at the same time we must put all the weight we can on them so that they are effective immediately.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president, a common currency requires a true economic union: the european union is not a system of rules and discipline but an economic government, based on democratic institutions and adequate resources. the european parliament therefore insists that there are no effective and legitimate solutions which are not based on the community method and the institutions of the union and that the european parliament is the parliament of the euro because the euro is the currency of the union. it is good that the european council's conclusions recall these principles, but they must be consistently and concretely rejected. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the union's budget is not used as a vehicle for the creation of new jobs. we are against individual contracts: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of the lack of democracy in the community. parliament proposes a different model: binding general economic and social objectives defined in co-decision at eu level; the european parliament has a duty to ensure that the european union is able to take action to achieve these objectives. this approach suggests a more ambitious and realistic vision of a europe in which stability, growth, social cohesion and democracy go hand in hand. this calls for a fifth social pillar and a federal transition aimed at building public consensus on the basis of a clear road map: 1) to correct the line of austerity and the intergovernmental method by rapid decisions that make the most of the possibilities offered by the treaties and give priority to growth and employment; 2) make the next european elections an election for the eu government; finally, to convene a convention to complete the building of a genuine democratic government for europe and its currency. parliament calls on you to act, and parliament will exercise its prerogatives to the full.
mr president, in the many e-mails you sent us inviting us to be present for this photograph, you explained that it would be used to welcome visitors to parliament and would therefore be used by the services. it is very good that president barroso and president van rompuy will also be in this picture, and that their presence in this picture will be a testimony to all those who come to brussels to the unity of action and intention of the european institutions.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as every year, due to the complexity of the procedure, there are some technical adjustments to be voted on. first, the general reference to be taken into account for the figures is the so-called "doc 6". in the case of multiple amendments, the vote shall be taken on all the lines to which they relate. secondly, there are some corrections to the pilot projects and preparatory actions which we will have to vote on. the pilot project 'development of indicators to measure the implementation of the european charter for equality between women and men in local life' is adopted under heading 3a and not under heading 1a. the preparatory action 'consumption of fruit and vegetables' is adopted under heading 2 and not under 3b. the pilot project 'promoting self-care health systems in the european union' has €1,000,000 in payments instead of €100,000. preparatory action 'climate mainstreaming and innovation' is reduced by 2 million compared to the db (both in commitments and payments). the preparatory action 'european voluntary humanitarian aid corps' is reduced by 1 million compared to the pb (both in commitments and payments). i should also point out that parliament's position does not take into account letter of amendment no 1/2013 adopted by the commission on 19 october, which will be supplemented during the conciliation. i would like to conclude by calling for a vote: parliament's unity and cohesion are more important than ever for the 2013 budget. we are facing a difficult and difficult conciliation with the council, which seems unwilling to make the necessary resources available. i therefore ask you to vote strongly, to show that parliament is united and to fight this battle together.
the rapporteur. mr president, i would like to emphasize very briefly that today we are adopting a new regulation which is more modern, simpler in terms of the way the funds are managed and with more effective rules to deal with and overcome the challenges of the current crisis. thank you, everybody.
mr president, the policy of austerity adopted to get out of the economic crisis has not produced the desired results. as mr la via's report has pointed out, it is only by investing more selectively and by supporting the ideal of a european budget to support growth and employment that the economies of the member states can be rebalanced. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the situation of european citizens. that is why i voted in favour.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank my colleagues la via and vaughan for the excellent work they have done on the 2013 budget; i would like to stress in particular the commitment of the european parliament to the erasmus programme: since 1987, more than 2.5 million european students have been involved in an opportunity to go abroad to study and work. we voted against the council's cuts and asked for some 30 million more than the commission's proposal. we must not only save erasmus, but we must also implement it and, more generally, we must propose a european strategy for young people, because young people cannot afford the costs of the crisis, especially at a time when youth unemployment is close to 25% in europe.
mr president, i would like to congratulate mr la via on the excellent work he has done in his report on the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013. the task facing my colleague was a difficult one, since agreement between the member states and the european parliament seemed distant and difficult to achieve. despite the protracted crisis and the continuing calls for cuts in eu spending, mr la via and mr vaughan have managed to ensure continuity in the policies and initiatives under way. i think it is particularly important that we have avoided a slowdown in the pilot initiatives on the environment and energy, a clear sign of the good work done by the european parliament in defending the prerogatives of the european union. that is why i have given my full support to this report.
mr president, the social and economic context in which the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 is being discussed is rather problematic. with member states committed to making fiscal adjustments to their national budgets to balance public finances, the european union is sometimes seen as adding to the financial burden on taxpayers. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the european social fund is based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in times of crisis, when member states are calling for a reduction in community aid, we must spend the funds available better, by allocating them to the real priorities: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the british rebate, which has so far amounted to some 97 billion euros, is unacceptable in my view. my country, italy, can no longer afford the luxury of being a net contributor and of paying out more than it receives, especially in order to finance these anachronistic rebates. in 2011 alone, italy had a negative balance of almost eur 6 billion. i would like to conclude, on the subject of cutting waste, by saying that today the european parliament has sent a clear message to get to a single seat quickly.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by reminding you that the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 are taking place in a very difficult social, economic and financial context. i regret to say that the union is increasingly seen by citizens as an entity which adds to the financial burden on taxpayers rather than as a valuable resource. i am convinced that this situation is caused by the fact that the budget of the european union is in contradiction with national budgets, since it has not been extended in relation to the scope of the tasks and competences conferred on the union by the treaty of lisbon, but also in relation to the important political decisions taken by the european council itself. i voted in favour of the report because i am aware of the need for an interinstitutional compromise and a clear signal to the citizens.

in writing. − at the sitting on 2 july 2012, the president announced, pursuant to rule 6 (2) of parliament's rules of procedure, that he had received a request from the vienna public prosecutor's office on 21 march 2012 to waive the parliamentary immunity of martin ehrenhauser in the context of pending proceedings against him, and referred this request to the committee on legal affairs. martin ehrenhauser was heard by that committee on 17 september 2012. considering the alleged actions for which the vienna prosecutor's office intends to bring proceedings against martin ehrenhauser, it is clear that these are not opinions or votes expressed by the member in the exercise of his functions under article 8 of the protocol on privileges and immunities. in line with the conclusion of the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights that the parliamentary immunity of martin ehrenhauser should be waived, i am voting in favour of the motion.
in writing. the vienna prosecutor's office intends to bring proceedings against martin ehrenhauser, a member of the european parliament. martin ehrenhauser is suspected of improper access to a computer system under paragraph 118a of the austrian criminal code, of breach of telecommunications secrecy under paragraph 119 of the code, of unlawful acquisition of data under paragraph 119a of the code, of unlawful use of a recording or interception device under paragraph 120 (2) of the code, and of breach of paragraph 51 of the data protection act 2000. furthermore, it is suspected that martin ehrenhauser made available a recording of an unofficial statement made by a person without his consent to a third party for whom it was not intended, by sending the recording of a conversation between several persons, including hans-peter martin, to one of the persons involved, who in turn would have forwarded it to the vienna public prosecutor's office. therefore, in view of the gravity of the facts, this vote in favour calls for the waiver of the immunity of the austrian member of parliament.

in writing. - all european countries are pursuing austerity policies, sometimes very harsh: it is not acceptable for europe to continue to look the other way, ignoring the serious situation that is affecting us all. the result achieved seems to me to be an acceptable compromise, in which the commitments are not overstated, but rather the focus is on payments: it would be nice to promise money and funding for everyone, but in the end the reckoning has to be made and we risk finding ourselves each year with dozens of cases like the one that recently concerned the erasmus programme. i am very pleased that the 2013 budget makes a clear and explicit reference to the need for a single seat for the european parliament, a battle that i myself started in february by collecting the necessary signatures to present an amendment that goes in this direction: it is not a question of demagogy or populism, but of acknowledging a reality which is absolutely unsustainable. the same can be said for the project of the "house of european history": i am glad that the appropriations have been reduced, although i think the whole project should be stopped and reviewed.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is intended to establish parliament's position on the draft budget of the european union for 2013. in addition, the budget for the distribution of food aid to the most deprived is maintained and funds are provided for competitiveness and innovation, in particular for erasmus mundus and to support lifelong learning. i voted against the paragraphs opposing the retention of the seat of the european parliament in strasbourg.
in writing. the house of european history, which is being built in brussels, a few steps from the european parliament, is an idea which would have been my absolute favourite in other times. the disproportionate increase in the costs of the work in progress and the recent opening of the new multimedia visitor centre 'parlamentarium' have led me today to accept amendments nos 16 and 26 calling for the freezing of funds for the 'house of european history' until the project itself is abolished.
in writing. − considering that the current economic climate in many member states is characterised by national austerity, weak growth, recession and lack of international competitiveness, parliament must act responsibly by approving the 2013 budget with a clear vision of how the budget can be used to boost growth and competitiveness within the european union. moreover, bearing in mind that many member states, after years of growth characterised by unsustainable public sector spending, are making extraordinary efforts to reduce national debt and deficits, eu public spending should be subject to the same discipline as member states. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal, stressing that parliament must provide the council with a draft budget which increases expenditure where it is important and cuts where it is not.
in writing. - the european parliament has decided to restore the commission's draft budget and to increase resources selectively in certain budget chapters closely linked to growth policies and job creation, especially for our young people. however, as regards payments, i note that the level set by the commission in the draft budget was determined on the basis of the member states' own estimates, revised downwards. we cannot today think of jeopardizing the implementation of certain european programmes. i think it is no exaggeration to say that we are facing a problem of credibility and reliability of the european union. paying bills is a legal obligation which we cannot afford to ignore and it is not for parliament to explain this to the member states. i therefore hope that during the conciliation process an agreement can be reached with the council on a satisfactory level of resources, which will ensure that the european budget is endowed with the necessary resources to invest in growth and development, create new jobs, and with a level of payments sufficient to honour all the commitments made in recent years.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal by mr böge and mr kalfin on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. this is the second time that parliament has spoken on this subject, after the report of the sure special committee, but we have decided to speak again as the negotiations are now about to enter a decisive phase, which will see a european council at the end of november devoted specifically to the discussion of this sensitive subject. as you know, the commission's proposal represents a kind of freezing of expenditure at the level of the previous mff and is therefore not a sufficient proposal for us to adequately meet the global challenges that lie ahead in the coming years. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them. we therefore considered amending the proposals which aimed to eliminate the differences in direct payments between member states, introducing instead a generic wording of reduction.
in writing. − the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 are not finding fertile ground in an economic and financial environment in which member states are forced to make tough fiscal consolidation moves. however, it is impossible not to recognise the union budget as a huge added value to the investments made at national level. the commission proposal, however, represents a freeze of ceilings at the 2013 level and significantly weakens the calls made by the sure committee to increase community policies aimed at competitiveness, small and medium-sized enterprises and sustainable infrastructure. parliament wants a 'responsible' reaction from the council. any attempt to reduce the ceilings proposed by the commission would result in a loss not only of effectiveness but also of credibility of the union budget.
in writing. − the contraction of the eu budget compared to national budgets is in flagrant contradiction with the extension of the tasks and competences conferred on the union by the treaty and with the important political decisions taken by the european council itself, notably the development of strengthened european economic governance. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i voted against amendment no 23, which denied the usefulness of decentralised european agencies. on what basis can we say that the food safety agency in parma, for example, is useless, since it was the first to sound the alarm immediately when 'blue mozzarella' from a german producer was discovered?
in writing. - i congratulate mr kalfin and mr böge on their work. by approving this document today, parliament, in the light of articles 311 and 312 tfeu and in the light of its resolution of 13 june 2012 on the multiannual financial framework and own resources, has taken a strong stand in pointing the way to growth and competitiveness in europe. in particular, it underlines the need for well-targeted, robust and appropriate support from member states to the eu budget, all in order to help coordinate and strengthen national efforts. the commission is therefore expressly calling for a significant increase in funding from the community budget to boost competitiveness, the development of small businesses, entrepreneurship, sustainable infrastructure, research and innovation. this increase, together with a reprogramming of own resources, will help the eu to cope with and overcome the crisis in the member states.
in writing. − it is necessary to insist that the eu budget prioritise helping member states to cope with the strains of the difficult economic and financial environment. we need concerted action to tackle the current challenges of loss of competitiveness and rising unemployment and poverty. with particular regard to italy, it is necessary to emphasise its role as one of the largest contributors to the eu budget. that is why i think it is necessary to ensure that the priority is to increase the impact of the funds on growth and employment. for the cap, the commission proposed a reduction, keeping its value in nominal terms stable compared to 2007-13. the largest reduction was in direct aids (from 322 to 281 billion (-12%). the commission is seeking to introduce greater equity in the distribution of aid (for which a system of convergence of all countries towards the community average of support per hectare is provided for). i cannot agree with the general approach of the proposal for the allocation of direct aid from the cap, which is exclusively linked to the quantitative criterion of agricultural area, contrary to the objective of growth and increased employment. i hope that my vote in favour will not lead to a reduction in the cap, which could make it too burdensome.
in writing. - we have already seen how the economic crisis has helped to accelerate the process of european integration; the report by mr dehaene, which i support, touches on a fundamental element of the construction of europe, namely its financing through fiscal autonomy and responsibility. i have no doubt that the system of collection by the national states is conceptually outdated, in the face of forms of integration driven by taxation, regulation and general policies. such an asymmetry denounces an anachronism, which the report proposes to overcome by an effective synthesis. in particular, the benefits in terms of transparency and lower costs for the member states will be able to compensate for the apparent additional loss of sovereignty linked to the exercise of activities which are in fact statistical and no longer managerial. in this sense, the transfer of more burdens to the commission appears justified. the report's predictions, if adopted, will help to develop a widespread european consciousness as a community of destiny, which will allow many of the issues currently under intense debate on sovereignty and governance to be shelved.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. the proposal for a new vat own resource at eu level is undoubtedly a major improvement on the current system and offers real prospects for future transformation into a genuine, stable and reliable own resource for the union budget.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the value added tax own resource because in a system of the internal market regulated by the european union it is functional that vat is paid and managed by the european union and not by the member states.
in writing. − the proposal for decision vii on own resources (drp) which involves abolishing the current vat own resource and replacing it with a new eu-wide vat resource would be a major improvement over the current system, with concrete possibilities for the future transformation of vat into a genuine, stable and reliable own resource for the union budget. given the considerable simplification of the calculation of vat, the reduced administrative burden, the equal treatment of all member states, and the wish that the vat own resource can be part of a general reform of the own resources system, which should considerably reduce the overall level of national contributions of the member states, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i congratulate mr dehaene on his work. in view of its resolution of 8 june 2011 entitled 'investing in the future: a new multiannual financial framework (mff) for a competitive, sustainable and inclusive europe' and article 311 tfeu, parliament today approved a proposal for a regulation which, supporting what has already been proposed by the commission, welcomes the abolition of the current vat own resources and the creation of a new vat own resource at eu level. in particular, it was stressed that a new key criterion for a genuine vat own resource should be that it be paid directly to the eu budget, thus eliminating the pass through of national administrations. this proposal is addressed to the commission if not for the period 2014-2020, at least for the next one, when the own resources system should be reformed so as to achieve full financing of the eu budget from own resources.
in writing. - the agreement on vat reform is necessary to define the method by which member states are to calculate this new resource and also the procedures for its transfer to the eu budget. i believe that a new vat own resource at eu level could be an improvement on the current system by being able to become a reliable own resource contributing to the eu budget. the vat own resource transfers to the european commission the bulk of the burden of the calculations currently carried out by the member states, with a consequent reduction in the overall level of the member states' national contributions. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal to abolish the current vat own resources and to create a new vat own resource at eu level.
in writing. − the financial regulation marks an important step towards simplifying the way the eu budget funds are managed. the set of rules (which, i recall, includes over 500 amendments negotiated with the council for almost a year) will enable us to have, as from 1 january 2013, new legal and operational instruments which will be more effective and efficient in order to face the challenges of an economic and political crisis. the new provisions are numerous, and one of them is the new title viii, which is entirely devoted to new financial instruments co-financed by the total budget of the union to promote new revenue to support community policies at this particular moment of crisis. new and simpler rules in shared management, namely those between the commission and the member states, provide for new control bodies, which will provide declarations certifying that appropriations have been spent for the intended purpose or the suspension of appropriations. new and simpler rules for the establishment and management of public-private partnerships (ppps), particularly in the fields of research and industry.
in writing. - i believe that europe, through its budgetary policies, can provide a viable solution to the crisis and that, through the right choice of priorities, starting with the growth and innovation policies of europe's rural areas, it can give a strong signal of change. i believe that it is within the european institutions, even before at local level, that the economic power of producers in the production chain must be strengthened through positive results of the budgetary procedures. negotiation with the council will lead to a proper implementation of the european programmes in terms of maintaining a strong common agricultural policy through a constant agricultural budget. by setting an effective framework for reforms in this sector, the rest of the economy can be strengthened. growth, at the heart of parliament's agenda, will be pursued through a cycle of funding aimed at pursuing long-term objectives, starting with strengthening the competitiveness of european agricultural enterprises on the world stage. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the acaa is a very good agreement in itself: it is a matter of simplification, which i certainly hope for, but to think that this is a technical agreement seems naive to me, or perhaps we are being ill-intentioned. there is a very long list of demands on the israeli authorities from the european union, from the high representative, from our consuls in east jerusalem and from this parliament on the west bank settlements, the continued annexation of east jerusalem, the situation in gaza and the resumption of the peace process. if we look at what we have achieved as the european union with these demands, we see no real progress and no serious concessions. for this reason i think this is anything but a politically neutral measure. my delegation will vote against the acaa and i ask the commission, if the acaa is approved, for the highest degree of surveillance, both for the traceability of the products of the colonies, which is a problem, which does not concern the good faith of the commission but israel, and for the extension to other products without the role of the european parliament.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, once again when we discuss relations between the european union and israel, our chamber is divided ideologically and passes a technical agreement over to the political confrontation, regardless of its content. this agreement is not an upgrade of relations between the european union and israel; it is not a text of international law that delimits borders and defines sovereign rights. the legal services of parliament and the commission support this, stressing that the acaa with israel does not go beyond the existing legal framework. it is a technical agreement which will make it easier for many european citizens to have access to high quality medicines at low cost, with considerable savings for our national health services. italy will save about 1 billion euros a year, which is not a small amount in this difficult economic situation. it is for these reasons that i think this agreement should be approved.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 2013 will rightly be the year of the european citizens. it is an important initiative because it is of the utmost importance to remember, reaffirm and disseminate, particularly among young people, the rights and gains they enjoy as a result of being a european citizen. today, thanks to the process of european integration, citizens of the union in the territory of other member states can live, work, study and travel without restrictions, have access to health care, enjoy rights and protections as passengers, as consumers and can also vote and be elected in elections to the european parliament and in municipal elections in the member state in which they reside. these are important achievements, which not only have a strong symbolic significance in strengthening and promoting the sense of belonging to europe, but also bring undisputed practical benefits and opportunities. yet, as the eurobarometer survey has confirmed and as i see daily in my work as a member of parliament, there is often a lack of awareness of these rights and the values and principles that inspire them. it is therefore important to spread and publicize as much as possible, particularly in schools but not only, the great wealth of our dual citizenship, the european one which complements and strengthens the national one.
mr president, the lack of information and awareness of their rights, together with language barriers and the non-recognition of diplomas and qualifications, are the most common problems encountered by union citizens when they live, study or work in another country of the european union. unfortunately, there is still a lack of visibility of the concept of union citizenship and its concrete benefits. that is why i have expressed my support for 2013 as the european year of citizens. the primary objective is to raise awareness of the rights attaching to citizenship of the union and to help citizens to exercise fully their right to move and reside freely within the territories of the member states.
mr president, almost 20 years after the legal definition of the concept of european citizenship, only 43% of union citizens consider the term 'european union citizen' to be familiar. they lack information, they lack awareness of their rights: language barriers and the non-recognition of diplomas, degrees and qualifications are the issues that european citizens face on a daily basis. i therefore share the commission's initiative to dedicate 2013 to the citizens of the union. i also fully support the rapporteur's approach to extending the scope of the decision, focusing on raising awareness among citizens, on their rights as european citizens and not just on the issue of free movement. i also hope that this year's theme for 2013 will not once again be merely celebratory but will set the stage for the creation of a political framework for future measures and actions needed to consolidate citizenship of the union.
mr president, establishing a year of citizens is a way of putting the european union's half a billion people back at the centre. is to be able to think that all the other measures we are discussing these days - the banking union, the economic and financial measures to combat the crisis - must have the interest of the citizens as their first objective: the european year we have just voted on is aimed at strengthening the rights of citizenship, the role of associations in the union, and the mobility of students, teachers, artists and cultural workers. in short, it is the strengthening of european identity through the inclusion of concrete actions in which citizens are the main actors. it is a way of really building the union from the ground up, and that is why i voted in favour.
mr president, i voted in favour of the foster report which calls for the commission to take strong action, including sanctions, to induce member states to reduce their borders in european skies. the single european sky is an ambitious project to create a single airspace that will increase capacity and efficiency in air traffic management from a functional, economic and environmental point of view. the implementation of the sesar programme, the technological pillar of the single sky, is vital to the success of the single european sky, especially since 2015, when the programme is due to start. unfortunately, the shortcomings of the single sky remain numerous, particularly in the implementation of fabs, functional airspace blocks. in this respect, however, i welcome the renewed impetus given a few days ago by italy and the other countries concerned in the blue med fab, which has strategic value because it involves the countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean.
mr president, the protection of passengers' rights is becoming increasingly important, especially in times of crisis such as the present one, where cuts in transport costs and the sudden bankruptcy of companies in the sector can lead to serious inconveniences for travellers. all too often the newspapers report reports of flights being cancelled and hundreds of passengers left stranded for days on end. and that's not to mention train delays and cancellations, which leave thousands of workers, students and entire families stranded, often without any useful information about alternatives to getting back home or to their jobs. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. work must be done to ensure that multilingual information points are provided for changes in itineraries and reservations in the event of flight or train cancellations, in order to maximise the protection of union citizens.
mr president, passenger rights must be at the heart of the debate when we talk about transport. the concept of accessibility is the key point of this report. accessibility for all in terms of physical, destination and information. it is necessary to be able to provide correct information to users, using different methods and taking into account different needs. in addition, passengers must be able to access assistance services through a helpdesk staffed by trained and competent staff. finally, we are calling again for the revision of the package travel directive, which provides a clearer and safer legal framework for consumers and businesses in both ordinary and extraordinary situations, avoiding abuses and unfair practices and ensuring greater transparency. mr bach's report covers all these aspects and for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour.
mr president, it is indisputable that if the european union is to emerge from the crisis, it must strengthen the competitiveness of european small and mediumsized enterprises, which are responsible for 85% of job creation. in view of this situation, which makes it necessary to harmonize national industrial policies more closely, i think it is equally essential to achieve another objective: the internationalisation of small and medium-sized enterprises. only 25% of smes operate across borders within the european union. i therefore agree with the commission's plans to promote the process of internationalisation and the rapporteur's need to provide specific information on the priority markets and details of the various support services available. i would like to conclude by stressing the need for greater coordination of the various initiatives at european union level. in a period of rationalisation of public spending, we cannot afford to duplicate efforts or policies, with the risk of generating unnecessary administrative and bureaucratic burdens.
mr president, i voted in favour of this resolution on trade and economic relations between the european union and the united states because it is an important, balanced and comprehensive report, for which i thank president moreira, and because it also gives us a comprehensive picture of the trade and economic prospects and the nodes and challenges of the meeting between the two major economies of the world, which account for 50% of output and a third of trade flows. after many years of stalemate, we are facing a possible turning point in our bilateral relations and the prospect of a possible broad-ranging agreement between europe and the united states could open up positive scenarios in transatlantic relations. of course there are the issues of tariff barriers and an agreement of this magnitude should also and above all have the ambition to eliminate the many trade and technical barriers which unfortunately still exist, as well as having to deal with important issues such as the protection of geographical indications, the opening up of the procurement market and the harmonization of rules of origin and of regulatory, sanitary and phytosanitary standards, which are still too different. but that does not diminish the importance of the acts we are about to undertake.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, since i think it is fully compatible with the report and does not raise any of the same issues.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs balzani on draft amending budget no 4/2012 to the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2012. the proposal aims to create four new budget lines, so as to reallocate resources, up to a maximum of 10% of the european regional development fund (erdf) and cohesion fund 2007-2013 allocations, to risk-sharing instruments. the rapporteur proposed to approve the council's position without amendments, but with particular attention to certain political considerations, such as that any transfer from cohesion policy to these financial instruments should be properly justified and carefully controlled, and that all relevant information should be transmitted to the european parliament in a timely manner.
in writing. − draft amending budget no 4/2012 to the general budget 2011 pursues a threefold objective, namely the creation of four budget lines to reallocate appropriations, up to a maximum of 10% of the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion fund 2007-2013, to risk-sharing instruments, the revision and budgeting of own resources forecasts, which involve a change in the distribution of their contributions to the eu budget by member states as own resources. whereas the above-mentioned draft is fully consistent with the amendments to the financial regulation agreed by the european parliament and the council; i am also hopeful that any shift from cohesion policy to the financial instruments to be defined will be duly justified and well controlled, and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - having regard to the final annual accounts of the european food safety authority for the financial year 2010, and to the annual report of the court of auditors, parliament approved the closure of the accounts of the european food safety authority for the financial year 2010, considering the discharge in this respect as a valuable instrument of the european parliament, which requires a decision based on factual and substantive arguments; recalling in this context the rules in force, namely the staff regulations of officials and the conditions of employment of other servants of the european communities, the financial regulation applicable to the european communities, the regulation establishing the authority and the specific policies and procedures within efsa; i am firmly convinced that the necessary action must be taken in the event of non-compliance with the rules in force, and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the pursuit of a high level of protection of human and animal health is one of efsa's key objectives. i welcome the efforts made by the food authority to resolve some of the criticisms that have been levelled at it: in particular the prevention and management of conflicts of interest. i acknowledge the commitment of efsa to ensure the integrity of its decision-making structure through ethics and transparency policies and actions to ensure compliance with the rules of the efsa code of conduct. i can only welcome the authority's decisions on its policy of independence and the actions it has taken to ensure the integrity of its members. the integrated approach to food safety adopted in the eu to combat foodborne zoonoses has been particularly significant. coordinated action has helped to tackle a serious and widespread public health threat, with over 320 000 confirmed cases in humans each year in the european union. for these reasons i am voting in favour of the report.
in writing. − according to the statement of the european food safety authority, appropriate measures have been taken to improve financial management. the main task of the authority is to provide independent and transparent scientific advice on matters with a direct or indirect impact on food and feed safety. it is therefore necessary to apply measures to safeguard the credibility of the authority, which should improve the accessibility and transparency of risk assessment procedures.
in writing. − having regard to the final annual accounts of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2010, and to the report of the court of auditors, parliament gives discharge to the executive director of the european medicines agency for the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2010. in this regard, considering the discharge as a valid instrument of the european parliament, which requires a decision based on factual and substantive arguments; firmly convinced that the necessary measures should be taken in the event of non-compliance with the rules in force; and considering that the discharge decision for the aem cannot be based on additional requirements, such as oecd guidelines, the application of which has not been formally requested by the community legislator, nor on specific provisions within the agency during the discharge procedure; i am voting in favour of the motion.
in writing. − the european medicines agency protects and promotes public and animal health by assessing and monitoring medicines for human and veterinary use. all medicinal products for human and animal use derived from biotechnologies and other advanced technological processes are to be approved by the centralised procedure. the same applies to all medicinal products for human use intended for the treatment of hiv/aids infections, cancer, diabetes or neurodegenerative diseases and to all 'orphan' medicinal products intended for the treatment of rare diseases. the agency also participates in referral procedures in relation to medicinal products approved or under examination by the member states. the closure of the accounts of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2010 is hereby approved.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. i agree that as regards materials in the 'qualified' category, these conditions should include the provision of information indicating whether or not the products have been genetically modified. such information should facilitate the application of the requirements of directive 2001/18/ec.
in writing. - having regard to the proposal from the commission to the european parliament and the council, after consulting the european economic and social committee, having regard to the report of the committee on agriculture and rural development and to parliament's request that the commission should re-submit its proposal, should the commission intend to substantially amend it or replace it with a new text, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i expressed my support for the text tabled by mr de castro, who proposed adopting the commission proposal on the inclusion of forest reproductive material in the 'qualified' category and the updating of the names of the authorities responsible for the recognition and control of production by a simplified procedure.
in writing. − the maastricht treaty established citizenship of the union with the aim of strengthening and enhancing european identity and enabling european citizens to participate actively in the process of community integration. when we speak of european citizenship, we are not talking about the legal status of the citizen, but about all aspects of life in a democratic society. the european union is the sum of all those countries that work together to improve the lives of their citizens. we have a duty to help them to exercise their rights fully: the right to education, to work, to freedom of enterprise, removing all the often bureaucratic obstacles that create barriers and impediments. and we must increasingly strengthen the participation of citizens in the european decision-making process, first by making the most of the right of petition and, above all, the right of popular legislative initiative introduced by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − the overall objective of the commission's proposal for a 'european year of citizens' is to raise awareness of the rights attached to union citizenship, with a view to helping citizens to exercise fully their right to move freely within the territory of the member states. this proposal, in my view, gives new impetus to the debate on citizenship of the union and puts the effective and conscious exercise of this right at the centre of the political agenda. today there is still a lack of visibility of the notion of citizenship of the union and its concrete benefits for european citizens. a eurobarometer study published in 2011 shows that lack of information and awareness of their rights, as well as language barriers and the non-recognition of diplomas and qualifications, are the most common problems faced by citizens when they live, study or work in another eu country. these problems are aggravated in the current period of economic and financial crisis by the negative impact of the crisis, including the increase in unemployment and social tensions. in this context, i believe that the european year of citizens is a valuable opportunity to raise citizens' awareness of union citizenship and to stimulate their participation in democratic life.
in writing. - the reports of eurobarometer and other research institutes are full of bitter surprises on the subject of the idea of union among european citizens. it is clear that the economic crisis has put the fundamental reasons for being together and the benefits that derive from it under pressure, to the benefit of negative underlining, sometimes used for internal political-electoral polemics. the report makes a proposal which, at this historic moment, is particularly important. it is not a question of prefiguring themes in the dom porfirio, in a revised edition for the 21st century, but of spreading a minimum awareness of the values and positive effects of european citizenship, also on the practical level and the opportunities, in the face of a continuous emphasis on the inadequacies of the european construction, real or presumed. we cannot let our young people's european citizenship be reduced to passport lines at non-eu airports: the european union is a major player in the world economy, and its role in the world economy is increasingly being recognized. i therefore welcome the report, including the detailed recommendations on the organisation and coordination of activities for the european year of citizens.
in writing. - next year marks the 20th anniversary of the birth of european citizenship. it is essential to put union citizenship and participatory democracy at the centre of the political agenda. it is more necessary than ever now, in a period of deep crisis which is putting european households, businesses and citizens to the test. today's vote confirmed the agreement to proclaim 2013 the european year of citizens, with the aim of raising awareness of the rights linked to european citizenship. eu citizens are often unaware of their rights, including the right to move and live freely in another member state, the right to vote and stand as a candidate in european and local elections, and the right to petition the european parliament. i hope that these measures to inform and involve the public will be put into effect.
in writing. - i support with my vote in favour the proposal of the commission for civil liberties, justice and home affairs to establish 2013 as the 'year of european citizens'. i believe, in fact, that as laid down in the maastricht and lisbon treaties, it is of fundamental importance to make citizens of the european union aware of their rights and guarantees. the european year aims to strengthen the active civic and democratic participation of the citizens of the union. as vice-president of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, i support this proposal because i hope that it will not only strengthen equality and solidarity between member states, but also strengthen gender equality between citizens and increase the participation of women in the economic, political and social life of the european union. i also consider this decision to be of great importance for an increase in the mobility of workers and the resulting employment rate.
in writing. - i agree with the proposal for a european year of citizens. it would be a great opportunity to raise awareness among the general public of the rights and responsibilities associated with union citizenship. it would also make an important contribution to raising citizens' awareness of their rights as citizens of the union.
in writing. − every citizen of a member state, in addition to national prerogatives, also enjoys a set of rights guaranteed by the eu treaties and the eu charter of fundamental rights; however, many of them are unaware of the rights they enjoy as community citizens. considering that the overall aim of the proposed european year is to raise awareness of the rights attached to union citizenship in order to help citizens to exercise fully their right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states, and wishing that the european year of citizenship should not once again be celebratory in nature but should pave the way for the new 'europe for citizens' programme 2014-2020 which supports initiatives to raise citizens' awareness of the european union, its history and its values, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the proclamation of 2013 as the european year of citizens is a clear attempt to raise awareness of the rights linked to european citizenship. the european parliament has already adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia. in the meantime, citizens of the union have acquired a number of fundamental rights, such as the freedom to move and live in another member state, to vote actively and passively in european elections and to petition the european parliament. in a time of economic, political and social crisis, it is absolutely essential to put union citizenship and participatory democracy at the centre of the political agenda.
in writing. − 2013 will be the european year of the citizen. on the occasion of the 20th anniversary of european citizenship, established by the maastricht treaty, i consider this a new moment to increase the degree of involvement of the citizens of the individual member states in the process of european integration. i believe that too often the citizens of my constituency, like those of other member states, are not aware of the rights and opportunities which belonging to the community gives them. the european union has achieved many important objectives in the field of protection of rights, health and freedom of movement in the member states, but i believe that it is still possible to improve the impact of europe on the daily lives of citizens. that is why, in order to promote a new phase of european citizenship through the effective exercise of the rights related to it, i voted in favour of the commission's proposal to proclaim 2013 the european year of citizens.
in writing. − i voted against this report because, although i totally support the necessity to ask for a further investigation on the magnistsky case and to reiterate, once again, the rejection of any violation of human rights, i believe that an order of visa restriction for people not condemned by a tribunal would be a clear act of inconsistency with our own legal standards. in fact, if on the one hand we ask russia to respect the basic principle of human rights, on the other hand we are violating the principle of presumption of innocence. in addition, i deem that the quest of making family members accountable for actions they have not done contradicts one of the basic principles of the rule of law.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. we must by all means call on russia to conduct a credible and independent investigation into all aspects of this tragic case, and to bring all those responsible to justice. the magnitsky case is also an opportunity to urge the russian authorities to end endemic corruption and to reform the judicial system to bring it into line with international standards by creating an independent system.
in writing. − whereas the arrest, detention conditions and subsequent death in custody of sergei magnitsky represent a well-documented and concrete case of violation of fundamental human rights; bearing in mind that the post-mortem prosecution of sergei magnitsky is a violation of international and domestic law and a clear expression of the malfunctioning of the russian criminal justice system; i am therefore in favour of the proposal, since it is a very important one, and i hope that the council will take a consistent and proactive stance on other serious cases of human rights violations in russia, based on well-documented, convergent and independent sources and convincing evidence, and introduce similar restrictive measures against those responsible.
in writing. − the russian federation, as a member of the council of europe and the osce, has committed itself to full respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law, and on several occasions the european union has additionally offered its assistance and expertise to help the country modernise and respect its constitutional and legal order. despite the 2011 findings of the human rights council's investigation of the russian president regarding the illegality of sergei magnitsky's arrest and detention and the fact that he was denied access to justice, the investigations are stalled and the officers involved have been exonerated and even given the case posthumously. by these acts the authorities demonstrate the political character of the prosecution of sergei magnitsky. the vote therefore calls for common visa restrictions to be applied to the russian officials involved in the case.
in writing. − in recent years, air traffic has rapidly reached its maximum capacity and, with reasonable certainty, the problem will continue to worsen over time. the basic processes of air traffic control have changed little since world war ii: the controllers continue to communicate instructions to the pilots by voice radio communication. the implementation of the single european sky legislation, by offering the possibility of a shift to a more modern industry, would enable air traffic controllers to contribute to a more flexible, robust and innovative sector. although much progress has been made in making the ess legislation operational, i am concerned about the timing of its implementation. the benefits of full and timely implementation of the ess are not negligible: a study on its macroeconomic impact shows a cumulative effect on the union's gdp of eur 419 billion, the creation of as many as 328 000 jobs and a reduction in co2 emissions of 50 million tonnes. the urgency of making european airspace as efficient as possible is therefore clear. i share the rapporteur's request that the european commission report to parliament on progress in implementing the ess legislation by a predetermined date.
in writing. − despite the fallout from the economic crisis, the growth trend in air transport demand also remained positive at european level, with rates of 9.3% in 2011 to 4% for 2012, just below the 5% average gradient identified by iata as a baseline. the fact remains that, including the asia-pacific economies, the increase in global demand exceeds 6% in the passenger sector and 5% in logistics. however, the impact of the crisis has not been negligible, as indicated by the association of european airlines, whose secretary ulriche schulte-strathaus predicted in a recent interview a loss of over two billion for the entire sector. this combination of rising demand and shrinking operating margins makes the implementation of the single sky legislation imperative, especially as corrections and restructuring (e.g. on the trends in supply towards elfa carriers) are indispensable. it is incredible, for example, that european carriers still have to operate on a pattern essentially of pre-union national economies. i therefore support the report with a favourable vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the foster report because it provides us with a timely analysis of the limits of a policy which was launched ten years ago but which, as we must now see, is not working. the single european sky, which was the aim when the legislation was drawn up, and which envisaged air traffic with greater capacity and lower costs in both economic and environmental terms, has not yet been achieved. i therefore share the rapporteur's approach, which identifies the need for the european commission to intervene, giving precise reasons for the limitations in place. among the various elements that are functional to the realization of the one sky, we note: the performance system, functional airspace blocks (fabs), the role of the network operator and, above all, the implementation of the sesar programme, the technological pillar of the single sky, which will end its research phase in 2015 and which will have to be introduced on the market in ground and on-board components over the next 15 years, also with the support of european funding, in order to contribute to increasing the benefits for passengers (above all, reducing waiting times and delays) and to reducing co2 emissions and costs related to flight operations.
in writing. - in the belief that we must prevent any further delay in achieving the objectives set by the single european sky project, i express my support for this report. it is very clear what benefits the implementation of this project would bring to the union's gdp, to the competitiveness of european industry and to job creation. fundamental to ending the current malfunctioning of airspace and maintaining the eu's leadership in research and innovation, the implementation of the single european sky would nevertheless fully respect the sovereignty of member states with regard to military aircraft or other state aircraft. for all these reasons, my vote was in favour.
in writing. − the most effective way to establish the single european sky is to follow a top-down approach and therefore to ask the commission to propose measures to eliminate the effects of the delay in the implementation of functional airspace blocks and to move quickly from the bottom-up approach to the opposite.
in writing. - i would like to express my support for the rapid implementation of the single european sky. air traffic is growing by leaps and bounds, and so are air fares, to the detriment of passengers, safety and efficiency. today, the highways of the sky are not straight because of the fragmentation of airspace, which causes longer travel times, resulting in higher co2 emissions and more expensive airfares. the national air traffic control areas in europe urgently need to be unified precisely to avoid congestion, increase safety, reduce flight times, delays and fares. moreover, the full and timely implementation of air traffic management research technology would lead to the creation of as many as 328 000 new jobs.
in writing. − although many positive steps have already been taken in the right direction, much remains to be done and 2012 is seen as a pivotal year for the implementation of the ess. considering that air traffic is rapidly reaching its maximum capacity and that the problem continues to worsen over time, it is necessary to implement the ses legislation effectively in order to avoid possible safety or operational risks due to increasingly heavy traffic flows and outdated technologies. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the environment, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs foster on her work. in adopting this text, parliament, having regard to the report of the committee on transport and tourism and the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs, has shown its firm determination to implement a genuine single european sky as soon as possible. the aim is to make the most efficient use of airspace and the technology of our time for traffic management, and above all to ensure that the consumer is not harmed in terms of time and money. it should also be noted that the commission considers that full and timely implementation of air traffic management technologies would bring major benefits in terms of employment, the environment and timing of flights. the commission was therefore invited to adopt a new approach which would include both sanctions and, where necessary, eu funding.
in writing. − the national air traffic control areas in europe need to be unified immediately: this is the only way to avoid congestion, increase safety and reduce flight times, delays and fares. the european commission must act immediately to ensure that national governments fulfil their obligations and seize the opportunity to create 328 000 jobs through the proper use of air traffic management research technology alone.
in writing. − the european union is the most congested area by air travel, both because of its economic importance and because of the number of states, even small ones, that make up the union. the single european sky project, whose objectives were set in 2004, was to give the aviation decision-making powers normally held by the member states within the community. the aim was to reduce the fragmentation of airspace caused by being regulated on the basis of national borders rather than traffic requirements. the forecast that such a choice would be made by 2012 could unfortunately be optimistic and the risk of further delays in achieving the set objectives cannot be excluded. it should be remembered that such a choice of european airspace management would fully respect the sovereignty and prerogatives of the states. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i believe that we need to think about improving the efficiency of airspace by applying the latest traffic management technologies to avoid the consumer having to pay twice: in time and money. increasing traffic flows bring with them a considerable increase in operational risks, which is why action must be taken quickly. the 'single european sky' is a set of measures covering both the civil and military sectors and covering regulation, the economy, security, the environment, technology and institutions. i am voting in favour of helping to change an air traffic management organisation that has remained unchanged for decades, hoping to meet future air safety needs.
in writing. - mrs foster's report examines the limits of the policy launched ten years ago in this area, calling for greater political input from the member states and stressing that the benefits of full and timely implementation of the 'single european sky' are too great to be ignored. the completion of this programme will lead to significant economic, safety and environmental savings, creating a more sustainable aviation sector and a more effective european-wide traffic management system.
in writing. - the disparity in the levels of application of the legislation, the emergence of new trends in supply, the intermodality which characterises certain areas of the union by its own particular features, are three elements which are given careful consideration in the report, which deserves a favourable vote. in respect of and in realistic consideration of the different situations between countries, it is necessary to complete a rationalization operation, in the sign of a clear and precise knowledge of a minimum and uniform level of passenger rights within the eu. i particularly welcome the attention paid to the e-commerce market, which is growing rapidly in the tourism sector according to the estimates of the italian trade confederation and which calls for greater discipline in respect of travellers' rights, especially with regard to withdrawals, refunds and price composition. in this connection, i particularly welcome the comments and forecasts in paragraphs 41, 48, 49 and 54 on the european declaration of 'exceptional circumstances' exempting travellers from obligations, in the light of the case-law on the matter which has developed in the meantime. the recommendations on incentives for new ticketing technologies, intermodality and interoperability of networks and carriers, as well as for good practice laboratory areas with positive effects on economies and for environmental effects are also particularly welcome.
in writing. the report by mr bach deals with one of the points which i think should be the focus of our interest as members of the committee on transport: the rights of passengers. the report draws our attention to the needs of our citizens who move for work, family or tourism. the commission's communication lists rights for all modes of transport to ensure a minimum level of protection for travellers in the eu. i believe that the rights to access, proper information and assistance which the report emphasizes must always be guaranteed. in particular, i welcome the reference to non-discrimination for disabled persons or persons with reduced mobility, passengers travelling with children and travellers in the event of disruption of services.
in writing. - i agree with the suggestion to the commission that it should include in its list of passenger rights the right to a minimum level of quality of service provided by carriers and that this level should be defined in a clear way. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i vote in favour of mr bach's report on passenger rights in all modes of transport. in the single market, which we have been living in for 20 years now, travel is increasingly important for the development of the economy and for the personal fulfilment of citizens. it is important that this is not an obstacle course, but a normal daily activity. we must therefore also promote the use of new technologies for all modes of transport, for example for the issuing of boarding passes which can be stored, validated and displayed by electronic means.
in writing. − for intermodal travel to be successful and become a regular reality in the eu internal market, a common basis of rights covering all modes of transport and a minimum level of service quality are needed, as well as a convergence approach of all carriers and enforcement bodies. the commission's efforts to develop a multimodal european travel planning system, which would allow travellers to plan their journey throughout europe using a variety of means of transport, have so far not produced positive results, and in the hope that the member states will contribute, in cooperation with the commission, to the removal of the obstacles which prevent companies from developing such a system, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - despite some criticisms such as the assumption of a common frame of reference for all transport systems and the adoption of new technologies as specific applications for smartphones, my vote is in favour as i believe it is essential to protect passenger rights. greater price transparency, a serious handling of complaints, more rights rather than prohibitions are all very useful objectives. i am pleased that better conditions of care for disabled people have been included. a similar proposal had been made by the undersigned, as rapporteur in envi, in the european disability strategy. it is no longer acceptable that disabled people should not be able to find suitable transport and it is often not even possible to know whether the vehicle for which the ticket is purchased has dedicated services.
in writing. − the european union guarantees a minimum level of protection for travellers. the vote also stressed the crucial importance of improving the quality of services for disabled people, including unhindered access to airport infrastructure, the development of uniform and coordinated information procedures, adequate staff training and clarification of liability issues in the event of damage or loss of mobility equipment. as regards rail transport, considerable improvements have been made in recent years in terms of the protection of passengers and their baggage in the event of delays and accidents, but there is still room for improvement in services. depending on the mode of transport, passengers' rights differ in scope and possible exceptions, in particular as regards the definition of delays, the level of assistance and support provided during the waiting time until recourse to re-protection, the amount of compensation, the conditions under which compensation is no longer payable, the time taken to respond to complaints. passenger rights are based on the principle of compliance with the terms of the transport contract.
in writing. − the commission's list of rights for all modes of transport, which guarantees a minimum level of protection for travellers in the eu, is of great value. the eu legislation has been formulated in accordance with the principle of proportionality and with the necessary distinctions, taking into account the diversity of each mode and the relevant markets. from the individual provisions it is possible to derive a common basis for all passenger rights. unfortunately, the implementation of the laws is incomplete and uneven both on the part of the carriers and on the part of the national authorities: in addition, passengers are given incomplete information about their rights, are dissatisfied with the circumstances and costs of exercising those rights, and the procedures are too complex. it is therefore necessary to clearly set out the conditions for the implementation of a single regulation on passenger rights in all modes of transport, with particular attention to the clarity and accessibility of information.
in writing. - having regard to the general budget of the european union, and bearing in mind that 'citizens have the right to know how taxpayers' money is spent and how political bodies manage the powers conferred on them', parliament rejects the discharge to the secretary-general of the council for the implementation of the council's budget for the financial year 2010. recalling that, in accordance with article 335 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, 'the union shall be represented by each of the institutions, in accordance with their administrative autonomy, in matters relating to the functioning of the respective institution', and stressing that effective control of the implementation of the budget is a great responsibility and that its achievement depends entirely on unhindered interinstitutional cooperation between the council and parliament, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - having regard to the final annual accounts of the european environment agency for the financial year 2010 and the related report of the court of auditors, parliament rejects the discharge to the director of the european environment agency for the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2010. convinced that appropriate action should be taken where there are instances of non-compliance with the rules in force and believing that in such cases the agency should draw up an action plan to remedy the deficiencies, ideally under the control of the european parliament as regards its implementation, and that the european parliament itself or the european legislator should address such problems by amending existing rules and regulations to eliminate any deficiencies, i vote in favour of the proposal.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument to support the reintegration of workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the globalisation of world markets. this fund is for the benefit of the workers and does not act for the benefit of the company which made the redundancies. as regards the mobilisation of the fund for the case in question, i voted in favour because there are no criticisms and the application meets the eligibility criteria. ireland requested assistance for 592 redundancies, of which 432 were eligible for assistance, at talk talk broadband services (ireland).

in writing. - i am voting in favour of the fjellner report, which aims to change the current community regime for the control of exports and transit of dual-use goods, both civil and military, from the ordinary legislative procedure to the more streamlined procedure of delegated acts. the movement of dual-use items is de facto governed by decisions taken by international bodies according to un rules, which the eu and its member states must follow by updating a list of such items on a regular basis. i believe that the updating procedure adopted so far is too complex and too long in relation to the needs of our market, since any late amendment of the list could seriously damage european competitiveness; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be given the right to vote in the council of ministers.
in writing. - rapid technological change requires frequent revision of the lists of dual-use items: the use of delegated acts, in such a technical area and where decisions are already taken within international regimes, allows, in my view, to avoid overly complex legislative procedures which damage the competitiveness of european exporters, and instead favours a rapid and regular update of the control lists. i also consider that the delegated acts do provide for parliament and the member states to monitor the european commission's initiatives and for the possibility of intervention, so i voted in favour.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. i support the rapporteur's call on the commission to step up its efforts to develop electronic management systems for the control of dual-use goods and european union training programmes on export controls, ensuring that small and mediumsized enterprises remain competitive inside and outside the internal market.
in writing. − considering that the export control regime for dual-use goods and technologies aims to limit the risk of proliferation and military use, without hampering legitimate trade, it is essential to strike the right balance between these two aspects. in addition, rapid technological developments require regular and timely updating of international dual-use control lists; it is therefore necessary to simplify and speed up the procedures in place in order to avoid the emergence of safety concerns in the event of delays in the implementation of decisions on the strengthening of controls, and to adapt quickly to changing external circumstances, both to counter emerging proliferation threats and to avoid putting european industry at a competitive disadvantage. with these objectives in mind, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - general export authorisations have proved to be very effective instruments in facilitating the export of certain products to certain destinations with lower risks. i believe that amending the community regime for the control of exports of dual-use items is a function of making such controls as effective, efficient and timely as possible. in my view, control of trade in certain products effectively helps to limit the risks of proliferation and at the same time ensures that legitimate trade is not impeded. nowadays, technological progress makes it necessary to update the list of controlled products regularly. it is therefore necessary to ensure that the current eu general export authorisations can be rapidly amended with regard to their destination and the scope of products, so that the eu export control system can adequately reflect new developments at global level. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 428/2009 regulates the export of products which, although of a civilian nature, may be used for military purposes. annex i to that regulation contains the list of controlled products which may not leave the customs territory of the european union without an export authorisation. the export control regime for dual-use goods and technology is intended to limit the risk of proliferation and military use, without impeding legitimate trade. it is therefore essential to strike the right balance between the two by simplifying the procedures of the eu's export control regime. the objective of the union export control system is to ensure non-proliferation without restricting competition and competitiveness.

in writing. - i believe that this proposal deserves support in many respects. firstly, it is necessary to avoid conflicts between international, community and member state law, following the amendments to the international convention on the standards of training of seafarers. secondly, it focuses on the fundamental aspects of safety and the procedure for the recognition of training systems of third countries by emsa. finally, i think that the amendments to the text are broadly acceptable, especially as regards the revival of the competitiveness of our fleets, which is also seen as a means of creating jobs in a period of economic and employment crisis such as the present one. for all these reasons, my vote was in favour.
