in writing. - i am voting in favour of stricter rules on the training of seafarers, with a view to ensuring greater safety for seafarers and any passengers they may carry. better technical and physical preparation, and also preparedness for piracy and armed assaults, can only make sea travel safer. the amendments will also bring european standards in line with international standards approved by the international maritime organisation.
in writing. − i am voting in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2008/106/ec on the minimum training requirements for seafarers. the training of seafarers is an essential element of maritime safety and therefore i find it of the utmost importance that crews trained in different countries and systems have the necessary skills to perform their duties safely. this proposal aims to bring union legislation on the training and certification of seafarers into line with existing international standards by improving the wording of the legislative text in terms of clarity. for these reasons, i consider the proposal to be an essential element in avoiding conflicts between the obligations at international level and those at eu level assumed by the member states.
in writing. − whereas it is of the utmost importance that crews trained in different countries and systems, operating on the same ship, have the necessary skills to perform their duties safely, therefore training plays an important role in maritime safety. taking into account that the training and certification of seafarers is governed by the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers ('the stcw convention'), adopted in 1978, substantially amended in 1995 and finally in 2010 by the manila convention, it is now necessary to transpose the amendments to the stcw convention already approved by the member states meeting within the international maritime organisation (imo) in order to bring european legislation into line with the amended stcw convention. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the imo (international maritime organisation) has recently updated standards for the training, certification and safety of seafarers to prevent fraud in certifications, increase medical requirements and improve safety training, including preparedness for piracy and armed assault. the rapporteur agrees that the commission proposal is essentially concerned with transposing the amendments to the stcw convention (international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers) already approved by the member states meeting in the imo in order to bring european legislation into line with the amended stcw convention. the report also confirms the european rules on minimum rest periods, which are stricter than international ones, and introduces the possibility for the european commission to collect data on crews operating in community waters.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe that stricter rules are needed to protect the safety of personnel working on board vessels, by aligning european standards with those approved by the international maritime organisation. upgrading standards for training and safety of seafarers, including by increasing medical requirements and improving training in the event of piracy and armed assault, is now a priority that we can no longer ignore.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2008/106/ec of the european parliament and of the council on the minimum training requirements for seafarers. the proposed amendments are designed to ensure: stricter rules on the issuing and recognition of certificates of seafarer's training issued by states parties to the convention, new criteria for determining the physical fitness of crew members and greater rigor in the prevention of fraudulent practices. in addition to these updates, the ec proposal also focuses on the procedure for the recognition of third countries' training systems by the european maritime safety agency (emsa), extending from 3 to 18 months the timeframe within which emsa carries out the necessary procedures to verify that a given third country has effectively integrated into its practices the provisions of the convention.
in writing. − it is of the utmost importance that crews trained in different countries and systems, operating on the same ship, have the necessary skills to perform their duties safely. training plays an important role in maritime safety. the vote will seek to push for stricter provisions on training and assessment, the issuing of certificates of competence and the prevention of fraud; more up-to-date rules on physical fitness, fitness for duty and alcohol abuse; new requirements for certification of seafarers' experts, electro-technical officers and safety training for all seafarers; updated requirements for personnel on board certain types of vessels; clarification and simplification of the definition of 'certificate'.
in writing. − the importance of maritime training activities and the homogenisation of the training of crews from different countries working together is high. the aim is to ensure the safety of shipping operations at sea and in ports. the training and certification of seafarers is governed by the stcw convention, which was adopted by the imo conference in 1978 and entered into force in 1984. the stcw convention was first incorporated into union law by directive 94/58/ec of 22 november 1994. in 2010, a conference of the parties to the stcw convention, held in manila, initiated a comprehensive review introducing important amendments to the stcw convention ('manila amendments'), which entered into force on 1 january 2012. in order to avoid a conflict between the eu's commitments and the international commitments undertaken by the member states, it is necessary that the union's legislation on the training and certification of seafarers continue to be in line with international standards. it is therefore essential to transpose the manila amendments into eu law.

in writing. - i support the report which proposes to add to the euro-mediterranean agreement already in force with israel the protocol on the conformity assessment and acceptance of israeli industrial products. the protocol will facilitate access for products from both parties and israel will fully implement community legislation, allowing european exporters to test and certify their production according to rules already standard for them, without having to incur additional costs to meet other assessment requirements to gain access to the israeli market.
in writing. − considering that israel currently applies all agreements concluded with the european union to 'the entire territory of the state of israel', as defined in israeli national law, and that the eu does not recognise either the application of these agreements by israel in its occupied territories or any legislation promoting the annexation and colonization of these territories, in this context, the terms of the proposed text could allow israel to implement the protocol on the basis of its national law. if that were to happen, the european union would not be applying community law and would not be fulfilling its obligations under international law. i would like to stress that the eu must not depart from the provisions of the treaty of lisbon, which imposes an explicit obligation to ensure coherence between the various areas of foreign policy and other policies, in the conduct of its foreign policy. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the state of israel, of the other part, on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products. the entry into force of this agreement will extend some of the benefits of the internal market to sectors already aligned and will thus facilitate market access by removing technical barriers to trade in industrial products. the protocol will allow community exporters, if they so wish, to test and certify their industrial products against the same requirements, giving them, in practice, the possibility of accessing the israeli market without having to meet any further conformity assessment requirements.
in writing. the acaa is a technical agreement which aims to facilitate market access by removing technical barriers to trade in industrial products. in this case, the eu-israel acaa protocol will cover good manufacturing practice for pharmaceutical products only. i am in favour of negotiating the agreement, which is a part of the euromed process and whose purpose is to complete and strengthen the network of free trade agreements with all the countries of the region. my vote in favour is based on a view of the agreement not as an upgrade of the political relations between the eu and israel but as a technical agreement provided for in an already shared document (the eu-israel action plan), which falls within the scope of the implementation of the association agreement and was approved by the council in 2010. the conclusion of the agreement must therefore be based on a technical rather than a political approach, which would facilitate mutual access to the pharmaceutical market, since commercial advantages are expected for both parties.

in writing. − from a financial, regulatory, administrative and social point of view, the creation of micro-enterprises and smes in developing countries, in order to stimulate entrepreneurship and private sector development, is essential to create favourable business environments in developing countries. my vote is in favour.
in writing. − considering that since the adoption of the millennium development goals in 2000, some important changes, already noticeable at the time, have been accentuated, both on the economic level, where the surprising development of china, india and brazil tends to shift the economic centre of gravity of countries with mature economies towards emerging countries, and on the demographic level, where our planet, which has gone from 6 to 7 billion human beings in less than 10 years, will exceed 9 billion in 2030, it is necessary to strengthen eu cooperation with developing countries. for the success of eu development policy, particular attention needs to be paid to new actors, in particular china and india, with regard to their impact on the situation of the poor in the global south. with these objectives in mind, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the resolution which parliament is about to adopt is an important political act, which takes account of the ambitions and concerns which the european productive world has not yet expressed towards a country which represents an extraordinary opportunity for our economy but also a major problem. japan and the european union together account for more than a third of world gdp and more than 20% of world trade. these two figures show the importance of the negotiations we are about to open. we would therefore have preferred that the negotiations had been preceded by stronger signals from the east, which we do not think have come so far. the most important issue remains the removal of the many non-tariff barriers on the japanese side and of those regulatory barriers which cannot be justified by cultural differences alone. this removal must be a precondition for reaching a balanced and mutually beneficial agreement. the results in the public procurement and automobile sectors are particularly decisive for the successful conclusion of the negotiations. japan will have to open up its market as much as ours, in a spirit of substantial reciprocity, particularly with regard to the so-called zoning regulation of cars and the tax treatment of key cars. the question of geographical indications for agricultural and food products, including wines and spirits, will also be important. finally, we ask that parliament be kept informed of the progress of the negotiations and that the commission carry out a second assessment of the impact of a possible free trade agreement with japan, with particular reference to the most sensitive sectors such as the automotive or electronics sectors. only then, in these times of crisis in the european economy, can we say that we have protected europe's productive sectors without compromising our commitment to free, sustainable and fair trade.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, twenty years of the internal market have certainly left us with a number of positive aspects, and others less so. the questions which remain are many, important and partly open to discussion. i am referring, for example, to the possibility for a european citizen to open an account in another member state, to the portability of pensions, to the problems of small and mediumsized enterprises. we are of course in agreement on all these points, but there is one aspect which i would like to stress and which is perhaps not being discussed enough. sometimes there are rules decided in brussels that may be good for many countries, but that do not always apply everywhere in the same way. i shall just give the example of italian bathing establishments, which are unique in our country: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is applied in a fairly uniform manner. it is therefore right to harmonize, but not to approve, always respecting the principle of subsidiarity, but also involving the national, regional and local authorities more closely in the choices.

in writing. − i would remind you that council decision 2003/17/ec establishing a list of countries for which the application of the principle of equivalence to imports from third countries of fodder plant, cereal, beet and oil and fibre plant seed is recognised, limits the period for which equivalence is recognised to five years and that this period expires on 31 december 2012; therefore, in order to ensure the necessary supply of seed to the european union market, it is necessary to amend those rules by extending the deadline until 31 december 2022, although currently only a temporary extension of 5 years is provided for. i also think that serbia should be added to the list of countries with an equivalent system and that the former yugoslavia should be deleted from the list. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.

in writing. − considering that the current 12-nautical-mile zone is effective but will cease to be in force on 31 december 2012, it is now necessary to extend its validity of application. although the management of fishery resources beyond the 12 nautical mile limit has been characterised by highly centralised and ineffective control by brussels, management within the coastal zones by the member states has proved to be stable and positive. i therefore hope for a reform of the cfp which will lead to a highly decentralised system in general and which will allow member states to take real management decisions, while cooperating at regional level, and stressing that the 12 nautical mile zone has really proved effective and that there are good reasons to be in favour of extending its distance, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the report by mr hudghton was voted on today at the strasbourg plenary session. the rapporteur supports the extension of the 12-nautical-mile zone in terms of both time and distance, and accepts that this debate should take place within the wider framework of the cfp reform. the current 12-nautical-mile zone is effective, but will cease to be in force on 31 december 2012, so today's vote extends this period until 31 december 2014. the area provides a degree of protection for vulnerable coastal communities. the rapporteur therefore proposes to approve the current proposal and to extend the scheme for two years, although the need for greater national control of coastal fisheries will continue to be strongly supported in the wider context of the cfp reform package.

in writing. - the common fisheries policy has had several failures over the last 30 years, while many people recognise that fisheries management in the 12 nautical mile zone has been a success. although the management of fishery resources beyond the 12 nautical mile limit has been characterised by highly centralised and ineffective control by brussels, management within the coastal zones by the member states has proved to be stable and positive. that is why, as the debate on a wider reform of the common fisheries policy continues, i have expressed my support for the extension of the derogation for fishing in the 12 nautical mile zone until 31 december 2014.

in writing. - i am voting in favour of mr deva's report because the food aid convention is fully in line with eu policies and the millennium development goals. the lisbon treaty makes poverty reduction and its eradication the main objective of the union's policy. food security remains a key challenge: about 14% of the world's population was undernourished in 2010, and malnutrition is now the underlying cause of more than a third of child deaths.
in writing. - as no amendments to the convention are possible, in announcing my vote in favour of the recommendations, i would like to join in some of the remarks in the report. the extension of eligible activities shall be in line with a timely approach to food assistance, the capabilities of donors and the needs of beneficiaries; the food assistance committee will be able to promote coordination policies, including to strengthen the conditions necessary for the effective adoption of assistance plans, in line with the general principles underlying eu cooperation and development policies, such as respect for human and civil rights, a minimum framework of administration and governance, essential levels of transparency, timely verification of results and completion of aid. the whole system must be developed from an original idea of how to use agricultural surpluses to an effective culture of supporting and developing agricultural productivity in the beneficiary countries. finally, i share the wish that the donors' commitment should be expressed in terms of value alone, since it is obvious that the ability to express in terms of quantity is an outdated legacy of a time when the global market for agricultural products was less volatile.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty has set the reduction and consequent eradication of poverty as the main objective of the european union's development policy. the food aid convention is fully in line with the union's policies and the millennium development goals, and malnutrition now affects about 14% of the world's population and kills more than two and a half million children every year.
in writing. − i approve and support the food assistance convention (faa) which adopts new criteria compared to the previous one, introducing a criterion of aid-independence rather than a continuous subsistence criterion which prevents growth and development. in addition, the criteria introduced, which aim at transparency and openness to new products and terms in the convention, make this revision of the caa certainly positive. as the rapporteur has pointed out, there are still a number of areas for improvement, but progress in the direction of more regulation of aid distribution and access to aid will undoubtedly make the convention more effective. finally, emphasis should be placed on the introduction of agricultural and food products which are not only intended to satisfy food requirements but also to safeguard subsistence in emergency conditions and rapid recovery, such as seeds, dairy and meat cattle.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. i agree with the call for the european union to formulate an ambitious minimum annual commitment for 2013 in accordance with article 5 of the convention and to duly honour its annual commitments. hunger and food insecurity remain challenges from which we cannot escape.
in writing. − considering that hunger and food insecurity currently remain global challenges, and despite the significant developments in the last decade on several fronts, progress on hunger and malnutrition remains inexorably slow, amendments to the food assistance convention (caa 1999) are necessary. underlining that the 2012 caa is fully in line with the measures currently being taken by the european union to help reduce poverty and eradicate hunger in the world under the millennium development goals, and calling for the establishment of an international, legally binding framework defining and providing for commitments and instruments for the provision of food aid to developing countries, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − i welcome the proposal to amend the previous food assistance convention (caa 1999) in order to provide, through the caa 2012, for the establishment of a legally binding international framework defining and providing for commitments and instruments for the provision of food aid to developing countries. food assistance policies that are able to address the challenges of hunger and malnutrition are needed. the needs of the most deprived populations require us to make greater efforts to improve the instruments of intervention. the 2012 caa will be geared towards a long-term perspective that can support functional rehabilitation and recovery programmes that are conducive to the growth of production and the strengthening of local livelihoods. i believe that a targeted update of the previous convention will make it possible to relieve the most vulnerable countries of longterm aid, for example by including among the eligible products not only those aimed at meeting food needs but also those aimed at safeguarding livelihoods in emergency situations. i am voting in favour of this with a view to pursuing these ambitious commitments.
in writing. some aspects of the convention should still be reassessed and improved, either at the implementation stage or in a future revision of the convention. however, the amendments to the food assistance convention (caa 1999) are a real step forward and the conclusion of the 2012 caa and the work of mr deva on his report should be welcomed. as a reminder, hunger and food insecurity remain global challenges today. while significant progress has been made in several areas over the past decade, progress in the fight against hunger and malnutrition has been very slow. in 2010, about 925 million people, or 13.6 percent of the world's population, were undernourished, despite a decline in monetary poverty in several regions. ninety-eight percent of the undernourished live in developing countries. 60% of them are women.
in writing. − despite considerable improvements over the past decade, progress on hunger, malnutrition and food insecurity remains inexorably slow. the 2012 food assistance convention is fully in line with the measures taken by the union to contribute to reducing poverty and eradicating hunger in the world under the millennium development goals. it is clear, however, that these objectives will only be attainable by establishing a legally binding international framework defining and providing for commitments and instruments for the provision of food aid to developing countries.
in writing. − the right of a national of an unrepresented member state to receive assistance from the consular authorities of other represented member states is one of the rights conferred by citizenship of the union. this is a right which has been in force for many years, but which the european citizens are still not fully aware of. as a member of the libe committee responsible for civil liberties, justice and home affairs, i must consider the work done on this report to be more than satisfactory. i believe that the measures adopted will be able to strengthen the exercise of this right, thanks to greater coordination between member states in the field of consular representation. the only remaining doubt is the publicity of these new measures among the european citizens. in this context, i believe that a coordinated information campaign at european level can be the most effective instrument for achieving the desired results.
in writing. − in a recent article, historian niall ferguson argued that the current system of european governance embodies the historical assumption of the united states of america facing the 21st century with the institutional instrument of the old articles of confederation, which survived only eight years after constitutional revisions imposed for obvious political and practical reasons. the point is that the european institutions must commit themselves to closing the gap between relatively advanced integration and its necessary implementation, which in various spheres shows delays and inadequacies. this report, which i support with a favourable vote, resolves one of these contradictions in the field of the diplomatic representation of european citizens, an area of particular importance if we were to compile an annual list of crisis situations which have required the intervention of the consular authorities of individual member states. at any time, the rights and widespread interests of our citizens can be threatened by sudden crises, even in remote areas. i therefore find the report's proposals (including the creation of the trust fund) appropriate, as an integration of consular protection activities, which is already informally practised in some areas of the world, would allow a more efficient defence of european interests and would substantiate the notion of citizenship of the union.
in writing. − consular protection of citizens abroad (protected under article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) and article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights of the union) is effective both in everyday practice and in crisis situations. the latter concern an increasing number of contexts, which is why it is desirable to simplify access to rights and increase the knowledge of these rights by the citizen, since as a community citizen he is therefore in a position to exploit solidarity between member states in the event that his country is not directly represented in the third country or he himself has difficulty reaching his diplomatic mission. i therefore welcome the report, but i also recognize the need for further action and clarification in the future, for example on the role and functions of delegations and the definition of the financial resources needed to make them practical.
in writing. - i fully agree with the views expressed in this report. any citizen of a member state of the union who finds himself in difficulty in a foreign country where his state is not represented should have the possibility of contacting the diplomatic and consular services of the other member states or, in the absence of such services, the delegation of the european union in that state. i also welcome the fact that the eu delegations in third countries are to be given a coordinating role between the member states, particularly with regard to representation and assistance to citizens in crisis situations. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - we voted by a very large majority today for this resolution which states that european citizens who find themselves in difficulty abroad can turn to the consulate or embassy of any member state of the european union or, if necessary, to the eu delegation for assistance. i congratulate my colleague, mrs edith bauer, who drew up the resolution. i agree with you completely: this resolution shows the face of a europe close to its citizens. the proposal strengthens consular rights by clarifying when a citizen is considered not to be represented and specifying the type of assistance that member states typically provide in cases of need.
in writing. − in crisis situations, union delegations should ensure the necessary coordination between member states. in order to fulfil that role, the european external action service (eeas) should be provided with the necessary financial means, including for training courses for consular staff of the member states.
in writing. - european citizens are moving more and more, thanks to better protection of their rights when travelling, for which this parliament has fought hard. consular protection for union citizens abroad who cannot rely on the diplomatic representation (consulate or embassy) of their country of origin is therefore a necessary act of a union which must insist on promoting a sense of european identity for all its citizens.
in writing. − although, under article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), every citizen of the union enjoys, in the territory of a third country in which the member state of which he is a national is not represented, protection by the diplomatic and consular authorities of any member state, under the same conditions as nationals of that state, there are cases where, although the union citizen has his embassy or consulate in the third country, it is inaccessible. it is therefore important to define the accessibility of the embassy or consulate in sufficient time to reach it and/or return to the place of departure on the same day; in addition, in crisis situations, the union delegation should be responsible for coordinating and providing assistance with regard to crisis preparedness. in order to facilitate access to their rights for eu citizens, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the consular and diplomatic services of all member states must protect any european citizen seeking help abroad, providing the same protection as they would a fellow citizen. any european citizen in difficulty abroad, for example after an accident, rape or theft, or arrest in a crisis situation, will be free to seek help from an embassy or consulate of any other eu member state or, if necessary, from the eu delegation, if his or her country is not represented. eu delegations in non-eu countries (run by the european external action service) will need to coordinate with member states to ensure that citizens who do not have a representation from their own country can be fully assisted during a crisis. many eu citizens were caught up in the crises of the past year, for example in libya, egypt and bahrain during the democratic uprisings of spring 2011 or in japan after the earthquake of march 2011. consular protection is often essential in everyday situations too, for example if you are seriously ill or a victim of crime. more europe can mean more help for the european citizens who need it.
in writing. − the right of a national of an unrepresented member state to receive assistance from the consular authorities of other represented member states is one of the rights conferred by citizenship of the union. all citizens of the european union living in or travelling to a third country where their member state of origin is not represented shall be entitled to diplomatic and consular protection by the authorities of any member state, under the same conditions as nationals of that state. in emergency or crisis situations, such as japan, libya or egypt, a union citizen abroad has the right to ask the consulate or embassy of another eu member state for assistance if his own is not available, and member states have an obligation to help all union citizens, like their own, evacuate the country. the treaty of lisbon requires that solidarity between member states be fostered, so in everyday cases of consular protection, such as in the case of loss of identity documents, arrest, detention or death, the unrepresented citizen has the right to seek the assistance of any diplomatic or consular authority of a member state. for these reasons i shall vote in favour of the proposal for a directive.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive on consular protection for citizens of the union because i believe that citizens who are abroad and who do not have a representation from their own country should enjoy the same assistance from the diplomatic services of all the member states. the level of protection must be equivalent to that which the member state in question guarantees to its own nationals. facilitating cooperation between diplomatic services at local level, coordinating emergency situations, providing information to citizens, including through the commission and member states' websites, must be objectives that the european union must soon be able to guarantee to its citizens.
in writing. − new rules will make it possible to simplify the right of eu citizens to protection in third countries. sharing new legislative instruments, with a view to a common approach to consular protection, will facilitate recourse to any diplomatic or consular authority of a member state in a plurality of cases ranging from the loss of identity documents to arrest, detention or death. i welcome the proposal that the coordination and assistance of crisis situations involving nationals of member states in a third country should be left to the union delegation. the idea of a leading coordinating role for the delegation will facilitate consular protection as well as strengthen the role of the extensive network of eu delegations in consular protection. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − under article 23 of the treaty, citizens of the union who are in a third country where their member state is not represented have the right to apply to the consulate or embassy of another member state of the european union. the report by mr bauer, supporting the idea of a common approach in this area, aims to strengthen the consular rights of european citizens and to facilitate access to their rights, including the right to protection in third countries, also in view of the ever increasing number of crisis zones.
in writing. − i believe that the european single market, which is a space comprising more than 500 million consumers and economic activities worth over eur 11 billion, is an essential element both for achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and for achieving its objectives of sustainable, smart and inclusive growth. the relaunch of the single market and the strengthening of its effectiveness are therefore essential if europe is to boost economic growth, employment and the confidence of its citizens. unfortunately, it is clear that european businesses and citizens continue to face obstacles to the exercise of their rights under the acquis in the single market. the gap between the expectations and the reality of the single market persists, and is caused by a number of shortcomings, such as the lack of information and/or assistance to citizens in exercising their rights and the legislative gaps that businesses encounter in certain areas when carrying out their activities. the importance of removing these obstacles and reviving the single market is clear, especially in the current context of the economic and financial crisis that has hit europe, as they contribute to growth, the promotion of competitiveness and job creation.
in writing. - parliament is working on several fronts to strengthen the notion of european citizenship and certainly in this context the social value of the internal market is a primary theme. i agree with mrs bastos' analysis of the gaps (communication, implementation and legislation), the resulting recommendations and corrective actions and therefore i vote in favour of the report. i would like to stress in particular the urgency of certain initiatives, in view of the reduction in the rights and opportunities of our fellow citizens, and in particular of small businesses, families and the elderly, in relation to the factors of competitiveness (training and human capital, access to public procurement in other states, energy supplies), the right of the taxpayer (double taxation of work or pension treatment, portability of pensions, european health service). the current barriers to the single market (including in the field of company law, the interoperability of technological, transport and educational networks) constitute an obstacle to competitiveness and a brake on competition, to the benefit of structures, patterns and mindsets characteristic of pre-maastricht economies, with measurable negative effects on citizens. the best way to combat this resistance is through transparency and oversight by the relevant european institutions, in partnership with consumers and the public.
in writing. the single market is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. this is an important step which demonstrates the importance of the single market, but which also requires a first assessment, highlighting its strengths and weaknesses. the single market has undoubtedly simplified certain aspects of communication, information, access to documents and commercial relations between citizens of the european union. but there's still work to be done. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council on the basis of a proposal from the commission. i therefore support the commission's recommendations which called, amongst other things, for measures to modernise the system for the recognition of professional qualifications and to improve access to public procurement opportunities.
in writing. − in the current time of severe crisis, the eu must step up its efforts to remove obstacles to the proper functioning of the single market, particularly in areas that can act as engines for sustainable growth, such as cross-border business and trade, the provision of services, mobility, access to finance and financial literacy. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which gives a good account of the concerns of the citizens: the european internal market is a single area comprising over eur 11 billion of economic activity and where goods can move freely. in the 20 years since its completion - 1992 - the internal market has been able to ensure competitiveness for businesses and benefits for consumers, who are now expressing even greater concerns. above all, there is a gap between the expectations and the reality of the single market, a gap caused by interrelated gaps such as information, as people are often unaware of their rights; implementation, as there is a gap between the eu legal framework and the actual implementation of legislation in many areas; finally, there is a legislative gap in certain areas where the eu legal framework does not meet the expectations of citizens and businesses.
in writing. − considering that the single market, completed in 1992, was created with the aim of strengthening the links between citizens and member states and is characterised by a borderless area within which people, goods, services and capital can move freely, it is an essential element for achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and for achieving its objectives of sustainable, smart and inclusive growth. however, the economic, financial and social crisis that has hit europe since 2008 has had a strong impact on the single market, which has led to a negative view of the single market by citizens and, at the same time, has led to the european institutions and member states taking note of the potential of the single market that has yet to be exploited. in order to revive the single market and to increase citizens' confidence in it, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs bastos on her work. in adopting this text, parliament, in the light of professor mario monti's report to the commission on the relaunch of the single market, called on the commission to present 'concrete actions and feasible proposals' to address the first 20 concerns expressed by citizens and businesses. parliament stressed that the banking system had prevented some 30 million european citizens from opening bank accounts, thus hindering mobility within the single market, and that the introduction of a european professional card was essential to speed up the recognition of professional qualifications and thus facilitate the mobility of workers between member states. finally, the commission, the member states, regional and local authorities and representatives of civil society must launch a campaign of information and dialogue with citizens on the single market.
in writing. - the single market has certainly brought benefits to our citizens and businesses. that is why i am voting in favour. the problem is that, unlike our competitors such as the united states, the european commission's trade policy towards third countries does not allow us to protect our interests. similarly, the single market cannot be invoked as the solution to every problem in europe. in fact, it is often precisely because of bad directives, such as the directive on services, that our workers and our businesses are in a lot of trouble. the single market is a good thing, but it should not be an instrument designed solely to meet the needs of multinationals.
in writing. − the european single market, created with the aim of facilitating the free movement of persons, goods, services and capital, is now considered a prime instrument for overcoming the economic and financial crisis. the european single market is also an essential tool for the pursuit of the europe 2020 strategy. nevertheless, there is still a significant information asymmetry between european citizens and the single market, making the barriers to access to the benefits it brings almost insurmountable. i believe that the approach to the existing system needs to be changed so that practical solutions are given priority, allowing citizens to become more familiar with eu projects and activities. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is a very good one. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the single market was created with the aim of strengthening the links between citizens and member states through a borderless area in which people, goods, services and capital can move freely. in the year of its 20th anniversary, the gap between expectations and reality has unfortunately become clear: european businesses and citizens continue to face obstacles to the exercise of their rights, and the economic and social crisis that has hit europe since 2008 has certainly not helped the situation. this has made it necessary to draw up proposals for modernisation in the area of recognition of professional qualifications or access to public procurement opportunities, in order to revive the very idea of the 'single market' and to increase the confidence of european citizens.

in writing. - i have expressed my favourable opinion on the proposal for an amendment to regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community, as i consider that, in the interests of legal certainty and the principle of good administration, it is necessary to provide that these amendments apply as soon as possible to all new and pending investigations. regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 should therefore be amended, in particular as regards the three-month period granted to the commission to decide on the market economy treatment applications. i therefore hope that the use of anti-dumping will be reduced, regardless of zero or minimum margins. it is for these reasons that the committee on international trade has adopted the draft resolution by a simplified procedure. i take this opportunity to congratulate mr vital moreira on his work in examining the proposal for a regulation in question.
in writing. − whereas on 2 february 2012 the court of justice of the european union, in case c-249/10 p brosmann, annulled regulation (ec) no 1472/2006 of 5 october 2006 imposing a definitive anti-dumping duty, by finding that the sampling technique provided for in article 17 of regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 cannot be applied for the purpose of determining individual met claims, it is considered appropriate to introduce a provision clarifying that the decision to limit the investigation to a reasonable number of producers, using samples on the basis of article 17 of that regulation, also applies to the parties subject to a met examination. i am therefore voting in favour of the proposal, as i hope that these amendments will apply as soon as possible to all new and pending investigations.

in writing. − following the annulment of regulation (ec) no 1472/2006 of 5 october 2006 imposing a definitive anti-dumping duty by the court of justice of the european union, the sampling technique provided for in article 17 of regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 cannot be applied for the purpose of determining individual met claims. i consider it appropriate to introduce the limitation of the investigation as provided for in article 17, namely to a reasonable number of producers in accordance with the sampling procedures provided for in article 17. i welcome the proposal to simplify the procedure in accordance with the principles of legal certainty and good administration. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.

policies and its policies aimed at correcting macroeconomic imbalances. the commission equally welcomes the call for member states to strictly follow the rules set by the stability and growth pact and for all parties involved to speedily agree on the two pack. at the same time, the commission has taken careful note of the suggestions made in the report for improving the european semester process, for example regarding the content and focus of the annual growth survey priorities, including the role of the eu budget and the single market. the commission will issue the new annual growth survey at the end of november 2012, together with the alert mechanism report and regulation (eu) no 1176/2011. allow me to go into some more detail with regard to the positions expressed in the report in three areas. firstly, the report calls on the commission to review its current approach and to issue only one recommendation to member states in the financial assistance programme in order to bring it more into line with the europe 2020 objectives. i would like to recall that the adjustment programmes already touch on areas covered by europe 2020. the economic adjustment programmes include important growth-enhancing structural reforms covering the most urgent issues in the respective member states’ economies. the commission has deliberately decided to issue one single, country-specific recommendation for programme countries, asking them to implement the measures as laid down in the respective programmes. therefore all efforts should concentrate on programme implementation, which covers the most urgent priorities for the countries concerned. secondly, the report calls on the commission to present a framework regulation specifying the role – including timelines – of the member states and the eu institutions at the various stages of the semester cycle. however, whether a new legislative proposal in this area is opportune can only be assessed once the results of the currently ongoing negotiations on the two pack are completed and the debate on the future of emu has sufficiently advanced. thirdly, the report calls for strengthening the democratic legitimacy of eu economic governance. the commission supports the strong involvement of the european parliament in the reinforced european semester and the active role of the european parliament in the new economic dialogue. the possibility for parliament, introduced by the six pack, to conduct economic dialogues with individual member states provides an important element for a transparent process of democratic accountability in european economic governance. the commission encourages the european parliament to continue taking the economic dialogue forward with the other institutions and with individual member states, as foreseen in the six pack.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, not for the first time today, i have no ministers today at this time. on behalf of the commission, we welcome your report and we really appreciate the efforts of the rapporteur, mrs gardiazábal. gathering wide support for your report is a test of your skill, and we need the commitment of parliament to the enhanced role of financial instruments in the next financial perspective (2014-2020) for a very simple reason. we are under huge constraints and should try to get as much as possible out of each euro of the european budget. we therefore need this multiplying effect of the other financial instruments. you are right that is not a replacement for the budget; it is a multiplying effect of the budget. but it cannot be seen as a strategy to reduce the budget or to replace the grants by loans. of course both are needed, and this is our message to the council: we need multiplying effects, given the gap between the needs and what is possibly available as our resources. but this is not a replacement for the real budget, nor is it replacement by loans and revolving funds of the grants, which are the essence of the european budget. why do we need them? because the gap is visible; because we see, in a time of crisis, a sort of risk aversion – but it is mainly about banking. banking is three-quarters of the financing in europe, which is the opposite of what happens on the other side of the atlantic where three-quarters comes from the capital markets. in europe, this is mainly about the banking system, and under the credit crunch – under present-day circumstances – there is especially a high-risk aversion towards long-term projects in infrastructure. therefore we need the involvement of the european budget to reduce the risk, to reduce the risk aversion and to finance long-term projects, especially in transportation, energy and telecoms. we will test the water now via these pilot projects. i am happy to inform you that we are about to sign an agreement with the european investment bank and to launch some interesting pilot projects under the present financial perspective (2007-2013) – again, fully in compliance with a statement in the report that it should be governed by very strict legislative budgetary rules. before authorising the launch of a financial instrument, the budgetary authority should be fully informed and, by means of ex ante evaluations, should also be fully involved in monitoring the projects and final reporting. that is why we need flexibility, which was also a point in the report. flexibility is needed to adjust to the fluctuations of the market and to the local environment in many countries of the european union. therefore, there is a need for the enhanced role of the financial instruments, which is absolutely necessary to fill the gap between what we need for europe and possibly restrained financial resources in the european budget. thank you for your cooperation. we are on the right road and this is the road to recovery, supplementing financial austerity with real growth prospects for europe.
the commission has already submitted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, any argument should start from the fact that the commissioner first stressed that the budgetary resources available are very insufficient, so the few resources we have cannot be just grants, but these should be exploited in the so-called innovative financial instruments, which are then the specific funds, project bonds and so on, which of course need to be strengthened. public and private participation should be strengthened within the ppp system, which will help to implement individual financing projects by driving the physical and virtual infrastructure works of sustainable projects. if they are, it means that we can also go further and issue bonds because these, if the projects are sustainable and therefore reach a break-even at a certain point, are not debts but are long-term loans. that, commissioner, is the real growth, and we must have the courage to go beyond the budget.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as every year, this year too we are taking stock of the activities of the european ombudsman. the budget, at least this one, can certainly be described as an asset. i would remind you that the european ombudsman derives his powers from article 298 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and his main role in the network of european ombudsmen is to ensure that the right of citizens to good administration is respected and in particular that the rights guaranteed by article 41 of the charter are respected, which stipulates that every person must be treated by public institutions and public administrations in a clear, fair and, above all, rapidly evolving manner. this year, and i am referring specifically to 2011, the european ombudsman registered a decrease in the number of complaints compared to 2010. we're going from 2,667 to 2,510 complaints overall. the new feature of these complaints is that over 61%, slightly more than 61% of these complaints, were submitted using the internet tool. of this 61%, 53% was made by citizens using the form available on the european ombudsman's web portal. this is a very important issue for me as chair of the committee on petitions, which has been calling for some time for the recognition of an internet service and for the establishment of a web portal of the committee on petitions that is more responsive to citizens' requests. the number of requests for information and clarification has certainly decreased in 2011, and we all agree that this is the result of the very good guidance produced by the european ombudsman, which has succeeded in reducing the number of requests for information and clarification. the number of errors in the presentation of cases to the european ombudsman has also been reduced, i.e. the number of cases which were not formulated correctly to the ombudsman because they did not fall within his competence has been reduced, and this is certainly also due to two other media which have been used and produced by the european ombudsman's office to help and facilitate the task of citizens. last but not least, the european ombudsman also made a speech on procedures in 2011 which concerned a simplification of procedures. these interventions and the good practices put in place by the european ombudsman have certainly helped to improve the outcome of the ombudsman's work. in the total of complaints lodged by citizens, the number of complaints against the european commission remains high, and it is the largest share of the total number of complaints lodged, at 58%. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very important one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. the parliament, on the other hand, has, it is worth noting, reduced the number of complaints against it by almost half, while those against the council have increased. the inquiries opened by the ombudsman were largely closed: 382 open, 318 closed, so i think it's a great performance. this activity and this is the annotation with which i close has a single node: as the ombudsman's work is carried out by all institutional actors participating in the civic network for the protection of citizens' rights who do not have the actual powers to try to implement citizens' requests in practice, the ombudsman's proceedings may end with a recommendation or, in extremely negative cases, with a critical note, but they cannot bring the answer directly to the citizen.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the legal basis for the mandate of the european ombudsman is article 228 of the tfeu, which empowers him to receive complaints concerning cases of maladministration in the activities of the institutions, bodies, offices or agencies of the union, with the exception of the court of justice of the european union in the exercise of its judicial functions. the right to have recourse to the european ombudsman is provided for in article 24 tfeu and article 43 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the ombudsman's mandate was extended to include possible cases of maladministration in the context of cfsp and esdp policy. most of the inquiries opened by the ombudsman in 2011 concerned the european commission, as the main institution of the european union whose decisions have direct consequences for citizens. the european ombudsman works closely with his counterparts in the member states. the cooperation shall be implemented within the framework of the european network of ombudsmen.

in writing. − the mifid directive establishes a regulatory framework to regulate the provision of investment services, thereby providing a high level of protection for investors and allowing investment firms to provide their services throughout the community. directive 2004/39/ec has also increased transparency and competition in markets and improved investor protection. however, i believe that it is necessary to take into account the problems that have emerged in the recent period, when there has been increased competition between trading venues for financial instruments and the choice for investors in terms of service providers and available financial instruments has increased. the benefits of increased competition were not evenly distributed among all market participants and were not always passed on to final investors. this has rendered the provisions of the directive obsolete. the purpose of the review of the mifid directive is to update the existing rules to take account of market developments, including the financial crisis and technological developments, and to improve their effectiveness, and i therefore vote in favour of it.

in writing. − the russian accession to the wto is a remarkable achievement for the country’s economic development and a significant opportunity for exporters and investors around the world. russia, with a population of 140 million, is the last major world economy to join the organisation. its membership ends the anomaly of having russia, a leading oil and natural gas exporter and a permanent member of the united nations security council, outside the world trade system. the world bank estimates that russia will gain between usd 53 and usd 177 billion per year because of wto membership, reducing poverty and raising the living standards of millions of people. i also would like to underline that this accession is a further step in improving the bilateral eu-russia relationship. the eu and russia are interdependent trading partners and for the first time both entities will be bound by multilateral rules and obligations for their mutual trade. for these reasons, i value the possibility of concluding a new eu-russia partnership and cooperation agreement as a further opportunity to contribute to an enhanced partnership for both.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the positive assessment of russia's accession to the wto, which was ratified by the russian state duma on 10 july 2012. russia's accession to the multilateral trading system and its rules is a major step towards strengthening eu-russia bilateral relations.
in writing. - last december, after 18 years of negotiations, the russian federation also joined the world trade organisation (wto). this resolution sets out some guidelines for regulating trade relations between the european union and russia, highlighting some key points which i fully agree with. firstly, there must be relations based on the principle of reciprocity, which should apply in a wide range of areas, from access to public procurement, to the recognition of intellectual property rights, to the protection of agricultural origin and quality marks. russia is a strategic partner for europe, especially in our energy supply: i therefore believe that we must establish common rules to regulate trade between these two vast markets, which still have a lot of untapped potential, which if properly exploited could open up new horizons and new prospects for many of our companies and products.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, russia's accession to the wto after 18 years of difficult negotiations is an important event, both from a historical, economic and commercial point of view. the choice of russia is also an advantage for the eu, considering that we represent its main source of imports and are a key partner for investment. this linking of russia to the multilateral trading system is a further step towards strengthening eu-russia bilateral relations. nevertheless, many problems remain to be solved: the main ones being the elimination of a number of potentially restrictive trade measures, preferential rules on public procurement and the introduction of seasonal duties on imports of certain types of sugar; the commission has also proposed a new regulation on vehicle recycling. provisional bans, temporary unilateral tariff increases, protectionist measures and barriers to open and fair trade must be eliminated. in addition, there are infringements and measures concerning intellectual property rights. it is also a matter of moving swiftly towards the establishment of the rule of law, since certain recent convictions and sentences are a threat to democracy. economic modernization has many facets and all must be considered by russia to enhance the new bilateral relations with europe.
in writing. − after 18 years of negotiations, russia joins the world trade organisation (wto) as its 156th member. i think that this accession is an important step for the eu, considering that the total value of trade in goods between the two countries in 2011 amounted to 308 billion euros. the eu is russia's main trading partner and russia is the eu's third largest trading partner. through russia's accession to the wto, mutual trade and trade activities will be bound by multilateral rules and obligations. i see this as an event which can provide great opportunities for russian and european businesses, facilitating trade and investment and shedding new light on russia's position in the world economy. this partnership will have a positive impact on access to the market for goods and services. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, at a time when talk of greater european integration sounds like a provocation to some nostalgic nationalists, we are about to vote on the revision of a regulation which forms the basis of the difficult but necessary process of harmonization and approximation of national legal systems. let me therefore congratulate mr zwiefka on his excellent work and on having succeeded, after some two years of difficult negotiations, in closing a process of revision of a regulation which is fundamental for the citizens of the union. brussels 1 lays down very important provisions to ensure wide access to justice and equal treatment before the competent courts within the european union. it lays down common rules in civil and commercial matters, clarifying which court has jurisdiction in crossborder disputes and making judgments given in the various states enforceable. the amendments to the regulation are necessary in order to give effect to the desire to create a european area of justice, which promotes legal certainty and predictability of decisions, thereby facilitating transnational exchanges and strengthening the single market. in this context, i am of the opinion that progress towards ever deeper harmonisation of substantive law rules must proceed with due caution and care in order to ensure legal certainty and protect the least-favoured parties. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's approach in favour of consumers, who will benefit from the principle of protecting the weaker party. a principle according to which, in a legal dispute between consumers and businesses, the consumer will always have the choice of going to a court in the member state in which he is domiciled. similarly, i share the cautious approach of my colleague zwiefka to the abolition of the exequatur: if, on the one hand, the abolition of the exequatur would make it possible to further speed up the recognition of judgments, on the other hand, i believe it is necessary to maintain measures to safeguard the rights of the accused. it is therefore necessary that the latter should have the possibility to challenge a decision if their right to a fair trial has been infringed and if the decision is contrary to public policy in the state of reference. i would like to conclude by extending my congratulations to the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs. i hope that we will reach a broad interinstitutional and political consensus on a regulation which will be the basis of judicial cooperation in civil matters and the political determination underlying the process of european integration.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, vice-president reding, i congratulate the rapporteur on the conclusion of this complex dossier, which comes at the end of a long and complex debate and finally sees an agreement with the council and which fully reflects the position of parliament since the abolition of the so-called exequatur without exception. this is a particularly important step, because it effectively abolishes an intermediate judicial procedure which, among other things, has proved to be a mere formality and reduces the costs and time of crossborder disputes. there will certainly be greater protection for citizens who can bring disputes against companies which are also active in third countries before the courts of their own country. in particular, there will be better agreement on the choice of the appropriate forum to prevent so-called unfair procedural tactics. this is important progress in further facilitating the free movement of decisions and, above all, in ensuring better access to justice, less bureaucracy, less waste of time and money, and more secure and accessible rules. i believe that in times of crisis, citizens, households and businesses can greatly appreciate this reduction in red tape and simplification of procedures.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, this proposal is indeed a major reform that this parliament and all the institutions should be proud of, because it will enable us to build bridges between the different judicial systems in our member states. i think that this is an important step, even if it was not possible to agree on everything, for instance arbitration or jurisdiction rules applied to industrial action. but it is certainly an important step in the right direction, and other steps will follow. i also thank those colleagues who have underlined how long the discussion on such subjects has already been going on, with no possibility of moving forward until we got the treaty of lisbon, which allowed us to take the steps which are needed in order to build up the contributions of all systems in all member states in a way that can be taken seriously. we are putting into practice a principle of ‘full faith and credit’ in the mutual recognition of judicial decisions. this means that we recognise and implement decisions by the national courts, ensuring that they are implemented in another jurisdiction as if they were being implemented domestically. that is what mutual recognition is about and that is what we need if we want to have freedom of movement, not only of goods and services, but also of citizens and of judicial decisions. this project which you have put on the table today will really benefit citizens and businesses and, historically speaking, it will also be one of those important steps in order to have a real continent of justice tomorrow.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank the committee on legal affairs for having raised this very important question because we all know that parental child abduction is a tragedy that has very often substantial long-term consequences for the child. the prevention of child abduction should therefore be a central part of eu policy to promote the rights of the child and, in international cases, multilateral rules are key to ensuring the protection of children. since 2007 the european union has been a full member of the hague conference on private international law and in that context the union supports the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction and encourages third states to accede to it. to date there are 87 contracting parties to the hague convention, including all the eu member states. the convention establishes a system of cooperation between the contracting parties to restore the status quo ante of the wrongfully removed or retained child, but for these systems to operate an explicit declaration of acceptance is necessary and this is why the commission last year presented a package of proposals for the eu’s acceptance of the accession of eight new contracting parties to the convention, including key partners such as russia and morocco. the adoption of such proposals would ensure that all member states have the possibility to use the hague mechanism with all the contracting parties of the convention for very concrete child abduction cases; this would be in the best interest of children and it would also respect the principle of the unity and external representation of the european union. i really do regret that this package has been blocked in the council for almost a year. in practice this means, for example, that singapore’s accession has been accepted by 10 member states, morocco’s by 14 and seychelles’ by 18 member states. it also means that after having promoted russia’s accession for many years and having finally persuaded russia to accede, the european union as a whole is now not able to accept this accession and the russian authorities are of course raising this with us in the regular high-level meetings we have. i deeply regret that despite their declarations of intent, the member states as a whole have so far failed to show the sensitivity and the political will which are needed in order to tackle the current fragmented situation in the field of international child abduction. i am afraid that we may need to ask the court of justice to deliver a verdict on this institutional dispute on competences which has very undesirable consequences. i would like to thank the rapporteur, ms lichtenberger, for having supported the commission’s proposal and the committee on legal affairs as a whole for having worked on this. we share the same urgent need to protect children, prevent child abductions and minimise the distress that families suffer due to the legal uncertainty and the lack of a simple and unified procedure at eu level in this matter. i really regret that we are fighting about procedures instead of fighting for the good of the child.
