member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank in particular mr el khadraoui who coordinated this report, but also other members for an important contribution to the debate and for emphasising that regulators should not forget some actors and entities commonly designated under the term ‘shadow banking sector’. the views expressed in the parliament report are in line with the commission’s concerns and the objectives: firstly, to strengthen the resilience capacities of the global financial sector and, secondly, to reduce regulatory arbitrage possibilities. i am glad to share these concerns with you. your concrete request to act reinforces our willingness to keep these issues very high on the commission’s agenda. what do we mean by shadow banking? shadow banking comprises financial entities or activities which carry out credit intermediation activities outside the regulated sector. in practice, risks linked to these activities were observed in 2008, when special purpose vehicles were purchased and then securitised illiquid assets and subprime mortgages were converted into assets such as collateralised debt obligations. these assets were bought by many investors worldwide and then turned out to be worthless and illiquid. unfortunately, we all now know the consequences of such strategies. why should regulators focus on the shadow banking sector? firstly, this sector constitutes a very large amount of financial activities. the fsb has roughly estimated the size of global shadow banking at around eur 46 trillion in 2010 having increased from eur 21 trillion in 2002. secondly, the sector is highly interlinked with the regulated sector and especially with banks. potential contagion effects are high and could materialise very quickly, with an impact on the whole economy. for instance, when money market funds suffered from financial pressures, they suddenly had to stop the investments in short instruments issued by banks and non-financial corporations. as a result, there was a credit crunch in this market. finally, at the same time that regulators are strongly strengthening potential rules for banks – crr, crd 4 – it would be highly undesirable to keep some actors or entities outside the supervisory oversight. i would directly generate regulatory arbitrage opportunities and give incentives for financial entities to develop risky activities in less regulated areas of shadow banking. for all these reasons the commission drafted a green paper on shadow banking to identify the appropriate measures to regulate these risks in europe. it is key to working in a consistent way with our g20 and financial stability board partners, while adjusting our work to specific european issues. the european systemic risk board contribution to this debate will be very helpful for the commission, as well as all the contributions to the green paper that have been received. in early 2013, the commission will present a roadmap on shadow banking in the eu focusing on three priorities: firstly, the strengthening of transparency and data collection and monitoring; secondly, money market funds, and, thirdly, strengthening policies in the field of repo and securities lending transactions. i thank parliament for its support, through this excellent report, for the commission’s work to strengthen our financial sector, to reduce systemic risk and to reduce the scope for regulatory arbitrage. i understand your request that the commission acts on the shadow banking sector. this is a clear signal and we will act on it in the coming months.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, 23 years after the un convention on the rights of the child, the internet is becoming the new frontier for protecting and promoting the rights of children, because of the growing penetration of the internet among european children and adolescents, a kind of symbiosis that shapes their personality and their way of relating to the outside world. the average age of first internet access a few years ago was around nine, but today digital natives are taking their first steps on the internet before they can read or write. children under 16 use computers to study, play games, watch videos, download videos and music, share files, visit chat rooms, blogs and virtual worlds. but most kids between the ages of 9 and 16 are registered on a social network with their profile; many present with fictitious identities, and a quarter of teenagers report being older than their real age. 12% of 9-12 year olds say they have been harassed, in particular, by bullying for 40% and by sexual content and approaches for 25%. so there are opportunities and risks on the net: the network is now indispensable for the social, educational and occupational integration of children, but the european institutions and the member states must work to ensure that children have access to education, information, rules for safe navigation and the responsibility of operators, businesses and educators. the report proposes a holistic approach to the promotion and protection of children's rights online. the exchange with the various political groups in the cult committee and the shadow rapporteurs, for which i am grateful, has made it possible to reach a compromise text which is broadly satisfactory, even though it is a matter on which there are different sensitivities and orientations. the cooperation of the libe committee and its rapporteur, anna hedh, was significant. the report welcomes and complements, with precise guidelines, the commission's recent communication on a safer internet for children. our aim was to balance the fundamental rights of the child in the digital world, the right to access education, the right to protection and the right to digital citizenship, in a new governance that puts the child's best interests as a person in training and as a european citizen at the centre on the basis of article 24 of the european charter and the treaty. in the area of governance, we ask the commission to integrate the rights of the child across all eu policies that refer to the network, to refinance specific programmes such as safer internet on the basis of reporting and monitoring, and to take appropriate measures also through the internet and to coordinate the implementation of the codes of conduct and the ceo coalition initiative. we also agree with the commission's proposal to intervene by means of legislation if the current self-regulatory codes are not adopted. as regards access to the internet in peace and security, we propose to support measures for an educational alliance between families, schools, associations and media and audiovisual services, to integrate these skills into school curricula and the training of educators and adults; the supervision of the marketing and advertising of harmful products online; the exchange of good practices on the role of non-formal education in the dissemination of positive and safe practices among adolescents in the network; the access of minors to pluralistic, quality and secure digital content in school curricula and services and, in particular, in the public media service. as regards the right to protection, the report clearly distinguishes between illegal content and inappropriate and dangerous content. for dangerous and inappropriate aspects, we call for actions to protect identity and privacy; preventing early exposure to sexuality, grooming, inappropriate behavior, including towards other minors, such as cyberbullying and sexting. we also ask the commission to support the initiative to classify inappropriate content and, in general, all technical innovations that can guide parents and children; we support the proposal by commissioner reding on the protection of personal data, privacy, the right to be forgotten, with specific measures on minors, including a parental consent requirement for the processing of their data. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the protection of personal data and the protection of privacy. finally, we encourage - and ask the commission to encourage - all those forms in the member states that can support digital citizenship, which is crucial for the development of an intelligent and inclusive union and for civic participation, including through the network, by minors.

in writing. in recent years, most responses to the financial and economic crisis have been based on objectives aimed at restoring the sustainability of public finances, which is a key element for the union's economy. i believe, however, that the negative effects that such austerity measures may have on employment and competitiveness in europe should not be overlooked and that they should be complemented by measures to promote employment, such as targeted social investment. the already complex situation of the labour market in europe is further aggravated by problems concerning education systems and the ageing of the population. on the one hand, the educational outcomes in the union are not adapted to the increasing intensity of specialised jobs required by the market, and on the other hand, due to the ageing of the population, the number of people entering the labour market is decreasing: this demographic trend will have serious repercussions on the labour market, economic growth potential and public savings. i believe that in order to restore sustainable growth in europe, it is imperative to respond to these challenges also with the help of targeted social investments aimed at preparing society to manage the transition to more flexible labour markets, to restore a suitable level of employment in the future and to improve europe's competitiveness.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the social economy has a high degree of resilience to crises and robustness in terms of business models, and all the requirements for the objectives of the 2020 strategy. support for social enterprises brings economic benefits, but it is above all the nature of their activities and their modus operandi that favours the creation of a society, a more democratic working environment and employment, which is active, cohesive, supportive and capable of contributing to job creation. actions to improve the legal and fiscal environment and a european social label - the principle of the most economically advantageous tender rather than the lowest price in public procurement - can therefore help to achieve financial independence and create an eco-social and highly innovative market economy. i therefore congratulate mr becker on his excellent work.

the agenda includes, for joint debate, the report by mr wim van de camp, on behalf of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the type-approval of two or three-wheel motor vehicles and quadricycles and on market surveillance (com (2010) 0542 - c7-0317/2010 - 2010/0271 (cod)) (a7-0445/2011) and the report by mr pier antonio panzeri, on behalf of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the type-approval of agricultural or forestry vehicles (com (2010) 0395 - c7-0204/2010 - 2010/0212 (cod)) (a7-0446/2011).
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the legislative process began in november 2010 and was a technical and political undertaking that lasted two years and involved three council presidencies. i think it is appropriate to thank all the actors involved, the shadow rapporteurs, the parliament's secretariat and the secretariats of the political groups and the members' assistants, and of course the commission and the council. the final text is agreed at first reading, which i consider very significant and important. the purpose of this regulation is to establish a set of harmonised standards for the manufacture of agricultural and forestry vehicles, in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and, in particular, to ensure the application of a number of important criteria which improve functional, occupational and road safety for users, workers and environmental standards. in this context, the introduction of new functional and occupational requirements in articles 7 and 8 can be considered a real success for the european parliament as a whole, which has succeeded in covering the risks that today affect many workers with often fatal consequences: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the current crisis. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of workers is not compromised, and that is why we have introduced provisions on the market surveillance of vehicles, systems and components, to ensure that all the provisions are properly implemented and made effective. finally, the regulation contributes to the competitiveness of the industry by simplifying the current legislation on vehicle typeapproval, increasing its transparency and reducing its administrative burden. the commission is proposing to repeal 24 basic directives and some 25 related amending directives on technical requirements, replacing them all with a single regulation. these aspects are important because this regulation is intended to achieve a number of other objectives, in addition to contributing to the construction of the regulated internal market and to creating a framework for a competitive, balanced and transparent system. but we are also contributing, i believe, to the strengthening of the sector and, finally, creating the conditions for the expansion of the productive base and employment. the work done is therefore very important and has been very fruitful: the compromise reached between all the political groups is the result of a great deal of cooperation, carried out in the right spirit and with the right spirit and with the will to finally deliver a common regulation to the european parliament.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank the two rapporteurs, and in particular mr panzeri, who has shown himself to be a good mediator. the debate concerns two regulations dealing with similar and highly technical issues. in one case, the type approval of agricultural and forestry vehicles and, in the other, that of two- or three-wheel motor vehicles or quadricycles. the discussion in committee and with the council resulted in a shared compromise agreement and a virtually unanimous vote in favour. the purpose of the measures is to simplify the current regulatory framework and introduce new administrative and technical requirements relating to environmental and safety aspects. as regards vehicles used for specific agricultural and forestry purposes, it was considered that, as there were only a limited number of vehicles, it was not necessary to place excessive environmental and technical performance requirements on them. the agreement also covers four-wheel vehicles, known as 'quads', divided into two categories: the one for sporting and private vehicle use and the one for agricultural and forestry use only. it is clear that quads for agricultural and forestry use will have to be adapted and thus differentiated from those produced for normal transport purposes. it is also positive that an agreement has been reached with the manufacturers of these vehicles on access to repair and maintenance information. as regards motorcycles, environmental requirements which would not be too burdensome for manufacturers to adapt were considered in this case, as they impact less than 3% of the total road transport mileage and therefore have almost no influence on air pollution. the vote on the two measures will therefore be favourable, partly because producers have been waiting for too long, as have users, for clearer, more precise and simpler rules, which are also more applicable.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the council of europe in june identified what we need most: that is, more europe. the european council in brussels in december last year, in the context of the european council in brussels, stressed the need to strengthen the european union's economic and monetary union. all the previous speakers have mentioned a number of problems, one of which is the need for greater democracy, which i would like to put first, followed by a single financial framework, a single budgetary framework and a single economic and monetary policy framework. these four conditions are necessary to move forward on the road to greater european integration. with this report, mrs thyssen is seeking to express the opinion of parliament, because that is the right thing to do. however, the report also provided an opportunity for the various political groups to express their views and concerns, which resulted in a substantial number of amendments. i congratulate mrs thyssen on her excellent work in drafting the compromise and on finding a solution that is as acceptable as possible. i realize that there are some perplexities and different positions, ladies and gentlemen, but we must work together to find the most balanced picture possible. the concerns concern mainly, but not exclusively, the single banking supervision system. i therefore believe that we must act quickly and send a clear message from the european parliament to the commission and the council. we must emphasize that the elements identified in june are an essential condition for a stronger european union, capable of guaranteeing economic growth and more jobs, especially for the new generations, because that is the challenge we are facing.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, you seem to understand that we must move towards a genuine economic and monetary union: does this mean that we have been joking about it all along, that all the measures taken so far were not real but the product of someone's imagination? unfortunately, that was not the case, and the fruit we were served was poisoned. the wrong assumptions are still being insisted on, such as the need to standardise the economy and the irreversibility of the euro. it is precisely the contract, the cornerstone of the euro, which will lead to the end of a single european union. the report indicates that the member states which do not yet have the single currency are interested in joining it. but that is not true at all, as shown by bulgaria and poland, which do not want to join the euro. the possibility of not joining the euro is also reiterated. that's good, that's great. so let us not say that the single currency is the very purpose of the european union and above all that measures are being taken to get out of the euro, as it is already possible to get out of the european union itself under article 50 of the treaty. the word 'binding' is used repeatedly in the report: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. it would therefore be that brussels would inevitably fall back on policies that are good for several european countries, and that is dangerous and unacceptable for us. we do not want to be slaves to brussels.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have appreciated the work of mrs thyssen. but i think we are now faced with a number of issues that go beyond the merits of your report. when we have spoken of banking supervision, when we have discussed on various occasions the general conditions for the management of economic activities and the defence of the currency in the european union, we have always been faced with difficulties which did not concern the specific subject but the relations between the individual institutions. parliament is the most exposed institution, being the only body directly elected by the citizens, but on the other hand, it is also the one with the least objective powers. i wonder if it's time to face the problem for what it is: we need a revision of the basic rules, that is, of the treaty. if we do not start from there, i fear that all our work will always be confronted with difficulties which represent insoluble contradictions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the commissioners for their presence in the house today. today, this house will have the opportunity to address, at two different times, a subject which is of the utmost importance, of great importance for europe at this moment and which is linked to growth and employment within our continent, within our union. i believe that the two commissioners here should be the reference point for all of us at this stage, for the policies they are pursuing and for the choices they are making. in this context, i ask commissioner tajani whether the work he has done so far can be concluded, as a first step, by a real strengthening of the commission's role at european level in relation to industrial policy, because this is the train that can really give us the satisfaction we expect.
vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president of the committee on industry, the european commission intends to play a role within the limits of the treaty, although i cannot ignore the letter i received from seven ministers from member states and the will expressed at the last competitiveness council, at which i presented the commission's draft on the reindustrialisation of the european union. the desire is emerging from many ministers of industry to have a european industrial policy, at least of coordination, and thus to give more weight to the competitiveness council as regards the strategies to be studied. i have responded positively to the ministers' letter, so much so that on the eve of the next meeting of the competitiveness council on 10 june i will be meeting the ministers of industry informally to discuss the car crisis and the action plan for the car which will be on the agenda of the competitiveness council. i too believe that some corrections must be made and that the commission must play a proactive role, because sometimes the competitiveness council risks becoming a sort of coreper, given the constant succession of ministers: sometimes states cannot send 4-5 ministers in the same day, so they prefer to leave a diplomatic representative. i believe that given the current situation and the fact that we want to get out of the crisis by focusing on the real economy, the competitiveness council should be given more weight and the european commission should be given a greater coordinating role, and i thank parliament for the support it has always given me in this direction.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, just a thought: i think it would be useful in a situation like this to reinstate the industry council on the one hand, and secondly, i think that a working group should be set up within the commission with germany on the one hand and the foreign trade commissioner on the other, because the problem of european industry is certainly a problem of european industry but at the same time it is also a problem of the rules of our internal market and of a more careful policy on external relations and the arrival in europe of all kinds of goods which do not conform to our rules.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european commission is considering, also internally, a competition policy which can enable europe to be competitive and to face up to globalisation. our competitors are not only within the union but also outside the union. that is why commissioner almunia is planning to present a proposal to amend the state aid rules as well, and the commission certainly intends to discuss the union's competitiveness policy as well, in an obviously free context and in an attempt to make our reality more competitive at global level.
member of the commission. − we already had a number of opportunities to discuss with the social partners, including trade unions sectorally but also with the umbrella organisations, the importance of industrial policy and the importance of human capital investment inside industrial policy. i believe the commission’s initiatives in the recent period have been welcomed by the social partners and it is understood especially in the context of a sectoral crisis like the automotive industry, for example, how important it is to have a strategic view – how important it is to connect all stakeholders together for an industrial revival in the eu. some aspects, of course, can be connected with existing formats for the dialogue with the social partners. for example, the tripartite social summit or the new opportunities for the social partners to participate in economic governance also provide room to address issues of industrial policy.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i would just like to add on the matters within my competence, since we cooperate very closely with commissioner andor on all industrial policy initiatives, especially on the action plans for the shipbuilding sector, the action plans for the car industry and the action plan for steel, that the commissioner or a representative of his cabinet has always attended all the meetings and the trade unions have always been involved in all our initiatives, including strictly industrial policy, not just in terms of restructuring. next week i will meet, before the industry representatives, the representatives of the european trade unions on the car action plan, and the trade unions will be an integral part of all our actions. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.
member of the commission. − indeed the quota of women is an important step in the commission’s life. but on the question of female entrepreneurs, there are existing eu financial instruments and programmes exist which can support women in becoming entrepreneurs. the european social fund can do this and has done so in a variety of ways. the progress microfinance facility, which was launched two years ago but only started to function at the beginning of last year, creates this opportunity. for example, in slovenia i recently had the opportunity to see a project supported by progress microfinance. this provides opportunities for women at various stages of their careers to become self-employed or entrepreneurs. we have to highlight this, because there are still about ten countries which have not taken concrete steps towards using the progress microfinance facility, and there are opportunities in this area.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i should also mention the initiative launched in 2009 to create the european network of women ambassadors for women entrepreneurs, which was modelled on the national networks of sweden and the united kingdom: it is a network which is now active in 22 countries of the european union. in addition, on 15 november last year, the commission launched the european mentoring network for women entrepreneurs, active in 17 european countries with some 170 women entrepreneurs, which is developing its activities to increase the number of women in entrepreneurship. so, as part of the strategy drawn up by commissioner andor, there are also these concrete initiatives so that there can be an exchange of information, a real network. moreover, as regards entrepreneurship, in a few weeks' time - before the end of the year - under the cypriot presidency, we will launch a commission initiative to encourage entrepreneurship. it is intended to make our young people understand that it is not necessary that they become employees in the public administration, the police or the armed forces, but that they can highlight their skills and talents - of course with aid, incentives, venture capital and start-ups and financing of all kinds possible - so that they can become entrepreneurs and, therefore, play their own future.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, preventing relocation is one of our main political objectives: that is why we are launching a series of growth missions - to try to ensure that our companies do not relocate but can explore, also from an industrial point of view, new markets and have opportunities for economic returns. i also believe that, as things stand, we have already set ourselves some very ambitious and important objectives. our whole industrial policy - the third industrial revolution we are fighting for - is and must be a leading player in the fight against climate change. it is no coincidence that jeremy rifkin was one of the protagonists of the event, with which we began to launch this strategy to re-industrialize europe. but the ambitious targets we have are certainly those of a 20% reduction in co2 emissions, with all the initiatives that can be taken, and the text of the commission's communication on the reindustrialisation of europe speaks of eco-friendly buildings and vehicles and the green economy. but it is obvious that the objectives to be set must be achievable. if we ask industry, at a time when there is no global agreement to reduce co2 emissions, to pursue objectives which they cannot achieve, we risk relocating industries, which will worsen the climate change situation. in fact, forcing our companies to go beyond the borders of the european union is to encourage them not to comply with our rules, because producing in countries around the world where there are no very strict rules on co2 emissions is to have a bad environmental policy. so i think that the demand for achievable targets is the best way of reconciling a correct, modern industrial policy, different from the industrial policy of the past, with a commitment to achievable and serious targets in the common action we all take to combat climate change.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, if we want to have more european and extra-european investment for a modern and competitive industrial policy which is environmentally friendly, we must of course provide legal certainty but also political certainty. the commission's decision which will be submitted to the council - and i hope that parliament will share this approach - is precisely to focus on a modern model of reindustrialisation. after many years of choices that have favoured one part of the economy - i am referring to the financial sector - europe is now setting itself, through the commission, the objective of 20% of gross domestic product by 2020 coming from the real economy. this is already a political and legal certainty, because it is included in an official text of the european commission. i also believe that an important message in terms of legal certainty, and therefore a guarantee for all those who want to invest, is represented by the directive on late payment by public administrations, which was approved thanks to the strong commitment of parliament and which will enter into force in all the countries of the union by march 2013 at the latest. three countries - cyprus, malta and italy - have already implemented it, and this decisive action by the european institutions is certainly a political and legal message which will, in my view, encourage european and non-european investment in the industrial and business sectors.
commissioner, i very much appreciate the work you are doing with your colleague mr andor. i think, and not just now, that it is very important to defend the system of production of goods and services in this part of the world: it's part of our history and our identity. of course, we must think of a modern production structure and reindustrialisation which selects some sectors and considers others objectively no longer viable. however, it is very important that, in order to revive industrial activity, action be taken on infrastructure, which is particularly lacking in some european countries. i think of the heavier ones - roads, airports and railways - but i also think of the system of energy production and use, which for many activities, even modern ones, matters a lot. i would also add to this a direct commitment to knowledge: innovation comes from there, from how much we invest in knowledge, research and innovation. i think these are the most important guidelines and i would like to know what your opinion is on this.

mr president, the brussels i regulation has undoubtedly been one of the most effective acts of union legislation, as it laid the foundations for a european judicial area and promoted legal certainty among european citizens. the recast of this regulation touches on issues which are fundamental to the development of european justice, including the extension of the rules on jurisdiction for disputes, with possible domiciles in third countries, and agreements on the choice of the competent forum. i am convinced that the adoption of the new regulation will ensure stronger consumer protection and greater legal certainty within the internal market, and that is why i voted in favour.
mr president, we all know how important it is to guarantee the safety of citizens within the member states. the proposal under consideration, for which i voted in favour, is aimed at reducing the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks by limiting the access of ordinary citizens to those chemicals in high concentrations which are commonly used and which can also be used to make explosives. in this respect, i consider it very interesting that the obligation to report suspicious transactions in these substances should be introduced, bearing in mind that the volumes covered by the proposal, which is addressed to wholesalers, retailers and member states, are modest compared to the total quantities sold.
mr president, with this report the european parliament is taking note of the rapid changes taking place in the consumer credit market, because the financial crisis is also a credit crisis and a sharp contraction in loans and mortgages to households is reflected in businesses and the whole economic system. if the commission can take action to increase access to crossborder credit, which is currently too low and represents only 2% of the community total, many europeans who are unable to obtain credit in their own country because of the difficulties of that country's system could find it in that of other member states and this would therefore guarantee the effectiveness of that single market for which the european institutions are fighting for its full implementation and overcoming national limits.
mr president, i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, which makes it possible to take an important step forward in the current debate on the recovery of the economies of the individual member states. while the priority is to repair the state budget, targeted social investment is also needed to prepare individuals, households and businesses for changes in economic conditions and labour market requirements. in addition to the sustainability of public finances, member states need to focus on how to create sustainable and quality employment, how to invest in training and further education, and how to combat poverty and social exclusion. this is why we need, and perhaps urgently need, a coordinated approach to social investment and, consequently, a social investment pact of european significance.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report because i have followed its progress very closely and i think the rapporteur has done a very good job both from a technical point of view, given his ability to get to the heart of such a complex and articulated dossier, but also from a political point of view, in submitting this final text to us after countless discussions and readings. i also think that the advanced braking system, i.e. the cbs or abs, is a good thing, particularly for safeguarding the production cycles of companies, and that greater safety has therefore been achieved, which is one of our main objectives, while taking into account the technological and performance differences and the costs of the different subcategories of motorcycles. the study on environmental issues for the 2020 phase is also commendable, as it allows the regulation to keep up with the latest technological developments. finally, i am pleased to emphasize the market surveillance aspect, so congratulations again to the rapporteur.
mr president, this proposal for a regulation aims to simplify the current regulatory framework and to introduce new administrative and technical requirements for the type approval of new l-category vehicles, which currently number some 30 million in europe. to date, the 2002 framework directive and 14 related directives have regulated the matter: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the report also provides for the introduction of more appropriate subcategories, stricter emission limits, the mandatory introduction of anti-lock systems on certain types of vehicle, and an automatic lighting system to improve the visibility of l-category vehicles. the advantages which will result in terms of safety, environmental protection and the better functioning of the internal market are undeniable and that is why i voted in favour of it.
mr president, i congratulate the rapporteur, mr panzeri, on this important achievement, which is to deliver a regulation which will have a significant impact on the market for agricultural and forestry vehicles. firstly, the simplification it produces, because the instrument of the regulation will replace as many as 24 existing directives and will make it possible to achieve effective harmonization in the member states, through direct effect in national legislation. moreover, common technical requirements for these vehicles at european level will also improve market competitiveness. the introduction of new technologies, including anti-lock braking systems and electronic stability control systems, will therefore help to improve the safety of these vehicles. as rapporteur for the previous european standardisation regulation, i think it is very appropriate that the technical services and the procedure for their evaluation should be upgraded to standards by means of delegated acts from the commission.
mr president, i express my opinion and vote in favour of the matter under discussion, because the proliferation of means of payment and the spread of the so-called electronic money require a discipline appropriate to the times, combining the drive towards greater openness to the internal market with the need for transparency. in fact, it has been achieved through some positive aspects, which are the fight against money laundering from illicit activities and the fight against tax evasion, which is a negative feature of many member states. but we must proceed in greater detail and i think it is essential to take note of the possible problems caused by multilateral interchange commissions to competitiveness, with costs and surcharges that affect a greater use of this currency. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the application of the competition rules to the internal market.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report because i see in it one of the main technological challenges of the coming years: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. so the use of mobile phones as a means of payment is already taking hold in other parts of the world, particularly where banks have not yet had time to set up a network of cash-out desks. in europe, such technologies would allow traceability, thereby better combating both theft and fraud, and at the same time help to consolidate the internal market by making cross-border payments easier even in areas with different currencies. particular attention is rightly paid to safety, standard-setting and interdependence. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the consumer is not left behind.
mr president, i voted in favour of this dossier in the costa report, in disagreement with my group, and i wanted to state that the reason why i voted in favour of this dossier is that i believe that the issues relating to the active fight against threats to children from the digital world are predominant in this dossier. child protection is an emergency in a technologically evolving world where the family, the school, the education system do not always resort to safeguards to prevent harmful effects. there is a lot to be done, but the positive aspects of this dossier are what made me vote in favour.
mr president, i congratulate mrs costa on her excellent work and on her timing in bringing this very sensitive subject to the table. more than ever, new technologies are putting the security of personal data at risk, especially when you are not fully aware of the consequences of sharing certain information. those who are both more exposed to such technologies and often less mature in their use are more likely to make mistakes. clearly, more and better education is part of the overall design of increasing protection but at the same time the fight against illegal and harmful content is largely part of the tools to be used in order to reduce the risks associated with digital citizenship of children.
mr president, i welcome the text adopted today, which builds on the commission's 2011 communication on the social entrepreneurship initiative. we are facing the europe 2020 strategy, which will have to respond to the growing need for social services, for example in the health and nursing sectors, and assess the demographic trend we are facing. but the new phrase will have to be accompanied by a high degree of innovation and experimentation, the success or failure of which will have to be assessed by the european institutions at certain times, so as to see whether this first approach can allow for improvement or optimisation and continue effectively with long-term development in this type of entrepreneurship. we must bear in mind that we are dealing with a particular nature in this type of business, which must combine economic growth with solidarity, and that is why i am in favour of this constructive approach being a fundamental pillar of a new society, which recovers the meaning and value of work in which man is at the centre of society in a new integral humanism.
mr president, i voted in favour of mr becker's report, which provides a better picture of the contribution of social enterprises to the resolution of the current crises. unfortunately, social entrepreneurship is often seen as a sort of appendage to the classic forms of entrepreneurship based solely on maximising profit. on the contrary, social enterprises play a key role in the development of european markets and the economy: they provide innovative responses to economic, social and environmental challenges through sustainable development, social inclusion and territorial cohesion. i therefore support the idea of setting up a fund for social enterprises, which would meet the main objective of not exposing these enterprises to uncontrolled competition, ensuring adequate financial support for them and facilitating their integration into the markets.
in writing. - i support the report by mr zwiefka analysing the commission proposal to update council regulation (ec) no 44/2001 of 22 december 2001 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, also known as 'brussels i'. the report not only proposes changes to strengthen the effectiveness of arbitration conventions within the member states and to avoid parallel judicial and arbitration proceedings, but also reiterates a firmly opposed position to all those unfair procedural practices which have been highlighted by the studies carried out by the commission in this regard.
in writing. - we welcome the revision of this regulation, which is today one of the most effective acts of community legislation, since it definitively lays the foundations for a european judicial area, to the benefit of citizens and businesses, and aims to promote legal certainty and the predictability of decisions. among other things, we support the abolition of the exequatur, as proposed by the commission, considering that a decision enforceable in the member state of origin is enforceable and enforced anywhere in the eu upon presentation of an authentic copy and a certificate in the prescribed form issued by the court of origin, without any intermediate procedure. the abolition of the exequatur for all decisions in civil and commercial matters therefore represents a significant step forward in access to justice for citizens and businesses. finally, we consider it necessary to consider whether the rules of this regulation should be extended in the near future. we believe that in the meantime we must have wide consultations and a wide political debate. at the present stage, we propose to include in the regulation rules aimed at introducing only a partial retroactive effect for disputes in the context of insurance contracts.
in writing. the zwiefka report on the revision of the regulation on the recognition of judgments in civil and commercial matters is a courageous and worthy step forward from the commission's proposal. the premise is that the implementation of judicial cooperation between states is a necessary prerequisite for promoting the internal market. it is not possible to support the european common space if there is no coherence between the exercise of a right and its protection. the parliament's proposal to overcome once and for all the costly and time-consuming obstacle of the delict procedure for the enforcement in one state of a judgment given in another state is a significant act of responsibility in the building of the union. this was done with great skill and without neglecting the respect of the fundamental guarantees. the report proposes to abolish the judgment of delict, while retaining the control of the right to cross-examine, the principle of the formal judge and the fundamental principles of the order in which the judgment is to be enforced. the one illustrated by mr zwiefka is the way forward and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - the recasting of the regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, known as the 'brussels i' regulation, is a very important basis for the development of the single european legislation. i consider the text to be a great opening up of national legislation towards a single system capable of giving european law its practical expression by giving it effectiveness and certainty through a broad management of competences at international level. this is the way forward for the implementation of a faster, more dynamic and comparative european law, which can assist citizens in the various cases.
in writing. − whereas regulation no 44/2001 laid the foundations for a european judicial area, has proved useful for citizens and businesses, promoting legal certainty and predictability of decisions, and is used as a reference and basic instrument for other acts. the recasting of this regulation is therefore extremely important as it also eliminates some of the difficulties encountered in this area over the last ten years. bearing in mind that the abolition of exequatur for all decisions in civil and commercial matters represents a significant advance in access to justice for citizens and businesses, and stressing the need to improve the effectiveness of arbitration conventions in order to give full effect to the will of the parties, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr zwiefka's report because i believe that legal cooperation in civil and commercial matters is a fundamental legal basis for the objective of strengthening the single market. the importance of this regulation lies in the fact that, by laying down provisions in civil and commercial matters at community level, it establishes with certainty which court has jurisdiction to hear and determine crossborder disputes. in addition, another positive aspect of the report is the decision to maintain safeguards for the rights of defendants and consumers, in the name of the principle of the weaker party.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr mulder's report, which seeks to regulate the placing on the market of explosives precursors. explosive precursors are all those chemicals which have been sold freely and which, when skillfully mixed, make it possible to manufacture homemade explosive devices, often used in terrorist attacks. these substances are currently available to european consumers in a number of ways. the report therefore aims to harmonise existing legislation on the subject by providing that consumers will be able to buy products with chemical concentrations below certain thresholds for domestic use without restrictions, while purchasers requiring higher concentrations will be issued special purchase licences and will be kept in specific registers to record their purchases.
in writing. - the regulation of trade and use of explosives precursors requires the adoption of a series of concrete measures aimed at a clearer delimitation of the safety limits that exist today. that is why i supported mr mulder's report. in the light of serious tragic events, such as the massacre in oslo, the need to make it increasingly difficult to obtain explosives is urgent. i therefore believe that some of the proposed changes, such as the ban on the public's buying of 15 types of explosives, are moving in the right direction, and can better define the boundaries of a subject which must be given the utmost attention.
in writing. − citizens' security and the prevention and fight against terrorism must also be taken into account from a legislative point of view. the control and/or prohibition of the purchase of substances considered dangerous because they may be used as components in the manufacture of handmade weapons does not mean restricting the freedom of consumers but ensuring their safety by making the market for these products transparent. the regulation i voted for aims to restrict public access to certain chemicals by using a system of traceability and/or registration of purchase. the member states will have to adapt to the market conditions imposed by the legislation.
in writing. − considering that certain commonly and widely used chemicals can also be misused as precursors to explosives, it is necessary to restrict public access to them in order to reduce the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks. agreeing on the list of eight substances (and mixtures thereof) in annex i to the proposed regulation for which the controls set out therein are mandatory; considering it reasonable to allow the sale of these substances in high concentrations to the public to continue only after obtaining a licence attesting to the legality of the intended end uses; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented.
in writing. - i congratulate my colleague jan mulder on his work. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the dangers of ionizing radiation. through this restriction, parliament wants to hit those terrorist organisations, such as the one it recently hit in norway, which had and still use these substances to carry out attacks against governments and populations. finally, although some products containing these chemicals will continue to be sold without restriction, their distribution will be under strict and careful controls, and everyone from wholesaler to trader will be required to report any 'suspicious transactions' to the competent authorities, for example if a customer purchases a large quantity of a particular product.
in writing. the aim of the legislative proposal on the placing on the market and use of explosives precursors is to reduce public access to 15 highly concentrated chemicals which are dangerous because they are suitable for the manufacture of homemade explosives. i therefore voted in favour of mr mulder's report because i believe that it can help to prevent possible terrorist attacks and is therefore a very important step towards ensuring the safety of citizens. in concrete terms, i think it is important that, for certain categories of substances, access to the public be authorized through the establishment of a licensing system, harmonized at european level, while, for other categories, it is necessary that such access be accompanied by a report and the traceability of suspicious transactions.
in writing. - i consider it a priority to restrict public access to certain substances which are commonly used but whose improper use could affect public safety. in fact, some freely available substances could be used as precursors to explosives. in order to protect the free movement of goods, it will be necessary to ensure that these substances can be marketed but their sale must be subject to strict regulation. the reduction in sales volumes will be minimal and will be sufficient to ensure that the rationale behind this decision, namely the fight against terrorism, is respected. this can be achieved by a framework of controls which prevent sales in high concentrations and allow a check on the legality of the end use. for the reasons i have just given, i am voting in favour.

in writing. − following the discovery of new fossil fuel deposits in the mediterranean sea, offshore activities in the area are likely to increase in the coming years, and should therefore be regulated. it is important to adopt a body of laws governing the exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf, the seabed and its subsoil, which guarantee safety and protect the environment. the european parliament has expressed its opinion on the 'offshore protocol' under the 'barcelona convention'. today's vote once again demonstrates the will to build an ever more secure and 'green' europe.
in writing. − the offshore protocol against pollution resulting from exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf and the seabed of the mediterranean sea is an important part of the barcelona convention which serves to help a number of member states in the eu. this protocol allows for international cooperation in regard to oil and gas exploitation in the mediterranean sea, establishing requirements for exploration and technology which will improve the safety of these processes and help to safeguard against any negative environmental impact. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the recommendation ms rosbach made on the accession of the eu to the protocol for the protection of the mediterranean sea.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the accession of the european union to the protocol on the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution resulting from exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf, the sea bed and its subsoil. the protocol entered into force on 24 march 2011 following its ratification by six contracting parties (albania, tunisia, morocco, libya, cyprus and syria) and has not yet been signed or ratified by the union. as offshore activities are expected to increase following the discovery of new fossil fuel deposits in the mediterranean, a possible accident could have immediate effects on a large scale. for this reason, i believe that the eu's ratification of the offshore protocol would be an important element in ensuring a good level of cooperation and a constant, concrete commitment by all mediterranean countries to achieving the highest possible level of safety for offshore activities.
in writing. − the need for greater safety of offshore activities in the hydrocarbon sector has been dramatically highlighted by recent accidents, in particular the deepwater horizon oil spill in the gulf of mexico in 2010. considering that offshore activities in the mediterranean are set to increase following the discovery of new fossil fuel deposits and that such an incident could have immediate effects on a large scale on a semi-enclosed sea such as the mediterranean, with deleterious consequences for its economy and fragile ecosystems, and undermine the efforts made by the member states bordering the mediterranean to achieve and maintain good environmental conditions in their marine waters, there is a clear need for the sustainable management of offshore activities in the field of hydrocarbons. i also hope that the eu will promote international cooperation to improve offshore safety, and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − i am in favour of the report on the 'offshore protocol' as i believe that it is necessary to ensure greater safety of offshore activities in the hydrocarbon sector, especially following the dramatic incident in the gulf of mexico in 2010. offshore activities in the mediterranean are set to increase following the discovery of new fossil fuel deposits and such an incident could have immediate effects on a large scale on a semi-enclosed sea such as the mediterranean, with deleterious consequences for its economy and fragile ecosystems, and undermine the efforts of the member states bordering the mediterranean to achieve and maintain good environmental conditions in their marine waters, as required by the marine strategy framework directive. given the importance of this protocol with regard to exploration and exploitation activities in the mediterranean, the disposal of hazardous waste and the removal of disused installations, i hope that it will be respected and implemented with provisions on safety and monitoring.

in writing. - i am very pleased that the house voted in favour of the 'protocol on the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution resulting from exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf, the seabed and its subsoil'. the protocol governs exploration and exploitation activities, the granting of authorizations, the removal of installations and the provisions relating to safety in the mediterranean. a protocol is necessary because the management of these activities is not just a matter for the european union but also for all the countries bordering the mediterranean. after the gulf of mexico disaster in 2012, we are all aware that if a disaster like this were to occur in the mediterranean, the consequences could be devastating. the mediterranean is not only a virtually enclosed sea, but also a unique marine ecosystem in terms of its size and diversity. the mediterranean is also a source of economic prosperity for many countries, which live off tourism and the sustainable exploitation of its coasts. we must therefore ensure that tourism and this very fragile ecosystem are best protected by ensuring a good level of cooperation between mediterranean countries in order to achieve the highest possible level of safety for offshore activities. i hope that in future the european parliament will be able to promote a new and even more stringent legislative initiative on this subject.

in writing. - i support the collin-langen report, which aimed to assess the state of implementation of the consumer credit directive 2008/48/ec in order to protect consumers and strengthen the internal market for cross-border consumer credit. the report stresses certain objective factors which make it difficult to implement the directive in the legal systems of the individual member states, such as the very short transposition period, the broad scope of the directive and the need to take account of the reality of individual national economic, social and budgetary situations, which are often different or even completely opposite; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. finally, the report does not fail to focus on consumer rights and the effects of the economic crisis on individuals and households across europe.

in writing. - the final harmonization of certain essential aspects of credit law has already undoubtedly made it possible to raise the level of consumer protection in europe considerably. however, the increase in cross-border consumer credit appears to be insignificant, due to the fact that only a few financial institutions offer cross-border consumer credit and that in recent years, due to the financial market crisis, the market has experienced a general decline. in highlighting the importance of verifying the transposition of the directive by the commission and its proper application in the member states, and of a thorough assessment of the impact of the directive on the legal and practical level, and then, if necessary, proposing amendments to the directive on that basis, i am voting in favour of the proposal.

in writing. − in a time of economic crisis in europe, it is necessary to impose a high level of consumer protection and to strengthen the internal market in crossborder consumer credit. the vote will achieve both of these objectives by harmonizing certain essential aspects of credit law, which have undoubtedly made it possible to raise the level of consumer protection in europe considerably. in 2011, the commission verified 562 websites related to consumer credit. the results showed that 46% of the websites checked lacked mandatory information in the advertising, 43% of them lacked clear information in the offer regarding the total costs, the duration of the contract as well as some credit-related costs, and 20% of them had misleading cost presentation. the transparency and clarity of consumer credit advertising should also be ensured.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs collin-langen's text, which has two objectives: a high level of consumer protection and the strengthening of the internal cross-border market in consumer credit. the final harmonization of certain essential aspects of credit law has undoubtedly made it possible to raise the level of consumer protection in europe considerably. the increase in crossborder consumer credit appears to be insignificant, however. this could be due to the fact that only a few financial institutions offer cross-border consumer credit and that in recent years, due to the financial market crisis, the market has seen a general decline. moreover, the factors hindering cross-border consumer credit are more due to language problems or lack of personal contact with the financial institution than to the legal framework.
in writing. - i abstained in the vote on the own-initiative report by mrs jazłowiecka on the 'social investment pact' because, although it is a document denouncing the deep economic, social and employment crisis affecting europe, while identifying shared objectives on which to act such as the fight against youth unemployment, coordination between the academic and the labour market, the creation of more stable pension models, support for smes, it is resolved by focusing on the scenario analysis without proposing convincing recovery actions useful in pursuing the proposed objectives.
in writing. − the crisis has long-term effects on the employment rate, public saving and social investment in europe. most responses to the crisis are short-term, and aim to restore sustainability; however, it is worth looking a little further: we must not ignore the negative effects that austerity measures can have on employment and competitiveness. that is why action is needed to promote employment and to encourage targeted social investment.
in writing. − we are going through a period of severe economic crisis, which requires great efforts both in terms of social and political cohesion. the unemployment rate, especially among young people, the difficulties of access to credit for small and mediumsized enterprises and the level of competitiveness of our companies are some of the crucial points on which action must be taken as soon as possible if we are to find a way out of the crisis together. the text in question, for which i voted in favour, aims to indicate some possible solutions to the problem. it calls for joint and coherent eu action to make effective the efforts demanded of european citizens by national governments. i believe, however, that all these legislative proposals cannot be properly implemented unless we proceed with the adoption of an appropriate multiannual financial framework aimed at implementing growth and employment in the eu. i hope that the negotiations between the member states will soon take a positive turn for the european recovery.
in writing. − the current economic and financial crisis is certain to have significant long-term effects not only on the european economy but also on the employment rate, public saving and social investment in europe. we believe it is essential to respond to these major challenges with well-targeted social investment. in addition to ensuring the sustainability of public finances, member states must now focus equally on productivity, the distribution of labour, and education and training. social investment is important to restore a proper level of employment and to improve europe's competitiveness: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. it is therefore urgent to create a coordinated eu approach: calls on the member states to sign a 'social investment pact' which will enable a better governance and control mechanism to be set up for the implementation of the employment, social and education objectives of europe 2020. we call on the commission and the council to ensure that the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, currently under discussion, contains the necessary budgetary resources for social investment in europe.
in writing. − small and medium-sized enterprises have a great potential for job creation and play a crucial role in the transition to a new sustainable economy. it is necessary to urge the commission to take all possible measures to encourage and assist member states to sign the 'social investment pact' and to introduce the evaluation of employment, social and education objectives in the european semester 2013. my vote is in favour.

in writing. − most recent and current responses to the crisis are based on short-term objectives, aimed primarily at restoring the sustainability of public finances, which is crucial for the eu economy. however, the current economic and financial crisis is certain to have significant long-term effects not only on the european economy but also on the employment rate, public saving and social investment in europe. it is therefore necessary to complement these austerity measures with measures aimed at promoting employment, such as targeted social investment, which prepare individuals, households and societies to adapt to the various transformations and to manage their transition to more flexible labour markets. in stressing the importance of social investment as a policy-encompassing instrument and as a means of restoring a suitable level of employment in the future and improving europe's competitiveness, i am voting in favour of the proposal.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this important resolution because i share its spirit and objectives. the european art and antiques market has a significant impact on the global market. it therefore deserves our utmost attention and protection, especially in the face of increasing competition from third countries. i was particularly struck by the impressive rise of china in this sector and the shift in the centre of gravity of the art market to emerging countries. i therefore believe that europe must make every effort to strengthen the european market and the european position on the world stage. as regards, in particular, the right of succession, i think it is right and proper that artists should be able to receive continuous remuneration for their works of art over time, especially for younger artists, who very often sell their works at a low price at the beginning of their career in order to make themselves known. moreover, this right does not adversely affect the market or the location of the market. finally, the provision of a copyright on a work of art on subsequent sales of the original can reasonably be a valid instrument to avoid discrimination against the artists themselves and i consider its introduction into the legal systems of several third countries to be a positive factor.
in writing. - the subject of intellectual property rights is certainly complex and raises questions of undoubted relevance to the protection of the rights of artists, all the more so in the context of an expanding and increasingly globalised sector. this directive sets out the rules governing the 'right of succession', that is to say, the right of the author of a work of art to the subsequent sales of the original. this is a very delicate issue and raises a number of problems, especially in relation to those who are at the lower end of the market and who are therefore harmed by the costs of administering the right itself. i share the rapporteur's call for the protection and safeguarding of young artists entering the market, who certainly need greater guarantees to be competitive.

in writing. the directive on the right of the author of a work of art to the resale of the original (hereinafter referred to as the 'right') was designed with the dual objective of ensuring that authors of graphic and plastic works of art have an economic share in the success of their creations and of harmonising the application of this right in the european union. however, in reality, the quality of the administration of the resale right varies from one member state to another and, as a result, the burden may be particularly heavy for those at the lower end of the market, who are most affected by the costs of administration of the right. furthermore, considering that the right of retention has no negative impact on the location of the art market or on the level of turnover, and wishing for greater cooperation by the commission with the parties concerned to strengthen the position of the european art market, i am voting in favour of the proposal.

in writing. − given the economic context in which we operate and the many commitments made by parliament in the 2012 budgetary procedure, it seems correct and appropriate to limit the use of the dual translation system as being excessively costly and not indispensable. in fact, an audio-visual recording of the discussions is provided with real-time interpretation in all languages. article 181 now provides for a full report of the discussions in all languages. such a practice requires four months' work and does not require remuneration for the interpreters involved. in the light of the amendment to rule 181, the full report will continue to exist in the form of a multilingual document in which the speeches are transcribed in the original language and translated only into english, so as to economize the de quo procedure without in the least impairing the final objective. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal in the light of what i have said here in summary.

in writing. - today we have given the green light to new rules that will make motorcycles safer and greener. from 2016, the rules will have to apply to all two- or three-wheeled motor vehicles, from mopeds to the most powerful motorcycles. these vehicles are involved in 16% of the fatalities on european roads, although they account for only 2% of road traffic, and that is why we have approved stricter safety requirements, as well as imposing stricter targets to reduce polluting emissions. of course, the responsibility for safe motorcycling lies primarily with the rider, but there is always some scope for making these vehicles safer and cleaner. among the new rules to make motorcycles safer is the requirement for motorcycles over 125 cc to have the anti-lock braking system (abs), while the abs or a full braking system (cbs) can be adapted to less powerful versions (under 125 cc), including scooters.

in writing. − the 2008 crisis, which has taken on a global dimension, started with financial services, whose weaknesses it has revealed. these include regulatory gaps, ineffective supervision, opaque markets and overly complex products. the international response was coordinated through the g20 and the financial stability board. in particular, the g20 deliberated on a whole range of regulatory measures aimed at making the financial system safer and more sustainable. since then, among a multitude of other measures, capital requirements for financial institutions have been strengthened, a first step towards stricter regulation of credit rating agencies has been taken and a new financial supervisory architecture has been developed. however, in my view, despite these new regulatory frameworks, a considerable part of credit intermediation is still not sufficiently supervised and regulated. i agree with the rapporteur that activities in the shadow banking system can have a positive effect on the economy by contributing to a greater allocation of risks outside the traditional banking sector, but only if this is done in the presence of a situation of transparency in the financial transactions market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which aims to clarify the so-called shadow banking system. these are entities and bodies that operate in parallel and sometimes in an obscure manner to the traditional and more regulated financial markets. the shadow banking system was estimated to have a worldwide turnover of some eur 50 trillion last year, a frightening figure and a considerable increase over previous years: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial markets are not affected by the crisis. the report therefore aims to monitor these activities better, and the implications and interconnections with the 'official' system. the financial crisis has been at the root of this crisis, which has also affected the real economy and industry, and it is therefore right and proper to take all the measures that can lead to greater transparency and regulation in this sector, which is so important, but which cannot and must not lead to the ruin of all citizens.
in writing. the global crisis we are in began when the market realised that mortgage securitisation was subject to incentives which led to a lowering of lending standards, the so-called subprime mortgages. in view of what has happened, it is increasingly important to make the connection between traditional banks and the shadow banking system transparent in order to counter this relationship from a regulatory point of view. therefore, in order to have a complete picture of the shadow banking system, it is essential to obtain complete and reliable data on it. indeed, some aspects of the shadow system may have beneficial effects on the real economy, while others may lead to dramatic situations and high systemic risk. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal in the light of what i have said here in summary.
in writing. - when we talk about shadow banking, we are talking about a system of credit intermediation that allows the transit of money without rules and outside the boundaries of traditional banking channels, a system that is growing at the rate of 6 trillion dollars a year. the operations of this system are blamed for many of the causes of the crisis that brought the world financial system to its knees. i believe that we need a regulatory framework to prevent dangerous practices. it is our duty to evaluate the advisability of new and profound changes which will make up for the lack of transparency and clear rules. the regulation and supervision of credit assets in the so-called 'shadow banking system' will help to prevent the risk of future crises and ensure financial stability. given the need to define the application of this parallel system and to identify the risks involved, i am voting in favour.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president-in-office of the council, i would like us to recover our awareness of what the budget of the european union is. the budget of the european union is not an additional budget to the budgets of the member states, because otherwise we would continue to conduct this debate with a fundamental misunderstanding, which risks disintegrating our efforts. the budget of the european union is a synthetic budget, which aims to multiply the effects of the investments made by the member states through the european budget. in this sense, it is to create more efficiency and more effectiveness. so every dollar taken from the budget of the european union increases the public expenditure of the member states, and this is the principle on which we are building the european union. if the european union is an entity which is added to the member states, as today the european union embassy in the various non-european countries is added to those of the member states, we are perpetuating the misunderstanding. so to think that by cutting back on the european union budget we are contributing to savings and to a general austerity is an unforgivable mistake. we, on the other hand, through the budget of the european union, allow the member states to save money, and thus reduce expenditure and encourage austerity. if we do not have this perception, because in relation to national public opinion each state has to justify its soft nationalism, the result is that we will always have the problem of reducing the budget of the european union and we will always have as the final outcome the problem of increasing the budget of the individual national states. in the end, these 140 billion will be spent by the national states anyway: but they will spend it by reducing efficiency, because the commission's studies already tell us that one euro makes 95 cents in the budget of the european union, but 50 cents when it is spent by the national states.
