in writing. - the draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the state of israel amending the annexes to protocols 1 and 2 to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the state of israel, of the other part, relates to a series of agreements between the various international actors on reciprocal liberalisation measures. these measures have enabled trade in agricultural products, processed agricultural products and fish and fishery products with certain mediterranean countries to be further liberalized. i believe that the amendment of the protocols under discussion can give greater weight to the areas under negotiation, giving greater weight to both traditional sectors and new commodity sectors. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i supported the report by mrs vaidere on the eu-russia agreement on the administration of tariff quotas for timber exports. following russia's accession to the world trade federation, a number of agreements and legislative adjustments between the eu and russia have become necessary, such as the reduction of export duties on raw timber, and the management by the eu of its share of the tariff quotas allocated to it. european companies, particularly those in the building and paper furniture sectors, will greatly benefit from this measure.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. it is important to avoid a repeat of the successive increases in timber export duties applied by russia since 2007 that affected many european producers. i hope that the agreement will be approved, because it will bring more predictability and better trading conditions.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs vaidere on her work. with the approval of this text by parliament, in view of the proposal for a council decision (16775/2011), european timber industries, including those supplying raw material to construction and paper mills, will import fir and pine from russia at reduced prices. in fact, given the reduction in customs duties for these types of wood by russia, the eu took the opportunity to conclude a trade agreement with that country, which will save member states' industries almost 70% compared to the past. the conclusion of this agreement will greatly benefit the industry in finland, latvia, lithuania, estonia, sweden, germany and poland, which had seen their imports blocked following the 80% increase in customs tariffs by russia in 2007. in italy, however, the furniture and furnishing industries will benefit the most from the reduction in the cost of raw materials.
in writing. - mr president, the russian federation has agreed to reduce its current export duties on raw materials, including wood products. for certain types of wood, in particular certain species of conifers, russia has introduced tariff quotas. for the quantities exported from russia that are within the quotas, the export duties are lower, for the products that are not within the quotas, the rates are higher, if not prohibitive. the european union aims to significantly improve the supply of timber from russia. the european union will thus undertake to administer quota authorisations, while the russian federation will retain the right to issue export licences on the basis of the relevant import documents issued by the european union.
in writing. − in the context of its wto accession process, the russian federation has agreed to reduce its current export duties on raw materials, including wood products. for certain types of wood, in particular certain species of conifers, russia has introduced tariff quotas. the quantities exported by russia under the quotas are subject to the lowest export duties; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the quota system is maintained. a specific part of the quotas has been allocated to exports to the eu: the quotas were set at a relatively high level for the eu, at least in relation to the demand expected in the short term. the bilateral agreement lays down the general provisions for the application of the tariff quota part. while the eu will manage the quota authorisations, the russian federation will retain the right to issue export licences on the basis of the relevant import documents issued by the eu.
in writing. − the schengen information system is the largest integrated database, designed to improve police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters and policy on visas, immigration and the free movement of persons. sis ii represents a significant advance in the system, allowing the introduction of new data, indications and functionalities which must, however, be protected and controlled. it is important that the timetable is respected, that no further delays are avoided, and that the second generation system is finally operational. i share mr coelho's disappointment that, although the sis is a very important issue for the citizens of the european union, the european parliament has been given a purely advisory role.
in writing. − sis ii, unlike sis 1+, is not a simple information system, but will be used as a means of police investigation, counter-terrorism and immigration control. in view of the importance of the role played by this system, i therefore consider it appropriate that the united kingdom and ireland also participate in it: my vote will therefore be in favour.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. the sis ii is an essential tool for strengthening the security of the schengen area. we must all work together to end the intergovernmental management of the system and to significantly improve data protection and the fundamental rights of individuals. the sis ii should therefore enter into force as soon as possible.
in writing. - we all know that the schengen information system (sis) is the main instrument for the security of the schengen area and is considered the backbone of a europe without borders and of an area of freedom, security and justice. we are now on the eve of the entry into force of a second generation sis, which will allow for the introduction of new data, new types of alerts and new functions, allowing for increased security and more efficient use of information through the interconnection of alerts. before the new system can be operational, a test is necessary to assess whether sis ii meets all the required technical and functional requirements, as well as the other necessary requirements in terms of stability, responsiveness and performance. i voted in favour because i believe that sis ii can be an essential tool for strengthening the security of the schengen area, putting an end to the intergovernmental management of the system and considerably improving data protection and the fundamental rights of individuals. i hope that sis ii will therefore be able to come into force as soon as possible.
in writing. the objective pursued by the schengen agreements of creating a common european area without internal frontiers in which the free movement of persons, goods, services and capital is ensured has necessitated the introduction of different and stricter rules on judicial and police cooperation. the architecture of the new system will allow for increased security and, through the introduction of new data, will make the collection of information more effective. i believe that the transition from one system to another will make it possible to implement cooperation between the supervisory authorities of the member states more effectively. i believe that this will make it possible to move away from an intergovernmental approach, through the joint management of border controls. i hope that, in view of the need to ensure the protection of data and the fundamental rights of individuals, sis ii will be implemented as soon as possible, and i therefore vote in favour.

in writing. − in its communication entitled 'energy roadmap 2050', the commission underlines that, in the face of declining conventional gas production, europe will have to rely on substantial gas imports, as well as on its own natural gas and shale gas reserves, if any. in recent years, the extraction of so-called 'unconventional' hydrocarbons, including shale gas and oil, has led to an unprecedented transformation of global energy markets: in particular, shale gas increased from 1,4% of the us gas market in 2000 to around 17% in 2011. global gas prices and trade patterns are changing, with clear consequences for the eu. several member states have already authorised exploration for shale gas and are preparing for the extraction phase. i believe that within the energy system shale gas and other sources of unconventional gas can open up new sources of supply for europe. at the same time, there is a need to monitor the practices and regulatory regimes of shale gas extraction in order to make this operation economically viable, and to identify and address concerns about the effects of shale gas extraction on the environment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr sonik's report on the environmental impact of shale gas and oil extraction. estimates of shale gas and oil reserves in the eu identify about 14000 billion mmc recoverable. the fears surrounding the possible environmental impact and repercussions in extraction procedures are well known and have been raised in this report which calls on the commission and the national authorities to pursue specific scientific studies addressing these fears and demonstrating on a scientific, non-biased basis the reality of the facts and the real environmental problems that could result from the application of this type of extraction. the report calls for monitoring of technological developments worldwide with a view to continuously assessing the adequacy and effectiveness of existing legislation. in this respect, due attention should be paid to the experience of north american bodies and regulations where these extractive practices have been tried and tested for over half a century.
in writing. - the vote today will certainly not put an end to the accession debate, because this is a subject which, on the one hand, divides public opinion and, on the other, it is useless to deny that it conceals great interests. while this is a resource that could help ensure energy security and diversification in the medium and long term, making the european union less dependent and at the same time helping to reduce co2 emissions, there are also continuing concerns about the effects of extraction techniques on the environment. the aim is to allow member states to extract shale gas and oil on the basis of the principle of subsidiarity and in compliance with existing environmental legislation.
in writing. − i agree with the request to the commission to present, by the end of 2012, an analysis of the future of the global and european gas market, including the impact of planned gas infrastructure projects, new lng terminals, the impact of shale gas on the us gas market and the impact of any developments in the european union in the shale gas sector on future security of supply and future gas prices.
in writing. − recent technological advances have already given impetus to rapid extraction of unconventional fossil fuels on a commercial scale in many parts of the world. there is still no commercial exploitation in the european union and the potential for reserves and possible impacts on the environment and public health need to be further examined. the exploitation of shale gas is not free from controversy in the european union and worldwide and therefore requires a full analysis of all effects. however, the development and production of shale gas could lower prices by increasing competitiveness, creating jobs, reducing energy imports and improving the union's energy independence. this favourable vote will encourage research into shale gas extraction.
in writing. - i support the report by mrs tzavela, which analyses the industrial, energy and other aspects of shale gas and oil. the presence of shale in our territories is not economically advantageous, whereas in other member states the situation is quite different. the fact that the european parliament is opposed to this, regardless of the will to deepen studies and research in this field, is in favour of dependence on foreign fossil energy sources. the text emphasises that the investments for this sector should be fully covered by the industry which would also bear the costs of any direct or indirect damage by applying the polluter pays principle.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs tzavela on her work. in adopting this document, parliament, in the light of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), in particular article 194, wanted to underline the need for regulation at european level as regards the exploration and exploitation of shale gas and oil. the adoption of a european regulation on the subject, while not affecting the autonomy of the state in the management of these resources, is considered by parliament as a necessary step for the management of all activities related to shale gas. the importance of using environmentally sustainable processes and techniques and the fact that the financing for the construction of the necessary infrastructure must be borne by the sector were also stressed. finally, although even the european commission has concluded that community rules adequately cover the exploration and production of shale gas, the prospect of extending the exploitation of unconventional fossil fuels requires a 'thorough analysis' of community legislation on the issue of fuels.
in writing. - i welcomed the report by mrs tzavela and appreciated the fact that the proposal for a moratorium was rejected. i agree with the recognition of the potential for the development of shale gas and oil in the european union. the wealth of energy resources is an opportunity to be seized, which is essential to transform europe into a major energy power and to strengthen its independence. european countries need more energy sources to break free from dependence on foreign energy supplies. it is therefore essential to look at different sources of energy, including shale gas. the use of this, although not the only solution to our energy needs, would be a huge advantage. we can take the united states experience as a model: in the united states, the use of shale gas has had a significant impact, causing its price to fall to three quarters of a dollar, much less than the price in europe, which is 13/14 dollars. i think, however, that a cautious approach is necessary, as shale gas extraction involves possible environmental risks. we must have a clear view of the situation, weighing the pros and cons, and above all, we must ensure that appropriate controls are in place.
in writing. - according to estimates of shale gas resources in europe, several member states have shale gas and oil reserves, i.e. potentially large local energy resources. to remain competitive and to meet its high need for gas imports, europe must therefore exploit its own shale gas and oil resources. to this end, a stable regulatory framework is essential, both to create an appropriate environment for the gas industries to invest in the necessary infrastructure as well as in research and development, and to prevent any market distortions. as regards environmental and societal impacts, the best way to ensure meaningful and timely participation of local communities is through a mandatory environmental impact assessment, coupled with a high level of transparency and public consultation on proposed shale gas projects, irrespective of their duration and scope.

i prefer to speak of 'political parties' rather than 'political families' - the possible president of the commission, precisely to show the need for the formation of genuine european political parties. this is very important, precisely because it helps to make europe a part of the european electorate. the decline in voter turnout is also largely due to the fact that during the european elections we talk about other things, we do not talk about europe, but about national problems. the european elections are seen only as a check on the internal political settings. we must talk about europe during elections and we must make sure that citizens have a serious and genuine conviction that their vote counts when it comes to european policies. so i think that the commission president's statement is one element that gives the citizens that feeling. there will certainly be much more debate than in europe's past in the next elections, precisely because the economic crisis has brought to light the underlying debate: i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question. so this is what we 're gonna talk about . the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. the third question concerns the composition of the commission, apart from the gender issue: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. this would also serve to give the voting public the feeling that they count something in their vote. in this sense i think the resolution deserves our support.

president of the court of auditors. − madam president, let me first thank the honourable members for their kind words to me and to those working in the court of auditors. rest assured that we do our utmost to contribute to the effort that addresses the key priority we face today: to ensure sound financial management of public finances in the european union. i have been asked whether, if receipts are missing, an auditor can accept a reply of ‘so what?’ i would say probably in some instances the receipts are not there, and you can go to our report and see that we have identified the problem and said there is a missing receipt and we have to draw the consequences. an auditor cannot accept ‘so what?’ as a reply. those responsible, like those in this house, also have a role to play in addressing the underlying courses of the problems. many members have stressed the need to improve from where we are. but we should remember where we were at the beginning of this framework programming period and note where we are today. this shows improvement: what the court is saying is that to make the best use of the funds available, there is scope to use them more efficiently and in a better targeted way. but here, indeed, the national authorities have a key fundamental role to play, because they are the first line of defence in terms of the best use of these funds. of course, if you add complexity because you devolve to national authorities the eligibility conditions for payments to be made, then you may end up with 27 different sets of eligibility conditions. that will certainly lead to complexity. but now, whilst we are addressing the future regulations for the next framework period, we have a golden opportunity to address the causes of the problems. systems are there for a period, so we would not expect that error rates or the most likely error will move from 0 to 10 or from 1 to 100. no: systems are there; if you do not solve the causes of the problems we cannot expect huge changes afterwards. our recommendation, honourable members, is clear: for a long time we have been calling for simpler schemes for using the funds, and for action on defining them and assigning to them clear objectives and cost-effective control systems. we should also aim to be in a position to see whether we want to tolerate the risk of error in some situations. that is a task this house and the council were invited to reflect upon by the court of auditors in 2004. our task, as auditors, is to address the risk areas. this is a matter of priority for us. we draw up clear recommendations for improvements. that is our role and we are doing that as much as we can. we are also aware, mr vaughan, that administrative errors may occur and if they are there they indicate that we have a potentially high risk in the system that will materialise afterwards in quantifiable situations which may put all the money at risk. i fully share the view of mrs gräßle that member states and the commission need to work together to make things revolve when they have a shared responsibility, and i want to reassure mr audy that i have taken good note of his suggestion of the court’s rôle d’alerte. there is scope to make an effort to bring problems to the attention of this house. my colleagues and i will duly consider that request.

in writing. - i am voting in favour of the gróbarczyk report on the regulation of baltic salmon fishing. the text was drawn up only after extensive consultation with all interested parties, fishermen, sport fishermen, institutions and ngos. the current lack of specific controls on recreational fisheries is a focal point, putting endangered species in particular at risk. this text lays down specific and clear rules which will make it possible to unify the principles of control and management of recreational fisheries.
in writing. - considering that this report has been drawn up following a wide consultation of stakeholders and that its purpose is to propose clear rules which will allow the management and control of recreational fisheries to be unified, i shall vote in favour.
in writing. - i believe that the proposal for a multiannual plan for the baltic salmon stock and the fisheries exploiting that stock can bring about significant improvements in the management of the baltic salmon fishery. the proposed amendments will strengthen controls by increasing reporting requirements and imposing a minimum landing size of 65 cm for both salmon and sea trout. this is aimed at protecting salmon breeding populations which have experienced a sharp reduction in relative volumes. particular attention should be paid to recreational fishing, which needs to be properly monitored in order to reduce its impact on the stock level. i believe that urgent action is needed to prevent the rapid increase in unreported catches. by voting in favour, i express my will to take concrete action to promote sustainable fishing by applying new, clear and transparent rules.
in writing. the multiannual plan for the protection of baltic salmon is a key element of fisheries stock management in the context of the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). the report by mr grobarczyk examines various issues concerning the protection of salmon in the baltic, including the breeding of the species concerned, sport fishing, artisanal fishing, catch controls and the impact of predators. the commission, in its proposal, delegates to the member states the regulation of certain areas which are considered to fall within the exclusive competence of the union (conservation of marine resources), in effect supporting the decentralisation and regionalisation of the management of the eu fisheries policy.
in writing. - i support the leichtfried report, which contains a package of 10 regulations on commercial policy already in force which need to be brought into line with the provisions of the treaties on delegated and implementing acts. i think it is essential to stress that this text has made it possible to increase parliamentary control, by giving the european commission powers for only five years, obliging it to produce a report on the delegation of acts within nine months of the expiry of the five-year period.
in writing. - the measures contained in the 'trade omnibus ii' package need to be brought into line with the treaty provisions on powers delegated to the european commission. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's trade policy is not distorted by the introduction of new measures. limiting the delegation of powers to the european commission to five years allows for greater parliamentary scrutiny, while the tacit extension of the delegation streamlines the procedure, facilitating the implementation of the common commercial policy. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. the proposal amends certain regulations relating to the common commercial policy as regards the delegation of powers for the adoption of the trade omnibus ii measure. it aims to bring 10 regulations in the field of commercial policy into line with the new provisions of the lisbon treaty and provides for the introduction of delegated acts for the first time in european union law. i am in favour of the circumscription and definition of these delegated acts, which is the european parliament's review.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. this report is necessary to enable the european parliament, as the democratic body of the union, to give full effect to the newly acquired powers and to exercise adequate parliamentary control over the commission, while allowing for flexible, timely and predictable implementation of the common commercial policy.
in writing. - this proposal will make it possible to adapt certain regulations on the common commercial policy to the new provisions of the treaty of lisbon. in this context, i think it is particularly important to confirm the wording of article 290. that provision empowers the legislator to delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general application amending non-essential elements of the legislative act. but the legislator retains the power to veto delegated acts. the aim of this intervention is to strengthen the role of the parliamentary body as the directly elected representative of the eu citizens. wishing to see the implementation of a renewed common commercial policy and the allocation of newly acquired powers to parliament more effectively.
in writing. - the text by mr leichtfried aims to bring the procedures of trade regulations, which were issued before the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, into line with the new system of delegated or implementing acts. i voted in favour of this because i think it is right to allow the european parliament, as the directly elected representative of the eu citizens, to give full effect to the newly acquired powers and to exercise adequate parliamentary control over the executive, while allowing for flexible, timely and predictable implementation of the common commercial policy.
in writing. - in adopting this document, parliament, in the light of the commission's proposal to the european parliament and the council, fully recognises the need for technical measures to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks and the conservation of the ecosystems in which they live. in the design and development of such measures, the need to take into account the continuous evolution of fisheries management, as well as scientific advice, is recognised. it is strongly emphasised that the importance of precise wording is further highlighted by the fact that poorly designed or inappropriate technical measures can lead to unsustainable fishing practices and, in some cases, endanger the lives and safety of fishermen. finally, it was pointed out that technical measures must be carefully designed on a zone-by-zone and case-by-case basis and cannot be considered as general rules applicable in the same way in all member states.
in writing. − the sustainability of fisheries must be ensured by enforcing compliance with technical conservation measures by fishermen throughout the european union. i believe that urgent action is needed to ensure that the current legislation is extended further, as is necessary to achieve the objectives of the common fisheries policy. i can only hope that, in addition to the extension of the validity of the technical measures in force, the adoption of a definitive regulatory framework will be ensured, so that the current framework, which gives rise to repeated abuses, will no longer be temporary. clear technical measures will ensure the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks and the conservation of the ecosystems in which they live, as well as compliance with a number of restrictions necessary to protect the lives and safety of fishermen. i am fully aware of the need for this extension and therefore i am voting in favour, but at the same time i would like to draw attention to the need to work together towards a more complex and effective regulatory framework.
in writing. − technical conservation measures are rules that fishermen throughout the european union are required to respect on a daily basis in their fishing trips, to ensure that fishing is always sustainable, regardless of how and where it is carried out. those measures concern, inter alia, minimum landing sizes, minimum mesh size of nets, no-take zones and periods, limitation of by-catches, criteria for the use of more selective fishing gear and measures to protect the marine environment, and therefore have a significant impact on the achievement of the objectives of the common fisheries policy. in view of the importance of the technical measures instrument in a regional approach to fisheries management, i have expressed my support for mr gallagher's text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs patrão neves because it represents a fundamental breakthrough in ensuring greater regulation of shark fishing. unfortunately, many shark species are being overfished due to increased market demand. to combat this ferocious fishing, it is necessary to impose strict rules requiring all fishing vessels to land in their home port with the bodies of the sharks intact, that is to say with the fins 'naturally attached to the body'. regulating shark fishing is not only a way of respecting the marine ecosystem but also of making the european market sustainable and fair and not just based on the logic of profit.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the barbaric practice of 'pushing' will be banned from the eu once and for all. this decision was considered the only viable one by both the european commission and the envi committee, in order to conserve this animal species and at the same time protect the ecosystem.
in writing. - finning is the most frequently used spinning operation on fishing vessels. drifting kills between 50 and 75 million sharks every year. it is a barbaric practice, permitted for frequent use by an exception provided for by eu legislation in 2003. parliament voted today to put an end to this loophole, namely the possibility of obtaining special fishing permits.
in writing. − the practice of finning, which involves taking shark fins on board fishing vessels and then discarding their bodies at sea, has been officially banned in the european union since 2003. to put a stop to this practice, it would be necessary to introduce an obligation to land sharks with their fins still attached. the mediterranean is now the prey of many fishing vessels engaged in this activity, as it is a sea rich in mako and green sharks, which are at risk of being certified as endangered species. illegal fishing is on the rise in the mediterranean, partly because of the high demand for shark fins and partly because of the high price they fetch. the marine ecosystem is seriously damaged by this unsustainable fishing practice, especially in recent years in the mediterranean sea, where several shark populations have been recorded to be affected by this activity. greater cooperation is needed to combat illicit fishing activities effectively. to make this happen, member states must step up controls both at sea and in ports, preventing the carcasses of sharks from being thrown overboard. the practice of finning therefore needs to be transparent, controlled and, above all, regulated in order to be considered a sustainable and non-invasive fishery.
in writing. - my vote in favour of mrs patrão neves' report expresses my total rejection of the cruelties perpetrated against sharks so far. the lack of adequate transparency in the legislation has in fact given the upper hand to those who have practiced the cutting of shark fins with impunity and then discarded the body in the sea. with today's vote we are calling for the sharks caught to be landed with their fins still attached to their bodies, so that the necessary checks can be carried out and that such barbaric acts by those who i do not think i can call 'fishermen' are discouraged by means of severe penalties, because they would bring into disrepute a category which i believe respects civil law and the marine ecosystem.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because an amendment was adopted which states that the removal of shark fins from fishing vessels, i.e. before landing, is absolutely prohibited: this is necessary to prevent the practice of 'spinning' - the removal of the fins of a shark that is caught and then thrown back into the sea, often still alive, but mutilated and destined to certain death. it is clear that this is an unnecessary barbarism, which does not respect animal life, nature and the environment, and which must therefore be stopped. i would like to point out, however, a worrying incident which took place in the margins of this report, and on which vice-president angelilli was right to speak: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services. i would say that this is a matter for reflection, because often we try to establish rules of protection and guarantee, which are then ignored even within the european parliament itself.
in writing. - i fully supported this vote on the report on the removal of shark fins, also taking into account the suggestions i have received from some ngos concerned with the protection of this marine species. i think that simultaneous landing of shark parts is an entirely inadequate response to the current problems, because unidentified finning activities could still be possible even with strict application of the fin-to-carcass matching, which would still be difficult, costly and laborious. i also think that the proposal to increase the ratio of fin to carcass to 14% of the working weight is an unprecedented indulgence in fining controls (well over 3 times higher than in most countries using the matching system). there is another problem: counting fins and matching them to carcasses in high-volume fisheries would complicate rather than improve enforcement; the traceability is actually much easier through the policy of attached fins. 'independent' control systems are costly and may involve the risk of inaccuracies. the claims made by industrial fishing for possible economic losses appear hasty and superficial and have been subject to minimal external controls, and remain arbitrary and inconsistent.
in writing. - today, at the strasbourg plenary session, we voted on the report by mr patrao neves. many shark species are exposed to heavy exploitation. in recent years, some species have been overfished and are now endangered due to the dramatic increase in demand for derived products, especially fins. the ban, in place since 2003, prohibits the spinning of sharks on board fishing vessels. the resolution adopted today in plenary removes the exceptions, namely those special permits for cutting fins at sea which suspended the ban so as to allow the spinning on vessels that demonstrated their ability to use all parts of the shark. later, the fins and carcasses could be landed in different ports, making it difficult to count accurately and thus to find those who violated the ban by throwing the sharks without fins into the sea.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. today's decision is particularly important in order to fully protect this species, which is very valuable for the marine habitat and is unfortunately at risk of extinction.
in writing. - i believe that the practice of removing shark fins is unacceptable and that action is needed in this context to prevent this practice from being carried out on board fishing vessels. the export of shark fins, also known as 'spinning', is already regulated in the eu, which has banned it but provides for a derogation from the ban whereby 'spinning' can be carried out on board fishing vessels subject to special authorisations. i think that we must reflect on the seriousness of this horrible practice from an environmental point of view, as regards the protection of certain animal species, but also from an economic point of view. in this last respect, in fact, 'spinning' - since it consists of removing the fins of pelagic sharks and then discarding the other parts of the animal's body into the sea - prevents the marketing of a food product. in order to ensure that the interests involved are respected, i shall vote in favour.
in writing. - shark finning is unacceptable both from an environmental point of view, as it threatens the sustainability of some shark species, and from a social and economic point of view, as it involves the waste of a food commodity with commercial value, and from an ethical point of view, as it shows a complete lack of respect for animal life. although this practice has been banned in european waters and for the european fleet since 2003, the commission has decided to present a proposal which also aims to abolish the derogation from the ban on removing shark fins on board union fishing vessels. this proposal will not only further ensure that sharks receive the protection they need, but will also enable the eu to actively contribute to the global effort to eradicate the cruel practice of shark finning in other parts of the world.
in writing. − the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is undoubtedly of great importance because it establishes a system which allows participating states to cooperate in finding a solution to international child abduction. i therefore agree with the content and the requests made to the council in this resolution.
in writing. - i believe that there is an urgent need to clarify the legal situation concerning the international abduction of children by defining jurisdiction and by solving the problem of the law applicable according to the place of residence of the child. i believe that cooperation between states is necessary to solve the problems of international child abduction by accepting the accession of new states to the hague convention by those countries which are already parties to it. i am therefore voting in favour of the report, which calls for the protection of the rights of children to be given priority.
in writing. − the conference will be an opportunity to highlight the importance of safeguarding robust internet services based on the principle of maximum effort, promoting innovation and freedom of expression, ensuring competition and avoiding the creation of a new digital divide.
in writing. - since its adoption in melbourne in 1988, the international telecommunications regulations (itrs) have never been amended. recently, there has been a need to amend the text of the itrs to bring it into line with the radically changed technological, economic and social context. i believe that international regulatory review processes require the widest participation and sharing of all stakeholders: citizens, businesses, associations and public administration. i also believe that when defining the international regulatory environment for the internet and telecommunications, the open, competitive and innovative nature of the internet in the future must be guaranteed, as well as respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, in particular freedom of expression and assembly.
in writing. − as the durban package contains measures that have proved insufficient to deal with the consequences of climate change, i hope that the doha conference will provide a platform for dialogue, leading to the adoption of a legally binding global agreement. the doha conference will have to provide the impetus to ensure that ambitious targets and specific instruments are pursued to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. it is necessary to recognise the urgency of taking concrete measures, taking into account, for example, the positive results achieved by innovations in the field of sustainable energy, which can create jobs, increase growth and address climate change. the next global agreement will be an opportunity to agree on a strengthened action capable of meeting the commitments made, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − i support this report because i value positively the new negotiating approach for future enlargements, which prioritises issues related to the judiciary and fundamental rights, as well as to justice and home affairs. enlargement has been part of the eu agenda since as early as the 1960s and has been a successful process for the eu and europe as a whole. it contributed to peace, stability and prosperity throughout europe. it also enhanced conflict prevention, stimulated reforms and consolidated the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. for these reasons, taking into account both the experience of past enlargements and the new realities created by the economic crises, the moment has come for a re-evaluation of the established related procedures and of enlargement policy as a whole, without prejudice to the ongoing negotiations.
in writing. - while i agree that the report is well thought out, i do not agree with the full support for enlargement policies and the paragraphs on the need for visa liberalisation and publicity to inform european citizens of the many benefits that the enlargement process would bring to them and to the member states. for these reasons, i think it is appropriate to abstain.
in writing. − enlargement policy is the future of the european union, to ensure cohesion and integration. the recent financial crisis has highlighted the link between the various national economies of member states and non-eu countries. it is therefore very important to strengthen relations, particularly economic ones, with the countries that will be candidates or are already candidates for accession to the union. it is essential to create a climate of harmony and reconciliation between different nations and peoples, fostering economic, cultural and religious dialogue. the peaceful settlement of conflicts and the establishment of good neighbourly relations between european countries are essential for sustainable peace and stability and contribute to a genuine process of integration. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european union is a very important one. finally, we must ensure that enlargement remains a credible policy based on democracy, human rights and reconciliation.
in writing. − i believe that a more efficient and forward-looking enlargement policy could be a valuable strategic tool for the eu's economic development. it should aim to create important budgetary synergies and better coordination between the various measures and types of assistance provided by the union, the states and the international financial institutions. in this sense, the eu's policies and strategic interests should be geared towards increasing political and economic cohesion. the actions undertaken within the european parliament are certainly a good sign in this direction. but that 's not enough . the member states must be the bearers of these instances and the messengers of a message of cohesion and efficiency for their communities, in line with the work that europe is doing through its institutional channels.
in writing. − the interdependence of economies, both within and outside the union, underlines the importance of further strengthening economic and financial stability and promoting growth, including in the candidate and potential candidate countries. it is therefore necessary to provide the candidate and potential candidate countries with adequate and more targeted pre-accession financial assistance.
in writing. - the issue of enlargement of the european union is a highly complex one and must be analysed from all points of view, both economically, for its geopolitical repercussions and for the social impact it may have. i believe that, especially in a time of economic crisis, it is appropriate to exercise the utmost caution and to learn from past mistakes. unlike the rapporteur, i do not believe that it is the eu's job to promote enlargement in the candidate countries, nor do i believe that enlargement has always been a positive thing, nor that visa liberalisation policies have always been beneficial. i am not in a position to vote for this report because of these doubts.
in writing. − the enlargement process needs to be fuelled by sustained interest and concrete support, also in the light of the new realities created by the economic crisis. through a reform policy aimed at the enlargement countries, it will be possible to contribute to greater stability and prosperity in europe. i believe that the improvement of this process must start with the identification of concrete objectives, such as strengthening democratic governance in certain countries and focusing on the consolidation of economic and financial stability. i believe that this instrument can be made more effective by providing for new criteria for membership which take account of the social implications. this will give a new impetus to the aspirant countries' efforts to achieve the objectives. it is also necessary to promote the prospect of prosperity and stability offered by eu membership, by sponsoring its political, socioeconomic and cultural benefits. each applicant country will have to demonstrate that it is honouring its commitments and the eu will have to commit itself to removing obstacles to the success of enlargement policy. in particular, the eu will have to commit itself to ensuring that smart, sustainable and inclusive growth is one of its priorities. i am voting in favour of supporting further enlargements and encouraging the candidate countries to pursue reforms.
in writing. the european parliament today reiterated the clear position it has expressed on several occasions: the only way to end the violence and hostility between palestine and israel is the establishment of two sovereign states for two peoples. the new escalation of violence, the innocent victims, including many women and children, demands an immediate and decisive solution to the conflict without any further delay. the european union, by virtue of its nobel peace prize, must step up its efforts to achieve a final ceasefire and to remove the causes of this perennial conflict. it is also important to have reaffirmed european support for the application by palestine to become a non-member observer state of the united nations.
in writing. − i support this resolution because we must send a signal to both sides of the conflict. we strongly condemn the new outbreak of violence in and around the gaza strip and we ask for an urgent de-escalation and cessation of hostilities. all attacks must end immediately as they cause unjustifiable suffering of innocent civilians. i believe in the urgent need to bring humanitarian assistance to all the people affected by the conflict, and in particular to the deprived population in the gaza strip. it must be reiterated again that, in protecting its population from the missile attacks, israel must act proportionately. unfortunately this is not what is happening. with this text we support the efforts of egypt to mediate for a rapid, sustainable ceasefire and welcome the mission of the united nations secretary-general to the region. the only way to achieve a just and lasting peace between israelis and palestinians is through the resumption of direct peace talks between both parties. for this reason i support palestine’s bid to become an un non-member observer.
in writing. - we must do everything possible to bring about an immediate cessation of hostilities between israel and palestine. the current situation once again highlights the urgent need to move towards a two-state solution, which allows both sides to live side by side in peace and security. the european union must continue to work with all the parties with influence in the region to achieve this solution.
in writing. the eu calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities between the gaza strip and israel. the eu expressed great concern at the situation in the strip, and reiterated its strong commitment to creating the conditions for the resumption of dialogue. i look with confidence to the role of moderator assumed by europe and i hope for maximum restraint in the conduct of military operations. in recent times, old tensions have been grafted onto a new scenario stemming from the arab spring. not only the individual european states but also the european union must increasingly assume its responsibilities. i look with confidence to the solution envisaged, namely the creation of two states, one israeli and the other palestinian. the latter is a solution which i believe has the potential to be long-lasting and sustainable. in this respect, it is imperative to move gradually by involving all the actors and, above all, by offering the necessary guarantees to all those involved.
in writing. − i voted against this report because, although i am in favour of the creation of a european defence force, i believe that this can be achieved through a further decrease in the member states’ national security budgets. this text suggests instead that defence cuts may lead to lack of credibility of the eu. concerning eu-nato cooperation, i believe in a clear separation of the eu from nato. we must consider that nato is a military-political alliance created to fight a threat, soviet communism, which ceased to exist 23 years ago. for this reason, in recent years, nato has tried to reinvent its role, creating new enemies. i believe that european countries should reduce year by year their share of the nato budget and refrain from stronger cooperation with it. to conclude, i would value it if a report like this one were to focus also on civil peaceful conflict solutions and not only on eu military interventionism.
in writing. - a review or rethinking of the european foreign policy strategy is a topical issue, especially in the light of the recent revolutionary events that have characterised, for over a year and a half now, several nations bordering the european union. there is a growing need to equip the eu with an effective and strong foreign policy, with credible civilian and military capabilities. however, it should also be remembered that the expenditure chapters devoted to security and foreign policy, as with other european policies, have to face the constraints of national economies, which are now the main protagonists in the debate on the new financial perspectives of the eu.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. it is urgent that the union assert its strategic autonomy through a strong and effective foreign, security and defence policy, which will enable it to act on its own if necessary. it is right to point out that this strategic autonomy will remain a mirage if we do not equip ourselves with the appropriate civilian and military instruments.
in writing. − the european union, as a global political actor, should protect its interests more effectively and guarantee the security of its citizens more vigorously, in order to ensure that it has a greater say on the international scene. i believe that if the eu is equipped with the appropriate means and is able to pursue the objective of promoting international peace and security, it will be able to gain greater strategic autonomy. in order to build up this strategic autonomy, greater efforts will be needed to make foreign, security and defence policy more effective. i believe that it is essential to take account of the evolution of global threats and to adapt the european security strategy so that europe can make a concrete contribution to peacekeeping operations in the world. only by putting in place political, economic, development and humanitarian instruments will the union be able to respond effectively to specific risks. i hope that this will give the union's action new credibility and political visibility, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − the major changes taking place in the geostrategic context of the common foreign and security policy, in particular the radical changes in the middle east and north africa and the emergence of new actors with regional or global ambitions on the international scene, must push the european union to develop its civil and military capabilities and to implement those concrete measures which will enable it to meet the new challenges. the union, which has the political, economic and humanitarian instruments it needs to operate effectively in the field of defence and security, must therefore act to ensure that these instruments are strengthened and implemented.
in writing. − i abstained from voting on this report because i disagree with the aim of the mutual defence clause itself. in practice this instrument, which makes obligatory mutual assistance within the eu by all possible means in the event of an attack on an eu member state, transforms the eu into a military alliance. moreover, in this report the solidarity clause is also applied to unarmed attacks, without clearly defining the latter, thus leading to possible dangerous interpretations.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the paşcu report. it draws the attention of the institutions to the mutual defence (article 42 (7) teu) and solidarity (article 222 tfeu) clauses, which were created with the intention of countering threats to the member states of the european union; however, three years after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, there are still no implementing regulations. this legislative vacuum is intolerable. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is essential that the commission makes a proposal and the council takes a decision on how these principles should be applied in practice.
in writing. − three years after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, there are still no regulations implementing the solidarity and common defence clauses, provided for in articles 222 tfeu and 42 (7) teu respectively. this means that, at present, if a member state were to request aid under those provisions, there would be no codified mechanisms through which the union could act. i therefore consider that a proposal from the commission is needed on how to give concrete expression to these principles, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − to strengthen their cooperation, both nato and the european union should commit to enhancing their core capabilities, improving coordination between their doctrines, planning, technologies, equipment and training methods. it is right to reiterate the wish for a harmonisation of military requirements.
in writing. − i voted against this report because, once again, this parliament adopted a text based on a clear example of threat exaggeration. cyber-terrorism is something that many experts of terrorism do not consider a serious threat. i believe that introducing the concept that cyber-terrorism could be faced from the european union by military means is completely wrong and instrumental to a distortion of the eu’s approach to the subject of the fight against new forms of criminality.
in writing. - i support the kelam report on cyber security and defence. europe is facing a problem which we might call new and at the same time powerfully inseparable from the lives of every citizen of the union. the text clearly highlights and contextualises all the facets of this problem, highlighting the challenges that individual member states and the eu have to face and will have to face. it highlights how political, legislative and organisational obstacles exist in the eu and in the states to the development of a comprehensive and unified approach to cybersecurity. coordination and sharing between countries and the european union is still poor, and there are no clear definitions of the concepts of "cyber security and defence". the text stresses the need to strike a clear balance between security measures and citizens' rights, such as the right to privacy, data protection and freedom of expression. europe must respond to all these challenges as soon as possible with a coordinated approach at the level of the european institutions and the individual member states, with both public and private cooperation.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. a cybersecurity strategy should be developed, providing for a common definition of cybersecurity and cyber defence and the elements constituting a cyber attack on defence, as well as a common operational vision, and taking into account the added value of the agencies and bodies already established and the good practices adopted by member states that already have national cybersecurity strategies.
in writing. - it was in the news yesterday that the french presidential computer system was attacked by us-based hackers during the first and second rounds of the french presidential elections, using one of the most popular tools of communication with citizens, which is currently facebook. i would remind you that facebook is also used in this european parliament because it allows for particularly horizontal communication between members and citizens. the resolution adopted today maintains a balance between different sensitivities: the need to ensure citizens' freedom of expression and the full use of the internet, while safeguarding the integrity of the internet against abuse. the example i gave of the cyberattack on the elysée is the key to the way we have to think in this european union, within ourselves and in our relations with third countries - where too often the servers or the places of origin of the attacks are guarded - effectively preventing an effective and timely repression of abuses and crimes.
in writing. - i congratulate mr kelam on his excellent work in tackling a problem which is entirely new to the european union but which is destined to become increasingly important in the future. we must recognise that in an increasingly interconnected and globalised world, there are new challenges that concern cyberspace. a coordinated eu response to cyber challenges needs to be defined by developing a comprehensive eu cybersecurity strategy, which can be integrated into broader collaboration with the us, brics countries and nato.
in writing. − in today's globalised world, cybersecurity, security in the use of information and digital technologies, and the resilience and reliability of information services and associated infrastructure have become of crucial importance to the european union and its member states. cyber-attacks are increasing significantly and pose a serious threat to the security, defence, stability and competitiveness of national states and the private sector. the commission has therefore decided to make a further contribution to the development of the community's energy policy. most highly visible and disruptive cyber incidents now have a political motive; furthermore, the vast majority of cyber incidents remain rudimentary and threats to critical elements are becoming increasingly sophisticated and require extensive protection. the vote will be a rapid completion of the respective national strategies on cyber security and defence.
in writing. several countries are actively preparing for cyberwarfare by setting up structures dedicated to defensive cyberwarfare, but also to espionage and cyber penetration. many public and private organizations are daily targets of attacks. large-scale cyberattacks have been carried out in recent years around the world. modern, highly computerised societies are vulnerable to this. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. on the technical side, never before has a set of technologies penetrated so rapidly and so deeply into human activity. the rise of a safer cyberspace requires increased involvement of states in network regulation and crisis management. it is therefore essential that europe emerges as the platform for discussion and regulation in this field. in fact, too often in recent times we have had in our hands, in the european parliament, texts with an unfortunate tendency to try to extinguish many individual freedoms, under various and varied pretexts. europe must guarantee to all its citizens that at no time is the boundary between security and privacy preserved and framed as much as possible!
in writing. − cyberspace now has almost two billion users connected globally and has become one of the most powerful and effective tools for promoting democratic ideas and for organising those citizens who seek to realise their aspirations for freedom and fight against dictatorships. given that there are many political, legislative and organisational obstacles in the european union and the member states to the development of a comprehensive and unified approach to defence and cyber security, and that there is a lack of common definitions, standards and measures in this area, i voted in favour of mr kelam's text, which aims to implement a comprehensive cyber security and cyber security strategy that is appropriate to the times we live in.
in writing. - i shall abstain on the tarand report. it is true that the effects of global climate change are becoming more and more severe, not only in terms of loss of human life, but also in economic terms of direct costs, for reconstruction and aid, and indirect costs, for the increase in the prices of insurance products and services. i also believe that it is not necessary for all european policies, instruments and policy papers to include a specific analysis of climate risks.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr tarand's report because the analysis of the impact of natural disasters on international security and political stability must be a point which can no longer be deferred in the agenda of international policy priorities. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption, and the council will be consulted on it. in this regard, it is of fundamental importance to develop emergency plans to enable the european union to respond to the effects of natural disasters and climate-related crises occurring outside the union but having direct or indirect repercussions on the security of european countries, as in the case of climate migration.
in writing. − recently, public debate has focused on a number of priority issues, leaving aside the issue of climate change, whose impact on global security cannot be underestimated. the disasters of recent years have had very serious consequences in terms of both direct costs, for reconstruction and aid, and indirect costs, for the increase in insurance premiums. developing countries are particularly vulnerable to such events and the resulting difficulties in accessing water and food have a lasting impact on the economic and social fabric . i believe that the security debate should be a starting point for re-examining the problem of climate change and natural disasters. specific instruments will have to be put in place to manage the consequences, especially for vulnerable populations. i believe in the eu's ability to improve its conduct in dealing with the risks of conflict and instability due to climate change and natural disasters, and that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i think that kazakhstan’s political will to further deepen partnership with the eu and the opening of the negotiations for an eu-kazakhstan partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) must be supported. i believe that the peoples of the eu and kazakhstan will benefit mutually from a closer cooperation. we must also consider that kazakhstan has played a positive role in central asia, making efforts to develop good neighbourly relations with bordering countries, resume regional cooperation and resolve all bilateral issues by peaceful means. on the other hand, i am convinced that the conclusion of the new pca negotiation should provide a framework for cooperation based on democratic rights. after the tragic events of december 2011 in zhanaozen, opposition parties, independent media, trade unions, activists and human rights defenders have become targets of repression. for these reasons, with this report we urge kazakhstan to maintain its declared commitment to further reforms, in order to build up an open society including a real political opposition and a deep respect for the rule of law.
in writing. - i strongly believe in the development of eu-kazakhstan relations. the establishment of renewed cooperation will enable both sides to benefit from each other's economic development and to encourage the necessary political reforms. i believe that europe must ensure that it is engaged in supporting those priority areas such as human rights, the rule of law, good governance and democratisation. promoting dialogue between the two actors must be a priority; the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i believe that kazakhstan's efforts to improve its good neighbourly relations with neighbouring countries and to resolve bilateral issues should be appreciated. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i support the report by mr ferreira on small-scale coastal fishing, artisanal fishing and the reform of the common fisheries policy. i agree with him that small-scale fishing (which includes artisanal fishing, certain types of coastal fishing, traditional aquaculture activities such as 'natural mollusc farming') is not adequately represented in the reform of the common fisheries policy that the commission is pursuing. we must safeguard the role that these activities play in our states, which are closely linked to local economies and traditions which are often unique. the commission's fisheries policy has proved to be a failure, and i believe that the reform of the cfp must also encourage and support the development of those operators who use instruments with a lower impact on resources and who bring greater benefits to the communities in which they operate, both in terms of quality and employment.
in writing. - i fully supported this report because small-scale fishing, which includes artisanal and certain types of coastal fishing, shellfish harvesting and other traditional extensive aquaculture activities, plays a crucial role in the economic system of many areas of the mediterranean, with very diverse territorial, social and cultural repercussions both on land and in island regions. i believe that the model of fisheries management which has characterised the common fisheries policy in recent decades has proved to be a failure, often failing to take due account of local, regional and national specificities. the commission has also proposed that the fishing fleet be given a special status in the fisheries sector, which is much better considered by a management of proximity, which through scientific knowledge and the consultation and participation of the sector in the definition, implementation and co-management of policies, is certainly the one that best meets the needs of small-scale fishing. i therefore hope that in the near future all the parties concerned will be involved in the formulation of small-scale coastal fishing and artisanal fishing policies by encouraging local and regional strategies and including development, research and training projects with adequate funding from the emff, the edf and the erdf.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to support small-scale fishing. this type of activity includes artisanal fishing, certain types of coastal fishing, shellfish harvesting and other traditional and extensive aquaculture activities. in recent decades, a centralised management model of the common european fisheries policy has prevailed, which has ended up harming this type of activity, which is necessary to ensure the supply of fishery products to local populations and to promote the development of coastal communities, also guaranteeing a certain level of employment. small-scale fishing is by its very nature exposed to certain types of economic risk, such as rapidly rising fuel prices, and is also particularly vulnerable to sudden changes in the availability of fishery resources; it is therefore reasonable that, within the new european maritime and fisheries fund, special support and financing measures should be provided for this sector. the union must therefore aim to promote a significant revival of this activity, while respecting the different realities and prerogatives which may vary not only at european level but also between the different areas of the same country.
in writing. − i believe that small-scale fishing should be recognised for a number of positive features including environmental sustainability by allowing the release of unwanted or illegally caught fish with a generally very low mortality rate. in addition, this is a fisheries sector which has shown extraordinary resilience to the pressure of the current global economic crisis, and it is also economically sustainable in terms of the number of jobs it supports. new and more coherent objectives must be set, which respond to the needs and specificities of small-scale fishing. this sector cannot be underestimated any further, and management must be improved by means of concrete proposals in its favour. the potential development of this sector depends on the strengthening of efforts to rejuvenate it. i am aware of the problems and the potential of small-scale fishing, which is also a factor in stabilising fishing communities in all coastal areas, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − small-scale fishing, which includes artisanal and certain types of coastal fishing, shellfish harvesting and other traditional extensive aquaculture activities, such as natural shellfish farming in coastal waters, has very diverse territorial, social and cultural impacts on the mainland and in island and outermost regions, and presents specific problems that distinguish it from large-scale fishing and intensive or industrial aquaculture. in particular, under the new fisheries policy regulation, a definition of artisanal fishing should be established, while taking into account the impact of this type of fishing on the financing of the new european maritime and fisheries fund: in this respect, projects with integrated solutions that benefit coastal communities should also be encouraged. the access of young people and women to the sector should also be facilitated by the creation of specific vocational training and initiation courses.
in writing. − with regard to future bilateral fisheries agreements (bfa), the eu must stand firm to achieve the legitimate exploitation of surplus resources at fair prices, while offering support to the development of the coastal state. in addition, urgent action is needed to prevent some countries fishing on the high seas from resorting to questionable techniques in accessing surplus resources. cooperation will be needed to ensure that concrete action is taken to ensure the sustainability of fisheries and respect for human rights in those contexts, which are today characterised by an odious climate of corruption. in view of the increased competition for fish stocks, i believe that it is urgent to address the question of equity in the distribution of resources. to this end, an efficient system of resource management must be established. shared political commitment at international level will make it possible to adopt sanctions for infringements and to pursue the specific objectives of the orgp, which will have to be managed by ensuring the protection of artisanal fisheries. for the reasons i have just given, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr lövin's report, although i felt that the text as a whole had some shortcomings. developing countries must take a regional approach to fisheries exploitation, taking into account both the cross-border dimension of fishing activity and the migratory nature of certain species. it is also desirable that, in order to establish a new generation of sustainable fisheries agreements, those countries commit to respect the essential and fundamental elements of human rights and democratic principles as set out in article 9 of the cotonou agreement.
in writing. - in the next consultation on the european parliament elections, i believe that greater gender balance in the choice of representatives should be promoted. i am aware of the interaction between the political representatives who make up the parliamentary institution and the role they play in our society, and i believe that it is urgent to take account of the continuing evolution of the needs and characteristics of society itself. in this context, concrete instruments should be put in place to ensure gender representation. the continuing difficulty in reversing the trend of low female representation in political representation can be addressed by focusing on the positive contribution of women's qualities and considering that the gender imbalance will have to be overcome to ensure the completion of democratic institutions. i am also pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to present a report on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which is a very important step in the development of the european union.
member of the commission. − mr president, we are deeply concerned at the latest reports regarding the situation of migrants, asylum seekers and other vulnerable foreign nationals in libya. we have raised these issues with the libyan authorities on a regular basis and will continue to do so in the future. in reply, the authorities have acknowledged the problems and have expressed their readiness to address these issues. the contradiction between these practices and the values that triggered the 17 february revolution is very clear. the eu supported the libyan revolution from the outset because it was rooted in values that we share, especially of course respect for human rights and democratic principles. the european union will continue to be a strong partner for libya during the process of democratic transition. nevertheless – in this same spirit of partnership – we will not hesitate to convey concerns on issues of fundamental importance, such as those we are discussing today. at the same time we are sensitive to the complex situation in libya at present. over the past four months libya has undergone a period of political uncertainty with a caretaker government having to deal with numerous challenges, including a major security crisis, not just in benghazi but in a number of other parts of the country. moreover, it faces a long list of urgent priorities to address, including state-building, disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration of the revolutionary militias, national reconciliation, the promotion of the rule of law and the protection of human rights. the new government was sworn in just over a week ago. we note our full political support to prime minister zidan’s new government and trust he will do his outmost to address the different challenges lying ahead. as is the case for every new government – and in particular for libya – the authorities need time to put their house in order. nevertheless, we will not be complacent. we will continue to follow this issue closely. we will continue to press the authorities to ensure respect for human rights standards and we will continue to help them meet their responsibilities under international law. in this regard, i would like to recall that the eu is already providing a eur 20 million support package aimed at improving the protection of vulnerable groups, including migrants. further measures and projects in this regard are in the pipeline. finally, with regard to our assistance in broader terms, we are also preparing a substantial programme on the security sector reform as well as on the rule of law under the european neighbourhood policy instrument, the design of which is being finalised. the overall objective of this programme is to promote the rule of law in libya by strengthening democratic control and good governance in the security and justice sectors. the specific objective is to respond to the needs expressed by the libyan authorities in managing the process of democratic transition, especially in the security and justice sector.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the association agreement between the european union and central america is an important precedent, since it is the first bi-regional association agreement signed by the european union since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. in this framework, the trade pillar forms a large part of the agreement, providing for a gradual expansion of a free trade and trade area. it is a balanced agreement, which is positive for both sides and which is fully in line with the relaunch of the bilateral partnership policies between the european union, latin america and the caribbean, a geopolitical area of the world which is extremely sensitive and also subject to the influence of the pacific area, which is strategic for the geopolitical future of europe as well. it is also important to bear in mind that all the recent events, including the less recent ones, in that geographical area of the world in recent decades have led the european union - this part of the world which is so free, so advanced and so democratic - to extend its human rights policy also through the contribution of trade. it is therefore an important agreement, the chapters of which will certainly have to be monitored over time, but which considers respect for human rights as a priority over trade, and as such it cannot fail to receive our favourable vote. this is also true of the chapters on cooperation, so that we can bring about greater integration between the very different countries of central america, and greater stability and economic, political and social development in an area which is extremely delicate but also important to us. for all these reasons, i believe that we must give our full support to this agreement and then also integrate it into the wider agreements. we shall then discuss colombia and peru and vote on these matters tomorrow. i therefore believe that we are giving a very useful direction to relations between the european union and latin america.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 11 december 2012.
