rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development. − madam president, we are going to vote on a good agreement. colombia and peru are two democracies which in recent times have made great improvements in almost all areas, even in the most controversial one, which is human rights. most of the extreme criticism against colombia and peru is unjustified and is made by people who do not know the changes which have occurred in these countries, not because there are no violations of human rights – they still occur – but they are a fraction of what was occurring 15 to 20 years ago. both countries show very positive trends. colombia 15 years ago was one of the most violent countries in the world, plagued by a staggering number of homicides, afflicted by drug cartels and blatant terrorism. it is not so anymore. drug cartels exist only in newspapers, killings have been reduced by 80 %, terrorism is at a historical minimum and poverty has been significantly reduced in both countries. colombia and peru are following the virtuous path of their continent. they are emancipating themselves from the big brother of the north and they deserve all our support and cooperation. blue-card answer. – madam president, i would just tell them that we fully support their fight; we greatly deplore these episodes. i have never said there is no violation of human rights. i say that they are still occurring and they are still worrying, but the path that we have to follow is to support the democratisation of the country. we should not take the attitude of constantly lecturing them about what they should do; we should not consider them just as our pupils. this is an issue of attitude that has to be shown in every part of our relationship with them. this is a trade agreement, and trade and economic development will help also these communities in terms of making them stronger, making them more aware of their rights. this is all we can do; we cannot simply say that these countries should be blamed, that these countries should be punished, that we should put 100 conditions on them. if we apply to them the same standards that we apply for human rights in the european union we will reach a dead end.

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the adoption of this regulation is an important step forward in the affirmation of one of the most innovative principles of the lisbon treaty, namely the exclusive competence of the community dimension in international trade. we support the work done by president moreira and the agreement reached with the council. there is nothing more pathetic, almost anachronistic, than to see individual european countries fighting alone to wrest away this or that trading condition which is favourable only to them. i believe that the commission can certainly be a better guarantor than the individual member states of agreements which are actually useful. it is also pathetic because of the small size of our countries in a global system. the regulation provides for a sharing of competences and a margin of flexibility, but above all it puts an end to what had become a cacophony where bilateral agreements were not only a protection of their legitimate interests but, at a certain point, could also become an instrument of competition with other countries of the union, all to the detriment of the smaller and less competitive eu states on the international scene. as always, much depends on the actual implementation of this regulation. the commission is acquiring very important power - we are happy about that - and a role which we support in order to ensure that there is a real guarantor of european interests. the time limits, authorizations, notification, withdrawal of authorizations, review and so on are subject to rules which we believe are balanced in this agreement. i ask the commission to pay particular attention to the interests and needs of small and mediumsized enterprises, which are often the victims of this type of investment agreement but which are at the same time the most innovative and often the most likely to create jobs in our countries. above all, it will be necessary to demonstrate that european protection is more ambitious and more effective than that of the individual member states, which, however, belong to a world of a fragmented europe which, after all, we only want to see in the past.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i hope that tomorrow the european parliament will be able to vote in favour of this regulation, which represents an important step towards the full implementation of the treaty of lisbon in trade policy. so i thank the commission for its legislative initiative and i thank especially mr vital moreira for bringing it to this point. it is certainly an important initiative because it implements the treaty, overcomes the fragmentation in the field of trade policy on investment and above all, as mr rinaldi also mentioned, avoids and overcomes internal dumping between the 27 - soon to be 28 - countries of the european union on such important matters as trade investment, which is an essential tool for competitiveness. it is therefore an agreement which provides legal certainty for investments made before the transfer of competence to the treaty of lisbon and which also regulates the transitional phase, and it is therefore a very significant and important aspect of trade policy.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, this report is part of the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. in particular, active ageing must become a priority for the 27 member states. demographic change is presenting the european union with a number of challenges, including the gradual increase in the population over 65 years of age. more than 87 million people, of whom more than 50 million are women. the gender gap in ageing is even more pronounced for people over 80: 3.1% of women compared to 1.6% of men in the total population. it is worth noting, however, that although women live longer than men, they are often affected by chronic and disabling diseases and are therefore subject to a deterioration in their quality of life. among the diseases that affect older women are cardiovascular diseases, which are mistakenly considered to be a typically male problem, respiratory diseases, cancer, diabetes, musculoskeletal disorders, neurovascular diseases and depression. there are many difficulties in accessing health services: the lack of guidance on the prevention of the most common diseases, the difficulty of booking specialist visits and diagnostic tests, and the often too long waiting lists, all of which discourage elderly patients in particular, who very often live in loneliness. 75.8% of women over 65 live alone. in addition, older women are more at risk of poverty. according to the latest available data, 24.5% of the female population in the union of 27 is at risk of poverty. the risk of poverty is affected by the wage gap - on average, as we know, women earn almost 17% less than men - but also by the occupational choices women are forced to make to reconcile family and working life. all this means that women accumulate lower pension contributions and therefore have lower pensions and fewer resources for therapy and medical care. the aim of this report is to encourage synergy between public institutions at european, national and territorial level to promote measures to enable healthy ageing for all. the objectives are first to ensure access to quality health care for recurrent diseases, invest in information and prevention to enable older people to remain as independent and healthy as possible for as long as possible, and then to carry out ad hoc screening for certain diseases which, if done at the right time, are a powerful tool for prevention. prevention can also be done by following good habits, from proper nutrition to the importance of physical activity, to combating alcohol and tobacco abuse. it is worth remembering that, according to who estimates, the proportion of women smokers in europe will rise from the current 12% to about 20% by 2025. i conclude by saying that we must ensure that the elderly can play an active role in society, avoiding the social exclusion which causes marginalization and depression.
member of the commission. − madam president, first of all i would like to congratulate mrs anna rosbach, who – speaking of antimicrobial resistance – has been contagious with her enthusiasm and energy on this subject which, of course, is extremely important, as many members have underlined. we all know that resistant microbes can spread between humans, animals and the environment and through food, and this highlights the need for a coordinated approach across human and animal sectors. control of antimicrobial resistance will require the joint efforts of all actors at eu level: the member states, healthcare professionals, industry, veterinarians and eu citizens as consumers of antibiotics. resistant microbes do not respect borders. borders are for human beings. therefore, resistance can easily spread from country to country when people and animals travel cross-border or where certain goods are traded. the need for coordinated efforts across borders is of pivotal importance. all the recognised means to combat antimicrobial resistance (amr) are addressed in the 12 concrete actions outlined in the 2011 communication from the commission. we are actively implementing the amr action plan and are making progress. at global level, the commission remains fully engaged in the antimicrobial resistance debate with the who and, importantly, the transatlantic taskforce. the development of new antibiotics has already been encouraged through new research- and innovation-related actions and partnerships. there was a question on funding. this year the commission – together with the european federation of pharmaceutical industries and associations, through their joint undertaking the innovative medicines initiative, launched a eur 223.7 million programme for this purpose. this was partially funded by the seventh framework programme for research. the commission has also further reinforced research activities in this field by supporting the joint programming initiative with member states, and by making eur 147 million available for antimicrobial resistance research in the last call, again under the seventh framework programme for research. pending the development of new and effective drugs, we should make strenuous efforts to preserve the efficacy of existing antibiotics by reducing their use whenever possible and by carefully monitoring antimicrobial resistance. the report states ‘it is imperative to ensure the prudent use of antimicrobials.’ this includes ensuring respect for the prescription-only use of antibiotics in place across the eu, the avoidance of self-medication by patients and preventing unnecessary consumption of antibiotics. in this last respect, i would point out that antimicrobials in medicated feed can now only be used on the basis of a prescription. the commission plans to propose modernised legislation to cover medicated feed in the near future to curb the risk of the development of anti-microbial resistance arising from residues of antimicrobials in feed and to set common production standards. finally, i can assure honourable members that the commission’s battle against antimicrobial resistance will continue. in 2013, we shall be publishing a roadmap to communicate, in detail, to all stakeholders, ongoing actions and the next steps, as well as an interim report on the progress made so far.
in writing. the phenomenon of antimicrobial resistance is a threat to the development of pharmacological science, as well as a major problem in terms of both human and financial costs. the figures from the commission underline this point: antimicrobial resistance causes an additional 25,000 human deaths per year and costs at least 1.5 billion euros. all caused by overuse of antibiotic drugs that cause antibiotic resistance. the report voted by this parliament stresses the importance of limiting the prophylactic prescription and use of antibiotics, encouraging medical research in the hope that it can produce new generation antimicrobials. improved training for doctors, pharmacists, veterinarians and farmers and better information for the public on the harm caused by the misuse of antimicrobials are also essential.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, with today's vote we are bringing to fruition a project which europe has been pursuing for over 40 years: the european union will finally be able to have an effective, low-cost and legally secure patent protection system. the system in place today is complex and legally uncertain and in some ways constitutes a veritable tax on innovation. the cost of validating a patent in 13 countries is now around eur 13 000, compared with the us where the cost is around eur 1 800 and is valid throughout the country. in addition, renewal fees are payable in each country and it costs six times more to maintain a patent in europe than in the united states or japan. finally, the lack of a single system for litigation means that companies are forced to initiate legal proceedings simultaneously in all the member states, which are likely to have, and often can have, different outcomes in each member state. so, there's not even a uniform jurisdiction. this situation has created a serious negative impact on the union's competitiveness, as innovation-related activities, which generate human capital, are static and fragmented. in the face of these negative consequences, the new unitary patent system will reduce costs, including translation costs, by between eur 4 000 and eur 6 000, naturally facilitating access to the patent market and providing legal certainty. in line with the main priorities, in my role as rapporteur i supported the idea of encouraging and facilitating access to the patent system for small and mediumsized enterprises. the regulation on the language arrangements includes specific measures to achieve this objective. a system of compensation for the total costs of translation will be available to small and medium-sized enterprises filing patent applications in a language other than the official languages and greater legal protection will be granted to small and medium-sized enterprises in the event of alleged infringement. following the same logic, the regulation on the unitary patent, for which mr rapkay is rapporteur, provides that the level of renewal fees is to be set taking into account the needs of small and mediumsized enterprises. finally, as regards the longstanding dispute over the language regime, i would point out that the transitional regime, which will last for 12 years, will orient the system towards the english language, paving the way for future revisions. let me say something about the compromise reached. it is not necessary to dwell on the absolutely wrong conduct of the european council, which has entered with its feet in the air into a legislative procedure for which this parliament and the council of ministers are responsible. we had two choices: the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, and i am sure that the commission will be able to take them up in the next few months. for this reason, the compromise gives the proprietor the right to prohibit third parties from infringing the patent throughout the territory of the member states in which it has unitary effect. at the same time, it is ensured that the scope of that right and its limits are uniform in all participating member states. i really believe that today, with the adoption of the package of proposals on the unitary patent, we will be giving the green light to a legally secure, low-cost patent system for small and mediumsized enterprises, which will help to develop innovation and european competitiveness.

in writing. after 30 years of trying, the european union will have a common patent system, saving european businesses over eur 250 million. until now, to obtain pan-european protection, an investor had to validate the patent in each member state through the european patent office, a body outside the union. this involved, mainly because of the translation of patents, a complicated and expensive system, making the european patent up to 10 times more expensive than the american one and 11 times more expensive than the japanese one. the new system provides for uniform protection throughout the union, with a significant reduction in costs for european businesses. the new european patent will be less expensive and more effective in protecting the inventions of individuals and businesses than the current system. according to recent estimates, when the new system is fully operational, the european patent will cost only 680 euros compared to the average price of a us patent of 1,850 euros. i welcome the success of parliament in introducing specific measures to facilitate access to the european patent for smes, and in particular to ensure strong legal protection and full reimbursement of translation costs.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, considering that smes in the union generate 75% of jobs in the private sector and considering that they have contributed to 80% of job creation over the last five years, it is clear that they are particularly important in exporting, importing and investing beyond the borders of the eu's single market. the lack of internationalisation of smes is mainly due to the lack of information they obtain about foreign markets. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. it is on these very points that the motion for a resolution is based and that is why i am voting in favour of it.

in writing. - i support the moreira report on the proposal for a regulation on transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries. according to article 207 tfeu, the european union institutions have exclusive competence in this area. the purpose of the text is to provide a high degree of legal certainty as regards the transitional provisions on bilateral agreements already concluded between member states and third countries.
in writing. − the report refers to a key step in the process of implementing the tfeu in relation to our economies, private enterprise and the presence, more generally, of european interests and investors in third countries. the council's position at first reading and the caveats set out in the attached joint declaration are to be approved. as the legal elements contained in the commission's proposal make it possible to guide an orderly transition, with broad guarantees as regards the conditions under which investors operate and precise procedural provisions to bring the many existing bilateral investment agreements into line with the provisions of the tfeu, i intend to vote in favour.
in writing. - i supported the report on 'transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries' because it is necessary to stress the need for a well-defined transitional period, since without a time limit the regulation would allow parallel and potentially incompatible investments to take place, thus increasing legal uncertainty. while a fairly long transitional period is envisaged, an indefinite dualism in the european union's investment policy would be unacceptable. through an authorisation process, bilateral investment agreements concluded by member states should be maintained in force and, under certain conditions, member states should be allowed to renegotiate agreements, complete those in the process of adoption and enter into negotiations to conclude new agreements. in the event of renegotiation of existing bilateral investment agreements or negotiation of new agreements, an obligation for member states to provide for a dispute settlement mechanism and to ensure the involvement of the commission in the procedures should be included.
in writing. - having regard to the information received at the meeting, the importance of the subject under discussion and the amendments to be made to the special regulation on transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries, i shall vote in favour of this proposal.
in writing. the text voted today concludes a difficult series of negotiations between parliament and the council to define the new framework for the transition from member states' to union competence in investment protection. the text adopted aims to protect all existing agreements which may henceforth be supplemented by agreements negotiated at eu level.

in writing. − with the intensification of maritime traffic and the resulting pollution, the establishment of a european maritime safety agency (emsa) with increasing powers became necessary. it is the common view of the member states that the agency is an effective and well-managed organisation which makes considerable savings as it operates at european level and allows economies of scale to be generated. the enlargement of powers which will result from this report is therefore a coherent and mandatory step. the amendments will in particular enable the agency to prevent and respond to environmental disasters such as oil spills, using the 'cleanseanet' information system, to work towards improving coordination between national authorities, enhancing prevention and promoting best practice, and speeding up the response to any disasters. i am very pleased with the work that has been done and therefore i could not but give my full support to the report and the work done by my colleague.

in writing. - i am against the promotion of a european maritime area without barriers because too many illegal or unmarked goods from third countries arrive in our ports. the only country in europe that actually checks and denounces counterfeit goods is italy, with 40% of the total sanctions imposed at community level. this means that in the large european ports there are already very few controls, let alone a liberalization of transit between european countries. since the proposal is at second reading and there is no final vote, an amendment was tabled by the efd group to reject the proposal. so my vote in favour of the rejection amendment to the proposal means that i am against it.

in writing. - the achievement of the single european patent today is a major milestone. the adoption of the package of rules on the creation of unitary patent protection is a step forward in the simplification of bureaucratic procedures for large, medium and small enterprises. as is known, italy and spain opposed the proposal during the negotiations, as it was decided to approve the new unitary patent protection allowing the filing and transposition of the documentation in only three eu languages (english, french and german). a different and more thoughtful assessment of this question would probably have been more appropriate, especially since our companies are already drafting patent applications in english, but this stumbling block does not detract from the validity of the action taken by parliament and the scope of this innovation in the industrial sector.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. jurisdiction for european patents with unitary effect should be established and governed by an instrument establishing a single system for the settlement of patent disputes for european patents and for european patents with unitary effect.
in writing. - having regard to the importance of the subject in question and the extensive amendment work on the proposal for a regulation, following the careful evaluation of the amendments, i shall vote in favour.
in writing. − in the eu, patent protection is currently provided by national patents issued by the member states or by european patents issued by the european patent office (epo), under the european patent convention (epc). i think that an analysis of the current procedure can only reveal the complexity of the patent system in force, an onerous system with an unnecessarily complicated machine translation system. i believe that, starting with the agreement on the language regime, in order to make the patent system cheap, simplified and legally secure and considering the urgency of an eu patent agreement valid throughout its territory, the costs could be considerably reduced. the difficulty we have encountered so far has been political, since we have not reached agreement on the language arrangements to be adopted. i believe that by using translation into the language which is the language of the trade relations, namely english, italy would avoid certain disadvantages in terms of distortion of competition and the competitiveness of undertakings, to the advantage of countries whose official language coincides with one of the three languages on which the proposed language scheme would be based. for the reasons i have just given, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the agreement reached after years of negotiations by the european patent institutions leads to the creation of a 'single european patent', i.e. a unitary patent title which can be issued, amended or revoked with the same effect in all participating member states. the new unitary patent will be based on the system of the current european patent, which uses the same procedural stage of filing, leaving the choice between unitary patent and european patent at the time of grant. this also applies to the language arrangements, which take over the trilingual arrangements (english, french and german) of the european patent office (epo). this system will lead to significant savings for businesses, especially in terms of registration and language arrangements.
in writing. - the european patent currently costs 13 times more than the american and 11 times more than the japanese patent. it is time, after almost half a century since the creation of the common economic market, for the european union to have a single community patent. for too long a system has been in place which, because of the different national laws, has seriously hindered small and mediumsized enterprises in the transition from the national market to the european one, not to mention the deleterious effects of having to go through several national courts in the event of litigation. the new proposal for a regulation, which has been simplified and has brought down costs, particularly translation costs, represents a step forward in the creation of a common economic market and provides practical help for european businesses in a time of economic difficulties.
in writing. - given the difficulty of reaching agreement on the creation of a community patent and the considerable costs incurred in the cost of validation and maintenance of the patent, it is essential to find a tool which will mitigate some of the problems listed above. it is legitimate to call for a uniform legal system leading to the harmonization of the instrument in question. the rapporteur proposes to amend the text to this end so that this regulation will only enter into force when the agreement on the judicial system has been ratified by at least nine member states, including the three states with the highest number of patent applications. the translation by the european patent office is also necessary, since it plays a key role. in view of the foregoing, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which will finally make it possible to achieve the unitary patent system, a project which we have been pursuing for 40 years and which is a really important step towards completing the single market. i believe that it is no longer possible to postpone the adoption of measures to improve the level of protection of intellectual property. today, in europe, it costs about € 13,000 to validate a patent in 13 countries, plus renewal fees for each country. in addition, to resolve disputes, legal proceedings must be initiated in each individual state, taking into account the possibility of obtaining different outcomes from state to state. the compromise we have reached, after five months of consultation, will lead to lower patent validation costs and bureaucratic burdens and ensure uniform legal interpretation within the european union. another aspect which i think is positive is the increased legal protection for small and mediumsized enterprises and the introduction of a transitional phase, lasting 12 years, which will gradually move the system towards a uniform language regime. i believe that this report can help to stimulate innovative discoveries and increase our global competitiveness.
in writing. - we must urgently protect intellectual property in the internal market, which i believe is essential for the development of innovation and creativity in europe. i think it is a priority to look first at smes. the latter are particularly affected by counterfeiting and the spread of pirated products. the limited financial resources available to them often do not allow them to bear the high legal costs. in order to meet the above needs, action carried out exclusively within a member state will not be sufficient. in order to be effective, harmonisation must be based on the national provisions which appear to be most appropriate to the needs of the injured party, while taking account of the legitimate interests of the defendant. this will ensure that intellectual property rights are respected in an equivalent and effective manner throughout the community. it is our duty to ensure that companies, research centres and inventors have easy access to protection for their new inventions. this will save on their costs and allow us to direct these resources to new investment in innovation, improving our competitiveness in emerging markets where, unlike in europe, the number of new patents is constantly growing.
in writing. - i voted in favour, recognising the importance for businesses of creating a single court system for patent disputes, which would ensure the predictability and quality of decisions, reduce the enormous costs of litigation before several national courts and give effect to the protections recognised by the single european act. the texts adopted by parliament are moving in this direction and can therefore be considered a very positive achievement for both italian and european industry. in particular, the new system will be simpler and more easily accessible to smes, and above all less costly, on the one hand because of the objective simplification of the procedure and on the other hand because of the lower translation costs.

in writing. - given the difficulty of reaching agreement on the creation of a community patent and the considerable costs incurred in the cost of validation and maintenance of the patent, it is essential to find a tool which will mitigate some of the problems listed above.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative package on the european patent, as reaching agreement on this was necessary to solve the problems of registration and management costs between member states. in the current market, the diversification of administrative requirements required implies a very complex patent management within the eu; in addition, limited transparency and high costs to obtain protection at european level are factors that severely harm smes. as a result, a market which should be one is fragmented in terms of patent protection and access, thus hindering innovation, growth and the competitiveness of european businesses. to deal with this situation, the unitary patent system will lead to savings for businesses and simplification of processes, as well as substantial cost reductions. in confirming the importance of reaching this agreement on a subject which has been under discussion for many years, i would like to stress that certain points should be improved, particularly as regards the linguistic issue. i believe it is essential to safeguard linguistic diversity, which is a basic value of the eu, and i reiterate that italian should not be discriminated against but recognised as a european language with a long history and rich traditions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the three reports on the single european patent. this new scheme will cut costs by up to 80%; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. given the considerable proportion of patents registered in italy, i consider it very serious that there is no agreement on the language regime and that the three languages have been imposed. in addition, there are doubts about the use of the enhanced cooperation procedure for this type of matter, on which an italian appeal to the court of justice is pending. the failure to reach agreement in the council was unfortunately followed by the impossibility of allocating the seat of the court of first instance to milan, the centre of italy's patent production, whose court already has a specific section on patents. the result was a compromise on the location of the court which once again satisfied the appetites of the franco-german axis, producing unnecessary administrative costs. nevertheless, also in view of the fact that about 90% of our companies register in english, i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of the package, in the hope that, once the ecj's ruling is acquired, italy will be able to join the european patent.
in writing. the european parliament adopted the european patent package today. inventors in the eu will finally be able to obtain a unitary patent at lower costs. after more than 30 years of discussions, the new regime will cut the cost of an eu patent by up to 80%, making it competitive with the us and japan. this has resulted in cost reductions for small and mediumsized enterprises and the new system has been designed to meet their needs. as everyone knows, italy, along with spain, is not participating in the new rules because of the lack of agreement on the language regime. a battle that was certainly fair but that probably lost sight of the goal. in fact, she missed the opportunity to team up and bring home the final result. sometimes the policy of categorical no does not pay. it would have been better to have sought to win consensus within the council and to have allied ourselves with parliament. the result would have been the same, but perhaps the single court would have been italy.
in writing. - i was against it because i think it is unacceptable that patents can be filed in three languages - english, french and german - instead of in all the languages recognised by the eu or, as a more effective and logical solution, in english alone. this is why italy, spain and other countries opposed it, and the european court itself raised objections. negotiations in the council have led to an agreement between the countries, with spain being the only country not to be included, providing for facilities and subsidies for smes to cover translation costs. the text also voted to give european patent powers to an international court instead of the court of justice, with increased costs for eu citizens. for these reasons i have abstained on all three measures.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with this budget of variation, the 2012 budget increases the level of resources available by over eur 6 billion. the total amount of payments available for the year now ending is therefore 135.8 billion compared with the initial 129 in the budget we voted on at the december part-session last year. it is clear that there is a growing discrepancy over the years between the initial level, the level of payments we vote on when we approve the forecast budget, and the final level, that at the end of the year. this discrepancy clearly shows that we always start with an underestimation of the bills we will have to pay during the year. this underestimation is due to many reasons, not to the commission's inability, but probably to the crisis, to many political reasons which have nothing to do with the ability to estimate properly. it is an underestimation, but it does carry risks. we saw this year what happened: the commission has also been active in the field of the environment. i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the community, but that we should be concerned about the future of the community. the slowdown and the freezing of programmes that has occurred this year will certainly be a reality that we will deal with very sharply next year, because we are starting with a budget for 2013 that is more than 2% smaller than this year's budget, and with a cut of 5 billion compared to the initial estimates of the commission in its budget proposal of april this year. parliament has made every effort possible - as it did last year, as it did two years ago - to ensure an adequate level of payments, and it has certainly succeeded in achieving useful results. i believe, however, that after this experience we shall be able to solve the serious problem of underestimation and inadequacy of the level of payments once and for all only when the european budget has finally been equipped with a proper system of own resources. until then, i think we shall suffer every year on this subject. but today, and this is the important fact, we are making available 6 billion euros. this is the way to get important policies, the european social fund and cohesion policy, but also programmes such as erasmus, which have been blocked, stopped, and which have put many students and universities in difficulty in recent months, back on track. i think the erasmus blockade was a useful shock to us all. it has made us understand, and this is something we must never forget, that the union's budget is a small budget compared to europe's gross domestic product, but it is a budget which, when it stops, stops useless, concrete and very real actions in the life of every european citizen.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr mavroyiannis, commissioner lewandowski, tomorrow parliament will give its green light to the so-called draft package on which the two arms of the budgetary authority have reached agreement in recent weeks. the package consists, as the honourable member said, of amending budget no 6 for 2012, adopted for an amount of eur 6 billion out of the eur 9 billion requested by the commission, the 2013 budget, which i shall deal with shortly, and three joint declarations which aim to ensure that all payment needs for 2012 and 2013 are covered in good time. what we are about to vote on tomorrow is therefore a political agreement and, like all political agreements, it is a compromise position which is of course only partially satisfied. in fact, we are faced with partial coverage of the legal and pending payment obligations of 2012, partially postponed in fact to 2013 through the artifice of suspended accounts. the level of payments for 2013 is also not satisfactory, as it was set at eur 132.836 billion, 5 billion less than the european commission's request, due to the council's intransigence. our agreement to this agreement was conditional on the signing, at the highest institutional level, of the three joint declarations as a guarantee of the commitment of the member states to pay in 2013 the resources needed to close the accounts for 2012 and to pay fresh resources, again in the course of 2013, in order not to prejudice in any way the correct implementation of the budget for the next year. during this long procedure we as parliament have fought - and will continue to do so in the course of the next year - for the proper implementation of all european policies, reaching an agreement which avoids the risk of discontinuity for some important european programmes such as those devoted to research, development and support for smes and the erasmus programme, already mentioned by mrs balzani. turning to the 2013 budget, and with specific reference to payments, the advance level is 5 billion lower than what was requested in the draft budget. in addition, the commission submitted its db on the assumption that all payments for 2012 would be actually paid in the same year, with no rollover effect on the 2013 budget. today, however, we are faced with €2.9 billion of suspended payments carried over to 2013, plus an estimated 6 million invoices that are currently arriving at the commission for november and december 2012. we are clearly aware that this level of resources will be insufficient to cover all payment needs in 2013, but we are equally convinced that the agreement reached is the best possible one given the difficult times member states are going through. i think, however, that the cost of non-agreement would have been much higher. we would have jeopardized the stability of the european economic system. i would like to stress that the agreement contains the main priorities expressed by parliament on heading 1a, which concerns research, innovation and small and mediumsized enterprises, and i would of course like to express my appreciation for the council's willingness to make these priorities, which are those of growth and development, the basis of this new year.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to thank mr la via, mr vaughan and mr balzani, the rapporteurs for the 2013 budget and the dab no 6, for reaching this difficult compromise following the negotiations with the council. parliament reached an agreement on the 2013 budget with payment appropriations of 5 billion, less than the amount foreseen in the draft budget initially submitted by the commission. this decision is a strong act of responsibility on the part of this institution. but parliament is not prepared to sacrifice growth and, above all, employment in the european union in the name of a policy of austerity. for this reason, the same high sense of responsibility will have to be expressed by the council when, in the course of 2013, additional allocation of resources is needed to ensure the proper financing of union programmes and, above all, the payment of overdue invoices. only a genuine system of own resources will put an end to these exhausting negotiations and safeguard the credibility and solvency of the european institutions.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is clear from the speeches which have been made in this chamber that the stomachaches and pains in this negotiation within parliament have been strong and the bitterness that remains at the end of the negotiation and the achievement of the agreement is still relevant. that is why we obviously wanted to emphasize, also in previous speeches, the sense of institutional responsibility which has characterized parliament in order to avoid a crisis between the institutions and within our beloved europe. on the other hand, i must point out that parliament has insisted that the joint declarations be signed by the three institutions represented at the highest level, because this is intended to be a guarantee for the coming financial year and for a commitment also on the part of the council to meet the accounts to be paid. we cannot accept as an institution that the accounts or the invoices to be paid are not honoured. the three declarations must therefore be understood by parliament as a need for fresh additional resources for the budget for the coming financial year. it will therefore not be possible to simply move figures from one budget line to another. in order to ensure proper implementation of the budget, additional fresh resources are needed, which the council will have to make available. i would like to conclude by thanking, of course, the other institutions for their cooperation in this difficult exercise, but also by expressing my sincere thanks to all our collaborators, officials from the political groups and from parliament, who have assisted us in this long negotiation and who obviously played an important role in the process of defining the 2013 budget.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner kallas, technical forecasts tell us that air traffic is set to double by 2030 and that europe will not be able to cope with much of this demand because of its limited airport capacity. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams is not a new agreement, but rather a new agreement between ryanair and ams. it is clear that europe is in serious danger of losing a large share of the aviation market because of airport capacity constraints, and it is clear that the european institutions, the commission and parliament in particular, are called upon to respond to this scenario by making more efficient use of existing capacity and, where possible, increasing it to meet the growing demand for transport services. but we know that economic resources are limited and that the availability of land is precious to consider new airports or new runways, so the revision of the slot allocation programmes is a concrete response in this respect. to put it another way, we could say that slots are like the beats of a heart that therefore regulate the life of the organism. the draft report submitted and adopted by the committee on transport on 6 november follows the text presented by commissioner kallas, although it contains the 80/20 rule, and strengthens the mechanisms for allocating and using time bands. the text provides, as a first step, for the possibility of legitimate recourse to the secondary market in slots, i.e. the exchange of slots, including through monetary compensation, which will enable airlines to adapt their slot portfolio to their respective scheduling needs. these exchanges must take place under the close supervision of the airport coordinators, so that the procedure for the sale or purchase of a time band is carried out in accordance with the rules and with the utmost transparency. for this reason, we in the committee on transport considered it useful to provide for the publication of the financial flows from the purchase and sale of slots in an annual report to be drawn up by a coordinator. with regard to the secondary market, it is also provided that part of the proceeds from the sale of slots will be allocated to a fund to support the development of airport infrastructure and the improvement of related services. in order to ensure fair competition between operators, the full independence of the role of airport coordinators is guaranteed. the latter are the central figure in the allocation pathway of slots, being responsible for managing the allocations of slots in an impartial, non-discriminatory and transparent manner. the text guarantees their full independence both in terms of financing, so that they are dependent on air carriers and airport operators, and in operational terms, but at the same time requires them to draw up an annual report outlining the general situation of slot allocation. another innovative element is the introduction of a system of penalties which imposes a precise discipline. there are, however, some aspects which i believe parliament and this house can still improve on, and these relate to the acceptance of certain amendments: the first is to restore the consistency that was foreseen in the original text, and the second is to provide for the legal definition of slots in such a way that it is clearly stated that the parties concerned by the allocation of slots are all the parties involved, air carriers, airport managers, but also citizens. finally, mr president, may i thank all the members and the shadow rapporteurs, fidanza, sassoli, lichtenberger, foster and kohlíček, who, together with the whole committee, have made a great contribution to the drafting of the text, for their effective cooperation.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, let me start by saying that i absolutely agree with the author of the question, because mediation is faster, it is, generally speaking, cheaper than ordinary court proceedings, and it also gives rise to a culture of non-litigious behaviour. in litigation there are only winners and losers, but there can be partners if you go to mediation. so cost savings in both legal and management time for individuals and businesses make mediation a particularly attractive case. we agree on the analysis. how to get it done? you know that the mediation directive was adopted in may 2008 and was to be transposed on 21 may 2011. the good news is that all member states have announced the measures transposing the directive. the commission considers that, after one year only of application of the directive by the member states, we need to give more time for evidence and experience before concluding whether the directive has been met or not. in order to accelerate things, i intend to present a communication on mediation next year in order to promote the use of mediation. in this context we are also collecting extensive information regarding the transposition and use of the directive by member states. this study will focus on the importance of the promotion of mediation, because it is very clear that if we have an interesting law, but nobody knows that it exists and lawyers and the judiciary are not utilising it, then it does not serve the use we want it for. we think there has to be a balanced relationship between mediation and judicial procedures and that mediation should be encouraged much more strongly and in cross-border disputes. consequently, we have requested that the individual national reports which will be collected as part of the ongoing study should also provide specific information on the existing relationship between mediation and judicial proceedings in the member states. on the basis of this information we would then reflect on future steps to increase the cases to be mediated in each country and to achieve what we call a balanced relationship between mediation and judicial proceedings. in accordance with the directive (although this is not something new) i can tell you that there is due to be a report in 2016. on the basis of this report the commission will see if the directive needs to be changed and whether there need to be amendments or new proposals. but i believe that in the meantime we should not wait until 2016 to go ahead with the proposals which i have made. i see mediation also in the context of our justice for growth programme. as you know, we have bound together a series of measures in order to bring an enhancement of economic activities – mostly cross-border for smes – with the help of justice reforms, and mediation is one of these. that is also why we have put mediation into the annual growth survey 2013, which sets a priority for the reforms in all member states. within the context of the european semester, the commission is developing a justice scoreboard for analysing the strengths and the weaknesses of the judicial systems in all member states. this will also serve as a tool for member states to improve the efficiency, quality and independence of their civil justice system. we have seen that the equality, independence and efficiency of these systems is a factor for growth or non-growth, so we have included this in our annual growth survey in the hope that by this means we can also push for more mediation to be taken up in the member states. this can also be achieved through appropriate training, information and awareness-raising, along with the introduction of incentives to make mediation interesting for the parties. this is work in progress, but work we are behind with and which we are pushing in order to advance more quickly.

in writing. − in recent years, the european motorcycle industry, and in particular the italian one, has been hit hard by the crisis. in italy alone, the leading european producer of two-wheelers, there was a decline in production and registrations of more than 30 percentage points from 2008 to 2010 and the cost was borne by many workers who lost their jobs due to this sharp slowdown. the european globalisation adjustment fund is designed to facilitate the reintegration of these people into the world of work, and in this case it will benefit emilian workers affected by redundancies due to the crisis in the motorcycle industry. this is one of the few examples of italian companies having access to this european fund, and it can serve as an example for other sectors and other companies affected by the crisis to receive this aid. of course, it would be better to prevent these problems from occurring in advance and not to seek remedies when the situation is compromised. we hope that europe will learn from its mistakes and defend its companies and workers vigorously from the outset, because, as a well-known advertisement said, prevention is better than cure.
in writing. - as a member of the european parliament from emilia-romagna, i can only rejoice at the adoption of this resolution, which i voted in favour of, to mobilise the european globalisation fund for a total amount of eur 2 658 495 for italy. the application concerns 512 redundancies in ten undertakings active in the manufacture of means of transport in my region. the european globalisation adjustment fund is an important instrument for industrial conversion which the european union makes available to companies at risk of closure as a result of globalisation. the contribution will be paid to the ministry of social policies and the emilia-romagna region will be the intermediate body of the managing authority. i am sorry to note, however, that once again a large tenth of this european parliament, the majority of which are british and dutch members of parliament and a few french members, continue to reject any gesture of solidarity with our country, on this occasion as well as on other recent ones such as the terrible earthquake which left many families, elderly people and children stranded on the streets on 20 may. it would be good to remind these members that italy is one of the largest contributors to the european budget, which their respective countries also benefit from through joint programmes.
in writing. - i consider the european globalisation adjustment fund to be an indispensable instrument for ensuring support for workers in the motorcycle sector in italy, who have been hit hard by the world financial and economic crisis. due to the major changes affecting the european motorcycle industry, there has been a significant decrease in the registration of two-wheel motor vehicles in europe. with regard to italy in particular, the production of motorcycles and motorcycles has been reduced in a worrying way and it cannot be overemphasized here that my country is the leading producer in europe of two-wheel motor vehicles. the egf will help to reintegrate into the labour market 502 workers made redundant by ten motorcycle and spare parts manufacturers in emilia-romagna. i am voting in favour because i believe that we must show the will to take concrete action to help save one of the most vulnerable sectors of industry.
in writing. − on 19 october 2012, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of italy to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in global trade flows due to globalisation. the application in question, for a total amount of eur 2 658 495, concerns approximately 500 redundancies in ten companies in emilia-romagna active in the motorcycle manufacturing sector. the coordinated package of personalised services to be financed, including compatibility with actions financed by the structural funds, shall include measures for the professional reintegration of the workers concerned, such as career guidance, assistance in actively seeking employment, training and retraining initiatives, relocation services, promotion of entrepreneurship and allowances for active research. i have, of course, voted in favour of this.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european statistics on crime prevention because it is on the basis of accurate and consistent statistical data that legislative and operational instruments can be developed at eu level. the phenomenon of organised crime has become transnational and therefore affects all member states. we need statistical data, obtained with uniform methodologies and criteria, which can be subsequently re-used at european level to develop coherent and effective policies. action against organised crime is essential to protect the security of citizens and the legal economy. increased judicial and police cooperation between member states and increasing levels of circulation of reliable information and statistics should also be promoted.
in writing. − the method of data collection for the production of european crime safety statistics has left some doubt about the actual effectiveness of this survey method and, consequently, about their actual statistical validity. in addition, the report presented by the commission contains further critical points, which are why i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of this resolution, which in fact rejects the statistical survey as a whole. i believe that some of the steps in the study and data processing process must therefore be revised and, finally, that the costs of this type of survey should be better accounted for and, where possible, while respecting the standards of efficiency and effectiveness, that costs should be reduced as much as possible.

in writing. − european security policies have always been implemented on the basis of information and statistical data, which have been used to provide appropriate and effective security tools. i do not think that the provision of reliable measurements justifies the methodology used for receiving data. i think that in future action must be taken in this respect, taking particular account of the sensitivity of the questions raised. when investigating crime perceptions, it is necessary to ask clear, precise questions that are consistent with the sensitive data being investigated. similar inquiries are useful in so far as the questions asked do not leave room for divergent interpretations and each member state has a duty to carry them out. it is thought that not all member states have the same duty to collect information on, for example, domestic violence. i am voting in favour of the proposal in the hope that new legislative proposals will improve the methodology for collecting statistical data.

in writing. - i do not support the zasada report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on groundhandling services at union airports and repealing council directive 96/67/ec. i believe that there is no credible evidence to justify a new legislative proposal to liberalize groundhandling services. i think that the available data show that such an act is only likely to destabilise the sector with repercussions for workers, who will risk further reductions in wages and already weak forms of protection at work.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the commission's proposal does not bring any benefit or improvement. i agree with the rapporteur who categorically rejects any further liberalization. the market for ground handling services has already reached a high level of productivity. increasing the social pressure on the workers in the sector and forcing them into a precarious situation is contrary to the interests of the security of the population. the objective of improving quality is not achieved by social dumping. the current standards, the regularity of operations and the strong motivation of workers are at risk. a full opening of the market would increase the pressure on ground staff, who would in turn be forced to reduce staff costs. this would lead to downward pressure on wages, less job stability, less training of staff and an increase in fixed-term work.
in writing. - ground support services, which are crucial to the smooth running of air operations, have long been the subject of debate. efficiency is being sought, in the knowledge of the importance of these. the objective of reducing delays and improving the quality of passenger services can be pursued through the reformulation of the legal framework of the regulation, which provides an opportunity to significantly improve the existing system. i believe, for example, that by providing self-service for each airline, the overall quality of service can be improved, particularly at large airports. since we have seen the negative effects of the experience of liberalization leading to the precariousness of work, i believe that the opening up of the care services market is a positive opportunity only if it is balanced, since a complete opening up of the market would lead to downward pressure on staff wages. it is also important to take into account the urgency of developing a common and transparent charging system for centralised airport infrastructure and facilities and of introducing improvements to tendering procedures. in the light of the foregoing considerations, i am in favour of ensuring the highest possible level of quality and safety.
in writing. - mr zasada's report is part of the so-called 'airports package'. although the commission's proposal on groundhandling services at eu airports can bring improvements to the current regulatory system, there are still several issues that deserve more appropriate scrutiny. only when this has been done will there be the requirements to ensure a real opening up of the market based on consistency, transparency and a better service for airport staff and consequently for european passengers.
in writing. − the new regulation on the allocation and use of airport slots represents, within the airport package, a step forward in efficiency and transparency in the allocation and use of slots at european level. while i share the commission's general objective of ensuring the optimal allocation and use of airport slots at congested airports in the european union, i nevertheless believe that the entire system of allocation of slots cannot be without a clear organisational and financial separation of coordinators from all the actors involved, such as airlines and airport operators. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that we need to seek greater independence for the role of coordinators, also through a more balanced presence of stakeholders within the coordination committee. i welcome two important developments: the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to take part in the negotiations on the new agreement with the united kingdom, which is currently being negotiated by the united kingdom.
in writing. - i do not support the uggias report on the allocation of slots at eu airports. the allocation of slots to air carriers is currently governed by regulation (eec) no 95/93. the mechanism provided for in the treaty has been suspended several times over the last decade. the 2009 suspension, which was due to the financial recession and the crisis in the aviation sector, had significant consequences in italy, leading to a de facto monopoly situation for alitalia-cai on linate. the text under vote contains a number of amendments to ensure that the mechanism for allocating slots continues to protect the free competition regime. but there is no provision for excluding any derogations, and that is precisely why i voted against it.
in writing. the new proposal for a regulation introduces parameters which would be too burdensome for airlines. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. moreover, the clause allowing for derogation from the application of this rule risks facilitating monopolistic positions, as was the case with alitalia - cai on the linate - fiumicino route. for these reasons, i vote against.
in writing. − the european union has been founded from the outset on the development of a common market as free and equal as possible. unfortunately, however, there are still pockets within the common market where various influences have prevented the free market from unfolding, and one of these concerns the european airport sector. this is why the management of airport take-off and landing slots needs to be improved, increasing the flexibility of their management and reducing distortions caused by external interference. the report we have voted on today goes in this direction: it is of great importance to regulate the allocation and exchange of landing and take-off slots between different carriers, by encouraging the exchange of unused slots and increasing the independence of slot coordinators from air carriers and airports.
in writing. − the european union is called upon to take concrete action to prepare for the future growth of air traffic: the number of people living in poverty is expected to double by 2030, with the greatest concentration in asia-pacific and the middle east. european airports are already congested and time slots are a valuable resource to be used in the best possible way. this report, which i support in its entirety, will enable us to review the current system of allocation of slots, by strengthening the mechanisms for allocation and use and ensuring their effective application, and by introducing the possibility of using the secondary market for slots. the report provides that slot allocation is to be managed by airport coordinators, independently of airport operators and airlines. in order to ensure maximum transparency, data relating to the sale of secondary slots will be published in annual reports and the proceeds from these sales will be used to improve services at airports.
in writing. − increasing air traffic has intensified pressure on available capacity at major eu airports. under the current legislation, airlines that have used their own time bands for at least 80% of the time during the summer/winter season are entitled to use the same bands during the same period of the following year. bands that are not sufficiently used are entrusted to the time band pool for reallocation . the regulation also allows airlines to transfer or exchange bands, but not to sell or buy them. an analysis shows that the current system prevents the optimal use of limited airport capacity, such as: abuse and late return of unused bands, barriers to entry and expansion of new competitors, lack of an eu framework for the secondary market and insufficient independence of band coordinators. i believe that in order to manage the limited capacity effectively, it would be appropriate to strengthen the systems for band allocation and not to increase the infrastructure in order not to harm the environment. i am in favour of the proposal to buy and sell time slots. however, i would stress the need for the secondary market not to jeopardize links with the main regional airports.
in writing. the leichtfreid report is based on the international civil aviation organisation (icao) estimates that the number of european citizens exposed to noise emissions from airports is set to increase significantly over the next few decades. i did not think i could support this text with my vote, because the measures identified in it and the way they are implemented will not be effective in achieving the objectives it sets out and will be highly counterproductive both for european industry and for the maintenance of socioeconomic balances. on the one hand, the european aircraft industry will be discriminated against in favour of production from third countries, and on the other hand the proposal does not assess the impact that further operational restrictions could have on the socioeconomic realities of our territories.
in writing. - the proposal contains the preconditions for a gradual reduction in the competitiveness of european airlines, mainly because of an article providing for exemption from the imposition of restrictions for aircraft registered in developing third countries. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the application of the principle of proportionality. the same regulation would also prohibit night flights, which would cause serious inconvenience to shipping companies and their customers who would see deliveries of mail considerably delayed. for these reasons, i vote against.
in writing. − the adoption of additional noise abatement measures must be based on a systematic environmental monitoring and control process and a conservative approach, aimed at the early identification of necessary management and/or operational corrective measures. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i voted for it. air transport also provides citizens with mobility, and in recent years low-cost airlines have played an important role in making it possible to fly for a few hours for a few euros. the downside, however, is that our skies are clogged with planes, it is not uncommon for people to wait in line on the tarmac for their takeoffs, and entire neighborhoods near airports are living in nightmares and legal battles to stop commercial flights at night. by day, as well as by night, planes fly over homes and dump tons of spent fuel. the right of european citizens to a quiet and healthy life must not be at the expense of the freedom of movement of others. this balance has now been achieved by this resolution, which provides for a better distribution of take-off and landing areas by setting noise thresholds based on criteria such as health, economy and a balanced social approach. finally, it is right that the proposal to improve competition between companies operating groundhandling services at strategic airports has been referred back to the committee on transport: with at least 5 million passengers; it is an incentive to return to the debate on how to make airport services more competitive.
in writing. − noise is one of the main environmental impacts of airport infrastructure. the noise nuisance problems faced by local communities living near airports need to be addressed by measures to reduce nuisance. updating and optimising existing measures is part of the union's special responsibility with regard to noise pollution. in view of the continuing growth of the air transport sector, emphasis should be placed on the use of aircraft capable of providing state-of-the-art performance and on the development of airport infrastructure in line with traffic management needs. a balanced approach to the problem will also allow consideration to be given to the best relationship between achievable results and costs. i hope that the most appropriate measures will be identified to achieve the maximum environmental benefit at the lowest cost and that economic incentives will be considered if necessary. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − this vote is part of the so-called 'airports package' and concerns the commission's proposal to update existing measures to enable local authorities to improve the noise environment around eu airports, within the international framework of the icao's balanced approach to noise management. this balanced approach shall be applied consistently, focusing on reducing aircraft noise at source. land use planning and management, noise abatement operating procedures (such as the use of runways, routes or specific procedures) and operating restrictions.
