in writing. - mr president, the crisis that began in september 2008 has had a devastating impact on public finances and the economies of all our countries. european citizens, especially those on the lowest incomes, are paying the price. the financial sector is clearly responsible. today's vote recognises this responsibility and takes a step forward with the 11 eu countries agreeing to establish enhanced cooperation on the financial transaction tax. this is an important achievement, but the journey has just begun. there is no doubt that the other countries which are still opposed or hesitant to introduce this basic and minimal tax will now have to join the 11 countries which have led the way. in fact, it is ultimately a matter of promoting a little social justice by making those who are responsible for this situation pay a little. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of this important report.
in writing. the financial transaction tax is the result of one of the battles in parliament to build a useful instrument to combat the crisis affecting europe. its entry into force, even if only in 11 member states, is of high value, considering the resistance that had to be overcome in order to introduce it in at least 9 countries (as provided for in the treaties). the european union's own resources are one of parliament's main assets. it considers it essential that the european budget be financed from european resources and not just from contributions from the member states. the financial transaction tax is one of these instruments. finally, in order to make this instrument more effective in its use, i believe it is necessary to accompany it with initiatives aimed at strengthening cooperation between the states on the methods of application and the methods of regulation.
in writing. − following the ecofin of 22 june 2012, which highlighted the impossibility of reaching a unanimous consensus on the commission's september 2011 proposal on the taxation of financial transactions, 11 member states requested the initiation of the enhanced cooperation procedure in this area, as provided for in the eu treaty - title iv. i decided to abstain on the podimata resolution on the authorization of enhanced cooperation because i do not agree with the acceleration that is being applied to the dossier, especially since the content of the legislative proposal that the european commission might present in the framework of enhanced cooperation is not known. i think the debate under way is useful, especially in terms of: generating new tax revenues for the eu; to combat speculation; avoid distortions of competition and the risks of double taxation arising from the application of national taxes in an uncoordinated manner. on the other hand, however, a thorough and careful evaluation of the best instruments for achieving these objectives is essential if we are to avoid the tobin tax becoming a boomerang for our economies.
in writing. - today in plenary we voted in favour of mr podimata's report, which gives the green light to the procedure for introducing a financial transaction tax (ftt) in 11 eu countries, including italy, in order to discourage excessive risk-taking in the future and to impose greater liability. the text stresses that the ultimate aim remains the introduction of a global ftt and calls on the eu to continue its efforts in this direction. the 11 eu member states which will participate in the enhanced cooperation procedure are: italy, austria, belgium, estonia, france, germany, greece, portugal, slovakia, slovenia and spain. together, they account for around 90% of the euro area's gdp. the council must now give its consent by a qualified majority in order to launch the procedure once and for all.
in writing. - i believe that the report by mrs podimata, to authorize enhanced cooperation in the field of the financial transaction tax, is a practical and necessary instrument to encourage the exit from the crisis. although a small group does not support this action, the existing coalition is already a positive sign and the enhanced cooperation, from the eleven currently involved, may be extended to other member states in the future. the financial crisis has been going on for five years, but now the creation of a common system can no longer be postponed and work must begin on the introduction of a financial transaction tax as soon as possible in order to meet the costs of the crisis in time. the financial transaction tax will be 60 times less than what citizens pay, but it will still send a message of justice to european citizens and help to ensure a fairer burden sharing.
in writing. the commission adopted a proposal for a council directive on a common system of taxation of financial transactions (ftt). i believe that in this connection it is important that all the states commit themselves to enhanced cooperation, as this will allow efforts to be directed towards the conclusion of an itf agreement at world level. the harmonization of the itf rules in the territories of the participating member states would encourage the introduction of this tax in the non-participating states. this is a tax which can generate a substantial revenue, which is necessary for the states in this difficult situation. this will help to avoid putting the cost of the crisis on the shoulders of the citizens, and will help to create a stronger and more cohesive single market and greater financial stability. for the reasons i have just given, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - following the failure to reach agreement among the 27 member states, it was decided to initiate enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction taxation, which, in addition to the european parliament's free hand, also requires the approval of the council by a qualified majority. while i am in favour of mrs podimata's text, which, on the basis of an analysis of the legal bases, approves the enhanced cooperation on this matter, i have some doubts about the distortive effects that the introduction of a financial transaction tax at eu level could have if it were not also applied at global level at the same time.
in writing. − the union has rules on the protection of animals during transport, which aim to remove technical barriers to trade in live animals while ensuring a high level of protection. i agree with the rapporteur that the uniform application of animal welfare rules is crucial to maintaining a high level of animal welfare and to avoiding distortions in the market. i am concerned about the commission's report on the state of implementation of regulation (ec) no 1/2005 because the data cited in it, which come from the member states and are not verifiable, may not fully reflect the reality of the facts, as different methods and control tools are used in each member state. the commission report finds serious shortcomings in the application of the rules in some member states. i therefore support the need for further measures to achieve better harmonisation in the context of their application and, in particular, the need to take action to establish uniform control mechanisms and penalties. i would ask the commission to consider the introduction of monitoring bodies to monitor compliance with the provisions on the protection and welfare of animals, including during transport.
in writing. - i support the wojciechowski report on the protection of animals during transport. i agree with the measures proposed to the commission in this respect, in particular the reference to the limitation of the transport time to not more than 8 hours and the suggestion to set up a network of local slaughterhouses with which, on the one hand, to promote rural areas and, on the other hand, to reduce distances and, with them, the suffering suffered by animals in the course of transport.
in writing. - considering that improving the efficiency of animal transport will have positive consequences in various areas, such as, among others, the reduction of co2 emissions, the development of 'local butchers' which will contribute to regional economic development, the transport of animals under more dignified conditions, the unification of community legislation in this field, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the protection and welfare requirements of animals during transport, insisting on more controls and prevention as sentient beings. i believe that animals should be slaughtered as close as possible to the place of production so that better quality can be guaranteed to consumers, in line with the '8hours.eu' petition, which calls for the introduction of a maximum limit of 8 hours for the transport of animals for slaughter. it would also be important to introduce improvements in particular with regard to the available space, such as the calculation of the kilogram per square metre ratio for the transport of horses. finally, i believe that the distance factor is important in ensuring a competitive balance both in the internal and external markets, by promoting the development of farms and consumption also at regional level, taking into account the particular disadvantaged geographical situation of the peripheral regions.
in writing. − member states must strengthen controls throughout the chain in order to eliminate practices that violate the regulation and worsen the conditions for the transport of animals: for example, allowing overloaded vehicles to continue to circulate or allowing control posts with inadequate facilities for feeding, watering and resting animals to continue to be used. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the wojciechowski report on the protection of animals during transport because i agree with its structure and its focal points. in particular, i agree with the emphasis on the need to implement and strengthen the current community legislation in this area, including through the provision of proportionate and dissuasive penalties, and the indication that slaughter should take place as close as possible and the call to review regulation 1/2005 in the light of recent scientific data published by efsa on the need to improve the conditions under which animals are transported. i also voted with conviction in favour of the call to introduce a limitation on the transport time of animals for slaughter, which should not exceed 8 hours, taking into account loading times. this indication had already been brought to the attention of the committee i chair, having been the subject of a petition to the european parliament and supported by more than one million citizens.
in writing. i have supported this resolution which reaffirms, after the adoption of written declaration no 49, the need to limit the transport of animals for slaughter to eight hours. mahatma gandhi said that the greatness of a nation and its moral progress can be judged by the way it treats its animals. we must do everything in our power to alleviate their suffering. our call for measures to reduce transport times for animals, including the creation of an eight-hour limit for the transport of animals for slaughter, demonstrates our commitment to their welfare. it shows that we are a union of states that wants to progress morally. the number of animals transported within the eu increased significantly over the five-year period 2005-09, up to 70% in the case of pigs. one third of these death journeys take more than eight hours. at least the last hours of these animals' lives are not suffering or torture.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of the report by mr wojciechowski on the protection of animals during transport, as it suggests to the commission a number of measures to be taken for the welfare of animals during transport. in fact, there is a clear reference to the petition "8hours.eu" (signed by over a million eu citizens), it is emphasised that animals are sensitive beings, the need to manage the transport of animals both inside and outside the eu more effectively and the possibility of having local slaughterhouses which in addition to promoting rural areas reduce the distances to the slaughterhouses with the consequent reduction of co2 emissions. as regards control systems, a navigation system is introduced to monitor animal transport by collecting data via satellite navigation and the key role of retailers, catering companies and food manufacturers in ensuring, in their internal quality standards, the origin of meat from animals raised and slaughtered locally and transported under welfare conditions is emphasised.
in writing. − there is a growing interest not only in public opinion but also in the european institutions in the welfare and protection of animals during transport. this increased sensitivity is partly due to modern scientific knowledge that tells us that animals are sentient beings that feel emotions and partly because animal welfare is closely related to the safety of the food that they produce. the transport phase should be subject to greater uniformity. i would like to stress in particular the major problems in the transport of live animals, due to irregularities in the documentation, excessive load density, malfunctioning or even the absence of the watering system and other devices provided for in the means of transport. in order to ensure that the conditions for transporting animals are improved, i shall vote in favour.
in writing. − the uniform implementation and application of animal protection rules is crucial to maintain a high level of animal protection and to avoid market distortions in the european union. in some member states, for example, there will still be serious shortcomings in the application of the rules. the overall number of live animals transported increased significantly in the period 2005-2009. new measures are therefore necessary to protect the welfare of these animals, including slaughter animals. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's position that, in order to protect the welfare of animals during transport, he suggests the development of an objective and reliable assessment system and the adoption of measures vis-à-vis the member states to ensure a comprehensive and uniform monitoring of compliance with the animal control provisions.
in writing. - mr president, i voted against the report because it is a completely uncritical reproduction of the positions which have unfortunately been entrenched for some time in the european institutions, which see the concerns and needs of all the expressions and sensitivities of the most diverse and disparate minorities as prevailing, with complete disregard for the rights of peoples. as a follower of guy héraud's ethno-federalist teaching, my approach to the matter starts exactly from the point of reference represented by the rights of peoples, convinced as i am - as silvius magnago rightly observed - that europe is an extraordinary mosaic enriched by differences, peculiarities and traditions. all this is regularly ignored, as our ethno-cultural identity is trampled underfoot and threatened even in its primary expression, the linguistic one. it is not by chance that i tabled a number of amendments aimed at specific protection for the use of one's own language, the effective implementation of the right of ethno-linguistic minorities to access local, national and european radio and television programmes, and the urgent implementation of measures to block the process of homologation of minority cultures that is under way, with the clear political consent of those who are currently leading the european union.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner reding, this week has been marked by a distinctly broad reflection, debate and vote on the question of the protection of human rights. there is no doubt that there is still a clear gap between the provision for the protection of fundamental rights and their effective protection. this is precisely the area in which we should be moving. this is a week in which we have seen important events, starting with the awarding of the nobel peace prize. peace and culture are linked in practical terms to a fundamental need, namely to widen the range of themes that the agency can deal with. we have noted that the council did not share the same view on police and judicial cooperation. we believe that, at a time when the european parliament is deciding to set up the special committee against mafias, corruption and money laundering, there is a need to acquire also significant information that the agency could provide. at the same time, we must not forget that other areas are also taken into account by the agency, including the disabled, the protection of victims of crime and the fight against discrimination on grounds of gender, language, religion and sexual orientation. what is more important today than ever is real and genuine access to justice, justice which must be combined with certain time limits and fundamental rights which must be guaranteed by the programmes and the work of the agency, but also by a framework of reference which is the one we are dealing with today. i think that the work of mrs ždanoka deserves support and that is why i believe that parliament can give further impetus to the question of judicial and police cooperation so that it can finally be included in the agency's areas of competence.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to express my appreciation for the sense of responsibility which mrs ždanoka has shown to her colleagues and to all the shadow rapporteurs in bringing the work on this report to a conclusion and in asking parliament to vote on it, despite her expressed dissatisfaction at the failure to obtain an extension of the mandate - i call it that - for the agency. i found the debate this morning to be in some parts overly partisan and instrumental. the agency is a support body, an assistance body for the eu institutions and for the member states, to which they can turn when they have a problem with the application of community law in relation to fundamental rights. with lisbon, the charter of fundamental rights of the union has become an integral part of the treaty material on which we must draw our inspiration. i am aware of this fact on a daily basis as chairman of the committee on petitions, since citizens turn to me to ask me to comment on the correctness of the institutions' conduct in the exercise and respect of fundamental rights. i believe that the agency's support in terms of information, study and in-depth study of the whole range of fundamental rights, in which we have included our action by transposing the charter of fundamental rights, is very important. i also believe that this mandate, which is implicit in the approval of the multiannual plan, cannot and should not be seen as restrictive. what we should be inspired by is the programme contained in the articles of the charter of fundamental rights.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam vice-president of the commission, today we are having the classic debate which always animates us in situations like this. renewing the agency's action, especially in times of crisis like the one we are going through, always brings with it the same question: is it right to spend new resources, maintain both physical and functional structures and stabilise constraints, sometimes interference and institutional conflicts? we are again reflecting this morning on whether to renew the european union agency for fundamental rights for the next multiannual framework and whether this is right or not. one thing we can say for sure: the judicial cooperation that this agency establishes is a good and right thing, especially in the field of fundamental rights which are so sensitive to our european institutions. moreover, we clearly cannot afford to block the multiannual framework, risking to stop or at any rate limit the work of an institution which intervenes in the field of racism, the protection of minors, asylum and against discrimination of any kind for the protection of justice and the participation of citizens. these are too important and too dear to us to stop and not give our consent. i know that in many member states there are institutions or agencies which work very well and have the same field of action, but the purpose of the european agency is precisely to be able to coordinate better what is happening in our member states and to improve the existing gaps, it is the possibility of comparing data and seeing how some phenomena develop globally in order to be able to give answers with appropriate policies. sure, that comes at a cost, but what doesn't? i think it's really important to move forward and then calmly evaluate the results.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to point out to the commissioner that there are two problems in this crisis situation, among the many that have been mentioned, but which i find particularly dangerous. in the face of the lack of growth we often emphasize the problem of employment, pointing to the decline in employment as the main phenomenon, but forgetting the increase in poverty, which is becoming a real emergency for many areas of community europe. poverty is so dangerous because we have introduced an american phenomenon that we did not know but which has also arrived here, which is that of poor work. women in particular are now in a position to have a productive activity, a working relationship, and to be unable, with the income they derive, to cross the poverty line. i believe that this is the main problem among the negative effects of lack of development and therefore deserves special attention and specific policies.
in writing. − due to shortcomings in certain areas, such as respect for economic, social and cultural rights; the weakness of the monitoring mechanism as regards the rights of disabled persons; the inclusion of a specific chapter on the roma, a group which is known to refuse to be included in host societies, at the expense of other issues, such as those mentioned above, was not my vote.
in writing. - i believe that written statements are a tool which could potentially have a significant impact on issues considered important, also in order to raise public awareness of the issues dealt with by parliament. the proposed amendments will ensure that a greater number of written statements are followed up, and that the necessary number of members are supported. i also believe that the rules governing them should be changed so that they can only be proposed in cases where they have an impact on union legislation. for the reasons just given, i vote in favour.
in writing. − i strongly support this report because it stresses the need for the eu to act consistently to enhance the effectiveness of its human rights policies and to be a credible actor in external relations. in particular i am happy about the significant victory achieved by all human rights supporters with the adoption of the amendment on western sahara. in this amendment we condemn the ongoing repression of the sahrawi people in the occupied territories, demand the release of all sahrawi political prisoners and ask for a lasting settlement of the western sahara issue on the basis of the right to self-determination of the sahrawi people. the rights of the sahrawi are those of us all and once again this parliament showed its commitment to end this blatant violation of international law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world in 2011 and on the european union's policy on the matter, because i believe it is essential not to accept the report in its entirety. strengthening the instruments for the promotion of human rights, fundamental freedoms and democracy by cooperating closely in the implementation of a human rights policy in the world is the preeminent role to which the european union is called. the proper functioning of civil society and the development of a democratic and rights-based community is a long-term process that must be achieved from below and requires national, regional, local and international support. the political dialogue on human rights between the eu and third countries needs to include a more inclusive and comprehensive definition of the concept of non-discrimination on the basis of factors such as religion, personal beliefs, sex, race, ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation and gender identity. the recent award of the nobel peace prize to the eu should not be seen as a milestone but as a first step which further encourages decisive action in the field of human rights, both now and in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of mr donskis’s report on the european union’s policy on the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world 2011 for a number of reasons. the report highlights the importance of international humanitarian law (ihl), and particularly urges the eu to take a stronger stance in implementing ihl and considering it when entering into bilateral agreements with third countries. not only is it important that the eu respect human rights, but we should do everything possible to ensure that basic standards of human rights are upheld in countries throughout the world, which the report directly encourages. additionally, i support the inclusion of women’s rights in the report, as establishing human rights relies upon establishing equal rights between the sexes.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. in the wake of the arab spring, it is important to develop a coherent and diversified eu policy on transitional justice in addition to strengthening the independence of the judiciary, including linking with the icc as a court of last resort, in order to help countries in transition address past human rights violations, fight impunity and prevent the recurrence of such violations.
in writing. − the european union must commit itself to promoting and consolidating the values of freedom, democracy, development and respect for human rights, the values on which it is founded, through political dialogue and cooperation with third countries. i therefore voted in favour of mr donskis' text, expressing the hope that the union will continue to play its leading role in defending human rights in the world by making effective, consistent and reasoned use of all the instruments at its disposal to ensure the promotion and protection of democratic systems.
in writing. - i support the tavares report on the review of the eu's human rights strategy. i agree with the rapporteur's proposals, the revision is based on the fundamental principle of respect for human rights in all european and member state policies. i think it is essential to recall the passage in this text in which the high representative and the commission are called upon to implement a european neighbourhood policy by applying more consistently and more strongly the principles of 'more aid for more commitment' and 'less aid for less commitment'. third countries in which there is a clear lack of progress on the rule of law should see less support from the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution because we know that the european union is founded on the principle of respect for human rights and has a legal obligation, laid down in the treaties, to place human rights at the centre of all the policies of the union and the member states without exception, as well as at the centre of all international agreements. member states and third countries must implement concrete measures to ensure that human rights remain at the heart of these policies. the promotion of human rights and democracy is a joint and shared responsibility of the eu and its member states, but only coordinated and consistent action by both sides can achieve results and make progress. we unanimously agree that every human being should enjoy the universal human rights and freedoms enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights, regardless of circumstances or situations, religion or personal belief, sex, racial or ethnic origin, age, disability, sexual orientation and gender identity.
in writing. − the eu's human rights strategy has repeatedly demonstrated its effectiveness and readiness to act in addressing problems related to this sensitive issue. however, as this report points out, it needs to be updated and revised, also in the light of the latest historical and social dynamics (e.g. the arab spring) in order to be able to continue to be effective and efficient. it also requires greater interinstitutional cooperation and greater coordination between the member states on policies relating to the subject.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. i agree with the rapporteur that it is essential to identify country-specific priorities, realistic objectives and forms of political influence in order to make eu action more effective and achieve measurable results. national human rights strategies must be integrated into the eu's common foreign and security policy and trade and development policies.
in writing. - development, democracy and the rule of law: these are the bases from which the european union must start to protect the ideals of democracy and respect for human rights. i therefore express my vote in favour and would like to stress the need for more effective action to support human rights activists in europe and in third countries, especially those who are threatened or forced to live in fear on a daily basis because of their work. i would like to conclude by stressing the need to include 'enforceable and non-negotiable' clauses on human rights in agreements between the union and third countries.
in writing. − i abstained on voting on this report because, although i support the need for the eu to enjoy a strategic relationship with russia and i praise the pragmatic view of this text, i cannot support a report which characterises mr khodorkovsky as a hero. whoever considers him a martyr of freedom is the victim of a blatant disinformation. mr khodorkovsky was one of the biggest oligarchs in russia during the nineties. his bad reputation is well established in his country and elsewhere, but he is still a rich man with a lot of capital deposited abroad. with this money, as some of us meps know from personal experience, he can pay the bills of prominent lobbyists and well-known public relations companies. this led to a shameful pro-khodorkovsky campaign in this parliament to which we must put an end.
in writing. - in voting on the swoboda report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the council, the commission and the european external action service on the negotiations for the new eu-russia agreement, i abstained. i consider the need for greater commercial interdependence in eu-russia relations to be fundamental, but i cannot hide my concern at the deterioration of the situation of respect for human rights and democracy in the russian federation. russia can be a great trading partner for the eu, but it is necessary to insist on a strengthening of the dialogue on respect for human rights, the union's founding value.
in writing. - we must cooperate with russia to ensure that it takes responsibility for improving stability, political cooperation and economic development in the common neighbourhood and to stress the sovereign right of each country to choose its own foreign policy and security arrangements. at the same time, we must be firm in calling on the russian authorities to put an end to the widespread climate of impunity for human rights violations and the absence of the rule of law in the north caucasus.
in writing. - i congratulate mr swoboda on his work. in the report adopted today, parliament, in the light of the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the russian federation, of the other part, which entered into force on 1 december 1997, reiterated that russia can only become a strategic partner for the european union if it begins to share and promote the democratic principles and values recognised by the 27 member states. to achieve these objectives, it will be necessary to continue and even strengthen the eu-russia talks, which will lead to the conclusion of a new and more precise pact of alliance and cooperation. finally, parliament rightly called on russia to take more seriously important issues such as impunity, endemic corruption, politically motivated persecution, arrests, detention and economic modernisation.
in writing. − the development of the european union's common foreign and energy policy, in line with the principle of conditionality, should include russia as a strategic partner, provided that the fundamental values on which the union is founded are shared and upheld, including democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity and respect for the principles of the united nations charter and international law. this vote will ensure that a new agreement provides a comprehensive, forward-looking and legally binding framework for the further development of relations with russia in the coming years, taking into account the need to make efforts to strengthen cooperation in all areas where eu and russian interests may coincide, while promoting european interests and values in areas where interests diverge.
in writing. the text by mr swoboda concerns the european parliament's recommendations on the negotiations for a new eu-russia agreement to replace the existing partnership and cooperation agreement in force since december 1997. the aim of this agreement is to build a closer relationship with russia, based on common core principles and values. the text stresses the need to strengthen dialogue with civil society and all the main political actors and to ensure the functioning of an independent and impartial judicial system in order to put an end to impunity in the country. the report rightly also points to the state of degradation of the development of civil society in russia, especially in the light of the recent adoption of laws on demonstrations, ngos, defamation and legal regulation of the internet.
in writing. − i strongly support this resolution because it condemns the israelis’ plan to proceed with the construction of 3 000 new settlement units in the west bank and east jerusalem. we must bear in mind that, if implemented, the announced plans will undermine the viability of the two-state solution, with special regard to the e1 area, where settlement constructions would divide the west bank in two, potentially cutting palestinians off from jerusalem and rendering the creation of a viable, contiguous and sovereign palestinian state impossible. israeli settlements in the west bank and in east jerusalem are illegal under international law. for this reason, with this text we call for an immediate, complete and permanent freeze of all israeli expansion activities. we cannot remain passive when israel keeps on violating human rights and international law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the israeli government's decision to expand settlements in the west bank. this decision is not only illegal under international law but also makes it impossible to establish a sovereign palestinian state with territorial integrity, as provided for in the 1993 oslo agreements. it is therefore a stone in the road to two peoples, two states, and it is a serious obstacle to any attempt at peace and increases tension in those areas. i am not going to go into the details of the situation, but i would like to say that the commission has been very careful in its work on the matter. finally, i hope that a solution will be found soon to the pretextous decision of the tel aviv authorities to withhold $100 million in palestinian tax revenue, which is detrimental to the pa budget. i hope that europe will once again make its voice heard, loudly and decisively, in order to reaffirm the 'two peoples, two states' solution and to achieve the cessation of all conflict and the stabilization of the entire area.
in writing. - we must reiterate our support for a two-state solution based on the 1967 borders, with jerusalem as the capital of both states, the state of israel and an independent, democratic, contiguous and self-sustaining state of palestine, coexisting side by side in peace and security.
in writing. the choice of the israeli government to expand settlements in the west bank, and especially in the e1 area, between the settlement town of ma'aleh adumim and east jerusalem, has raised unanimous disagreement. the international community's condemnation and the european union's disappointment are motivated by the catastrophic consequences that would result. this is a decision that would prevent the creation of two separate states, and expansion in that area would isolate east jerusalem from the rest of the west bank, threatening the future of the palestinian state in that territory. europe firmly supports the idea of the development of the two states. this would create a balance in support of lasting peace and security. i hope that an active european role can bring about a revival of these tormented territories, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − i agree that the eu need to establish closer political and economic ties with ukraine, but i cannot give my vote to a text which asks for the freeing and political rehabilitation of mrs yulia tymoshenko. i support the demand for a fair trial for mrs tymoshenko, but i dissent from a text which makes the assumption that the former prime minister of ukraine deserves to be supported as if she was a champion of freedom and justice in her country. she was and is just a very questionable politician, already arrested for corruption and seen negatively by most ukrainians.
in writing. − the ukrainian government must, together with all political parties, remedy electoral irregularities, including inconclusive results in some constituencies.
in writing. - i express my sincere concern about the situation in ukraine due to the human rights violations and the total lack of transparency which characterised the recent electoral consultations. cooperation between the european union and ukraine cannot continue in the absence of the reforms needed to establish a genuine democratic state. europe has committed itself to supporting ukraine on its path towards democracy. the commitment will only be continued after the mortifying violations of freedom of expression in relation to sexual orientation and gender identity have ceased, as they constitute a clear violation of the european convention on human rights and the international covenant on civil and political rights. i cannot help but draw attention to the disparity of treatment, the intimidation and irregularities in the counting of votes which characterized the voting process. i believe that europe can, through effective action, provide an incentive for future reform processes, and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − i support this resolution because it reiterates our full support for albania’s future accession to the european union. as the commission’s assessment underlined, the country should be granted candidate status without further delay. in this past year indeed, albania engaged in the adoption of key reforms in the judiciary and public administration. with this text we praise the developing dialogue between the civil society and the albanian government and call on all the albanian political forces to continue to adopt concrete reforms leading to tangible results for the benefit of all citizens. nevertheless, we urge the albanian authorities to take further action to ensure the real independence, integrity, transparency and efficiency of the judiciary as this is a key element for a complete european integration
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr chountis' report on albania's progress towards eu membership, as i believe that he has taken due account of the commission's assessment that albania has met four of the 12 priorities, is on track to meet the other two and has positively recognised these results. as stated by the general affairs council last monday, i welcome the constructive role that albania continues to play in the region, but i would stress the need to intensify further efforts, particularly in the field of judicial reform in order to strengthen its independence, efficiency and accountability, the fight against corruption and organised crime, the protection of all minorities and the implementation of reforms. the successful conduct of the 2013 parliamentary elections will be a crucial test for the proper functioning of the country's democratic institutions. sustainable political dialogue and sustained engagement in all priority areas will be essential to implement the reforms needed for albania's european future.
in writing. − there has been limited progress in reforming the judicial system. the authorities should therefore be urged to take further measures to ensure the effective independence, integrity, transparency, accountability and efficiency of the judiciary and its freedom from political interference and corruption, in order to guarantee citizens' fair access to the courts, to ensure that trials take place within a reasonable timeframe and to accelerate progress in the implementation of the strategy for reforming the judiciary.
in writing. − the european parliament recognises that the political dialogue with albania so far is an important factor in achieving progress on the 12 priorities set by the eu with albania. parliament called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external relations were not jeopardised by the threat of a military coup in iraq. finally, the improvements made by albania in the protection of minorities - although effective protection against domestic violence, forced prostitution and trafficking in women and children is still lacking - and the slight improvements made in the unemployment situation were highlighted. in addition, the balkan government was recommended to undertake reforms on the rule of law and to deepen the issue of property rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of granting candidate country status to albania on condition that the main reforms in the judicial system and public administration are completed and adopted. it is also essential that the albanian government commits itself to guaranteeing freedom of the media and respect for human rights. i would like to stress that all political parties and actors in albania, including the media and civil society, must work in the near future to improve the political climate in the country so as to allow for that dialogue and mutual understanding which are indispensable in the path to accession to the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the crisis in the steel sector because i believe it is essential, especially at a time of crisis, to ensure the safeguarding of sectors which are the engine of the eu economy. the steel industry is facing major challenges today, made inevitable by the current crisis and by increasingly fierce competition from third countries with less stringent environmental regulations and cheaper access to raw materials. it is essential that the eu protects more highly technological sectors, ensures the employment of workers and enhances their skills. it is a priority for the commission to plan a competitive and long-term industrial policy. this would ensure a level playing field and stricter social and environmental standards. it is also important to develop a concrete and well-defined action plan, as well as the introduction of quality certification for steel products, to strengthen the industrial sector and avoid relocations which are counterproductive for the eu-wide economy. support measures for workers in all establishments at risk of closure are a priority for safeguarding employment in the eu.
in writing. the steel industry is going through a period of deep crisis, as are other economic and industrial sectors. the eu can do much to safeguard a sector which, including the industry, provides employment for hundreds of thousands of citizens. i therefore agree with the commission's proposal to draw up and implement a new plan for the steel industry, so as to encourage its competitive practices and support it in the long and difficult process of recovering from the crisis.
in writing. − a competitive european steel industry is the backbone of development and value creation for many important industrial sectors, such as automotive, construction and mechanical engineering. the commission must therefore give careful thought to medium- and long-term initiatives to support and preserve the steel industry and its industries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, hoping that europe would finally react to the crisis in the steel industry. in recent years, if not decades, there has been a steady decline in steel production at european level, not so much because of a decrease in demand, but because of unfair competition, especially from asia, which offers materials at very low costs. this is because elsewhere the economic and social rules laid down by the european union are not respected, and the consequence is that more and more establishments are in danger of closing down and leaving thousands of workers at home. the steel industry has been the basis of the economy and development of many areas that revolved around it: the case of piombino is a clear example of this, and i am pleased that it has been explicitly mentioned in this report. the situation in the tuscan city is very serious, as i pointed out in this chamber last month: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the european union must defend its steel: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − the commission and the council must develop a new policy for the steel industry that stimulates growth and employment in the context of the economic crisis and is compatible with the health and safety of all eu citizens, as well as its residents.
in writing. - in a difficult period like the one we are going through, the european union must strongly support its industrial base if it is to return to growth. this is why it is important to support the steel sector, which has been particularly affected by the economic crisis. to counteract the negative trend of recent years, it is therefore necessary to give serious thought to the introduction of measures to promote a purchase price for energy above the current average. there is therefore a need to create a more effective industrial policy for the eu, one that is aware of global challenges and able to safeguard our production fabric, even in the face of fierce competition from outside europe.
